entries.zh: 上怒曰：「汝罪人，何得擅離禁所！」
entries.en: The emperor angrily said, "You are a convicted man—how dare you leave confinement on your own!"
entries.literal: The sovereign in anger said, "You are a criminal—how dare you leave your place of confinement on your own!"

entries.zh: 詔誅守者，復置於獄。
entries.en: An edict ordered the guards put to death, and he was returned to prison.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the guards executed, and he was again placed in prison.

entries.zh: 及改元保寧，乃宥之，妻以皇后之姊，復爵，王宋。
entries.en: When the era was changed to Baoning he was pardoned, married to the empress's elder sister, restored to rank, and enfeoffed as Prince of Song.
entries.literal: When the era was changed to Baoning he was pardoned, given in marriage the empress's elder sister, restored to rank, and enfeoffed as Prince of Song.

entries.zh: 喜隱輕僄無恒，小得志即驕。
entries.en: Xiyin was frivolous and unreliable; the least success made him arrogant.
entries.literal: Xiyin was frivolous and inconstant; with the slightest success he grew arrogant.

entries.zh: 上嘗召，不時至，怒而鞭之，由是憤怨謀亂。
entries.en: Once when the emperor summoned him he failed to come promptly; the emperor in anger had him flogged, and from then on he nursed resentment and plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: The sovereign once summoned him and he did not come promptly; in anger the sovereign flogged him, and from this he nursed resentment and plotted disorder.

entries.zh: 貶而復召，適見上與劉繼元書，辭意卑遜，諫曰：「本朝於漢為祖，書旨如此，恐虧國體。」
entries.en: Though demoted he was summoned again; seeing the emperor's letter to Liu Jiyuan, whose tone was abject, he remonstrated, "Our dynasty is ancestor to Han—with wording like this, the dignity of the state will suffer."
entries.literal: Demoted yet summoned again, he happened to see the sovereign's letter to Liu Jiyuan, its wording humble and submissive, and remonstrated, saying, "Our dynasty is ancestor to Han—if the letter's intent is thus, I fear the dignity of the state will be impaired."

entries.zh: 帝尋改之。
entries.en: The emperor soon revised the letter.
entries.literal: The emperor soon revised it.

entries.zh: 授西南面招討使，命之河東索吐蕃戶，稍見進用。
entries.en: He was appointed southwestern frontier pacification commissioner and sent east of the river to seek out Tibetan households; he gradually won greater favor.
entries.literal: He was appointed southwestern frontier pacification commissioner and ordered to the east of the Yellow River to seek out Tibetan households; he gradually came into favor.

entries.zh: 復誘群小謀叛，上命械其手足，築圜土，囚祖州。
entries.en: He again incited petty followers to rebel; the emperor ordered his limbs shackled, a round-walled cell built, and him imprisoned at Zuzhou.
entries.literal: He again enticed petty men to plot rebellion; the sovereign ordered his hands and feet shackled, a round-walled enclosure built, and him imprisoned at Zuzhou.

entries.zh: 宋降卒二百餘人欲劫立喜隱，以城堅不得入，立其子留禮壽，上京留守除室擒之。
entries.en: More than two hundred surrendered Song soldiers tried to seize the city and install Xiyin; failing to enter because the walls were strong, they installed his son Liulishou instead; Upper Capital regent Chushi captured him.
entries.literal: More than two hundred surrendered Song soldiers wished to seize and install Xiyin; unable to enter because the walls were strong, they installed his son Liulishou; Upper Capital regent Chushi captured him.

entries.zh: 留禮壽伏誅，賜喜隱死。
entries.en: Liulishou was put to death, and Xiyin was sentenced to death.
entries.literal: Liulishou was executed, and Xiyin was granted death.

entries.zh: 順宗，名濬，小字耶魯斡，道宗長子，母宣懿皇后蕭氏。
entries.en: Shunzong, whose personal name was Jun and childhood name Yeluwo, was Daozong's eldest son; his mother was Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan.
entries.literal: Shunzong, personal name Jun, childhood name Yeluwo, eldest son of Daozong, mother Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan.

entries.zh: 幼而能言，好學知書。
entries.en: As a child he could speak early, loved learning, and was well read.
entries.literal: As a child he could speak; he loved learning and knew books.

entries.zh: 道宗嘗曰：「此子聰慧，殆天授歟！」
entries.en: Daozong once said, "This boy is clever—perhaps Heaven itself bestowed it!"
entries.literal: Daozong once said, "This child is clever—perhaps Heaven bestowed it!"

entries.zh: 六歲，封梁王。
entries.en: At six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: At age six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 明年，從上獵，矢連發三中。
entries.en: The next year he joined the emperor on a hunt and with three arrows in swift succession scored three hits.
entries.literal: The next year he followed the sovereign on a hunt and with arrows in swift succession hit three times.

entries.zh: 上顧左右曰：「朕祖宗以來，騎射絕人，威震天下。
entries.en: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Since my ancestors, our horsemanship and archery have been unmatched and our might has shaken the realm.
entries.literal: The sovereign turned to those beside him and said, "From my ancestors onward, horsemanship and archery have been unmatched and awe has shaken the realm.

entries.zh: 是兒雖幼，不墜其風。」
entries.en: Though this boy is young, he does not fall short of that tradition."
entries.literal: Though this boy is young, he does not fall short of that tradition."

entries.zh: 後遇十鹿，射獲其九。
entries.en: Later, meeting ten deer, he brought down nine.
entries.literal: Later encountering ten deer, he shot and took nine.

entries.zh: 帝喜，設宴。
entries.en: Delighted, the emperor held a banquet.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and held a banquet.

entries.zh: 八歲，立為皇太子。
entries.en: At eight he was made crown prince.
entries.literal: At age eight he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 大康元年，兼領北南樞密院事。
entries.en: In Dakang year 1 he also took charge of the Northern and Southern Bureaus of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dakang he concurrently directed the affairs of the Northern and Southern Bureaus of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 論曰：道宗知太子之賢，而不能辨乙辛之詐，竟絕父子之親，為萬世惜。
entries.en: Commentary: Daozong knew his son's worth yet could not see through Yixin's deceit, and in the end destroyed the bond between father and son—a loss the ages lament.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Daozong knew the crown prince's worth yet could not discern Yixin's fraud, and in the end severed father-son kin—a thing for ten thousand generations to lament.

entries.zh: 乙辛知為一身之計，不知有君臣之義，豈復知有太子乎！
entries.en: Yixin cared only for himself and knew nothing of the duty between ruler and minister—how could he spare a thought for the crown prince!
entries.literal: Yixin knew only schemes for his own person and did not know the righteousness between ruler and minister—how could he still know there was a crown prince!

entries.zh: 奸邪之臣亂人家國如此，可不戒哉！
entries.en: When treacherous ministers can overturn a household and a realm like this, who would not take warning!
entries.literal: Wicked and treacherous ministers throw households and states into disorder like this—can one fail to take warning!

entries.zh: 可不戒哉！
entries.en: Who would not take warning!
entries.literal: Can one fail to take warning!

entries.zh: 論曰：天祚不君，臣下謀立其子，適以殺之。
entries.en: Commentary: Tianzuo failed as a ruler; his ministers plotted to put his son on the throne—and thereby brought about the son's death.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Tianzuo did not act as ruler; his ministers plotted to install his son, and thereby brought about his death.

entries.zh: 敖盧斡重君父之命，不亡而死，申生其恭矣乎！
entries.en: Aolugan honored his sovereign and father, refusing flight though it meant death—was he not as dutiful as Prince Sheng of Jin!
entries.literal: Aolugan honored the command of ruler and father, not fleeing yet dying—was he not as dutiful as Shen Sheng!

entries.zh: ○義宗倍
entries.en: Yizong Bei
entries.literal: ○ Yizong Bei

entries.zh: 〈（子平王隆先晉王道隱）〉
entries.en: (Sons: Prince of Ping Longxian and Prince of Jin Daoyin)
entries.literal: (Sons: Prince of Ping Longxian and Prince of Jin Daoyin)

entries.zh: 章肅皇帝李胡
entries.en: Emperor Zhangsu Li Hu
entries.literal: Emperor Zhangsu Li Hu

entries.zh: 〈（子宋王喜隱）〉
entries.en: (Son: Prince of Song Xiyin)
entries.literal: (Son: Prince of Song Xiyin)

entries.zh: 順宗濬晉王敖盧斡
entries.en: Shunzong Jun and Prince of Jin Aolugan
entries.literal: Shunzong Jun; Prince of Jin Aolugan

entries.zh: 耶律曷魯，字控溫，一字洪隱，叠剌部人。
entries.en: Yelu Helu, whose style was Kongwen and who was also known as Hongyin, came from the Yila tribe.
entries.literal: Yelu Helu, style name Kongwen, also known by the style Hongyin, was a man of the Yila tribe.

entries.zh: 祖匣馬葛，簡憲皇帝兄。
entries.en: His grandfather Xiamage was the elder brother of Emperor Jianxian.
entries.literal: His grandfather was Xiamage, elder brother of Emperor Jianxian.

entries.zh: 父偶思，遙輦時為本部夷離堇，曷魯其長子也。
entries.en: His father Ousi had been yilijin of the tribe in the Yaolian era, and Helu was his eldest son.
entries.literal: His father Ousi, in the Yaolian period, served as yilijin of his tribe; Helu was his eldest son.

entries.zh: 性質厚。
entries.en: He was sincere and steadfast by nature.
entries.literal: His nature was sincere and steadfast.

entries.zh: 在髫鬌，與太祖遊，從父釋魯奇之曰：「興我家者，必二兒也。」
entries.en: As a child he roamed with Taizu, and Shilu, his paternal uncle, remarked in wonder, "These two boys will be the ones to restore our house."
entries.literal: While still in childhood, he kept company with the Taizu; his paternal uncle Shilu marveled at them and said: "Those who will raise up our house will surely be these two boys."

entries.zh: 太祖既長，相與易裘馬為好，然曷魯事太祖彌謹。
entries.en: When Taizu came of age, they exchanged garments and horses in friendship, yet Helu served him with ever greater devotion.
entries.literal: After the Taizu had grown up, they exchanged fur coats and horses in friendship, yet Helu served the Taizu with ever greater care.

entries.zh: 會滑哥弒其父釋魯，太祖顧曷魯曰：「滑哥弒父，料我必不能容，將反噬我。
entries.en: When Huage murdered his father Shilu, Taizu told Helu, "Huage has killed his father. He assumes I cannot bear it and will turn on me.
entries.literal: It happened that Huage murdered Shilu, his father; the Taizu turned to Helu and said: "Huage murdered his father. He reckons I cannot tolerate it and will turn to strike at me.

entries.zh: 今彼歸罪臺哂為解，我姑與之。
entries.en: He is shifting the blame onto Taishan for now, so I shall pretend to accept it for the moment.
entries.literal: Now he shifts the blame onto Taishan as an excuse; for the moment I shall go along with him.

entries.zh: 是賊吾不忘也！」
entries.en: But I will not forget that villain!"
entries.literal: That villain—I shall not forget him!"

entries.zh: 自是曷魯常佩刀從太祖，以備不虞。
entries.en: From then on Helu always kept a sword at his side and stayed with Taizu against any surprise.
entries.literal: From then on Helu constantly wore a blade and followed the Taizu, to guard against the unexpected.

entries.zh: 居久之，曷魯父偶思病，召曷魯曰：「阿保機神略天授，汝率諸弟赤心事之。」
entries.en: Some time later, when Helu's father Ousi fell ill, he called Helu and said, "Abaoji has a heaven-given genius for strategy. Lead your brothers and serve him with all your hearts."
entries.literal: After some time, Helu's father Ousi fell ill and summoned Helu, saying: "Abaoji's divine strategy is heaven-bestowed; you must lead your younger brothers to serve him with utter loyalty."

entries.zh: 已而太祖來問疾，偶思執其手曰：「爾命世奇才。
entries.en: When Taizu came to visit him, Ousi took his hand and said, "You are a talent born once in an age.
entries.literal: Soon the Taizu came to inquire after his illness; Ousi seized his hand and said: "You are a once-in-an-age extraordinary talent.

entries.zh: 吾兒曷魯者，他日可委以事，吾已諭之矣。」
entries.en: My son Helu may be entrusted with matters hereafter. I have already spoken with him."
entries.literal: My son Helu may one day be entrusted with affairs; I have already instructed him."

entries.zh: 既而以諸子屬之。
entries.en: He then entrusted his sons to Taizu.
entries.literal: He then entrusted his sons to him.

entries.zh: 太祖為撻馬狘沙裏，參預部族事，曷魯領數騎召小黃室韋來附。
entries.en: While Taizu was tamagh boshuli and took part in tribal council, Helu led a small party of horsemen to bring the Lesser Yellow Shiwei into allegiance.
entries.literal: When the Taizu served as tamagh boshuli and took part in tribal affairs, Helu led a few horsemen to summon the Lesser Yellow Shiwei to come and submit.

entries.zh: 太祖素有大志，而知曷魯賢，軍國事非曷魯議不行。
entries.en: Taizu had long cherished great ambitions and knew Helu's worth; no military or civil measure went forward without Helu's counsel.
entries.literal: The Taizu had long harbored great ambitions and knew Helu to be worthy; no military or state matter proceeded without Helu's counsel.

entries.zh: 會討越兀與烏古部，曷魯為前鋒，戰有功。
entries.en: On campaigns against the Yuewu and the Uighur tribe, Helu led the van and won merit in battle.
entries.literal: When he campaigned against the Yuewu and the Uighur tribe, Helu served as vanguard and distinguished himself in battle.

entries.zh: 及太祖為叠剌部夷離堇，討奚部，其長術裏逼險而壘，攻莫能下，命曷魯持一笴往諭之。
entries.en: When Taizu became yilijin of the Yila tribe and attacked the Xi, their chief Shuli held the high ground behind fortifications and could not be dislodged. Taizu sent Helu with a single arrow as envoy to reason with them.
entries.literal: When the Taizu became yilijin of the Yila tribe and campaigned against the Xi tribe, their chief Shuli held a defensible position and built fortifications; the attack could not take them, so he ordered Helu to carry a single arrow and go to persuade them.

entries.zh: 既入，為所執。
entries.en: Once he entered, they seized him.
entries.literal: Once inside, he was seized by them.

entries.zh: 乃說奚曰：「契丹與奚言語相通，實一國也。
entries.en: He then addressed the Xi: "The Khitan and the Xi speak the same tongue and are in truth one people.
entries.literal: He then addressed the Xi, saying: "The Khitan and the Xi share a language and are in truth one people.

entries.zh: 我夷離堇於奚豈有夌轢之心哉？
entries.en: Why would our yilijin harbor any thought of grinding the Xi down?
entries.literal: How could our yilijin harbor any thought of grinding down the Xi?

entries.zh: 漢人殺我祖奚首，夷離堇怨次骨，日夜思報漢人。
entries.en: The Han killed our ancestor the Xi chief. Our yilijin bears a hatred to the marrow and thinks day and night of repaying the Han.
entries.literal: The Han killed our ancestor, the Xi chief; the yilijin bears hatred to the marrow and day and night thinks of repaying the Han.

entries.zh: 顧力單弱，使我求援於奚，傳矢以示信耳。
entries.en: His strength alone is too slight, so he sent me to seek aid from the Xi and to pass this arrow as proof of good faith.
entries.literal: Only his strength is slight and isolated, so he sent me to seek aid from the Xi and to pass an arrow as a token of trust.

entries.zh: 夷離堇受命於天，撫下以德，故能有此眾也。
entries.en: Our yilijin received Heaven's mandate and rules his people with virtue. That is why he commands such a host.
entries.literal: The yilijin received his mandate from Heaven and rules his people with virtue; that is why he can command such a host.

entries.zh: 今奚殺我，違天背德，不祥莫大焉。
entries.en: If the Xi kill me now, you defy Heaven and turn from virtue. No omen could be more dire!
entries.literal: If the Xi now kill me, they defy Heaven and turn from virtue—no ill omen could be greater.

entries.zh: 且兵連禍結，當自此始，豈爾國之利乎！」
entries.en: And when war chains one disaster to the next, it will begin here. How could that serve your people's good?"
entries.literal: Moreover, when war links one disaster to the next, it will begin from this—how could that benefit your state!"

entries.zh: 術裏感其言，乃降。
entries.en: Shuli was moved by his words and submitted.
entries.literal: Shuli was moved by his words and thereupon submitted.

entries.zh: 太祖為於越，秉國政，欲命曷魯為叠剌部夷離堇。
entries.en: When Taizu became Yuyue and held state power, he wished to appoint Helu yilijin of the Yila tribe.
entries.literal: When the Taizu became Yuyue and held the reins of state, he wished to appoint Helu yilijin of the Yila tribe.

entries.zh: 辭曰：「賊在君側，未敢遠去。」
entries.en: Helu declined, saying, "The villain is at your side. I dare not go far away."
entries.literal: Helu declined, saying: "The villain is at the ruler's side; I dare not go far away."

entries.zh: 太祖討黑車子室韋，幽州劉仁恭遣養子趙霸率眾來救。
entries.en: Taizu campaigned against the Black Cart Shiwei. Liu Rengong of Youzhou sent his adopted son Zhao Ba with an army to relieve them.
entries.literal: The Taizu campaigned against the Black Cart Shiwei; Liu Rengong of Youzhou sent his adopted son Zhao Ba at the head of a force to rescue them.

entries.zh: 曷魯伏兵桃山，俟霸眾過半而要之；
entries.en: Helu lay in ambush at Mount Tao and waited until more than half of Ba's force had passed before striking;
entries.literal: Helu lay in ambush at Mount Tao and waited until more than half of Ba's force had passed before intercepting them;

entries.zh: 與太祖合擊，斬獲甚眾，遂降室韋。
entries.en: then joined Taizu in a combined attack, killed and captured a great host, and the Shiwei submitted.
entries.literal: he joined the Taizu in a combined attack, killed and captured a great host, and the Shiwei thereupon submitted.

entries.zh: 太祖會李克用於雲州，時曷魯侍，克用顧而壯之曰：「偉男子為誰？」
entries.en: Taizu met Li Keyong at Yunzhou with Helu in attendance. Keyong looked him over and said in admiration, "Who is this imposing man?"
entries.literal: The Taizu met Li Keyong at Yunzhou; Helu was in attendance, and Keyong looked at him and, impressed, said: "Who is this imposing man?"

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「吾族曷魯也。」
entries.en: Taizu said, "He is Helu of my clan."
entries.literal: The Taizu said: "He is Helu of my clan."

entries.zh: 會遙輦痕德堇可汗歿，群臣奉遺命請立太祖。
entries.en: When the Yaolian khan Hendijin died, the ministers invoked his dying command and asked that Taizu be enthroned.
entries.literal: When the Yaolian khan Hendijin died, the ministers, following his final command, asked that the Taizu be enthroned.

entries.zh: 太祖辭曰：「昔吾祖夷離堇雅裏嘗以不當立而辭，今若等復為是言，何歟？」
entries.en: Taizu declined, saying, "Long ago my ancestor the yilijin Yali refused the throne on the grounds that he ought not to rule. If you now repeat such words, what does that mean?"
entries.literal: The Taizu declined, saying: "In former times my ancestor, the yilijin Yali, once declined the throne on the grounds that he ought not to rule. If you now repeat such words, what of it?"

entries.zh: 曷魯進曰：「曩吾祖之辭，遺命弗及，符瑞未見，第為國人所推戴耳。
entries.en: Helu stepped forward and said, "When our ancestor declined, there was no dying command, no auspicious signs had appeared. The people simply pressed him forward.
entries.literal: Helu advanced and said: "When our ancestor declined in the past, no dying command had yet been given, no auspicious signs had appeared—it was only that the people of the state pressed him forward.

entries.zh: 今先君言猶在耳，天人所與，若合符契。
entries.en: Now the late ruler's words still ring in our ears. Heaven and men bestow the throne as if tally and seal matched.
entries.literal: Now the late ruler's words still ring in our ears; Heaven and men bestow the throne as if tally and seal matched.

entries.zh: 天不可逆，人不可拂，而君命不可違也。」
entries.en: Heaven cannot be turned back, men cannot be resisted, and a ruler's command cannot be disobeyed."
entries.literal: Heaven cannot be turned back, men cannot be resisted, and a ruler's command cannot be disobeyed."

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「遺命固然，汝焉知天道？」
entries.en: Taizu said, "The dying command is indeed so. But how do you know the Way of Heaven?"
entries.literal: The Taizu said: "The dying command is indeed so—but how do you know the Way of Heaven?"

entries.zh: 曷魯曰：「聞於越之生也，神光屬天，異香盈幄，夢受神誨，龍錫金佩。
entries.en: Helu said, "I have heard that at your birth divine light reached to Heaven, strange fragrance filled the tent, you received divine instruction in dreams, and a dragon bestowed a golden pendant.
entries.literal: Helu said: "I have heard that at the Yuyue's birth divine light reached to Heaven, strange fragrance filled the tent, in dreams he received divine instruction, and a dragon bestowed a golden pendant.

entries.zh: 天道無私，必應有德。
entries.en: The Way of Heaven is impartial and must respond to the virtuous.
entries.literal: The Way of Heaven is without partiality and must respond to the virtuous.

entries.zh: 我國削弱，齮龁於鄰部日久，以故生聖人以興起之。
entries.en: Our state had grown weak and for long had been gnawed at by neighboring tribes. For this reason a sage was born to raise it up.
entries.literal: Our state had grown weak and for long had been gnawed at by neighboring tribes; for this reason a sage was born to raise it up.

entries.zh: 可汗知天意，故有是命。
entries.en: The khan knew Heaven's intent and therefore gave this command.
entries.literal: The khan knew Heaven's intent, and therefore gave this command.

entries.zh: 且遙輦九營棋布，非無可立者；
entries.en: Moreover, the nine camps of Yaolian are set out like chess pieces. There are others who could be enthroned.
entries.literal: Moreover, the nine camps of Yaolian are set out like chess pieces—there are not none who could be enthroned;

entries.zh: 小大臣民屬心於越，天也。
entries.en: Yet ministers great and small and the people all set their hearts on you. That is Heaven's doing.
entries.literal: yet ministers great and small and the people all set their hearts on the Yuyue—that is Heaven's doing.

entries.zh: 昔者於越伯父釋魯嘗曰：『吾猶蛇，兒猶龍也。』
entries.en: Long ago your uncle Shilu said, 'I am still a snake; my son is already a dragon.'
entries.literal: In former days your uncle Shilu once said: 'I am still a snake; my son is already a dragon.'

entries.zh: 天時人事，幾不可失。」
entries.en: The season of Heaven and the affairs of men—such a moment can scarcely be missed."
entries.literal: The season of Heaven and the affairs of men—such a moment can scarcely be missed."

entries.zh: 太祖猶未許。
entries.en: Taizu still did not consent.
entries.literal: The Taizu still did not consent.

entries.zh: 是夜，獨召曷魯責曰：「眾以遺命迫我。
entries.en: That night he summoned Helu alone and reproached him. "The multitude forces me with the dying command.
entries.literal: That night he summoned Helu alone and reproached him: "The multitude forces me with the dying command.

entries.zh: 汝不明吾心，而亦俯隨耶？」
entries.en: You do not understand my heart, yet you too bow and follow?"
entries.literal: You do not understand my heart, yet you too bow and follow?"

entries.zh: 曷魯曰：「在昔夷離堇雅裏雖推戴者眾，辭之而立阻午為可汗。
entries.en: Helu said, "In the past, though many pressed the yilijin Yali forward, he declined and enthroned Zuowu as khan.
entries.literal: Helu said: "In the past, though many pressed the yilijin Yali forward, he declined and enthroned Zuowu as khan.

entries.zh: 相傳十餘世，君臣之分亂，紀綱之統隳。
entries.en: The succession passed through more than ten generations. The distinction between ruler and minister fell into disorder, and law and regulation collapsed.
entries.literal: The succession passed through more than ten generations; the distinction between ruler and minister fell into disorder, and the bonds of law and regulation were broken.

entries.zh: 委質他國，若綴斿然。
entries.en: They submitted to other states like a trailing pennant.
entries.literal: They submitted to other states like a trailing pennant.

entries.zh: 羽檄蜂午，民疲奔命。
entries.en: Urgent dispatches swarmed like bees at noon, and the people grew weary running to and fro on command.
entries.literal: Urgent dispatches swarmed like bees at noon, and the people grew weary running to and fro on command.

entries.zh: 興王之運，實在今日。
entries.en: The fortune of a king who would raise the state truly lies in this day.
entries.literal: The fortune of a king who would raise the state truly lies in this day.

entries.zh: 應天順人，以答顧命，不可失也。」
entries.en: To answer Heaven, follow the people, and respond to the dying charge—this must not be lost."
entries.literal: To answer Heaven and follow the people, and thereby respond to the dying charge—this must not be lost."

entries.zh: 太祖乃許。
entries.en: Taizu then consented.
entries.literal: The Taizu then consented.

entries.zh: 明日，即皇帝位，命曷魯總軍國事。
entries.en: The next day he took the imperial throne and put Helu in charge of all military and state affairs.
entries.literal: The next day he took the imperial throne and appointed Helu to oversee all military and state affairs.

entries.zh: 時制度未講，國用未充，扈從未備，而諸弟剌葛等往往覬非望。
entries.en: Institutions were not yet ordered, revenue was not yet ample, and the imperial escort was not yet complete, while his younger brothers Cige and others often cast covetous eyes on the throne.
entries.literal: At that time institutions were not yet ordered, state revenue was not yet ample, and the imperial escort was not yet complete, while the Taizu's younger brothers Cige and others often cast covetous eyes on what was not theirs to seek.

entries.zh: 太祖宮行營始置腹心部，選諸部豪健二千餘充之，以曷魯及蕭敵魯總焉。
entries.en: Taizu's palace traveling camp first established the Inner Guard Corps, selecting more than two thousand stalwarts from the tribes to fill it, with Helu and Xiao Dilu placed in overall charge.
entries.literal: The Taizu's palace traveling camp first established the Inner Guard Corps, selecting more than two thousand stalwarts from the tribes to fill it, with Helu and Xiao Dilu placed in overall charge.

entries.zh: 已而諸弟之亂作，太祖命曷魯總領軍事，討平之，以功為叠剌部夷離堇。
entries.en: Before long the rebellion of the younger brothers broke out. Taizu put Helu in overall command of the armies, pacified it, and for his merit made him yilijin of the Yila tribe.
entries.literal: Before long the rebellion of the younger brothers broke out; the Taizu ordered Helu to take overall command of the armies, pacified it, and for his merit made him yilijin of the Yila tribe.

entries.zh: 時民更兵焚剽，日以抏敝，曷魯撫輯有方，畜牧益滋，民用富庶。
entries.en: The people had suffered war, fire, and plunder in turn and daily grew exhausted. Helu pacified and gathered them with skill, livestock flourished, and the people's livelihood grew prosperous.
entries.literal: At that time the people suffered alternately war, fire, and plunder and daily grew exhausted; Helu pacified and gathered them with skill, livestock increased ever more, and the people's livelihood grew prosperous.

entries.zh: 乃討烏古部，破之。
entries.en: He then campaigned against the Uighur tribe and defeated them.
entries.literal: He then campaigned against the Uighur tribe and broke them.

entries.zh: 自是震懾，不敢復叛。
entries.en: From then on they were awed and did not dare rebel again.
entries.literal: From then on they were awed and did not dare rebel again.

entries.zh: 乃請制朝儀、建元，率百官上尊號。
entries.en: He then requested that court ritual be instituted and an era name established, and led the hundred officials in offering a honorific title.
entries.literal: He then requested that court ritual be instituted and an era name established, and led the hundred officials in offering a honorific title.

entries.zh: 太祖既備禮受冊，拜曷魯為阿魯敦於越。
entries.en: After Taizu had completed the rites and received the investiture, he appointed Helu Arudun Yuyue.
entries.literal: After the Taizu had completed the rites and received the investiture, he appointed Helu Arudun Yuyue.

entries.zh: 「阿魯敦」者，遼言盛名也。
entries.en: "Arudun" in the Liao language means great renown.
entries.literal: "Arudun" in the Liao language means great renown.

entries.zh: 後太祖伐西南諸夷，數為前鋒。
entries.en: Later, when Taizu campaigned against the tribes of the southwest, Helu often led the van.
entries.literal: Later, when the Taizu campaigned against the various tribes of the southwest, Helu often served as vanguard.

entries.zh: 神冊二年，從逼幽州，與唐節度使周德威拒戰可汗州西，敗其軍，遂圍幽州，未下。
entries.en: In the second year of Shence he joined the advance on Youzhou and, west of Kehan Prefecture, fought the Tang military governor Zhou Dewei, defeated his army, and then besieged Youzhou without taking it.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shence, he followed the advance on Youzhou and, west of Kehan Prefecture, fought the Tang military governor Zhou Dewei in a blocking engagement, defeated his army, and then besieged Youzhou without taking it.

entries.zh: 太祖以時暑班師，留曷魯與盧國用守之。
entries.en: Taizu withdrew because of the summer heat and left Helu and Lu Guoyong to hold the city.
entries.literal: The Taizu withdrew the army because of the season's heat and left Helu and Lu Guoyong to hold it.

entries.zh: 俄而救兵繼至，曷魯等以軍少無援，退。
entries.en: Before long relief forces arrived in succession. Helu and the others, their army being few and without support, withdrew.
entries.literal: Before long relief forces arrived in succession; Helu and the others, their army being few and without support, withdrew.

entries.zh: 三年七月，皇都既成，燕群臣以落之。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the third year, when the imperial capital was completed, [the emperor] banqueted the ministers to celebrate its completion.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, when the imperial capital was completed, [he] banqueted the assembled ministers to celebrate its completion.

entries.zh: 曷魯是月得疾薨，年四十七。
entries.en: That month Helu fell ill and died at the age of forty-seven.
entries.literal: That month Helu fell ill and died at age forty-seven.

entries.zh: 既葬，賜名其阡宴答，山曰於越峪，詔立石紀功。
entries.en: After burial, his burial path was named Yanda and the mountain Yuyue Valley; an edict ordered a stone erected to record his achievements.
entries.literal: After burial, his path was granted the name Yanda and the mountain was named Yuyue Valley; an edict ordered a stone erected to record his merit.

entries.zh: 清寧間，命立祠上京。
entries.en: During the Qingning era, an order was issued to establish a shrine to him at Shangjing.
entries.literal: During Qingning, he was ordered to have a shrine established at Shangjing.

entries.zh: 初，曷魯病革，太祖臨視，問所欲言。
entries.en: When Helu was critically ill, Taizu came in person to visit him and asked what he wished to say.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Helu was critically ill, the Taizu came in person to visit and asked what he wished to say.

entries.zh: 曷魯曰：「陛下聖德寬仁，群生咸遂，帝業隆興。
entries.en: Helu said, "Your Majesty's sagely virtue is broad and humane; all living things flourish, and the imperial enterprise rises in glory.
entries.literal: Helu said: "Your Majesty's sagely virtue is broad and humane; all living things flourish, and the imperial enterprise rises in glory.

entries.zh: 臣既蒙寵遇，雖瞑目無憾。
entries.en: I have received favor and regard; though I close my eyes, I have no regret.
entries.literal: Your subject has received favor and regard; though I close my eyes, I have no regret.

entries.zh: 惟析叠剌部議未決，願亟行之。」
entries.en: Only the proposal to divide the Yila tribe remains unsettled; I beg that it be carried out at once."
entries.literal: Only the proposal to divide the Yila tribe remains unsettled; I beg that it be carried out swiftly."

entries.zh: 及薨，太祖流涕曰：「斯人若登三五載，吾謀蔑不濟矣！」
entries.en: When he died, Taizu wept and said, "If this man had lived another three or five years, none of my plans would have failed!"
entries.literal: When he died, the Taizu wept and said: "If this man had lived another three or five years, none of my plans would have failed!"

entries.zh: 後太祖二十一功臣，各有所擬，以曷魯為心雲。
entries.en: Later, when Taizu matched his twenty-one meritorious ministers each to a bodily metaphor, Helu was likened to the heart.
entries.literal: Later, when the Taizu matched his twenty-one meritorious ministers each to a bodily metaphor, Helu was likened to the heart.

entries.zh: 子惕剌、撒剌，俱不仕。
entries.en: His sons Tila and Sala both declined office.
entries.literal: His sons Tila and Sala both did not take office.

entries.zh: 頗德，字兀古鄰。
entries.en: Pide, whose style was Wugulin.
entries.literal: Pide, style name Wugulin.

entries.zh: 弱冠事太祖。
entries.en: In his youth he entered Taizu's service.
entries.literal: In his youth he entered the Taizu's service.

entries.zh: 天顯初，為左皮室詳穩，典宿衛，遷南院夷離堇，治有聲。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianxian he served as Left Pishi xiangwen and directed the palace guard, then was transferred to yilijin of the Southern Yuan, where his governance won renown.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianxian he served as Left Pishi xiangwen, directing the palace guard, then was transferred to yilijin of the Southern Yuan, where his governance won renown.

entries.zh: 石敬瑭破張敬達軍於太原北，時頗德勒兵為援，敬達遁。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang defeated Zhang Jingda's army north of Taiyuan. Pide led troops in relief at the time, and Jingda fled.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang defeated Zhang Jingda's army north of Taiyuan; at the time Pide led troops in relief, and Jingda fled.

entries.zh: 敬瑭追至晉安寨圍之，頗德領輕騎襲潞州，塞其餉道。
entries.en: Jingtang pursued to Jin'an Stockade and besieged it. Pide led light cavalry to strike Luzhou and cut off their supply route.
entries.literal: Jingtang pursued to Jin'an Stockade and besieged it; Pide led light cavalry to strike Luzhou and cut off their supply route.

entries.zh: 唐諸將懼，殺敬達以降。
entries.en: The Tang generals were afraid and killed Jingda to submit.
entries.literal: The Tang generals were afraid and killed Jingda to submit.

entries.zh: 會同初，改叠剌部夷離堇為大王，即拜頗德，既而加采訪使。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huitong the office of yilijin of the Yila tribe was changed to Grand Prince, and Pide was immediately appointed. Shortly thereafter he was additionally made Investigation Commissioner.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, the office of yilijin of the Yila tribe was changed to Grand Prince, and Pide was immediately appointed; shortly thereafter he was additionally made Investigation Commissioner.

entries.zh: 舊制，肅祖以下宗室稱院，德祖宗室號三父房，稱橫帳，百官子弟及籍沒人稱著帳。
entries.en: Under the old system, imperial clansmen from Suzu downward were called yuan. Dezong's imperial clan was styled the Three Fathers' Houses and called the Horizontal Account. Sons of the hundred officials and persons on the confiscated registers were called the Attached Account.
entries.literal: Under the old system, imperial clansmen from Suzu downward were called yuan; Dezong's imperial clan was styled the Three Fathers' Houses and called the Horizontal Account; sons of the hundred officials and persons on the confiscated registers were called the Attached Account.

entries.zh: 耶律斜的言，橫帳班列，不可與北、南院並。
entries.en: Yelu Xiedi said that the Horizontal Account's place in court ranks could not be placed alongside the Northern and Southern Yuan.
entries.literal: Yelu Xiedi said that the Horizontal Account's place in court ranks could not be placed alongside the Northern and Southern Yuan.

entries.zh: 太宗詔在廷議，皆曰然，乃詔橫帳班列居上。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong ordered discussion in court. All agreed, and an edict placed the Horizontal Account's rank above.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizong ordered discussion in court; all said it was so, and an edict placed the Horizontal Account's rank above.

entries.zh: 頗德奏曰：「臣伏見官制，北、南院大王品在惕隱上。
entries.en: Pide memorialized, "Your subject has observed the official system: the rank of the Northern and Southern Yuan grand princes is above that of the tiyin.
entries.literal: Pide memorialized: "Your subject has observed the official system: the rank of the Northern and Southern Yuan grand princes is above that of the tiyin.

entries.zh: 今橫帳始圖爵位之高，願與北、南院參任；
entries.en: Now the Horizontal Account is just beginning to seek high noble rank and wishes to share appointments with the Northern and Southern Yuan;
entries.literal: Now the Horizontal Account is just beginning to seek high noble rank and wishes to share appointments with the Northern and Southern Yuan;

entries.zh: 茲又恥與同列。
entries.en: yet they are ashamed to stand in the same row.
entries.literal: yet they are ashamed to stand in the same row.

entries.zh: 夫橫帳與諸族皆臣也，班列奚以異？」
entries.en: The Horizontal Account and the various tribes are all subjects. Why should court ranks differ?"
entries.literal: The Horizontal Account and the various tribes are all subjects—why should court ranks differ?"

entries.zh: 帝乃諭百官曰：「朕所不知，卿等不宜面從。」
entries.en: The emperor then instructed the hundred officials, "What I do not understand, you should not simply agree to my face."
entries.literal: The emperor then instructed the hundred officials: "What I do not understand, you should not simply agree to my face."

entries.zh: 詔仍舊制。
entries.en: An edict restored the old system.
entries.literal: An edict restored the old system.

entries.zh: 其強直不撓如此。
entries.en: His firm uprightness and refusal to yield were like this.
entries.literal: His firm uprightness and refusal to yield were like this.

entries.zh: 頗德狀貌秀偉，初，太祖見之曰：「是子風骨異常兒，必為國器。」
entries.en: Pide was handsome and imposing in appearance. Early on Taizu saw him and said, "This boy's bearing is unlike ordinary children. He will surely be an instrument of state."
entries.literal: Pide's appearance was handsome and imposing; early on the Taizu saw him and said: "This boy's bearing is unlike ordinary children; he will surely be an instrument of state."

entries.zh: 後果然。
entries.en: Later it proved so.
entries.literal: Later it proved so.

entries.zh: 卒年四十九。
entries.en: He died at the age of forty-nine.
entries.literal: He died at age forty-nine.

entries.zh: 論曰：曷魯以肺腑之親，任帷幄之寄，言如蓍龜，謀成戰勝，可謂算無遺策矣。
entries.en: The commentary says: Helu, by virtue of kinship at the ruler's very core, bore the trust of the command tent. His words were like divination with yarrow and tortoise, his plans achieved victory in battle. One may say his calculations left no strategy unspent.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Helu, by virtue of kinship at the ruler's very core, bore the trust of the command tent; his words were like divination with yarrow and tortoise, his plans achieved victory in battle—one may say his calculations left no strategy unspent.

entries.zh: 其君臣相得之誠，庶吳漢之於光武歟？
entries.en: The sincerity with which ruler and minister found one another perhaps resembles Wu Han toward Emperor Guangwu?
entries.literal: The sincerity with which ruler and minister found one another perhaps resembles Wu Han toward Emperor Guangwu?

entries.zh: 夫信其所可信，智也，太祖有焉。
entries.en: To trust what is truly trustworthy is wisdom, and Taizu possessed it.
entries.literal: To trust what is truly trustworthy is wisdom, and the Taizu possessed it.

entries.zh: 故曰：惟聖知聖，惟賢知賢，斯近之矣。
entries.en: Hence it is said: only the sage knows the sage, only the worthy knows the worthy. This comes close to the mark.
entries.literal: Hence it is said: only the sage knows the sage, only the worthy knows the worthy—this comes close to the mark.

entries.zh: 蕭敵魯，字敵輦，其母為德祖女弟，而淳欽皇后又其女兄也。
entries.en: Xiao Dilu, whose style was Dilian, was born to Dezong's younger sister; Empress Chunqin was also his elder sister.
entries.literal: Xiao Dilu, style name Dilian, was born to Dezong's younger sister by a different mother, while Empress Chunqin was also his elder sister by a different mother.

entries.zh: 五世祖曰胡母裏，遙輦氏時嘗使唐，唐留之幽州。
entries.en: His fifth-generation ancestor Humuli was once sent as envoy to Tang in the Yaolian era; Tang detained him at Youzhou.
entries.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was Humuli; in the Yaolian era he was once sent as envoy to Tang, and Tang detained him at Youzhou.

entries.zh: 一夕，折關遁歸國，由是世為決獄官。
entries.en: One night he broke through the pass and fled home; thereafter the family for generations served as judicial adjudicators.
entries.literal: One night he broke through the pass and fled home; from this the family for generations served as judicial adjudicators.

entries.zh: 敵魯性寬厚，膂力絕人，習軍旅事。
entries.en: Dilu was generous and steadfast by nature, possessed extraordinary strength, and was versed in military affairs.
entries.literal: Dilu was generous and steadfast by nature, with strength surpassing other men, and versed in military affairs.

entries.zh: 太祖潛藩，日侍左右，凡征討必與行陣。
entries.en: While Taizu was still in his princely household, Dilu attended him daily; on every campaign he marched in the ranks.
entries.literal: While the Taizu was still in his princely household, Dilu attended him daily; on every campaign he marched in the ranks.

entries.zh: 既即位，敵魯與弟阿古只、耶律釋魯、耶律曷魯偕總宿衛。
entries.en: After the enthronement, Dilu together with his younger brother Aguzhi, Yelu Shilu, and Yelu Helu jointly directed the palace guard.
entries.literal: After the enthronement, Dilu together with his younger brother Aguzhi, Yelu Shilu, and Yelu Helu jointly directed the palace guard.

entries.zh: 拜敵魯北府宰相，世其官。
entries.en: Dilu was appointed Northern Chancellery chancellor, and the office became hereditary in his family.
entries.literal: Dilu was appointed Northern Chancellery Chancellor, and the office became hereditary in his family.

entries.zh: 太祖征奚及討劉守光，敵魯略地海濱，殺獲甚眾。
entries.en: When Taizu campaigned against the Xi and attacked Liu Shouguang, Dilu overran the seacoast lands and killed and captured a great host.
entries.literal: When the Taizu campaigned against the Xi and attacked Liu Shouguang, Dilu overran the seacoast lands and killed and captured a great host.

entries.zh: 頃之，剌葛等作亂，潰而北走。
entries.en: Before long Cige and others rebelled, were routed, and fled north.
entries.literal: Before long Cige and others rebelled, broke, and fled north.

entries.zh: 敵魯率輕騎追之，兼晝夜行。
entries.en: Dilu led light cavalry in pursuit, traveling day and night.
entries.literal: Dilu led light cavalry in pursuit, traveling day and night.

entries.zh: 至榆河，敗其黨，獲剌葛以獻。
entries.en: At the Yu River he defeated their faction and captured Cige to present him.
entries.literal: At the Yu River he defeated their faction and captured Cige to present him.

entries.zh: 太祖嘉之，錫賚甚渥。
entries.en: Taizu praised him and bestowed rewards in great abundance.
entries.literal: The Taizu praised him and bestowed rewards in great abundance.

entries.zh: 後討西南夷，功居諸將先。
entries.en: Later, in campaigns against the southwestern tribes, his merit ranked ahead of the other generals.
entries.literal: Later, in campaigns against the southwestern tribes, his merit ranked ahead of the other generals.

entries.zh: 神冊三年十二月卒。
entries.en: He died in the twelfth month of Shence 3.
entries.literal: He died in the twelfth month of the third year of Shence.

entries.zh: 敵魯有膽略，聞敵所在即馳赴，親冒矢石，前後戰未嘗少恤，必勝乃止。
entries.en: Dilu possessed daring and strategy; hearing where the enemy was, he galloped to the spot, personally braved arrows and stones, and in battle after battle never held back until victory was won.
entries.literal: Dilu possessed daring and strategy; hearing where the enemy was, he galloped to the spot, personally braved arrows and stones, and in battle after battle never held back until victory was won.

entries.zh: 以故在太祖功臣列，喻以手雲。
entries.en: For this reason, among Taizu's meritorious ministers he was likened to the hand.
entries.literal: For this reason, among the Taizu's meritorious ministers he was likened to the hand.

entries.zh: 弟阿古只。
entries.en: His younger brother was Aguzhi.
entries.literal: Younger brother Aguzhi.

entries.zh: 阿古只，字撒本。
entries.en: Aguzhi, whose style was Saben.
entries.literal: Aguzhi, style name Saben.

entries.zh: 少卓越自放不羈。
entries.en: In youth he was outstanding, self-reliant, and unrestrained.
entries.literal: In youth he was outstanding, self-reliant, and unrestrained.

entries.zh: 長驍勇善射，臨敵敢前。
entries.en: Grown up, he was fierce, brave, and skilled in archery, daring to advance before the enemy.
entries.literal: Grown up, he was fierce and brave and skilled in archery, daring to advance before the enemy.

entries.zh: 每射甲楯輒洞貫。
entries.en: Whenever he shot at armor or shields, his arrows pierced clean through.
entries.literal: Whenever he shot at armor or shields, his arrows pierced clean through.

entries.zh: 太祖為於越時，以材勇充任使。
entries.en: When Taizu was Yuyue, Aguzhi was employed for missions on account of his talent and courage.
entries.literal: When the Taizu was Yuyue, Aguzhi was employed for missions on account of his talent and courage.

entries.zh: 既即位，與敵魯總腹心部。
entries.en: After the enthronement, he and Dilu jointly directed the Inner Guard Corps.
entries.literal: After the enthronement, he and Dilu jointly directed the Inner Guard Corps.

entries.zh: 剌葛之亂也，淳欽皇后軍黑山，阻險自固。
entries.en: During Cige's rebellion, Empress Chunqin encamped at Black Mountain and held the defensible ground to secure herself.
entries.literal: During Cige's rebellion, Empress Chunqin encamped at Black Mountain and held the defensible ground to secure herself.

entries.zh: 太祖方經略奚地，命阿古只統百騎往衛之。
entries.en: Taizu was then securing Xi territory and ordered Aguzhi to lead a hundred horsemen to guard her.
entries.literal: The Taizu was then securing Xi territory and ordered Aguzhi to lead a hundred horsemen to guard her.

entries.zh: 逆黨叠裏特、耶律滑哥素憚其勇略，相戒曰：「是不可犯也！」
entries.en: The rebels Dielite and Yelu Huage had long feared his courage and strategy and warned one another, "He must not be provoked!"
entries.literal: The rebels Dielite and Yelu Huage had long feared his courage and strategy and warned one another, saying: "He must not be provoked!"

entries.zh: 剌葛既北走，與敵魯追擒於榆河。
entries.en: After Cige fled north, Aguzhi and Dilu pursued and captured him at the Yu River.
entries.literal: After Cige fled north, Aguzhi and Dilu pursued and captured him at the Yu River.

entries.zh: 神冊初元，討西南夷有功；
entries.en: In the first year of Shence he won merit campaigning against the southwestern tribes;
entries.literal: In the first year of Shence he won merit campaigning against the southwestern tribes;

entries.zh: 徇山西諸郡縣，又下之，敗周德威軍。
entries.en: he overran the commanderies and counties of western Shanxi, took them, and defeated the army of Zhou Dewei.
entries.literal: he overran the commanderies and counties of western Shanxi, took them, and defeated the army of Zhou Dewei.

entries.zh: 三年，以功拜北府宰相，世其職。
entries.en: In the third year, for his merit he was appointed Northern Chancellery chancellor, and the office became hereditary.
entries.literal: In the third year, for his merit he was appointed Northern Chancellery Chancellor, and the office became hereditary.

entries.zh: 天贊初，與王郁略地燕、趙，破磁窯鎮。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianzan, he and Wang Yu overran the lands of Yan and Zhao and took Ciyao town.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianzan, he and Wang Yu overran the lands of Yan and Zhao and took Ciyao town.

entries.zh: 太祖西征，悉諉以南面邊事。
entries.en: When Taizu campaigned west, he entrusted all southern frontier affairs to Aguzhi.
entries.literal: When the Taizu campaigned west, he entrusted all southern frontier affairs to Aguzhi.

entries.zh: 耶律斜涅赤，字撒剌，六院部舍利古直之族。
entries.en: Yelu Xieniechi, whose style was Sala, came from the clan of Sheluguzhi in the Six Yuan tribes.
entries.literal: Yelu Xieniechi, style name Sala, was of the clan of Sheluguzhi in the Six Yuan tribes.

entries.zh: 始字鐸碗，早隸太祖幕下，嘗有疾，賜樽酒飲而愈，遼言酒樽曰「撒剌」，故詔易字焉。
entries.en: His original style was Duowan. Early on he entered Taizu's service. Once when he fell ill, he was granted a jar of wine to drink and recovered. In the Liao language a wine jar is called "sala," and therefore an edict changed his style name.
entries.literal: His original style was Duowan. Early on he entered the Taizu's service; once when he fell ill, he was granted a jar of wine to drink and recovered. In the Liao language a wine jar is called "sala," and therefore an edict changed his style name.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，掌腹心部。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne, Xieniechi directed the Inner Guard Corps.
entries.literal: When the Taizu took the throne, Xieniechi directed the Inner Guard Corps.

entries.zh: 天贊初，分叠剌部為北、南院，斜涅赤為北院夷離堇。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianzan, the Yila tribe was divided into Northern and Southern Yuan, and Xieniechi became yilijin of the Northern Yuan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianzan, the Yila tribe was divided into Northern and Southern Yuan; Xieniechi became yilijin of the Northern Yuan.

entries.zh: 帝西徵至流沙，威聲大振，諸夷潰散，乃命斜涅赤撫集之。
entries.en: The emperor campaigned west as far as the drifting sands. His martial renown shook all sides and the various tribes scattered in rout, whereupon he ordered Xieniechi to pacify and gather them.
entries.literal: The emperor campaigned west as far as the drifting sands; his martial renown shook all sides and the various tribes scattered in rout, whereupon he ordered Xieniechi to pacify and gather them.

entries.zh: 及討渤海，破扶餘城，斜涅赤從太子大元帥率眾夜圍忽汗城，大諲譔降。
entries.en: When Bohai was attacked and Fuyu city taken, Xieniechi followed the crown prince, grand marshal, in leading the host to besiege Hohan city by night, and Dayinzan submitted.
entries.literal: When Bohai was attacked and Fuyu city taken, Xieniechi followed the crown prince, grand marshal, in leading the host to besiege Hohan city by night; Dayinzan submitted.

entries.zh: 已而復叛，命諸將分地攻之。
entries.en: Before long they rebelled again, and the emperor ordered the generals to attack them each in his assigned territory.
entries.literal: Before long they rebelled again, and the emperor ordered the generals to attack them each in his assigned territory.

entries.zh: 詰旦，斜涅赤感勵士伍，鼓噪登陴，敵震懾，莫敢禦，遂破之。
entries.en: At dawn the next day, Xieniechi roused and encouraged the soldiers, beating drums and shouting as they scaled the battlements. The enemy was awed and dared not resist, and the city fell.
entries.literal: At dawn the next day, Xieniechi stirred and encouraged the soldiers, beating drums and shouting as they scaled the battlements; the enemy was awed and dared not resist, and the city was thereupon taken.

entries.zh: 天顯中卒，年七十，居佐命功臣之一。
entries.en: He died in the Tianxian era at the age of seventy and ranked among the founding ministers who aided the throne.
entries.literal: He died in the Tianxian era at age seventy and ranked among the founding ministers who aided the throne.

entries.zh: 侄老古、頗德。
entries.en: His nephews were Laogu and Pide.
entries.literal: Nephews Laogu and Pide.

entries.zh: 老古，字撒懶，其母淳欽皇后姊也。
entries.en: Laogu, whose style was Salan, was born to Empress Chunqin's elder sister.
entries.literal: Laogu, style name Salan, was born to Empress Chunqin's elder sister.

entries.zh: 老古幼養宮掖，既長，沈毅有勇略，隸太祖帳下。
entries.en: Laogu was reared in the palace from childhood; grown up, he was grave, resolute, and possessed courage and strategy, and entered service under Taizu's command.
entries.literal: Laogu was reared in the palace from childhood; grown up, he was grave, resolute, and possessed courage and strategy, and entered service under the Taizu's command.

entries.zh: 既即位，屢有戰功。
entries.en: After the enthronement he repeatedly won merit in battle.
entries.literal: After the enthronement he repeatedly won merit in battle.

entries.zh: 剌葛之亂也，欲乘我不備為掩襲計，紿降。
entries.en: During Cige's rebellion, the rebels planned a surprise attack while our guard was down and feigned surrender.
entries.literal: During Cige's rebellion, the rebels planned a surprise attack while our guard was down and feigned surrender.

entries.zh: 太祖將納之，命老古、耶律欲穩嚴號令，勒士卒，控轡以防其變。
entries.en: Taizu was about to accept their submission and ordered Laogu and Yelu Yuwen to enforce strict commands, marshal the soldiers, and hold the reins to guard against treachery.
entries.literal: The Taizu was about to accept their submission and ordered Laogu and Yelu Yuwen to enforce strict commands, marshal the soldiers, and hold the reins to guard against treachery.

entries.zh: 逆黨知有備，懼而遁。
entries.en: The rebels, knowing preparations had been made, were afraid and fled.
entries.literal: The rebels, knowing preparations had been made, were afraid and fled.

entries.zh: 以功授右皮室詳穩，典宿衛。
entries.en: For his merit he was appointed Right Pishi xiangwen and directed the palace guard.
entries.literal: For his merit he was appointed Right Pishi xiangwen and directed the palace guard.

entries.zh: 太祖侵燕、趙，遇唐兵雲碧店，老古恃勇輕敵，直犯其鋒。
entries.en: When Taizu invaded Yan and Zhao and met Tang troops at Yunbi, Laogu relied on his courage, underrated the enemy, and charged straight at their front.
entries.literal: When the Taizu invaded Yan and Zhao and met Tang troops at Yunbi Inn, Laogu relied on his courage, underrated the enemy, and charged straight at their front.

entries.zh: 戰久之，被數創，歸營而卒。
entries.en: After fighting long, he suffered many wounds, returned to camp, and died.
entries.literal: After fighting long, he suffered many wounds, returned to camp, and died.

entries.zh: 太祖深悼惜之，佐命功臣其一也。
entries.en: Taizu deeply mourned and regretted his loss; he ranked among the founding ministers who aided the throne.
entries.literal: The Taizu deeply mourned and regretted his loss; he ranked among the founding ministers who aided the throne.

entries.zh: 耶律欲穩，字轄剌幹，突呂不部人。
entries.en: Yelu Yuwen, whose style was Xialagan, came from the Tulubu tribe.
entries.literal: Yelu Yuwen, style name Xialagan, was a man of the Tulubu tribe.

entries.zh: 祖臺押，遙輦時為北邊拽剌。
entries.en: His grandfather Taiya had served on the northern frontier as zhuaila in the Yaolian era.
entries.literal: His grandfather Taiya, in the Yaolian period, served as northern frontier zhuaila.

entries.zh: 簡獻皇后與諸子之罹難也，嘗倚之以免。
entries.en: When Empress Jianxian and her sons suffered calamity, they once relied on him to escape harm.
entries.literal: When Empress Jianxian and her sons suffered calamity, they once relied on him to escape harm.

entries.zh: 太祖思其功不忘，又多欲穩嚴重有濟世誌，乃命典司近部，以遏諸族窺覬之想。
entries.en: Taizu, mindful of his merit and never forgetting it, and also because Yuwen was solemn and possessed the ambition to aid the age, ordered him to supervise the nearby tribes to curb the covetous designs of the various clans.
entries.literal: The Taizu, mindful of his merit and never forgetting it, and also because Yuwen was solemn and possessed the ambition to aid the age, ordered him to supervise the nearby tribes to curb the covetous designs of the various clans.

entries.zh: 欲穩既見器重，益感奮思報。
entries.en: Once Yuwen was shown such favor, he was all the more stirred to repay with service.
entries.literal: Once Yuwen was shown such favor, he was all the more stirred to repay with service.

entries.zh: 太祖始置宮分以自衛，欲穩率門客首附宮籍。
entries.en: When Taizu first established the palace partition for his own protection, Yuwen led his retainers to be the first enrolled on the palace register.
entries.literal: When the Taizu first established the palace partition for his own protection, Yuwen led his retainers to be the first enrolled on the palace register.

entries.zh: 帝益嘉其忠，詔以臺押配享廟廷。
entries.en: The emperor further praised his loyalty and ordered Taiya to share sacrifice in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: The emperor further praised his loyalty and ordered Taiya to share sacrifice in the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 及平剌葛等亂，以功遷奚叠剌部夷離堇。
entries.en: When the rebellion of Cige and others was pacified, for his merit he was transferred to yilijin of the Xi-Yila tribe.
entries.literal: When the rebellion of Cige and others was pacified, for his merit he was transferred to yilijin of the Xi-Yila tribe.

entries.zh: 從征渤海有功。
entries.en: He followed the campaign against Bohai and won merit.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Bohai and won merit.

entries.zh: 天顯初卒。
entries.en: He died at the beginning of Tianxian.
entries.literal: He died at the beginning of Tianxian.

entries.zh: 後諸帝以太祖之與欲穩也為故，往往取其子孫為友。
entries.en: Later emperors, because of Taizu's bond with Yuwen, often took his descendants as friends.
entries.literal: Later emperors, because of the Taizu's bond with Yuwen, often took his descendants as friends.

entries.zh: 宮分中稱「八房」，皆其後也。
entries.en: Among the palace partition they were called the "Eight Houses," all his descendants.
entries.literal: Among the palace partition they were called the "Eight Houses," all his descendants.

entries.zh: 弟霞裏，終奚六部禿裏。
entries.en: His younger brother Xiali ultimately became chief of the Xi Liu tribes.
entries.literal: His younger brother Xiali ultimately became chief of the Xi Liu tribes.

entries.zh: 耶律海裏，字涅剌昆，遙輦昭古可汗之裔。
entries.en: Yelu Haili, whose style was Nielikun, was a descendant of the Yaolian khan Zhaogu.
entries.literal: Yelu Haili, style name Nielikun, was a descendant of the Yaolian khan Zhaogu.

entries.zh: 太祖傳位，海裏與有力焉。
entries.en: When the throne was transferred to Taizu, Haili contributed force to it.
entries.literal: When the Taizu transferred the throne, Haili contributed force to it.

entries.zh: 初受命，屬籍比局萌覬覦，而遙輦故族尤觖望。
entries.en: At the first receiving of the mandate, clansmen in the registrar's bureau nursed covetous thoughts, and the old families of Yaolian were especially resentful.
entries.literal: At the first receiving of the mandate, clansmen in the registrar's bureau nursed covetous thoughts, and the old families of Yaolian were especially resentful.

entries.zh: 海裏多先帝知人之明，而素服太祖威德，獨歸心焉。
entries.en: Haili knew well the late emperor's gift for discerning men, yet had long submitted to Taizu's martial virtue and alone set his heart on him.
entries.literal: Haili knew well the late emperor's gift for discerning men, yet had long submitted to the Taizu's martial virtue and alone set his heart on him.

entries.zh: 以故太祖托為耳目，數從征討。
entries.en: For this reason Taizu entrusted him as eyes and ears and often took him on campaigns.
entries.literal: For this reason the Taizu entrusted him as eyes and ears and often took him on campaigns.

entries.zh: 既清內亂，始置遙輦敞穩，命海裏領之。
entries.en: Once internal rebellion was cleared, the Yaolian Changwen guard was first established and Haili was ordered to lead it.
entries.literal: Once internal rebellion was cleared, the Yaolian Changwen guard was first established and Haili was ordered to lead it.

entries.zh: 天顯初，征渤海，海裏將遙輦糺破忽汗城。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianxian, in the campaign against Bohai, Haili led the Yaolian jiu and stormed Hohan city.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianxian, in the campaign against Bohai, Haili led the Yaolian jiu and stormed Hohan city.

entries.zh: 師般，卒。
entries.en: On the army's return he died.
entries.literal: On the army's return he died.

entries.zh: 耶律曷魯 蕭敵魯 耶律斜涅赤 耶律欲穩 耶律海里
entries.en: Yelu Helu, Xiao Dilu, Yelu Xieniechi, Yelu Yuwen, and Yelu Haili
entries.literal: Yelu Helu, Xiao Dilu, Yelu Xieniechi, Yelu Yuwen, Yelu Haili

entries.zh: 耶律敵剌，字合魯隱，遙輦鮮質可汗之子。
entries.en: Yelu Dila, whose courtesy name was Heluyin, was a son of the Xianzhi Khan of the Yaolian clan.
entries.literal: Yelu Dila, courtesy name Heluyin, was a son of the Jianzhi Khan of the Yaolian clan.

entries.zh: 太祖踐阼，與敞穩海裏同心輔政。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, he and Changwen Haili worked together in loyal support of the government.
entries.literal: When the Taizu Emperor ascended the throne, he and Changwen Haili assisted in government with one mind.

entries.zh: 太祖知其忠實，命掌禮儀，且諉以軍事。
entries.en: Emperor Taizu recognized his loyalty and integrity, put him in charge of ceremonial matters, and also delegated military affairs to him.
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor knew his loyalty and honesty, appointed him to oversee rites and ceremonies, and also entrusted him with military affairs.

entries.zh: 後以平內亂功，代轄裏為奚六部吐裏，卒。
entries.en: Later, for his success in quelling internal strife, he succeeded Zaruli as tuli of the Six Xi Tribes and died in office.
entries.literal: Later, for his merit in pacifying internal disorder, he replaced Zaruli as tuli of the Six Xi Tribes, and died.

entries.zh: 敵剌善騎射，頗好禮文。
entries.en: Dila was skilled in horsemanship and archery and had a marked taste for ritual and literary learning.
entries.literal: Dila excelled at mounted archery and was quite fond of ritual and literary culture.

entries.zh: 蕭痕篤，字兀裏軫，叠剌部人。
entries.en: Xiao Hendu, whose courtesy name was Wulizhen, came from the Diela tribe.
entries.literal: Xiao Hendu, courtesy name Wulizhen, was a man of the Diela tribe.

entries.zh: 其先相遙輦氏。
entries.en: His forebears had long been chancellors to the Yaolian.
entries.literal: His ancestors had served as chancellors to the Yaolian clan.

entries.zh: 痕篤少慷慨，以才能自任。
entries.en: From youth Hendu was open-handed and spirited, trusting fully in his own abilities.
entries.literal: Hendu was generous and bold in youth and took confidence in his own talent.

entries.zh: 早隸太祖帳下，數從征討。
entries.en: He entered the Taizu Emperor's service early and took part in many expeditions.
entries.literal: Early on he served under the Taizu Emperor's banner and repeatedly followed him on campaigns.

entries.zh: 既踐阼，除北府宰相。
entries.en: After the enthronement he was made chancellor of the Northern Administration.
entries.literal: Once the throne had been taken, he was appointed Northern Chancellor.

entries.zh: 痕篤事親孝，為政尚寬簡。
entries.en: Hendu was dutiful to his parents, and his rule favored clemency and restraint.
entries.literal: Hendu was filial toward his parents, and in government he favored leniency and simplicity.

entries.zh: 初，延徽南奔，太祖夢白鶴自帳中出；
entries.en: When Yanhui first fled south, Emperor Taizu dreamed that a white crane flew out of his tent;
entries.literal: Earlier, when Yanhui fled south, the Taizu Emperor dreamed a white crane flew out from the tent;

entries.zh: 比還，復入帳中。
entries.en: when it came back it flew in again.
entries.literal: when it returned, it re-entered the tent.

entries.zh: 詰旦，謂侍臣曰：「延徽至矣。」
entries.en: At dawn he told his attendants: "Yanhui is here."
entries.literal: At daybreak he told the attending ministers: "Yanhui has arrived."

entries.zh: 已而果然。
entries.en: And so it proved.
entries.literal: And indeed it was so.

entries.zh: 太祖初元，庶事草創，凡營都邑，建宮殿，正君臣定，名分，法度井井，延徽力也。
entries.en: In the dynasty's founding days, when institutions were still being shaped—from planning capitals and palaces to setting proper relations between ruler and ministers and establishing ranks and laws—Yanhui's hand was everywhere.
entries.literal: In the founding years of Taizu, when all affairs were in raw beginning, in establishing capital cities, building palaces, rectifying ruler and ministers and fixing names and ranks, with rites and laws in good order—all was Yanhui's effort.

entries.zh: 為佐命功臣之一。
entries.en: He ranked among the founding merit ministers.
entries.literal: He was one of the founding merit ministers.

entries.zh: 子德樞。
entries.en: His son was Deshu.
entries.literal: His son Deshu.

entries.zh: 天贊四年，從征渤海，大諲譔乞降。
entries.en: In Tianzan year 4, on the expedition against Bohai, Dayinzan offered surrender.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianzan, on the campaign against Bohai, Dayinzan begged to surrender.

entries.zh: 既而復叛，與諸將破其城，以功拜左僕射。
entries.en: He soon rebelled again; Yanhui joined the other generals in storming his city and was rewarded with the post of Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he rebelled again; with the generals Yanhui stormed his city, and for his merit was appointed Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 又與康默記攻長嶺府，拔之。
entries.en: He then joined Kang Moji in taking Changling Prefecture.
entries.literal: Again with Kang Moji he attacked Changling Prefecture and took it.

entries.zh: 師還，太祖崩，哀動左右。
entries.en: On the army's return Emperor Taizu had died; Yanhui grieved so deeply that all around him were moved.
entries.literal: When the army returned, the Taizu Emperor died; grief moved those at his side.

entries.zh: 太宗朝，封魯國公，仍為政事令。
entries.en: Under Emperor Taizong he was enfeoffed Duke of Lu and kept his post as governance director.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Taizong he was enfeoffed Duke of Lu and remained governance director.

entries.zh: 使晉還，改南京三司使。
entries.en: After an embassy to Jin he was made Nanjing commissioner of the three revenue bureaus.
entries.literal: Returning from a mission to Jin, he was transferred to commissioner of the three bureaus at Nanjing.

entries.zh: 世宗朝，遷南府宰相，建政事省，設張理具，稱盡力吏。
entries.en: Under Emperor Shizong he rose to Southern chancellor, founded the Governance Office with its document systems, and was praised as an official who spared no effort.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Shizong he was promoted to chancellor of the Southern Administration, established the Governance Office, set up filing racks, and was called an official who gave his utmost.

entries.zh: 天祿五年六月，河東使請行冊禮，帝詔延徽定其制，延徽奏一遵太宗冊晉帝禮，從之。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Tianlu year 5 an envoy from Hedong asked that investiture rites be performed; the emperor charged Yanhui to set the protocol, and Yanhui proposed following exactly Emperor Taizong's ceremony for investing the Jin emperor—the court agreed.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Tianlu, the envoy from Hedong requested that investiture rites be performed; the emperor ordered Yanhui to fix the protocol, and Yanhui memorialized that all should follow the Taizong Emperor's rites for investing the Jin emperor, and this was approved.

entries.zh: 應歷中，致仕。
entries.en: During the Yingli era he retired from office.
entries.literal: During Yingli he retired.

entries.zh: 子德樞鎮東平，詔許每歲東歸省。
entries.en: His son Deshu was posted at Dongping; the court allowed him an annual visit home.
entries.literal: His son Deshu garrisoned Dongping; an edict permitted him to return east each year for family visits.

entries.zh: 九年卒，年七十八。
entries.en: He died in year 9, at seventy-eight.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged seventy-eight.

entries.zh: 上聞震悼，贈尚書令，葬幽州之魯郭，世為崇文令公。
entries.en: The emperor was stricken with grief and posthumously made him Director of the Department of State Affairs; he was buried at Luguo in Youzhou, and his family was known for generations as the Chongwen Dukes.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard, he was shaken with grief; he was posthumously granted Director of the Department of State Affairs, buried at Luguo in Youzhou, and his house was known for generations as the Chongwen Duke line.

entries.zh: 康默記，本名照。
entries.en: Kang Moji, whose original name was Zhao.
entries.literal: Kang Moji's original name was Zhao.

entries.zh: 少為薊州衙校，太祖侵薊州得之，愛其材，隸麾下。
entries.en: As a youth he served as a guard officer in Jizhou. When Emperor Taizu took Jizhou and captured him, he valued his ability and took him into his retinue.
entries.literal: In youth he was a guard officer of Jizhou; when the Taizu Emperor invaded Jizhou and obtained him, he admired his talent and enrolled him under his banner.

entries.zh: 一切蕃、漢相涉事，屬默記折衷之，悉合上意。
entries.en: Every affair that touched both Khitan and Han he entrusted to Moji to settle; each decision matched the emperor's wishes.
entries.literal: All matters involving Khitan and Han interrelation were assigned to Mojie to adjudicate, and all accorded with the emperor's intent.

entries.zh: 時諸部新附，文法未備，默記推析律意，論決重輕，不差毫厘。
entries.en: The tribes had only just submitted and the legal code was still incomplete; Mojie parsed the spirit of the statutes and weighed penalties and pardons with flawless precision.
entries.literal: At the time the tribes had newly submitted and statutes were not yet complete; Mojie analyzed the intent of the laws and decided the weight of guilt and leniency, without error by a hair's breadth.

entries.zh: 罹禁網者，人人自以為不冤。
entries.en: Those brought before the law all believed themselves treated fairly.
entries.literal: Those caught in the penal net each considered themselves not wronged.

entries.zh: 頃之，拜左尚書。
entries.en: Before long he was made Left Minister.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Left Minister.

entries.zh: 神冊三年，始建都，默記董役，人咸勸趨，百日而訖事。
entries.en: In Shence year 3, as the capital was first being built, Mojie oversaw construction; workers were driven hard, and the project was finished in a hundred days.
entries.literal: In the third year of Shence, when the capital was first established, Mojie supervised the labor; all were urged to press on, and the work was completed in a hundred days.

entries.zh: 五年，為皇都夷離畢。
entries.en: In year 5 he was made yilü-bi of the imperial capital.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he became yilü-bi of the imperial capital.

entries.zh: 會太祖出師居庸關，命默記將漢軍進逼長蘆水寨，俘馘甚眾。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu took the field through Juyong Pass, he sent Mojie with the Han army against Changlu Water Fortress, taking a great number of prisoners and heads.
entries.literal: When the Taizu Emperor marched out through Juyong Pass, he ordered Mojie to lead the Han army to press against Changlu Water Fortress; captive heads were very many.

entries.zh: 天贊四年，親征渤海，默記與韓知古從。
entries.en: In Tianzan year 4 he accompanied the emperor's expedition against Bohai, alongside Han Zhigu.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianzan, on the personal campaign against Bohai, Mojie followed with Han Zhigu.

entries.zh: 後大諲譔叛，命諸將攻之。
entries.en: Later Dayinzan rose in rebellion, and the emperor ordered his commanders against him.
entries.literal: Later Dayinzan rebelled, and the emperor ordered the generals to attack him.

entries.zh: 默記分薄東門，率驍勇先登。
entries.en: Mojie pressed the east gate and led elite troops in the assault.
entries.literal: Mojie assigned forces to press the east gate and led crack troops in the first ascent.

entries.zh: 既拔，與韓延徽下長嶺府。
entries.en: After the city fell he joined Han Yanhui in taking Changling Prefecture.
entries.literal: Once it was taken, with Han Yanhui he descended on Changling Prefecture.

entries.zh: 軍還，已下城邑多叛，默記與阿古只平之。
entries.en: On the march home many captured towns rebelled; Mojie and Aguozi put them down.
entries.literal: When the army returned, many of the cities already taken rebelled; Mojie with Aguozi quelled them.

entries.zh: 既破回跋城，歸營太祖山陵畢，卒。
entries.en: After storming Huiba City he returned to camp, finished work on Emperor Taizu's tomb, and died.
entries.literal: After breaking Huiba City, he returned to camp, completed the Taizu Emperor's tomb, and died.

entries.zh: 佐命功臣其一也。
entries.en: He was numbered among the founding merit ministers.
entries.literal: He was one of the merit ministers who assisted in founding the dynasty.

entries.zh: 韓延徽，字藏明，幽州安次人。
entries.en: Han Yanhui, whose courtesy name was Cangming, came from Anci in Youzhou.
entries.literal: Han Yanhui, courtesy name Cangming, was a native of Anci in Youzhou.

entries.zh: 父夢殷，累官薊、儒、順三州刺史。
entries.en: His father Mengyin had served in turn as prefect of Ji, Ru, and Shun.
entries.literal: His father Mengyin held successive posts as prefect of Ji, Ru, and Shun.

entries.zh: 延徽少英，燕帥劉仁恭奇之，召為幽都府文學、平州錄事參軍，同馮道祗候院，授幽州觀察度支使。
entries.en: A gifted youth, Yanhui caught the eye of the Yan commander Liu Rengong, who made him literary instructor at the Youdu prefectural office and recorder-assistant of Pingzhou, assigned with Feng Dao to the reception bureau, then Youzhou observation revenue commissioner.
entries.literal: Yanhui was outstanding in youth; the Yan commander Liu Rengong was struck by him and summoned him as literary instructor of the Youdu Prefecture office and recorder-assistant of Pingzhou, attached to the Di-hou Court with Feng Dao; he was appointed Youzhou observation revenue commissioner.

entries.zh: 後守光為帥，延徽來聘，太祖怒其不屈，留之。
entries.en: When Shouguang later became commander, Yanhui came as envoy; Emperor Taizu, angered that he refused to submit, kept him.
entries.literal: Later, when Shouguang became commander, Yanhui came on a diplomatic mission; the Taizu Emperor was angered that he would not bow and detained him.

entries.zh: 述律後諫曰：「彼秉節弗撓，賢者也，奈何困辱之？」
entries.en: Empress Shulü urged: "He keeps his integrity and will not yield—a worthy man. Why subject him to hardship and shame?"
entries.literal: Empress Shulü remonstrated: "He holds to his integrity and will not bend—a worthy man. How can we humiliate and abuse him?"

entries.zh: 太祖召與語，合上意，立命參軍事。
entries.en: Emperor Taizu summoned him for an audience, was pleased with him, and at once put him on his staff.
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor summoned him to converse; it accorded with his intent, and he immediately ordered him to assist in military affairs.

entries.zh: 攻党項、室韋，服諸部落，延徽之籌居多。
entries.en: In campaigns against the Tangut and Shiwei and in bringing the tribes to heel, Yanhui's counsel was decisive.
entries.literal: In attacking the Tangut and Shiwei and subduing the tribes, Yanhui's planning figured largely.

entries.zh: 乃請樹城郭，分市裏，以居漢人之降者。
entries.en: He proposed building walled towns with separate wards and markets for surrendered Han settlers.
entries.literal: He then requested to erect walls and cities, divide wards and market blocks, and settle surrendering Han there.

entries.zh: 又為定配偶，教墾藝，以生養之。
entries.en: He arranged marriages, taught farming, and saw to their livelihood.
entries.literal: He also arranged marriages, taught clearing and cultivation, and nourished them for growth.

entries.zh: 以故逃亡者少。
entries.en: Consequently few fled.
entries.literal: For this reason fugitives were few.

entries.zh: 居久之，慨然懷其鄉里，賦詩見意，遂亡歸唐。
entries.en: After a long stay he yearned for home, wrote a poem to say so, and fled back to Tang.
entries.literal: After dwelling there long, he sighed with longing for his homeland, composed a poem to express his intent, and thereupon fled and returned to Tang.

entries.zh: 已而與他將王緘有隙，懼及難，乃省親幽州，匿故人王德明舍。
entries.en: Soon he fell out with the general Wang Jian and, fearing reprisal, visited his family in Youzhou and hid with his friend Wang Deming.
entries.literal: Before long he had a rift with another commander Wang Jian, feared disaster would reach him, and so went to visit family in Youzhou, hiding in the house of his old acquaintance Wang Deming.

entries.zh: 德明問所適，延徽曰：「吾將復走契丹。」
entries.en: Deming asked where he was headed. Yanhui said: "I mean to flee back to the Khitan."
entries.literal: Deming asked where he was bound; Yanhui said: "I intend to flee again to the Khitan."

entries.zh: 德明不以為然。
entries.en: Deming thought this unwise.
entries.literal: Deming did not approve.

entries.zh: 延徽笑曰：「彼失我如失左右手，其見我必喜。」
entries.en: Yanhui smiled: "They will miss me as they would their own hands—when they see me again they will be delighted."
entries.literal: Yanhui smiled and said: "They will lose me as one loses left and right hands; when they see me they are sure to rejoice."

entries.zh: 既至，太祖問故。
entries.en: When he arrived Emperor Taizu asked why he had come.
entries.literal: When he arrived, the Taizu Emperor asked the reason.

entries.zh: 延徽曰：「忘親非孝，棄君非忠。
entries.en: Yanhui said: "To forget one's parents is unfilial; to abandon one's lord is disloyal.
entries.literal: Yanhui said: "To forget one's parents is not filial; to abandon one's lord is not loyal.

entries.zh: 臣雖挺身逃，臣心在陛下。
entries.en: Though I fled in body, my heart remained with you.
entries.literal: Although I fled with my person, my heart was with Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 臣是以復來。」
entries.en: That is why I have returned."
entries.literal: Therefore I have come again."

entries.zh: 上大悅，賜名曰匣列。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased and gave him the name Xialie.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed the name Xialie.

entries.zh: 「匣列」，遼言復來也。
entries.en: In Khitan, "Xialie" means "one who comes back."
entries.literal: "Xialie"—in Liao speech it means "return again."

entries.zh: 即命為守政事令、崇文館大學士，中外事悉令參決。
entries.en: He was promptly made acting governance director and Chongwen Hall grand academician, with authority over both palace and frontier affairs.
entries.literal: He was immediately appointed acting governance director and grand academician of the Chongwen Hall; all internal and external affairs were ordered for him to deliberate and decide.

entries.zh: 韓知古，薊州玉田人，善謀有識量。
entries.en: Han Zhigu, from Yutian in Jizhou, was a skilled strategist of steady judgment.
entries.literal: Han Zhigu, a native of Yutian in Jizhou, was skilled in planning and possessed discernment and breadth.

entries.zh: 太祖平薊時，知古六歲，為淳欽皇后兄欲穩所得。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu took Ji, Zhigu was six; he was taken by Yuwen, elder brother of Empress Chunqin.
entries.literal: When the Taizu Emperor pacified Ji, Zhigu was six years old and was taken by Yuwen, elder brother of Empress Chunqin.

entries.zh: 後來嬪，知古從焉，未得省見。
entries.en: When she later entered the palace harem Zhigu came with her but never gained audience with the emperor.
entries.literal: Later when she entered the harem Zhigu accompanied her but could not obtain an imperial audience.

entries.zh: 久之，負其有，怏怏不得志，挺身逃庸保，以供資用。
entries.en: Long unrecognized despite his talents, he grew restless and slipped away to hire himself out for a living.
entries.literal: After long waiting, confident of his worth yet frustrated and unfulfilled, he cast off restraint and fled to hire himself out for wages to supply his needs.

entries.zh: 其子匡嗣得親近太祖，因間言。
entries.en: His son Kuangsi had the emperor's ear and mentioned him in passing.
entries.literal: His son Kuangsi gained closeness to the Taizu Emperor and spoke of him in private.

entries.zh: 太祖召見與語，賢之，命參謀議。
entries.en: Emperor Taizu summoned him, found him capable, and put him on the planning staff.
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor summoned him, conversed with him, deemed him worthy, and ordered him to assist in planning.

entries.zh: 神冊初，遙授彰武軍節度使。
entries.en: At the opening of Shence he received the honorary post of Zhangwu Army military commissioner.
entries.literal: At the start of Shence he was remotely appointed military commissioner of the Zhangwu Army.

entries.zh: 久之，信任益篤，總知漢兒司事，兼主諸國禮儀。
entries.en: Over time the emperor's trust deepened; he took charge of Han administration and also oversaw ceremonial protocol.
entries.literal: After long service trust deepened further; he was put in overall charge of Han affairs and concurrently directed the rites and ceremonies of all domains.

entries.zh: 時儀法疏闊，知古援據故典，參酌國俗，與漢儀雜就之，使國人易知而行。
entries.en: Ritual protocol was still rudimentary; Zhigu drew on ancient precedents, adapted Khitan custom, and blended in Han practice until the people could follow them with ease.
entries.literal: At the time ritual law was loose and incomplete; Zhigu drew on old statutes, weighed national custom, and blended them with Han rites so that countrymen would easily understand and put them into practice.

entries.zh: 頃之，拜左僕射，與康默記將漢軍征渤海有功，遷中書令。
entries.en: Before long he was made Left Vice Director; campaigning against Bohai with Kang Moji at the head of the Han army earned him promotion to Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Left Vice Director; with Kang Moji he led the Han army on the Bohai campaign with merit and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 天顯中卒，為佐命功臣之一。
entries.en: He died in the Tianxian era, numbered among the founding merit ministers.
entries.literal: He died during Tianxian and was one of the founding merit ministers.

entries.zh: 子匡嗣。
entries.en: His son was Kuangsi.
entries.literal: His son Kuangsi.

entries.zh: 匡嗣以善醫，直長樂宮，皇后視之猶子。
entries.en: Skilled in medicine, Kuangsi served at Changle Palace, where the empress treated him like a son.
entries.literal: Kuangsi, for skill in medicine, served directly at Changle Palace; the empress regarded him as her own son.

entries.zh: 應歷十年，為太祖廟詳穩。
entries.en: In Yingli year 10 he was made temple officer for Emperor Taizu's shrine.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Yingli he was detailed stable officer of the Taizu Emperor's temple.

entries.zh: 後宋王喜隱謀叛，辭引匡嗣，上置不問。
entries.en: When Prince of Song Xiyin later plotted rebellion and named Kuangsi in his confession, the emperor took no action.
entries.literal: Later when Prince of Song Xiyin plotted rebellion, his testimony implicated Kuangsi; the emperor set the matter aside without inquiry.

entries.zh: 初，景宗在藩邸，善匡嗣。
entries.en: In his days as heir apparent Emperor Jingzong had been close to Kuangsi.
entries.literal: Early on, when Jingzong was at the princely residence, he was on good terms with Kuangsi.

entries.zh: 即位，拜上京留守。
entries.en: When he took the throne he made Kuangsi defender of the Upper Capital.
entries.literal: Upon accession Kuangsi was appointed defender of the Upper Capital.

entries.zh: 頃之，王燕，改南京留守。
entries.en: Soon enfeoffed Prince of Yan, Kuangsi was transferred to Nanjing as defender.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter enfeoffed Prince of Yan, he was changed to defender of Nanjing.

entries.zh: 保寧末，以留守攝樞密使。
entries.en: Near the end of Baoning he served as defender while also acting as privy commissioner.
entries.literal: At the end of Baoning, as defender he also acted as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 時耶律虎古使宋還，言宋人必取河東，合先事以為備。
