entries.en: Yelü Hugu, returning from an embassy to Song, warned that the Song would seize Hedong and urged early preparations.
entries.literal: At the time Yelü Hugu returned from a mission to Song and said the Song would certainly take Hedong; it was fitting to prepare ahead.

entries.zh: 匡嗣詆之曰：「寧有是！」
entries.en: Kuangsi scoffed: "Nonsense!"
entries.literal: Kuangsi denounced him, saying: "How could there be such a thing!"

entries.zh: 已而宋人果取太原，乘勝逼燕。
entries.en: Soon the Song took Taiyuan and pressed toward Yan in victory.
entries.literal: Before long the Song indeed took Taiyuan and, pressing the victory, threatened Yan.

entries.zh: 匡嗣與南府宰相沙、惕隱休哥侵宋，軍於滿城。
entries.en: Kuangsi joined Southern Chancellor Yelu Sha and tithen Xiuge in an incursion against Song and encamped at Mancheng.
entries.literal: Kuangsi with Southern Chancellor Yelu Sha and tithen Xiuge invaded Song and encamped at Mancheng.

entries.zh: 方陣，宋人請降。
entries.en: As the armies drew up, the Song offered surrender.
entries.literal: As battle lines were forming, the Song requested surrender.

entries.zh: 匡嗣欲納之，休哥曰：「彼軍氣甚銳，疑誘我也。
entries.en: Kuangsi wanted to accept; Xiuge said: "Their morale is too high—they mean to bait us.
entries.literal: Kuangsi wished to accept them; Xiuge said: "Their army's spirit is very sharp; I suspect they mean to lure us.

entries.zh: 可整頓士卒以禦。」
entries.en: Ready the men for a stand."
entries.literal: We should ready the troops to resist."

entries.zh: 匡嗣不聽。
entries.en: Kuangsi refused to listen.
entries.literal: Kuangsi did not listen.

entries.zh: 俄而宋軍鼓噪薄我，眾蹙踐，塵起漲天。
entries.en: Suddenly the Song charged with drums and shouts; our ranks buckled and trampled one another; dust blotted out the sky.
entries.literal: Before long the Song army beat drums and clamored, pressing on us; the masses crowded and trampled; dust rose flooding the sky.

entries.zh: 匡嗣倉卒諭諸將，無當其鋒。
entries.en: Kuangsi hurriedly told his commanders not to meet the charge.
entries.literal: Kuangsi in haste instructed the generals that none should meet their spearhead.

entries.zh: 眾既奔，遇伏兵扼要路，匡嗣棄旗鼓遁，其眾走易州山，獨休哥收所棄兵械，全軍還。
entries.en: As the army broke, ambushers blocked the retreat; Kuangsi abandoned his standards and fled, his troops scattering into the Yizhou hills; only Xiuge recovered the abandoned arms and brought his command safely back.
entries.literal: Once the masses had fled they met ambush troops blocking the vital road; Kuangsi cast away banners and drums and fled; his army fled to the mountains of Yizhou; only Xiuge gathered the abandoned weapons and returned with the whole army intact.

entries.zh: 帝怒匡嗣，數之曰：「爾違眾謀，深入敵境，爾罪一也；
entries.en: The emperor raged at Kuangsi and listed his offenses: "You rejected your officers' counsel and drove deep into enemy country—first offense;
entries.literal: The emperor was angry with Kuangsi and reckoned his crimes: "You defied collective counsel and penetrated deep into enemy territory—your first crime;

entries.zh: 號令不肅，行伍不整，爾罪二也；
entries.en: Your orders were lax and ranks disordered—second offense;
entries.literal: Your orders were lax and ranks disordered—your second crime;

entries.zh: 棄我師旅，挺身鼠竄，爾罪三也；
entries.en: You abandoned your command and scurried off like a rat—third offense;
entries.literal: You abandoned your army and scurried off like a rat—your third crime;

entries.zh: 偵候失機，守禦弗備，爾罪四也；
entries.en: You failed your scouts and left defenses unprepared—fourth offense;
entries.literal: Your scouts failed and defenses were unprepared—your fourth crime;

entries.zh: 捐棄旗鼓，損威辱國，爾罪五也。」
entries.en: You cast away your banners and disgraced the realm—fifth offense."
entries.literal: You cast away your banners and disgraced the realm—your fifth crime."

entries.zh: 促令誅之。
entries.en: He ordered execution at once.
entries.literal: He ordered execution at once.

entries.zh: 皇后引諸內戚徐為開解，上重違其請。
entries.en: The empress and her kinsmen gradually pleaded for mercy; reluctant to refuse her, the emperor stayed his hand.
entries.literal: The empress led the inner kin to intercede gradually and open the matter; the emperor greatly hesitated to go against her plea.

entries.zh: 良久，威稍霽，乃杖而免之。
entries.en: Eventually his anger cooled and he had Kuangsi beaten and released.
entries.literal: After a long while his wrath eased slightly, and he had him beaten with the staff and spared.

entries.zh: 既而遙授晉昌軍節度使。
entries.en: He was later given the honorary post of Jinchang Army military commissioner.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was remotely appointed military commissioner of the Jinchang Army.

entries.zh: 乾亨三年，改西南面招討使，卒。
entries.en: In Qianheng year 3 he was made Southwest Route pacification commissioner and died.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qianheng he was changed to Southwest Route pacification commissioner and died.

entries.zh: 睿智皇后聞之，遣使臨吊，賻贈甚厚，後追贈尚書令。
entries.en: When the Wise Empress heard, she sent envoys to mourn and gave lavish funeral gifts; later he was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: When the Wise Empress heard, she sent envoys to mourn and gave lavish funeral gifts; later he was posthumously granted Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 五子：德源，德讓，後賜名隆運，德威，德崇，德凝。
entries.en: He had five sons: Deyuan; Derang, later granted the name Longyun; Dewei; Dechong; and Dening.
entries.literal: Five sons: Deyuan; Derang, later granted the name Longyun; Dewei; Dechong; and Dening.

entries.zh: 德源、德凝附傳，余各有傳。
entries.en: Deyuan and Dening are treated in appendices here; the others have separate biographies.
entries.literal: Deyuan and Dening are treated in appendices here; the others have separate biographies.

entries.zh: 孫延壽，字胤昌，少倜儻，謂其所親：「大丈夫為將，當效節邊垂，馬革裹屍。」
entries.en: His grandson Yanshou, whose courtesy name was Yinchang, was dashing from youth. He told his intimates: "A man who takes command should stand his post on the frontier and meet death wrapped in horsehide."
entries.literal: His grandson Yanshou, courtesy name Yinchang, was bold and free-spirited in youth; he told those close to him: "A true man who becomes a general should prove his loyalty on the frontier border, wrapped in horsehide for burial."

entries.zh: 景宗特授千牛衛大將軍。
entries.en: Emperor Jingzong specially appointed him general of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
entries.literal: Emperor Jingzong specially awarded him general of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

entries.zh: 宋人攻南京，諸將既成列，延壽獨奮擊陣前，敵遂大潰。
entries.en: When the Song attacked Nanjing and the commanders had drawn up battle lines, Yanshou alone charged the front; the enemy broke and fled.
entries.literal: When Song forces attacked Nanjing, the generals had already formed ranks; Yanshou alone charged fiercely before the lines, and the enemy thereupon routed in great disorder.

entries.zh: 以功遙授保大軍節度使。
entries.en: For this exploit he received the honorary title of Baoda Army military commissioner.
entries.literal: For his merit he was remotely appointed military commissioner of the Baoda Army.

entries.zh: 乾亨三年卒。
entries.en: He died in Qianheng year 3.
entries.literal: He died in the third year of Qianheng.

entries.zh: 德源，性愚而貪，早侍景宗邸。
entries.en: Deyuan was dull-witted and greedy; he entered the heir apparent Jingzong's service early.
entries.literal: Deyuan was dull-witted and greedy; he entered the heir apparent Jingzong's service early.

entries.zh: 及即位，列近侍。
entries.en: When Jingzong took the throne he was ranked among the close attendants.
entries.literal: When Jingzong took the throne he was ranked among the close attendants.

entries.zh: 保寧間，官崇義、興國二軍節度使，加檢校太師。
entries.en: During Baoning he held the posts of Chongyi and Xingguo army military commissioner and was made honorary Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: During Baoning he held the posts of Chongyi and Xingguo army military commissioner and was made honorary Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 以賄名，德讓貽書諫之，終不悛。
entries.en: His reputation for bribery was notorious; Derang wrote urging reform, but he never changed.
entries.literal: His reputation for bribery was notorious; Derang wrote urging reform, but he never changed.

entries.zh: 以故論者少之。
entries.en: Critics therefore held him in low regard.
entries.literal: Critics therefore held him in low regard.

entries.zh: 後加同政事門下平章事，遙攝保寧軍節度使。
entries.en: Later he was made associate director of the Gate Department and acting Baoning Army military commissioner in absentia.
entries.literal: Later he was made associate director of the Gate Department and acting Baoning Army military commissioner in absentia.

entries.zh: 乾亨初卒。
entries.en: He died at the start of Qianheng.
entries.literal: He died at the start of Qianheng.

entries.zh: 耶律敵剌蕭痕篤康默記
entries.en: Yelu Dila, Xiao Hendu, and Kang Moji
entries.literal: Yelu Dila, Xiao Hendu, Kang Moji

entries.en: (Yanshou)
entries.literal: (Yanshou)

entries.zh: 韓延徽
entries.en: Han Yanhui
entries.literal: Han Yanhui

entries.zh: 〈（德樞紹勛紹芳資讓）〉
entries.en: (Deshu, Shaoxun, Shaofang, and Zirang)
entries.literal: (Deshu, Shaoxun, Shaofang, Zirang)

entries.zh: 韓知古
entries.en: Han Zhigu
entries.literal: Han Zhigu

entries.zh: 〈（匡嗣德源德凝）〉
entries.en: (Kuangsi, Deyuan, and Dening)
entries.literal: (Kuangsi, Deyuan, Dening)

entries.zh: 羽之，小字兀裏，字寅底哂。
entries.en: Yuzhi, whose childhood name was Wuli and whose courtesy name was Yindi Shen,
entries.literal: Yuzhi, childhood name Wuli, courtesy name Yindi Shen.

entries.zh: 幼豪爽不群，長嗜學，通諸部語。
entries.en: was bold and unconventional as a youth; when grown he devoted himself to learning and mastered the languages of the various tribes.
entries.literal: As a child he was bold and unorthodox; when grown he loved learning and mastered the languages of the various tribes.

entries.zh: 太祖經營之初，多預軍謀。
entries.en: In the early years of Emperor Taizu's state-building, he took part in many military plans.
entries.literal: In the early period of the Emperor Taizu's founding efforts, he took part in many military plans.

entries.zh: 天顯元年，渤海平，立皇太子為東丹王，以羽之為中臺省右次相。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianxian, after Bohai was pacified, the heir apparent was installed as King of Eastern Dan and Yuzhi was appointed Right Vice Chancellor of the Central Court.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianxian, when Bohai was pacified, the heir apparent was installed as King of Eastern Dan, and Yuzhi was made Right Vice Chancellor of the Central Court.

entries.zh: 時人心未安，左大相叠剌不逾月薨，羽之蒞事勤恪，威信並行。
entries.en: Popular sentiment was still unsettled at the time; the Left Grand Chancellor Diechi died within a month of taking office, yet Yuzhi handled affairs with diligence and rigor, and authority and trust went hand in hand.
entries.literal: At that time popular sentiment was still unsettled; the Left Grand Chancellor Diechi died within a month of taking office, but Yuzhi conducted affairs with diligence and strictness, and authority and trust went hand in hand.

entries.zh: 太宗即位，上表曰：「我大聖天皇始有東土，擇賢輔以撫斯民，不以臣愚而任之，國家利害，敢不以聞。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, Yuzhi submitted a memorial that read: "Our Great Sage Heavenly Emperor first secured the eastern lands and chose worthy ministers to govern the people. Though he did not regard me as capable, he still entrusted me with office; how could I fail to speak of what helps or harms the state?
entries.literal: When Emperor Taizong acceded, he submitted a memorial saying: "Our Great Sage Heavenly Emperor first gained the eastern lands and chose worthy men to comfort the people. Though he did not regard this subject as wise, he still entrusted me with office; the gains and losses of the state—how dare I not report them?

entries.zh: 渤海昔畏南朝，阻險自衛，居忽汗城。
entries.en: Bohai once feared the Southern Court, held itself behind natural barriers, and made its seat at Hohan.
entries.literal: Bohai in the past feared the Southern Court, relied on natural barriers for self-defense, and dwelt at Hohan city.

entries.zh: 今去上京遼邈，既不為用，又不罷戍，果何為哉？
entries.en: It now lies far from the Supreme Capital, yet we neither put it to use nor withdraw the garrisons—what is the point?
entries.literal: Now it lies far from the Supreme Capital; it is neither useful nor are the garrisons withdrawn—what purpose does this serve?

entries.zh: 先帝因彼離心，乘釁而動，故不戰而克。
entries.en: The late emperor took advantage of their divided loyalties and struck when the moment was ripe, and so conquered them without a battle.
entries.literal: The late emperor, because their hearts were divided, seized the opportunity and moved; therefore he conquered without fighting.

entries.zh: 天授人與，彼一時也。
entries.en: Heaven granted the opportunity and men seized it—that was a moment that will not return.
entries.literal: Heaven bestowed and men granted—that was a moment in time.

entries.zh: 遺種浸以蕃息，今居遠境，恐為後患。
entries.en: Their surviving people have gradually multiplied; living now on distant frontiers, they may yet become a future threat.
entries.literal: The surviving people have gradually multiplied; now they dwell on distant borders and may become a later trouble.

entries.zh: 梁水之地，乃其故鄉，地衍土活，有木鐵鹽魚之利。
entries.en: The Liangshui region is their ancestral homeland: the land is broad, the soil fertile, and it offers timber, iron, salt, and fish.
entries.literal: The land of Liangshui is their old homeland; the soil is broad and fertile, and there are advantages in timber, iron, salt, and fish.

entries.zh: 乘其微弱，徙還其民，萬世長策也。
entries.en: While they are still weak, move their people back home—that is a policy for the ages.
entries.literal: Taking advantage of their weakness, relocate their people back—a long-term policy for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 彼得故鄉，又獲木鐵鹽魚之饒，必安居樂業。
entries.en: Once they regain their homeland and the bounty of timber, iron, salt, and fish, they will surely settle down and prosper.
entries.literal: When they regain their homeland and also obtain the abundance of timber, iron, salt, and fish, they will surely settle in peace and take joy in their work.

entries.zh: 然後選徒以翼吾左，突厥、党項、室韋夾輔吾右，可以坐制南邦，混一天下，成聖祖未集之功，貽後世無疆之福。」
entries.en: Then choose settlers to strengthen our left, with the Turks, Tanguts, and Shiwei flanking our right, and we can hold the southern states in check from a secure position, unite the realm, finish the work our sage founder left incomplete, and bequeath boundless blessings to posterity."
entries.literal: Then select settlers to strengthen our left flank; with the Turks, Tanguts, and Shiwei flanking our right, we can control the southern states from a fixed position, unite all under Heaven, complete the unfinished work of the sage ancestor, and bequeath boundless blessings to later generations."

entries.zh: 表奏，帝嘉納之。
entries.en: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor praised it and accepted his advice.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.

entries.zh: 是歲，詔徙東丹國民於梁水，時稱其善。
entries.en: That year an edict moved the people of Eastern Dan to Liangshui, and contemporaries praised the policy as wise.
entries.literal: That year an edict ordered the people of Eastern Dan relocated to Liangshui; at the time his policy was praised as good.

entries.zh: 人皇王奔唐，羽之鎮撫國人，一切如故。
entries.en: When the Renhuang King fled to Tang, Yuzhi pacified the populace and kept everything as it had been.
entries.literal: When the Renhuang King fled to Tang, Yuzhi pacified the people of the state and kept everything as before.

entries.zh: 以功加守太傅，遷中臺省左相。
entries.en: For his service he was additionally appointed Acting Grand Tutor and promoted to Left Chancellor of the Central Court.
entries.literal: For his merit he was additionally made Acting Grand Tutor and transferred to Left Chancellor of the Central Court.

entries.zh: 會同初，以冊禮赴闕，加特進。
entries.en: At the opening of the Huitong era he went to court for the enthronement ceremonies and was granted the rank of Special Advancement.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, he went to court for the investiture rites and was given the special advancement rank.

entries.zh: 表奏左次相渤海蘇貪墨不法事，卒。
entries.en: He submitted a memorial exposing the corruption and lawlessness of Su of Bohai, the Left Vice Chancellor, then died.
entries.literal: He memorialized reporting that Su of Bohai, the Left Vice Chancellor, was corrupt and lawless, then died.

entries.zh: 子和裏，終東京留守。
entries.en: His son Heli eventually served as Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: His son Heli ended as Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 耶律鐸臻，字敵輦，六院部人。
entries.en: Yelu Duozhen, whose courtesy name was Dinian, came from the Six Yuan Divisions.
entries.literal: Yelu Duozhen, courtesy name Dinian, was a man of the Six Yuan Divisions.

entries.zh: 祖蒲古只，遙輦氏時再為本部夷離堇。
entries.en: His grandfather Pugu Zhi had twice served as tribal chieftain of their division under the Yaolian clan.
entries.literal: His grandfather Pugu Zhi twice served as Yilijin of this division in the time of the Yaolian clan.

entries.zh: 耶律狼德等既害玄祖，暴橫益肆。
entries.en: After Yelu Langde and his faction murdered the Mysterious Ancestor, their violence and arrogance grew ever bolder.
entries.literal: After Yelu Langde and others had killed the Mysterious Ancestor, their violence and arrogance grew ever more unrestrained.

entries.zh: 蒲古只以計誘其黨，悉誅夷之。
entries.en: Pugu Zhi lured their faction into a trap by stratagem and put them all to death.
entries.literal: Pugu Zhi by stratagem lured out their faction and executed them all.

entries.zh: 鐸臻幼有誌節，太祖為於越，常居左右。
entries.en: Duozhen showed moral resolve even as a youth; while Emperor Taizu still held the title of Yuyue, he kept Duozhen constantly at his side.
entries.literal: Duozhen in youth had resolve and integrity; when the Emperor Taizu was Yuyue, he constantly attended at his side.

entries.zh: 後即位，梁人遣使求轅軸材，太祖難之。
entries.en: After he took the throne, Liang sent envoys requesting timber for chariot axles, and Emperor Taizu was at a loss how to respond.
entries.literal: Later, when he took the throne, the people of Liang sent envoys requesting axle-hub timber, and the Emperor Taizu found it difficult.

entries.zh: 鐸臻曰：「梁名求材，實覘吾輕重。
entries.en: Duozhen said, "Liang claims to want timber, but in truth they are testing our strength.
entries.literal: Duozhen said: "Liang asks for timber in name, but in fact they are probing our strength.

entries.zh: 宜答曰：『材之所生，必深山窮谷，有神司之，須白鼻赤驢禱祠，然後可伐。』
entries.en: We should answer that the timber grows only in deep mountains and remote valleys, that a spirit oversees it, and that it cannot be cut until one has prayed with a white-nosed red donkey.
entries.literal: We should answer: 'Where the timber grows must be deep mountains and remote valleys; a spirit oversees it, and one must pray with a white-nosed red donkey before it can be cut.'

entries.zh: 如此，則其語自塞矣。」
entries.en: If we say that, their request will collapse of its own absurdity."
entries.literal: In this way their words will choke themselves off."

entries.zh: 已而果然。
entries.en: And so it proved.
entries.literal: Before long it proved exactly so.

entries.zh: 天贊三年，將伐渤海，鐸臻諫曰：「陛下先事渤海，則西夏必躡吾後。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianzan, as the emperor prepared to attack Bohai, Duozhen remonstrated: "If Your Majesty strikes at Bohai first, Western Xia will surely fall upon our rear.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianzan, when he was about to attack Bohai, Duozhen remonstrated: "If Your Majesty deals with Bohai first, Western Xia will surely tread on our rear.

entries.zh: 請先西討，庶無後顧憂。」
entries.en: Attack the west first, so that we need not fear what lies behind us."
entries.literal: Please attack west first, so that there may be no worry behind."

entries.zh: 太祖從之。
entries.en: Emperor Taizu followed his counsel.
entries.literal: The Emperor Taizu followed his advice.

entries.zh: 及淳欽皇后稱制，惡鐸臻，囚之，誓曰：「鐵鎖朽，當釋汝！」
entries.en: When Empress Chunqin assumed the regency, she took a dislike to Duozhen and imprisoned him, swearing, "When the iron chains rust through, I shall release you!"
entries.literal: When Empress Chunqin assumed regency, she disliked Duozhen, imprisoned him, and swore: "When the iron chains rot, I shall release you!"

entries.zh: 既而召之，使者欲去鎖，鐸臻辭曰：「鐵未朽，可釋乎？」
entries.en: Later she summoned him; when the messenger moved to remove his chains, Duozhen refused: "The iron has not yet rusted—may I be released?"
entries.literal: Later she summoned him; the envoy wished to remove the locks, but Duozhen declined: "The iron has not rotted—may I be released?"

entries.zh: 後聞，嘉嘆，趣召釋之。
entries.en: When she heard of this, she marveled and sighed with approval, and at once ordered him freed.
entries.literal: When she heard of this afterward, she praised and sighed, and urgently summoned and released him.

entries.zh: 天顯二年卒。
entries.en: He died in the second year of Tianxian.
entries.literal: He died in the second year of Tianxian.

entries.zh: 弟古、突呂不。
entries.en: His younger brothers were Gu and Tulubu.
entries.literal: His younger brothers were Gu and Tulubu.

entries.zh: 論曰：神冊初元，將相大臣拔起風塵之中，翼扶王運，以任職取名者，固一時之材，亦由太祖推誠禦下，不任獨斷，用能總攬群策而為之用歟！
entries.en: The commentary says: At the opening of the Shence era, generals and ministers rose from the turmoil of the age to support the royal enterprise. Men who won renown through office were indeed talents of their day, yet it was also because Emperor Taizu dealt sincerely with his subordinates, refused to decide everything alone, and so could gather every counsel and put it to use.
entries.literal: The commentary says: At the beginning of Shence, generals, ministers, and great officials were raised from the dust of turmoil to wing and support the royal fortune. Those who gained fame through office were indeed talents of their time, but it was also because the Emperor Taizu treated subordinates with sincerity, did not rely on solitary decisions, and thus could gather all strategies and put them to use!

entries.zh: 其投天隙而列功庸，至有心腹、耳目、手足之喻，豈偶然哉！
entries.en: That they seized Heaven's openings and won their places of honor, even to the point of being called the ruler's heart, eyes, ears, hands, and feet—could that have been mere chance?
entries.literal: That they seized Heaven's openings and ranked their achievements, even to the metaphors of heart, eyes and ears, and hands and feet—was this accidental?

entries.zh: 討党項，走敵魯，平剌葛，定渤海，功亦偉矣。
entries.en: In subduing the Tanguts, driving off Dilu, pacifying Lage, and settling Bohai, their achievements were likewise magnificent.
entries.literal: In punishing the Tanguts, driving off Dilu, pacifying Lage, and settling Bohai, their achievements were also grand.

entries.zh: 若默記治獄不冤，頗德持論不撓，延徽立經陳紀，紹勛秉節而死，圖魯窘料敵制勝，豈器博者無近用，道長者其功遠歟？
entries.en: Consider Kang Moji, who judged cases without injustice; Pode, who held to his principles without yielding; Han Yanhui, who established institutions and set forth the laws; Shaoxun, who died holding to his integrity; and Tulujiong, who read the enemy and secured victory—are men of broad talent useless in the present, and men of far-reaching vision rewarded only in the long run?
entries.literal: As for Moji in governing cases without injustice, Pode in holding to argument without yielding, Yanhui in establishing classics and setting forth institutions, Shaoxun in holding to integrity unto death, and Tulujiong in gauging the enemy and controlling victory—can those whose vessels are broad have no near use, and those whose Way is long have achievements that reach far?

entries.zh: 稱為佐命，固宜。
entries.en: To call them founders of the dynasty was only fitting.
entries.literal: To call them assistants in establishing the mandate was surely fitting.

entries.zh: 古，字涅剌昆，初名霞馬葛。
entries.en: Gu, whose courtesy name was Nielakun and whose original name was Xiamage,
entries.literal: Gu, courtesy name Nielakun, original name Xiamage.

entries.zh: 太祖為於越，嘗從略地山右。
entries.en: when Emperor Taizu was still Yuyue, once accompanied him in campaigns west of the mountains.
entries.literal: when the Emperor Taizu was Yuyue, once followed him in raiding the lands west of the mountains.

entries.zh: 會李克用於雲州，古侍，克用異之曰：「是兒骨相非常，不宜使在左右。」
entries.en: He met Li Keyong at Yunzhou while attending the emperor; Keyong remarked in wonder, "This boy's bearing is extraordinary—he should not be kept close at hand."
entries.literal: He met Li Keyong at Yunzhou; Gu attended him, and Keyong marveled, saying: "This boy's bone structure is extraordinary; he should not be kept at one's side."

entries.zh: 以故太祖頗忌之。
entries.en: For this reason Emperor Taizu grew somewhat wary of him.
entries.literal: For this reason the Emperor Taizu came to be somewhat wary of him.

entries.zh: 時方西討，諸弟亂作，聞變，太祖問古與否，曰無。
entries.en: While the army was campaigning in the west, the emperor's younger brothers rose in revolt. On hearing the news, Emperor Taizu asked whether Gu had taken part; he was told no.
entries.literal: At that time they were campaigning west; the emperor's younger brothers rose in revolt. On hearing of the disturbance, the Emperor Taizu asked whether Gu was involved; the answer was no.

entries.zh: 喜曰：「吾無患矣！」
entries.en: The emperor rejoiced: "Then I have nothing to fear!"
entries.literal: He rejoiced: "I have no worry!"

entries.zh: 趣召古議。
entries.en: He at once summoned Gu to counsel him.
entries.literal: He urgently summoned Gu to deliberate.

entries.zh: 古陳殄滅之策，後皆如言，以故錫賚甚厚。
entries.en: Gu laid out a plan for their destruction, and events afterward unfolded exactly as he had said; for this the emperor lavished rewards upon him.
entries.literal: Gu set forth a plan for their extermination; afterward events all matched his words, and for this reason rewards were very generous.

entries.zh: 神冊末，南伐，以古佐右皮室詳穩老古，與唐兵戰於雲碧店，老古中流矢，傷甚，太祖疑古陰害之。
entries.en: At the end of the Shence era, during the southern campaign, Gu served as deputy to Laogu, commander of the Right Pishi Division; they fought Tang forces at Yunbi, where Laogu was struck by an arrow and badly wounded. Emperor Taizu suspected that Gu had plotted against him in secret.
entries.literal: At the end of Shence, on the southern campaign, Gu was made assistant to Laogu, Xiangwen of the Right Pishi Division; they fought Tang troops at Yunbi post, Laogu was struck by a flying arrow and badly wounded, and the Emperor Taizu suspected Gu of secretly harming him.

entries.zh: 古知上意，跪曰：「陛下疑臣恥居老古麾下耶？
entries.en: Gu understood the emperor's suspicion, knelt, and said, "Does Your Majesty think I was ashamed to serve under Laogu?
entries.literal: Gu knew the emperor's mind, knelt, and said: "Does Your Majesty suspect that this subject was ashamed to serve under Laogu?

entries.zh: 及今老古在，請遣使問之。」
entries.en: Laogu is still alive—send someone to ask him."
entries.literal: Since Laogu is still alive, please send an envoy to ask him."

entries.zh: 太祖使問老古，對曰：「臣於古無可疑者。」
entries.en: Emperor Taizu did so; Laogu replied, "I have no suspicion of Gu whatsoever."
entries.literal: The Emperor Taizu sent to ask Laogu, who answered: "This subject has nothing doubtful about Gu."

entries.zh: 上意乃釋。
entries.en: The emperor's doubts were dispelled.
entries.literal: The emperor's mind was then released.

entries.zh: 老古卒，遂以古為右皮室詳穩。
entries.en: After Laogu died, Gu was appointed commander of the Right Pishi Division.
entries.literal: When Laogu died, Gu was then made Xiangwen of the Right Pishi Division.

entries.zh: 既卒，太祖謂左右曰：「古死，猶長松自倒，非吾伐之也。」
entries.en: After his death Emperor Taizu told those around him, "When Gu died, it was like a great pine toppling of its own weight—not because I felled it."
entries.literal: After he died, the Emperor Taizu said to those around him: "When Gu died, it was like a tall pine falling of itself—not because I cut it down."

entries.zh: 突呂不，字鐸袞，幼聰敏嗜學。
entries.en: Tulubu, whose courtesy name was Duogun, was clever and devoted to learning from childhood.
entries.literal: Tulubu, courtesy name Duogun, in youth was clever and loved learning.

entries.zh: 事太祖見器重。
entries.en: In serving Emperor Taizu he won deep trust.
entries.literal: In serving the Emperor Taizu he was regarded with esteem.

entries.zh: 及制契丹大字，突呂不贊成為多。
entries.en: When the Khitan large script was created, Tulubu contributed more than anyone else to bringing it to completion.
entries.literal: When the Khitan large script was devised, Tulubu contributed much to its completion.

entries.zh: 未幾，為文班林牙，領國子博士、知制誥。
entries.en: Before long he was made Linya of the Civil Class and concurrently served as Doctor of the National University and Drafter of Imperial Edicts.
entries.literal: Before long he became Linya of the Civil Class, and concurrently held the posts of Doctor of the National University and Drafter of Imperial Edicts.

entries.zh: 明年，受詔撰決獄法。
entries.en: The following year he received an edict to draft the law on judicial decisions.
entries.literal: The next year he received an edict to compile the law on deciding cases.

entries.zh: 太祖略燕，詔與皇太子及王郁攻定州。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu overran Yan, he was ordered to attack Dingzhou with the heir apparent and Wang Yu.
entries.literal: When the Emperor Taizu overran Yan, he was ordered to attack Dingzhou together with the heir apparent and Wang Yu.

entries.zh: 師還至順州，幽州馬步軍指揮使王千率眾來襲，突呂不射其馬躓，擒之。
entries.en: On the army's return to Shunzhou, Wang Qian, commander of the Youzhou horse and foot forces, led a raid; Tulubu shot his horse from under him and took him prisoner.
entries.literal: On the army's return to Shunzhou, Wang Qian, commander of the Youzhou horse and foot forces, led troops to attack; Tulubu shot his horse so that it stumbled and captured him.

entries.zh: 天贊二年，皇子堯骨為大元帥，突呂不為副，既克平州，進軍燕、趙，攻下曲陽、北平。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianzan, Prince Yaogu served as grand marshal with Tulubu as his deputy; after taking Pingzhou they advanced into Yan and Zhao and captured Quyang and Beiping.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianzan, the prince Yaogu was Grand Marshal and Tulubu was his deputy; after they took Pingzhou they advanced into Yan and Zhao and captured Quyang and Beiping.

entries.zh: 至易州，易人來拒，逾濠而陣。
entries.en: At Yizhou the defenders came out to resist, forming their lines beyond the moat.
entries.literal: Reaching Yizhou, the people of Yi came out to resist and formed battle lines beyond the moat.

entries.zh: 李景章出降，言城中人無鬥志。
entries.en: Li Jingzhang came out to surrender and reported that the city had lost the will to fight.
entries.literal: Li Jingzhang came out to surrender and said the people in the city had no fighting spirit.

entries.zh: 大元帥將修攻具，突呂不諫曰：「我師遠來，人馬疲憊，勢不可久留。」
entries.en: The grand marshal was about to prepare siege engines when Tulubu remonstrated: "Our army has marched far; men and horses are exhausted—we cannot afford to linger."
entries.literal: The Grand Marshal was about to prepare siege engines; Tulubu remonstrated: "Our army has come from afar; men and horses are weary—the situation cannot allow a long stay."

entries.zh: 乃止。
entries.en: The assault was called off.
entries.literal: He then stopped.

entries.zh: 軍還，大元帥以其謀聞，太祖大悅，賜賚優渥。
entries.en: On the army's return the grand marshal reported his counsel to the throne; Emperor Taizu was greatly pleased and rewarded him lavishly.
entries.literal: When the army returned, the Grand Marshal reported his counsel; the Emperor Taizu was greatly pleased and bestowed generous rewards.

entries.zh: 車駕西征，突呂不與大元帥為先鋒，伐党項有功，太祖犒師水精山。
entries.en: On the western campaign Tulubu and the grand marshal led the vanguard; their attack on the Tanguts succeeded, and Emperor Taizu feasted the army at Crystal Mountain.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned west, Tulubu and the Grand Marshal served as vanguard; in attacking the Tanguts they had merit, and the Emperor Taizu feasted the army at Shuijing Mountain.

entries.zh: 大元帥東歸，突呂不留屯西南部，復討党項，多獲而還。
entries.en: When the grand marshal returned east, Tulubu remained to garrison the southwest, raided the Tanguts again, took many captives, and returned.
entries.literal: The Grand Marshal returned east; Tulubu remained to garrison the southwestern region, again attacked the Tanguts, took many captives, and returned.

entries.zh: 太祖東伐，大諲譔降而復叛，攻之，突呂不先登。
entries.en: On Emperor Taizu's eastern campaign, Dayinzan surrendered and then rebelled again; in the assault Tulubu was first over the wall.
entries.literal: When the Emperor Taizu campaigned east, Dayinzan surrendered then rebelled again; in the attack Tulubu was first to scale the walls.

entries.zh: 渤海平，承詔銘太祖功德於永興殿壁。
entries.en: After Bohai was pacified, he received an edict to inscribe Emperor Taizu's achievements on the walls of the Hall of Everlasting Prosperity.
entries.literal: When Bohai was pacified, he received an edict to inscribe the Emperor Taizu's merit on the walls of the Yongxing Hall.

entries.zh: 班師，已下州郡往往復叛，突呂不從大元帥攻破之。
entries.en: On the withdrawal many districts rebelled again; Tulubu followed the grand marshal in reducing them.
entries.literal: On the withdrawal, prefectures and districts below often rebelled again; Tulubu followed the Grand Marshal in reducing them.

entries.zh: 淳欽皇后稱制，有飛語中傷者，後怒，突呂不懼而亡。
entries.en: When Empress Chunqin assumed the regency, slanders reached her ears; enraged, she drove Tulubu to flee in fear.
entries.literal: When Empress Chunqin assumed regency, there were slanders that wounded him; the empress was angry, and Tulubu, in fear, fled.

entries.zh: 太宗知其無罪，召還。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong knew he was innocent and recalled him.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizong knew he was guiltless and summoned him back.

entries.zh: 天顯三年，討烏古部，俘獲甚眾。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianxian he attacked the Wugu tribe and took a great many captives.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianxian he attacked the Wugu tribe and took very many captives.

entries.zh: 伐唐，以突呂不為左翼，攻唐軍霞沙寨，降之。
entries.en: In the campaign against Tang he commanded the left wing, attacked the Tang garrison at Xiasha, and received its surrender.
entries.literal: In the campaign against Tang, Tulubu was made left wing; he attacked the Tang army's Xiasha stockade and received its surrender.

entries.zh: 十一年，送晉主石敬瑭入洛。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he escorted the Jin ruler Shi Jingtang into Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he escorted the Jin ruler Shi Jingtang into Luoyang.

entries.zh: 及大冊，突呂不總禮儀事，加特進檢校太尉。
entries.en: At the grand enthronement ceremony he oversaw all ritual affairs and was granted the ranks of Special Advancement and Acting Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: At the great investiture he oversaw ritual affairs in general and was given Special Advancement and Acting Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 會同五年卒。
entries.en: He died in the fifth year of Huitong.
entries.literal: He died in the fifth year of Huitong.

entries.zh: 王郁，京兆萬年人，唐義武軍節度使處直之孽子。
entries.en: Wang Yu, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, was the illegitimate son of Wang Chuzhi, military governor of the Yiwu Army under Tang.
entries.literal: Wang Yu, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, was the illegitimate son of Wang Chuzhi, Tang Military Governor of Yiwu Army.

entries.zh: 伯父處存鎮義武，卒，三軍推其子郜襲，處直為都知兵馬使。
entries.en: His uncle Chucun had governed Yiwu; when he died the army installed his son Gao as successor, with Chuzhi as director of military affairs.
entries.literal: His uncle Chucun held Yiwu; when he died the three armies installed his son Gao as successor, and Chuzhi became Director of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 光化三年，梁王朱全忠攻定州，郜遣處直拒於沙河。
entries.en: In the third year of Guanghua, Zhu Quanzhong of Liang attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist him at Shahe.
entries.literal: In the third year of Guanghua, Liang King Zhu Quanzhong attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist at Shahe.

entries.zh: 兵敗，入城逐郜，郜奔太原。
entries.en: Defeated in battle, they entered the city and drove Gao out; he fled to Taiyuan.
entries.literal: The army was defeated; they entered the city and drove out Gao, and Gao fled to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 亂兵推處直為留後，遣人請事梁王。
entries.en: The mutineers installed Chuzhi as acting governor and sent envoys to submit to the Liang court.
entries.literal: The mutinous troops installed Chuzhi as acting governor and sent men to request allegiance to the Liang king.

entries.zh: 梁與晉王克用絕好，表處直為義武軍節度使。
entries.en: Liang broke with Li Keyong of Jin and memorialized Chuzhi as military governor of the Yiwu Army.
entries.literal: Liang broke relations with Jin Prince Li Keyong and memorialized Chuzhi as Military Governor of Yiwu Army.

entries.zh: 初，郜之亡也，郁從之。
entries.en: When Gao first fled, Yu went with him.
entries.literal: At first, when Gao fled, Yu followed him.

entries.zh: 晉王克用妻以女，用為新州防禦使。
entries.en: Li Keyong of Jin gave him his daughter in marriage and appointed him defender of Xinzhou.
entries.literal: Jin Prince Li Keyong gave him his daughter in marriage and employed him as Defender of Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 處直料晉必討張文禮，鎮亡，則定不獨存，益自疑。
entries.en: Chuzhi reckoned that Jin would surely move against Zhang Wenli; if the commandery fell, Dingzhou could not survive on its own, and his suspicions deepened.
entries.literal: Chuzhi reckoned that Jin would surely punish Zhang Wenli; if the commandery perished, Dingzhou could not stand alone, and he grew ever more suspicious.

entries.zh: 陰使郁北導契丹入塞，以牽晉兵，且許為嗣。
entries.en: He secretly sent Yu north to guide the Khitan across the border and tie down Jin's forces, promising him the succession as well.
entries.literal: He secretly sent Yu north to guide the Khitan into the passes, to tie down Jin's army, and also promised him the succession.

entries.zh: 郁自奔晉，常恐失父心，得使，大喜。
entries.en: Yu had fled to Jin and constantly feared he had lost his father's favor; when this mission came he was overjoyed.
entries.literal: Yu had himself fled to Jin and constantly feared losing his father's favor; when he received this mission he was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 神冊六年，奉表送款，舉室來降，太祖以為養子。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Shence he submitted a memorial of allegiance and came over with his entire household; Emperor Taizu adopted him as a son.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Shence he submitted a memorial offering allegiance; his whole household came to surrender, and the Emperor Taizu took him as an adopted son.

entries.zh: 未幾，郁兄都囚父，自為留後，帝遣郁從皇太子討之。
entries.en: Before long Yu's elder brother Du imprisoned their father and made himself acting governor; the emperor sent Yu with the heir apparent to punish him.
entries.literal: Before long Yu's elder brother Du imprisoned their father and installed himself as acting governor; the emperor sent Yu to follow the heir apparent in punishing him.

entries.zh: 至定州，都堅壁不出，掠居民而還。
entries.en: At Dingzhou, Du held the walls and refused to come out; they plundered the countryside and withdrew.
entries.literal: Reaching Dingzhou, Du held fast behind the walls and would not come out; they plundered the inhabitants and returned.

entries.zh: 明年，從皇太子攻鎮州，遇唐兵於定州，破之。
entries.en: The following year he followed the heir apparent against Zhenzhou, met Tang forces at Dingzhou, and routed them.
entries.literal: The next year he followed the heir apparent in attacking Zhenzhou; they met Tang troops at Dingzhou and defeated them.

entries.zh: 天贊二年秋，郁及阿古只略地燕、趙，攻下磁窯務。
entries.en: In the autumn of the second year of Tianzan, Yu and Aguzhi raided Yan and Zhao and captured Ciyaowu.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Tianzan, Yu and Aguzhi overran the lands of Yan and Zhao and took Ciyaowu.

entries.zh: 從太祖平渤海，戰有功，加同政事門下平章事，改崇義軍節度使。
entries.en: He followed Emperor Taizu in pacifying Bohai, distinguished himself in battle, was made associate director of the Secretariat with the rank of grand councilor, and was then appointed military governor of the Chongyi Army.
entries.literal: Following the Emperor Taizu in pacifying Bohai, he had merit in battle and was made Associate Director of the Secretariat with the rank of Grand Councilor, then transferred to Military Governor of Chongyi Army.

entries.zh: 太祖崩，郁與妻會葬，其妻泣訴於淳欽皇后，求歸鄉國，許之。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu died, Yu and his wife attended the funeral; his wife wept before Empress Chunqin and begged to return home, and the empress granted her request.
entries.literal: When the Emperor Taizu died, Yu and his wife attended the funeral; his wife wept and appealed to Empress Chunqin, asking to return to their native land, and permission was granted.

entries.zh: 郁奏曰：「臣本唐主之婿，主已被弒，此行夫妻豈能相保？
entries.en: Yu submitted a memorial: "I was once the son-in-law of a Tang ruler; my lord has already been murdered—on this journey how can my wife and I keep each other safe?
entries.literal: Yu memorialized: "This subject was originally the son-in-law of the Tang ruler; my lord has already been assassinated—on this journey how can husband and wife protect each other?

entries.zh: 願常侍太后。」
entries.en: I beg to remain in constant attendance upon the empress dowager."
entries.literal: I wish to attend the empress dowager constantly."

entries.zh: 後喜曰：「漢人中，惟王郎最忠孝。」
entries.en: The empress was delighted: "Among the Han, none is more loyal and filial than Lord Wang."
entries.literal: The empress rejoiced: "Among the Han, only Lord Wang is most loyal and filial."

entries.zh: 以太祖嘗與李克用約為兄弟故也。
entries.en: This was because Emperor Taizu had once sworn brotherhood with Li Keyong.
entries.literal: This was because the Emperor Taizu had once sworn brotherhood with Li Keyong.

entries.zh: 尋加政事令。
entries.en: Before long he was additionally appointed director of government affairs.
entries.literal: Before long he was additionally made Director of Government Affairs.

entries.zh: 還宜州，卒。
entries.en: He returned to Yizhou, where he died.
entries.literal: He returned to Yizhou and died.

entries.zh: 耶律覿烈
entries.en: Yelu Dilie
entries.literal: Yelu Dilie

entries.en: (Yuzhi)
entries.literal: (Yuzhi)

entries.zh: 耶律鐸臻
entries.en: Yelu Duozhen
entries.literal: Yelu Duozhen

entries.zh: 〈（古突呂不）〉
entries.en: (Gu and Tulubu)
entries.literal: (Gu and Tulubu)

entries.zh: 王郁耶律圖魯窘
entries.en: Wang Yu; Yelu Tulujiong
entries.literal: Wang Yu; Yelu Tulujiong

entries.zh: 耶律魯不古，字信寧，太祖從侄也。
entries.en: Yelu Lubugu, whose courtesy name was Xinning, was a paternal cousin of Emperor Taizu.
entries.literal: Yelu Lubugu, courtesy name Xinning, was a younger cousin of Taizu on the father's side.

entries.zh: 初，太祖制契丹國字，魯不古以贊成功，授林牙、監修國史。
entries.en: When Taizu first devised the Khitan national script, Lubugu helped bring the project to completion and was appointed linya and supervisor of the national history.
entries.literal: At first, when Taizu devised the Khitan national script, Lubugu assisted in completing the work and was appointed linya and supervisor of compiling the national history.

entries.zh: 後率偏師，為西南邊大詳穩，從伐党項有功。
entries.en: Later he led a detached force, became great xianwen on the southwestern frontier, and distinguished himself in campaigns against the Tangut.
entries.literal: Later he led a detached column, served as great xianwen of the southwestern frontier, and rendered merit in campaigns against the Tangut.

entries.zh: 會河東節度使石敬瑭為其主所討，遣人求援，魯不古導送於朝，如其請。
entries.en: When the Hedong military governor Shi Jingtang was attacked by his own ruler and sent envoys to seek help, Lubugu escorted them to court and the plea was granted as requested.
entries.literal: When Hedong military governor Shi Jingtang was attacked by his sovereign and sent men to seek aid, Lubugu guided the envoys to court and the request was granted as he asked.

entries.zh: 帝親率師往援，魯不古從擊唐將張敬達於太原北，敗之。
entries.en: The emperor led the army in person to relieve him; Lubugu joined the attack on the Tang general Zhang Jingda north of Taiyuan and routed him.
entries.literal: The emperor personally led the army to the rescue; Lubugu followed and struck the Tang general Zhang Jingda north of Taiyuan and defeated him.

entries.zh: 會同初，從討党項，俘獲最諸將，師還。
entries.en: Early in the Huitong era he took part in the campaign against the Tangut; among the generals his haul of prisoners was the greatest, and then the army returned.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he followed the campaign against the Tangut; his captives were the most among the generals, and the army returned.

entries.zh: 天祿中，拜於越。
entries.en: During the Tianlu era he was made yuyue.
entries.literal: During the Tianlu era he was appointed yuyue.

entries.zh: 六年，為北院大王。
entries.en: In the sixth year he became Great King of the Northern Court.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he became Great King of the Northern Court.

entries.zh: 終年五十五。
entries.en: He died at the age of fifty-five.
entries.literal: He died at the age of fifty-five.

entries.zh: 趙延壽，本姓劉，恒山人。
entries.en: Zhao Yanshou, whose original surname was Liu, came from Hengshan.
entries.literal: Zhao Yanshou, original surname Liu, was a man of Hengshan.

entries.zh: 父邟，令蓚。
entries.en: His father Kuai had been magistrate of Tiao.
entries.literal: His father Kuai was magistrate of Tiao.

entries.zh: 梁開平初，滄州節度使劉守文陷蓚，其稗將趙德鈞獲延壽，養以為子。
entries.en: Early in the Liang Kaiping era, when Cangzhou military governor Liu Shouwen seized Shuo, his lieutenant Zhao Dejun captured Yanshou and adopted him as a son.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping of Liang, Cangzhou military governor Liu Shouwen took Shuo; his subordinate general Zhao Dejun captured Yanshou and raised him as a son.

entries.zh: 少美容貌，好書史。
entries.en: As a youth he was handsome and loved books and history.
entries.literal: In youth he was handsome in appearance and fond of books and history.

entries.zh: 唐明宗先以女妻之，及即位，封其女為興平公主，拜延壽駙馬都尉、樞密使。
entries.en: Emperor Mingzong of Tang had already married a daughter to him; when he came to the throne he enfeoffed her as Princess of Xingping and appointed Yanshou imperial son-in-law commandant and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: Tang Emperor Mingzong had first given him a daughter in marriage; when he took the throne he enfeoffed the daughter as Princess of Xingping and appointed Yanshou imperial son-in-law commandant and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 明宗子從榮恃權跋扈，內外莫不震懾，延壽求補外避之，出為宣武軍節度使。
entries.en: Mingzong's son Congrong wielded power arrogantly, and everyone inside and outside the court trembled before him; Yanshou asked for a provincial post to keep clear of him and was sent out as military governor of the Xuanwu army.
entries.literal: Mingzong's son Congrong relied on power and was overbearing; within and without none were not awed in fear; Yanshou sought an outside appointment to avoid him and went out as military governor of the Xuanwu army.

entries.zh: 清泰初，加魯國公，復為樞密使，鎮許州。
entries.en: Early in the Qingtai era he was made Duke of Lu, again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and took charge at Xu Prefecture.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made Duke of Lu, again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and garrisoned Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 石敬瑭發兵太原，唐遣張敬達往討。
entries.en: When Shi Jingtang raised an army at Taiyuan, Tang dispatched Zhang Jingda to suppress him.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang raised troops at Taiyuan; Tang sent Zhang Jingda to attack him.

entries.zh: 會敬達敗保晉安寨，延壽與德鈞往救，聞晉安已破，走團柏峪。
entries.en: When Jingda was beaten back and held Jin'an stockade, Yanshou and Dejun marched to relieve him; learning that Jin'an had already fallen, they fled to Tuanbai Valley.
entries.literal: When Jingda was defeated and held Jin'an stockade, Yanshou and Dejun went to the rescue; hearing that Jin'an had already fallen, they fled to Tuanbai Valley.

entries.zh: 太宗追及，延壽與其父俱降。
entries.en: Taizong caught up with them, and Yanshou and his father both surrendered.
entries.literal: Taizong overtook them; Yanshou and his father both surrendered.

entries.zh: 明年，德鈞卒，以延壽為幽州節度使，封燕王。
entries.en: The following year Dejun died; Yanshou was appointed military governor of Youzhou and enfeoffed as King of Yan.
entries.literal: The next year Dejun died; Yanshou was made military governor of Youzhou and enfeoffed as King of Yan.

entries.zh: 及改幽州為南京，遷留守，總山南事。
entries.en: When Youzhou was redesignated the Southern Capital, he was moved to regent there with overall authority over affairs south of the mountains.
entries.literal: When Youzhou was renamed the Southern Capital, he was transferred to be regent there and given overall charge of affairs south of the mountains.

entries.zh: 天顯末，以延壽妻在晉，詔取之以歸。
entries.en: Late in the Tianxian era, because Yanshou's wife was still in Jin territory, an edict was issued to fetch her and bring her home.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianxian, because Yanshou's wife was in Jin, an edict ordered that she be brought back.

entries.zh: 自是益自激昂圖報。
entries.en: From that time on he burned all the more fiercely to repay the favor.
entries.literal: From then on he became all the more ardent in plotting repayment.

entries.zh: 會同初，帝幸其第，加政事令。
entries.en: Early in the Huitong era the emperor visited his home and further appointed him chief of governmental affairs.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong the emperor visited his residence and additionally made him chief of governmental affairs.

entries.zh: 六年冬，晉人背盟，帝親征，延壽為先鋒，下貝州，授魏、博等州節度使，封魏王。
entries.en: In the winter of the sixth year, when Jin broke the alliance, the emperor marched in person with Yanshou as vanguard; he captured Beizhou, was appointed military governor of Wei, Bo, and other prefectures, and was enfeoffed as King of Wei.
entries.literal: In the winter of the sixth year the Jin broke the covenant; the emperor campaigned in person, Yanshou served as vanguard, took Beizhou, was made military governor of Wei, Bo, and other prefectures, and enfeoffed as King of Wei.

entries.zh: 敗晉軍於南樂，獲其將賽項羽。
entries.en: He routed the Jin army at Nanle and took their general Sai Xiangyu prisoner.
entries.literal: He defeated the Jin army at Nanle and captured their general Sai Xiangyu.

entries.zh: 軍元城，晉將李守貞、高行周率兵來逆，破之。
entries.en: When the army was at Yuancheng, the Jin generals Li Shouzhen and Gao Xingzhou came out to meet him with their forces, and he put them to rout.
entries.literal: The army was at Yuancheng; the Jin generals Li Shouzhen and Gao Xingzhou led troops to oppose him, and he defeated them.

entries.zh: 至頓丘，會大霖雨，帝欲班師，延壽諫曰：「晉軍屯河濱，不敢出戰，若徑入澶州，奪其橋，則晉不足平。」
entries.en: At Dunqiu a great downpour struck, and the emperor wanted to withdraw. Yanshou urged him, saying, "The Jin forces are camped on the river and dare not come out; if we press straight into Chanzhou and seize their bridge, Jin will not be hard to subdue."
entries.literal: At Dunqiu they encountered heavy rains; the emperor wished to withdraw the army. Yanshou remonstrated, saying, "The Jin army is encamped on the riverbank and dares not come out to fight; if we go straight into Chanzhou and seize its bridge, then Jin will not be hard to pacify."

entries.zh: 上然之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The sovereign approved this.

entries.zh: 適晉軍先歸澶州，高行周至析城，延壽將輕兵逆戰；
entries.en: By then the Jin army had already fallen back to Chanzhou; when Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, Yanshou led light troops out to give battle;
entries.literal: Just then the Jin army had already returned to Chanzhou; Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, and Yanshou led light troops to meet them in battle;

entries.zh: 上親督騎士突其陣，敵遂潰。
entries.en: the emperor personally directed the cavalry in a charge through their lines, and the enemy broke and fled.
entries.literal: the sovereign personally directed the horsemen in a charge through their formation, and the enemy then broke and fled.

entries.zh: 師還，留延壽徇貝、冀、深三州。
entries.en: On the army's return, Yanshou was left behind to bring the three prefectures of Bei, Ji, and Shen to heel.
entries.literal: When the army returned, Yanshou was left to pacify the three prefectures of Bei, Ji, and Shen.

entries.zh: 八年，再伐晉，晉主遣延壽族人趙行實以書來招。
entries.en: In the eighth year the army marched against Jin again; the Jin ruler sent Yanshou's kinsman Zhao Xingshi with a letter inviting him to defect.
entries.literal: In the eighth year they campaigned against Jin again; the Jin sovereign sent Yanshou's clansman Zhao Xingshi with a letter to entice him.

entries.zh: 時晉人堅壁不出，延壽紿曰：「我陷虜久，寧忘父母之邦？
entries.en: The Jin were holding their walls and refusing battle; Yanshou deceived them, saying, "I have been a captive so long—could I forget the land of my fathers?
entries.literal: At the time the Jin held their walls and would not come out; Yanshou deceived them, saying, "I have long been trapped among the captors—how could I forget the land of my parents?

entries.zh: 若以軍逆，我即歸。」
entries.en: Send an army to meet me and I will come home at once."
entries.literal: If you come out with an army to meet me, I will return at once."

entries.zh: 晉人以為然，遣杜重威率兵迎之。
entries.en: The Jin took him at his word and sent Du Chongwei with an army to welcome him.
entries.literal: The Jin believed this and sent Du Chongwei to lead troops to welcome him.

entries.zh: 延壽至滹沱河，據中渡橋，與晉軍力戰，手殺其將王清，兩軍相拒。
entries.en: Yanshou reached the Hutuo River, seized the Zhongdu Bridge, and fought the Jin army fiercely; he killed their general Wang Qing with his own hand, and the two armies remained locked in stalemate.
entries.literal: Yanshou reached the Hutuo River, held the Zhongdu Bridge, and fought the Jin army fiercely; with his own hand he killed their general Wang Qing, and the two armies stood locked against each other.

entries.zh: 太宗潛由他渡濟，留延壽與耶律朔古據橋，敵不能奪，屢敗之，杜重威掃厥眾降。
entries.en: Taizong secretly crossed at another ford, leaving Yanshou and Yelu Shuogu to hold the bridge; the enemy could not take it, and after repeated defeats Du Chongwei surrendered with his entire force.
entries.literal: Taizong secretly crossed by another ford; he left Yanshou and Yelu Shuogu to hold the bridge; the enemy could not seize it, and they repeatedly defeated them until Du Chongwei swept away his whole host and surrendered.

entries.zh: 上喜，賜延壽龍鳳赭袍，且曰：「漢兵皆爾所有，爾宜親往撫慰。」
entries.en: The emperor was delighted, gave Yanshou a dragon-and-phoenix ochre robe, and said, "All these Han soldiers are yours now; you should go in person to reassure them."
entries.literal: The sovereign rejoiced, bestowed on Yanshou a dragon-and-phoenix ochre robe, and said, "All the Han troops are yours; you should go in person to comfort them."

entries.zh: 延壽至營，杜重威、李守貞迎謁馬首。
entries.en: When Yanshou reached the camp, Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen came out to pay their respects at his stirrup.
entries.literal: When Yanshou reached the camp, Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen came out to greet him at his horse's head.

entries.zh: 高模翰，一名松，渤海人。
entries.en: Gao Mohan, who was also known as Song, came from Bohai.
entries.literal: Gao Mohan, also named Song, was a man of Bohai.

entries.zh: 有膂力，善騎射，好談兵。
entries.en: He was powerfully built, excelled at riding and archery, and loved to talk of military affairs.
entries.literal: He had great physical strength, was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and loved to discuss warfare.

entries.zh: 初，太祖平渤海，模翰避地高麗，王妻以女。
entries.en: When Taizu first pacified Bohai, Mohan fled to Goryeo, where the king gave him a daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: At first, when Taizu pacified Bohai, Mohan took refuge in Goryeo and the king gave him a daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 因罪亡歸。
entries.en: After committing an offense he fled back home.
entries.literal: Because of an offense he fled home.

entries.zh: 坐使酒殺人下獄，太祖知其才，貰之。
entries.en: He was jailed for killing a man while drunk; Taizu recognized his ability and pardoned him.
entries.literal: He was imprisoned for killing a man while drunk; Taizu knew his talent and pardoned him.

entries.zh: 天顯十一年七月，唐遣張敬達、楊光遠帥師五十萬攻太原，勢銳甚。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the eleventh year of Tianxian, Tang sent Zhang Jingda and Yang Guangyuan at the head of five hundred thousand men against Taiyuan; their advance was fierce.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year of Tianxian, Tang sent Zhang Jingda and Yang Guangyuan to command five hundred thousand troops in an attack on Taiyuan; their momentum was very sharp.

entries.zh: 石敬瑭遣人求救，太宗許之。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang sent envoys to beg for aid, and Taizong agreed.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang sent men to seek rescue; Taizong granted it.

entries.zh: 九月，征兵出雁門，模翰與敬達軍接戰，敗之，太原圍解。
entries.en: In the ninth month the army was levied and marched out through Yanmen Pass; Mohan engaged Jingda's force, routed it, and the siege of Taiyuan was raised.
entries.literal: In the ninth month troops were levied and marched out through Yanmen; Mohan joined battle with Jingda's army, defeated it, and the siege of Taiyuan was lifted.

entries.zh: 敬瑭夜出謁帝，約為父子。
entries.en: Jingtang came out by night to pay homage to the emperor and agreed to enter a father-and-son bond with him.
entries.literal: Jingtang came out by night to pay court to the emperor and agreed to become father and son.

entries.zh: 帝召模翰等賜以酒饌，親饗士卒，士氣益振。
entries.en: The emperor summoned Mohan and his fellows, gave them wine and food, and personally feasted the troops, and their spirit soared.
entries.literal: The emperor summoned Mohan and the others, bestowed wine and food, and personally feasted the soldiers; morale rose all the more.

entries.zh: 翌日，復戰，又敗之。
entries.en: The next day they fought again and routed them once more.
entries.literal: The next day they fought again and defeated them once more.

entries.zh: 敬達鼠竄晉安寨，模翰獻俘於帝。
entries.en: Jingda scurried like a rat into Jin'an stockade; Mohan presented prisoners to the emperor.
entries.literal: Jingda fled like a rat into Jin'an stockade; Mohan presented captives to the emperor.

entries.zh: 會敬瑭自立為晉帝，光遠斬敬達以降，諸州悉下。
entries.en: When Jingtang declared himself emperor of Jin, Guangyuan killed Jingda and surrendered, and every prefecture fell in line.
entries.literal: When Jingtang declared himself emperor of Jin, Guangyuan beheaded Jingda to surrender, and all the prefectures submitted.

entries.zh: 上諭模翰曰：「朕自起兵，百餘戰，卿功第一，雖古名將無以加。」
entries.en: The emperor told Mohan, "Since I first took up arms, through more than a hundred battles your merit has stood first; not even the great generals of antiquity could surpass it."
entries.literal: The sovereign addressed Mohan, saying, "Since I raised the army, in more than a hundred battles your achievement ranks first; even the famous generals of old cannot surpass it."

entries.zh: 乃授上將軍。
entries.en: He was then appointed General-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was then appointed General-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 會同元年，冊禮告成，宴百官及諸國使於二儀殿。
entries.en: In the first year of Huitong, when the enthronement rites were complete, he held a banquet for the officials and envoys of the various states in the Hall of the Two Principles.
entries.literal: In the first year of Huitong, when the investiture rites were completed, he feasted the hundred officials and envoys of the various states in the Hall of the Two Principles.

entries.zh: 帝指模翰曰：「此國之勇將，朕統一天下，斯人之力也。」
entries.en: The emperor pointed to Mohan and said, "Here is this state's bravest general; when I brought all under Heaven to heel, it was this man's doing."
entries.literal: The emperor pointed to Mohan and said, "This is the valiant general of the state; in my unification of all under Heaven, it is this man's strength."

entries.zh: 群臣皆稱萬歲。
entries.en: All the ministers shouted "Long live the emperor!"
entries.literal: All the ministers cried ten thousand years of life.

entries.zh: 及晉叛盟，出師南伐。
entries.en: When Jin broke the alliance, the army marched south on campaign.
entries.literal: When Jin broke the covenant, the army marched south in campaign.

entries.zh: 模翰為統軍副使，與僧遏前驅，拔赤城，破德、貝諸寨。
entries.en: Mohan served as deputy army commander; with Senge in the van he captured Chicheng and stormed the stockades at De, Bei, and elsewhere.
entries.literal: Mohan served as deputy commander of the army; with Senge as vanguard he took Chicheng and broke the stockades of De, Bei, and others.

entries.zh: 是冬，兼總左右鐵鷂子軍，下關南城邑數十。
entries.en: That winter he also took command of the left and right Iron Hawk regiments and captured several dozen walled towns south of the pass.
entries.literal: That winter he also took overall command of the left and right Iron Hawk units and reduced several tens of walled towns south of the pass.

entries.zh: 三月，敕虎官楊覃赴乾寧軍，為滄州節度使田武名所圍，模翰與趙延壽聚議往救。
entries.en: In the third month the tiger officer Yang Tan was dispatched to Qianning army, where Cangzhou military governor Tian Wuming besieged him; Mohan and Zhao Yanshou held council and set out to relieve him.
entries.literal: In the third month the tiger officer Yang Tan was sent to Qianning army but was besieged by Cangzhou military governor Tian Wuming; Mohan and Zhao Yanshou met in council to go to the rescue.

entries.zh: 俄有光自模翰目中出，縈繞旗矛，焰焰如流星久之。
entries.en: Suddenly a light shot from Mohan's eyes, wound around the flags and spears, and blazed like a meteor for a long time.
entries.literal: Suddenly a light issued from Mohan's eyes, coiled around flags and spears, and blazed like a meteor for a long while.

entries.zh: 模翰喜曰：「此天贊之祥！」
entries.en: Mohan rejoiced and said, "This is Heaven's blessing upon us!"
entries.literal: Mohan rejoiced and said, "This is an omen of Heaven's approval!"

entries.zh: 遂進兵，殺獲甚眾。
entries.en: He then pressed forward, killing and capturing a great host.
entries.literal: He then advanced the army and killed and captured in great numbers.

entries.zh: 以功加侍中。
entries.en: For his achievements he was further appointed Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: For his merit he was additionally made Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 略地鹽山，破饒安，晉人震怖，不敢接戰。
entries.en: He overran Yanshan, stormed Rao'an, and the Jin were so terrified they dared not give battle.
entries.literal: He overran the territory of Yanshan, broke Rao'an, and the Jin were shaken in terror and dared not join battle.

entries.zh: 加太傅。
entries.en: He was appointed Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: He was made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 晉以魏府節度使杜重威領兵三十萬來拒，模翰謂左右曰：「軍法在正不在多。
entries.en: Jin sent Wei prefecture military governor Du Chongwei with three hundred thousand men to oppose him; Mohan told his attendants, "The art of war rests on justice, not on numbers.
entries.literal: Jin sent Wei prefecture military governor Du Chongwei at the head of three hundred thousand troops to resist; Mohan said to those beside him, "The art of war lies in righteousness, not in numbers.

entries.zh: 以多陵少，不義必敗。
entries.en: To crush the few with the many is unjust and is bound to end in defeat.
entries.literal: To use the many to overwhelm the few is unjust and must end in defeat.

entries.zh: 其晉之謂乎！」
entries.en: Is that not exactly Jin's case!"
entries.literal: Is this not what is meant by Jin!"

entries.zh: 詰旦，以麾下三百人逆戰，殺其先鋒梁漢璋，餘兵敗走。
entries.en: At dawn the next day he met them with three hundred men under his command, killed their vanguard Liang Hanzhang, and the rest broke and fled.
entries.literal: At dawn the next day he met them in battle with three hundred men under his command, killed their vanguard Liang Hanzhang, and the rest of the troops were defeated and fled.

entries.zh: 手詔褒美，比漢之李陵。
entries.en: The emperor wrote him a personal edict of praise, comparing him to Li Ling of Han.
entries.literal: An imperial letter in the sovereign's own hand praised him and compared him to Li Ling of Han.

entries.zh: 頃之，杜重威等復至滹沱河，帝召模翰問計。
entries.en: Before long Du Chongwei and his force were again at the Hutuo River; the emperor summoned Mohan to ask his counsel.
entries.literal: Before long Du Chongwei and the others again reached the Hutuo River; the emperor summoned Mohan to ask his plan.

entries.zh: 上善其言曰：「諸將莫及此。」
entries.en: The emperor approved his plan and said, "None of the other generals can equal this."
entries.literal: The sovereign approved his counsel and said, "None of the generals can match this."

entries.zh: 乃令模翰守中渡橋。
entries.en: He then ordered Mohan to hold the Zhongdu Bridge.
entries.literal: He then ordered Mohan to hold the Zhongdu Bridge.

entries.zh: 及戰，復敗之，上曰：「朕憑高觀兩軍之勢，顧卿英銳無敵，如鷹逐雉兔。
entries.en: In the fighting they routed the enemy again; the emperor said, "From the heights I watched both armies; seeing how fierce and unmatched you were, it was like a hawk chasing pheasant and hare.
entries.literal: When battle was joined they defeated them again; the sovereign said, "I watched from a height the momentum of the two armies; looking at you, fierce and unrivaled, it was like a hawk pursuing pheasant and hare.

entries.zh: 當圖形麟閣，爵貤後裔。」
entries.en: Your portrait belongs in the Qilin Pavilion, and noble rank should descend to your heirs."
entries.literal: Your likeness should be painted in the Qilin Pavilion, and noble rank passed down to your descendants."

entries.zh: 已而杜重威等降。
entries.en: Before long Du Chongwei and his men surrendered.
entries.literal: Before long Du Chongwei and the others surrendered.

entries.zh: 車駕入汴，加特進檢校太師，封悊郡開國公，賜璽書、劍器。
entries.en: When the emperor entered Bian, Mohan was further made Special Advancement and Acting Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of the Ti Commandery state, and given an imperial letter and ceremonial sword.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Bian, Mohan was additionally made Special Advancement and Acting Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of the Ti Commandery state, and bestowed an imperial letter and sword regalia.

entries.zh: 為汴州巡檢使，平汜水諸山土賊，遷鎮中京。
entries.en: He served as inspection commissioner of Bianzhou, pacified the mountain bandits around Sishui, and was transferred to garrison the Central Capital.
entries.literal: He served as inspection commissioner of Bianzhou, pacified the mountain bandits of Sishui and the region, and was transferred to garrison the Central Capital.

entries.zh: 天祿二年，加開府儀同三司，賜對衣、鞍勒、名馬。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianlu he was further appointed Honored Companion with the Three Excellencies and given matching robes, saddle and bridle, and a fine horse.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianlu he was additionally made Honored Companion with the Three Excellencies and bestowed matching robes, saddle and bridle, and a famous horse.

entries.zh: 應歷初，召為中臺省右相。
entries.en: At the start of the Yingli era he was summoned to serve as Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yingli he was summoned to be Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 至東京，父老歡迎曰：「公起戎行，致身富貴，為鄉里榮，相如、買臣輩不足過也。」
entries.en: When he reached the Eastern Capital, the local elders welcomed him, saying, "You rose from the ranks to wealth and honor and have brought glory to our home—men like Sima Xiangru and Zhu Maichen are not your equal."
entries.literal: When he reached the Eastern Capital, the elders welcomed him, saying, "Sir, you rose from the army to attain wealth and rank, bringing glory to your home district—men like Xiangru and Maichen cannot surpass you."

entries.zh: 九年正月，遷左相，卒。
entries.en: In the first month of the ninth year he was moved to Left Chancellor and died.
entries.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he was transferred to Left Chancellor and died.

entries.zh: 耶律解裏，字潑單，突呂不部人，世為小吏。
entries.en: Yelu Jieli, whose courtesy name was Podan, came from the Tülübu tribe; his family had served as petty clerks for generations.
entries.literal: Yelu Jieli, courtesy name Podan, was a man of the Tülübu tribe; for generations his family had served as petty clerks.

entries.zh: 解裏早隸太宗麾下，擢為軍校。
entries.en: Jieli entered Emperor Taizong's service while still young and was promoted to army cadet.
entries.literal: Jieli entered Taizong's service early and was promoted to army cadet.

entries.zh: 天顯間，唐攻定州，既陷，解裏為唐兵所獲。
entries.en: During the Tianxian era, when Tang attacked Dingzhou and took it, Jieli was captured by the Tang army.
entries.literal: During the Tianxian era Tang attacked Dingzhou; after it fell, Jieli was captured by Tang troops.

entries.zh: 晉高祖立，始歸國。
entries.en: Only when Emperor Gaozu of Later Jin took the throne did he return home.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Jin ascended, he at last returned to his state.

entries.zh: 太宗貰其罪，拜御史大夫。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong pardoned his offense and appointed him Grand Censor.
entries.literal: Taizong remitted his offense and appointed him Grand Censor.

entries.zh: 會同九年伐晉，師次滹沱河，奪中渡橋，降其將杜重威。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Huitong, when the army marched against Jin, it halted at the Hutuo River, seized the Zhongdu Bridge, and forced the Jin general Du Chongwei to surrender.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Huitong they campaigned against Jin; the army halted at the Hutuo River, seized the Zhongdu Bridge, and compelled the surrender of the Jin general Du Chongwei.

entries.zh: 上命解裏與降將張彥澤率騎兵三千疾趨河南，所至無敢當其鋒。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Jieli and the surrendered general Zhang Yanze to lead three thousand horsemen in a swift drive into Henan; nowhere they went did anyone dare stand against their charge.
entries.literal: The sovereign ordered Jieli and the surrendered general Zhang Yanze to lead three thousand cavalry in a rapid advance into Henan; wherever they went none dared confront their edge.

entries.zh: 既入汴，解裏等遷晉主重貴於開封府。
entries.en: Once they had entered Bian, Jieli and his party relocated the Jin emperor Chonggui to Kaifeng prefecture.
entries.literal: After entering Bian, Jieli and the others moved the Jin sovereign Chonggui to Kaifeng prefecture.

entries.zh: 彥澤恣殺掠，亂宮掖，解裏不能禁，百姓騷然，莫不怨憤。
entries.en: Yanze killed and plundered at will and threw the inner palace into chaos; Jieli could not stop him, the people were in an uproar, and everyone seethed with resentment.
entries.literal: Yanze wantonly killed and plundered and threw the palace quarters into disorder; Jieli could not restrain him, the common people were in uproar, and none did not resent it in fury.

entries.zh: 車駕至京，數彥澤罪，斬於市，汴人大悅。
entries.en: When the emperor reached the capital, he recounted Yanze's crimes and had him beheaded in the marketplace, to the great joy of the people of Bian.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage reached the capital, the emperor enumerated Yanze's crimes and executed him in the marketplace; the people of Bian were greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 解裏亦被詰責，尋釋之。
entries.en: Jieli was questioned and rebuked as well, but was soon released.
entries.literal: Jieli was also interrogated and rebuked, but was released shortly thereafter.

entries.zh: 天祿間，加守太子太傅。
entries.en: During the Tianlu era he was further appointed Guardian of the Heir Apparent Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: During the Tianlu era he was additionally made Guardian of the Heir Apparent Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 應歷初，置本部令穩，解裏世其職，卒。
entries.en: At the start of the Yingli era the post of tribal chief wen of the department was created; Jieli held it as a hereditary office in his line and then died.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yingli the post of tribal chief wen of the department was established; Jieli inherited the office in his family line and died.

entries.zh: 趙思溫，字文美，盧龍人。
entries.en: Zhao Siwen, whose courtesy name was Wenmei, came from Lulong.
entries.literal: Zhao Siwen, courtesy name Wenmei, was a man of Lulong.

entries.zh: 少果銳，膂力兼人，隸燕帥劉仁恭幕。
entries.en: As a youth he was bold and keen, possessed the strength of several men, and served on the staff of the Yan commander Liu Rengong.
entries.literal: In youth he was resolute and sharp, his strength the equal of several men, and he served on the staff of Yan commander Liu Rengong.

entries.zh: 李存勖問罪於燕，思溫統偏師拒之。
entries.en: When Li Cunxu marched against Yan, Siwen led a detached force to hold him off.
entries.literal: Li Cunxu called Yan to account; Siwen commanded a detached force to resist him.

entries.zh: 流矢中目，裂裳漬血，戰猶不已。
entries.en: A stray arrow struck his eye; he tore his robe to staunch the blood and still would not stop fighting.
entries.literal: A stray arrow struck his eye; he tore his robe to soak the blood and still did not cease fighting.

entries.zh: 為存勖將周德威所擒，存勖壯而釋其縛。
entries.en: Cunxu's general Zhou Dewei captured him; impressed by his spirit, Cunxu had his bonds cut.
entries.literal: He was captured by Cunxu's general Zhou Dewei; Cunxu admired his spirit and released his bonds.

entries.zh: 久之，日見信用。
entries.en: In time he won greater trust each day.
entries.literal: After a long while he came to be trusted day by day.

entries.zh: 與梁戰於莘縣，以驍勇聞，授平州刺史，兼平、營、薊三州都指揮使。
entries.en: He fought the Liang at Shen county and won fame for fierce courage; he was made prefect of Pingzhou and overall commander of Ping, Ying, and Ji.
entries.literal: He fought Liang at Shen county and became known for fierce valor; he was appointed prefect of Pingzhou and concurrently overall commander of Ping, Ying, and Ji prefectures.

entries.zh: 神冊二年，太祖遣大將經略燕地，思溫來降。
entries.en: In the second year of Shence, when Taizu sent a great general to take charge of the Yan region, Siwen came over to surrender.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shence, Taizu sent a great general to oversee the Yan region; Siwen came to surrender.

entries.zh: 及伐渤海，以思溫為漢軍都團練使，力戰，拔扶餘城。
entries.en: In the campaign against Bohai he was made overall regimental commissioner of the Han forces; he fought hard and captured Fuyu.
entries.literal: When they campaigned against Bohai, Siwen was made overall regimental commissioner of the Han army; he fought fiercely and took Fuyu city.

entries.zh: 身被數創，太祖親為調藥。
entries.en: He was wounded several times, and Taizu personally prepared medicine for him.
entries.literal: His body received several wounds; Taizu personally prepared medicine for him.

entries.zh: 太宗即位，以功擢檢校太保、保靜軍節度使。
entries.en: When Taizong came to the throne, Siwen was promoted for his achievements to Acting Grand Guardian and military governor of the Baojing army.
entries.literal: When Taizong took the throne, for his merit Siwen was promoted to Acting Grand Guardian and military governor of the Baojing army.

entries.zh: 天顯十一年，唐兵攻太原，石敬瑭遣使求救，上命思溫自嵐、憲間出兵援之。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Tianxian, when Tang attacked Taiyuan, Shi Jingtang sent envoys begging for aid; the emperor ordered Siwen to march out through Lan and Xian to relieve the city.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianxian, Tang troops attacked Taiyuan; Shi Jingtang sent envoys to seek rescue, and the sovereign ordered Siwen to march out between Lan and Xian to relieve him.

entries.zh: 既罷兵，改南京留守、盧龍軍節度使、管內觀察處置等使、開府儀同三司，兼侍中，賜協謀靜亂翊聖功臣，尋改臨海軍節度使。
entries.en: When the campaign ended he became regent of the Southern Capital, military governor of Lulong, commissioner for observation and disposition within the circuit, Honored Companion with the Three Excellencies, and concurrent Palace Attendant, and was granted the title Merit Lord Who Conspires in Counsel, Pacifies Disorder, and Assists the Sage; soon after he was transferred to military governor of the Linhai army.
entries.literal: After the army was dismissed, he was made regent of the Southern Capital, military governor of the Lulong army, commissioner for observation and disposition within the circuit, Honored Companion with the Three Excellencies, and concurrently Palace Attendant, and was granted the title of Merit Lord Who Conspires in Counsel, Pacifies Disorder, and Assists the Sage; shortly thereafter he was changed to military governor of the Linhai army.

entries.zh: 會同初，從耶律牒摐使晉行冊禮，還，加檢校太師。
entries.en: Early in the Huitong era he accompanied Yelu Diezeng to Jin on the investiture mission; on his return he was further appointed Acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he followed Yelu Diezeng as envoy to Jin to perform the investiture rites; on his return he was additionally made Acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 二年，有星隕於庭，卒。
entries.en: In the second year a meteor fell in his courtyard, and he died.
entries.literal: In the second year a star fell in his courtyard and he died.

entries.zh: 上遣使賻祭，贈太師、魏國公。
entries.en: The emperor sent envoys with funeral gifts and sacrifices and posthumously enfeoffed him Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wei.
entries.literal: The sovereign sent envoys with funeral gifts and sacrifices and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wei.

entries.zh: 子延照、延靖，官至使相。
entries.en: His sons Yanzhao and Yanjing both rose to the rank of commissioner-chancellor.
entries.literal: His sons Yanzhao and Yanjing rose to the rank of commissioner-chancellor.

entries.zh: 張礪，磁州人，初仕唐為掌書記，遷翰林學士。
entries.en: Zhang Li came from Cizhou; he first served Tang as a secretarial aide and was later promoted to Hanlin academician.
entries.literal: Zhang Li, a man of Cizhou, at first served Tang as secretarial aide and was promoted to Hanlin academician.

entries.zh: 會石敬瑭起兵，唐主以礪為招討判官，從趙德鈞援張敬達於河東。
entries.en: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the Tang ruler made Li judge on the pacification campaign and sent him with Zhao Dejun to relieve Zhang Jingda in Hedong.
entries.literal: When Shi Jingtang raised troops, the Tang sovereign made Li pacification campaign judge and had him follow Zhao Dejun to relieve Zhang Jingda in Hedong.

entries.zh: 及敬達敗，礪入契丹。
entries.en: After Jingda was defeated, Li went over to the Khitan.
entries.literal: When Jingda was defeated, Li entered Khitan territory.

entries.zh: 後太宗見礪剛直有文彩，擢翰林學士。
entries.en: Later Taizong saw that Li was upright and gifted with letters and appointed him Hanlin academician.
entries.literal: Later Taizong saw that Li was upright and possessed literary talent and promoted him to Hanlin academician.

entries.zh: 礪臨事必盡言，無所避，上益重之。
entries.en: In office Li always spoke his mind fully and held nothing back, and the emperor came to esteem him all the more.
entries.literal: In office Li always spoke his full mind without evasion, and the sovereign valued him all the more.

entries.zh: 未幾，謀亡歸，為追騎所獲。
entries.en: Before long he plotted to escape home and was caught by pursuing horsemen.
entries.literal: Before long he plotted to flee home and was captured by pursuing horsemen.

entries.zh: 上責曰：「汝何故亡？」
entries.en: The emperor rebuked him: "Why did you run away?"
entries.literal: The sovereign rebuked him, saying, "Why did you flee?"

entries.zh: 礪對曰：「臣不習北方土俗，飲食居處，意常郁郁，以是亡耳。」
entries.en: Li answered, "I am not used to northern ways of eating, drinking, and living; I have been miserable—that is why I fled."
entries.literal: Li replied, "Your servant is not accustomed to northern customs in food, drink, and dwelling; my mind is often depressed—that is why I fled."

entries.zh: 上顧通事高彥英曰：「朕嘗戒汝善遇此人，何乃使失所而亡？
entries.en: The emperor turned to the interpreter Gao Yanying and said, "I told you to treat this man well—how could you drive him to flee?
entries.literal: The sovereign turned to the interpreter Gao Yanying and said, "I once warned you to treat this man well—how could you let him lose his place and flee?

entries.zh: 礪去，可再得耶？」
entries.en: If Li were lost, could we ever get him back?"
entries.literal: If Li were gone, could he be obtained again?"

entries.zh: 遂杖彥英而謝礪。
entries.en: He had Yanying beaten and apologized to Li.
entries.literal: He then had Yanying beaten with the staff and apologized to Li.

entries.zh: 會同初，升翰林承旨，兼吏部尚書，從太宗伐晉。
entries.en: Early in Huitong he was promoted to Hanlin commissioner and concurrent Minister of Personnel, and accompanied Taizong on the campaign against Jin.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he was promoted to Hanlin commissioner and concurrently made Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and followed Taizong in the campaign against Jin.

entries.zh: 入汴，諸將蕭翰、耶律郎五、麻答輩肆殺掠，礪奏曰：「今大遼始得中國，宜以中國人治之，不可專用國人及左右近習。
entries.en: After entering Bian, generals such as Xiao Han, Yelu Langwu, and Mada killed and plundered at will; Li memorialized, "Great Liao has only just won China; it should be governed by Chinese, not entrusted solely to Khitan and personal favorites.
