entries.en: Such was the depth of his dedication.
entries.literal: Such was his concentration.

entries.zh: 會同初，登進士第，為盧龍巡捕官。
entries.en: In the early Huitong reign he earned the jinshi degree and was appointed a patrol officer in Lulong.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he passed the jinshi examination and became a patrol officer in Lulong.

entries.zh: 太宗入汴受冊禮，詔昉知制誥，總禮儀事。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong entered Bian to receive the investiture rites, Fang was appointed Director of Imperial Edicts with overall charge of ceremonial matters.
entries.literal: When Emperor Taizong entered Bian and received the investiture rites, Fang was ordered to serve as Director of Imperial Edicts and to oversee all ritual affairs.

entries.zh: 天祿中，為南京留守判官。
entries.en: During the Tianlu reign he served as registrar to the Nanjing retention commissioner.
entries.literal: During Tianlu he was registrar to the Nanjing retention commissioner.

entries.zh: 應歷間，累遷翰林學士，出入禁闥十餘年。
entries.en: In the Yingli period he rose through repeated promotions to Hanlin Academician and for more than ten years passed in and out of the inner palace.
entries.literal: During Yingli he was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academician and for more than ten years went in and out of the forbidden gates.

entries.zh: 保寧間，兼政事舍人，數延問古今治亂得失，奏對稱旨。
entries.en: Under Baoning he also held the post of Secretariat drafter; the emperor often called him in to discuss what had succeeded or failed in governance through the ages, and his answers always pleased the throne.
entries.literal: During Baoning he also served as Secretariat Drafter; the emperor often summoned him to inquire about the gains and losses of order and disorder in past and present, and his replies accorded with the imperial will.

entries.zh: 上多昉有理劇才，改南京副留守，決訟平允，人皆便之。
entries.en: The emperor admired Fang's gift for settling knotty legal disputes; he was made deputy Nanjing retention commissioner, where his judgments were fair and even-handed, to everyone's satisfaction.
entries.literal: The emperor praised Fang for his talent in deciding difficult cases; he was transferred to be deputy Nanjing retention commissioner, judged lawsuits fairly and impartially, and everyone found him convenient.

entries.zh: 遷工部尚書，尋改樞密副使，參知政事。
entries.en: He was promoted to Minister of Works, then shortly afterward made deputy commissioner of military affairs and participant in governance.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Works, then soon made Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs and Participant in Governance.

entries.zh: 頃之，拜樞密使，兼北府宰相，加同政事門下平章事。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed commissioner of military affairs and concurrent northern chancellery chancellor, with the added title of associate chief administrator under the Gate.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs, concurrently Northern Chancellery Chancellor, with the added title of Associate Chief Administrator under the Gate.

entries.zh: 乾亨初，監修國史。
entries.en: At the opening of the Qianheng reign he supervised compilation of the national history.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng he supervised compilation of the national history.

entries.zh: 統和元年，告老，不許。
entries.en: In the first year of Tonghe he asked to retire on account of age, but the request was denied.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tonghe he requested retirement on grounds of age, but was not permitted.

entries.zh: 進《尚書·無逸篇》以諫，太后聞而嘉獎。
entries.en: He submitted the "Against Dissipation" chapter of the Documents as a remonstrance; when the empress dowager heard of it, she praised him.
entries.literal: He presented the "Against Dissipation" chapter of the Documents to remonstrate; the empress dowager heard of it and commended him.

entries.zh: 二年秋，詔修諸嶺路，昉發民夫二十萬，一日畢功。
entries.en: That autumn in the second year, when an edict ordered repairs to the mountain passes, Fang drafted two hundred thousand laborers and finished the work in a single day.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year an edict ordered repair of the various mountain passes; Fang mobilized two hundred thousand laborers and completed the work in a single day.

entries.zh: 是時，昉與韓德讓、耶律斜軫相友善，同心輔政，整析蠹弊，知無不言，務在息民薄賦，以故法度修明，朝無異議。
entries.en: At this time Fang was close to Han Derang and Yelu Xiezhen; working in concert they helped govern the realm, rooted out entrenched abuses, and spoke frankly on every matter they knew; their aim was to give the people respite and lighten taxes, so that statutes were kept in good order and the court heard no dissent.
entries.literal: At this time Fang was on friendly terms with Han Derang and Yelu Xiezhen; together they assisted in government, sorted out corrupt abuses, and spoke out on whatever they knew; their aim was to give the people rest and lighten levies, and for this reason the laws were well ordered and the court had no dissenting voices.

entries.zh: 八年，復請致政。
entries.en: In the eighth year he again asked to retire from office.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he again requested to relinquish office.

entries.zh: 詔入朝免拜，賜几杖，太后遣閣門使李從訓持詔勞問，令常居南京，封鄭國公。
entries.en: He was ordered, when coming to court, to be excused from bowing and was granted a folding stool and staff; the empress dowager sent the gate commissioner Li Congxun with an edict to comfort and inquire after him, directed that he make his permanent home at Nanjing, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zheng.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that on entering court he be excused from bowing, and granted him a folding stool and staff; the empress dowager sent Gate Commissioner Li Congxun with an edict to comfort and inquire after him, ordered that he permanently reside at Nanjing, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zheng.

entries.zh: 初，晉國公主建佛寺於南京，上許賜額。
entries.en: Earlier the Princess of Jin had built a Buddhist temple at Nanjing, and the emperor had agreed to bestow an imperial inscription for its plaque.
entries.literal: Earlier the Princess of Jin had built a Buddhist temple at Nanjing, and the emperor had agreed to grant it an imperial plaque inscription.

entries.zh: 昉奏曰：「詔書悉罪無名寺院。
entries.en: Fang submitted a memorial saying, "Imperial edicts have condemned every unlicensed monastery.
entries.literal: Fang memorialized, saying: "Edicts have condemned in full all nameless monasteries.

entries.zh: 今以主請賜額，不惟違前詔，恐此風愈熾。」
entries.en: To grant a plaque now simply because the princess asks would not only violate those earlier orders but would, I fear, only fan this trend."
entries.literal: Now to grant a plaque inscription at the princess's request not only violates the earlier edict but I fear this practice will grow ever more rampant."

entries.zh: 上從之。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his view.
entries.literal: The emperor followed his advice.

entries.zh: 表進所撰《實錄》二十卷，手詔褒之，加政事令，賜帛六百匹。
entries.en: He presented in a memorial the twenty-scroll Veritable Records he had compiled; the emperor answered with a handwritten commendation, promoted him to chief administrator, and granted six hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: He presented in a memorial the twenty scrolls of the Veritable Records he had compiled; the emperor wrote a commendation in his own hand, added the title Chief Administrator, and granted six hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 九年，薦韓德讓自代，不從。
entries.en: In the ninth year he recommended Han Derang to succeed him, but the throne did not agree.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he recommended Han Derang to replace himself, but the request was not granted.

entries.zh: 上以昉年老苦寒，賜貂皮衾褥，許乘輦入朝。
entries.en: Seeing that Fang was old and suffering in the bitter cold, the emperor gave him a sable quilt and bedding and allowed him to come to court by palanquin.
entries.literal: Because Fang was old and the cold was bitter, the emperor granted him a sable fur quilt and mattress and permitted him to enter court by palanquin.

entries.zh: 病劇，遣翰林學士張幹就第授中京留守，加尚父。
entries.en: When his illness grew grave, the emperor sent the Hanlin academician Zhang Gan to his home to appoint him Zhongjing retention commissioner and add the honorific Father of the State.
entries.literal: When his illness grew severe, he sent Hanlin Academician Zhang Gan to his residence to appoint him Zhongjing retention commissioner and add the honorific Father of the State.

entries.zh: 卒，年七十五。
entries.en: He died at the age of seventy-five.
entries.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.

entries.zh: 上嗟悼，輟朝二日，贈尚書令。
entries.en: The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: The emperor sighed in grief, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 遺言戒厚葬。
entries.en: In his final instructions he warned against an extravagant funeral.
entries.literal: His testament warned against lavish burial.

entries.zh: 恐人譽過情，自誌其墓。
entries.en: Fearing that others would praise him beyond what was deserved, he composed his own tomb inscription.
entries.literal: Fearing that people would praise him beyond measure, he wrote his own tomb inscription.

entries.zh: 耶律阿沒裏，字蒲鄰，遙輦嘲古可汗之四世孫。
entries.en: Yelu Ameli, whose courtesy name was Pulian, was a fourth-generation descendant of the Yaolian khan Chaogu.
entries.literal: Yelu Ameli, courtesy name Pulian, was a fourth-generation descendant of the Yaolian Khan Chaogu.

entries.zh: 幼聰敏。
entries.en: Even as a boy he was quick-witted.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever.

entries.zh: 保寧中，為南院宣徽使。
entries.en: During Baoning he served as south chancellery commissioner of the palace directorate.
entries.literal: During Baoning he was South Chancellery Commissioner of the Palace Directorate.

entries.zh: 統和初，皇太后稱制，與耶律斜軫參預國論，為都統。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tonghe, when the empress dowager held the regency, he joined Yelu Xiezhen in deliberating on affairs of state and was made commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe the empress dowager held the regency; together with Yelu Xiezhen he participated in deliberations on state affairs and was made Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 以征高麗功，遷北院宣徽使，加政事令。
entries.en: For his services in the campaign against Goryeo he was promoted to north chancellery commissioner of the palace directorate and given the added title of chief administrator.
entries.literal: For merit in the campaign against Goryeo he was transferred to North Chancellery Commissioner of the Palace Directorate and added the title Chief Administrator.

entries.zh: 四年春，宋將曹彬、米信等侵燕，上親征，阿沒裏為都監，屢破敵軍。
entries.en: In the spring of the fourth year the Song generals Cao Bin, Mi Xin, and others invaded Yan; the emperor took the field in person, with Ameli as chief overseer, and repeatedly routed the enemy.
entries.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Song generals Cao Bin, Mi Xin, and others invaded Yan; the emperor campaigned in person, Ameli served as chief overseer, and repeatedly defeated the enemy armies.

entries.zh: 十二年，行在多盜，阿沒裏立禁捕法，盜始息。
entries.en: In the twelfth year theft was rampant at the mobile palace; Ameli instituted strict prohibition and arrest measures, and the thefts finally subsided.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year there were many thieves at the mobile palace; Ameli established prohibition and arrest regulations, and theft then ceased.

entries.zh: 先是，叛逆之家，兄弟不知情者亦連坐。
entries.en: Previously, in cases of treason, brothers who had known nothing of the plot were still punished by association.
entries.literal: Previously, in families of rebels, brothers who did not know of the crime were also punished by association.

entries.zh: 阿沒裏諫曰：「夫兄弟雖曰同胞，賦性各異，一行逆謀，雖不與知，輒坐以法，是刑及無罪也。
entries.en: Ameli remonstrated, saying, "Brothers may share the same womb, yet their natures differ; when one commits treason, to punish even those who knew nothing is to extend the law to the innocent.
entries.literal: Ameli remonstrated, saying: "Although brothers are called born of the same womb, their natures differ; when one commits treason, to punish by law even those who did not know is to extend punishment to the guiltless.

entries.zh: 自今雖同居兄弟，不知情者免連坐。」
entries.en: Henceforth, even among brothers living under the same roof, those who were ignorant of the crime shall be exempt from associated punishment."
entries.literal: From now on, even among brothers living together, those who did not know shall be exempt from associated punishment."

entries.zh: 太后嘉納，著為令。
entries.en: The empress dowager praised and accepted his advice, and it was written into law.
entries.literal: The empress dowager commended and accepted this, and it was written into regulation.

entries.zh: 致仕，卒。
entries.en: He retired from office and later died.
entries.literal: He retired from office and died.

entries.zh: 耶律賢適，字阿古真，於越魯不古之子。
entries.en: Yelu Xianshi, whose courtesy name was Aguzhen, was the son of the yuyue Lubugu.
entries.literal: Yelu Xianshi, courtesy name Aguzhen, was the son of Yuyue Lubugu.

entries.zh: 嗜學，有大志，滑稽玩世，人莫之知。
entries.en: He loved learning and harbored great ambitions, yet affected a witty, world-weary manner, and no one recognized his true capacity.
entries.literal: He loved learning and had great ambitions, yet was witty and playful with the world, so that no one knew his true worth.

entries.zh: 惟於越屋質器之，嘗謂人曰：「是人當國，天下幸甚。」
entries.en: Only the yuyue Wuzhi valued him and once said to others, "If this man should govern the realm, the world would be most fortunate."
entries.literal: Only the yuyue Wuzhi treasured him and once told others: "If this man holds the state, the realm will be greatly fortunate."

entries.zh: 應歷中，朝臣多以言獲譴，賢適樂於靜退，遊獵自娛，與親朋言不及時事。
entries.en: In the Yingli period many courtiers were punished for what they said; Xianshi took pleasure in quiet withdrawal, diverted himself with hunting, and in conversation with kin and friends never mentioned affairs of the day.
entries.literal: During Yingli many courtiers were punished for their words; Xianshi delighted in quiet retirement, amused himself with hunting, and in speaking with kin and friends never touched on current affairs.

entries.zh: 會討烏古還，擢右皮室詳穩。
entries.en: On returning from the campaign against the Wugu, he was promoted to detailed commissioner of the right pishi guard.
entries.literal: When he returned from campaigning against the Wugu, he was promoted to Right Pishi Detailed Commissioner.

entries.zh: 景宗在藩邸，常與韓匡嗣、女裏等遊，言或刺譏，賢適勸以宜早疏絕，由是穆宗終不見疑，賢適之力也。
entries.en: While Jingzong still lived in the princely residence he often went about with Han Kuangsi, Nuli, and others, and their talk sometimes turned cutting and satirical; Xianshi urged him to break off such ties early, and for this reason Muzong never came to suspect him—a service owed to Xianshi.
entries.literal: When Jingzong was at the princely residence he often went about with Han Kuangsi, Nuli, and others, and their talk sometimes included barbed mockery; Xianshi urged that they should sever ties early, and thereby Muzong never came to suspect him—it was Xianshi's doing.

entries.zh: 景宗立，以功加檢校太保，尋遙授寧江軍節度使，賜推忠協力功臣。
entries.en: When Jingzong ascended the throne, he was made acting grand guardian for his services, then soon given the remote appointment of military commissioner of the Ningjiang army and granted the title Merit of Loyal Cooperation.
entries.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, for merit he was given acting Grand Guardian, soon remotely appointed Military Commissioner of the Ningjiang Army, and granted the title Merit of Loyal Cooperation.

entries.zh: 時帝初踐阼，多疑諸王或萌非望，陰以賢適為腹心，加特進同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: The emperor had only just taken the throne and feared that some of the princes might harbor designs beyond their station; he secretly made Xianshi his trusted confidant and specially advanced him to grand mentor with concurrent rank as associate chief administrator of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor had just ascended and was suspicious that the princes might harbor improper ambitions; he secretly made Xianshi his confidant and specially advanced him to Grand Mentor with concurrent rank as Associate Chief Administrator of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 保寧二年秋，拜北院樞密使，兼侍中，賜保節功臣。
entries.en: In the autumn of the second year of Baoning he was appointed north chancellery commissioner of military affairs and concurrent palace attendant, and granted the title Merit of Protecting the Realm.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Baoning he was appointed North Chancellery Commissioner of Military Affairs, concurrently Palace Attendant, and granted the title Merit of Protecting the Realm.

entries.zh: 三年，為西北路兵馬都部署。
entries.en: In the third year he was made commander-in-chief of troops on the northwest route.
entries.literal: In the third year he became Commander-in-Chief of troops on the Northwest Route.

entries.zh: 賢適忠介膚敏，推誠待人，雖燕息不忘政務。
entries.en: Xianshi was loyal, upright, and keenly perceptive; he dealt with others in good faith and never set state affairs aside, even in moments of leisure.
entries.literal: Xianshi was loyal, upright, quick-witted, and sincere with people; even in repose he never forgot state affairs.

entries.zh: 以故百司首職，罔敢偷惰，累年滯獄悉決之。
entries.en: For this reason the heads of every office dared not slacken, and lawsuits that had languished for years were all brought to judgment.
entries.literal: For this reason the leading offices of every department dared not be lazy, and cases stalled for years were all decided.

entries.zh: 大丞相高勛、契丹行宮都部署女裏席寵放恣，及帝姨母、保母勢薰灼，一時納賂請謁，門若賈區。
entries.en: Grand Chancellor Gao Xun and the Khitan mobile-palace chief deployment Nuli basked in favor and gave free rein to their desires; together with the emperor's aunt and his nurses their power blazed so hot that for a time their gates, crowded with bribes and petitioners, seemed a marketplace.
entries.literal: Grand Chancellor Gao Xun and the Khitan mobile-palace chief deployment Nuli enjoyed favor and indulged in license; together with the emperor's aunt and nurses their influence blazed, and for a time those offering bribes and seeking audiences made their gates like a market quarter.

entries.zh: 賢適患之，言於帝，不報；
entries.en: Xianshi was troubled by this and spoke to the emperor, but received no answer;
entries.literal: Xianshi was distressed by this and spoke to the emperor, but received no response;

entries.zh: 以病解職，又不允，令鑄手印行事。
entries.en: he asked to resign on grounds of illness, but that too was refused, and he was ordered to have an official seal cast so that he might continue to transact business.
entries.literal: he sought release from office on grounds of illness, but again was not permitted and was ordered to cast an official seal to conduct affairs.

entries.zh: 乾亨初，疾篤，得請。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qianheng his illness became grave, and his request was finally granted.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng his illness grew severe and his request was granted.

entries.zh: 明年，封西平郡王，薨，年五十三。
entries.en: The following year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping and died at the age of fifty-three.
entries.literal: The next year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping and died at the age of fifty-three.

entries.zh: 子觀音，大同軍節度使。
entries.en: His son Guanyin became military commissioner of the Datong army.
entries.literal: His son Guanyin was Military Commissioner of the Datong Army.

entries.zh: 郭襲，不知何郡人。
entries.en: Guo Xi came from an unknown commandery.
entries.literal: Guo Xi—of what commandery he came is unknown.

entries.zh: 性端介，識治體。
entries.en: He was upright by nature and understood the fundamentals of good government.
entries.literal: His nature was upright and principled, and he understood the essentials of governance.

entries.zh: 久淹外調。
entries.en: For many years he languished in provincial appointments.
entries.literal: For a long time he was detained in outside assignments.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，召見，對稱旨，知可任以事，拜南院樞密使，尋加兼政事令。
entries.en: When Jingzong came to the throne, Xi was summoned to court; his answers pleased the emperor, who saw that he could be entrusted with serious business; he was appointed south chancellery commissioner of military affairs and soon given the concurrent title of chief administrator.
entries.literal: When Jingzong took the throne he was summoned for an audience; his replies accorded with the imperial will, and the emperor knew he could be entrusted with affairs; he was appointed South Chancellery Commissioner of Military Affairs and soon added the concurrent title Chief Administrator.

entries.zh: 以帝數遊獵，襲上書諫曰：「昔唐高祖好獵，蘇世長言不滿十旬未足為樂，高祖即日罷，史稱其美。
entries.en: Because the emperor went hunting so often, Xi submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, "In former times Emperor Gaozu of Tang was fond of the chase; when Su Shichang remarked that less than ten days could hardly count as pleasure, Gaozu gave it up that very day, and the historians praised him for it.
entries.literal: Because the emperor frequently went hunting, Xi submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "In former times Emperor Gaozu of Tang loved the hunt; Su Shichang said that less than ten days was not enough to count as pleasure, and Gaozu stopped the same day—history praises this.

entries.zh: 伏念聖祖創業艱難，修德布政，宵旰不懈。
entries.en: I reflect that our sacred founder built the realm through hardship, cultivated virtue, spread good government, and from dawn to dusk never slackened his efforts.
entries.literal: I reflect that the sacred ancestor founded the enterprise amid hardship, cultivated virtue and spread governance, and from dawn to dusk never slackened.

entries.zh: 穆宗逞無厭之欲，不恤國事，天下愁怨。
entries.en: Emperor Muzong gave free rein to insatiable desires and neglected the affairs of state, until the realm groaned with resentment.
entries.literal: Emperor Muzong indulged insatiable desires and did not care for state affairs, and the realm groaned in resentment.

entries.zh: 陛下繼統，海內翕然望中興之治。
entries.en: When Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, the realm as one looked to a restoration of good government.
entries.literal: When Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, within the seas all looked with one accord to a restoration of good government.

entries.zh: 十餘年間，征伐未已，而寇賊未弭；
entries.en: For more than ten years campaigns have not ceased, yet bandits and enemies remain unquelled;
entries.literal: For more than ten years campaigns have not ceased, yet bandits and enemies are not pacified;

entries.zh: 年谷雖登，而瘡痍未復。
entries.en: though the harvest has been good, the wounds of the land are not yet healed.
entries.literal: though the year's grain has been harvested, the wounds of the land are not yet healed.

entries.zh: 正宜戒懼修省，以懷永圖。
entries.en: This is precisely the time for vigilance, restraint, and self-examination, with a far-reaching design always in view.
entries.literal: This is precisely the time for vigilance, fear, and self-examination, keeping in mind a long-range design.

entries.zh: 側聞恣意遊獵，甚於往日。
entries.en: I have heard, moreover, that Your Majesty now indulges in hunting more freely than ever before.
entries.literal: I have heard on the side that Your Majesty indulges in hunting at will more than in former days.

entries.zh: 萬一有銜橛之變，搏噬之虞，悔將何及？
entries.en: Should there by any chance be an accident with the bridle or the risk of being torn by beasts, what regret could then avail?
entries.literal: If by any chance there should be an accident with the bit or the danger of mauling, what regret could avail?

entries.zh: 況南有強敵，伺隙而動，聞之得無生心乎？
entries.en: Moreover, a powerful enemy lies to the south, watching for an opening to strike; on hearing of this, would he not take heart?
entries.literal: Moreover, to the south there is a powerful enemy watching for an opening to move; on hearing of this, would he not take heart?

entries.zh: 伏望陛下節從禽酣飲之樂，為生靈社稷計，則有無疆之休。」
entries.en: I humbly beg Your Majesty to restrain the pleasures of the chase and deep drinking and act for the sake of the people and the altars of state; then blessing without limit will follow."
entries.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will restrain the pleasures of following game and deep drinking, and act for the sake of the people and the altars of state; then there will be boundless blessing."

entries.zh: 上覽而稱善，賜協贊功臣，拜武定軍節度使，卒。
entries.en: The emperor read the memorial and praised it, granted him the title Merit of Co-assisting, appointed him military commissioner of the Wuding army, and he later died.
entries.literal: The emperor read it and praised it, granted him the title Merit of Co-assisting, appointed him Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army, and he died.

entries.zh: 論曰：景宗之世，人望中興，豈其勤心庶績而然，蓋承穆宗醟虐之餘，為善易見；
entries.en: The historian remarks: In Jingzong's reign the people looked for a restoration of good government—was this because the emperor himself labored diligently at every task? Rather, coming after Muzong's dissipation and cruelty, even modest acts of goodness stood out plainly;
entries.literal: The discussion says: In the age of Jingzong people looked to a restoration—was it because he diligently attended to the myriad tasks? Rather, coming after the dissipation and cruelty of Muzong, doing good was easy to see;

entries.zh: 亦由群臣多賢，左右弼諧之力也。
entries.en: it was also because so many of his ministers were worthy men, and because of the supporting counsel of those at his side.
entries.literal: it was also because many ministers were worthy and the power of those at left and right who assisted and harmonized.

entries.zh: 室昉進《無逸》之篇，郭襲陳諫獵之疏，阿沒裏請免同氣之坐，所謂仁人之言，其利溥哉。
entries.en: Shi Fang presented the "Against Dissipation" chapter, Guo Xi submitted his memorial against excessive hunting, and Ameli asked that innocent brothers be spared associated punishment—these are what are called the words of humane men, whose benefit spreads far indeed.
entries.literal: Shi Fang presented the chapter "Against Dissipation," Guo Xi set forth the memorial remonstrating against the hunt, and Ameli requested exemption from associated punishment among those of the same breath—what are called the words of a humane man, whose benefit is far-reaching indeed.

entries.zh: 賢適忠介，亦近世之名臣。
entries.en: Xianshi, loyal and upright, ranks among the celebrated ministers of recent times as well.
entries.literal: Xianshi was loyal and upright and also a famous minister of recent times.

entries.zh: 女裏貪猥，後人所當取鑒者也。
entries.en: Nuli, greedy and base, is a man later generations ought to take as a warning.
entries.literal: Nuli was greedy and base—a man later generations ought to take as a warning.

entries.zh: 女裏，字涅烈袞，逸其氏族，補積慶宮人。
entries.en: Nuli, whose courtesy name was Nieliegün, came from a clan not recorded in the sources; he was appointed a palace attendant at Jiqing Palace.
entries.literal: Nuli, courtesy name Nieliegün; his clan is not recorded. He was made a palace attendant at Jiqing Palace.

entries.zh: 應歷初，為習馬小底，以母憂去。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Yingli reign he served as a junior horse-training attendant and left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yingli he served as a junior horse-training attendant and left office to mourn his mother.

entries.zh: 一日至雅伯山，見一巨人，惶懼走。
entries.en: One day he went to Mount Yabo, saw a giant, and fled in fear.
entries.literal: One day he came to Mount Yabo and saw a giant; frightened, he fled.

entries.zh: 巨人止之曰：「勿懼，我地祇也。
entries.en: The giant stopped him and said, "Do not fear; I am an earth spirit.
entries.literal: The giant stopped him and said: "Do not fear; I am an earth spirit.

entries.zh: 葬爾母於斯，當速詣闕，必貴。」
entries.en: Bury your mother here, go quickly to the court, and you are certain to rise to eminence."
entries.literal: Bury your mother here, and go quickly to the court—you are certain to rise to eminence."

entries.zh: 女裏從之，累遷馬群侍中。
entries.en: Nuli followed this counsel and rose through repeated promotions until he became Commissioner of Horse Herds.
entries.literal: Nuli followed this counsel and was repeatedly promoted, eventually becoming Commissioner of Horse Herds.

entries.zh: 時景宗在藩邸，以女裏出自本宮，待遇殊厚，女裏亦傾心結納。
entries.en: At that time Jingzong was still in the princely residence; because Nuli came from the same palace household, he was treated with exceptional favor, and Nuli in turn devoted himself and formed close ties with him.
entries.literal: At that time Jingzong was in the princely residence; because Nuli came from the same palace, he was treated with exceptional favor, and Nuli in turn devoted himself and formed close ties.

entries.zh: 及穆宗遇弒，女裏奔赴景宗。
entries.en: When Muzong was assassinated, Nuli rushed to Jingzong's side.
entries.literal: When Muzong was assassinated, Nuli hastened to Jingzong's side.

entries.zh: 是夜，集禁兵五百以衛。
entries.en: That night he gathered five hundred imperial guards to protect him.
entries.literal: That night he gathered five hundred forbidden troops to guard him.

entries.zh: 既即位，以翼戴功，加政事令、契丹行宮都部署，賞賚甚渥，尋加守太尉。
entries.en: After Jingzong took the throne, for his merit in supporting the enthronement Nuli was made chief administrator and chief deployment of the Khitan mobile palace; he was richly rewarded, and soon thereafter was further made Defender Grandee.
entries.literal: After Jingzong took the throne, for his merit in supporting the enthronement Nuli was made Chief Administrator and chief deployment of the Khitan mobile palace; he was richly rewarded, and soon thereafter was further made Defender Grandee.

entries.zh: 北漢主劉繼元聞女裏為上信任，遇其生日必致禮。
entries.en: The Northern Han ruler Liu Jiyuan, hearing that Nuli enjoyed the emperor's trust, invariably sent gifts on his birthday.
entries.literal: The Northern Han ruler Liu Jiyuan, hearing that Nuli enjoyed the emperor's trust, invariably sent gifts on his birthday.

entries.zh: 室昉耶律賢適女裏郭襲耶律阿沒裏
entries.en: Shi Fang, Yelu Xianshi, Nuli, Guo Xi, and Yelu Ameli.
entries.literal: Shi Fang, Yelu Xianshi, Nuli, Guo Xi, Yelu Ameli.

entries.zh: 張儉，宛平人，性端愨，不事外飾。
entries.en: Zhang Jian, a native of Wanping, was by nature upright and sincere and did not cultivate outward display.
entries.literal: Zhang Jian was a man of Wanping; his nature was upright and sincere, and he did not pursue outward adornment.

entries.zh: 統和十四年，舉進士第一，調雲州幕官。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year of Tonghe he placed first among jinshi graduates and was posted as a staff officer in Yun Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tonghe he took first place in the jinshi examination and was assigned as a staff officer in Yun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 故事，車駕經行，長吏當有所獻。
entries.en: By long-standing custom, whenever the imperial carriage passed through a region, the chief local official was expected to present a tribute.
entries.literal: By established precedent, when the imperial carriage passed through, the chief local official was obliged to present something.

entries.zh: 聖宗獵雲中，節度使進曰：「臣境無他產，惟幕僚張儉，一代之寶，願以為獻。」
entries.en: When Shengzong was hunting in Yunzhong, the military commissioner came forward and said, "My territory has no other notable product to offer; only my staff officer Zhang Jian, a treasure of his age — I wish to present him to Your Majesty."
entries.literal: When Shengzong hunted in Yunzhong, the military commissioner advanced and said: "Within my jurisdiction there is no other product; only my staff officer Zhang Jian, a treasure of a generation — I wish to present him."

entries.zh: 先是，上夢四人侍側，賜食人二口，至聞儉名，始悟。
entries.en: Earlier the Emperor had dreamed of four men standing at his side and of two mouths being given food; when he heard Jian's name, he understood the omen at last.
entries.literal: Earlier the Emperor had dreamed of four men attending at his side and of two mouths given food to eat; when he heard Jian's name, he understood at last.

entries.zh: 召見，容止樸野。
entries.en: When summoned to audience, his bearing and manner were plain and unadorned.
entries.literal: Summoned to audience, his bearing and manner were rustic and plain.

entries.zh: 訪及世務，占奏三十餘事。
entries.en: Questioned on affairs of the day, he presented memorials on more than thirty topics.
entries.literal: Asked about affairs of the age, he submitted advisories on more than thirty matters.

entries.zh: 由此顧遇特異，踐歷清華，號稱明幹。
entries.en: From this his favor was singular; he rose through the highest offices and was acclaimed as clear-sighted and capable.
entries.literal: From this his favor was exceptionally marked; he ascended through exalted offices and was acclaimed as clear-sighted and capable.

entries.zh: 開泰中，累遷同知樞密院事。
entries.en: During the Kaitai era he was repeatedly promoted to deputy director of the Commission for Military Affairs.
entries.literal: In the Kaitai era he was repeatedly promoted to deputy director of the Commission for Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 太平五年，出為武定軍節度使，移鎮大同。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Taiping he was appointed military commissioner of the Wuding Army and later transferred to command at Datong.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping he went out as military commissioner of the Wuding Army and was transferred to command at Datong.

entries.zh: 六年，入為南院樞密使。
entries.en: In the sixth year he returned to court as commissioner of the Southern Academy.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he entered court as Southern Academy commissioner.

entries.zh: 帝方眷倚，參知政事吳叔達與儉不相能，帝怒，出叔達為康州刺史，拜儉左丞相，封韓王。
entries.en: The Emperor was then leaning heavily on him; Participating State Counselor Wu Shuda could not work with Jian, and the Emperor in anger sent Shuda out as prefect of Kangzhou, appointed Jian left chief councilor, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Han.
entries.literal: The Emperor was just then relying on him heavily; Participating State Counselor Wu Shuda could not get along with Jian; the Emperor in anger sent Shuda out as prefect of Kangzhou, appointed Jian left chief councilor, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Han.

entries.zh: 帝不豫，受遺詔輔立太子，是為興宗，賜貞亮弘靖保義守節耆德功臣，拜太師、中書令，加尚父，徙王陳。
entries.en: When the Emperor fell ill, Jian received the deathbed edict to assist in establishing the heir, who became Xingzong; he was granted the title of meritorious minister of steadfast integrity and aged virtue, appointed Grand Preceptor and Secretariat Director, raised to Honored Father, and transferred to Prince of Chen.
entries.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, he received the final edict to assist in establishing the heir — this was Xingzong — and was granted the title of meritorious minister preserving loyalty and aged virtue; he was appointed Grand Preceptor and Secretariat Director, raised to Honored Father, and transferred to Prince of Chen.

entries.zh: 蕭樸，字延寧，國舅少父房之族。
entries.en: Xiao Pu, style name Yanning, belonged to the clan of the empress's father's younger branch.
entries.literal: Xiao Pu, style name Yanning, was of the clan of the empress's father's younger branch.

entries.zh: 父勞古，以善屬文為聖宗詩友。
entries.en: His father Laogu, skilled in literary composition, was Shengzong's companion in poetry.
entries.literal: His father Laogu, being skilled in literary composition, was Shengzong's companion in poetry.

entries.zh: 樸幼如老成人。
entries.en: As a boy, Pu was grave and mature like an old man.
entries.literal: Pu in youth was like a seasoned adult.

entries.zh: 及長，博學多智。
entries.en: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and full of resource.
entries.literal: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and full of wisdom.

entries.zh: 開泰初，補牌印郎君，為南院承旨，權知轉運事，尋改南面林牙。
entries.en: At the beginning of Kaitai he was appointed seal-and-plaque gentleman, served as director of the Southern Academy, was given acting charge of transport affairs, and soon was transferred to Southern Face linya.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaitai he was appointed seal-and-plaque gentleman, served as Southern Academy director, was given acting charge of transport affairs, and soon was transferred to Southern Face linya.

entries.zh: 帝問以政，樸具陳百姓疾苦，國用豐耗，帝悅曰：「吾得人矣！」
entries.en: The Emperor questioned him on government; Pu set forth in detail the people's hardships and whether state revenue was abundant or depleted; the Emperor said with pleasure, "I have found my man!"
entries.literal: The Emperor questioned him on government; Pu set forth in detail the people's hardships and whether state revenue was abundant or depleted; the Emperor said with pleasure: "I have found my man!"

entries.zh: 擢左夷離畢。
entries.en: He was promoted to left yilibi.
entries.literal: He was promoted to left yilibi.

entries.zh: 時蕭合卓為樞密使，樸知部署院事，以酒廢事，出為興國軍節度使，俄召為南面林牙。
entries.en: At the time Xiao Hezhuo was commissioner; Pu managed Deployment Court affairs; because drink caused him to neglect his duties, he was sent out as military commissioner of the Xingguo Army, but before long he was recalled as Southern Face linya.
entries.literal: At the time Xiao Hezhuo was commissioner; Pu managed Deployment Court affairs; because of wine he neglected his duties and was sent out as military commissioner of the Xingguo Army; before long he was recalled as Southern Face linya.

entries.zh: 太平三年，守太子太傅。
entries.en: In the third year of Taiping he served as guardian Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiping he served as guardian Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 明年，拜北府宰相，遷北院樞密使。
entries.en: The following year he was appointed chief councilor of the Northern Prefecture and promoted to commissioner of the Northern Academy.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed Northern Prefecture chief councilor and transferred to Northern Academy commissioner.

entries.zh: 時太平日久，帝留心翰墨，始畫譜牒以別嫡庶，由是爭訟紛起。
entries.en: Peace had then lasted long; the Emperor turned his attention to records and genealogy, and for the first time drew up registers to distinguish legitimate from secondary lines; from this lawsuits arose in profusion.
entries.literal: Peace had then lasted long; the Emperor turned his mind to brush and ink, and for the first time drew up genealogical registers to distinguish legitimate from secondary lines; from this lawsuits arose in profusion.

entries.zh: 樸有吏才，能知人主意，敷奏稱旨，朝議多取決之。
entries.en: Pu had administrative talent; he could grasp the ruler's intent; his presentations accorded with the Emperor's wishes; and court deliberations often followed his judgment.
entries.literal: Pu had talent for administration; he could grasp the ruler's intent; his presentations accorded with the Emperor's wishes; court deliberations often took his word as decisive.

entries.zh: 封蘭陵郡王，進王恒，加中書令。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling, advanced to Prince of Heng, and given the additional title of Secretariat Director.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling commandery, advanced to Prince of Heng, and given the additional title of Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 及大延琳叛，詔安撫東京，以便宜從事。
entries.en: When Da Yanlin rebelled, an edict ordered him to pacify the Eastern Capital, with authority to act at his discretion as circumstances required.
entries.literal: When Da Yanlin rebelled, an edict ordered him to pacify the Eastern Capital, acting at his discretion as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 興宗即位，皇太后稱制，國事一委弟孝先。
entries.en: When Xingzong took the throne, the Empress Dowager assumed regency and entrusted all state affairs to her younger brother Xiaoxian.
entries.literal: When Xingzong took the throne, the Empress Dowager assumed regency; state affairs were wholly entrusted to her younger brother Xiaoxian.

entries.zh: 方仁德皇后以馮家奴所誣被害，樸屢言其冤，不報。
entries.en: Empress Rendu had been destroyed through a false accusation by the Feng family slave; Pu repeatedly spoke of her injustice, but received no response.
entries.literal: Empress Rendu had been harmed through the false accusation of the Feng family slave; Pu repeatedly spoke of her injustice, but received no response.

entries.zh: 每念至此，為之嘔血。
entries.en: Whenever he thought of it, he would vomit blood in grief.
entries.literal: Whenever he thought of this, he vomited blood for her sake.

entries.zh: 重熙初，改王韓，拜東京留守。
entries.en: At the beginning of Chongxi he was transferred to Prince of Han and appointed garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi he was transferred to Prince of Han and appointed garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 及遷太后於慶州，樸徙王楚，升南院樞密使。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager was moved to Qing Prefecture, Pu was transferred to Prince of Chu and promoted to commissioner of the Southern Academy.
entries.literal: When the Empress Dowager was moved to Qing Prefecture, Pu was transferred to Prince of Chu and promoted to Southern Academy commissioner.

entries.zh: 四年，王魏。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was made Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was made Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 薨，年五十，贈齊王。
entries.en: He died, aged fifty, and was posthumously granted the title of Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: He died, aged fifty, and was posthumously granted Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 子鐸剌，國舅詳穩。
entries.en: His son Duola served as detailed inspector of the empress's kin.
entries.literal: His son Duola was a detailed inspector of the empress's kin.

entries.zh: 馬得臣，南京人，好學博古，善屬文，尤長於詩。
entries.en: Ma Dechen, a native of Nanjing, loved study and was broad in ancient learning; he was skilled in literary composition and especially accomplished in poetry.
entries.literal: Ma Dechen was a man of Nanjing; he loved study and was broad in ancient learning, skilled in literary composition, and especially accomplished in poetry.

entries.zh: 保寧間，累遷政事舍人、翰林學士，常預朝議，以正直稱。
entries.en: During Baoning he rose through repeated promotions to drafting academician for political affairs and Hanlin academician, regularly took part in court deliberations, and was acclaimed for uprightness.
entries.literal: During Baoning he was repeatedly promoted to drafting academician for political affairs and Hanlin academician, regularly took part in court deliberations, and was acclaimed for uprightness.

entries.zh: 乾亨初，宋師屢犯邊，命為南京副留守，復拜翰林學士承旨。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qianheng, when Song armies repeatedly violated the frontier, he was appointed deputy garrison commander of Nanjing and again invested as Hanlin academician director.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng, when Song armies repeatedly violated the frontier, he was appointed deputy garrison commander of Nanjing and again invested as Hanlin academician director.

entries.zh: 聖宗即位，皇太后稱制，兼侍讀學士。
entries.en: When Shengzong succeeded to the throne and the Empress Dowager assumed regency, he was additionally made attendant reader academician.
entries.literal: When Shengzong succeeded to the throne and the Empress Dowager assumed regency, he was additionally made attendant reader academician.

entries.zh: 上閱唐高祖、太宗、玄宗三《紀》，得臣乃錄其行事可法者進之。
entries.en: When the Emperor read the three annals of Tang Gaozu, Taizong, and Xuanzong, Dechen selected and presented their conduct worth emulating.
entries.literal: The Emperor read the three Annals of Tang Gaozu, Taizong, and Xuanzong; Dechen then selected and presented their conduct worth emulating.

entries.zh: 及扈從伐宋，進言降不可殺，亡不可追，二三其德者別議。
entries.en: When he followed the campaign against Song, he advised that those who surrendered should not be killed, fugitives should not be pursued, and those of divided loyalty should be discussed separately.
entries.literal: When he followed the campaign against Song, he advised that the surrendered should not be killed, the fugitive should not be pursued, and those of divided loyalty should be discussed separately.

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: An edict adopted his advice.
entries.literal: An edict followed his advice.

entries.zh: 俄兼諫議大夫，知宣徽院事。
entries.en: Before long he was additionally made Remonstrance and Review Grand Master and administrator of the Palace Privy Office affairs.
entries.literal: Before long he was additionally made Remonstrance and Review Grand Master and administrator of the Palace Privy Office.

entries.zh: 時上擊鞠無度，上書諫曰：臣竊觀房玄齡、杜如晦，隋季書生，向不遇太宗，安能為一代名相？
entries.en: At the time the Emperor played cuju without restraint; Dechen submitted a remonstrance, saying, "Your servant has observed Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui — mere scholars of the late Sui — who could never have become the great ministers of an age had they not met Emperor Taizong?"
entries.literal: At the time the Emperor played cuju without restraint; Dechen submitted a remonstrance, saying: "Your servant has privately observed Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui — bookish men of the Sui season — how could they have become famous ministers of a generation had they not met Taizong?"

entries.zh: 臣雖不才，陛下在東宮，幸列侍從，今又得侍聖讀，未有裨補聖明。
entries.en: Though I am without talent, when Your Majesty was in the Eastern Palace I was fortunate to serve among your attendants; now again I attend your sacred readings, yet I have made no contribution to Your Majesty's enlightenment.
entries.literal: Though I am without talent, when Your Majesty was in the Eastern Palace I was fortunate to rank among your attendants; now again I attend your sacred readings; I have as yet made no contribution to Your Majesty's enlightenment.

entries.zh: 陛下嘗問臣以貞觀、開元之事，臣請略陳之。
entries.en: Your Majesty once asked me about the reigns of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan; I beg leave to set them forth briefly.
entries.literal: Your Majesty once questioned me about the reigns of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan; I beg leave to set them forth briefly.

entries.zh: 臣聞唐太宗侍太上皇宴罷，則挽輦至內殿；
entries.en: Your servant has heard that after banquets with the retired emperor, Emperor Taizong of Tang would draw the imperial carriage himself to the inner hall;
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that when Emperor Taizong of Tang attended the Supreme Emperor at banquet's end, he would draw the carriage to the inner hall;

entries.zh: 玄宗與兄弟歡飲，盡家人禮。
entries.en: and that Emperor Xuanzong drank merrily with his brothers and observed all the rites of kinship within a family.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuanzong drank merrily with his brothers and fulfilled all the rites of family.

entries.zh: 陛下嗣祖考之祚，躬侍太后，可謂至孝。
entries.en: Your Majesty has inherited the throne of your forefathers and in person attends the Empress Dowager — this may truly be called utmost filial piety.
entries.literal: Your Majesty has inherited the throne of your ancestors and in person attends the Empress Dowager — this may be called utmost filial piety.

entries.zh: 臣更望定省之餘，睦六親，加愛敬，則陛下親親之道，比隆二帝矣。
entries.en: Your servant further hopes that beyond your daily attendance, Your Majesty will bring harmony among the six degrees of kin, increase love and respect among them, and then Your Majesty's devotion to kin will rival that of those two emperors.
entries.literal: Your servant further hopes that beyond morning and evening attendance, Your Majesty will harmonize the six kin, increase love and respect, and then Your Majesty's way of cherishing kin will equal the elevation of those two emperors.

entries.zh: 臣又聞二帝耽玩經史，數引公卿講學，至於日昃。
entries.en: Your servant has also heard that those two emperors were absorbed in the classics and histories, repeatedly summoning dukes and ministers to lecture on learning until the sun had passed the meridian.
entries.literal: Your servant has also heard that the two emperors were absorbed in the classics and histories, repeatedly summoning dukes and ministers to lecture on learning, even until the sun slanted west.

entries.zh: 故當時天下翕然向風，以隆文治。
entries.en: Therefore the realm at that time turned as one toward their example, and civil governance flourished.
entries.literal: Therefore at that time the realm turned as one toward their influence, and literary governance was elevated.

entries.zh: 今陛下遊心典籍，分解章句，臣願研究經理，深造而篤行之，二帝之治，不難致矣。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty's mind dwells in the canonical texts and you parse passages and clauses; your servant wishes to study statecraft in depth, pursue it further, and practice it steadfastly — the governance of those two emperors would not be hard to attain.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty's mind roves in the canonical texts and you parse passages and clauses; your servant wishes to study statecraft in depth, pursue it further, and practice it steadfastly — the governance of the two emperors would not be hard to attain.

entries.zh: 臣又聞太宗射豕，唐儉諫之；
entries.en: Your servant has also heard that when Taizong shot at a boar, Tang Jian remonstrated with him;
entries.literal: Your servant has also heard that when Taizong shot at a boar, Tang Jian remonstrated with him;

entries.zh: 玄宗臂鷹，韓休言之；
entries.en: when Xuanzong carried a hawk on his arm, Han Xiu spoke against it;
entries.literal: when Xuanzong carried a hawk on his arm, Han Xiu spoke of it;

entries.zh: 二帝莫不樂從。
entries.en: and both emperors gladly accepted their counsel.
entries.literal: and neither of the two emperors failed to follow with pleasure.

entries.zh: 今陛下以球馬為樂，愚臣思之，有不宜者三，故不避斧鉞言之：竊以君臣同戲，不免分爭，君得臣愧，彼負此喜，一不宜。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty takes pleasure in ball games and horsemanship; your foolish servant has reflected on this and finds three improprieties, and therefore speaks though it may cost his life: when ruler and minister play together, contention cannot be avoided — the ruler wins and the minister is shamed, one side loses and the other rejoices — the first impropriety.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty takes ball and horse for pleasure; your foolish servant reflects on this and finds three points of impropriety; therefore I do not avoid the axe and halberd in speaking: I venture to think that when ruler and minister play together, contention cannot be avoided — the ruler wins and the minister is shamed, one side loses and the other rejoices — the first impropriety.

entries.zh: 躍馬揮杖，縱橫馳騖，不顧上下之分，爭先取勝，失人臣禮，二不宜。
entries.en: Leaping horses and brandishing mallets, galloping freely without regard for the distinction between superior and inferior, striving to win — this violates the rites owed by a minister to his ruler; the second impropriety.
entries.literal: Leaping horses and brandishing sticks, galloping freely in every direction, heedless of the distinction between superior and inferior, striving to win first — this loses the rites of a minister toward his ruler; the second impropriety.

entries.zh: 輕萬乘之尊，圖一時之樂，萬一有銜勒之失，其如社稷、太后何？
entries.en: To treat lightly the dignity of the Son of Heaven and seek a moment's pleasure — if by any chance there should be an accident with bridle or reins, what would become of the altars of state and the Empress Dowager?
entries.literal: To treat lightly the dignity of the ten-thousand chariots and seek a moment's pleasure — if by any chance there should be a mishap with bridle or reins, what of the altars of state and the Empress Dowager?

entries.zh: 三不宜。
entries.en: The third impropriety.
entries.literal: The third impropriety.

entries.zh: 儻陛下不以臣言為迂，少賜省覽，天下之福，群臣之願也。
entries.en: If Your Majesty does not regard your servant's words as impractical and will grant them a little consideration, it will be the fortune of the realm and the wish of all your ministers.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not regard your servant's words as impractical and will grant them a little consideration, it will be the fortune of the realm and the wish of all your ministers.

entries.zh: 論曰：張儉名符帝夢，遂結主知，服弊袍不易，誌敦薄俗，功著兩朝，世稱賢相，非過也。
entries.en: The commentary says: Zhang Jian's name matched the Emperor's dream, and thus he won the ruler's trust; he wore a threadbare robe and would not replace it, bearing witness to his devotion to plain living; his achievements stood out across two reigns; the age calls him a worthy chief minister — and that is no exaggeration.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Zhang Jian's name matched the Emperor's dream, and thus he won the ruler's confidence; he wore a worn robe and would not change it, recording his devotion to plain custom; his achievements stood out in two reigns; the age calls him a worthy chief minister — this is no exaggeration.

entries.zh: 邢抱樸甄別守令，大愜人望，兩決滯獄，民無冤濫。
entries.en: Xing Baopu distinguished competent from incompetent magistrates, greatly satisfying public expectation; twice he cleared long-pending cases, and the people suffered no wrongful punishment.
entries.literal: Xing Baopu distinguished competent from incompetent magistrates, greatly satisfying public expectation; twice he settled cases in arrears, and the people knew no wrongful punishment.

entries.zh: 馬得臣引盛唐之治以諫其君，蕭樸痛皇后之誣，至於嘔血。
entries.en: Ma Dechen cited the governance of High Tang to remonstrate with his ruler; Xiao Pu grieved over the false accusation against the empress until he vomited blood.
entries.literal: Ma Dechen cited the governance of High Tang to remonstrate with his ruler; Xiao Pu grieved over the calumny against the empress to the point of vomiting blood.

entries.zh: 四人者，皆以明經致位，忠藎若此，宜矣。
entries.en: These four men all rose to office through mastery of the classics; such loyalty and earnest devotion as this was only fitting.
entries.literal: These four men all rose to office through mastery of the classics; such loyalty and earnestness as this was fitting.

entries.zh: 聖宗得人，於斯為盛。
entries.en: In gathering such men, Shengzong's reign reached its fullest height.
entries.literal: In gaining such men, Shengzong's time was at its richest.

entries.zh: 邢抱樸，應州人，刑部郎中簡之子也。
entries.en: Xing Baopu, a native of Ying Prefecture, was the son of Xing Jian, director of the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: Xing Baopu was a man of Ying Prefecture and the son of Xing Jian, director of the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 抱樸性穎悟，好學博古。
entries.en: Baopu was quick-witted by nature, devoted to study, and broad in classical learning.
entries.literal: Baopu was by nature quick and perceptive, fond of study, and broad in ancient learning.

entries.zh: 保寧初，為政事舍人、知制誥，累遷翰林學士，加禮部侍郎。
entries.en: At the beginning of Baoning he served as drafting academician for political affairs and edicts, rose through repeated promotions to Hanlin academician, and was given the additional title of vice minister of Rites.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoning he served as drafting academician for political affairs and edicts, was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin academician, and was given the additional title of vice minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 統和四年，山西州縣被兵，命抱樸鎮撫之，民始安，加戶部尚書。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when the prefectures and counties of western Shanxi were ravaged by war, Baopu was ordered to pacify them; the people first regained security, and he was made minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when western Shanxi prefectures and counties suffered from warfare, Baopu was ordered to pacify the region; the people first knew security; he was made minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 遷翰林學士承旨，與室昉同修《實錄》。
entries.en: He was promoted to Hanlin academician director and, with Shi Fang, jointly compiled the Veritable Records.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin academician director and, with Shi Fang, jointly compiled the Veritable Records.

entries.zh: 決南京滯獄還，優詔褒美。
entries.en: After settling long-pending cases at Nanjing and returning, he received a gracious edict of praise.
entries.literal: After adjudicating long-pending cases at Nanjing and returning, he received a gracious edict of praise.

entries.zh: 十年，拜參知政事。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was appointed participating state counselor.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed participating state counselor.

entries.zh: 以樞密使韓德讓薦，按察諸道守令能否而黜陟之，大協人望。
entries.en: On the recommendation of Commissioner Han Derang, he inspected magistrates throughout the circuits for competence and promoted or dismissed them accordingly; this accorded greatly with public expectation.
entries.literal: On recommendation of commissioner Han Derang, he inspected prefectural and county magistrates throughout the circuits for competence and promoted or demoted them; this accorded greatly with popular expectation.

entries.zh: 尋以母憂去官，詔起視事。
entries.en: Before long, on his mother's death he left office, but an edict recalled him to resume his duties.
entries.literal: Before long, on his mother's death he left office; an edict recalled him to resume duties.

entries.zh: 表乞終制，不從；
entries.en: He memorialized asking to complete the full mourning period; the request was denied.
entries.literal: He memorialized begging to complete mourning rituals; this was not granted.

entries.zh: 宰相密諭上意，乃視事。
entries.en: The chief councilors privately conveyed the Emperor's wishes, and only then did he resume office.
entries.literal: The chief councilors secretly conveyed the Emperor's mind, and only then did he resume office.

entries.zh: 人以孝稱。
entries.en: People praised him for his filial devotion.
entries.literal: People acclaimed him for filial piety.

entries.zh: 及耶律休哥留守南京，又多滯獄，復詔抱樸平決之，人無冤者。
entries.en: When Yelü Xiuge held Nanjing in garrison and again accumulated many cases in arrears, an edict once more ordered Baopu to settle them, and no one was left wronged.
entries.literal: When Yelü Xiuge held Nanjing in garrison and again had many cases in arrears, an edict once more ordered Baopu to settle them; no one remained wronged.

entries.zh: 改南院樞密使，卒，贈侍中。
entries.en: He was transferred to commissioner of the Southern Academy; he died and was posthumously granted the title of palace attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Southern Academy commissioner; he died and was posthumously granted palace attendant.

entries.zh: 初，抱樸與弟抱質受經於母陳氏，皆以儒術顯，抱質亦官至侍中，時人榮之。
entries.en: Earlier, Baopu and his younger brother Baozhi had studied the classics under their mother, Lady Chen; both rose to prominence through Confucian learning, and Baozhi also reached the post of palace attendant; men of the time took pride in the family.
entries.literal: Earlier, Baopu and his younger brother Baozhi had received the classics from their mother, Lady Chen; both rose to eminence through Confucian learning; Baozhi also reached the post of palace attendant; men of the time took pride in them.

entries.zh: 書奏，帝嘉嘆良久。
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised it and sighed over it for a long while.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised and sighed over it for a long while.

entries.zh: 未幾卒，贈太子太保，詔有司給葬。
entries.en: Before long he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and an edict ordered the relevant offices to provide for his burial.
entries.literal: Before long he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and an edict ordered the relevant offices to provide burial.

entries.zh: 耶律八哥，字烏古鄰，五院部人。
entries.en: Yelu Bagge, style name Wugulin, was a man of the Five-Yuan Division.
entries.literal: Yelu Bagge, style name Wugulin, was a man of the Five-Yuan Division.

entries.zh: 幼聰慧，書一覽輒成誦。
entries.en: As a boy he was clever; after a single reading he could recite a text from memory.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever; after one reading of a text he could recite it from memory.

entries.zh: 統和中，以世業為本部吏。
entries.en: During the Tonghe era, through hereditary office he became an officer of his native division.
entries.literal: In the Tonghe era, through hereditary office he became an officer of his native division.

entries.zh: 未幾，升閘撒狘，尋轉樞密院侍御。
entries.en: Before long he was promoted to zhasa mo, and soon was transferred to attendant of the Commission for Military Affairs.
entries.literal: Before long he was promoted to zhasa mo, and soon was transferred to attendant of the Commission for Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 會宋將曹彬、米信侵燕，八哥以扈從有功，擢上京留守。
entries.en: When Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin invaded Yan, Bagge, for meritorious service in the imperial retinue, was promoted to garrison commander of the Upper Capital.
entries.literal: When Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin invaded Yan, Bagge, for meritorious service in the imperial retinue, was promoted to garrison commander of the Upper Capital.

entries.zh: 開泰四年，召為北院樞密副使。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Kaitai he was summoned as deputy commissioner of the Northern Academy.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Kaitai he was summoned as deputy commissioner of the Northern Academy.

entries.zh: 頃之，留守東京。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: Before long he was garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 七年，上命東平王蕭排押帥師伐高麗，八哥為都監，至開京，大掠而還。
entries.en: In the seventh year the Emperor ordered Eastern Pacification Prince Xiao Paiya to command an army against Goryeo; Bagge served as army supervisor; they reached Kaesong and returned after extensive plunder.
entries.literal: In the seventh year the Emperor ordered Eastern Pacification Prince Xiao Paiya to command an army against Goryeo; Bagge served as army supervisor; they reached Kaesong and returned after great plunder.

entries.zh: 濟茶、陀二河，高麗追兵至。
entries.en: At the Jicha and Tuo rivers, Goryeo pursuit troops caught up with them.
entries.literal: At the Jicha and Tuo rivers, Goryeo pursuit troops arrived.

entries.zh: 諸將皆欲使敵渡兩河擊之，獨八哥以為不可，曰：「敵若渡兩河，必殊死戰，乃危道也；
entries.en: The generals all wished to let the enemy cross the two rivers and then attack; only Bagge thought this unwise and said, "If the enemy crosses both rivers, they will fight to the death — that would be a perilous course;
entries.literal: The generals all wished to let the enemy cross the two rivers and then strike them; only Bagge thought this wrong and said: "If the enemy crosses the two rivers, they will fight to the death — that is a perilous course;

entries.zh: 不若擊於兩河之間。」
entries.en: It would be better to attack them between the two rivers."
entries.literal: It would be better to strike them between the two rivers."

entries.zh: 排押從之，戰，敗績。
entries.en: Paiya followed his advice; they gave battle and were defeated.
entries.literal: Paiya followed this advice; they fought and were defeated.

entries.zh: 明年，還東京，奏渤海承奉官宜有以統領之，上從其言，置都知押班。
entries.en: The following year, after returning to the Eastern Capital, he memorialized that Bohai tribute officials ought to be placed under unified supervision; the Emperor accepted his proposal and established the post of director of supervisory escort shifts.
entries.literal: The next year, returning to the Eastern Capital, he memorialized that Bohai tribute-presenting officials ought to have someone to oversee them; the Emperor followed his advice and established the post of director of supervisory escort shifts.

entries.zh: 後以茶、陀之敗，削使相，降西北路都監，卒。
entries.en: Later, because of the defeat at Jicha and Tuo, he was stripped of his commissioner rank, demoted to army supervisor of the Northwestern Route, and died.
entries.literal: Later, because of the defeat at Jicha and Tuo, he was stripped of commissioner rank, demoted to Northwestern Route army supervisor, and died.

entries.zh: 張儉邢抱樸馬得臣蕭樸耶律八哥
entries.en: Zhang Jian, Xing Baopu, Ma Dechen, Xiao Pu, and Yelu Bagge
entries.literal: Zhang Jian, Xing Baopu, Ma Dechen, Xiao Pu, Yelu Bagge

entries.zh: 耶律室魯，字乙辛隱，六院部人。
entries.en: Yelü Shilu, whose style was Yixin Yin, came from the Six Courts tribe.
entries.literal: Yelü Shilu, style name Yixin Yin, was a man of the Six Courts tribe.

entries.zh: 魁岸美容儀。
entries.en: He was tall and striking, with a handsome presence.
entries.literal: He was imposing in stature and handsome in bearing.

entries.zh: 聖宗同年生，帝愛之。
entries.en: Born in the same year as Emperor Shengzong, he won the emperor's affection.
entries.literal: He was born in the same year as Emperor Shengzong; the emperor loved him.

entries.zh: 甫冠，補祗候郎君。
entries.en: As soon as he came of age, he was made an attendant gentleman.
entries.literal: Upon first putting on the cap, he was appointed attendant gentleman.

entries.zh: 未幾，為宿直官。
entries.en: Before long he was assigned to night duty at court.
entries.literal: Before long he became a night-duty officer.

entries.zh: 及出師伐宋，為隊帥，從南府宰相耶律奴瓜、統軍使蕭撻覽略地趙、魏，有功，加檢校太師，為北院大王。
entries.en: When troops were sent against Song, he served as column commander under the Southern Chancellery chancellor Yelü Nugua and the army commander Xiao Talan, helping seize territory in Zhao and Wei. For this service he was promoted to acting grand preceptor and made grandee of the Northern Chancellery.
entries.literal: When the army marched out to attack Song, he served as column commander, following the Southern Chancellery Chancellor Yelü Nugua and the army commander Xiao Talan in seizing territory in Zhao and Wei; for his merit he was made acting Grand Preceptor and Northern Chancellery Grandee.

entries.zh: 攻拔通利軍。
entries.en: He captured Tongli Circuit.
entries.literal: He stormed and took Tongli Circuit.

entries.zh: 宋和議成，特進門下平章事，賜推誠竭節保義功臣。
entries.en: After peace with Song was concluded, he was made specially advanced grand councilor of the Secretariat and granted the title Meritorious Subject of Sincere Devotion and Steadfast Loyalty.
entries.literal: When the Song peace treaty was concluded, he was made specially advanced grand councilor of the Secretariat and granted the title Meritorious Subject of Sincere Devotion and Steadfast Loyalty.

entries.zh: 以本部俸羊多闕，部人空乏，請以羸老之羊及皮毛歲易南中絹，彼此利之。
entries.en: Because stipend sheep for his tribe were chronically short and his tribesmen were impoverished, he asked to trade each year old or weak sheep and hides for southern silk, to the benefit of both sides.
entries.literal: Because stipend sheep for his tribe were often lacking and his tribesmen were impoverished, he requested to exchange each year lean old sheep and hides for silk from the south, to the mutual benefit of both sides.

entries.zh: 拜北院樞密使，封韓王。
entries.en: He was appointed commissioner of the Northern Chancellery and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
entries.literal: He was appointed Northern Chancellery commissioner and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

entries.zh: 自韓德讓知北院，職多廢曠，室魯拜命之日，朝野相慶。
entries.en: Ever since Han Derang had overseen the Northern Chancellery, many of its duties had lapsed; when Shilu took office, the court and the realm rejoiced together.
entries.literal: Since Han Derang had overseen the Northern Chancellery, many duties had fallen into neglect; on the day Shilu received his appointment, court and countryside alike rejoiced.

entries.zh: 從上獵松林，至沙嶺卒，年四十四，贈守司徒、政事令。
entries.en: While accompanying the emperor on a hunt in Songlin, he died at Shaling at the age of forty-four and was posthumously granted the ranks of acting minister over the masses and director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a hunt in Songlin, he died at Shaling, aged forty-four; posthumously he was given the offices of acting Minister over the Masses and Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 二子：十神奴、歐裏斯。
entries.en: He had two sons: Shishennu and Orris.
entries.literal: He had two sons: Shishennu and Orris.

entries.zh: 十神奴，南院大王。
entries.en: Shishennu rose to grandee of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: Shishennu became Southern Chancellery Grandee.

entries.zh: 王繼忠，不知何郡人。
entries.en: Wang Jizhong was a man of unknown native commandery.
entries.literal: Wang Jizhong—it is not known from which commandery he came.

entries.zh: 仕宋為鄆州刺史、殿前都虞候。
entries.en: In Song service he held the posts of prefect of Yanzhou and chief adjutant of the Palace Front.
entries.literal: He served Song as prefect of Yanzhou and chief adjutant of the Palace Front.

entries.zh: 統和二十一年，宋遣繼忠屯定之望都，以輕騎覘我軍，遇南府宰相耶律奴瓜等，獲之。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year of Tonghe, Song posted Jizhong at Wangdu in Ding prefecture; he led light cavalry to scout our forces, met the Southern Chancellery chancellor Yelü Nugua and others, and was taken prisoner.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Tonghe, Song sent Jizhong to garrison Wangdu in Dingzhou; with light cavalry he reconnoitered our army, encountered the Southern Chancellery Chancellor Yelü Nugua and others, and was captured.

entries.zh: 太后知其賢，授戶部使，以康默記族女女之。
entries.en: Recognizing his talent, the empress dowager made him commissioner of the household bureau and gave him a daughter of the Kang Mojiji clan in marriage.
entries.literal: The empress dowager knew him to be worthy and appointed him commissioner of the Household Bureau; she gave him a daughter of the Kang Mojiji clan in marriage.

entries.zh: 繼忠亦自激昂，事必盡力。
entries.en: Jizhong likewise threw himself into his duties and spared no effort in whatever he undertook.
entries.literal: Jizhong too roused himself in spirit and in every matter gave his utmost effort.

entries.zh: 宋以繼忠先朝舊臣，每遣使，必有附賜，聖宗許受之。
entries.en: Song treated Jizhong as a former minister of the prior dynasty and, whenever it sent envoys, always included gifts for him; Emperor Shengzong allowed him to accept them.
entries.literal: Because Song regarded Jizhong as a former minister of the previous reign, whenever it sent envoys there were always attached gifts for him; Emperor Shengzong permitted him to accept them.

entries.zh: 二十二年，宋使來聘，遺繼忠弧矢、鞭策及求和劄子，有曰：「自臨大位，愛養黎元。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year a Song envoy arrived on a diplomatic mission and sent Jizhong a bow and arrows, a riding crop, and a memorial seeking peace, which read: "Since I took the throne, I have cherished and nurtured the people.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, a Song envoy came on a mission of courtesy and sent Jizhong a bow and arrows, a riding crop, and a memorial seeking peace, which read: "Since I assumed the great throne, I have cherished and nurtured the common people.

entries.zh: 豈欲窮兵，惟思息戰。
entries.en: I have no wish to exhaust the realm in war; I think only of ending the fighting.
entries.literal: How could I wish to exhaust the realm in war? I think only of ceasing hostilities.

entries.zh: 每敕邊事，嚴諭守臣。
entries.en: Whenever I issue orders on border affairs, I sternly instruct the frontier officials.
entries.literal: Whenever I issue orders on border affairs, I sternly instruct the frontier officials.

entries.zh: 至於北界人民，不令小有侵擾，眾所具悉，爾亦備知。
entries.en: As for the people on the northern frontier, I allow no harassment, however slight; everyone knows this, and you are fully aware of it as well.
entries.literal: As for the people of the northern border, I do not allow even slight harassment; all know this fully, and you too are well aware of it.

entries.zh: 向以知雄州何承矩已布此懇，自後杳無所聞。
entries.en: I had understood that He Chengju of Xiong prefecture had already conveyed this plea; since then I have heard nothing more.
entries.literal: Earlier I learned that He Chengju of Xiongzhou had already conveyed this plea; since then I have heard nothing further.

entries.zh: 汝可密言，如許通和，即當別使往請。」
entries.en: You may tell them privately that if they agree to peace, I shall immediately send another envoy to request it."
entries.literal: You may speak to them in secret: if they agree to peace, I shall at once send another envoy to request it."

entries.zh: 詔繼忠與宋使相見，仍許講和。
entries.en: The court ordered Jizhong to meet the Song envoy and authorized peace talks.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Jizhong to meet the Song envoy and peace negotiations were permitted.

entries.zh: 以繼忠家無奴隸，賜宮戶三十，加左武衛上將軍，攝中京留守。
entries.en: Because Jizhong's household had no servants, he was granted thirty palace households; he was promoted to left martial guard general and made acting defender of the Central Capital.
entries.literal: Because Jizhong's household had no slaves, thirty palace households were granted him; he was made left martial guard general and acting defender of the Central Capital.

entries.zh: 開泰五年，為漢人行宮都部署，封瑯邪郡王。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Kai Tai he was made overall commander of the Han palace encampment and enfeoffed as prince of Langye commandery.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Kai Tai he became overall commander of the Han Chinese palace encampment and was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye commandery.

entries.zh: 六年，進楚王，賜國姓。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was advanced to Prince of Chu and granted the imperial clan surname.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced to Prince of Chu and granted the imperial surname.

entries.zh: 上嘗燕飲，議以蕭合卓為北院樞密使，繼忠曰：「合卓雖有刀筆才，暗於大體。
entries.en: At a banquet the emperor once discussed appointing Xiao Hezhuo commissioner of the Northern Chancellery; Jizhong said, "Hezhuo may have a gift for paperwork, but he lacks grasp of the larger picture.
entries.literal: Once at a banquet the emperor discussed appointing Xiao Hezhuo Northern Chancellery commissioner; Jizhong said: "Although Hezhuo has clerical talent, he is blind to the larger picture.

entries.zh: 蕭敵烈才行兼備，可任。」
entries.en: Xiao Dilie has both talent and character and would be fit for the post."
entries.literal: Xiao Dilie has both talent and conduct and can fill the post."

entries.zh: 上不納，竟用合卓。
entries.en: The emperor did not heed him and in the end appointed Hezhuo.
entries.literal: The emperor did not accept this and in the end employed Hezhuo.

entries.zh: 及遣合卓伐高麗，繼忠為行軍副部署，攻興化鎮，月餘不下。
entries.en: When Hezhuo was dispatched against Goryeo, Jizhong served as deputy campaign commander; they attacked Xinghua garrison for more than a month without capturing it.
entries.literal: When Hezhuo was sent to attack Goryeo, Jizhong served as deputy campaign commander; they besieged Xinghua garrison for more than a month without taking it.

entries.zh: 師還，上謂明於知人，拜樞密使。
entries.en: After the army returned, the emperor declared that he had shown sound judgment of men and appointed him commissioner.
entries.literal: When the army returned, the emperor said he was clear-sighted in judging men and appointed him commissioner.

entries.zh: 太平三年致仕，卒。
entries.en: In the third year of Taiping he retired from office and died.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiping he retired from office and died.

entries.zh: 子懷玉，仕至防禦使。
entries.en: His son Huaiyu rose in service to the rank of defense commissioner.
entries.literal: His son Huaiyu rose in service to defense commissioner.

entries.zh: 陳昭袞，小字王九，雲州人。
entries.en: Chen Zhaogun, known in youth as Wang Jiu, was a native of Yunzhou.
entries.literal: Chen Zhaogun, childhood name Wang Jiu, was a man of Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 工譯鞮，勇而善射。
entries.en: He was skilled at Khitan interpretation, brave, and an excellent archer.
entries.literal: He was skilled at translating the Khitan language, brave, and adept at archery.

entries.zh: 統和中，補祗候郎君，為奚拽剌詳穩，累遷敦睦宮太保，兼掌圍場事。
entries.en: During the Tonghe era he was made an attendant gentleman, then overseer of the Xi Zhuaila guard, and was repeatedly promoted to grand guardian of Dunmu Palace while also overseeing the imperial hunting grounds.
entries.literal: During Tonghe he was appointed attendant gentleman, became overseer of the Xi Zhuaila guard, and was repeatedly promoted to grand guardian of the Dunmu Palace, concurrently managing the hunting grounds.

entries.zh: 開泰五年秋，大獵，帝射虎，以馬馳太速，矢不及發。
entries.en: In the autumn of the fifth year of Kai Tai, during a grand hunt, the emperor charged a tiger; his horse ran too fast and he could not loose his arrow in time.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Kai Tai, during a great hunt, the emperor shot at a tiger; his horse galloped too fast and the arrow could not be loosed in time.

entries.zh: 虎怒，奮勢將犯蹕。
entries.en: The tiger, enraged, gathered itself to charge the imperial train.
entries.literal: The tiger grew enraged and, gathering its strength, was about to charge the imperial train.

entries.zh: 左右辟易，昭袞舍馬，捉虎兩耳騎之。
entries.en: Those around the emperor scattered; Zhaogun leapt from his horse, seized the tiger by both ears, and rode astride it.
entries.literal: Those at left and right scattered; Zhaogun abandoned his horse, seized the tiger by both ears, and mounted it.

entries.zh: 虎駭，且逸。
entries.en: Terrified, the tiger bolted.
entries.literal: The tiger was terrified and fled.

entries.zh: 上命衛士追射，昭袞大呼止之。
entries.en: The emperor ordered the guards to pursue and shoot, but Zhaogun shouted for them to stop.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered the guards to pursue and shoot; Zhaogun shouted loudly for them to stop.

entries.zh: 虎雖軼山，昭袞終不墮地。
entries.en: Though the tiger bounded over hill after hill, Zhaogun never fell.
entries.literal: Though the tiger leapt over hills, Zhaogun in the end did not fall to the ground.

entries.zh: 伺便，拔佩刀殺之。
entries.en: When he saw his chance, he drew his belt knife and killed it.
entries.literal: Watching for an opening, he drew his belt knife and killed it.

entries.zh: 輦至上前，慰勞良久。
entries.en: Brought before the emperor's carriage, he was comforted and praised at length.
entries.literal: When he came before the emperor in the imperial carriage, the emperor comforted and praised him at length.

entries.zh: 即日設燕，悉以席上金銀器賜之，特加節鉞，遷圍場都太師，賜國姓，命張儉、呂德懋賦以美之。
entries.en: That same day a banquet was held and every gold and silver vessel on the table was given to him; he was specially granted the command baton, promoted to grand master of the hunting grounds, granted the imperial clan surname, and Zhang Jian and Lü Demao were ordered to compose verses in his praise.
entries.literal: That same day a banquet was held and all the gold and silver vessels on the table were bestowed on him; he was specially granted the command baton, promoted to grand master of the hunting grounds, granted the imperial surname, and Zhang Jian and Lü Demao were ordered to compose verses in his praise.

entries.zh: 遷歸義軍節度使，同知上京留守，歷西南面招討都監，卒。
entries.en: He was made military commissioner of the Guiyi Army and associate defender of the Supreme Capital, later served as overall overseer of punitive campaigns in the southwest, and died in office.
entries.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of the Guiyi Army, associate defender of the Supreme Capital, and served successively as overall overseer of punitive campaigns in the Southwest; he died.

entries.zh: 蕭合卓，字合魯隱，突呂不部人。
entries.en: Xiao Hezhuo, whose style was Helu Yin, came from the Tulübu tribe.
entries.literal: Xiao Hezhuo, style name Helu Yin, was a man of the Tulübu tribe.

entries.zh: 始為本部吏。
entries.en: He began as a clerk in his tribe.
entries.literal: He began as a clerk of his tribe.

entries.zh: 統和初，以謹恪，補南院侍郎。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tonghe era, his scrupulous diligence won him appointment as vice minister of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe, for his careful diligence he was appointed Southern Chancellery vice minister.

entries.zh: 十八年，北院樞密使韓德讓舉合卓為中丞，以太后遺物使宋。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year the Northern Chancellery commissioner Han Derang recommended Hezhuo as chief censor and sent him to Song bearing the empress dowager's parting gifts.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, the Northern Chancellery Commissioner Han Derang recommended Hezhuo as chief censor and sent him as envoy to Song bearing the empress dowager's parting gifts.

entries.zh: 還，遷北院樞密副使。
entries.en: On his return he was made deputy commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.
entries.literal: On his return he was transferred to deputy Northern Chancellery commissioner.

entries.zh: 開泰三年，為左夷離畢。
entries.en: In the third year of Kai Tai he was made Left Yilibi.
entries.literal: In the third year of Kai Tai he became Left Yilibi.

entries.zh: 合卓久居近職，明習典故，善占對。
entries.en: Hezhuo had long held posts close to the throne, was well versed in precedent, and excelled at court repartee.
entries.literal: Hezhuo had long held posts close to the throne, was well versed in precedent, and skilled at responsive discourse.

entries.zh: 以是尤被寵渥，升北院樞密使。
entries.en: For this he was especially favored and promoted to commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.
entries.literal: For this he was especially favored and promoted to Northern Chancellery commissioner.

entries.zh: 時議以為無完行，不可大用；
entries.en: Contemporary opinion held that he lacked integrity and should not be entrusted with great responsibility;
