entries.literal: Contemporary opinion held that he lacked integrity of conduct and could not be entrusted with great responsibility;

entries.zh: 南院樞密使王繼忠侍宴，又譏其短。
entries.en: at a banquet the Southern Chancellery commissioner Wang Jizhong again mocked his shortcomings.
entries.literal: the Southern Chancellery Commissioner Wang Jizhong, attending a banquet, again mocked his shortcomings.

entries.zh: 帝頗不悅。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly displeased.
entries.literal: The emperor was quite displeased.

entries.zh: 六年，遣合卓伐高麗，還，時求進者多附之；
entries.en: In the sixth year Hezhuo was sent against Goryeo; on his return, many office-seekers flocked to him;
entries.literal: In the sixth year Hezhuo was sent to attack Goryeo; on his return, many who sought advancement attached themselves to him;

entries.zh: 然其服食、仆馬不加於舊。
entries.en: yet his food, clothing, servants, and horses were no more lavish than before.
entries.literal: yet his food, drink, and servants and horses were no more than before.

entries.zh: 帝知其廉，以族屬女妻其子，詔許親友饋獻，豪貴奔趨於門。
entries.en: The emperor recognized his integrity, gave a clanswoman in marriage to his son, and issued an edict permitting friends and kin to send gifts; the powerful and wealthy thronged his gate.
entries.literal: The emperor knew him to be incorrupt and gave him a clanswoman in marriage to his son; an edict permitted friends and kin to send gifts, and the powerful and wealthy rushed to his gate.

entries.zh: 太平五年，有疾，帝欲臨視，合卓辭曰：「臣無狀，猥蒙重任。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Taiping he fell ill; the emperor wished to visit him in person. Hezhuo declined, saying, "Your subject is without merit, yet I have presumptuously received a weighty post.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping he fell ill; the emperor wished to visit him in person. Hezhuo declined, saying: "Your subject is without merit yet has presumptuously received a weighty post.

entries.zh: 今形容毀瘁，恐陛下見而動心。」
entries.en: My appearance is now wasted and haggard; I fear that if Your Majesty sees me, it will distress you."
entries.literal: Now my appearance is wasted and haggard; I fear that if Your Majesty sees me, it will stir your heart."

entries.zh: 帝從之。
entries.en: The emperor assented.
entries.literal: The emperor assented.

entries.zh: 會北府宰相蕭樸問疾，合卓執其手曰：「吾死，君必為樞密使，慎勿舉勝己者。」
entries.en: When the Northern Prefecture chancellor Xiao Pu came to inquire after his illness, Hezhuo took his hand and said, "When I die, you are sure to become commissioner; be careful never to recommend anyone better than yourself."
entries.literal: When the Northern Prefecture Chancellor Xiao Pu came to inquire after his illness, Hezhuo took his hand and said: "When I die, you are certain to become commissioner; be careful not to recommend anyone better than yourself."

entries.zh: 樸出而鄙之。
entries.en: Pu left and despised him for it.
entries.literal: Pu left and despised him for it.

entries.zh: 是日卒。
entries.en: That same day he died.
entries.literal: That same day he died.

entries.zh: 子烏古，終本部節度使。
entries.en: His son Wugu ended his career as military commissioner of the tribe.
entries.literal: His son Wugu ended his career as tribal military commissioner.

entries.zh: 耶律室魯
entries.en: Yelü Shilu
entries.literal: Yelü Shilu

entries.zh: 〈（歐裏斯）〉
entries.en: (Orris)
entries.literal: (Orris)

entries.zh: 王繼忠蕭孝忠陳昭袞蕭合卓
entries.en: Wang Jizhong, Xiao Xiaozhong, Chen Zhaogun, and Xiao Hezhuo
entries.literal: Wang Jizhong, Xiao Xiaozhong, Chen Zhaogun, Xiao Hezhuo

entries.zh: 耶律隆運，本姓韓，名德讓，西南面招討使匡嗣之子也。
entries.en: Yelu Longyun was born Han Derang, son of Kuangsi, the Southwestern Frontier Pacification Commissioner.
entries.literal: Yelu Longyun, originally surnamed Han, named Derang, was the son of the Southwestern Frontier Pacification Commissioner Kuangsi.

entries.zh: 統和十九年，賜名德昌；
entries.en: In the nineteenth year of the Tonghe era, he was granted the name Dechang.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Tonghe, he was granted the name Dechang.

entries.zh: 二十二年，賜姓耶律；
entries.en: In the twenty-second year, he was granted the imperial surname Yelu.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was granted the surname Yelu.

entries.zh: 二十八年，復賜名隆運。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year, he was again granted the name Longyun.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was again granted the name Longyun.

entries.zh: 重厚有智略，明治體，喜建功立事。
entries.en: Steady and weighty in bearing, resourceful in counsel, versed in the principles of governance, and eager to win merit through great undertakings.
entries.literal: Deep and grave, possessed of strategy, clear in governing principles, fond of establishing achievements and undertakings.

entries.zh: 侍景宗，以謹飭聞，加東頭承奉官，補樞密院通事，轉上京皇城使，遙授彰德軍節度使，代其父匡嗣為上京留守，權知京事，甚有聲。
entries.en: In service to Emperor Jingzong he won renown for scrupulous conduct. He rose through Eastern Head Attendant Officer and Han Chinese Affairs Commissioner of the Privy Council to Shangjing Imperial City Commissioner, received the honorary title of Zhangde Army Military Commissioner, and succeeded his father Kuangsi as Shangjing Military Governor with full charge of capital affairs—an appointment that brought him wide acclaim.
entries.literal: When attending Emperor Jingzong, he was known for careful discipline; he was promoted to Eastern Head Attendant Officer, appointed Han Chinese Affairs Commissioner of the Privy Council, transferred to Shangjing Imperial City Commissioner, given the honorary post of Zhangde Army Military Commissioner, replaced his father Kuangsi as Shangjing Military Governor with delegated authority over capital affairs—his reputation was considerable.

entries.zh: 尋復代父守南京，時人榮之。
entries.en: Soon afterward he again took his father's place as defender of the Southern Capital, to the envy of his contemporaries.
entries.literal: Before long he again replaced his father in guarding Nanjing; the people of the time took it as an honor.

entries.zh: 宋兵取河東，侵燕，五院糺詳穩奚底、統軍蕭討古等敗歸，宋兵圍城，招脅甚急，人懷二心。
entries.en: When Song forces seized Hedong and pressed into Yan, the Five Yuan detailed commandants Xidi and Grand General Xiaotaogu were driven back in defeat. The Song army laid siege to the city, its summons and threats pressing hard, and loyalty within the walls began to falter.
entries.literal: Song troops took Hedong and invaded Yan; the Five Yuan corps detailed commandants Xidi and Grand General Xiaotaogu and others were defeated and returned; Song troops besieged the city, their summons and threats extremely urgent, and people's hearts wavered.

entries.zh: 隆運登城，日夜守禦。
entries.en: Longyun took the ramparts himself and held the defenses day and night.
entries.literal: Longyun ascended the walls and defended day and night.

entries.zh: 援軍至，圍解。
entries.en: Relief arrived and the siege was broken.
entries.literal: When relief troops arrived, the siege was lifted.

entries.zh: 及戰高梁河，宋兵敗走，隆運邀擊，又破之。
entries.en: At Gaoliang River the Song army was routed in flight; Longyun cut off their retreat and shattered them once more.
entries.literal: At the battle of Gaoliang River the Song army was defeated and fled; Longyun intercepted them and broke them again.

entries.zh: 以功拜遼興軍節度使，徵為南院樞密使。
entries.en: For these services he was made Liaoxing Army Military Commissioner and summoned to the Southern Chancellery as Privy Councilor.
entries.literal: For his merit he was appointed Liaoxing Army Military Commissioner and summoned as Southern Chancellery Privy Councilor.

entries.zh: 景宗疾大漸，與耶律斜軫俱受顧命，立梁王為帝，皇后為皇太后，稱制。
entries.en: When Emperor Jingzong fell gravely ill, he and Yelu Xiezhen together received the dying command: they enthroned the Prince of Liang as emperor, made the empress the empress dowager, and she assumed regency.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jingzong fell gravely ill, he and Yelu Xiezhen received the dying command together, enthroned the Prince of Liang as emperor, made the empress dowager, and she assumed regency.

entries.zh: 隆運總宿衛事，太后益寵任之。
entries.en: Longyun took overall charge of the palace guards, and the empress dowager favored and trusted him all the more.
entries.literal: Longyun took overall charge of palace guard affairs, and the empress dowager favored and trusted him all the more.

entries.zh: 統和元年，加開府儀同三司，兼政事令。
entries.en: In the first year of the Tonghe era he was given the additional title Director of the Office with Peerage and made concurrent Administrator of Affairs.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tonghe he was given the additional title Director of the Office with Peerage and made concurrent Administrator of Affairs.

entries.zh: 四年，宋遣曹彬、米信將十萬眾來侵，隆運從太后出師敗之，加守司空，封楚國公。
entries.en: In the fourth year, when Song sent Cao Bin and Mi Xin with a hundred thousand men to invade, Longyun accompanied the empress dowager on campaign and routed them. He received the additional title Defender of the Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, Song sent Cao Bin and Mi Xin with a hundred thousand troops to invade; Longyun accompanied the empress dowager on campaign and defeated them; he was given the additional title Defender of the Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.

entries.zh: 師還，與北府宰相室昉共執國政。
entries.en: After the army returned, he and Northern Chancellery Chancellor Shi Fang jointly directed state affairs.
entries.literal: When the army returned, together with Northern Chancellery Chancellor Shi Fang he jointly held state affairs.

entries.zh: 上言山西四州數被兵，加以歲饑，宜輕稅賦以來流民，從之。
entries.en: He memorialized that the four Shanxi prefectures had repeatedly suffered warfare and, with famine added, taxes and levies should be lightened to draw back displaced people, and the court approved.
entries.literal: He memorialized that the four prefectures of Shanxi had repeatedly suffered warfare and, with famine added, taxes and levies should be lightened to draw back displaced people; the proposal was approved.

entries.zh: 六年，太后觀擊鞠，胡裏室突隆運墜馬，命立斬之。
entries.en: In the sixth year, while the empress dowager watched a cuju match, Hu Lishi charged out and knocked Longyun from his horse; she ordered him beheaded on the spot.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, while the empress dowager watched cuju, Hu Lishi charged out and knocked Longyun from his horse; she ordered him beheaded on the spot.

entries.zh: 詔率師伐宋，圍沙堆，敵乘夜來襲，隆運嚴軍以待，敗走之，封楚王。
entries.en: Ordered to lead troops against Song, he besieged Shadui. When the enemy attacked by night, Longyun held the army in strict readiness, routed them, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu.
entries.literal: By edict he led troops to campaign against Song and besieged Shadui; the enemy came in a night attack; Longyun kept the army strict and ready, defeated them and put them to flight, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu.

entries.zh: 九年，復言燕人挾奸，茍免賦役，貴族因為囊橐，可遣北院宣徽使趙智戒諭，從之。
entries.en: In the ninth year he again memorialized that people in Yan harbored malfeasance, sought to evade taxes and corvée, and the nobility profited from it; Northern Chancellery Palace Attendant Commissioner Zhao Zhi could be sent to admonish them, and the court approved.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he again memorialized that the people of Yan harbored malfeasance, sought to evade taxes and corvée, and the nobility used this as a purse; Northern Chancellery Palace Attendant Commissioner Zhao Zhi could be sent to admonish and instruct them; the proposal was approved.

entries.zh: 十一年，丁母憂，詔強起之。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, when he entered mourning for his mother, an edict forcibly recalled him to office.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, when his mother's mourning period began, an edict forcibly recalled him to office.

entries.zh: 明年，室昉致政，以隆運代為北府宰相，仍領樞密使，監修國史，賜興化功臣。
entries.en: The following year Shi Fang retired, and Longyun replaced him as Northern Chancellery Chancellor while retaining the Privy Council, supervising compilation of the national history, and receiving the merit title Xinghua.
entries.literal: The next year Shi Fang retired from office, and Longyun replaced him as Northern Chancellery Chancellor, still heading the Privy Council, supervising compilation of the national history, and was granted the merit title Xinghua.

entries.zh: 十二年六月，奏三京諸鞫獄官吏，多因請托，曲加寬貸，或妄行搒掠，乞行禁止。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he memorialized that judicial officers in the three capitals often, through patronage, bent cases to grant undue leniency or recklessly beat and plunder, and asked that this be forbidden.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he memorialized that judicial officers in the three capitals often, through patronage, bent cases to grant undue leniency or recklessly applied beating and plunder, and requested that this be forbidden.

entries.zh: 上可其奏。
entries.en: The emperor approved the memorial.
entries.literal: The emperor approved the memorial.

entries.zh: 又表請任賢去邪，太后喜曰：「進賢輔政，真大臣之職。」
entries.en: He also memorialized requesting appointment of the worthy and removal of the corrupt. The empress dowager said with pleasure, "To advance the worthy and assist governance is truly the duty of a great minister."
entries.literal: He also memorialized requesting appointment of the worthy and removal of the corrupt; the empress dowager said with pleasure: "To advance the worthy and assist governance is truly the duty of a great minister."

entries.zh: 優加賜賚。
entries.en: He received especially generous gifts and rewards.
entries.literal: He was especially favored with gifts and rewards.

entries.zh: 服闋，加守太保、兼政事令。
entries.en: When mourning ended, he received the additional titles Defender of the Grand Mentor and concurrent Administrator of Affairs.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he was given the additional titles Defender of the Grand Mentor and concurrent Administrator of Affairs.

entries.zh: 會北院樞密使耶律斜軫薨，詔隆運兼之。
entries.en: When Northern Chancellery Privy Councilor Yelu Xiezhen died, an edict ordered Longyun to hold the post concurrently.
entries.literal: When Northern Chancellery Privy Councilor Yelu Xiezhen died, an edict made Longyun hold the post concurrently.

entries.zh: 久之，拜大丞相，進王齊，總二樞府事。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Grand Chancellor, advanced to Prince of Qi, and took overall charge of both privy councils.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Chancellor, advanced to Prince of Qi, and took overall charge of both privy councils.

entries.zh: 以南京、平州歲不登，奏免百姓農器錢，及請平諸郡商賈價，並從之。
entries.en: Because Nanjing and Pingzhou had poor harvests, he memorialized to exempt the people from the farm-implement levy and requested standardization of merchant prices in the various commanderies; both were approved.
entries.literal: Because Nanjing and Pingzhou had poor harvests, he memorialized to exempt the people from the farm-implement levy and requested standardization of merchant prices in the various commanderies; both were approved.

entries.zh: 二十二年，從太后南征，及河，許宋成而還。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year he accompanied the empress dowager on the southern campaign; reaching the river, Song sued for peace and the army withdrew.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he accompanied the empress dowager on the southern campaign; reaching the river, Song sued for peace and the army returned.

entries.zh: 徙王晉，賜姓，出宮籍，隸橫帳季父房後，乃改賜今名，位親王上，賜田宅及陪葬地。
entries.en: He was transferred to Prince of Jin, granted the imperial surname, removed from the palace register, and attached to the Horizontal-Banner Younger-Father house. He was then granted his present name, ranked above the imperial princes, and given fields, residences, and burial land beside the imperial tombs.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Prince of Jin, granted the imperial surname, removed from the palace register, attached to the Horizontal-Banner Younger-Father house, then again granted his present name, ranked above the imperial princes, and given fields, residences, and burial land beside the imperial tombs.

entries.zh: 從伐高麗還，得末疾，帝與後臨視醫藥。
entries.en: Returning from the campaign against Goryeo, he contracted a terminal illness; the emperor and empress came in person to oversee his medical care.
entries.literal: Returning from the campaign against Goryeo, he contracted a terminal illness; the emperor and empress came in person to oversee his medical care.

entries.zh: 薨，年七十一。
entries.en: He died at seventy-one.
entries.literal: He died at seventy-one.

entries.zh: 贈尚書令，謚文忠，官給葬具，建廟乾陵側。
entries.en: He was posthumously appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, supplied with funeral goods by the state, and given the posthumous title Wenzhong; a temple was built beside Qianling.
entries.literal: He was posthumously appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, given the posthumous title Wenzhong, supplied funeral goods by the state, and a temple was built beside Qianling.

entries.zh: 無子。
entries.en: He had no sons.
entries.literal: He had no sons.

entries.zh: 清寧三年，以魏王貼不子耶魯為嗣。
entries.en: In the third year of Qingning, Yelu, son of Prince of Wei Tiebu, was made his heir.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qingning, Tiebu's son Yelu of Prince of Wei was made his heir.

entries.zh: 天祚立，以皇子敖盧斡繼之。
entries.en: When Tianzuo succeeded, Prince Aoluwo was made his successor.
entries.literal: When Tianzuo succeeded, Prince Aoluwo was made his successor.

entries.zh: 弟德威，侄制心。
entries.en: His younger brother was Dewei; his nephew was Zhixin.
entries.literal: His younger brother was Dewei; his nephew was Zhixin.

entries.zh: 滌魯神情秀徹，聖宗子視之，興宗待以兄禮，雖貴愈謙。
entries.en: Dilu possessed a clear, penetrating grace of manner. Emperor Shengzong treated him as a son, and Emperor Xingzong honored him with the courtesy owed an elder brother; the higher he rose, the more modest he became.
entries.literal: Dilu had a refined and penetrating spirit; Emperor Shengzong regarded him as a son, and Emperor Xingzong treated him with the courtesy due an elder brother—though exalted he became ever more modest.

entries.zh: 初為都點檢，扈從獵黑嶺，獲熊。
entries.en: He first served as Chief Inspector. On a hunt at Black Ridge in the imperial train he brought down a bear.
entries.literal: Initially he was Chief Inspector; accompanying a hunt on Black Ridge he captured a bear.

entries.zh: 上因樂飲，謂滌魯曰：「汝有求乎？」
entries.en: The emperor, merry with wine, said to Dilu: "Do you have any request?"
entries.literal: The emperor, taking pleasure in drinking, said to Dilu: "Do you have any request?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣富貴逾分，不敢他望。
entries.en: He answered: "Your subject already enjoys wealth and rank beyond his desert; I dare not ask for more.
entries.literal: He replied: "Your subject's wealth and honor exceed my station; I dare not look elsewhere.

entries.zh: 惟臣叔先朝優遇，身歿之後，不肖子坐罪籍沒，四時之薦享，諸孫中得赦一人以主祭，臣願畢矣。」
entries.en: Only this: my uncle was favored in the former reign, but after his death his unworthy son was condemned and the family estate confiscated. For the seasonal offerings, if one grandson among them might be pardoned to preside at the ancestral rites, your subject's wish would be complete."
entries.literal: Only my uncle received exceptional favor in the former court; after his death his unworthy son was punished and his property confiscated. For the seasonal sacrifices, if one among the grandsons could be pardoned to preside at the rites, your subject's wish would be fulfilled."

entries.zh: 詔免籍，復其產。
entries.en: An edict cleared the register and restored the confiscated property.
entries.literal: An edict exempted him from the register and restored his property.

entries.zh: 子燕五，官至南京步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: His son Yanwu became Nanjing Commander of the Foot Soldiers.
entries.literal: His son Yanwu rose to Nanjing Infantry Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 耶律勃古哲，字蒲奴隱，六院夷離堇蒲古只之後。
entries.en: Yelu Boguzhe, whose style name was Punuyin, was a descendant of Puguzhi, Chancellery Commissioner of the Six Yuan.
entries.literal: Yelu Boguzhe, style name Punuyin, was a descendant of Chancellery Commissioner Puguzhi of the Six Yuan.

entries.zh: 勇悍，善治生。
entries.en: Brave and fierce, he was skilled at managing livelihood.
entries.literal: Brave and fierce, skilled at managing livelihood.

entries.zh: 保寧中，為天德軍節度使，歷南京侍衛馬步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: During Baoning he served as Tiande Army Military Commissioner and then as Nanjing Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry and Infantry.
entries.literal: During Baoning he served as Tiande Army Military Commissioner and successively as Nanjing Palace Guard Cavalry and Infantry Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 以討平党項羌阿理撒米、仆裏鱉米，遷南院大王。
entries.en: For suppressing the Tangut chiefs Ali Sami and Pulibie Mi, he was promoted to Grand Prince of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: For suppressing and pacifying the Tangut chiefs Ali Sami and Pulibie Mi, he was transferred to Southern Chancellery Grand Prince.

entries.zh: 聖宗即位，太后稱制，會群臣議軍國事，勃古哲上疏陳便宜數事，稱旨，即日兼領山西路諸州事。
entries.en: When Emperor Shengzong succeeded and the empress dowager assumed regency, ministers met to deliberate on military and state affairs. Boguzhe submitted a memorial with several expedient proposals; it pleased the throne, and that same day he was given concurrent charge of the western-circuit prefectures of Shanxi.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shengzong succeeded, the empress dowager held regency; at a gathering of ministers to deliberate on military and state affairs, Boguzhe submitted a memorial setting forth several expedient measures; it accorded with the imperial intent, and that same day he was given concurrent charge of the western-circuit prefectures of Shanxi.

entries.zh: 統和四年，宋將曹彬等侵燕，勃古哲擊之甚力，賜輸忠保節致主功臣，總知山西五州。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when Song generals led by Cao Bin invaded Yan, Boguzhe struck them hard. He received the merit title of Loyal Submission, Integrity Preservation, and Sovereign Service and was given overall charge of the five Shanxi prefectures.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when Song generals led by Cao Bin invaded Yan, Boguzhe struck them with great force; he was granted the merit title of Loyal Submission, Integrity Preservation, and Sovereign Service, and given overall charge of the five Shanxi prefectures.

entries.zh: 會有告勃古哲曲法虐民者，按之有狀，以大杖決之。
entries.en: When someone reported that Boguzhe had bent the law and abused the people, investigation found grounds, and he was beaten with the great staff.
entries.literal: When someone reported that Boguzhe had bent the law and abused the people, investigation found grounds; he was punished with the great staff.

entries.zh: 八年，為南京統軍使，卒。
entries.en: In the eighth year he became Nanjing Grand General and died.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he became Nanjing Grand General and died.

entries.zh: 子爻裏，官至詳穩。
entries.en: His son Yaoli rose to detailed commandant.
entries.literal: His son Yaoli ultimately rose to detailed commandant.

entries.zh: 蕭陽阿，字稍隱。
entries.en: Xiao Yanga, whose style name was Shaoyin.
entries.literal: Xiao Yanga, style name Shaoyin.

entries.zh: 端毅簡嚴，識遼、漢字，通天文、相法。
entries.en: Upright, resolute, concise, and stern, he knew Khitan and Chinese script and was versed in astronomy and physiognomy.
entries.literal: Upright, resolute, concise, and stern, he knew Khitan and Chinese characters and was versed in astronomy and physiognomy.

entries.zh: 父卒，自五蕃部親挽喪車至奚王嶺，人稱其孝。
entries.en: When his father died, he personally drew the funeral cart from the Five Fan tribes to Xiwang Ridge, and people praised his filial devotion.
entries.literal: When his father died, he personally drew the funeral cart from the Five Fan tribes to Xiwang Ridge; people praised his filial piety.

entries.zh: 年十九，為本班郎君。
entries.en: At nineteen he became an attendant of his corps.
entries.literal: At nineteen he became an attendant of his corps.

entries.zh: 歷鐵林、鐵鷂、大鷹三軍詳穩。
entries.en: He served in turn as detailed commandant of the Iron Forest, Iron Hawk, and Great Hawk armies.
entries.literal: He successively served as detailed commandant of the Iron Forest, Iron Hawk, and Great Hawk armies.

entries.zh: 乾統元年，由烏古敵烈部屯田太保為易州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Qiantong he went from Grand Guardian of the Ugu and Dilie tribal garrisons to prefect of Yi Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qiantong he went from Grand Guardian of the Ugu and Dilie Tribal Garrisons to prefect of Yi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 幸臣劉彥良嘗以事至州，怙寵恣橫，為陽阿所沮。
entries.en: The favored minister Liu Yanliang once came to the prefecture on business and, relying on imperial favor, acted wantonly; Yanga blocked him.
entries.literal: The favored minister Liu Yanliang once came to the prefecture on business and, relying on favor, acted wantonly; Yanga blocked him.

entries.zh: 彥良歸，妄加毀訾，尋遣人代陽阿。
entries.en: Yanliang returned and slandered him without cause; before long an envoy was sent to replace Yanga.
entries.literal: Yanliang returned and slandered him without cause; before long someone was sent to replace Yanga.

entries.zh: 州民千餘詣闕請留，即日授武安州觀察使。
entries.en: More than a thousand people of the prefecture went to court asking that he remain, and that same day he was appointed Observation Commissioner of Wu'an Prefecture.
entries.literal: More than a thousand people of the prefecture went to court requesting that he remain; that same day he was appointed Observation Commissioner of Wu'an Prefecture.

entries.zh: 歷烏古涅裏、順義、彰信等軍節度使，權知東北路統軍使事。
entries.en: He served in turn as military commissioner of the Wugu Nieli, Shunyi, and Zhangxin armies and was given provisional charge of Northeast Route grand general affairs.
entries.literal: He successively served as military commissioner of the Wugu Nieli, Shunyi, and Zhangxin armies and was given provisional charge of Northeast Route grand general affairs.

entries.zh: 聞耶律狼不、鐸魯斡等叛，獨引麾下三十餘人追捕之，身被二創，生擒十餘人，送之行在。
entries.en: Hearing that Yelu Langbu, Duoluwo, and others had rebelled, he alone led a little more than thirty men in pursuit. He received two wounds, captured more than ten men alive, and sent them to the imperial camp.
entries.literal: Hearing that Yelu Langbu, Duoluwo, and others had rebelled, he alone led more than thirty men under his command in pursuit; he received two wounds, captured more than ten men alive, and sent them to the imperial camp.

entries.zh: 坐不獲首惡，免官。
entries.en: Because he failed to capture the chief culprit, he was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: Because he failed to capture the chief culprit, he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 未幾，權南京留守，卒。
entries.en: Before long he served provisionally as Nanjing Military Governor and died.
entries.literal: Before long he served provisionally as Nanjing Military Governor and died.

entries.zh: 武白，不知何郡人。
entries.en: Wu Bai was a man of unknown native commandery.
entries.literal: Wu Bai—of what commandery he came is unknown.

entries.zh: 為宋國子博士，差知相州，至通利軍，為我軍所俘。
entries.en: He had been a National University Erudite of Song and was dispatched to administer Xiangzhou. At Tongli Army he was taken prisoner by Liao forces.
entries.literal: He served as Song National University Erudite, was dispatched to know Xiangzhou, reached Tongli Army, and was captured by our army.

entries.zh: 詔授上京國子博士。
entries.en: An edict appointed him Shangjing National University Erudite.
entries.literal: By edict he was appointed Shangjing National University Erudite.

entries.zh: 改臨潢縣令，遷廣德軍節度副使。
entries.en: He was made magistrate of Linhuang county and then promoted to deputy military commissioner of Guangde Army.
entries.literal: He was changed to Linhuang county magistrate and transferred to Guangde Army deputy military commissioner.

entries.zh: 先是，有訟宰相劉慎行與子婦姚氏私者，有司出其罪。
entries.en: Earlier, a suit had accused Chancellor Liu Shenxing of impropriety with his son's wife, Lady Yao, and the authorities had found grounds for punishment.
entries.literal: Earlier, someone sued Chancellor Liu Shenxing and his son's wife Lady Yao for impropriety; the authorities established their guilt.

entries.zh: 聖宗詔白鞫之，白正其事。
entries.en: Emperor Shengzong ordered Bai to hear the case, and Bai upheld the accusation.
entries.literal: Emperor Shengzong ordered Bai to try the case; Bai upheld the charge.

entries.zh: 使高麗還，權中京留守。
entries.en: On his return from an embassy to Goryeo he was given provisional charge as Zhongjing Military Governor.
entries.literal: Returning from an embassy to Goryeo, he served provisionally as Zhongjing Military Governor.

entries.zh: 時慎行諸子皆處權要，以白斷百姓分籍事不直，坐左遷。
entries.en: Shenxing's sons then held every lever of power. Bai was demoted on the charge that his ruling in a dispute over commoners' household registers had been unjust.
entries.literal: At that time all of Shenxing's sons held positions of power; because Bai's ruling in the matter of commoners' household registers was deemed unjust, he was demoted by assignment.

entries.zh: 未幾，遷尚書左丞，知樞密事，拜遼興軍節度使。
entries.en: Before long he was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, put in charge of Privy Council affairs, and appointed Liaoxing Army Military Commissioner.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, given charge of Privy Council affairs, and appointed Liaoxing Army Military Commissioner.

entries.zh: 致仕，卒。
entries.en: He retired from office and died.
entries.literal: He retired from office and died.

entries.zh: 制心，小字可汗奴。
entries.en: Zhixin, whose childhood name was Khan Slave.
entries.literal: Zhixin, childhood name Khan Slave.

entries.zh: 父德崇，善醫，視人形色，輒決其病，累官至武定軍節度使。
entries.en: His father Dechong was a physician who could read illness at a glance from a patient's face and bearing; he rose through successive posts to Wuding Army Military Commissioner.
entries.literal: His father Dechong was skilled in medicine; observing a person's complexion he would at once determine the illness, and rose through repeated offices to Wuding Army Military Commissioner.

entries.zh: 制心善調鷹隼。
entries.en: Zhixin excelled at training hawks and falcons.
entries.literal: Zhixin was skilled at training hawks and falcons.

entries.zh: 統和中，為歸化州刺史。
entries.en: During the Tonghe era he was made prefect of Guihua.
entries.literal: During Tonghe he served as Guihua Prefecture prefect.

entries.zh: 開泰中，拜上京留守，進漢人行宮都部署，封漆水郡王。
entries.en: In the Kaitai era he was appointed Shangjing Military Governor, promoted to Commander of the Han Chinese Imperial Palace Detachment, and enfeoffed as Prince of Qishui.
entries.literal: During Kaitai he was appointed Shangjing Military Governor, advanced to Commander of the Han Chinese Imperial Palace Detachment, and enfeoffed as Prince of Qishui Commandery.

entries.zh: 以皇后外弟，恩遇日隆。
entries.en: As the empress's younger brother, his favor at court grew day by day.
entries.literal: As the empress's younger brother by a different mother, imperial favor daily grew.

entries.zh: 樞密副使蕭合卓用事，制心奏合卓寡識度，無行檢，上默然。
entries.en: Deputy Privy Councilor Xiao Hezhuo dominated affairs. Zhixin memorialized that Hezhuo was shallow in judgment and lax in conduct. The emperor said nothing.
entries.literal: Deputy Privy Councilor Xiao Hezhuo held power; Zhixin memorialized that Hezhuo lacked breadth of judgment and personal restraint; the emperor was silent.

entries.zh: 每內宴歡洽，輒避之。
entries.en: Whenever palace banquets grew convivial, he would withdraw.
entries.literal: Whenever inner banquets were merry and intimate, he would avoid them.

entries.zh: 皇后不悅曰：「汝不樂耶？」
entries.en: The empress, displeased, said: "Are you unhappy?"
entries.literal: The empress was displeased and said: "Are you not pleased?"

entries.zh: 制心對曰：「寵貴鮮能長保，以是為憂耳！」
entries.en: Zhixin answered: "Those who enjoy favor and high rank seldom keep them long—that is what troubles me!"
entries.literal: Zhixin replied: "Few who receive favor and exalted rank can long preserve them—therefore I am anxious!"

entries.zh: 太平中，歷中京留守、惕隱、南京留守，徙王燕，遷南院大王。
entries.en: In the Taiping era he served in turn as Zhongjing Military Governor, Privy Councilor, and Nanjing Military Governor, was transferred to Prince of Yan, and was promoted to Grand Prince of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: During Taiping he successively served as Zhongjing Military Governor, Privy Councilor, and Nanjing Military Governor, was transferred to Prince of Yan, and moved to Southern Chancellery Grand Prince.

entries.zh: 或勸制心奉佛，對曰：「吾不知佛法，惟心無私，則近之矣。」
entries.en: Some urged Zhixin to take up Buddhism. He replied: "I do not know the Buddhist teachings; only that when the heart is without selfishness, one draws near to them."
entries.literal: Some urged Zhixin to embrace Buddhism; he replied: "I do not know the Buddhist Law; only that when the heart is without selfishness, one draws near to it."

entries.zh: 一日，沐浴更衣而臥，家人聞絲竹之聲，怪而入視，則已逝矣。
entries.en: One day he bathed, changed his garments, and lay down. His household heard the sound of pipes and strings; alarmed, they entered and found he had already passed away.
entries.literal: One day he bathed, changed clothes, and lay down; his family heard music; startled they entered to look and found he had already departed.

entries.zh: 年五十三。
entries.en: He was fifty-three years old.
entries.literal: He was fifty-three.

entries.zh: 贈政事令，追封陳王。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Administrator of Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
entries.literal: Posthumously given Administrator of Affairs and retroactively enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.

entries.zh: 耶律隆運
entries.en: Yelu Longyun
entries.literal: Yelu Longyun

entries.zh: 〈（德威滌魯制心）〉
entries.en: (Dewei, Dilu, Zhixin)〉
entries.literal: (Dewei, Dilu, Zhixin)〉

entries.zh: 耶律勃古哲蕭陽阿武白蕭常哥耶律虎古
entries.en: Yelu Boguzhe, Xiao Yanga, Wu Bai, Xiao Changge, and Yelu Hugu
entries.literal: Yelu Boguzhe, Xiao Yanga, Wu Bai, Xiao Changge, Yelu Hugu

entries.zh: 〈（磨魯古）〉
entries.en: (Morlugu)〉
entries.literal: (Morlugu)〉

entries.zh: 耶律奚低，孟父楚國王之後。
entries.en: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage.
entries.literal: Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage.

entries.zh: 便弓馬，勇於攻戰。
entries.en: He was skilled with bow and horse and bold in attack.
entries.literal: Skilled with bow and horse, bold in attack and battle.

entries.zh: 景宗時，多任以軍事。
entries.en: Under Emperor Jingzong he was often entrusted with military command.
entries.literal: In Emperor Jingzong's time he was often entrusted with military affairs.

entries.zh: 統和四年，為右皮室詳穩。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Tonghe he became Right Pishi Xiangwen.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe he was Right Pishi Xiangwen.

entries.zh: 時宋將楊繼業陷山西郡縣，奚低從樞密使斜軫討之。
entries.en: When the Song general Yang Ye overran the Shanxi commanderies, Xidi followed Privy Council Commissioner Xiezhen against him.
entries.literal: At that time the Song general Yang Ye overran the commanderies and counties of Shanxi; Xidi followed the Privy Council commissioner Xiezhen to suppress him.

entries.zh: 凡戰必以身先，矢無虛發。
entries.en: In every battle he led from the front, and never wasted an arrow.
entries.literal: In every battle he must take the lead in person; no arrow went without its mark.

entries.zh: 繼業敗於朔州之南，匿深林中。
entries.en: Ye was defeated south of Shuozhou and hid in deep forest.
entries.literal: Ye was defeated south of Shuozhou and hid in a deep forest.

entries.zh: 奚低望袍影而射，繼業墮馬。
entries.en: Xidi caught sight of a robe's shadow and shot; Ye fell from his horse.
entries.literal: Xidi, sighting the shadow of a robe, shot; Ye fell from his horse.

entries.zh: 先是，軍令須生擒繼業，奚低以故不能為功。
entries.en: Earlier orders had required Ye to be taken alive, so for that reason Xidi could not claim the credit.
entries.literal: Earlier, army orders required Ye to be captured alive; for this reason Xidi could not claim the merit.

entries.zh: 後太后南伐，屢有戰績。
entries.en: On the empress dowager's later southern campaigns he won repeated victories.
entries.literal: Later on the empress dowager's southern campaign he repeatedly had battle achievements.

entries.zh: 以病卒。
entries.en: He died of illness.
entries.literal: He died of illness.

entries.zh: 耶律休哥，字遜寧。
entries.en: Yelu Xiuge, whose courtesy name was Xunning.
entries.literal: Yelu Xiuge, courtesy name Xunning.

entries.zh: 祖釋魯，隋國王。
entries.en: His grandfather Shilu had been King of Sui.
entries.literal: His grandfather was Shilu, King of Sui.

entries.zh: 父綰思，南院夷離堇。
entries.en: His father Wansi had served as Yilibi of the Southern Court.
entries.literal: His father was Wansi, Yilibi of the Southern Court.

entries.zh: 休哥少有公輔器。
entries.en: Even in youth Xiuge showed the makings of a chief minister.
entries.literal: Xiuge in youth had the makings of a chief minister.

entries.zh: 初烏古、室韋二部叛，休哥從北府宰相蕭幹討之。
entries.en: When the Ugu and Shiwei tribes first rebelled, Xiuge accompanied Northern Court Chancellor Xiao Gan to suppress them.
entries.literal: At first the two tribes Ugu and Shiwei rebelled; Xiuge followed the Northern Court chancellor Xiao Gan to suppress them.

entries.zh: 應歷末，為惕隱。
entries.en: At the close of the Yingli reign he was made Tiyi.
entries.literal: At the end of Yingli, he became Tiyi.

entries.zh: 乾亨元年，宋侵燕，北院大王奚底、統軍使蕭討古等敗績，南京被圍。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianheng, when Song invaded Yan, the Northern Court Great King Xidi, army commander Xiao Taogu, and others suffered defeat and the Southern Capital came under siege.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianheng, Song invaded Yan; the Northern Court great king Xidi, army commander Xiao Taogu, and others were defeated, and the Southern Capital was besieged.

entries.zh: 帝命休哥代奚底，將五院軍往救。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Xiuge to replace Xidi and march to the relief with the armies of the Five Corps.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Xiuge to replace Xidi and lead the Five Corps armies to the rescue.

entries.zh: 遇大敵於高梁河，與耶律斜軫分左右翼，擊敗之。
entries.en: At the Gaoliang River he met the main enemy force; he and Yelu Xiezhen took the left and right wings and put them to flight.
entries.literal: He met the main enemy force at the Gaoliang River; with Yelu Xiezhen he took left and right wings and defeated them.

entries.zh: 追殺三十餘里，斬首萬餘級，休哥被三創。
entries.en: The pursuit ran more than thirty li, and heads numbered above ten thousand; Xiuge himself took three wounds.
entries.literal: Pursuit and slaughter extended more than thirty li; over ten thousand heads were taken; Xiuge received three wounds.

entries.zh: 明旦，宋主遁去，休哥以創不能騎，輕車追至涿州，不及而還。
entries.en: At dawn the Song ruler fled. Too badly wounded to ride, Xiuge pursued in a light cart as far as Zhuozhou but could not catch up and turned back.
entries.literal: At dawn the next day the Song emperor fled; Xiuge, unable to ride because of his wounds, pursued in a light cart to Zhuozhou but failed to overtake them and returned.

entries.zh: 是年冬，上命韓匡嗣、耶律沙伐宋，以報圍城之役。
entries.en: That winter the emperor sent Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha against Song to repay the siege.
entries.literal: That winter the emperor ordered Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha to attack Song in reprisal for the siege.

entries.zh: 休哥率本部兵從匡嗣等戰於滿城。
entries.en: Xiuge led his own troops to join Kuangsi and fought at Mancheng.
entries.literal: Xiuge led his own troops to follow Kuangsi and the others in battle at Mancheng.

entries.zh: 翌日將復戰，宋人請降，匡嗣信之。
entries.en: When battle was to resume the next day, the Song troops offered surrender and Kuangsi believed them.
entries.literal: The next day, as battle was to be resumed, the Song troops asked to surrender and Kuangsi believed them.

entries.zh: 休哥曰：「彼眾整而銳，必不肯屈，乃誘我耳。
entries.en: Xiuge said, "Their ranks are tight and their troops are keen—they will never truly yield; this is a ruse.
entries.literal: Xiuge said: "Their force is ordered and keen; they will surely not submit—this is only to lure us.

entries.zh: 宜嚴兵以待。」
entries.en: We should keep the army under strict guard and wait."
entries.literal: We ought to hold the army in strict readiness and await them."

entries.zh: 匡嗣不聽。
entries.en: Kuangsi would not listen.
entries.literal: Kuangsi would not listen.

entries.zh: 休哥引兵憑高而視。
entries.en: Xiuge drew his men up on high ground to watch.
entries.literal: Xiuge drew up his troops on high ground to watch.

entries.zh: 須臾南兵大至，鼓噪疾馳。
entries.en: Presently the southern army arrived in force, beating drums and charging at full speed.
entries.literal: In a moment the southern troops arrived in force, shouting and galloping hard.

entries.zh: 匡嗣倉卒不知所為，士卒棄旗鼓而走，遂敗績。
entries.en: Kuangsi, caught off guard, did not know what to do; his men threw down flags and drums and fled, and the army was routed.
entries.literal: Kuangsi in haste knew not what to do; soldiers cast aside flags and drums and fled; thus defeat.

entries.zh: 休哥整兵進擊，敵乃卻。
entries.en: Xiuge reformed his lines and pressed forward, and only then did the enemy fall back.
entries.literal: Xiuge reformed his troops and pressed the attack; the enemy then withdrew.

entries.zh: 詔總南面戍兵，為北院大王。
entries.en: He was ordered to take command of all southern garrison troops and was made Great King of the Northern Court.
entries.literal: He was ordered to take overall command of the southern garrison troops and was made Great King of the Northern Court.

entries.zh: 明年，車駕親征，圍瓦橋關。
entries.en: The next year the emperor led a personal campaign and laid siege to Waqiao Pass.
entries.literal: The next year the emperor campaigned in person and besieged Waqiao Pass.

entries.zh: 宋兵來救，守將張師突圍出。
entries.en: Song troops marched to relieve the pass, and the defending general Zhang Shi broke out through the encirclement.
entries.literal: Song troops came to the relief; the defending general Zhang Shi broke out of the encirclement.

entries.zh: 帝親督戰，休哥斬師，餘眾退走入城。
entries.en: The emperor personally directed the battle; Xiuge killed Zhang Shi, and the survivors fled back into the city.
entries.literal: The emperor personally supervised the battle; Xiuge slew Shi, and the rest retreated into the city.

entries.zh: 宋陣於水南。
entries.en: The Song army drew up south of the river.
entries.literal: The Song army formed battle lines south of the water.

entries.zh: 將戰，帝以休哥馬介獨黃，慮為敵所識，乃賜玄甲、白馬易之。
entries.en: Before battle the emperor saw that Xiuge's horse wore a distinctive yellow saddle cloth that might mark him to the enemy, so he gave him black armor and a white horse in exchange.
entries.literal: Before the fight, because Xiuge's horse had a saddle cloth of distinctive yellow and he feared the enemy would know him, the emperor bestowed dark armor and a white horse in exchange.

entries.zh: 休哥率精騎渡水，擊敗之，追至莫州。
entries.en: Xiuge led crack cavalry across the river, routed them, and pursued as far as Mozhou.
entries.literal: Xiuge led picked cavalry across the water, defeated them, and pursued to Mozhou.

entries.zh: 橫屍滿道，靫矢俱罄，生獲數將以獻。
entries.en: Corpses choked the roads; quivers were empty of arrows; several generals were taken alive and presented to the throne.
entries.literal: Corpses lay across the road; quivers and arrows were all spent; several generals were captured alive and presented.

entries.zh: 帝悅，賜御馬、金盂，勞之曰：「爾勇過於名，若人人如卿，何憂不克？」
entries.en: Delighted, the emperor gave him an imperial horse and a golden bowl and praised him: "Your courage outstrips your fame. If every man were like you, how could we fail to prevail?"
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and bestowed his own horse and a golden bowl, encouraging him and saying: "Your courage surpasses your fame; if every man were like you, what worry would there be of not conquering?"

entries.zh: 師還，拜於越。
entries.en: When the army returned, he was appointed Yuyue.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Yuyue.

entries.zh: 耶律斜軫，字韓隱，於越曷魯之孫。
entries.en: Yelu Xiezhen, whose courtesy name was Hanyin, was a grandson of yuyue Helu.
entries.literal: Yelu Xiezhen, courtesy name Hanyin, was a grandson of yuyue Helu.

entries.zh: 性明敏，不事生產。
entries.en: He was bright and quick-witted by nature and did not concern himself with farming or trade.
entries.literal: By nature he was bright and keen and did not engage in production.

entries.zh: 保寧元年，樞密使蕭思溫薦斜軫有經國才，上曰：「朕知之，第佚蕩，豈可羈屈？」
entries.en: In Baoning 1, Privy Council Commissioner Xiao Siwen recommended Xiezhen as possessing talent to govern the state. The emperor said, "I know him, but he is free-spirited and unruly—how can he be confined to office?"
entries.literal: In the first year of Baoning, Commissioner of Military Affairs Xiao Siwen recommended Xiezhen as having talent to govern the state. The emperor said, "I know him—but he is unrestrained and dissolute; how can he be kept in harness?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「外雖佚蕩，中未可量。」
entries.en: He replied, "Though he appears unrestrained outwardly, what lies within cannot yet be judged."
entries.literal: He replied, "Outwardly he may seem unrestrained, but what lies within cannot yet be measured."

entries.zh: 乃召問以時政，占對剴切，帝器重之。
entries.en: He was then summoned and questioned on current affairs; his replies were sharp and apt, and the emperor came to esteem him highly.
entries.literal: He was then summoned and questioned on current affairs; his answers were incisive and exact, and the emperor valued him greatly.

entries.zh: 妻以皇后之侄，命節制西南面諸軍，仍援河東。
entries.en: The emperor married him to the empress's niece, appointed him to command the southwestern armies, and ordered him to reinforce Hedong.
entries.literal: He was given in marriage the empress's niece, ordered to take command of the armies of the Southwest, and still to support Hedong.

entries.zh: 改南院大王。
entries.en: He was made Great King of the Southern Court.
entries.literal: He was changed to Great King of the Southern Court.

entries.zh: 乾亨初，宋再攻河東，從耶律沙至白馬嶺遇敵，沙等戰不利；
entries.en: Early in Qianheng, when Song again attacked Hedong, he followed Yelu Sha to White Horse Ridge and encountered the enemy; Sha and the others were defeated;
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng, when Song again attacked Hedong, he followed Yelu Sha to White Horse Ridge and met the enemy; Sha and the others fought without success;

entries.zh: 斜軫赴之，令麾下萬矢齊發，敵氣褫而退。
entries.en: Xiezhen hurried to the scene, ordered his men to unleash ten thousand arrows at once, and the enemy lost heart and withdrew.
entries.literal: Xiezhen hurried to them, ordered his troops to let ten thousand arrows fly together, and the enemy's spirit was cowed and they withdrew.

entries.zh: 是年秋，宋下河東，乘勝襲燕，北院大王耶律奚底與蕭討古逆戰，敗績，退屯清河北。
entries.en: That autumn Song overran Hedong and, pressing their advantage, struck at Yan; Great King of the Northern Court Yelu Xidi and Xiao Taogu met them in battle, were routed, and fell back to encamp north of the Qing River.
entries.literal: That autumn Song descended on Hedong and, riding their victory, raided Yan; Great King of the Northern Court Yelu Xidi and Xiao Taogu met them in battle, suffered defeat, and withdrew to encamp north of the Qing River.

entries.zh: 斜軫取奚底等青幟軍於得勝口以誘敵，敵果爭赴。
entries.en: Xiezhen took Xidi's green-banner force at Desheng Pass to lure the enemy, and the enemy rushed to meet them as expected.
entries.literal: Xiezhen took Xidi's green-banner army at Desheng Pass to lure the enemy, and the enemy indeed rushed to engage.

entries.zh: 斜軫出其後，奮擊敗之。
entries.en: Xiezhen struck from behind and routed them.
entries.literal: Xiezhen came out behind them and struck hard, defeating them.

entries.zh: 及高梁之戰，與耶律休哥分左右翼夾擊，大敗宋軍。
entries.en: At the battle of Gaoliang he and Yelu Xiuge took the left and right wings in a pincer attack and routed the Song army.
entries.literal: At the battle of Gaoliang he and Yelu Xiuge took left and right wings in a pincer attack and inflicted a great defeat on the Song army.

entries.zh: 聖宗即位，太后稱制，令休哥總南面軍務，以便宜從事。
entries.en: When Emperor Shengzong ascended the throne and the empress dowager assumed regency, Xiuge was placed in overall charge of southern military affairs with full discretion.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shengzong took the throne, the empress dowager held regency and ordered Xiuge to take overall southern military affairs with discretion to act as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 休哥均戍兵，立更休法，勸農桑，修武備，邊境大治。
entries.en: Xiuge equalized the garrisons, instituted rotation and rest for the troops, promoted farming and sericulture, and strengthened defenses until the borderlands were thoroughly settled.
entries.literal: Xiuge equalized garrison troops, established rotation and rest regulations, encouraged farming and sericulture, repaired armaments, and the frontier was greatly well governed.

entries.zh: 統和四年，宋復來侵，其將範密、楊繼業出雲州；
entries.en: In the fourth year of Tonghe the Song invaded again: Fan Mi and Yang Ye advanced from Yunzhou;
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe, Song again invaded; its generals Fan Mi and Yang Ye came out from Yunzhou;

entries.zh: 曹彬、米信出雄、易，取歧溝、涿州，陷固安，置屯。
entries.en: while Cao Bin and Mi Xin marched from Xiong and Yi, seized Qigou and Zhuozhou, took Gu'an, and entrenched.
entries.literal: Cao Bin and Mi Xin came out from Xiong and Yi, took Qigou and Zhuozhou, captured Gu'an, and set up camps.

entries.zh: 時北南院、奚部兵未至，休哥力寡，不敢出戰。
entries.en: The armies of the Northern and Southern Courts and the Xi tribes had not yet arrived, and with his small force Xiuge did not dare to offer battle.
entries.literal: At that time the troops of the Northern and Southern Courts and the Xi tribes had not yet arrived; Xiuge's force was few and he dared not give battle.

entries.zh: 夜以輕騎出兩軍間，殺其單弱以脅餘眾；
entries.en: By night he sent light cavalry between the enemy armies to cut down stragglers and isolated parties and intimidate the rest;
entries.literal: By night he sent light cavalry out between the two armies, killing their isolated and weak to intimidate the rest;

entries.zh: 晝則以精銳張其勢，使彼勞於防禦，以疲其力。
entries.en: by day he paraded elite troops to inflate his apparent strength and wear them down with constant defense.
entries.literal: by day he displayed elite troops to magnify his force and make them weary at defense to exhaust their strength.

entries.zh: 又設伏林莽，絕其糧道。
entries.en: He laid ambushes in the woods as well and severed their supply lines.
entries.literal: He also set ambushes in woods and thickets and cut their supply routes.

entries.zh: 曹彬等以糧運不繼，退保白溝。
entries.en: When supplies failed, Cao Bin and his colleagues fell back to Baigou.
entries.literal: Cao Bin and the others, because grain transport did not continue, withdrew to defend Baigou.

entries.zh: 月餘，復至。
entries.en: After little more than a month they returned.
entries.literal: After a little more than a month, they came again.

entries.zh: 休哥以輕兵薄之，伺彼蓐食，擊其離伍單出者，且戰且卻。
entries.en: Xiuge harassed them with light troops, striking men who left the ranks alone at mealtimes, fighting and giving ground by turns.
entries.literal: Xiuge pressed them with light troops, watching for when they took mat rations, striking those who left formation alone, fighting while withdrawing.

entries.zh: 由是南軍自救不暇，結方陣，塹地兩邊而行。
entries.en: The southern army could barely defend itself; they formed squares and dug trenches on both flanks as they advanced.
entries.literal: Thereby the southern army had no leisure even to save themselves; they formed square arrays and dug ditches on both sides as they marched.

entries.zh: 軍渴乏井，漉淖而飲，凡四日始達於涿。
entries.en: Thirsty and short of wells, they strained muddy water to drink, and only after four days did they reach Zhuozhou.
entries.literal: The army thirsted and wells were scarce; they strained mud and drank; only after four days did they reach Zhuo.

entries.zh: 聞太后軍至，彬等冒雨而遁。
entries.en: When they heard the empress dowager's army was coming, Bin and his commanders fled through the rain.
entries.literal: Hearing the empress dowager's army had arrived, Bin and the others fled through rain.

entries.zh: 太后益以銳卒，追及之。
entries.en: The empress dowager reinforced the pursuit with crack troops and overtook them.
entries.literal: The empress dowager added crack troops and overtook them.

entries.zh: 彼力窮，環糧車自衛，休哥圍之。
entries.en: With their strength spent, they circled their grain wagons for protection; Xiuge surrounded them.
entries.literal: Their strength was spent; they ringed grain wagons to defend themselves; Xiuge besieged them.

entries.zh: 至夜，彬、信以數騎亡去，餘眾悉潰。
entries.en: By night Cao Bin and Mi Xin slipped away with a few horsemen while the rest broke and fled.
entries.literal: By night Bin and Xin escaped with several horsemen; the rest all scattered.

entries.zh: 追至易州東，聞宋師尚有數萬，瀕沙河而爨，促兵往擊之。
entries.en: The pursuit reached east of Yizhou, where he learned that tens of thousands of Song troops were cooking along the Sha River; he pressed his men to attack at once.
entries.literal: Pursuit reached east of Yizhou; hearing the Song army still numbered tens of thousands cooking along the Sha River, he urged troops to attack.

entries.zh: 宋師望塵奔竄，墮岸相蹂死者過半，沙河為之不流。
entries.en: The Song army fled at the first dust of the pursuit; more than half perished tumbling from the banks or trampling one another, and the Sha River was dammed with the dead.
entries.literal: The Song army fled at the sight of dust; more than half died falling from banks and trampling one another; the Sha River ceased to flow for it.

entries.zh: 太后旋旆，休哥收宋屍為京觀。
entries.en: As the empress dowager turned homeward, Xiuge heaped the Song dead into a victory mound.
entries.literal: The empress dowager turned her banners home; Xiuge gathered Song corpses into a victory mound.

entries.zh: 封宋國王。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as King of Song.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as King of Song.

entries.zh: 又上言，可乘宋弱，略地至河為界。
entries.en: He also memorialized that with Song weakened, they could seize territory as far as the river for a new border.
entries.literal: He also submitted a memorial saying that while Song was weak, territory might be taken with the river as border.

entries.zh: 書奏，不納。
entries.en: The memorial was rejected.
entries.literal: The memorial was presented and not accepted.

entries.zh: 及太后南征，休哥為先鋒，敗宋兵於望都。
entries.en: On the empress dowager's southern campaign, Xiuge served as vanguard and defeated the Song at Wangdu.
entries.literal: When the empress dowager campaigned south, Xiuge was vanguard and defeated Song troops at Wangdu.

entries.zh: 時宋將劉廷讓以數萬騎並海而出，約與李敬源合兵，聲言取燕。
entries.en: The Song general Liu Tingrang then led tens of thousands of cavalry along the coast, intending to join Li Jingyuan and proclaiming that they would take Yan.
entries.literal: At that time the Song general Liu Tingrang led tens of thousands of cavalry along the coast, agreeing to join forces with Li Jingyuan, proclaiming the taking of Yan.

entries.zh: 休哥聞之，先以兵扼其要地。
entries.en: Xiuge heard of this and preemptively seized the key positions.
entries.literal: Xiuge heard of it and first sent troops to block the strategic places.

entries.zh: 會太后軍至，接戰，殺敬源，廷讓走瀛州。
entries.en: When the empress dowager's army arrived they gave battle, killed Li Jingyuan, and Tingrang fled to Yingzhou.
entries.literal: When the empress dowager's army arrived they joined battle; Jingyuan was killed and Tingrang fled to Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 七年，宋遣劉廷讓等乘暑潦來攻易州，諸將憚之；
entries.en: In the seventh year Liu Tingrang and others exploited the summer floods to attack Yizhou, and the other generals were wary;
entries.literal: In the seventh year Song sent Liu Tingrang and others, taking advantage of summer floods to attack Yizhou; the generals were afraid of them;

entries.zh: 獨休哥率銳卒逆擊於沙河之北，殺傷數萬，獲輜重不可計，獻於朝。
entries.en: only Xiuge led crack troops to meet them north of the Sha River, killing and wounding tens of thousands and capturing baggage beyond count, all of which he presented at court.
entries.literal: only Xiuge alone led crack troops to meet the attack north of the Sha River, killing and wounding tens of thousands, capturing baggage beyond reckoning, and presenting it at court.

entries.zh: 太后嘉其功，詔免拜、不名。
entries.en: The empress dowager praised his achievements and decreed that he need not bow when appearing and that his name was not to be spoken aloud in his presence.
entries.literal: The empress dowager praised his merit and decreed exemption from bowing and from naming his name.

entries.zh: 自是宋不敢北向。
entries.en: From that time Song dared not campaign northward.
entries.literal: From this Song dared not turn northward.

entries.zh: 時宋人欲止兒啼，乃曰：「於越至矣！」
entries.en: In Song, mothers hushed crying infants by saying, "The Yuyue is here!"
entries.literal: At that time when Song people wished to stop a child crying they would say: "The Yuyue has come!"

entries.zh: 休哥以燕民疲弊，省賦役，恤孤寡，戒戍兵無犯宋境，雖馬牛逸於北者悉還之。
entries.en: Seeing the people of Yan worn out and impoverished, Xiuge reduced taxes and corvée labor, cared for widows and orphans, and ordered the garrison not to violate Song territory; even cattle and horses that strayed north were all sent back.
entries.literal: Xiuge, seeing the people of Yan worn out and impoverished, reduced taxes and corvée labor, cared for widows and orphans, and warned the garrison troops not to violate Song territory; even cattle and horses that strayed north were all returned.

entries.zh: 遠近向化，邊鄙以安。
entries.en: Near and far submitted to his rule, and the borderlands were settled.
entries.literal: Near and far turned toward his rule, and the borderlands were thereby settled.

entries.zh: 十六年，薨。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year he died.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.

entries.zh: 是夕，雨木冰。
entries.en: That night rain froze on trees.
entries.literal: That night rain froze on trees.

entries.zh: 聖宗詔立祠南京。
entries.en: Emperor Shengzong decreed that a shrine be established at the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: Emperor Shengzong decreed that a shrine be established at the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 馬哥，字訛特懶。
entries.en: Mage, whose courtesy name was Wotelan.
entries.literal: Mage, courtesy name Wotelan.

entries.zh: 興宗時，以散職入見，上問：「卿奉佛乎？」
entries.en: Under Emperor Xingzong he appeared at court in a minor post. The emperor asked, "Do you worship the Buddha?"
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xingzong he entered audience in a minor post; the emperor asked: "Do you worship the Buddha?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣每旦誦太祖、太宗及先臣遺訓，未暇奉佛。」
entries.en: He answered, "Each morning I recite the precepts left by Taizu, Taizong, and my late forebear; I have had no time for Buddhism."
entries.literal: He replied: "Each morning your servant recites the teachings left by Taizu, Taizong, and my forebear; I have no leisure to worship the Buddha."

entries.zh: 帝悅。
entries.en: The emperor was pleased.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased.

entries.zh: 清寧中，遷唐古部節度使。
entries.en: During the Qingning era he was made military commissioner of the Tanggu tribes.
entries.literal: In Qingning he was transferred to military commissioner of the Tanggu tribes.

entries.zh: 咸雍中，累遷匡義軍節度使。
entries.en: Under the Xianyong era he rose in stages to military commissioner of the Kuangyi Army.
entries.literal: In Xianyong he was repeatedly promoted to military commissioner of the Kuangyi Army.

entries.zh: 大康初，致仕，卒。
entries.en: At the beginning of Dakang he retired from office and died.
entries.literal: At the start of Dakang he retired; he died.

entries.zh: 耶律休哥
entries.en: Yelu Xiuge
entries.literal: Yelu Xiuge

entries.zh: 耶律沙，字安隱。
entries.en: Yelu Sha, whose courtesy name was Anyin.
entries.literal: Yelu Sha, courtesy name Anyin.

entries.zh: 其先嘗相遙輦氏。
entries.en: His family had once served as ministers to the Yaolian clan.
entries.literal: His ancestors had once been ministers to the Yaolian clan.

entries.zh: 應歷間，累官南府宰相。
entries.en: During the Yingli era he rose through successive posts to become Chancellor of the Southern Office.
entries.literal: During the Yingli reign, through repeated offices he reached Southern Chancellor.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，總領南面邊事。
entries.en: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, Sha was placed in overall charge of affairs along the southern frontier.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he took overall charge of southern frontier affairs.

entries.zh: 保寧間，宋攻河東，沙將兵救之，有功，加守太保。
entries.en: In the Baoning period, when the Song attacked Hedong, Sha led troops to its relief and distinguished himself; he was promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: During Baoning, Song attacked Hedong; Sha led troops to rescue it, had merit, and was promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 乾亨初，宋復北侵，沙將兵由間道至白馬嶺，阻大澗遇敵。
entries.en: Early in the Qianheng era, when the Song again pressed northward, Sha marched by a concealed route to White Horse Ridge, where a deep ravine brought him face to face with the enemy.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng, Song again invaded north; Sha led troops by a hidden route to White Horse Ridge, blocked by a great ravine where he met the enemy.

entries.zh: 沙與諸將欲待後軍至而戰，冀王敵烈、監軍耶律抹只等以為急擊之便，沙不能奪。
entries.en: Sha and his fellow commanders wanted to hold action until the rear guard came up; the Prince of Ji, Dilie, the army supervisor Yelu Mozhi, and others argued for an immediate assault, and Sha could not prevail against them.
entries.literal: Sha and the generals wished to wait until the rear army arrived before fighting; the Prince of Ji, Dilie, the army supervisor Yelu Mozhi, and others held that a swift attack would be advantageous, and Sha could not overrule them.

entries.zh: 敵烈等以先鋒渡澗，未半，為宋人所擊，兵潰。
entries.en: Dilie and his colleagues took the vanguard across the ravine, but before they were even halfway over the Song struck them and the force broke in rout.
entries.literal: Dilie and the others led the vanguard across the ravine; before they were halfway over, they were struck by the Song and the army collapsed.

entries.zh: 敵烈及其子蛙哥、沙之子德裏、令穩都敏、詳穩唐筈等五將俱沒。
entries.en: Dilie, his son Wage, Sha's son Deli, the lingwen Dumin, and the xiangwen Tanghua—five generals in all—were killed.
entries.literal: Dilie, his son Wage, Sha's son Deli, Lingwen Dumin, Xiangwen Tanghua, and five generals in all perished.

entries.zh: 會北院大王耶律斜軫兵至，萬矢俱發，敵軍始退。
entries.en: At that moment the Northern Chancellor Yelu Xiezhen arrived with his troops; when ten thousand arrows flew as one, the enemy at last drew back.
entries.literal: Just then the Northern Chancellor Yelu Xiezhen's troops arrived; ten thousand arrows flew together, and the enemy army only then withdrew.

entries.zh: 沙將趨太原，會漢駙馬都尉盧俊來奔，言太原已陷，遂勒兵還。
entries.en: Sha was pressing toward Taiyuan when the Han Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Lu Jun came over to his side and reported that Taiyuan had already fallen; Sha thereupon turned his army back.
entries.literal: Sha was about to hurry to Taiyuan when the Han Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Lu Jun came fleeing to him, saying Taiyuan had already fallen, and he thereupon reined in the army and returned.

entries.zh: 宋乘銳侵燕，沙與戰於高梁河，稍卻；
entries.en: The Song, emboldened by their momentum, thrust into Yan; Sha met them at the Gaoliang River and gave ground;
entries.literal: The Song, riding their momentum, invaded Yan; Sha fought them at Gaoliang River and fell back slightly;

entries.zh: 遇耶律休哥及斜軫等邀擊，敗宋軍。
entries.en: but then Yelu Xiuge, Xiezhen, and others cut across their path and routed the Song army.
entries.literal: he encountered Yelu Xiuge and Xiezhen and others intercepting and striking, and defeated the Song army.

entries.zh: 宋主宵遁，至涿州，微服乘驢車，間道而走。
entries.en: The Song emperor fled under cover of night; reaching Zhuozhou, he went in disguise in a donkey cart along back roads to safety.
entries.literal: The Song ruler fled by night; reaching Zhuozhou, in plain dress he rode a donkey cart and escaped by byways.

entries.zh: 上以功釋前過。
entries.en: The emperor pardoned his earlier failures in light of this success.
entries.literal: The emperor, for this merit, released his earlier fault.

entries.zh: 是年，復從韓匡嗣伐宋，敗績，帝欲誅之，以皇后營救得免。
entries.en: That same year he again joined Han Kuangsi in a campaign against the Song and met with defeat; the emperor meant to put him to death, but the empress pleaded for him and he was spared.
entries.literal: That year he again followed Han Kuangsi in attacking Song, suffered defeat, and the emperor wished to execute him; through the empress's intercession he was spared.

entries.zh: 睿智皇后稱制，召賜几杖，以優其老。
entries.en: When the Sagacious Empress Dowager assumed the regency, she summoned him and granted him a folding stool and staff as marks of esteem for his advanced years.
entries.literal: When the Sagacious Empress Dowager held the regency, she summoned him and bestowed a folding stool and staff to honor his age.

entries.zh: 復從伐宋，敗劉廷讓、李敬源之軍，賜賚優渥。
entries.en: He took the field once more against the Song, routed the forces of Liu Tingrang and Li Jingyuan, and received a generous grant of rewards.
entries.literal: He again followed in attacking Song, defeated the armies of Liu Tingrang and Li Jingyuan, and received lavish rewards.

entries.zh: 統和六年卒。
entries.en: He died in the sixth year of the Tonghe reign.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tonghe he died.

entries.zh: 蕭幹，小字項烈，字婆典，北府宰相敵魯之子。
entries.en: Xiao Gan, whose childhood name was Xianglie and courtesy name Podian, was the son of the Northern Chancellor Diru.
entries.literal: Xiao Gan, childhood name Xianglie, courtesy name Podian, son of the Northern Chancellor Diru.

entries.zh: 性質直。
entries.en: By nature he was forthright and plain-spoken.
entries.literal: His nature was upright and plain.

entries.zh: 初，察割之亂，其黨胡古只與幹善，使人召之。
entries.en: Early in Chagai's rebellion, one of his partisans, Huguzhi, who was on friendly terms with Gan, sent envoys to summon him.
entries.literal: Earlier, during Chagai's rebellion, his partisan Huguzhi was on good terms with Gan and sent someone to summon him.

entries.zh: 幹曰：「吾豈能從逆臣！」
entries.en: Gan replied, "How could I follow a traitor!"
entries.literal: Gan said: "How could I follow a rebellious minister!"

entries.zh: 縛其人送壽安王。
entries.en: He bound the envoy and sent him to the Prince of Shou'an.
entries.literal: He bound the man and sent him to the Prince of Shou'an.

entries.zh: 賊平，上嘉其忠，拜群牧都林牙。
entries.en: After the rebels were suppressed, the emperor commended his loyalty and appointed him Chief Forest Master of the Herds.
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the emperor praised his loyalty and appointed him Chief Forest Master of the Herds.

entries.zh: 復以伐烏古功，遷北府宰相，改突呂不部節度使。
entries.en: He was later promoted to Northern Chancellor for his service against the Wugu and made Military Commissioner of the Tulübu tribe.
entries.literal: Again, for merit in attacking the Wugu, he was transferred to Northern Chancellor and made Military Commissioner of the Tulübu tribe.

entries.zh: 乾亨初，宋伐河東，乘勝侵燕，詔幹拒之，戰於高梁河。
entries.en: Early in Qianheng, when the Song attacked Hedong and, riding their victory, pressed into Yan, the court ordered Gan to hold them off; he gave battle at the Gaoliang River.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng, Song attacked Hedong and, pressing their advantage, invaded Yan; the emperor ordered Gan to resist them, and he fought at Gaoliang River.

entries.zh: 耶律沙退走，幹與耶律休哥等並力戰敗之，上手敕慰勞。
entries.en: Yelu Sha had already fallen back, but Gan joined Yelu Xiuge and others in a combined assault that broke the enemy; the emperor sent a personal edict of commendation.
entries.literal: Yelu Sha had retreated; Gan together with Yelu Xiuge and others joined forces, defeated the enemy, and the emperor sent a hand-written edict to console and reward them.

entries.zh: 自是每征伐必參決軍事。
entries.en: From then on he took part in every major military decision.
entries.literal: From this time on, in every campaign he was sure to take part in deciding military affairs.

entries.zh: 加政事令。
entries.en: He was further appointed Chief of Political Affairs.
entries.literal: He was given the additional title of Chief of Political Affairs.

entries.zh: 二年，宋兵圍瓦橋，夜襲我營，幹及耶律勻骨戰卻之。
entries.en: In the second year, when Song forces besieged Wagiao and raided the Liao camp by night, Gan and Yelu Jungu drove them back.
entries.literal: In the second year, Song troops besieged Wagiao; at night they raided our camp, and Gan together with Yelu Jungu fought them off.

entries.zh: 時皇后以父呼幹。
entries.en: The empress addressed him as "Father."
entries.literal: At the time the empress addressed Gan as "Father."

entries.zh: 及後為皇太后稱制，幹數條奏便宜，多見聽用。
entries.en: Later, when she ruled as empress dowager, Gan submitted one practical proposal after another, and many of his recommendations were adopted.
entries.literal: Later, when she became empress dowager regent, Gan repeatedly submitted proposals of practical benefit, and many were adopted.

entries.zh: 統和四年卒。
entries.en: He died in the fourth year of the Tonghe reign.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe he died.

entries.zh: 侄討古。
entries.en: His nephew was Taogu.
entries.literal: Nephew Taogu.

entries.zh: 耶律抹只，字留隱，仲父隋國王之後。
entries.en: Yelu Mozhi, whose courtesy name was Liuyin, was of the younger line of the King of Sui.
entries.literal: Yelu Mozhi, courtesy name Liuyin, was of the younger line of the King of Sui.

entries.zh: 初以皇族入侍。
entries.en: He first entered palace service as a member of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: At first he entered attendance by virtue of imperial clan status.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，為林牙，以幹給稱。
entries.en: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, he was made linya and won repute for resourceful service.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he became linya and was praised for resourceful service.

entries.zh: 保寧間，遷樞密副使。
entries.en: In the Baoning period he was promoted to vice privy commissioner.
entries.literal: During Baoning he was transferred to vice privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 乾亨元年春，宋攻河東，南府宰相耶律沙為都統，將兵往援，抹只臨其軍。
entries.en: In the spring of the first year of Qianheng, when the Song attacked Hedong, Southern Chancellor Yelu Sha was made supreme commander and marched to its relief; Mozhi supervised the army.
entries.literal: In spring of the first year of Qianheng, Song attacked Hedong; the Southern Chancellor Yelu Sha served as supreme commander, led troops to relieve it, and Mozhi supervised his army.

entries.zh: 及白馬嶺之敗，僅以身免。
entries.en: After the defeat at White Horse Ridge he barely escaped with his life.
entries.literal: At the defeat at White Horse Ridge he barely escaped with his life.

entries.zh: 宋乘銳攻燕，將奚兵翊休哥擊敗之。
entries.en: The Song, emboldened by their momentum, thrust into Yan; Mozhi led Xi troops to assist Yelu Xiuge and routed them.
entries.literal: The Song, riding their momentum, attacked Yan; leading Xi troops he assisted Xiuge and defeated them.

entries.zh: 上以功釋前過。
entries.en: The emperor pardoned his earlier failures in light of this success.
entries.literal: The emperor, for this merit, released his earlier fault.

entries.zh: 是年冬，從都統韓匡嗣伐宋，戰於滿城，為宋將所紿，諸軍奔潰；
entries.en: That winter he followed Supreme Commander Han Kuangsi against the Song and fought at Mancheng; tricked by a Song commander, the armies broke in rout;
entries.literal: That winter he followed the supreme commander Han Kuangsi in attacking Song and fought at Mancheng; deceived by a Song general, the armies broke in rout;

entries.zh: 獨抹只部伍不亂，徐整旗鼓而歸。
entries.en: only Mozhi’s unit held its formation, and he slowly reformed his banners and drums and withdrew in order.
entries.literal: only Mozhi’s ranks did not fall into disorder, and he slowly reformed banners and drums and returned.

entries.zh: 璽書褒諭，改南海軍節度使。
entries.en: An imperial commendation arrived in seal script, and he was made Military Commissioner of the Nanhai Army.
entries.literal: An imperial edict in seal script commended and instructed him, and he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Nanhai Army.

entries.zh: 乾亨二年，拜樞密副使。
entries.en: In the second year of Qianheng he was appointed vice privy commissioner.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qianheng he was appointed vice privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 統和初，為東京留守。
entries.en: Early in Tonghe he was made regent of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe he became regent of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 宋將曹彬、米信等侵邊，抹只引兵至南京，先繕守禦備。
entries.en: When the Song generals Cao Bin, Mi Xin, and others invaded the frontier, Mozhi marched to Nanjing and first strengthened the city’s defenses.
entries.literal: When the Song generals Cao Bin, Mi Xin, and others invaded the frontier, Mozhi led troops to Nanjing and first repaired defenses and preparations.

entries.zh: 及車駕臨幸，抹只與耶律休哥逆戰於涿之東，克之，遷開遠軍節度使。
entries.en: When the emperor arrived on inspection, Mozhi and Yelu Xiuge gave battle east of Zhuo, carried the day, and Mozhi was transferred to Military Commissioner of Kaiyuan Army.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived on inspection, Mozhi together with Yelu Xiuge met the enemy in battle east of Zhuo, took it, and was transferred to Military Commissioner of Kaiyuan Army.

entries.zh: 故事，州民歲輸稅，鬥粟折錢五，抹只表請折錢六，部民便之。
entries.en: By precedent the people of the commandery paid yearly taxes with each dou of grain valued at five cash; Mozhi memorialized to raise the rate to six cash, and the people welcomed the change.
entries.literal: By precedent the commandery people paid yearly taxes with each dou of grain converted at five cash; Mozhi memorialized requesting conversion at six cash, and the people of the division found it convenient.

entries.zh: 統和末卒。
entries.en: He died late in the Tonghe reign.
entries.literal: At the end of Tonghe he died.

entries.zh: 耶律善補，字瑤升，孟父楚國王之後。
entries.en: Yelu Shanbu, whose courtesy name was Yaosheng, was a descendant of the Mengfu line of the King of Chu.
entries.literal: Yelu Shanbu, courtesy name Yaosheng, descendant of the Mengfu King of Chu.

entries.zh: 純謹有才智。
entries.en: He was conscientious, prudent, and gifted with ability.
entries.literal: Pure, careful, and possessed of talent and wisdom.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，授千牛衛大將軍，遷大同軍節度使。
entries.en: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne, he was made Grand General of the Thousand-Ox Guard and then Military Commissioner of the Datong Army.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he was appointed Grand General of the Thousand-Ox Guard and transferred to Military Commissioner of Datong Army.

entries.zh: 及伐宋，韓匡嗣與耶律沙將兵由東路進，善補以南京統軍使由西路進。
entries.en: In the campaign against the Song, Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha advanced along the eastern route while Shanbu, as Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Capital, moved up the western route.
entries.literal: When they attacked Song, Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha led troops in by the eastern route; Shanbu as Southern Capital Commander-in-Chief advanced by the western route.

entries.zh: 善補聞匡嗣失利，斂兵還。
entries.en: When Shanbu learned that Kuangsi had been defeated, he drew his troops back.
entries.literal: Shanbu heard that Kuangsi had suffered defeat and gathered in his troops and returned.

entries.zh: 乾亨末，與宋軍戰於滿城，為伏兵所圍，斜軫救之獲免。
entries.en: Late in Qianheng he fought the Song at Mancheng, was caught in an ambush, and was saved only when Xiezhen came to his relief.
entries.literal: At the end of Qianheng he fought Song troops at Mancheng, was surrounded by ambush troops, and Xiezhen rescued him so he escaped harm.

entries.zh: 以失備，大杖決之。
entries.en: For his lack of preparedness he was sentenced to a severe beating.
entries.literal: For lack of preparedness he was sentenced to heavy cudgeling.

entries.zh: 統和初，為惕隱。
entries.en: Early in Tonghe he was made tiyin.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe he became tiyin.

entries.zh: 會宋來侵，善補為都元帥逆之，不敢戰，故嶺西州郡多陷，罷惕隱。
entries.en: When the Song invaded again, Shanbu went out as supreme commander to meet them but would not give battle; many districts west of the passes therefore fell, and he was dismissed from the office of tiyin.
entries.literal: When Song came to invade, Shanbu as supreme commander went to meet them but did not dare fight; therefore many prefectures and districts west of the passes fell, and he was removed as tiyin.

entries.zh: 以其叔安端有匡輔世宗功，上湣之，征善補為南府宰相，遷南院大王。
entries.en: Because his uncle Anduan had helped secure Emperor Shizong's succession, the court showed him favor: Shanbu was recalled to serve as Southern Chancellor and promoted to Great King of the Southern Office.
entries.literal: Because his uncle Anduan had the merit of supporting and assisting Emperor Shizong, the emperor pitied him and summoned Shanbu to be Southern Chancellor, transferring him to Great King of the Southern Office.

entries.zh: 會再舉伐宋，欲攻魏府，召眾集議。
entries.en: On a later campaign against the Song, when the court planned to strike Weizhou, he called the commanders together for counsel.
entries.literal: When they again raised troops to attack Song and wished to assault Weizhou, he summoned the host to assemble for deliberation.

entries.zh: 將士以魏城無備，皆言可攻。
entries.en: The officers and men, seeing Weizhou undefended, all urged an assault.
entries.literal: The officers and soldiers, because Weizhou was undefended, all said it could be attacked.

entries.zh: 善補曰：「攻固易，然城大叵量，若克其城，士卒貪俘掠，勢必不可遏。
entries.en: Shanbu said, "The assault would be easy enough, but the city is vast; if we took it, the men would gorge on captives and loot, and the rush would be impossible to hold in check.
entries.literal: Shanbu said: "The attack is indeed easy, yet the city is large beyond measure; if we take it, the soldiers will be greedy for captives and plunder, and the momentum will surely be impossible to restrain.

entries.zh: 且傍多巨鎮，各出援兵，內有重敵，何以當之？」
entries.en: Besides, great fortified towns lie all around; each would send relief, and we would face powerful enemies on every side—how could we stand against them?"
entries.literal: Moreover, nearby are many great strongholds; each will send relief troops—within we would have a heavy enemy; how could we withstand it?"

entries.zh: 上乃止。
entries.en: The emperor thereupon abandoned the plan.
entries.literal: The emperor then stopped.

entries.zh: 善補性懦，守靜。
entries.en: By nature Shanbu was timid and preferred quiet.
entries.literal: Shanbu's nature was timid; he kept to quietude.

entries.zh: 凡征討，憚攻戰，急還，以故戰多不利。
entries.en: On campaign he shrank from battle and withdrew at the first opportunity, and for this reason his engagements usually went badly.
entries.literal: In every campaign he dreaded fighting, hurried back, and for this reason battles were often unfavorable.

entries.zh: 年七十四卒。
entries.en: He died at the age of seventy-four.
entries.literal: At age seventy-four he died.

entries.zh: 耶律沙 耶律抹只 蕭幹附:討古 耶律善補 耶律海裏
entries.en: Yelu Sha, Yelu Mozhi, Xiao Gan, appended biography Taogu, Yelu Shanbu, and Yelu Haili
entries.literal: Yelu Sha, Yelu Mozhi, Xiao Gan with appendix: Taogu, Yelu Shanbu, Yelu Haili

entries.zh: 耶律奴瓜，字延寧，太祖異母弟南府宰相蘇之孫。
entries.en: Yelu Nugua, whose style name was Yanning, was a grandson of Su, Southern Chancellery Chancellor and younger half-brother of the dynastic founder.
entries.literal: Yelu Nugua, style name Yanning, was grandson of Su, Southern Chancellery Chancellor and the Founding Emperor's younger half-brother.

entries.zh: 有膂力，善調鷹隼。
entries.en: He possessed exceptional strength and was adept at training hawks and falcons.
entries.literal: He had great physical strength and was skilled at training hawks and falcons.

entries.zh: 統和四年，宋楊繼業來侵，奴瓜為黃皮室糺都監，擊敗之，盡復所陷城邑。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when Yang Ye invaded from Song territory, Nugua—then chief of the Yellow Pishi Regiment—defeated him and recovered every town the Song had taken.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when Song's Yang Ye came to invade, Nugua as Chief Commander of the Yellow Pishi Regiment defeated him and fully recovered the lost cities and towns.

entries.zh: 軍還，加諸衛小將軍。
entries.en: On the army's return he was promoted to Junior General of the Guards.
entries.literal: When the army returned he was given the rank of Junior General of the Guards.

entries.zh: 及伐宋，有功，遷黃皮室詳穩。
entries.en: On the campaign against Song he distinguished himself and was made Commander of the Yellow Pishi.
entries.literal: When they attacked Song he had merit and was transferred to Commander of the Yellow Pishi.

entries.zh: 六年，再舉，將先鋒軍，敗宋遊兵於定州，為東京統軍使，加金紫崇祿大夫。
