entries.en: In the sixth year, on a renewed invasion, he commanded the vanguard, routed Song scouts at Dingzhou, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Capital, and received the rank of Golden Purple Glory Grandee.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, on a renewed campaign, he led the vanguard army, defeated Song skirmishers at Dingzhou, became Eastern Capital Commander-in-Chief, and was given the title of Golden Purple Glory Grandee.

entries.zh: 從奚王和朔奴伐兀惹，以戰失利，削金紫崇祿階。
entries.en: He followed the Xi King Heshuonu against the Wunai tribe but met defeat and was demoted from his Golden Purple Glory rank.
entries.literal: Following the Xi King Heshuonu in attacking the Wunai, he suffered defeat in battle and was stripped of his Golden Purple Glory rank.

entries.zh: 十九年，拜南府宰相。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Southern Chancellery Chancellor.

entries.zh: 二十一年，復伐宋，擒其將王繼忠於望都，俘殺甚眾，以功加同政事門下平章事。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year he again campaigned against Song, captured the Song general Wang Jizhong at Wangdu, and killed or took a great multitude of prisoners; for this he was made Associate Director of the Directorate of Affairs.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year he again attacked Song, captured their general Wang Jizhong at Wangdu, and took or killed very many; for his merit he was given the additional post of Associate Director of the Directorate of Affairs.

entries.zh: 二十六年，為遼興軍節度使，尋復為南府宰相。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year he was made Military Commissioner of the Liaoxing circuit and soon returned to the chancellorship of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he became Military Commissioner of Liaoxing Army and soon again became Southern Chancellery Chancellor.

entries.zh: 開泰初，加尚父，卒。
entries.en: Early in the Kaitai era he received the honorific title of Esteemed Father and soon after died.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaitai he was given the title of Esteemed Father and died.

entries.zh: 高勛，字鼎臣，晉北平王信韜之子。
entries.en: Gao Xun, whose style name was Dingchen, was a son of Xin Tao, Prince of Beiping under the Jin.
entries.literal: Gao Xun, style name Dingchen, was son of Jin Prince of Beiping Xin Tao.

entries.zh: 性通敏。
entries.en: He was quick-witted and perceptive by nature.
entries.literal: By nature he was quick and perceptive.

entries.zh: 仕晉為閣門使。
entries.en: Under the Jin he served as Gate Commissioner.
entries.literal: He served Jin as Gate Commissioner.

entries.zh: 會同九年，與杜重威來降。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Huitong (946) he surrendered to Liao together with Du Chongwei.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Huitong he came to surrender with Du Chongwei.

entries.zh: 太宗入汴，授四方館使。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong entered Bian (Kaifeng) he was appointed Commissioner of the Four Directions Bureau.
entries.literal: When Emperor Taizong entered Bian he was appointed Commissioner of the Four Directions Bureau.

entries.zh: 好結權貴，能服勤大臣，多推譽之。
entries.en: He cultivated ties with powerful figures, served senior ministers diligently, and won their frequent praise.
entries.literal: He liked to cultivate ties with the powerful and could attend diligently on great ministers, who often praised him.

entries.zh: 天祿間，為樞密使，總漢軍事。
entries.en: During the Tianlu era he became Grand Councilor with overall charge of Han military affairs.
entries.literal: During Tianlu he became Grand Councilor and oversaw Han military affairs.

entries.zh: 五年，劉崇遣使來求封冊，詔勛冊崇為大漢神武皇帝。
entries.en: In the fifth year Liu Chong sent envoys requesting formal investiture, and the court ordered Xun to invest him as Emperor Shenwu of Great Han.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Liu Chong sent envoys requesting investiture; an edict ordered Xun to invest Chong as Emperor Shenwu of Great Han.

entries.zh: 應歷初，封趙王，出為上京留守，尋移南京。
entries.en: Early in the Yingli era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao, appointed regent of the Supreme Capital, and soon transferred to the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yingli he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao, went out as regent of the Supreme Capital, and soon was moved to the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 會宋欲城益津，勛上書請假巡僥以擾之，帝然其奏，宋遂不果城。
entries.en: When Song planned to fortify Yijin, Xun memorialized asking permission to patrol the frontier and harass their works. The emperor approved, and Song abandoned the project.
entries.literal: When Song wished to fortify Yijin, Xun memorialized requesting leave to patrol the border and harass them; the emperor approved his memorial and Song therefore did not complete the fortification.

entries.zh: 十七年，宋略地益津關，勛擊敗之，知南院樞密事。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year, when Song forces seized ground around the Yijin passes, Xun defeated them and was appointed Director of Southern Chancellery Council affairs.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year Song seized territory around the Yijin passes; Xun defeated them and was made Director of Southern Chancellery Council affairs.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，以定策功，進王秦。
entries.en: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, Xun was advanced to Prince of Qin for his role in securing the succession.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, for his merit in settling the succession he was advanced to Prince of Qin.

entries.zh: 保寧中，以南京郊內多隙地，請疏畦種稻，帝欲從之。
entries.en: During Baoning he noted much unused land in the Southern Capital suburbs and memorialized to open paddy fields; the emperor was inclined to approve.
entries.literal: During Baoning, because within the Southern Capital suburbs there was much vacant land, he requested to open fields and plant rice; the emperor wished to agree.

entries.zh: 林邪耶律昆宣言於朝曰：「高勛此奏，必有異志。
entries.en: Academician Yelu Kun declared at court, "Gao Xun's proposal surely conceals ulterior motives.
entries.literal: Academician Yelu Kun proclaimed at court, "This memorial of Gao Xun surely conceals a different intent.

entries.zh: 果令種稻，引水為畦，設以京叛，官軍何自而入？」
entries.en: If rice fields are opened and irrigation ditches cut through the suburbs, and the capital then rebels, how will government troops enter at all?"
entries.literal: If rice is indeed planted, drawing water for fields—suppose the capital rebels, how would government troops enter of themselves?"

entries.zh: 帝疑之，不納。
entries.en: The emperor grew suspicious and rejected the plan.
entries.literal: The emperor became suspicious and did not adopt it.

entries.zh: 尋遷南院樞密使。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to Grand Councilor of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Southern Chancellery Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 以毒藥饋駙馬都尉蕭啜裏，事覺，流銅州。
entries.en: He sent poison to Imperial Son-in-Law Xiao Chuoli; when the plot was exposed he was exiled to Tongzhou.
entries.literal: He presented poison to Imperial Son-in-Law Xiao Chuoli; when the matter was discovered he was exiled to Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 尋又謀害尚書令蕭思溫，詔獄誅之，沒其產，皆賜思溫家。
entries.en: He soon plotted again, this time against Chief Minister Xiao Siwen. By imperial order he was executed in prison; his property was confiscated and given entirely to Siwen's family.
entries.literal: Soon he again plotted to harm Chief Minister Xiao Siwen; by imperial order he was executed in prison, his property confiscated, and all given to Siwen's family.

entries.zh: 耶律撒合，字率懶，乙室部人，南府宰相歐禮斯子。
entries.en: Yelu Sahe, whose style name was Shuailan, came from the Yishi Division and was a son of Southern Chancellery Chancellor Oulisi.
entries.literal: Yelu Sahe, style name Shuailan, was of the Yishi Division, son of Southern Chancellor Oulisi.

entries.zh: 天祿間始仕。
entries.en: He entered government service during the Tianlu era.
entries.literal: He began service during Tianlu.

entries.zh: 應歷中，拜乙室大王，兼知兵馬事。
entries.en: During Yingli he was appointed Great King of the Yishi Division with concurrent authority over military affairs.
entries.literal: During Yingli he was appointed Great King of Yishi and concurrently in charge of military affairs.

entries.zh: 乾亨初，宋來侵，詔以本部兵守南京，與北院大王奚底、統軍蕭討古等逆戰，奚底等敗走，獨撒合全軍還。
entries.en: Early in Qianheng, when Song invaded, an edict ordered his tribal troops to defend the Southern Capital. He joined Northern Chancellery Great King Xidi, Commander Xiao Taogu, and others to meet the enemy; Xidi's forces were routed, but Sahe alone brought his army back intact.
entries.literal: Early in Qianheng, when Song invaded, an edict ordered his tribal troops to defend the Southern Capital; with Northern Chancellery Great King Xidi, Commander Xiao Taogu, and others he met them in battle; Xidi and others fled defeated, but Sahe alone returned with his army intact.

entries.zh: 上諭之曰：「拒敵當如此。
entries.en: The emperor told him, "This is how one should resist the enemy.
entries.literal: The emperor told him, "To resist the enemy should be like this.

entries.zh: 卿勉之，無憂不富貴。」
entries.en: Press on, and you need not fear that wealth and honor will elude you."
entries.literal: You exert yourself—do not worry that wealth and honor will not come."

entries.zh: 加守太保。
entries.en: He was then given the additional rank of Guardian Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: He was given the additional post of Guardian Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 統和間卒。
entries.en: He died during the Tonghe era.
entries.literal: He died during Tonghe.

entries.zh: 蕭撻凜蕭觀音奴耶律題子耶律諧理耶律奴瓜蕭柳高勛奚和朔奴蕭塔列葛耶律撒合
entries.en: Xiao Talin, Xiao Guanyinnu, Yelu Tizi, Yelu Xieli, Yelu Nugua, Xiao Liu, Gao Xun, Xi Heshuonu, Xiao Taliege, and Yelu Sahe.
entries.literal: Xiao Talin, Xiao Guanyinnu, Yelu Tizi, Yelu Xieli, Yelu Nugua, Xiao Liu, Gao Xun, Xi Heshuonu, Xiao Taliege, Yelu Sahe.

entries.zh: 耶律合住，字粘袞，太祖弟叠剌之孫。
entries.en: Yelu Hezhu, whose style name was Niangun, was a grandson of Diela, a younger brother of Taizu.
entries.literal: Yelu Hezhu, style name Niangun, was a grandson of Taizu's younger brother Diela.

entries.zh: 幼不好弄，臨事明敏，善談論。
entries.en: From childhood he shunned idle play; in office he was quick and perceptive, and an able conversationalist.
entries.literal: As a child he did not care for play; in affairs he was bright and keen, and skilled in discourse.

entries.zh: 初以近族入侍，每從征伐有功。
entries.en: He first entered court service as a near kinsman of the throne and repeatedly distinguished himself on campaign.
entries.literal: At first, as a close kinsman, he entered palace service and repeatedly followed campaigns with merit.

entries.zh: 保寧初，加右龍虎衛上將軍。
entries.en: Early in the Baoning era he received the additional post of General-in-Chief of the Right Dragon-Tiger Guards.
entries.literal: At the start of the Baoning era he was given the additional rank of General-in-Chief of the Right Dragon-Tiger Guards.

entries.zh: 以宋師屢梗南邊，拜涿州刺史，西南兵馬都監、招安、巡檢等使，賜推忠奉國功臣。
entries.en: As Song armies repeatedly harassed the southern border, he was made prefect of Zhuo, Southwest Military Commissioner, and Pacification and Patrol Commissioner, among other posts, and granted the merit title Loyal and Faithful Servant of the State.
entries.literal: Because Song forces repeatedly obstructed the southern frontier, he was appointed prefect of Zhuo, Southwest Military Commissioner, Pacification Commissioner, Patrol Commissioner, and the like, and granted the title Merit Subject of Loyalty and Service to the State.

entries.zh: 合住久任邊防，雖有克獲功，然務鎮靜，不妄生事以邀近功。
entries.en: Hezhu served long on the frontier. Though he won his share of victories, he kept the border calm and would not stir up trouble merely to win quick acclaim.
entries.literal: Hezhu long held frontier posts; though he had victories in capture, he nevertheless sought calm and did not rashly provoke incidents to win quick credit.

entries.zh: 鄰壤敬畏，屬部乂安。
entries.en: Neighboring territories respected him, and the tribes under his charge lived in peace.
entries.literal: Neighboring lands held him in awe, and subordinate tribes were at peace.

entries.zh: 宋數遣人結歡，冀達和意，合住表聞其事，帝許議和。
entries.en: The Song court repeatedly sent envoys to open friendly contact in hope of peace; Hezhu reported this to the throne, and the emperor agreed to negotiate.
entries.literal: Song repeatedly sent men to establish goodwill, hoping to convey a desire for peace; Hezhu memorialized the matter, and the emperor permitted talks of peace.

entries.zh: 安邊懷敵，多有力焉。
entries.en: He did much to pacify the frontier and win over the enemy.
entries.literal: In securing the border and winning over foes, he contributed much.

entries.zh: 拜左金吾衛上將軍。
entries.en: He was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Golden Crow Guards.
entries.literal: He was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Golden Crow Guards.

entries.zh: 秩滿，遙攝鎮國軍節度使，卒。
entries.en: When his term expired he was given titular charge of the Zhenguo circuit as military commissioner, and soon after died.
entries.literal: When his term ended he was given remote charge as Military Commissioner of the Zhenguo circuit and died.

entries.zh: 劉景，字可大，河間人。
entries.en: Liu Jing, whose style name was Keda, came from Hejian.
entries.literal: Liu Jing, style name Keda, was a man of Hejian.

entries.zh: 四世祖怦，即朱滔之甥，唐右僕射、盧龍軍節度使。
entries.en: His fourth-generation ancestor Bing was Zhu Tao's nephew and had served the Tang as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and military commissioner of Lulong.
entries.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Bing was a nephew of Zhu Tao of Tang, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Military Commissioner of the Lulong circuit.

entries.zh: 父守敬，南京副留守。
entries.en: His father Shoujing had been deputy regent of the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: His father Shoujing was Deputy Regent of the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 景資端厚，好學能文。
entries.en: Jing was sober and upright by nature, fond of study, and skilled with the pen.
entries.literal: Jing's endowment was steady and substantial; he loved learning and could write.

entries.zh: 燕王趙延壽辟為幽都府文學。
entries.en: Zhao Yanshou, Prince of Yan, took him on as literary officer of the Youdu prefectural staff.
entries.literal: Prince of Yan Zhao Yanshou recruited him as Literary Officer of the Youdu Prefecture office.

entries.zh: 應歷初，遷右拾遺、知制誥，為翰林學士。
entries.en: Early in the Yingli reign he was promoted to Right Reminder and drafter of edicts, and appointed a Hanlin academician.
entries.literal: At the start of the Yingli era he was moved to Right Reminder, drafter of edicts, and made Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 九年，周人侵燕，留守蕭思溫上急變，帝欲俟秋出師，景諫曰：「河北三關已陷於敵，今復侵燕，安可坐視！」
entries.en: In the ninth year the Zhou attacked Yan. Regent Xiao Siwen reported the crisis, but the emperor wanted to wait until autumn before marching. Jing urged him, saying, "The three passes of Hebei have already fallen to the enemy, and now they invade Yan again—how can we simply look on!"
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Zhou invaded Yan; Regent Xiao Siwen reported the emergency. The emperor wished to wait until autumn to take the field. Jing remonstrated, saying, "The three passes of Hebei have already fallen to the enemy; now they invade Yan again—how can we sit and watch!"

entries.zh: 上不聽。
entries.en: The emperor would not listen.
entries.literal: The sovereign did not heed this.

entries.zh: 會父憂去。
entries.en: He then left office to observe mourning for his father.
entries.literal: He happened to leave office on his father's death.

entries.zh: 未幾，起復舊職。
entries.en: Before long he was recalled from mourning to his former post.
entries.literal: Before long he was recalled from mourning to his former post.

entries.zh: 一日，召草赦，既成，留數月不出。
entries.en: One day he was ordered to draft an amnesty edict; when it was finished, it was kept back for months without being promulgated.
entries.literal: One day he was summoned to draft an amnesty; when it was finished, it was held back for months without issue.

entries.zh: 景奏曰：「唐制，赦書日行五百里，今稽期弗發，非也。」
entries.en: Jing submitted a memorial, saying, "Under Tang practice an amnesty edict was to travel five hundred li a day; to hold it back now is wrong."
entries.literal: Jing memorialized, saying, "Under Tang regulations an amnesty edict travels five hundred li a day; now it is delayed and not issued—this is wrong."

entries.zh: 上亦不報。
entries.en: Again the emperor made no response.
entries.literal: The sovereign again gave no reply.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，以景忠實，擢禮部侍郎，遷尚書、宣政殿學士。
entries.en: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne, Jing's integrity won him promotion to Vice Minister of Rites and then to Minister and academician of the Xuanzheng Hall.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, because Jing was loyal and solid he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and moved to Minister and Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall.

entries.zh: 上方欲倚用，乃書其笏曰：「劉景可為宰相。」
entries.en: The emperor was preparing to rely on him heavily and wrote on his court tablet, "Liu Jing is fit to be chief minister."
entries.literal: The sovereign was about to rely on him heavily and wrote on his tablet, "Liu Jing can serve as chief minister."

entries.zh: 頃之，為南京副留守。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was made deputy regent of the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: Before long he became Deputy Regent of the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 時留守韓匡嗣因扈從北上，景與其子德讓共理京事。
entries.en: The regent Han Kuangsi had accompanied the court north, and Jing governed the capital together with Han's son Derang.
entries.literal: At the time Regent Han Kuangsi had followed the court north; Jing and Han's son Derang jointly administered capital affairs.

entries.zh: 俄召為戶部使，歷武定、開遠二軍節度使。
entries.en: He was soon recalled to serve as commissioner of the Household Bureau and later held military commissions in the Wuding and Kaiyuan circuits.
entries.literal: Soon he was summoned as Commissioner of the Household Bureau and successively served as Military Commissioner of the Wuding and Kaiyuan circuits.

entries.zh: 統和六年致仕，加兼侍中。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tonghe he retired from office and was given the additional rank of Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tonghe he retired and was given the additional rank of Concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 卒，年六十七。
entries.en: He died at the age of sixty-seven.
entries.literal: He died at age sixty-seven.

entries.zh: 贈太子太師。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 子慎行，孫一德、二玄、三嘏、四端、五常、六符，皆具六符傳。
entries.en: His son was Shenxing; his grandsons Yide, Erxuan, Sangu, Siduan, Wuchang, and Liufu are all covered in the following account of Liu Liufu.
entries.literal: His son was Shenxing; his grandsons were Yide, Erxuan, Sangu, Siduan, Wuchang, and Liufu—all are treated in the biography of Liufu.

entries.zh: 劉六符，父慎行，由膳部員外郎累遷至北府宰相、監修國史。
entries.en: Liu Liufu was the son of Shenxing, who had risen from vice director of the Board of Foodstuffs to grand councilor of the Northern Chancellery and supervisor of the national history.
entries.literal: Liu Liufu—his father Shenxing rose from Vice Director of the Board of Foodstuffs to Northern Chancellery Grand Councilor and Supervisor of the National History.

entries.zh: 時上多即宴飲行誅賞，慎行諫曰：「以喜怒加威福，恐未當。」
entries.en: At that time the emperor often pronounced punishments and rewards while drinking at court. Shenxing urged him, saying, "To grant authority and favor according to mood is hardly proper."
entries.literal: At the time the sovereign often pronounced executions and rewards at banquets. Shenxing remonstrated, saying, "To mete out authority and favor according to joy and anger—this is perhaps not fitting."

entries.zh: 帝悟，諭政府「自今宴飲有刑賞事，翌日稟行」。
entries.en: The emperor took the point and instructed the government, "From then on, any punishments or rewards decided at banquets are to be reported and carried out only on the following day."
entries.literal: The emperor understood and instructed the government, "From now on, whenever punishments or rewards arise at banquets, they are to be reported and carried out the next day."

entries.zh: 為都統，伐高麗，以失軍期下吏，議貴乃免，出為彰武軍節度使。
entries.en: As supreme commander against Goryeo he missed the campaign schedule and was handed over to the courts; because of his noble rank the penalty was waived, and he was sent out as military commissioner of Zhangwu.
entries.literal: As supreme commander he campaigned against Goryeo; for missing the army schedule he was handed to the officials, but after deliberation on his noble rank he was pardoned and sent out as Military Commissioner of the Zhangwu circuit.

entries.zh: 賜保節功臣。
entries.en: He was granted the merit title Preserver of Integrity.
entries.literal: He was granted the title Merit Subject of Preserving Integrity.

entries.zh: 子六人：一德、二玄、三嘏、四端、五常、六符。
entries.en: He had six sons: Yide, Erxuan, Sangu, Siduan, Wuchang, and Liufu.
entries.literal: He had six sons: Yide, Erxuan, Sangu, Siduan, Wuchang, and Liufu.

entries.zh: 德早世。
entries.en: Yide died young.
entries.literal: Yide died young.

entries.zh: 玄終上京留守。
entries.en: Erxuan eventually became regent of the Supreme Capital.
entries.literal: Erxuan ended as Regent of the Supreme Capital.

entries.zh: 常歷三司使、武定軍節度使。
entries.en: Wuchang served in turn as commissioner of the Three Bureaus and as military commissioner of Wuding.
entries.literal: Wuchang successively served as Commissioner of the Three Bureaus and Military Commissioner of the Wuding circuit.

entries.zh: 嘏、端、符皆第進士。
entries.en: Sangu, Siduan, and Liufu all passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: Sangu, Siduan, and Liufu all passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 嘏、端俱尚王，為駙馬都尉。
entries.en: Sangu and Siduan both married imperial princesses and became commandants of escort.
entries.literal: Sangu and Siduan both married princesses and became Commandants of Escort.

entries.zh: 三嘏獻聖宗《一矢斃雙鹿賦》，上嘉其贍麗。
entries.en: Sangu presented to Emperor Shengzong his fu 《One Arrow Slays Two Deer》, which the emperor praised for its richness and polish.
entries.literal: Sangu presented to Emperor Shengzong the fu 《One Arrow Slays Two Deer》; the sovereign praised its richness and beauty.

entries.zh: 與公主不諧，奔宋；
entries.en: He fell out with his princess and fled to Song;
entries.literal: He was not harmonious with the princess and fled to Song;

entries.zh: 歸，殺之。
entries.en: when he returned he was put to death.
entries.literal: when he returned, he was executed.

entries.zh: 四端以衛尉少卿使宋賀生辰，方宴，大張女樂，竟席不顧，人憚其嚴。
entries.en: Siduan went to Song as vice director of the Court of Imperial Stud to congratulate the emperor on his birthday. At the banquet the Song court set out a great display of female musicians, but he never once looked their way; all who saw him feared his sternness.
entries.literal: Siduan, as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud, was envoy to Song to congratulate the emperor on his birthday. At the banquet Song greatly deployed female musicians, but he sat through the feast without looking—men feared his severity.

entries.zh: 還，拜樞密直學士。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: On his return he was appointed Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 耶律履，字海鄰，六院夷離堇蒲古只之後。
entries.en: Yelu Lü, whose style name was Hailin, was a descendant of Puguzhi, yilijin of the Six Divisions.
entries.literal: Yelu Lü, style name Hailin, was a descendant of Puguzhi, yilijin of the Six Divisions.

entries.zh: 風神爽秀，工於畫。
entries.en: He was handsome and spirited, and a skilled painter.
entries.literal: His bearing was bright and elegant, and he was skilled at painting.

entries.zh: 重熙間，累遷同知點檢司事。
entries.en: During the Chongxi era he rose to associate director of the Inspection Office.
entries.literal: During the Chongxi era he was repeatedly promoted to Associate Director of the Inspection Office.

entries.zh: 駙馬都尉蕭胡睹為夏人所執，奉詔索之，三返以歸，轉永興宮使、右祗候郎君班詳穩。
entries.en: When Commandant of Escort Xiao Huzhu was captured by the Tangut, Lü was ordered to secure his release and brought him back after three missions. He was then made commissioner of the Yongxing Palace and detailed commander of the Right Palace Attendant Gentlemen Company.
entries.literal: Commandant of Escort Xiao Huzhu was captured by the Tangut; by imperial order Lü sought his return, and after three journeys brought him back. He was transferred to Commissioner of the Yongxing Palace and detailed commander of the Right Palace Attendant Gentlemen Company.

entries.zh: 履將娶秦晉長公主孫，其母與公主婢有隙，謂履曰：「能去婢，乃許爾婚。」
entries.en: Lü was to marry a granddaughter of the Qin-Jin Senior Princess. The girl's mother bore a grudge against one of the princess's maids and told Lü, "Remove that maid, and I will consent to the marriage."
entries.literal: Lü was to marry a granddaughter of the Qin-Jin Senior Princess; her mother had a feud with a maid of the princess and told Lü, "If you can remove the maid, then your marriage will be granted."

entries.zh: 履以計殺之，婚成。
entries.en: Lü contrived her death, and the marriage went ahead.
entries.literal: Lü killed her by a stratagem, and the marriage was concluded.

entries.zh: 事覺，有司以大辟論。
entries.en: When the affair came to light, the courts sought the death penalty.
entries.literal: When the affair came to light, the officials proposed the death penalty.

entries.zh: 履善畫，寫聖宗真以獻，得減坐，長流邊戍。
entries.en: Because he was a skilled painter, he painted a portrait of Emperor Shengzong and presented it, winning a reduced sentence and lifelong exile to the frontier garrisons.
entries.literal: Lü was skilled at painting; he painted a true likeness of Emperor Shengzong and presented it, thereby reducing his sentence, and was banished for life to frontier garrison duty.

entries.zh: 復以寫真，召拜同知南院宣徽事。
entries.en: He was later recalled through his portraiture and appointed associate commissioner of the Southern Chancellery Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: Again through portraiture he was summoned and appointed Associate Commissioner of the Southern Chancellery Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 使宋賀正，寫宋主容以歸。
entries.en: Sent to Song to congratulate the New Year, he painted the Song emperor's likeness and brought it home.
entries.literal: As envoy to Song to congratulate the New Year, he painted the Song ruler's likeness and returned with it.

entries.zh: 清寧間，復使宋。
entries.en: During the Qingning era he was again sent as envoy to Song.
entries.literal: During the Qingning era he was again envoy to Song.

entries.zh: 宋主賜宴，瓶花隔面，未得其真。
entries.en: At a banquet given by the Song emperor, flowers in vases blocked his view, and he could not capture a true likeness.
entries.literal: The Song ruler gave a banquet; vase flowers blocked the face, and he did not obtain a true likeness.

entries.zh: 陛辭，僅一視，及境，以像示餞者，駭其神妙。
entries.en: At his farewell audience he had only a single glance; when he reached the border he showed the portrait to those who had come to see him off, and they marveled at its lifelike brilliance.
entries.literal: At his farewell audience he glanced only once; when he reached the border he showed the portrait to those who saw him off, and they were awed by its divine subtlety.

entries.zh: 聞重元亂，不即勤王。
entries.en: When he heard of Chongyuan's rebellion, he did not hurry to the emperor's aid.
entries.literal: When he heard of Chongyuan's rebellion, he did not hurry to aid the throne.

entries.zh: 賊平入賀，帝責讓之。
entries.en: After the rebels were crushed he came to offer congratulations, and the emperor rebuked him.
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified he entered to offer congratulations, and the emperor reproached him.

entries.zh: 宴酣，顧履曰：「重元事成，卿必得為上客！」
entries.en: As the banquet grew lively, the emperor turned to Lü and said, "If Chongyuan had succeeded, you would surely have been his honored guest!"
entries.literal: When the banquet was merry, the emperor turned to Lü and said, "If Chongyuan's affair had succeeded, you would surely have been a chief guest!"

entries.zh: 履大慚。
entries.en: Lü was deeply ashamed.
entries.literal: Lü was deeply ashamed.

entries.zh: 咸雍中，加太子太師，卒。
entries.en: During the Xianyong era he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and died.
entries.literal: During the Xianyong era he was given the additional rank of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and died.

entries.zh: 六符有誌操，能文。
entries.en: Liufu was a man of principle and an able writer.
entries.literal: Liufu had resolve and integrity and could write.

entries.zh: 重熙初，遷政事舍人，擢翰林學士。
entries.en: Early in the Chongxi era he was made administrative drafting attendant and then promoted to Hanlin academician.
entries.literal: At the start of the Chongxi era he was moved to Administrative Drafting Attendant and promoted to Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 十一年，與宣徽使蕭特末使宋索十縣地；
entries.en: In the eleventh year he went with Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Xiao Temuo as envoy to Song to demand the return of ten counties;
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, together with Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Xiao Temuo, he was envoy to Song to demand the ten counties;

entries.zh: 還，為漢人行宮副部署。
entries.en: on his return he was made deputy commissioner of the Han palaces.
entries.literal: on his return he became Deputy Commissioner of the Han Palaces.

entries.zh: 會宋遣使增歲幣以易十縣，復與耶律仁先使宋，定「進貢」名，宋難之。
entries.en: When Song sent envoys offering to increase the annual payments in exchange for the ten counties, he went again with Yelu Renxian to fix the term "tribute presentation," which the Song court resisted.
entries.literal: When Song sent envoys to increase the annual tribute in exchange for the ten counties, he again went with Yelu Renxian as envoy to Song to fix the term "tribute presentation"; Song found this hard to accept.

entries.zh: 六符曰：「本朝兵強將勇，海內共知，人人願從事於宋。
entries.en: Liufu said, "Our dynasty's armies are strong and its generals brave—the whole world knows it, and every soldier would gladly march against Song.
entries.literal: Liufu said, "Our court's soldiers are strong and its generals brave—the whole realm knows this, and every man wishes to take service against Song.

entries.zh: 若恣其俘獲以飽所欲，與『進貢』字孰多？
entries.en: If they were turned loose to take captives and booty to their hearts' content, how would that weigh against the word 'tribute'?
entries.literal: If they were allowed free rein in captives and plunder to satisfy their desires, how would that compare with the word 'tribute presentation'?

entries.zh: 況大兵駐燕，萬一南進，何以禦之！
entries.en: And with a great army stationed at Yan, if it should march south, how would you withstand it!
entries.literal: Moreover, with a great army stationed at Yan, if it should advance south by any chance, how could you resist it!

entries.zh: 顧小節，忘大患，悔將何及！」
entries.en: To cling to a petty point and forget a grave danger—when regret comes, it will be too late!"
entries.literal: To cling to a small point and forget a great peril—when regret comes, how will it be in time!"

entries.zh: 宋乃從之，歲幣稱「貢」。
entries.en: Song then yielded, and the annual payments were henceforth styled "tribute."
entries.literal: Song then yielded, and the annual payments were called "tribute."

entries.zh: 六符還，加同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On his return Liufu was made associate chief councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
entries.literal: When Liufu returned he was given the additional rank of Associate Chief Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 及宋幣至，命六符為三司使以受之。
entries.en: When the Song payments arrived, he was appointed commissioner of the Three Bureaus to receive them.
entries.literal: When Song's payments arrived, Liufu was ordered to serve as Commissioner of the Three Bureaus to receive them.

entries.zh: 六符與參知政事杜防有隙，防以六符嘗受宋賂，白其事，出為長寧軍節度使，俄召為三司使。
entries.en: Liufu and Vice Director Du Fang were at odds; Fang reported that Liufu had once taken bribes from Song. He was sent out as military commissioner of Changning, but was soon recalled as commissioner of the Three Bureaus.
entries.literal: Liufu and Vice Director of the Secretariat Du Fang were at odds; Fang reported that Liufu had once accepted bribes from Song. He was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Changning circuit, but soon recalled as Commissioner of the Three Bureaus.

entries.zh: 道宗即位，將行大冊禮，北院樞密使蕭革曰：「行大禮備儀物，必擇廣地，莫若黃川。」
entries.en: When Emperor Daozong came to the throne and prepared the great investiture rite, Northern Chancellery Military Affairs Commissioner Xiao Ge said, "A great ceremony requires ample space and full ritual equipment—no place is better than Huangchuan."
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong took the throne and was about to perform the great investiture rite, Northern Chancellery Military Affairs Commissioner Xiao Ge said, "To perform a great rite with full ritual objects, one must choose broad ground—none is better than Huangchuan."

entries.zh: 六符曰：「不然。
entries.en: Liufu said, "That will not do.
entries.literal: Liufu said, "Not so.

entries.zh: 禮儀國之大體，帝王之樂不奏於野。
entries.en: Ritual is the great foundation of a state; an emperor's music is not performed in the open countryside.
entries.literal: Rites and etiquette are the great foundation of a state; the music of emperors is not performed in the wilds.

entries.zh: 今中京四方之極，朝覲各得其所，宜中京行之。」
entries.en: The Central Capital is the hub of the realm, where audiences from every quarter can be properly received—it should be held there."
entries.literal: Now the Central Capital is the center of the four directions; audiences each find their proper place—there it should be performed."

entries.zh: 上從其議。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his view.
entries.literal: The sovereign followed his proposal.

entries.zh: 尋以疾卒。
entries.en: He soon died of illness.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.

entries.zh: 杜防，涿州歸義縣人。
entries.en: Du Fang came from Guiyi County in Zhuo Prefecture.
entries.literal: Du Fang was a man of Guiyi County in Zhuo Prefecture.

entries.zh: 開泰五年，擢進士甲科，累遷起居郎、知制誥，人以為有宰相器。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Kaitai he passed the jinshi examination in the top class, rose to court diarist and drafter of edicts, and was widely regarded as chief-minister material.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Kaitai he was selected in the top class of the jinshi examination, was repeatedly promoted to Court Diarist and drafter of edicts, and men considered him to have the makings of a chief minister.

entries.zh: 太平中，遷政事舍人，拜樞密副使。
entries.en: During the Taiping era he became administrative drafting attendant and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: During the Taiping era he was moved to Administrative Drafting Attendant and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 重熙九年，夏人侵宋。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Chongxi the Tangut attacked Song.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Chongxi the Tangut invaded Song.

entries.zh: 宋遣郭稹來告，請與夏和，上命防使夏解之。
entries.en: Song sent Guo Zhen to report the crisis and ask for peace with the Tangut; the emperor ordered Fang to mediate with the Tangut.
entries.literal: Song sent Guo Zhen to report and request peace with the Tangut; the sovereign ordered Fang to go to the Tangut to settle it.

entries.zh: 如約罷兵，各歸侵地，拜參知政事。
entries.en: As agreed, both sides halted hostilities and returned seized territory, and he was made vice director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: As agreed, the armies were halted and each side returned the territory it had seized; he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 韓紹芳、劉六符忌之，防待以誠。
entries.en: Han Shaofang and Liu Liufu were jealous of him, yet Fang treated them with sincerity.
entries.literal: Han Shaofang and Liu Liufu were jealous of him, but Fang treated them with sincerity.

entries.zh: 十二年，紹芳等罷，愈見信任。
entries.en: In the twelfth year Shaofang and his faction were dismissed, and Fang won still greater trust.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year Shaofang and the others were dismissed, and he was ever more trusted.

entries.zh: 十三年，拜南府宰相。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was made grand councilor of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Southern Chancellery.

entries.zh: 十五年，防生子，帝幸其第，賜名王門奴。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year Fang had a son; the emperor visited his home and gave the child the name Wangmennu.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Fang had a son; the emperor visited his residence and bestowed the name Wangmennu.

entries.zh: 以進奏有誤，出為武定軍節度使。
entries.en: After an error in a memorial report he was sent out as military commissioner of Wuding.
entries.literal: For an error in a memorial report he was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Wuding circuit.

entries.zh: 十七年，復召為南府宰相。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he was recalled as grand councilor of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he was again summoned as Grand Councilor of the Southern Chancellery.

entries.zh: 二十一年秋，祭仁德皇后，詔儒臣賦詩，防為冠，賜金帶。
entries.en: In the autumn of the twenty-first year, at the rites for Empress Rende, the court ordered scholar-officials to compose poems; Fang's ranked first, and he was granted a gold belt.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-first year, at the sacrifice for Empress Rende, the court ordered Confucian officials to compose poems; Fang's was foremost, and he was granted a gold belt.

entries.zh: 道宗諒陰，為大行皇帝山陵使。
entries.en: During Emperor Daozong's mourning for his father, he served as commissioner for the late emperor's tomb.
entries.literal: During Emperor Daozong's mourning for his father, he served as commissioner for the late emperor's mausoleum.

entries.zh: 清寧二年，上諭防曰：「朕以卿年老嗜酒，不欲煩以劇務。
entries.en: In the second year of Qingning the emperor told Fang, "You are old and fond of wine, and I do not wish to burden you with heavy duties.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qingning the sovereign instructed Fang, saying, "Because you are old and fond of wine, I do not wish to burden you with heavy duties.

entries.zh: 朝廷之事，總綱而已。」
entries.en: In court affairs you need only hold the general lines."
entries.literal: In court affairs, hold only the general lines."

entries.zh: 頃之，拜右丞相，加尚父，卒。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was made right chief councilor and honored as Exalted Father, then died.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed Right Chief Councilor, given the title Exalted Father, and died.

entries.zh: 上嘆悼不已，赗贈加等，官給葬具，贈中書令，謚曰元肅。
entries.en: The emperor mourned him deeply, increased the funeral gifts, supplied state burial goods, posthumously made him director of the Secretariat, and gave him the posthumous title Yuansu.
entries.literal: The sovereign lamented without end, increased the funeral gifts, supplied burial goods from the state, posthumously made him Director of the Secretariat, and gave the posthumous title Yuansu.

entries.zh: 子公謂，終南府宰相。
entries.en: His son Gongwei eventually became grand councilor of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: His son Gongwei ended as Grand Councilor of the Southern Chancellery.

entries.zh: 耶律頗的，字撒版，季父房奴瓜之孫。
entries.en: Yelu Pode, whose style name was Saban, was a grandson of Nugua of the Shufu branch.
entries.literal: Yelu Pode, style name Saban, was a grandson of Nugua of the Shufu branch.

entries.zh: 孤介寡合。
entries.en: He was aloof by nature and kept little company.
entries.literal: He was aloof and solitary, keeping little company.

entries.zh: 重熙初，補牌印郎君。
entries.en: Early in Chongxi he entered service as seal and tablet attendant.
entries.literal: At the start of Chongxi he was appointed Seal and Tablet Attendant.

entries.zh: 清寧初，稍遷知易州。
entries.en: Early in Qingning he was promoted to prefect of Yi.
entries.literal: At the start of Qingning he was gradually promoted to prefect of Yi.

entries.zh: 去官，部民請留，許之。
entries.en: When he left office the people of his jurisdiction petitioned to keep him, and the request was granted.
entries.literal: When he left office the people of his circuit asked that he remain, and this was granted.

entries.zh: 咸雍八年，改彰國軍節度使。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Xianyong he was transferred as military commissioner of Zhangguo.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Xianyong he was transferred as Military Commissioner of the Zhangguo circuit.

entries.zh: 上獵大牢古山，頗的謁於行宮。
entries.en: When the emperor hunted on Mount Dalaogu, Pode presented himself at the traveling palace.
entries.literal: When the sovereign hunted at Mount Dalaogu, Pode presented himself at the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 帝問邊事，對曰：「自應州南境至天池，皆我耕牧之地。
entries.en: Asked about frontier affairs, he replied, "From the southern border of Ying Prefecture to Heaven Pool, all is our land for farming and grazing.
entries.literal: The emperor asked about frontier affairs. He replied, "From the southern border of Ying Prefecture to Heaven Pool, all is our land for farming and grazing.

entries.zh: 清寧間，邊將不謹，為宋所侵，烽堠內移，似非所宜。」
entries.en: During Qingning our frontier commanders were careless; Song encroached, and our beacon towers were pulled back inland—which seems unwise."
entries.literal: During Qingning the frontier generals were not careful; Song encroached, and beacon towers were moved inward—this seems not fitting."

entries.zh: 道宗然之。
entries.en: Emperor Daozong agreed.
entries.literal: Emperor Daozong approved of this.

entries.zh: 拜北面林牙。
entries.en: He was appointed northern secretary.
entries.literal: He was appointed Northern Secretary.

entries.zh: 後遣人使宋，得其侵地，命頗的往定疆界。
entries.en: Later an envoy to Song recovered the seized territory, and Pode was ordered to go demarcate the border.
entries.literal: Later an envoy was sent to Song and recovered the encroached territory; Pode was ordered to go fix the border.

entries.zh: 還，拜南院宣徽使。
entries.en: On his return he was made commissioner of the Southern Chancellery Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: On his return he was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Chancellery Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 大康四年，遷忠順軍節度使，尋為南院大王，改同知南京留守事，召拜南府宰相，賜貞良功臣，封吳國公，為北院樞密使。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Dakang he was made military commissioner of Zhongshun; soon he became great king of the Southern Chancellery, associate regent of the Southern Capital, and grand councilor of the Southern Chancellery, was granted the merit title of Integrity, enfeoffed as Duke of Wu, and appointed military affairs commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Dakang he was transferred as Military Commissioner of the Zhongshun circuit; soon he became Great King of the Southern Chancellery, was changed to Associate Regent of the Southern Capital, summoned as Grand Councilor of the Southern Chancellery, granted the title Merit Subject of Integrity, enfeoffed as Duke of Wu, and made Military Affairs Commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.

entries.zh: 廉謹奉公，知無不為。
entries.en: He was incorrupt, conscientious in public service, and did whatever duty required.
entries.literal: Incorrupt and careful in serving the public, he did whatever he knew should be done.

entries.zh: 大安中致仕，卒。
entries.en: He retired during the Da'an era and died.
entries.literal: During the Da'an era he retired and died.

entries.zh: 子霞抹，北院樞密副使。
entries.en: His son Xiamo became vice military affairs commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.
entries.literal: His son Xiamo became Vice Military Affairs Commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.

entries.zh: 耶律合裏只，字特滿，六院夷離堇蒲古只之後。
entries.en: Yelu Helizhi, whose style name was Teman, was a descendant of Puguzhi, yilijin of the Six Divisions.
entries.literal: Yelu Helizhi, style name Teman, was a descendant of Puguzhi, yilijin of the Six Divisions.

entries.zh: 重熙中，累遷西南面招討都監。
entries.en: During the Chongxi era he rose to southwest pacification and suppression commissioner-in-chief.
entries.literal: During the Chongxi era he was repeatedly promoted to Southwest Pacification and Suppression Commissioner-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 充宋國生辰使，館於白溝驛。
entries.en: As envoy to Song for the emperor's birthday, he lodged at the Baigou post station.
entries.literal: Serving as envoy to Song for the emperor's birthday, he lodged at the Baigou post station.

entries.zh: 宋宴勞，優者嘲蕭惠河西之敗。
entries.en: At the banquet held in his honor, an actor mocked Xiao Hui's defeat on the western frontier.
entries.literal: At Song's banquet in his honor, an actor mocked Xiao Hui's defeat west of the river.

entries.zh: 合裏只曰：「勝負兵家常事。
entries.en: Helizhi said, "Victory and defeat are common in war.
entries.literal: Helizhi said, "Victory and defeat are common matters in warfare.

entries.zh: 我嗣聖皇帝俘石重貴，至今興中有石家寨。
entries.en: Our Emperor Shizong took Shi Chonggui prisoner, and to this day Xingzhong has a Shijia Stockade to prove it.
entries.literal: Our Emperor Shizong captured Shi Chonggui; to this day in Xingzhong there is a Shijia Stockade.

entries.zh: 惠之一敗，何足較哉！」
entries.en: What is one defeat of Hui's beside that!"
entries.literal: What is one defeat of Hui's to compare!"

entries.zh: 宋人慚服。
entries.en: The Song were silenced and impressed.
entries.literal: The Song were ashamed and convinced.

entries.zh: 帝聞之曰：「優令失辭，何可傷兩國交好！」
entries.en: When the emperor heard of it he said, "The actor spoke out of turn—how could that be allowed to harm relations between our two states!"
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of it he said, "The actor's lines were improper—how could they harm the friendship of the two states!"

entries.zh: 鞭二百，免官。
entries.en: The actor was given two hundred lashes and dismissed from office.
entries.literal: He was given two hundred lashes and dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 清寧初，起為懷化軍節度使。
entries.en: Early in Qingning he was recalled as military commissioner of Huaihua.
entries.literal: At the start of Qingning he was recalled to serve as Military Commissioner of the Huaihua circuit.

entries.zh: 七年，入為北院大王，封豳國公。
entries.en: In the seventh year he entered court as great king of the Northern Chancellery and was enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he entered court as Great King of the Northern Chancellery and was enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.

entries.zh: 歷遼興軍節度使、東北路詳穩，加兼侍中。
entries.en: He served in turn as military commissioner of Liaoxing and detailed commander of the northeast route, and was given the additional rank of palace attendant.
entries.literal: He successively served as Military Commissioner of the Liaoxing circuit and detailed commander of the Northeast Route, and was given the additional rank of Concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 致仕，卒。
entries.en: He retired from office and died.
entries.literal: He retired and died.

entries.zh: 耶律合住劉景劉六符耶律甗履牛溫舒杜防蕭和尚
entries.en: Yelu Hezhu, Liu Jing, Liu Liufu, Yelu Lü, Niu Wenshu, Du Fang, and Xiao Heshang
entries.literal: Yelu Hezhu, Liu Jing, Liu Liufu, Yelu Lü, Niu Wenshu, Du Fang, Xiao Heshang

entries.en: (Temuo)
entries.literal: (Temuo)

entries.zh: 耶律合裏只耶律頗的
entries.en: Yelu Helizhi and Yelu Pode
entries.literal: Yelu Helizhi, Yelu Pode

entries.zh: 興宗即位，徙王秦，尋復為南京留守。
entries.en: When Emperor Xingzong took the throne, Xiaomu was transferred to Prince of Qin and soon again became Military Governor of Nanjing.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xingzong took the throne, Xiaomu was transferred to Prince of Qin and soon again became Military Governor of Nanjing.

entries.zh: 重熙六年，進封吳國王，拜北院樞密使。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Chongxi he was advanced to Prince of Wu and appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Chongxi, he was advanced to Prince of Wu and appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 八年，表請籍天下戶口以均徭役，又陳諸部及舍利軍利害。
entries.en: In the eighth year he memorialized requesting a household register for the whole realm to equalize corvée and tax burdens, and also explained the advantages and disadvantages of the various tribes and the Sheli Army.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, he memorialized requesting registration of households throughout the realm to equalize corvée and tax burdens, and also set forth the advantages and disadvantages of the various tribes and the Sheli Army.

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court approved it.
entries.literal: The request was approved.

entries.zh: 由是政賦稍平，眾悅。
entries.en: From this, government levies gradually became fairer, and the people were pleased.
entries.literal: From this, government levies gradually became equitable, and the people were pleased.

entries.zh: 九年，徙王楚。
entries.en: In the ninth year his title was changed to Prince of Chu.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, his princedom was changed to Chu.

entries.zh: 時天下無事，戶口蕃息，上富於春秋，每言及周取十縣，慨然有南伐之志。
entries.en: At that time the realm was at peace and the population was growing. The emperor, still in the prime of life, would sigh with resolve whenever he spoke of recovering the ten counties south of the passes and harbored a desire for a southern campaign.
entries.literal: At that time the realm was at peace, the population was growing, and the emperor, still in the prime of life, whenever he spoke of Zhou's recovery of the ten counties would sigh with resolve and harbor a desire for a southern campaign.

entries.zh: 群臣多順旨。
entries.en: Most of the ministers echoed his wishes.
entries.literal: Most of the ministers followed his intent.

entries.zh: 孝穆諫曰：「昔太祖南伐，終以無功。
entries.en: Xiaomu remonstrated, saying, "In former times Taizu campaigned south and ultimately achieved no success.
entries.literal: Xiaomu remonstrated, saying: "In former times Taizu campaigned south and ultimately achieved no success.

entries.zh: 嗣聖皇帝仆唐立晉，後以重貴叛，長驅入汴，鑾馭始旋，反來侵軼。
entries.en: The Succeeding Sage Emperor overthrew Tang and established Jin; later, when Chonggui rebelled, he marched deep into Bian, and scarcely had the imperial carriage returned when raids came in turn.
entries.literal: The Succeeding Sage Emperor overthrew Tang and established Jin; later, when Chonggui rebelled, he marched deep into Bian, and scarcely had the imperial carriage returned when raids came in turn.

entries.zh: 自後連兵二十餘年，僅得和好，蒸民樂業，南北相通。
entries.en: After that armies fought for more than twenty years before peace was barely restored; the common people lived in contentment and north and south were linked once more.
entries.literal: After that armies fought for more than twenty years before peace was barely restored; the common people lived in contentment and north and south were linked once more.

entries.zh: 今國家比之曩日，雖曰富強，然勛臣宿將，往往物故。
entries.en: Now, though the state is said to be stronger than in former days, meritorious ministers and veteran generals have often passed away.
entries.literal: Now, though the state is said to be stronger than in former days, meritorious ministers and veteran generals have often passed away.

entries.zh: 且宋人無罪，陛下不宜棄先帝盟約。」
entries.en: Moreover, the Song people are without guilt; Your Majesty should not abandon the covenant of the late emperor."
entries.literal: Moreover, the Song people are without guilt; Your Majesty should not abandon the covenant of the late emperor."

entries.zh: 時上意已決，書奏不報。
entries.en: At that time the emperor's mind was already made up; the memorial went unanswered.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor's mind was already made up; the memorial was submitted but received no response.

entries.zh: 以年老乞骸骨，不許。
entries.en: On grounds of age he requested retirement, but permission was refused.
entries.literal: On grounds of age he requested retirement, but was not permitted.

entries.zh: 十二年，復為北院樞密使，更王齊，薨。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he again became Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs, his title was changed to Prince of Qi, and he died.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, he again became Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs, his princedom was changed to Qi, and he died.

entries.zh: 追贈大丞相、晉國王，謚曰貞。
entries.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Chancellor and Prince of Jin, with the posthumous title Zhen.
entries.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Chancellor and Prince of Jin, with the posthumous title Zhen.

entries.zh: 耶律蒲古，字提隱，太祖弟蘇之四世孫。
entries.en: Yelü Pugu, whose style name was Tiyin, was a fourth-generation descendant of Su, the younger brother of Emperor Taizu.
entries.literal: Yelü Pugu, style name Tiyin, was a fourth-generation descendant of Su, younger brother of Emperor Taizu.

entries.zh: 以武勇稱。
entries.en: He was famed for martial valor.
entries.literal: He was known for martial courage and valor.

entries.zh: 統和初，為涿州刺史，從伐高麗有功。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tonghe he served as Prefect of Zhuozhou and distinguished himself in the campaign against Goryeo.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe, he was Prefect of Zhuozhou and distinguished himself in the campaign against Goryeo.

entries.zh: 開泰末，為上京內客省副使。
entries.en: At the end of the Kaitai era he was Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Guest Bureau at Shangjing.
entries.literal: At the end of Kaitai, he was Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Guest Bureau at Shangjing.

entries.zh: 太平二年，城鴨淥江，蒲古守之，在鎮有治績。
entries.en: In the second year of Taiping, when fortifications were raised along the Yalu River, Pugu held the post and won a strong record of governance.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taiping, when fortifications were built at the Yalu River, Pugu garrisoned them and achieved notable results in his command.

entries.zh: 五年，改廣德軍節度使，尋遷東京統軍使。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was made Military Commissioner of the Guangde Army and soon transferred to Commander of Dongjing.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was made Military Commissioner of the Guangde Army and soon transferred to Commander of Dongjing.

entries.zh: 蒞政嚴肅，諸部懾服。
entries.en: His rule was stern and disciplined, and the tribes submitted in awe.
entries.literal: His administration was stern and grave; all tribes were awed into submission.

entries.zh: 九年，大延琳叛，以書結保州。
entries.en: In the ninth year, when Da Yanlin rebelled, he sent letters to win over Baozhou.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, when Da Yanlin rebelled, he sent letters to win over Baozhou.

entries.zh: 夏行美執其人送蒲古，蒲古入據保州，延琳氣沮。
entries.en: Xia Xingmei seized the envoy and sent him to Pugu. Pugu then entered and took Baozhou, and Yanlin's morale collapsed.
entries.literal: Xia Xingmei seized the envoy and sent him to Pugu; Pugu entered and occupied Baozhou, and Yanlin's spirit was broken.

entries.zh: 以功拜惕隱。
entries.en: For this achievement he was appointed Tiyin.
entries.literal: For his merit he was appointed Tiyin.

entries.zh: 十一年，為子鐵驪所弒。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he was murdered by his son Tieli.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he was murdered by his son Tieli.

entries.zh: 孝先，字延寧，小字海裏。
entries.en: Xiaoxian, whose style name was Yanning and whose childhood name was Haili.
entries.literal: Xiaoxian, style name Yanning, childhood name Haili.

entries.zh: 統和十八年，補祗候郎君。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year of Tonghe he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year of Tonghe, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 尚南陽公主，拜駙馬都尉。
entries.en: He married Princess Nanyang and was made Commandant of Escort.
entries.literal: He married Princess Nanyang and was appointed Commandant of Escort.

entries.zh: 開泰五年，為國舅詳穩。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Kaitai he became Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Kaitai, he became Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

entries.zh: 將兵城東鄙。
entries.en: He led troops to fortify the eastern frontier.
entries.literal: He led troops to fortify the eastern frontier.

entries.zh: 還，為南京統軍使。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed Commander of Nanjing.
entries.literal: On his return, he was made Commander of Nanjing.

entries.zh: 太平三年，為漢人行宮都部署，尋加太子太傅。
entries.en: In the third year of Taiping he became Chief Deployment Commissioner of the Chinese Palatial Camp and was soon made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiping, he became Chief Deployment Commissioner of the Chinese Palatial Camp and soon received the additional title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 五年，遷上京留守。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was transferred to Military Governor of Shangjing.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Military Governor of Shangjing.

entries.zh: 以母老求侍，復為國舅詳穩。
entries.en: When his mother grew old he asked to attend her at home and again took up the post of Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
entries.literal: Because his mother was old, he requested to attend her and again became Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

entries.zh: 改東京留守。
entries.en: He was then made Military Governor of Dongjing.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Dongjing.

entries.zh: 會大延琳反，被圍數月，穴地而出。
entries.en: When Da Yanlin rebelled, he was besieged for months before digging his way out underground.
entries.literal: When Da Yanlin rebelled, he was besieged for several months and escaped by tunneling underground.

entries.zh: 延琳平，留守上京。
entries.en: After Yanlin was suppressed, he stayed on as Military Governor of Shangjing.
entries.literal: After Yanlin was pacified, he remained as Military Governor of Shangjing.

entries.zh: 十一年，帝不豫，欽哀召孝先總禁衛事。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, when the emperor fell ill, Empress Qin'ai summoned Xiaoxian to take overall charge of the palace guard.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Emperor was unwell, Qin'ai summoned Xiaoxian to take overall charge of the palace guard.

entries.zh: 興宗諒陰，欽哀弒仁德皇后，孝先與蕭浞卜、蕭匹敵等謀居多。
entries.en: While Emperor Xingzong was in mourning, Qin'ai murdered Empress Rende; Xiaoxian, together with Xiao Fubu, Xiao Pidi, and others, played the leading part in the plot.
entries.literal: During Emperor Xingzong's mourning period, Qin'ai murdered Empress Rende; Xiaoxian, Xiao Fubu, Xiao Pidi, and others were chief among the conspirators.

entries.zh: 及欽哀攝政，遙授天平軍節度使，加守司徒，兼政事令。
entries.en: When Qin'ai took the regency, he received a remote appointment as Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army, was made Acting Minister of Education, and served concurrently as Chief Councilor.
entries.literal: When Qin'ai assumed regency, he was appointed in absentia Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army, made Acting Minister of Education, and concurrently Chief Councilor.

entries.zh: 重熙初，封楚王，為北院樞密使。
entries.en: At the opening of the Chongxi era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu and appointed Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu and made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 孝先以椒房親，為太后所重。
entries.en: As a kinsman of the empress's clan, Xiaoxian enjoyed the Empress Dowager's special favor.
entries.literal: Because Xiaoxian was a maternal-clan kinsman, the Empress Dowager held him in high regard.

entries.zh: 在樞府，好惡自恣，權傾人主，朝多側目。
entries.en: At the Bureau of Military Affairs he indulged his own likes and dislikes; his power overshadowed the throne, and many at court watched him with unease.
entries.literal: In the Bureau of Military Affairs he indulged his likes and dislikes at will; his power overshadowed the sovereign, and many at court looked askance at him.

entries.zh: 三年，太后與孝先謀廢立事，帝知之，勒衛兵出宮，召孝先至，諭以廢太后意。
entries.en: In the third year the Empress Dowager and Xiaoxian plotted to depose the emperor and enthrone another. When the emperor learned of it, he ordered the palace guards out of the palace, summoned Xiaoxian, and told him of his plan to depose the Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: In the third year, the Empress Dowager and Xiaoxian plotted deposition and enthronement; the Emperor learned of it, ordered the palace guards out of the palace, summoned Xiaoxian, and informed him of his intent to depose the Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 孝先震懾不能對。
entries.en: Xiaoxian was struck dumb with fear and could not answer.
entries.literal: Xiaoxian was shaken with fear and could not reply.

entries.zh: 遷太后於慶州。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager was sent away to Qingzhou.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager was moved to Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 孝先恒郁郁不樂。
entries.en: Xiaoxian remained perpetually downcast.
entries.literal: Xiaoxian was constantly depressed and unhappy.

entries.zh: 四年，徙王晉。
entries.en: In the fourth year his title was changed to Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, his princedom was changed to Jin.

entries.zh: 後為南京留守，卒，謚忠肅。
entries.en: He later served as Military Governor of Nanjing, died in office, and was posthumously titled Loyal and Solemn.
entries.literal: Later he became Military Governor of Nanjing, died, and was given the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.

entries.zh: 孝友，字撻不衍，小字陳留。
entries.en: Xiaoyou, whose style name was Tabuyan and whose childhood name was Chenliu.
entries.literal: Xiaoyou, style name Tabuyan, childhood name Chenliu.

entries.zh: 開泰初，以戚屬為小將軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Kaitai he entered service as a Junior General through his imperial connections.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaitai, through imperial kinship he became a Junior General.

entries.zh: 太平元年，以大冊，加左武衛大將軍、檢校太保，賜名孝友。
entries.en: In the first year of Taiping, at the grand enthronement ceremony, he was made General of the Left Martial Guard and Grand Guardian of Ceremonies and was granted the name Xiaoyou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiping, at the great enthronement ceremony, he was made General of the Left Martial Guard, Grand Guardian of Ceremonies, and granted the name Xiaoyou.

entries.zh: 重熙元年，累遷西北路招討使，封蘭陵郡王。
entries.en: In the first year of Chongxi he rose through successive appointments to Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling Commandery.
entries.literal: In the first year of Chongxi, he was repeatedly promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit and enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling Commandery.

entries.zh: 八年，進王陳。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was advanced to Prince of Chen.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, he was advanced to Prince of Chen.

entries.zh: 先是，蕭惠為招討使，專以威制西羌，諸夷多叛。
entries.en: Earlier, when Xiao Hui had been Pacification Commissioner, he had relied solely on intimidation to control the Western Qiang, and many tribes rebelled.
entries.literal: Previously, when Xiao Hui was Pacification Commissioner, he relied solely on intimidation to control the Western Qiang, and many tribes rebelled.

entries.zh: 孝友下車，厚加綏撫，每入貢，輒增其賜物，羌人以安。
entries.en: When Xiaoyou took office, he treated them with generous reassurance; whenever they came to offer tribute, he increased their gifts, and the Qiang peoples lived at peace.
entries.literal: When Xiaoyou took office, he treated them generously with soothing measures; whenever they came to offer tribute, he always increased their gifts, and the Qiang people were at peace.

entries.zh: 久之，浸成姑息，諸夷桀驁之風遂熾，議者譏其過中。
entries.en: In time his policy slid into mere indulgence; the fierce and unruly temper of the tribes grew stronger, and critics said he had gone too far.
entries.literal: Over time this gradually became excessive indulgence; the fierce and unruly ways of the tribes grew strong, and critics mocked him for going too far.

entries.zh: 十年，加政事令，賜效節宣庸定遠功臣，更王吳。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was made Chief Councilor, granted the merit title Devoted in Service, Proclaiming Merit, and Settling the Distance, and his title was changed to Prince of Wu.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, he was made Chief Councilor, granted the merit title Devoted in Service, Proclaiming Merit, and Settling the Distance, and his princedom was changed to Wu.

entries.zh: 後以葬兄孝穆、孝忠，還京師，拜南院樞密使，加賜翊聖協穆保義功臣，進王趙，拜中書令。
entries.en: Later, after returning to the capital to bury his elder brothers Xiaomu and Xiaozhong, he was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs, granted the additional merit title Assisting the Sage, Harmonizing with Mu, and Preserving Righteousness, advanced to Prince of Zhao, and made Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Later, to bury his elder brothers Xiaomu and Xiaozhong, he returned to the capital, was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs, granted the additional merit title Assisting the Sage, Harmonizing with Mu, and Preserving Righteousness, advanced to Prince of Zhao, and appointed Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 丁母憂，起復北府宰相，出知東京留守。
entries.en: When his mother died he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning to become Chancellor of the Northern Commission and was sent out as Military Governor of Dongjing.
entries.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning to become Chancellor of the Northern Commission and went out to serve as Military Governor of Dongjing.

entries.zh: 會伐夏，孝友與樞密使蕭惠失利河南，帝欲誅之，太后救免。
entries.en: During a campaign against Xia, Xiaoyou and Commissioner Xiao Hui were defeated south of the Yellow River. The emperor wished to put them to death, but the Empress Dowager intervened and spared them.
entries.literal: When a campaign was launched against Xia, Xiaoyou and Commissioner Xiao Hui suffered defeat south of the Yellow River; the Emperor wished to execute them, but the Empress Dowager intervened and spared them.

entries.zh: 復為東京留守，徙王燕，改上京留守，更王秦。
entries.en: He again became Military Governor of Dongjing, was transferred to Prince of Yan, then made Military Governor of Shangjing, and his title was changed again to Prince of Qin.
entries.literal: He again became Military Governor of Dongjing, was transferred to Prince of Yan, then changed to Military Governor of Shangjing, and his title was changed again to Prince of Qin.

entries.zh: 清寧初，加尚父。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qingning he was given the honorific title Imperial Father.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, he was given the honorific title Imperial Father.

entries.zh: 頃之，復留守東京。
entries.en: Before long he again served as Military Governor of Dongjing.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward, he again served as Military Governor of Dongjing.

entries.zh: 明年，復為北府宰相。
entries.en: The following year he again became Chancellor of the Northern Commission.
entries.literal: The following year, he again became Chancellor of the Northern Commission.

entries.zh: 帝親制誥詞以褒寵之。
entries.en: The emperor personally drafted an edict to praise and honor him.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally composed an edict to praise and honor him.

entries.zh: 以柴冊恩，遙授洛京留守，益賜純德功臣，致仕，進封豐國王。
entries.en: In recognition of his service at the imperial succession ceremony, he received a remote appointment as Military Governor of Luojing, was granted the additional merit title Pure Virtue, retired from office, and was advanced to Prince of Feng.
entries.literal: Because of the merit of the imperial succession tablets, he was appointed in absentia Military Governor of Luojing, granted the additional merit title Pure Virtue, retired from office, and was advanced to Prince of Feng.

entries.zh: 坐子胡睹首與重元亂，伏誅，年七十三。
entries.en: When his son Hudu led the rebellion of Chongyuan, he was executed on that account at the age of seventy-three.
entries.literal: Because his son Hudu was the ringleader in Chongyuan's rebellion, he was executed; he was seventy-three years old.

entries.zh: 胡睹在《逆臣傳》。
entries.en: Hudu is treated in the 《Biographies of Rebellious Subjects》.
entries.literal: Hudu is treated in the 《Biographies of Rebellious Subjects》.

entries.zh: 蕭孝穆
entries.en: Xiao Xiaomu
entries.literal: Xiao Xiaomu

entries.zh: 〈（撒八孝先孝友）〉
entries.en: (See the biographies of Saba, Xiaoxian, and Xiaoyou)
entries.literal: (Saba, Xiaoxian, and Xiaoyou have separate biographies)

entries.zh: 蕭蒲奴耶律蒲古夏行美
entries.en: Xiao Punu, Yelü Pugu, and Xia Xingmei
entries.literal: Xiao Punu, Yelü Pugu, Xia Xingmei

entries.zh: 蕭排押，字韓隱，國舅少父房之後。
entries.en: Xiao Paiya, whose style name was Hanyin, was descended from the Lesser Father House of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
entries.literal: Xiao Paiya, style name Hanyin, was descended from the Lesser Father House of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

entries.zh: 多智略，能騎射。
entries.en: He was resourceful in stratagem and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
entries.literal: He was full of stratagems and skilled at mounted archery.

entries.zh: 統和初，為左皮室詳穩，討阻卜有功。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tonghe he was Detailed Commandant of the Left Pishi and won merit campaigning against the Zubu.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe he was Detailed Commandant of the Left Pishi and achieved merit in campaigns against the Zubu.

entries.zh: 四年，破宋將曹彬、米信兵於望都。
entries.en: In the fourth year he defeated the Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin at Wangdu.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he defeated the Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin at Wangdu.

entries.zh: 凡軍事有疑，每預參決。
entries.en: Whenever military affairs were in doubt, he was regularly called in to deliberate.
entries.literal: Whenever military affairs were in doubt, he was regularly consulted in the decision.

entries.zh: 尋總永興宮分糺及舍利、拽剌、二皮室等軍，與樞密使耶律斜軫收復山西所陷城邑。
entries.en: Soon he took overall command of the Yongxing Palace Division troops together with the Shali, Zhuala, and two Pishi armies, and with Privy Councilor Yelü Xiezhen recovered the prefectures and districts lost in Shanxi.
entries.literal: Soon he took overall command of the Yongxing Palace Division troops and the Shali, Zhuala, and two Pishi armies, and with Privy Councilor Yelü Xiezhen recovered the prefectures and districts lost in Shanxi.

entries.zh: 是冬，攻宋，隸先鋒，圍滿城，率所部先登，拔之，改南京統軍使。
entries.en: That winter, on the attack against Song, he served under the vanguard, besieged Mancheng, led his own troops in the first assault, took the city, and was made Military Commissioner of Nanjing.
entries.literal: That winter, attacking Song, he served under the vanguard, besieged Mancheng, led his own troops in the first ascent, took it, and was made Military Commissioner of Nanjing.

entries.zh: 尚衛國公主，拜駙馬都尉，加同政事門下平章事。
entries.en: He married the Princess of Weiguo, was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, and made Associate Director under the Gate and Chancellor of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He married the Princess of Weiguo, was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, and made Associate Director under the Gate and Chancellor of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十三年，歷北、南院宣徽使。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he served in succession as Commissioner of the Northern and Southern Division Court of Palace Attendants.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he served in succession as Commissioner of the Southern and Northern Division Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 條上時政得失及賦役法，上嘉納焉。
entries.en: He submitted a memorial on the strengths and weaknesses of current policy and on tax and corvée law; the emperor praised and adopted it.
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial on the gains and losses of current policy and the tax and corvée laws; the emperor praised and adopted it.

entries.zh: 十五年，加政事令，遷東京留守。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was made Director of Affairs and transferred to regent of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was made Director of Affairs and transferred to regent of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 二十二年，復攻宋，將渤海軍，下德清軍。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year he again attacked Song, led the Bohai army, and captured Deqing Army.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he again attacked Song, led the Bohai army, and took Deqing Army.

entries.zh: 後蕭撻凜卒，專任南面事。
entries.en: After Xiao Talin died, he was entrusted alone with southern affairs.
entries.literal: After Xiao Talin died, he was solely entrusted with southern affairs.

entries.zh: 宋和議成，為北府宰相。
entries.en: When peace with Song was concluded, he became Chancellor of the Northern Administration.
entries.literal: When the Song peace was concluded, he became Chancellor of the Northern Administration.

entries.zh: 聖宗征高麗，將兵由北道進，至開京西嶺，破敵兵，斬數千級。
entries.en: When Emperor Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo, he led troops along the northern route to Xiling west of Kaesong, defeated the enemy, and took several thousand heads.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo, he led troops by the northern route to Xiling west of Kaesong, defeated the enemy, and took several thousand heads.

entries.zh: 高麗王詢懼，奔平州。
entries.en: Goryeo King Sun was afraid and fled to Pingzhou.
entries.literal: King Sun of Goryeo was afraid and fled to Pingzhou.

entries.zh: 排押入開京，大掠而還。
entries.en: Paiya entered Kaesong, plundered extensively, and returned.
entries.literal: Paiya entered Kaesong, plundered on a great scale, and returned.

entries.zh: 帝嘉之，封蘭陵郡王。
entries.en: The emperor commended him and enfeoffed him as Prince of Lanling.
entries.literal: The emperor commended him and enfeoffed him as Prince of Lanling.

entries.zh: 開泰二年，以宰相知西南面招討使。
entries.en: In the second year of Kaitai, while serving as chancellor, he was made Southwestern Pacification Commissioner.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaitai, as chancellor he was made Commissioner for the Southwestern Pacification Commissioner.

entries.zh: 五年，進王東平。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was advanced to Prince of Dongping.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to Prince of Dongping.

entries.zh: 排押為政寬裕而善斷，諸部畏愛，民以殷富，時議多之。
entries.en: Paiya governed with leniency yet firm judgment; the tribes both feared and loved him, the people grew prosperous, and contemporaries greatly praised him.
entries.literal: Paiya's government was lenient yet decisive; the tribes feared and loved him, the people grew prosperous, and opinion at the time greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 七年，再伐高麗，至開京，敵奔潰，縱兵俘掠而還。
entries.en: In the seventh year he again campaigned against Goryeo. Reaching Kaesong, he routed the enemy and led his troops in capture and plunder before returning.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he again campaigned against Goryeo; reaching Kaesong, the enemy fled in rout and he led his troops in capture and plunder before returning.

entries.zh: 渡茶、陀二河，敵夾射，排押委甲仗走，坐是免官。
entries.en: Crossing the Cha and Tuo rivers, the enemy shot at them from both flanks. Paiya cast off his armor and arms and fled, and for this was removed from office.
entries.literal: Crossing the Cha and Tuo rivers, the enemy shot at them from both sides; Paiya cast off armor and arms and fled, and for this was removed from office.

entries.zh: 太平三年，復王豳，薨。
entries.en: In the third year of Taiping he was again made Prince of Bin and died.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiping he was again made Prince of Bin and died.

entries.zh: 弟恒德。
entries.en: His younger brother Hengde.
entries.literal: His younger brother Hengde.

entries.zh: 耶律資忠，字沃衍，小字劄剌，系出仲父房。
entries.en: Yelü Zizhong, whose style name was Woyan and childhood name Zhala, came from the Second Father House line.
entries.literal: Yelü Zizhong, style name Woyan, childhood name Zhala, was of the Second Father House line.

entries.zh: 兄國留善屬文，聖宗重之。
entries.en: His elder brother Guoliu was skilled at letters, and Emperor Shengzong valued him highly.
entries.literal: His elder brother Guoliu was skilled at letters, and Emperor Shengzong valued him.

entries.zh: 時妻弟之妻阿古與奴通，將奔女直國，國留追及奴，殺之，阿古自經。
entries.en: At that time Agu, wife of his wife's younger brother, had an affair with a slave and was about to flee to the Jurchen state. Guoliu overtook the slave and killed him, and Agu hanged herself.
entries.literal: At that time the wife of his wife's younger brother, Agu, had an affair with a slave and was about to flee to the Jurchen state; Guoliu overtook the slave and killed him, and Agu hanged herself.

entries.zh: 阿古母有寵於太后，事聞，太后怒，將殺之。
entries.en: Agu's mother was favored by the empress dowager. When the matter was reported, the empress dowager was furious and was about to have him executed.
entries.literal: Agu's mother was favored by the empress dowager; when the matter was reported, the empress dowager was angry and was about to kill him.

entries.zh: 帝度不能救，遣人訣別，問以後事。
entries.en: The emperor judged that he could not save him, sent someone to bid him farewell, and asked about affairs afterward.
entries.literal: The emperor judged he could not save him, sent someone to bid farewell, and asked about affairs afterward.

entries.zh: 國留謝曰：「陛下憫臣無辜，恩漏九泉，死且不朽！」
entries.en: Guoliu thanked him, saying: "Your Majesty pities my innocence; your grace reaches the nine springs. Dead, I am not destroyed!"
entries.literal: Guoliu thanked him, saying: "Your Majesty pities my innocence; grace reaching the nine springs—dead, I am not destroyed!"

entries.zh: 既死，人多冤之。
entries.en: After he died, many considered it a grave injustice.
entries.literal: After he died, many considered it a miscarriage of justice.

entries.zh: 在獄著《兔賦》、《寤寐歌》，為世所稱。
entries.en: In prison he composed the "Rabbit Rhapsody" and "Songs of Waking and Dreaming," works praised in his time.
entries.literal: In prison he composed "Rabbit Rhapsody" and "Songs of Waking and Dreaming," praised by the age.

entries.zh: 蕭敵烈，字涅魯袞，宰相撻烈四世孫。
entries.en: Xiao Dilie, whose style name was Nielugun, was a fourth-generation descendant of Chancellor Talie.
entries.literal: Xiao Dilie, style name Nielugun, was a fourth-generation descendant of Chancellor Talie.

entries.zh: 識度弘遠，為鄉里推重。
entries.en: He was far-sighted and widely respected in his home district.
entries.literal: His breadth of vision was far-reaching, and he was esteemed in his home district.

entries.zh: 始為牛群敞史。
entries.en: He began his career as Herald of the Cattle Herds.
entries.literal: He began as Herald of the Cattle Herds.

entries.zh: 帝聞其賢，召入侍，遷國舅詳穩。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of his talent, he summoned him to attend at court and promoted him to Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of his worth, he summoned him to attend at court and promoted him to Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

entries.zh: 統和二十八年，帝謂群臣曰：「高麗康肇弒其君誦，立誦族兄詢而相之，大逆也。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year of Tonghe, the emperor told his ministers: "In Goryeo, Kang Zhao murdered King Song and installed Song's clansman Sun as king while serving as his minister. This is the gravest treason.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Tonghe, the emperor said to his ministers: "Goryeo's Kang Zhao murdered his lord Song and installed Song's clansman Sun as king while serving as his minister—this is supreme treason.

entries.zh: 宜發兵問其罪。」
entries.en: We ought to send troops to demand an accounting for his crime."
entries.literal: We should send troops to call him to account for his crime."

entries.zh: 群臣皆曰可。
entries.en: All the ministers agreed.
entries.literal: All the ministers said this was right.

entries.zh: 敵烈諫曰：「國家連年征討，士卒抏敝。
entries.en: Dilie remonstrated: "The state has fought campaign after campaign, and the troops are exhausted.
entries.literal: Dilie remonstrated, saying: "The state has campaigned year after year, and the soldiers are worn out.

entries.zh: 況陛下在諒陰，年谷不登，創痍未復。
entries.en: Moreover, Your Majesty is still in mourning, the harvests have been poor, and the scars of war have not yet healed.
entries.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty is in mourning, the harvests have failed, and the wounds of war are not yet healed.

entries.zh: 島夷小國，城壘完固，勝不為武，萬一失利，恐貽後悔。
entries.en: That island kingdom is small, yet its walls and defenses are strong. Victory would add little to our martial renown, while a single setback could bring lasting regret.
entries.literal: That island realm is a small country with stout walls and defenses; victory would not redound to our martial glory, and if we should meet defeat we may come to regret it.

entries.zh: 不如遣一介之使，往問其故。
entries.en: It would be better to send a lone envoy to inquire into the affair.
