entries.literal: It would be better to send a single envoy to inquire into the matter.

entries.zh: 彼若伏罪則已；
entries.en: If they submit to judgment, well and good;
entries.literal: If they submit to judgment, so be it;

entries.zh: 不然，俟服除歲豐，舉兵未晚。」
entries.en: if not, wait until mourning is ended and the harvest is full—then it will not be too late to take the field."
entries.literal: if not, wait until mourning is ended and the year's grain is abundant—raising troops then will not be too late."

entries.zh: 時令已下，言雖不行，識者韙之。
entries.en: Although the command had already been issued and his counsel was not adopted, men of judgment approved it.
entries.literal: Although the order had already been issued and his words were not followed, those of insight approved them.

entries.zh: 明年，同知左夷離畢事。
entries.en: The following year he became Associate Director of the Left Irbi.
entries.literal: The next year he served as Associate Director of the Left Irbi.

entries.zh: 改右夷離畢。
entries.en: He was transferred to Right Irbi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to the Right Irbi.

entries.zh: 開泰初，率兵巡西邊。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Kaitai era he led troops on patrol along the western frontier.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaitai he led troops to patrol the western frontier.

entries.zh: 時夷離堇部下閘撒狘撲裏、失室、勃葛率部民遁，敵烈追擒之，令復業，遷國舅詳穩。
entries.en: At that time, under the Irbi Chief, the tribal leaders Zhapusa Puli, Shishi, and Boge led their people in flight. Dilie pursued them, captured them, restored them to their livelihoods, and was again appointed Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
entries.literal: At that time under the Irbi Chief, the tribal leaders Zhapusa Puli, Shishi, and Boge led their people in flight; Dilie pursued and captured them, had them resume their livelihoods, and was transferred to Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

entries.zh: 從樞密使耶律世良伐高麗。
entries.en: He followed Privy Councilor Yelü Shiliang on the campaign against Goryeo.
entries.literal: He followed Privy Councilor Yelü Shiliang in the campaign against Goryeo.

entries.zh: 還，加同政事門下平章事，拜上京留守。
entries.en: On his return he was made Associate Director under the Gate and Chancellor of the Secretariat and appointed regent of the Supreme Capital.
entries.literal: On his return he was made Associate Director under the Gate and Chancellor of the Secretariat, and appointed Regent of the Supreme Capital.

entries.zh: 敵烈為人寬厚，達政體，廷臣皆謂有王佐才。
entries.en: Dilie was magnanimous by nature and well versed in governance; officials at court all said he had the talent to assist a ruler.
entries.literal: Dilie was by nature magnanimous and versed in government; court officials all said he had the talent to assist a king.

entries.zh: 漢人行宮都部署王繼忠薦其材可為樞密使，帝疑其黨而止。
entries.en: Wang Jizhong, Chief Deployment Officer of the Han Palace Establishment, recommended him as fit for Privy Councilor, but the emperor suspected clique-building and held back.
entries.literal: Wang Jizhong, Chief Deployment Officer of the Han Palace Establishment, recommended that his ability suited him for Privy Councilor, but the emperor suspected faction and did not act.

entries.zh: 為中京留守，卒。
entries.en: He served as regent of the Central Capital and died in office.
entries.literal: He served as regent of the Central Capital and died.

entries.zh: 族子忽古，有傳。
entries.en: His clansman Hugu has a separate biography.
entries.literal: His clansman Hugu has a separate biography.

entries.zh: 弟拔剌。
entries.en: His younger brother Balaci.
entries.literal: His younger brother Balaci.

entries.zh: 匹敵，字蘇隱，一名昌裔。
entries.en: Pike, whose style name was Suyin, was also known as Changyi.
entries.literal: Pike, style name Suyin, also called Changyi.

entries.zh: 生未月，父母俱死，育於禁掖。
entries.en: Within a month of his birth both parents had died, and he was reared in the inner palace.
entries.literal: Within a month of birth both parents died; he was reared in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 既長，尚秦晉王公主，拜駙馬都尉，為殿前副點檢。
entries.en: When he came of age he married the Princess of the Qin-Jin King, was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, and made Deputy Chief Inspector of the Palace Front.
entries.literal: When he grew up he married the Princess of the Qin-Jin King, was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, and made Deputy Chief Inspector of the Palace Front.

entries.zh: 統和八年，改北面林牙。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Tonghe he was transferred to Northern Division Linya.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Tonghe he was transferred to Northern Division Linya.

entries.zh: 太平四年，遷殿前都點檢，出為國舅詳穩。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Taiping he was made Chief Inspector of the Palace Front and then appointed Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping he was transferred to Chief Inspector of the Palace Front and went out as Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan.

entries.zh: 九年，渤海大延琳叛，劫掠鄰部，與南京留守蕭孝穆往討。
entries.en: In the ninth year, when the Bohai leader Dayan Lin rebelled and raided neighboring tribes, he campaigned with Nanjing Regent Xiao Xiaomu to suppress him.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, when the Bohai leader Dayan Lin rebelled and raided neighboring tribes, he went with Nanjing Regent Xiao Xiaomu to suppress him.

entries.zh: 孝穆欲全城降，乃築重城圍之，數月，城中人陰來納款，遂擒延琳，東京平，以功封蘭陵郡王。
entries.en: Xiaomu wished to secure the city by surrender and built heavy fortifications to besiege it. After several months people inside secretly came to submit, Dayan Lin was captured, the Eastern Capital was pacified, and for this Pike was enfeoffed Prince of Lanling.
entries.literal: Xiaomu wished to take the whole city by surrender and built heavy fortifications to besiege it; after several months people in the city secretly came to submit, and they captured Dayan Lin; the Eastern Capital was pacified, and for this he was enfeoffed Prince of Lanling.

entries.zh: 十一年，聖宗不豫。
entries.en: In the eleventh year Emperor Shengzong fell ill.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year Emperor Shengzong fell ill.

entries.zh: 先是，欽哀與仁德皇后有隙，以匹敵嘗為後所愛，忌之。
entries.en: Earlier, Qinai and Empress Rendé had been at odds. Because Pike had once been favored by the empress, Qinai resented him.
entries.literal: Earlier, Qinai and Empress Rendé had been at odds; because Pike had once been loved by the empress, she resented him.

entries.zh: 時護衛馮家奴上變，誣後弟浞卜與匹敵謀逆，以皇后攝政，徐議當立者。
entries.en: At that time the guard Feng Jianu submitted a report of treason, falsely accusing the empress's younger brother Chubuo and Pike of plotting rebellion so that the empress might hold the regency, and they might then deliberate who should be enthroned.
entries.literal: At that time the guard Feng Jianu submitted a report of treason, falsely accusing the empress's younger brother Chubuo and Pike of plotting rebellion while the empress dowager held the regency, to deliberate in time who should be enthroned.

entries.zh: 公主竊聞其謀，謂匹敵曰：「爾將無罪被戮。
entries.en: The princess secretly heard of the plot and said to Pike: "You will soon be put to death though guilty of nothing.
entries.literal: The princess secretly heard of the plot and said to Pike: "You will soon be executed without crime.

entries.zh: 與其死，何若奔女直國以全其生！」
entries.en: Rather than die, why not flee to the Jurchen state and save your life!"
entries.literal: Rather than die, why not flee to the Jurchen state to preserve your life!"

entries.zh: 匹敵曰：「朝廷詎肯以飛語害忠良？
entries.en: Pike said: "Would the court truly harm the loyal on mere rumor?
entries.literal: Pike said: "Would the court truly harm the loyal on mere rumor?

entries.zh: 寧死弗適他國。」
entries.en: I would rather die than go to another country."
entries.literal: Better to die than go to another country."

entries.zh: 及欽哀攝政，殺之。
entries.en: When Qinai took the regency, she had him killed.
entries.literal: When Qinai took the regency, she killed him.

entries.zh: 資忠博學，工辭章，年四十未仕。
entries.en: Zizhong was broadly learned and skilled at literary composition, yet had not taken office by the age of forty.
entries.literal: Zizhong was broadly learned, skilled at literary composition, and had not taken office by age forty.

entries.zh: 聖宗知其賢，召補宿衛。
entries.en: Emperor Shengzong knew his worth and summoned him to serve in the palace guard.
entries.literal: Emperor Shengzong knew his worth and summoned him to fill a post in the palace guard.

entries.zh: 數問以古今治亂，資忠對無隱。
entries.en: Several times the emperor asked him about order and disorder in past and present times; Zizhong answered without concealment.
entries.literal: Several times he was asked about order and disorder in past and present; Zizhong answered without concealment.

entries.zh: 開泰中，授中丞，眷遇日隆。
entries.en: During the Kaitai era he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, and imperial favor toward him grew daily.
entries.literal: During Kaitai he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and his favor grew daily.

entries.zh: 初，高麗內屬，取女直六部地以賜。
entries.en: Earlier, when Goryeo was an inner dependency, the lands of the six Jurchen tribes had been granted to it.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Goryeo was an inner dependency, it had been given the lands of the six Jurchen tribes.

entries.zh: 至是，貢獻不時至，詔資忠往問故。
entries.en: By this time tribute and offerings did not arrive on schedule. An edict ordered Zizhong to go and inquire into the cause.
entries.literal: By this time tribute and offerings did not arrive on schedule; an edict ordered Zizhong to go inquire into the cause.

entries.zh: 高麗無歸地意。
entries.en: Goryeo had no intention of returning the land.
entries.literal: Goryeo had no intention of returning the land.

entries.zh: 由是權貴數短於上，出為上京副留守。
entries.en: For this the powerful often spoke ill of him to the emperor, and he was sent out as Deputy Regent of the Supreme Capital.
entries.literal: For this the powerful often spoke ill of him to the emperor; he was sent out as Deputy Regent of the Supreme Capital.

entries.zh: 三年，再使高麗，留弗遣。
entries.en: In the third year he was again sent to Goryeo and detained without being allowed to return.
entries.literal: In the third year he was again sent to Goryeo and detained without being sent back.

entries.zh: 資忠每懷君親，輒有著述，號《西亭集》。
entries.en: Zizhong always yearned for sovereign and kin and would compose writings, which he titled Collected at the Western Pavilion.
entries.literal: Zizhong always yearned for sovereign and kin and would compose writings, titled Collected at the Western Pavilion.

entries.zh: 帝與群臣宴，時一記憶曰：「資忠亦有此樂乎？」
entries.en: The emperor feasted with his ministers and at one point recalled: "Does Zizhong also enjoy pleasures such as these?"
entries.literal: The emperor feasted with his ministers; at one point he recalled: "Does Zizhong also have this pleasure?"

entries.zh: 九年，高麗上表謝罪，始送資忠還。
entries.en: In the ninth year Goryeo submitted a memorial begging pardon and at last sent Zizhong back.
entries.literal: In the ninth year Goryeo submitted a memorial begging pardon and at last sent Zizhong back.

entries.zh: 帝郊迎，同載以歸，命大臣宴勞，留禁中數日。
entries.en: The emperor met him in the suburbs and rode back with him in the same carriage. He ordered the great ministers to feast and reward him and kept him in the palace several days.
entries.literal: The emperor met him in the suburbs and rode back with him in the same carriage; he ordered the great ministers to feast and reward him and kept him in the palace several days.

entries.zh: 謂曰：「朕將屈卿為樞密，何如？」
entries.en: He said to him: "I intend to appoint you Privy Councilor. What do you think?"
entries.literal: He said to him: "I intend to bend you to Privy Councilor—what do you think?"

entries.zh: 資忠對曰：「臣不才，不敢奉詔。」
entries.en: Zizhong replied: "Your servant lacks talent and dares not accept the edict."
entries.literal: Zizhong replied: "Your servant is without talent and dares not accept the edict."

entries.zh: 乃以為林牙，知惕隱事。
entries.en: He was then made Linya and given charge of Tiyin affairs.
entries.literal: He was then made Linya and given charge of Tiyin affairs.

entries.zh: 初，資忠在高麗也，弟昭為著帳郎君，坐罪沒家產。
entries.en: Earlier, while Zizhong was in Goryeo, his younger brother Zhao was a Registered Langjun. For a crime his family property was confiscated.
entries.literal: Earlier, while Zizhong was in Goryeo, his younger brother Zhao was a Registered Langjun; for a crime his family property was confiscated.

entries.zh: 至是，乃復橫帳，且還舊產，詔以外戚女妻之。
entries.en: By this time he was restored to the Horizontal Tent and his former property was returned. An edict gave him a woman of the imperial maternal clan in marriage.
entries.literal: By this time he was restored to the Horizontal Tent and his former property returned; an edict gave him an imperial maternal-clan woman in marriage.

entries.zh: 是時，樞密使蕭合卓、少師蕭把哥有寵，資忠不背俯附，詆之。
entries.en: At that time Privy Councilor Xiao Hezhuo and Junior Tutor Xiao Bage were in favor. Zizhong would not bow and follow them and spoke against them.
entries.literal: At that time Privy Councilor Xiao Hezhuo and Junior Tutor Xiao Bage were in favor; Zizhong would not bow and follow them and slandered them.

entries.zh: 帝怒，奪官。
entries.en: The emperor was angry and stripped him of his office.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry and stripped his office.

entries.zh: 數歲，出知來遠城事，歷保安、昭德二軍節度使。
entries.en: After several years he went out to manage affairs at Laiyuan City and served in succession as Military Commissioner of the Bao'an and Zhaode armies.
entries.literal: After several years he went out to manage affairs at Laiyuan City and served in succession as Military Commissioner of Bao'an and Zhaode armies.

entries.zh: 聖宗崩，表請會葬。
entries.en: When Emperor Shengzong died, he submitted a memorial requesting permission to attend the funeral.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shengzong died, he submitted a memorial requesting to attend the funeral.

entries.zh: 既至，伏梓宮大慟曰：「臣幸遇聖明，橫被構譖，不獲盡犬馬報。」
entries.en: When he arrived he prostrated himself before the bier and wailed greatly: "Your servant was fortunate to meet a sage ruler, yet was slandered on every side and could not exhaust himself in loyal service like a dog or horse."
entries.literal: When he arrived he prostrated himself before the bier and wailed greatly: "Your servant was fortunate to meet a sage ruler yet was slandered across the board and could not exhaust himself like a dog or horse in service."

entries.zh: 氣絕而蘇，興宗命醫治疾。
entries.en: He fainted and revived. Emperor Xingzong ordered physicians to treat his illness.
entries.literal: He fainted and revived; Emperor Xingzong ordered physicians to treat his illness.

entries.zh: 久之，言國舅侍中無憂國心，陛下不當復用唐景福舊號，於是用事者惡之，遣歸鎮，卒。
entries.en: After a long while he said the imperial maternal-clan attendant lacked a mind to worry for the state and that Your Majesty ought not again to use the old title of Tang Jingfu. For this those in power hated him, sent him back to his command, and he died.
entries.literal: After a long while he said the imperial maternal-clan attendant lacked a mind to worry for the state, and that Your Majesty ought not again to use the old title of Tang Jingfu; for this those in power hated him, sent him back to his command, and he died.

entries.zh: 弟昭，有傳。
entries.en: His younger brother Zhao has a separate biography.
entries.literal: His younger brother Zhao has a separate biography.

entries.zh: 拔剌，字別勒隱。
entries.en: Balaci, whose style name was Biele Yin.
entries.literal: Balaci, style name Biele Yin.

entries.zh: 多智，善騎射。
entries.en: He was clever and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
entries.literal: He was resourceful and skilled at mounted archery.

entries.zh: 開泰間，以兄為右夷離畢，始補郎君，累遷奚六部禿裏太尉。
entries.en: During the Kaitai period, as his elder brother served as Right Irbi, he was first appointed Langjun and rose through several posts to Grand Commandant of the Six Xi Tribes Tulü.
entries.literal: During Kaitai, because his elder brother was Right Irbi, he was first appointed Langjun and rose through several posts to Grand Commandant of the Six Xi Tribes Tulü.

entries.zh: 太平末，大延琳叛，拔剌將北、南院兵往討，遇於蒲水，南院兵少卻。
entries.en: At the end of the Taiping era, when Dayan Lin rebelled, Balaci led the Northern and Southern Division armies to suppress him. They met at Pushui, where the Southern Division had fewer troops and fell back.
entries.literal: At the end of Taiping, when Dayan Lin rebelled, Balaci led the Northern and Southern Division armies to suppress him; they met at Pushui, and the Southern Division troops were few and fell back.

entries.zh: 至手山，復與賊遇。
entries.en: At Mount Shou they encountered the rebels again.
entries.literal: At Mount Shou they again encountered the rebels.

entries.zh: 拔剌乃易兩院旗幟，鼓勇力戰，破之。
entries.en: Balaci then exchanged the banners of the two divisions, roused their fighting spirit, and broke the enemy.
entries.literal: Balaci then exchanged the banners of the two divisions, roused their courage, and fought fiercely, breaking the enemy.

entries.zh: 上聞，以手詔褒獎，賜內廄馬。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of it, he rewarded him with a handwritten edict and gave him a stallion from the imperial stables.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he rewarded him with a handwritten edict and bestowed a stallion from the inner stables.

entries.zh: 重熙中，遷四捷軍詳穩，謝事歸鄉里。
entries.en: During the Chongxi era he was made Detailed Commandant of the Four Swift Armies, then resigned and returned to his home district.
entries.literal: During Chongxi he was transferred to Detailed Commandant of the Four Swift Armies and resigned to return to his home district.

entries.zh: 數歲，起為昭德軍節度使，尋改國舅詳穩，卒。
entries.en: Several years later he was recalled as Military Commissioner of the Zhaode Army, soon after made Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan, and died.
entries.literal: After several years he was recalled as Military Commissioner of the Zhaode Army, then soon changed to Detailed Commandant of the Imperial Maternal Clan, and died.

entries.zh: 耶律盆奴，字胡獨堇，惕隱涅魯古之孫。
entries.en: Yelü Pennu, whose style name was Hudujin, was a grandson of Tiyin Nielugu.
entries.literal: Yelü Pennu, style name Hudujin, was a grandson of Tiyin Nielugu.

entries.zh: 景宗時，為烏古部詳穩，政尚嚴急，民苦之。
entries.en: Under Emperor Jingzong he served as Detailed Commandant of the Wugu Tribe. His rule was harsh and severe, and the people suffered.
entries.literal: During Emperor Jingzong's reign he was Detailed Commandant of the Wugu Tribe; his government was severe and harsh, and the people suffered under it.

entries.zh: 有司以聞，詔曰：「盆奴任方面寄，以細故究問，恐損威望。」
entries.en: The responsible office reported this, and an edict said: "Pennu holds a frontier commission; to pursue him over trifles would damage his authority."
entries.literal: The responsible office reported this, and an edict said: "Pennu holds a frontier post; to pursue petty matters in inquiry would damage his authority."

entries.zh: 尋遷馬群太保。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to Grand Guardian of the Horse Herds.
entries.literal: Soon after he was transferred to Grand Guardian of the Horse Herds.

entries.zh: 統和十六年，隱實燕軍之不任事者，汰之。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year of Tonghe he secretly identified men in the Hidden Elite Yan Army unfit for duty and removed them.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year of Tonghe he secretly identified those in the Hidden Elite Yan Army unfit for duty and culled them.

entries.zh: 二十八年，駕征高麗，盆奴為先鋒。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year, when the emperor campaigned against Goryeo, Pennu served as vanguard.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when the emperor campaigned against Goryeo, Pennu served as vanguard.

entries.zh: 至銅州，高麗將康肇分兵為三以抗我軍：一營於州西，據三水之會，肇居其中；
entries.en: At Tongzhou, the Goryeo general Kang Zhao divided his army into three to resist our forces: one camp west of the prefecture at the confluence of the Three Waters, with Zhao in the center;
entries.literal: When they reached Tongzhou, the Goryeo general Kang Zhao divided his forces into three to resist our army: one camp west of the prefecture at the confluence of the Three Waters, with Zhao in the center;

entries.zh: 一營近州之山；
entries.en: one camp on the hills near the prefecture;
entries.literal: one camp on the hills near the prefecture;

entries.zh: 一附城而營。
entries.en: and one camped against the city walls.
entries.literal: and one camped against the city wall.

entries.zh: 盆奴率耶律弘古擊破三水營，擒肇，李玄蘊等軍望風潰。
entries.en: Pennu led Yelü Honggu, broke the Three Waters camp, and captured Zhao. The forces of Li Xuanyun and others fled at the sight of them.
entries.literal: Pennu led Yelü Honggu, broke the Three Waters camp, captured Zhao, and the army of Li Xuanyun and others collapsed at the mere sight of them.

entries.zh: 會大軍至，斬三萬餘級，追至開京，破敵於西嶺。
entries.en: When the main army arrived, more than thirty thousand heads were taken. They pursued to Kaesong and defeated the enemy at Xiling.
entries.literal: When the main army arrived, more than thirty thousand heads were taken; they pursued to Kaesong and defeated the enemy at Xiling.

entries.zh: 高麗王詢聞邊城不守，遁去。
entries.en: When Goryeo King Sun heard that the border cities had fallen, he fled.
entries.literal: When King Sun of Goryeo heard that the border cities were lost, he fled.

entries.zh: 盆奴入開京，焚其王宮，乃撫慰其民人。
entries.en: Pennu entered Kaesong, burned the royal palace, and then reassured the populace.
entries.literal: Pennu entered Kaesong, burned the royal palace, and then comforted the people.

entries.zh: 上嘉其功，遷北院大王，薨。
entries.en: The emperor praised his achievement and made him Grand Prince of the Northern Division; he later died.
entries.literal: The emperor praised his achievement, transferred him to Grand Prince of the Northern Division, and he died.

entries.zh: 恒德，字遜寧。
entries.en: Hengde, whose style name was Xunning.
entries.literal: Hengde, style name Xunning.

entries.zh: 有膽略而善謀。
entries.en: He was bold and resourceful and skilled in planning.
entries.literal: He had daring and stratagem and was skilled in planning.

entries.zh: 統和元年，尚越國公主，拜駙馬都尉，遷南面林牙。
entries.en: In the first year of Tonghe he married the Princess of Yueguo, was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, and transferred to Southern Division Linya.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tonghe he married the Princess of Yueguo, was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, and transferred to Southern Division Linya.

entries.zh: 從宣徽使耶律阿沒裏征高麗還，改北面林牙。
entries.en: Following Imperial Clan Commissioner Yelü Amoli on the campaign against Goryeo, on his return he was transferred to Northern Division Linya.
entries.literal: Following Imperial Clan Commissioner Yelü Amoli on the campaign against Goryeo, on his return he was changed to Northern Division Linya.

entries.zh: 會宋將曹彬、米信侵燕，耶律休哥與恒德議軍事，多見信用，為東京留守。
entries.en: When the Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin invaded Yan, Yelü Xiuge and Hengde deliberated on military affairs. Hengde was often trusted and made regent of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: When the Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin invaded Yan, Yelü Xiuge and Hengde deliberated on military affairs; he was often trusted and made regent of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 六年，上攻宋，圍沙堆，恒德獨當一面。
entries.en: In the sixth year, attacking Song, they besieged Shadui; Hengde alone held one sector of the siege.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, on the attack against Song, they besieged Shadui; Hengde alone held one face of the siege.

entries.zh: 城上矢石如雨，恒德意氣自若，督將士奪其陴。
entries.en: Arrows and stones rained on the walls, yet Hengde remained calm and urged his officers and men to seize the parapet.
entries.literal: Arrows and stones rained on the wall like rain, yet Hengde remained calm in spirit and urged his officers and men to seize the parapet.

entries.zh: 城陷，中流矢，太后親臨視，賜藥。
entries.en: When the city fell he was struck by a stray arrow. The empress dowager came in person to visit him and bestowed medicine.
entries.literal: When the city fell he was struck by a flying arrow; the empress dowager came in person to visit him and bestowed medicine.

entries.zh: 攻長城口，復先登，太后益多其功。
entries.en: Attacking Changcheng Pass, he again led the first assault; the empress dowager praised his merit all the more.
entries.literal: Attacking Changcheng Pass, he again led the first ascent; the empress dowager praised his merit all the more.

entries.zh: 時高麗未附，恒德受詔，率兵拔其邊城。
entries.en: At that time Goryeo had not yet submitted. Hengde received an edict and led troops to capture its border cities.
entries.literal: At that time Goryeo had not yet submitted; Hengde received an edict and led troops to capture its border cities.

entries.zh: 王始懼，上表請降。
entries.en: The king then grew afraid and submitted a memorial requesting surrender.
entries.literal: The king then grew afraid and submitted a memorial requesting surrender.

entries.zh: 十二年八月，賜啟聖竭力功臣。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the twelfth year he was granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Exhausts Himself for Qisheng.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year he was granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Exhausts Himself for Qisheng.

entries.zh: 從都部署和朔奴討兀惹，未戰，兀惹請降。
entries.en: He followed Chief Deployment Officer Heshuonu in the campaign against Wunai. Before battle was joined, Wunai requested surrender.
entries.literal: He followed Chief Deployment Officer Heshuonu in the campaign against Wunai; before battle was joined, Wunai requested surrender.

entries.zh: 恒德利其俘獲，不許。
entries.en: Hengde coveted the captives and would not permit it.
entries.literal: Hengde coveted the captives and would not allow it.

entries.zh: 兀惹死戰，城不能拔。
entries.en: Wunai fought to the death and the city could not be taken.
entries.literal: Wunai fought to the death and the city could not be taken.

entries.zh: 和朔奴議欲引退，恒德曰：「以彼倔強，吾奉詔來討，無功而還，諸部謂我何！
entries.en: Heshuonu deliberated on withdrawing. Hengde said: "They are so stubborn, yet we came by imperial edict to chastise them. If we return without achievement, what will the tribes say of us!
entries.literal: Heshuonu deliberated on withdrawing; Hengde said: "Given their stubborn defiance, we have come by imperial edict to chastise them—if we return without achievement, what will the tribes say of us!

entries.zh: 若深入多獲，猶勝徒返。」
entries.en: If we penetrate deep and take much booty, that is still better than turning back empty-handed."
entries.literal: If we penetrate deep and take much booty, that is still better than returning empty-handed."

entries.zh: 和朔奴不得已，進擊東南諸部，至高麗北鄙。
entries.en: Heshuonu had no choice. They advanced and attacked the southeastern tribes, reaching the northern marches of Goryeo.
entries.literal: Heshuonu had no choice; they advanced and attacked the southeastern tribes, reaching the northern marches of Goryeo.

entries.zh: 比還，道遠糧絕，士馬死傷者眾，坐是削功臣號。
entries.en: By the time they returned, the road was long and provisions were exhausted. Many soldiers and horses died or were wounded, and for this his meritorious title was stripped.
entries.literal: By the time they returned, the road was long and provisions exhausted; many soldiers and horses died or were wounded, and for this his meritorious title was stripped.

entries.zh: 十四年，為行軍都部署，伐蒲盧毛朵部。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was Chief Campaign Deployment Officer and campaigned against the Pulü Maoduo tribe.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was Chief Campaign Deployment Officer and campaigned against the Pulü Maoduo tribe.

entries.zh: 還，公主疾，太后遣宮人賢釋侍之，恒德私焉。
entries.en: On his return the princess fell ill. The empress dowager sent the palace woman Xian Shi to nurse her, and Hengde took her privately.
entries.literal: On his return, the princess fell ill; the empress dowager sent the palace woman Xian Shi to attend her, and Hengde had an affair with her.

entries.zh: 公主恚而薨，太后怒，賜死。
entries.en: The princess died in anger. The empress dowager was furious and ordered him put to death.
entries.literal: The princess died of rage, the empress dowager was angry, and he was sentenced to death.

entries.zh: 後追封蘭陵郡王。
entries.en: He was later posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling.
entries.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling.

entries.zh: 子匹敵。
entries.en: His son Pike.
entries.literal: His son Pike.

entries.zh: 耶律瑤質，字拔裏堇，積慶宮人。
entries.en: Yelü Yaozhi, whose style name was Balijin, was a man of the Jiqing Palace.
entries.literal: Yelü Yaozhi, style name Balijin, was a man of the Jiqing Palace.

entries.zh: 父侯古，室韋部節度使。
entries.en: His father Hougu was Military Commissioner of the Shivei Tribe.
entries.literal: His father Hougu was Military Commissioner of the Shivei Tribe.

entries.zh: 瑤質篤學廉介，有經世誌。
entries.en: Yaozhi was devoted to learning, upright and self-restrained, and had the will to bring order to the age.
entries.literal: Yaozhi was devoted in learning, upright and self-restrained, and had the will to order the age.

entries.zh: 統和十年，累遷至積慶宮使。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Tonghe he rose through several posts to Commissioner of the Jiqing Palace.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Tonghe he rose through several posts to Commissioner of the Jiqing Palace.

entries.zh: 聖宗嘗諭瑤質曰：「聞卿正直，是以進用。
entries.en: Emperor Shengzong once instructed Yaozhi: "I have heard you are upright, and for this I advance you.
entries.literal: Emperor Shengzong once instructed Yaozhi: "I have heard you are upright, and for this I advance you.

entries.zh: 國有利害，爾言宜無所隱。」
entries.en: Where the state has benefit or harm, you should speak without concealment."
entries.literal: Where the state has benefit or harm, in your words you should conceal nothing."

entries.zh: 由是所陳多見嘉納。
entries.en: For this what he presented was often praised and adopted.
entries.literal: For this what he presented was often praised and adopted.

entries.zh: 上征高麗，破康肇軍於銅州，瑤質之力為多。
entries.en: When the emperor campaigned against Goryeo and defeated Kang Zhao's army at Tongzhou, Yaozhi's effort counted for much.
entries.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Goryeo and defeated Kang Zhao's army at Tongzhou, Yaozhi's effort counted for much.

entries.zh: 王詢乞降，群臣議皆謂宜納。
entries.en: King Sun begged to surrender. The ministers deliberated and all said he should be accepted.
entries.literal: King Sun begged to surrender; the ministers deliberated and all said he should be accepted.

entries.zh: 瑤質曰：「王詢始一戰而敗，遽求納款，此詐耳，納之恐墮其奸計。
entries.en: Yaozhi said: "King Sun was defeated in a single battle and hastily sought to submit. This is deceit; to accept him now may fall into his treacherous scheme.
entries.literal: Yaozhi said: "King Sun was defeated in a single battle and hastily sought to submit—this is deceit; to accept him may fall into his treacherous scheme.

entries.zh: 待其勢窮力屈，納之未晚。」
entries.en: Wait until his strength is exhausted and his power spent—then it will not be too late to accept him."
entries.literal: Wait until his strength is exhausted and his power spent—accepting him then will not be too late."

entries.zh: 已而詢果遁，清野無所獲。
entries.en: Before long Sun indeed fled. They cleared the countryside but took nothing.
entries.literal: Before long Sun indeed fled; clearing the countryside, nothing was taken.

entries.zh: 其眾阻險而壘，攻之不下，瑤質以計降之。
entries.en: His troops held difficult terrain and built ramparts. The attack could not succeed, and Yaozhi reduced them by stratagem.
entries.literal: His troops held difficult terrain and built ramparts; the attack could not succeed, and Yaozhi reduced them by stratagem.

entries.zh: 擢拜四蕃部詳穩。
entries.en: He was promoted and appointed Detailed Commandant of the Four Fan Tribes.
entries.literal: He was promoted and appointed Detailed Commandant of the Four Fan Tribes.

entries.zh: 時招討使耶律頗的為總官，瑤質恥居其下，上表曰：「臣先朝舊臣，今既垂老，乞還新命，覬得常侍左右。」
entries.en: At that time Pacification Commissioner Yelü Pode was overall commander. Yaozhi was ashamed to serve beneath him and submitted a memorial: "Your servant is an old minister of the former court. Now that I am old, I beg to return the new appointment and hope to attend constantly at Your Majesty's side."
entries.literal: At that time Pacification Commissioner Yelü Pode was overall commander; Yaozhi was ashamed to be beneath him and submitted a memorial: "Your servant is an old minister of the former court; now that I am old, I beg to return the new appointment and hope to attend constantly at Your Majesty's side."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「朕不使汝久處是任。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "I will not let you remain long in that post."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I will not let you long remain in that post."

entries.zh: 且命無隸招討，得專奏事到部。
entries.en: He also ordered that he not be subordinate to the Pacification Commissioner and might memorialize directly on arrival in his district.
entries.literal: He also ordered that he not be subordinate to the Pacification Commissioner and might memorialize directly on arrival in his district.

entries.zh: 戢暴懷善，政績顯著。
entries.en: He restrained violence and cherished kindness. His administrative achievements were conspicuous.
entries.literal: He restrained violence and cherished kindness; his administrative achievements were conspicuous.

entries.zh: 卒於官。
entries.en: He died in office.
entries.literal: He died in office.

entries.zh: 高正，不知何郡人。
entries.en: Gao Zheng—his native commandery is unknown.
entries.literal: Gao Zheng—his native commandery is unknown.

entries.zh: 統和初，舉進士第，累遷樞密直學士。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tonghe he passed the jinshi examination and rose through several posts to Academician Direct of the Privy Council.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe he passed the jinshi examination and rose through several posts to Academician Direct of the Privy Council.

entries.zh: 上將伐高麗，遣正先往諭意。
entries.en: When the emperor was about to campaign against Goryeo, he sent Zheng ahead to announce his intent.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to campaign against Goryeo, he sent Zheng ahead to announce his intent.

entries.zh: 及還，遷右僕射。
entries.en: On his return he was transferred to Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: On his return he was transferred to Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 時高麗王詢表請入覲，上許之，遣正率騎兵千人迓之。
entries.en: At that time Goryeo King Sun memorialized requesting to come to court. The emperor permitted it and sent Zheng with a thousand cavalry to meet him.
entries.literal: At that time Goryeo King Sun memorialized requesting to come to court; the emperor permitted it and sent Zheng with a thousand cavalry to meet him.

entries.zh: 館於路，為高麗將卓思正所圍。
entries.en: He was lodged on the road and was surrounded by the Goryeo general Zhuo Sizheng.
entries.literal: He was lodged on the road and was surrounded by the Goryeo general Zhuo Sizheng.

entries.zh: 正以勢不可敵，與麾下壯士突圍出，士卒死傷者眾。
entries.en: Zheng judged the force could not be resisted. With stalwart men under him he broke through the encirclement, and many soldiers died or were wounded.
entries.literal: Zheng judged the force could not be resisted; with stalwart men under him he broke through the encirclement, and many soldiers died or were wounded.

entries.zh: 上悔輕發，釋其罪。
entries.en: The emperor regretted having acted rashly and remitted his crime.
entries.literal: The emperor regretted having sent lightly and remitted his crime.

entries.zh: 明年，遷工部侍郎，為北院樞密副使。
entries.en: The following year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and made Deputy Privy Councilor of the Northern Division.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and made Deputy Privy Councilor of the Northern Division.

entries.zh: 開泰五年卒。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Kaitai he died.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Kaitai he died.

entries.zh: 耶律的錄，字耶寧，仲父房之後。
entries.en: Yelü Delu, whose style name was Yening, came from the Second Father House line.
entries.literal: Yelü Delu, style name Yening, was of the Second Father House line.

entries.zh: 習兵事，為左皮室詳穩。
entries.en: He studied military affairs and served as Detailed Commandant of the Left Pishi.
entries.literal: He studied military affairs and was Detailed Commandant of the Left Pishi.

entries.zh: 統和二十八年，伐高麗，的錄率本部軍與盆奴等擒康肇、李玄蘊於銅州。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year of Tonghe, on the campaign against Goryeo, Delu led his own division army together with Pennu and others and captured Kang Zhao and Li Xuanyun at Tongzhou.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Tonghe, campaigning against Goryeo, Delu led his own division army with Pennu and others and captured Kang Zhao and Li Xuanyun at Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 帝壯之曰：「以卿英才，為國戮力，真吾家千里駒也！」
entries.en: The emperor praised him, saying: "With your outstanding talent exerted for the state, you are truly our family's thousand-li colt!"
entries.literal: The emperor praised him, saying: "With your outstanding talent exerted for the state, you are truly our family's thousand-li colt!"

entries.zh: 乃賜御馬及細鎧。
entries.en: He then bestowed an imperial horse and fine armor.
entries.literal: He then bestowed an imperial horse and fine armor.

entries.zh: 明年，為北院大王，出為烏古敵烈部都詳穩。
entries.en: The following year he was made Grand Prince of the Northern Division and went out as Overall Detailed Commandant of the Wugu and Dilie Tribes.
entries.literal: The next year he was made Grand Prince of the Northern Division and went out as Overall Detailed Commandant of the Wugu and Dilie Tribes.

entries.zh: 年七十二卒。
entries.en: He died at the age of seventy-two.
entries.literal: He died at age seventy-two.

entries.zh: 蕭敵烈
entries.en: Xiao Dilie
entries.literal: Xiao Dilie

entries.en: (See the biography of Balaci)〉
entries.literal: (Balaci has a separate biography)〉

entries.zh: 耶律盆奴蕭排押
entries.en: Yelü Pennu and Xiao Paiya
entries.literal: Yelü Pennu, Xiao Paiya

entries.zh: 〈（恒德匹敵）〉
entries.en: (See the biographies of Hengde and Pike)〉
entries.literal: (Hengde and Pike have separate biographies)〉

entries.zh: 耶律資忠耶律瑤質耶律弘古高正耶律的錄大康乂
entries.en: Yelü Zizhong, Yelü Yaozhi, Yelü Honggu, Gao Zheng, Yelü Delu, and Da Kangyi
entries.literal: Yelü Zizhong, Yelü Yaozhi, Yelü Honggu, Gao Zheng, Yelü Delu, Da Kangyi

entries.zh: 耶律庶成
entries.en: Yelu Shucheng
entries.literal: Yelu Shucheng

entries.zh: 〈（庶箴 蒲魯）〉
entries.en: (Shuzhen and Pulu)]〉
entries.literal: (Shuzhen, Pulu)]〉

entries.zh: 楊皙 耶 律韓留 楊佶 耶律和尚
entries.en: Yang Xi, Yelu Hanliu, Yang Ji, and Yelu Heshang
entries.literal: Yang Xi, Yelu Hanliu, Yang Ji, Yelu Heshang

entries.zh: 楊佶，字正叔，南京人。
entries.en: Yang Ji, whose style name was Zhengshu, was a native of Nanjing.
entries.literal: Yang Ji, style name Zhengshu, was a man of Nanjing.

entries.zh: 幼穎悟異常，讀書自能成句，識者奇之。
entries.en: As a child his intelligence was extraordinary: when he read he could compose sentences on his own, and observers regarded him as remarkable.
entries.literal: From youth his intelligence was extraordinary; when he read books he could form sentences on his own, and those who knew him marveled at him.

entries.zh: 弱冠，聲名籍甚。
entries.en: By the time he came of age his reputation was already widespread.
entries.literal: By his coming of age his reputation was already great.

entries.zh: 統和二十四年，舉進士第一，歷校書郎、大理正。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year of Tonghe he placed first in the jinshi examination and served successively as collator and director of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Tonghe he took first place in the jinshi examination and served as Collator and as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 開泰六年，轉儀曹郎，典掌書命，加諫議大夫。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Kaitai he was transferred to Gentleman of the Bureau of Rites, placed in charge of written commands, and given the additional title Remonstrating Grand Master.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Kaitai he was transferred to Gentleman of the Bureau of Rites, took charge of written commands, and was given the additional title Remonstrating Grand Master.

entries.zh: 出知易州，治尚清簡，征發期會必信。
entries.en: Posted as prefect of Yizhou, he governed with clarity and restraint, and in levies and scheduled deliveries he was always reliable.
entries.literal: He went out as Prefect of Yizhou; his administration favored clarity and simplicity, and in levies and scheduled deliveries he was always trustworthy.

entries.zh: 入為大理少卿。
entries.en: He was recalled to the capital as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 累遷翰林學士，文章號得體。
entries.en: He rose through successive appointments to Hanlin Academician, and his writings were praised as always apt in tone.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academician; his writings were praised as well suited to occasion.

entries.zh: 八年，燕地饑疫，民多流殍，以佶同知南京留守事，發倉廩，振乏絕，貧民鬻子者計傭而出之。
entries.en: In the eighth year famine and pestilence struck the Yan region, and many people died wandering in destitution. Ji was appointed associate administrator of the Nanjing garrison, opened the granaries, and relieved the needy; for poor families who had sold their children, he calculated wages so they could be redeemed.
entries.literal: In the eighth year famine and pestilence struck the Yan region, and many people wandered off and starved to death; Ji was made Associate Administrator of the Nanjing garrison, opened the granaries, relieved the destitute, and for poor people who had sold their children he calculated wages to redeem them.

entries.zh: 宋遣梅詢賀千齡節，詔佶迎送，多唱酬，詢每見稱賞。
entries.en: When Song sent Mei Xun to congratulate the Thousand-Year Festival, the emperor ordered Ji to receive and escort him. They exchanged many poems in correspondence, and Mei repeatedly praised him in their meetings.
entries.literal: Song sent Mei Xun to congratulate the Thousand-Year Festival; the emperor ordered Ji to receive and escort him; they exchanged many poems in reply, and Xun repeatedly praised him when they met.

entries.zh: 復為翰林學士。
entries.en: He was again appointed Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: He again became Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 重熙元年，升翰林學士承旨。
entries.en: In the first year of Chongxi he was promoted to chief Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: In the first year of Chongxi he was promoted to Chief Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 丁母憂，起復工部尚書。
entries.en: After his mother's death he entered mourning, but was soon recalled to serve as Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When his mother died he entered mourning, then was recalled from mourning to serve as Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 歷忠順軍節度使，朔武等州觀察處置使，天德軍節度使，加特進檢校太師、同中書門下平章事，復拜參知政事，兼知南院樞密使。
entries.en: He served as military governor of Zhongshun Circuit, commissioner for observation and disposition of Shuowu and other prefectures, and military governor of the Tiande Army. He received the additional titles Special Advanced Grand Master and Acting Grand Preceptor with the title associate grand councilor, was again appointed participant in governance, and concurrently served as commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: He served as Military Governor of Zhongshun Circuit, Commissioner for Observation and Disposition of Shuowu and other prefectures, Military Governor of Tiande Army, was given the additional titles of Special Advanced Grand Master and Acting Grand Preceptor with the title Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, was again appointed Participant in Governance, and concurrently served as Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 十五年，出為武定軍節度使。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was posted as military governor of Wuding Circuit.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he went out as Military Governor of Wuding Circuit.

entries.zh: 境內亢旱，苗稼將槁。
entries.en: His jurisdiction suffered severe drought, and the crops were on the verge of withering.
entries.literal: Within his jurisdiction there was severe drought, and the grain crops were about to wither.

entries.zh: 視事之夕，雨澤沾足。
entries.en: On the evening he assumed office, rain fell in abundance.
entries.literal: On the evening he took up office, rain and moisture were fully sufficient.

entries.zh: 百姓歌曰：「何以蘇我？
entries.en: The people sang, "How shall we be revived?
entries.literal: The common people sang: "By what shall we be revived?

entries.zh: 上天降雨。
entries.en: Heaven sends rain.
entries.literal: Heaven sends down rain.

entries.zh: 誰其撫我？
entries.en: Who will care for us?
entries.literal: Who will comfort us?

entries.zh: 楊公為主。」
entries.en: Lord Yang is our lord."
entries.literal: Lord Yang is our master."

entries.zh: 漯陽水失故道，歲為民害，乃以己俸創長橋，人不病涉。
entries.en: The Luoyang River had left its old channel and each year brought harm to the people, so he used his own salary to build a long bridge, sparing travelers the hardship of crossing.
entries.literal: The Luoyang River had lost its old course and every year harmed the people; he therefore used his own salary to build a long bridge, so that people were not troubled in crossing.

entries.zh: 及被召，郡民攀轅泣送。
entries.en: When he was recalled to court, the people of the commandery clung to his carriage and wept as they bade him farewell.
entries.literal: When he was summoned back, the people of the commandery clung to his carriage shafts and wept as they saw him off.

entries.zh: 上御清涼殿宴勞之，即日除吏部尚書，兼門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: The emperor entertained him in the Qingliang Hall to honor his service and that same day appointed him Minister of Personnel with concurrent posts as vice director of the Gate Department and associate grand councilor.
entries.literal: The emperor received him in the Qingliang Hall with a feast to console him and that same day appointed him Minister of Personnel, concurrently Vice Director of the Gate Department and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

entries.zh: 上曰：「卿今日何減呂望之遇文王！」
entries.en: The emperor said, "How is the favor shown you today any less than what Lü Wang received from King Wen!"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "How is your reception today any less than Lü Wang's meeting King Wen!"

entries.zh: 佶對曰：「呂望比臣遭際有十年之晚。」
entries.en: Ji replied, "Compared with me, Lü Wang met his opportunity a full ten years too late."
entries.literal: Ji replied: "Compared with your servant, Lü Wang met his opportunity ten years too late."

entries.zh: 上悅。
entries.en: The emperor was delighted.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased.

entries.zh: 其居相位，以進賢為己任，事總大綱，責成百司，人人樂為之用。
entries.en: In office as chancellor he made advancing worthy men his chief duty, kept to the broad outlines of policy, held every office accountable, and all were glad to serve under him.
entries.literal: When he held the chancellorship, he took advancing the worthy as his own task, kept affairs to the great outlines, held the hundred offices accountable, and everyone was glad to be put to use by him.

entries.zh: 三請致政，許之，月給錢粟傔隸，四時遣使存問。
entries.en: He asked three times to retire from government and was permitted to do so, receiving monthly stipends of money, grain, and attendants, with envoys sent in every season to inquire after his welfare.
entries.literal: Three times he requested to retire from government; permission was granted, and each month he was given money, grain, and attendants; in the four seasons envoys were sent to inquire after him.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 有《登瀛集》行於世。
entries.en: His collection Ascending to the Immortal Isles circulated widely.
entries.literal: His Ascending to the Immortal Isles Collection circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 論曰：庶成定法令，治民者不容高下其手。
entries.en: The appraisal says: By fixing the statutes, Shucheng ensured that those who governed the people could not manipulate penalties at will.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Shucheng fixed the statutes, so that those who governed the people could not raise or lower their hands at will.

entries.zh: 庶箴雖嘗表請廣姓氏，以秩典禮，其隨勢俯仰，則有愧於其子蒲魯矣。
entries.en: Although Shuzhen once memorialized to expand the clan registers and set ritual precedence, his readiness to bend with changing fortunes left him shamed before his son Pulu.
entries.literal: Although Shuzhen once memorialized requesting expansion of the surname registers to order ritual precedence, in bending with the times he had reason to feel ashamed before his son Pulu.

entries.zh: 楊皙為上寵遇，叠封王爵，而功業不少概見。
entries.en: Yang Xi enjoyed the emperor's favor and received repeated enfeoffments as prince, yet his substantive achievements are scarcely to be seen.
entries.literal: Yang Xi received the emperor's favor and was repeatedly enfeoffed with princely titles, yet his achievements are scarcely visible in outline.

entries.zh: 然得愛民治國之要，其楊佶哉！
entries.en: Yet in mastering the essentials of caring for the people and governing the realm—surely that was Yang Ji!
entries.literal: Yet in grasping the essentials of loving the people and governing the state—was it not Yang Ji!

entries.zh: 耶律庶成，字喜隱，小字陳六，季父房之後。
entries.en: Yelu Shucheng, whose style name was Xiyin and childhood name Chenliu, came from the Shufu branch of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Yelu Shucheng, style name Xiyin, childhood name Chenliu, was a descendant of the Shufu branch.

entries.zh: 父吳九，檢校太師。
entries.en: His father Wu Jiu held the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: His father Wu Jiu was an acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 庶成幼好學，書過目不忘。
entries.en: From childhood Shucheng loved learning and never forgot a book after a single reading.
entries.literal: Shucheng from youth loved learning; what he read he did not forget after one look.

entries.zh: 善遼、漢文字，於詩尤工。
entries.en: He was adept in both Khitan and Chinese writing and was especially accomplished in poetry.
entries.literal: He was skilled in Khitan and Han script; in poetry he was especially accomplished.

entries.zh: 重熙初，補牌印郎君，累遷樞密直學士。
entries.en: Early in the Chongxi reign he entered service as a Seal and Patent Attendant and rose through successive appointments to Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Chongxi era he was appointed Seal and Patent Attendant and was repeatedly promoted to Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 與蕭韓家奴各進《四時逸樂賦》，帝嗟賞。
entries.en: He and Xiao Hanjianu each submitted Rhapsodies on Leisure through the Four Seasons, which the emperor received with warm admiration.
entries.literal: He and Xiao Hanjianu each presented "Rhapsodies on Leisure through the Four Seasons," and the emperor sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 初，契丹醫人鮮知切脈審藥，上命庶成譯方脈書行之，自是人皆通習，雖諸部族亦知醫事。
entries.en: At first Khitan physicians seldom knew pulse diagnosis or how to judge medicines. The emperor ordered Shucheng to translate works on pulse lore and put them into practice, after which the art became widely known, and even the tribal peoples learned medical practice.
entries.literal: At first Khitan physicians rarely knew how to take the pulse and judge medicines. The emperor ordered Shucheng to translate books on pulse diagnosis and circulate them; from then on everyone learned them, and even the various tribes came to know medical matters.

entries.zh: 時入禁中，參決疑議。
entries.en: He was regularly summoned into the inner palace to help settle doubtful matters.
entries.literal: At the time he entered the inner palace to take part in resolving doubtful questions.

entries.zh: 偕林牙蕭韓家奴等撰《實錄》及《禮書》。
entries.en: Together with Grand Preceptor Xiao Hanjianu and others, he compiled the Veritable Records and the Book of Rites.
entries.literal: Together with Grand Preceptor Xiao Hanjianu and others he compiled the Veritable Records and the Book of Rites.

entries.zh: 與樞密副使蕭德修定法令，上詔庶成曰：「方今法令輕重不倫。
entries.en: Working with Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao De, he revised the statutes. The emperor addressed Shucheng: "At present the penalties in our statutes are inconsistent in severity.
entries.literal: With Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao De he revised the statutes. The emperor issued an edict to Shucheng saying: "At present the statutes' severity and leniency are not in proper order.

entries.zh: 法令者，為政所先，人命所系，不可不慎。
entries.en: Statutes come first in government and bind human lives; they must be handled with the utmost care.
entries.literal: Statutes are what government puts first and what human lives depend on; they cannot be treated without care.

entries.zh: 卿其審度輕重，從宜修定。」
entries.en: Weigh severity and leniency and revise them as you see fit."
entries.literal: You should examine severity and leniency and revise them as appropriate."

entries.zh: 庶成參酌古今，刊正訛謬，成書以進。
entries.en: Shucheng drew on past and present models, corrected errors, completed the work, and submitted it to the throne.
entries.literal: Shucheng weighed past and present, corrected errors, completed the book, and presented it.

entries.zh: 帝覽而善之。
entries.en: The emperor read it and expressed his approval.
entries.literal: The emperor reviewed it and approved it.

entries.zh: 庶成方進用，為妻胡篤所誣，以罪奪官，絀為「庶耶律」。
entries.en: Just as Shucheng was coming into high favor, his wife Hu Du slandered him; he was stripped of office for a crime and reduced in clan rank to the humiliating designation "Commoner Yelu."
entries.literal: Just as Shucheng was rising in favor, he was slandered by his wife Hu Du, stripped of office for a crime, and demoted in clan standing to "Commoner Yelu."

entries.zh: 使吐蕃凡十二年，清寧間始歸。
entries.en: He was posted to Tibet for twelve years and did not return until the Qingning reign.
entries.literal: He was sent to Tibet for twelve years in all and did not return until the Qingning era.

entries.zh: 帝知其誣，詔復本族，仍遷所奪官，卒。
entries.en: The emperor knew he had been wronged, ordered his clan status restored, reinstated the offices that had been stripped from him, and shortly afterward he died.
entries.literal: The emperor knew he had been slandered, issued an edict restoring him to his original clan, and also restored the offices that had been taken from him; then he died.

entries.zh: 庶箴，字陳甫，善屬文。
entries.en: Shuzhen, whose style name was Chenfu, was skilled at literary composition.
entries.literal: Shuzhen, style name Chenfu, was skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 重熙中，為本族將軍。
entries.en: During the Chongxi reign he served as general of his clan.
entries.literal: During the Chongxi era he served as general of his clan.

entries.zh: 咸雍元年，同知東京留守事，俄徙烏衍突厥部節度使。
entries.en: In the first year of Xianyong he became associate Eastern Capital regent and was soon transferred to military commissioner of the Wuyan Tujue tribe.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianyong he became associate Eastern Capital regent; before long he was transferred to military commissioner of the Wuyan Tujue tribe.

entries.zh: 九年，知薊州事。
entries.en: In the ninth year he took charge of Jizhou.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he administered Jizhou.

entries.zh: 明年，遷都林牙。
entries.en: The following year he was transferred to chief grand preceptor.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to Chief Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 上表乞廣本國姓氏曰：「我朝創業以來，法制修明；
entries.en: He memorialized requesting expansion of the national surnames, saying, "Since our dynasty's founding, institutions and laws have been well ordered;
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting expansion of the national surnames, saying: "Since our dynasty's founding, institutions and laws have been well ordered;

entries.zh: 惟姓氏止分為二，耶律與蕭而已。
entries.en: surnames are divided into only two, Yelu and Xiao.
entries.literal: surnames are divided into only two, Yelu and Xiao.

entries.zh: 始太祖制契丹大字，取諸部鄉里之名，續作一篇，著於卷末。
entries.en: At the outset Taizu devised the great Khitan script, taking names from the townships and villages of the various tribes, composed a further piece, and placed it at the end of the roll.
entries.literal: At the outset the Taizu devised the great Khitan script, taking names from the townships and villages of the various tribes; he composed a further piece and placed it at the end of the roll.

entries.zh: 臣請推廣之，使諸部各立姓氏，庶男女婚媾有合典禮。」
entries.en: I request that this be extended so each tribe may establish its own surname and men's and women's marriages may conform to ritual propriety."
entries.literal: I request that this be extended, so that each tribe may establish its own surname, and that men's and women's marriages may conform to ritual propriety."

entries.zh: 帝以舊制不可遽厘，不聽。
entries.en: The emperor held that the old system could not be abruptly changed and did not assent.
entries.literal: The emperor held that the old system could not be abruptly changed and did not assent.

entries.zh: 大康二年，出耶律乙辛為中京留守，庶箴與耶律孟簡表賀。
entries.en: In the second year of Dakang, Yelü Yixin was sent out as commissioner of the Central Capital; Shuzhen and Yelü Mengjian submitted a congratulatory memorial.
entries.literal: In the second year of Dakang, Yelü Yixin was sent out as commissioner of the Central Capital; Shuzhen together with Yelü Mengjian submitted a congratulatory memorial.

entries.zh: 頃之，乙辛復為樞密使，專權恣虐。
entries.en: Before long Yixin returned as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and wielded power arbitrarily with cruel abuse.
entries.literal: Before long Yixin returned as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and wielded power arbitrarily with cruel abuse.

entries.zh: 庶箴私見乙辛泣曰：「前抗表，非庶箴之願也。」
entries.en: Shuzhen privately visited Yixin and wept, saying, "My earlier memorial opposing him was not Shuzhen's true wish."
entries.literal: Shuzhen privately visited Yixin and wept, saying: "My earlier memorial opposing him was not Shuzhen's true wish."

entries.zh: 乙辛信其言，乃得自安。
entries.en: Yixin believed him and was thus able to feel secure.
entries.literal: Yixin believed his words and was thus able to feel secure.

entries.zh: 聞者鄙之。
entries.en: Those who heard of it despised him.
entries.literal: Those who heard of it despised him.

entries.zh: 八年，致仕，卒。
entries.en: In the eighth year he retired from office and died.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he retired from office and died.

entries.zh: 子蒲魯。
entries.en: His son was Pulu.
entries.literal: His son was Pulu.

entries.zh: 蒲魯，字乃展。
entries.en: Pulu, whose style name was Naizhan,
entries.literal: Pulu, style name Naizhan.

entries.zh: 幼聰悟好學，甫七歲，能誦契丹大字。
entries.en: was clever and studious from childhood; at only seven he could recite the great Khitan script.
entries.literal: From youth he was clever and loved learning; at only seven he could recite the great Khitan script.

entries.zh: 習漢文，未十年，博通經籍。
entries.en: He studied Chinese writing and within less than ten years had mastered the classical canon.
entries.literal: He studied Han writing, and in less than ten years he thoroughly mastered the classics.

entries.zh: 重熙中，舉進士第。
entries.en: During the Chongxi reign he passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: During the Chongxi era he passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 主文以國制無契丹試進士之條，聞於上，以庶箴擅令子就科目，鞭之二百。
entries.en: The chief examiner reported to the throne that national law contained no provision for Khitans to sit the jinshi examination. Shuzhen was judged to have presumptuously placed his son in the examination and was given two hundred strokes of the whip.
entries.literal: The chief examiner, because the national regulations had no provision for Khitan candidates in the jinshi examination, reported it to the emperor; Shuzhen was held to have presumptuously allowed his son to enter the examination category and was flogged two hundred strokes.

entries.zh: 尋命莆魯為牌印郎君。
entries.en: Soon afterward Pulu was appointed Seal and Patent Attendant.
entries.literal: Before long Pulu was appointed Seal and Patent Attendant.

entries.zh: 應詔賦詩，立成以進。
entries.en: When called upon to compose verse at imperial command, he finished a poem on the spot and presented it.
entries.literal: When summoned to compose poetry at imperial command, he finished it on the spot and presented it.

entries.zh: 帝嘉賞，顧左右曰：「文才如此，必不能武事。」
entries.en: The emperor was delighted and remarked to his attendants, "With literary talent like this, he surely cannot be skilled in arms."
entries.literal: The emperor praised him and, turning to those at his side, said: "With literary talent like this, he surely cannot handle military affairs."

entries.zh: 蒲魯奏曰：「臣自蒙義方，兼習騎射，在流輩中亦可周旋。」
entries.en: Pulu replied, "Your servant has been properly instructed from youth and has also trained in riding and archery; among my peers I can still hold my own."
entries.literal: Pulu memorialized: "Your servant from childhood has received proper instruction and has also practiced riding and archery; among my peers I can still hold my own."

entries.zh: 帝未之信。
entries.en: The emperor was not yet convinced.
entries.literal: The emperor did not yet believe him.

entries.zh: 會從獵，三矢中三兔，帝奇之，轉通進。
entries.en: Once on a hunt he brought down three hares with three arrows. The emperor was astonished and promoted him to Tongjin.
entries.literal: On one occasion when he accompanied a hunt, three arrows hit three hares; the emperor marveled at him and transferred him to Tongjin.

entries.zh: 是時，父庶箴嘗寄《戒諭詩》，蒲魯答以賦，眾稱其典雅。
entries.en: About that time his father Shuzhen sent him an admonitory poem, to which Pulu replied with a rhapsody that everyone praised for its refinement.
entries.literal: At that time his father Shuzhen had once sent him an "Admonitory Poem"; Pulu answered with a rhapsody, and everyone praised its elegance.

entries.zh: 寵遇漸隆。
entries.en: Imperial favor toward him steadily increased.
entries.literal: Favor toward him gradually rose.

entries.zh: 清寧初卒。
entries.en: He died early in the Qingning reign.
entries.literal: He died at the beginning of the Qingning era.

entries.zh: 楊皙，字昌時，安次人。
entries.en: Yang Xi, whose style name was Changshi, was a native of Anci.
entries.literal: Yang Xi, style name Changshi, was a man of Anci.

entries.zh: 幼通《五經》大義。
entries.en: From childhood he grasped the essential meaning of the Five Classics.
entries.literal: From youth he understood the great meaning of the Five Classics.

entries.zh: 聖宗聞其穎悟，詔試講，授秘書省校書郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Shengzong heard of his exceptional intelligence, he ordered a trial lecture and appointed him Collator of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Emperor Shengzong heard of his keen intelligence, ordered him tested in lecturing, and appointed him Collator of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 太平十一年，擢進士乙科，為著作佐郎。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of the Taiping era he passed the jinshi examination in the second class and was appointed Assistant Gentleman for Compilation.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Taiping he was selected in the second class of the jinshi examination and made Assistant Gentleman for Compilation.

entries.zh: 重熙十二年，累遷樞密都承旨，權度支使。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Chongxi he rose through successive appointments to Chief Secretariat Attendant of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Commissioner of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Chongxi he was repeatedly promoted to Chief Secretariat Attendant of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Commissioner of Revenue.

entries.zh: 登對稱旨，進樞密副使。
entries.en: His answers in audience pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: In audience his answers matched the emperor's intent, and he was advanced to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 歷長寧軍節度使，山西路轉運使，知興中府。
entries.en: He served as military governor of Changning Circuit, transport commissioner of the Shanxi Route, and prefect of Xingzhong.
entries.literal: He served as Military Governor of Changning Circuit, Transport Commissioner of the Shanxi Route, and Prefect of Xingzhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 清寧初，入知南院樞密使，與姚景行同總朝政。
entries.en: Early in Qingning he entered court service as Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs and, together with Yao Jingxing, directed the government.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning he entered the court as Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs and, together with Yao Jingxing, jointly oversaw court government.

entries.zh: 請行柴冊禮。
entries.en: He petitioned for the performance of the firewood-register enthronement rite.
entries.literal: He requested that the firewood-register rite be performed.

entries.zh: 封趙國公。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

entries.zh: 以足疾，復知興中府。
entries.en: Because of a foot ailment he returned to serve as prefect of Xingzhong.
entries.literal: Because of a foot ailment, he again became Prefect of Xingzhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 咸雍初，徙封齊，召賜同德功臣、尚書左僕射，兼中書令，拜樞密使，改封晉，給宰相、樞密使兩廳傔從，封趙王。
entries.en: Early in Xianyong his fief was transferred to Qi. Summoned to court, he received the title Meritorious Minister of Shared Virtue, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as Central Secretariat Director, and was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. His fief was then changed to Jin, he was granted the attendants allotted to both the chancellor's and the commissioner's offices, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xianyong his fief was changed to Qi; he was summoned and granted the title Meritorious Minister of Shared Virtue, made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Central Secretariat Director, appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, had his fief changed to Jin, was given attendants of both the chancellor's and the commissioner's offices, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 屢請歸政，益賜保節功臣，致仕。
entries.en: He repeatedly asked to retire from government, was further granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Preserves Integrity, and left office.
entries.literal: He repeatedly requested to return power, was further granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Preserves Integrity, and retired from office.

entries.zh: 大康五年，例改遼西郡王，薨。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Dakang his title was changed by precedent to Prince of Liaoxi Commandery, and he died.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dakang, by precedent his title was changed to Prince of Liaoxi Commandery, and he died.

entries.zh: 蕭塔剌葛，字陶哂，六院部人。
entries.en: Xiao Talage, styled Taoshen, was from the Six Yuan Division.
entries.literal: Xiao Talage, style name Taoshen, was a man of the Six Yuan Division.

entries.zh: 素剛直。
entries.en: By nature he was upright and unyielding.
entries.literal: By nature he was upright and firm.

entries.zh: 太祖時，坐叔祖臺哂謀殺於越釋魯，沒入弘義宮。
entries.en: Under Taizu he was implicated when his granduncle Taishan plotted to murder yuyue Shilu and was entered into the Hongyi Palace rolls.
entries.literal: In Taizu's time he was implicated because his granduncle Taishan plotted to murder yuyue Shilu and was confiscated into the Hongyi Palace division.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，以舅氏故，出其籍，補國舅別部敞史。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, because of his maternal kinship he was removed from the rolls and appointed chanshi of the imperial maternal uncle separate division.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, because of his maternal kinship his register was cleared and he was appointed chanshi of the imperial maternal uncle separate division.

entries.zh: 或言泰寧王察割有無君心。
entries.en: Some said Prince of Taining Chaguo harbored disloyal thoughts toward the throne.
entries.literal: Some said Prince of Taining Chaguo harbored thoughts of disloyalty to the ruler.

entries.zh: 塔剌葛曰：「彼縱忍行不義，人孰肯從！」
entries.en: Talage said, "Even if he could endure acting unjustly, who would follow him!"
entries.literal: Talage said, "Even if he could bear to act unjustly, who would follow him!"

entries.zh: 他日侍宴，酒酣，塔剌葛捉察割耳，強飲之曰：「上固知汝傲狠，然以國屬，曲加矜憫，使汝在左右，且度汝才何能為。
entries.en: On another banquet day, when the wine was deep, Talage seized Chaguo by the ear and forced him to drink, saying, "The emperor surely knows you are arrogant and fierce, yet because you are of the imperial clan he has bent to show compassion, kept you at his side, and judged what your talents could accomplish.
entries.literal: Another day at a feast, when the wine was deep, Talage seized Chaguo by the ear and forced him to drink, saying, "The emperor surely knows you are arrogant and fierce, yet because you are of the imperial clan he has bent to show compassion, kept you at his side, and measured what your talents could accomplish.

entries.zh: 若長惡不悛，徒自取赤族之禍！」
entries.en: If you persist in evil without reform, you will bring annihilation on your house for nothing!"
entries.literal: If you persist in evil without reform, you will bring extermination on your house for nothing!"

entries.zh: 察割不能答，強笑曰：「何戲之虐也！」
entries.en: Chaguo could not answer and forced a laugh, saying, "Why such cruel jesting!"
entries.literal: Chaguo could not answer and forced a laugh, saying, "Why such cruel jesting!"

entries.zh: 天祿末，塔剌葛為北府宰相，及察割作亂，塔剌葛醉詈曰：「吾悔不殺此逆賊！」
entries.en: At the end of the Tianlu era Talage was Northern Court chancellor; when Chaguo rebelled, Talage drunkenly cursed, saying, "I regret I did not kill this traitor!"
entries.literal: At the end of the Tianlu era Talage was Northern Court chancellor; when Chaguo rose in rebellion, Talage drunkenly cursed, saying, "I regret I did not kill this traitor!"

entries.zh: 尋為察割所害。
entries.en: Soon afterward Chaguo killed him.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was killed by Chaguo.

entries.zh: 耶律敵祿，字陽隱，孟父楚國王之後。
entries.en: Yelü Dilu, styled Yangyin, was a descendant of the Mengfu Prince of Chu.
entries.literal: Yelü Dilu, style name Yangyin, was a descendant of the Mengfu Prince of Chu.

entries.zh: 性質直，多膂力。
entries.en: Plain and upright by nature, he possessed great physical strength.
entries.literal: By nature he was plain and upright, with great physical strength.

entries.zh: 察割作亂，敵祿聞之，入見壽安王，慷慨言曰：「願得精兵數百，破賊黨。」
entries.en: When Chaguo rebelled, Dilu heard the news, went to see Prince Shou'an, and declared passionately, "Give me several hundred crack troops and I will smash the rebel band."
entries.literal: When Chaguo rebelled, Dilu heard of it, went in to see Prince Shou'an, and declared with passion, "I wish to have several hundred crack troops to smash the rebel band."

entries.zh: 王嘉其忠。
entries.en: The prince praised his loyalty.
entries.literal: The prince praised his loyalty.

entries.zh: 穆宗即位，為北院宣徽使。
entries.en: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, he was appointed Northern Court palace commissioner.
entries.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, he was made Northern Court palace commissioner.

entries.zh: 上以飛狐道狹，詔敵祿廣之。
entries.en: Because the Feihu route was narrow, the emperor ordered Dilu to widen it.
entries.literal: Because the Feihu route was narrow, the emperor ordered Dilu to widen it.

entries.zh: 明年，將兵援河東，至太原，與漢王會於高平，擊周軍，敗之，仍降其眾。
entries.en: The next year he led troops to relieve Hedong, reached Taiyuan, joined the King of Han at Gaoping, attacked the Zhou army, defeated it, and also won the surrender of its troops.
entries.literal: The next year he led troops to aid Hedong, reached Taiyuan, met with the King of Han at Gaoping, attacked the Zhou army, defeated it, and also induced its troops to surrender.

entries.zh: 忻、代二州叛，將兵討之。
entries.en: When Xin and Dai prefectures rebelled, he led troops to suppress them.
entries.literal: When Xin and Dai prefectures rebelled, he led troops to suppress them.

entries.zh: 會耶律撻烈至，敗周師於忻口。
entries.en: When Yelü Talie arrived, the Zhou army was defeated at Xinkou.
entries.literal: When Yelü Talie arrived, the Zhou forces were defeated at Xinkou.

entries.zh: 師還，卒。
entries.en: When the army returned, he died.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he died.

entries.zh: 蕭阿剌耶律義先
entries.en: Xiao Ala; Yelu Yixian
entries.literal: Xiao Ala; Yelu Yixian

entries.en: (Xinxian)〉
entries.literal: (Xinxian)〉

entries.zh: 蕭陶隗蕭塔剌葛耶律敵祿
entries.en: Xiao Taowei; Xiao Talage; Yelu Dilu
entries.literal: Xiao Taowei; Xiao Talage; Yelu Dilu

entries.zh: 耶律韓八，字嘲隱，倜儻有大志，北院詳穩古之五世孫。
entries.en: Yelu Hanba, style name Chaoyin, was dashing and ambitious, a fifth-generation descendant of Gu, Details Steady of the Northern Court.
entries.literal: Yelu Hanba, whose style name was Chaoyin, was unconventionally talented and had great ambitions; he was the fifth-generation descendant of Gu, Details Steady of the Northern Court.

entries.zh: 太平中，遊京師，寓行宮側，惟囊衣匹馬而已。
entries.en: During the Taiping reign, he came to the capital and lodged by the traveling palace with nothing but a bag of clothes and one horse.
entries.literal: During the Taiping era, he traveled to the capital, lodged beside the traveling palace, and had only a bag of clothes and a single horse.

entries.zh: 帝微服出獵，見而問之曰：「汝為何人？」
entries.en: The emperor went out hunting in disguise, saw him, and asked, "Who are you?"
entries.literal: The emperor went hunting in plain clothes, saw him, and asked: "Who are you?"

entries.zh: 韓八初不識，漫應曰：「我北院部人韓八，來覓官耳。」
entries.en: Hanba did not recognize him at first and answered offhandedly, "I am Hanba of the Northern Court tribes, here to seek an appointment."
entries.literal: Hanba did not recognize him at first and answered casually: "I am Hanba of the Northern Court tribes, here to seek an office."

entries.zh: 帝與語，知有長才，陰識之。
entries.en: After speaking with him, the emperor perceived his great ability and marked him in secret.
entries.literal: After conversing with him, the emperor recognized his great talent and took note of him privately.

entries.zh: 會北院奏南京疑獄久不決，帝召韓八馳驛審錄，舉朝皆驚。
entries.en: When the Northern Court reported that a doubtful case at Nanjing had long remained unsettled, the emperor summoned Hanba to ride post-haste and examine the records, and the whole court was astonished.
entries.literal: When the Northern Court reported that a doubtful case at Nanjing had long gone unresolved, the emperor summoned Hanba to ride post-haste and review the records; the whole court was astonished.

entries.zh: 韓八量情處理，人無冤者。
entries.en: Hanba judged each case on its merits, and no one was wrongfully convicted.
entries.literal: Hanba handled matters according to circumstances; no one suffered wrongful conviction.

entries.zh: 上嘉之。
entries.en: The emperor commended him.
entries.literal: The emperor praised him.

entries.zh: 籍群牧馬，闕其二，同事者考尋不已，韓八略不加詰，即先馳奏，帝益信任。
entries.en: When the collective herd horses were inventoried, two were missing; his colleagues kept investigating without end, but Hanba barely pressed the matter and first sent an urgent report to court, and the emperor trusted him all the more.
entries.literal: When counting the collective herd horses, two were missing; his colleagues kept investigating without cease, but Hanba scarcely questioned further and first sent a hurried report; the emperor trusted him all the more.

entries.zh: 景福元年，為左夷離畢，徙北面林牙，眷遇優異。
entries.en: In the first year of the Jingfu era he was made Left Yilibi, transferred to Northern Forest Ya, and received exceptionally generous favor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jingfu he became Left Yilibi, was transferred to Northern Forest Ya, and received exceptionally favored treatment.

entries.zh: 重熙六年，改北院大王，政務寬仁，復為左夷離畢。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Chongxi he was made Great King of the Northern Court; his administration was lenient and humane, and he again became Left Yilibi.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Chongxi he was changed to Great King of the Northern Court; his governance was lenient and humane, and he again became Left Yilibi.

entries.zh: 十二年，再為北院大王。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he again became Great King of the Northern Court.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he again became Great King of the Northern Court.

entries.zh: 入朝，帝從容謂曰：「卿守邊任重，當實府庫、振貧乏以報朕。」
entries.en: When he came to court, the emperor said at ease, "You bear heavy responsibility on the frontier; you should fill the treasuries and relieve the poor to repay Us."
entries.literal: On entering court, the emperor said at ease: "You bear heavy responsibility guarding the frontier; you should fill the treasuries and relieve the impoverished to repay Us."

entries.zh: 既受詔，愈竭忠謹，知無不言，便益為多。
entries.en: Once he received the edict, he became ever more utterly loyal and careful, spoke freely of whatever he knew, and his beneficial counsel was abundant.
entries.literal: Once he received the edict, he became ever more utterly loyal and cautious, speaking of whatever he knew without reserve, and his perquisites grew numerous.

entries.zh: 卒，年五十五。
entries.en: He died at the age of fifty-five.
entries.literal: He died at age fifty-five.

entries.zh: 上聞，悼惜。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of it, he mourned and grieved.
entries.literal: On hearing of it, the emperor mourned and regretted his loss.

entries.zh: 死之日，篋無舊蓄，椸無新衣，遣使吊祭，給葬具。
entries.en: On the day of his death his chest held no old stores and his wardrobe no new clothes; the emperor sent envoys to mourn him and provide funeral goods.
entries.literal: On the day of his death his chest held no old stores and his wardrobe no new clothes; the emperor sent envoys to mourn and provide funeral goods.

entries.zh: 耶律玦，字吾展，遙輦鮮質可汗之後。
entries.en: Yelu Jue, style name Wuzhan, was a descendant of Khan Xianzhi of the Yaolian.
entries.literal: Yelu Jue, whose style name was Wuzhan, was a descendant of Khan Xianzhi of the Yaolian.

entries.zh: 重熙初，召修國史，補符寶郎，累遷知北院副部署事。
entries.en: Early in Chongxi he was summoned to compile the national history, appointed credential bearer gentleman, and was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner of the northern court deputy office.
entries.literal: Early in Chongxi he was summoned to compile the national history, appointed Credential Bearer Gentleman, and repeatedly promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Northern Court Deputy Office.

entries.zh: 入見太后，後顧左右曰：「先皇謂玦必為偉人，果然。」
entries.en: On audience with the empress dowager, she looked back at those beside her and said, "The former emperor said Jue would surely prove a great man — and so it has come to pass."
entries.literal: On audience with the empress dowager, she looked back at those beside her and said: "The former emperor said Jue would surely be a great man — and so it proves."

entries.zh: 除樞密副使，出為西南面招討都監，歷同簽南京留守事、南面林牙。
entries.en: He was made vice privy commissioner, sent out as southwest pacification superintendent, and successively served as co-signatory of the Nanjing military governorship and southern forest ya.
entries.literal: He was made Vice Privy Commissioner, sent out as Southwest Pacification Superintendent, and successively served as Co-signatory of Nanjing Military Governorship and Southern Forest Ya.

entries.zh: 皇弟秦國王為遼興軍節度使，以玦同知使事，多所匡正。
entries.en: When the emperor's younger brother the Prince of Qin was military commissioner of Liaoxing Army, Jue was made co-administrator of the commission and corrected many matters.
entries.literal: When the emperor's younger brother the Prince of Qin was Military Commissioner of Liaoxing Army, Jue was made co-administrator and corrected many matters.

entries.zh: 十年，復為樞密副使。
entries.en: In the tenth year he again became vice privy commissioner.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he again became Vice Privy Commissioner.

entries.zh: 咸雍初，兼北院副部署。
entries.en: Early in Xianyong he concurrently held northern court vice commissioner.
entries.literal: Early in Xianyong he concurrently held Northern Court Vice Commissioner.

entries.zh: 及秦國王為西京留守，請玦為佐，從之。
entries.en: When the Prince of Qin became military governor of the Western Capital, he requested Jue as his assistant, and the emperor assented.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Qin became Military Governor of the Western Capital, he requested Jue as assistant; the emperor assented.

entries.zh: 歲中獄空者三，召為孟父房敞穩。
entries.en: Within the year the prisons were empty three times; he was summoned as Details Steady of the Mengfu House.
entries.literal: Within the year the prisons were empty three times; he was summoned as Details Steady of the Mengfu House.

entries.zh: 玦不喜貨殖，帝知其貧，賜宮戶十。
