entries.en: Jue did not care for profit-seeking; the emperor knew he was poor and bestowed ten palace households on him.
entries.literal: Jue did not care for profit-seeking; the emperor knew he was poor and bestowed ten palace households.

entries.zh: 嘗謂宰相曰：「契丹忠正無如玦者，漢人則劉伸而已。
entries.en: He once told the chancellor, "Among the Khitan none is so loyal and upright as Jue; among the Han, only Liu Shen.
entries.literal: He once told the chancellor: "Among Khitan none is so loyal and upright as Jue; among Han only Liu Shen.

entries.zh: 然熟察之，玦優於伸。」
entries.en: Yet on close examination, Jue surpasses Shen."
entries.literal: Yet on close examination, Jue surpasses Shen."

entries.zh: 先是，西北諸部久不能平，上遣玦問狀，執弛慢者痛繩之。
entries.en: Earlier the northwestern tribes had long gone unpacified; the emperor sent Jue to investigate, seized those who were negligent, and punished them severely.
entries.literal: Earlier the northwestern tribes had long not been pacified; the emperor sent Jue to investigate, seized the negligent, and sternly punished them.

entries.zh: 以酒疾卒。
entries.en: He died of an illness brought on by wine.
entries.literal: He died of wine sickness.

entries.zh: 蕭朮哲，字石魯隱，孝穆弟高九之子。
entries.en: Xiao Paizhe, style name Shiluyin, was the son of Gao Jiu, younger brother of Xiaomu.
entries.literal: Xiao Paizhe, whose style name was Shiluyin, was son of Gao Jiu, younger brother of Xiaomu.

entries.zh: 以戚屬加監門衛上將軍。
entries.en: By virtue of imperial kinship he was made general of the Gate Guards.
entries.literal: By imperial kinship he was made General of the Gate Guards.

entries.zh: 重熙十三年，將衛兵討李元昊有功，遷興聖宮使。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Chongxi he led the guard troops against Li Yuanhao with merit and was promoted to director of the Xingsheng Palace.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chongxi he led guard troops against Li Yuanhao with merit and was promoted to Director of the Xingsheng Palace.

entries.zh: 蒲奴裏部長陶得裏叛，朮哲為統軍都監，從都統耶律義先擊之，擒陶得裏。
entries.en: When the Punnuli chieftain Taodeli rebelled, Paizhe served as army superintendent and followed the commander-in-chief Yelu Yixian in the attack, capturing Taodeli.
entries.literal: When the Punnuli chieftain Taodeli rebelled, Paizhe served as Army Superintendent and followed Commander-in-chief Yelu Yixian to attack, capturing Taodeli.

entries.zh: 朮哲與義先不協，誣義先罪，免官。
entries.en: Paizhe did not get along with Yixian, falsely accused him of a crime, and had him removed from office.
entries.literal: Paizhe did not get along with Yixian, falsely accused him of crime, and had him removed from office.

entries.zh: 稍遷西南面招討都監，坐事下獄，以太后言，杖而釋之。
entries.en: He was gradually promoted to southwest pacification superintendent; for an offense he was imprisoned, but at the empress dowager's word he was beaten with the staff and released.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Southwest Pacification Superintendent; for an offense he was imprisoned, but at the empress dowager's word he was beaten with the staff and released.

entries.zh: 清寧初，為國舅詳穩、西北路招討使，私取官粟三百斛，及代，留畜產，令主者鬻之以償。
entries.en: Early in Qingning he was imperial uncle Details Steady and northwest pacification commissioner; he privately took three hundred hu of official grain, and on leaving office left livestock for the custodian to sell in repayment.
entries.literal: Early in Qingning he was Imperial Uncle Details Steady and Northwest Pacification Commissioner; he privately took three hundred hu of official grain, and on leaving office left livestock for the custodian to sell in repayment.

entries.zh: 後族弟胡睹到部發其事，帝怒，決以大杖，免官。
entries.en: Later his clansman cousin Hudu came to the post and exposed the matter; the emperor was enraged, sentenced him to the great staff, and removed him from office.
entries.literal: Later his clansman cousin Hudu came to the post and exposed the matter; the emperor was angry, sentenced him to the great staff, and removed him from office.

entries.zh: 尋起為昭德軍節度使，徵為北院宣徽使。
entries.en: Soon he was reappointed military commissioner of Zhaode Army and summoned as northern court palace commissioner.
entries.literal: Soon he was reappointed Military Commissioner of Zhaode Army and summoned as Northern Court Palace Commissioner.

entries.zh: 九年，上以朮哲先為招討，威行諸部，復為西北路招討使。
entries.en: In the ninth year, because Paizhe had earlier served as pacification commissioner and his authority extended through the tribes, he was again made northwest pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, because Paizhe had earlier served as pacification commissioner and his authority extended through the tribes, he was again made Northwest Pacification Commissioner.

entries.zh: 訓士卒，增器械，省追呼，嚴號令。
entries.en: He trained the soldiers, increased weapons, reduced forced levies, and enforced strict orders.
entries.literal: He trained soldiers, increased weapons, reduced forced levies, and enforced strict orders.

entries.zh: 人不敢犯，邊境晏然。
entries.en: No one dared offend him, and the border was tranquil.
entries.literal: No one dared offend him; the border was tranquil.

entries.zh: 十年，入朝，封柳城郡王。
entries.en: In the tenth year he came to court and was enfeoffed as prince of Liucheng commandery.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he entered court and was enfeoffed Prince of Liucheng commandery.

entries.zh: 咸雍二年，拜北府宰相，為北院樞密使耶律乙辛所忌，誣朮哲與護衛蕭忽古等謀害乙辛。
entries.en: In the second year of Xianyong he was appointed northern chancellery chancellor; Yelu Yixin, northern court privy commissioner, envied him and accused Paizhe of plotting with the guardsman Xiao Hugu and others to harm Yixin.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianyong he was appointed Northern Chancellery Chancellor; Yelu Yixin, Northern Court Privy Commissioner, envied him and accused Paizhe of plotting with guardsman Xiao Hugu to harm Yixin.

entries.zh: 詔獄無狀，罷相，出鎮順義軍。
entries.en: An imperial investigation found no substance to the charge; he was dismissed as chancellor and sent out to govern Shunyi Army.
entries.literal: Imperial investigation found no substance; he was dismissed as chancellor and sent out to govern Shunyi Army.

entries.zh: 卒，追王晉、宋、梁三國。
entries.en: On his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as king of Jin, Song, and Liang — the three states.
entries.literal: On death he was posthumously enfeoffed as king of Jin, Song, and Liang — the three states.

entries.zh: 侄藥師奴。
entries.en: His nephew was Yaoshinu.
entries.literal: Nephew Yaoshinu.

entries.zh: 藥師奴，幼穎悟，謹禮法，補祗候郎君。
entries.en: Yaoshinu was clever from childhood, careful in ritual and law, and was appointed attendant gentleman.
entries.literal: Yaoshinu was clever from youth, careful in ritual and law, and appointed Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 大康中，為興聖宮使，累遷同知殿前點檢司事。
entries.en: During the Dakang era he was director of the Xingsheng Palace and was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Palace Front Inspection Office.
entries.literal: During Dakang he was Director of Xingsheng Palace and repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Front Inspection Office.

entries.zh: 上嘉其宿衛嚴肅，遷右夷離畢。
entries.en: The emperor commended his stern palace guard service and promoted him to Right Yilibi.
entries.literal: The emperor commended his stern palace guard service and promoted him to Right Yilibi.

entries.zh: 夏王李乾順為宋所攻，求解，帝命藥師奴持節使宋，請罷兵通好，宋從之。
entries.en: When the Xia king Li Qianshun was attacked by Song and sought relief, the emperor ordered Yaoshinu to go as envoy to Song bearing credentials, asking that hostilities cease and friendly relations be restored; Song agreed.
entries.literal: When Xia King Li Qianshun was attacked by Song and sought relief, the emperor ordered Yaoshinu to bear credentials as envoy to Song, asking cessation of hostilities and renewed friendship; Song agreed.

entries.zh: 拜南面林牙，改漢人行宮副部署。
entries.en: He was appointed southern forest ya and transferred to deputy commissioner of the Han traveling palace.
entries.literal: He was appointed Southern Forest Ya and transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Han traveling palace.

entries.zh: 乾統初，出為安東軍節度使，卒。
entries.en: Early in Qiantong he went out as military commissioner of Andong Army and died.
entries.literal: Early in Qiantong he went out as Military Commissioner of Andong Army and died.

entries.zh: 耶律韓八 耶律唐古 蕭朮哲
entries.en: Yelu Hanba, Yelu Tanggu, and Xiao Paizhe
entries.literal: Yelu Hanba, Yelu Tanggu, Xiao Paizhe

entries.zh: 〈（藥師奴）〉
entries.en: (Yaoshinu)
entries.literal: (Yaoshinu)

entries.zh: 耶律玦 耶律仆里篤
entries.en: Yelu Jue and Yelu Pulidu
entries.literal: Yelu Jue, Yelu Pulidu

entries.zh: 耶律何魯掃古，字烏古鄰，孟父房之後。
entries.en: Yelu Helusaogu, whose courtesy name was Wugulin, was a descendant of the Mengfu branch of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Yelu Helusaogu, courtesy name Wugulin, was a descendant of the Mengfu house.

entries.zh: 重熙末，補祗候郎君。
entries.en: Late in the Chongxi era he was appointed an attendant gentleman.
entries.literal: At the end of Chongxi, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 清寧初，加安州團練使。
entries.en: Early in Qingning he was made training commissioner of An Prefecture.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, he was made Training Commissioner of An Prefecture.

entries.zh: 大康中，歷懷德軍節度使、奚六部禿裏太尉。
entries.en: During Dakang he served in turn as military commissioner of the Huaide army and as grand commandant tuli of the Six Xi Tribes.
entries.literal: During Dakang, he successively held the posts of Military Commissioner of the Huaide Army and Grand Commandant Tuli of the Six Xi Tribes.

entries.zh: 詔與樞密官措畫東北邊事，改左護衛太保。
entries.en: He was ordered to work with privy council officials on northeastern frontier strategy and was made senior commissioner of the left guard.
entries.literal: He was ordered with privy council officials to plan northeastern frontier affairs and was made Senior Guard Commissioner of the Left.

entries.zh: 侍上，言多率易，察無他腸，以故上優貸之。
entries.en: In the emperor's presence he spoke bluntly and without ceremony; inquiry showed no hidden designs, and for that reason the throne treated him with indulgence.
entries.literal: In attendance on the emperor his speech was often blunt and unguarded; investigation showed no ulterior motives, and for this reason the emperor treated him leniently.

entries.zh: 大安八年，知西北路招討使事。
entries.en: In Da'an 8 he took charge of northwestern route frontier campaigns.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Da'an, he was made commander of Northwestern Route campaigns.

entries.zh: 時邊部耶睹刮等來侵，何魯掃古誘北阻卜酋豪磨古斯攻之，俘獲甚眾，以功加左僕射。
entries.en: When the frontier tribes led by Yeduogua raided the border, Helusaogu induced the Northern Zubu chieftain Mogusi to strike them, took a great haul of captives, and was promoted to left vice director for his service.
entries.literal: At that time the frontier tribes Yeduogua and others invaded; Helusaogu induced the Northern Zubu chieftain Mogusi to attack them, taking many captives, and for his merit was made Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 復討耶睹刮等，誤擊磨古斯，北阻卜由是叛命。
entries.en: On a renewed campaign against Yeduogua and his allies he mistakenly attacked Mogusi, and the Northern Zubu thereupon rebelled.
entries.literal: Campaigning again against Yeduogua and others, he mistakenly struck Mogusi, and the Northern Zubu therefore rebelled.

entries.zh: 遣都監張九討之，不克，二室韋與六院部、特滿群牧、宮分等軍俱陷於敵。
entries.en: The overseer Zhang Jiu was sent to suppress them but failed; the two Shiwei divisions, together with the Six Yuan Division, the Temun herd office, the palace garrison troops, and other units, were all lost to the enemy.
entries.literal: Commissioner Zhang Jiu was dispatched to subdue them but failed; the two Shiwei divisions together with the Six Yuan Divisions, Temun Herd Office, Garrison Division, and other forces all fell to the enemy.

entries.zh: 何魯掃古不以實聞，坐是削官，決以大杖。
entries.en: Helusaogu failed to report what had really happened; for that his offices were stripped and he was sentenced to a heavy beating.
entries.literal: Helusaogu did not report the truth; for this his office was stripped and he was sentenced to heavy beating.

entries.zh: 壽隆間，累遷惕隱，兼侍中，賜保節功臣。
entries.en: During Shoulong he rose through several posts to tiyin and vice director, and was granted the title of meritorious minister who preserves integrity.
entries.literal: During Shoulong he was repeatedly promoted to Tiyin, concurrently Vice Director, and granted the title Meritorious Minister who Preserves Integrity.

entries.zh: 道宗崩，與宰相耶律儼總山陵事。
entries.en: When Emperor Daozong died, he and the chancellor Yelu Yi jointly directed the imperial tomb works.
entries.literal: When Daozong died, he together with Chancellor Yelu Yi oversaw the imperial tomb.

entries.zh: 乾統中，致仕，卒。
entries.en: Under Qiantong he retired from office and died.
entries.literal: During Qiantong he retired and died.

entries.zh: 耶律化哥耶律斡臘耶律速撒蕭阿魯帶耶律那也耶律何魯掃古耶律世良
entries.en: Yelu Huage, Yelu Wola, Yelu Susa, Xiao Aludai, Yelu Naye, Yelu Helusaogu, and Yelu Shiliang.
entries.literal: Yelu Huage, Yelu Wola, Yelu Susa, Xiao Aludai, Yelu Naye, Yelu Helusaogu, Yelu Shiliang.

entries.zh: 耶律弘古，字胡篤堇，樞密使化哥之弟。
entries.en: Yelu Honggu, whose style name was Hudujin, was the younger brother of Huage, Commissioner of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: Yelu Honggu, style name Hudujin, was the younger brother of the Commissioner of Military Affairs Huage.

entries.zh: 統和間，累遷順義軍節度使，入為北面林牙。
entries.en: During the Tonghe reign, he rose through successive appointments to Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army and then entered the capital as Northern Chancellor Linya.
entries.literal: During the Tonghe era, he was repeatedly promoted to Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army, then entered court as Northern Chancellor Linya.

entries.zh: 太平元年，加同政事門下平章事，出為彰國軍節度使，兼山北道兵馬都部署，徙武定軍節度使。
entries.en: In the first year of Taiping, he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Secretariat, then sent out as Military Commissioner of the Zhangguo Army with concurrent command of all armies and horses on the Shanbei Circuit, and later transferred to Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiping, he was made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat, sent out as Military Commissioner of the Zhangguo Army, concurrently Grand Commander of armies and horses of the Shanbei Circuit, then transferred to Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.

entries.zh: 六年，拜惕隱。
entries.en: In the sixth year, he was appointed Texun.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Texun.

entries.zh: 討阻卜有功。
entries.en: He distinguished himself in campaigns against the Zubu.
entries.literal: He had merit in campaigning against the Zubu.

entries.zh: 聖宗嘗刺臂血與弘古盟為友，禮遇尤異，拜南府宰相，改上京留守。
entries.en: Emperor Shengzong once drew blood from his own arm to seal a bond of friendship with Honggu and treated him with exceptional honor. Honggu was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office, then reassigned as Garrison Commander of the Supreme Capital.
entries.literal: Emperor Shengzong once pricked his arm and drew blood to swear friendship with Honggu; his courtesy toward him was especially extraordinary. Honggu was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office, then changed to Garrison Commander of the Supreme Capital.

entries.zh: 重熙六年，遷南院大王，御制誥辭以寵之。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Chongxi, he was made Great King of the Southern Court, and the emperor personally composed an edict of appointment to show his favor.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Chongxi, he was transferred to Great King of the Southern Court; the emperor personally composed an edict of appointment to honor him.

entries.zh: 十二年，加於越。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, he was granted the exalted title Yuyue.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, he was given the title Yuyue.

entries.zh: 帝閔其勞，復授武定軍節度使，卒。
entries.en: The emperor, moved by his long service, again appointed him Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army, after which he died.
entries.literal: The emperor pitied his labors, again appointed him Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army, and he died.

entries.zh: 訃聞，上哭曰：「惜哉善人！」
entries.en: When word of his death arrived, the emperor wept and said, "What a loss — such a good man!"
entries.literal: When the death report arrived, the emperor wept and said: "Alas, what a good man!"

entries.zh: 喪至，親臨奠焉。
entries.en: When the coffin arrived, he went in person to offer libations.
entries.literal: When the coffin arrived, he went in person to offer libations.

entries.zh: 耶律陳家奴，字綿辛，懿祖弟葛剌之八世孫。
entries.en: Yelu Chenjianu, whose style name was Mianxin, was an eighth-generation descendant of Gelü, younger brother of Emperor Yizu.
entries.literal: Yelu Chenjianu, style name Mianxin, was an eighth-generation descendant of Gelü, younger brother of Emperor Yizu.

entries.zh: 重熙中，補牌印郎君。
entries.en: During the Chongxi reign, he was appointed Langjun of the Seals.
entries.literal: During Chongxi, he was appointed Langjun of the Seals.

entries.zh: 坐直日不至，降本班。
entries.en: For failing to appear on his assigned duty day, he was demoted to the basic roster.
entries.literal: Because on his duty day he failed to appear, he was demoted to the basic roster.

entries.zh: 會帝獵，陳家奴逐鹿圍內，鞭之二百。
entries.en: Once when the emperor was hunting, Chenjianu chased a deer inside the hunting enclosure and was flogged two hundred strokes.
entries.literal: When the emperor was hunting, Chenjianu chased a deer inside the enclosure and was flogged two hundred strokes.

entries.zh: 時耶律仁先薦陳家奴健捷比海東青鶻，授禦盞郎君。
entries.en: At that time Yelu Renxian recommended Chenjianu, praising his vigor and agility as rivaling the eastern-sea green falcon, and he was appointed Langjun of the Imperial Cup.
entries.literal: At that time Yelu Renxian recommended Chenjianu, saying his vigor and agility rivaled the eastern sea green falcon, and he was appointed Langjun of the Imperial Cup.

entries.zh: 歷鷹坊、尚廄、四方館副使，改徒魯古皮室詳穩。
entries.en: He served successively as Vice Commissioner of the Falconry Office, the Imperial Stables, and the Four Directions Bureau, then was made Xiangwen of the Tulugu Pishi Detachment.
entries.literal: He served as Vice Commissioner of the Falconry Office, the Imperial Stables, and the Four Directions Bureau, then was changed to Xiangwen of the Tulugu Pishi Detachment.

entries.zh: 會太后生辰，進詩獻馴鹿，太后嘉獎，賜珠二琲，雜彩二百段。
entries.en: On the empress dowager's birthday, he presented a poem and offered a tame deer. The empress dowager commended him and bestowed two strings of pearls and two hundred lengths of assorted silks.
entries.literal: When the empress dowager's birthday came, he presented a poem and offered a tame deer; the empress dowager commended him and bestowed two strings of pearls and two hundred lengths of assorted silks.

entries.zh: 兄撒缽卒，陳家奴聞訃，不告而去。
entries.en: When his elder brother Sabo died, Chenjianu learned of it and left his post without permission.
entries.literal: When his elder brother Sabo died, Chenjianu heard the death report and left without informing anyone.

entries.zh: 帝怒，鞭之。
entries.en: The emperor was furious and had him flogged.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry and flogged him.

entries.zh: 清寧初，累遷右夷離畢。
entries.en: Early in the Qingning reign, he rose through successive promotions to Right Yilibi.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, he was repeatedly promoted to Right Yilibi.

entries.zh: 適帝與燕國王射鹿俱中，王時年九歲，帝悅，陳家奴應制進詩。
entries.en: Once when the emperor and the Prince of Yan both struck the deer in a hunt — the prince was only nine — the emperor was delighted, and Chenjianu composed a poem on imperial command.
entries.literal: Just then the emperor and the Prince of Yan both hit the deer in a shooting match; the prince was nine years old. The emperor was pleased, and Chenjianu composed a poem on imperial command.

entries.zh: 帝喜，解衣以賜。
entries.en: The emperor was pleased and removed his own garment to bestow on him.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and removed his own garment to bestow it on him.

entries.zh: 後皇太子廢，帝疑陳家奴黨附，罷之。
entries.en: Later, when the crown prince was deposed, the emperor suspected Chenjianu of siding with the deposed heir and dismissed him from office.
entries.literal: Later, when the crown prince was deposed, the emperor suspected Chenjianu of factional attachment and dismissed him.

entries.zh: 時西北諸部寇邊，以陳家奴為烏古部節度使行軍都監，賜甲一屬、馬二匹，討諸部，擒其酋送於朝。
entries.en: When the northwestern tribes raided the frontier, Chenjianu was appointed Military Commissioner of the Wugu Division with overall command of the field army, given a suit of armor and two horses, and sent to campaign against them. He captured their chieftain and sent him to court.
entries.literal: At that time the tribes of the northwest raided the border; Chenjianu was made Military Commissioner of the Wugu Division and Grand Overseer of the campaign army, given one suit of armor and two horses, and sent to campaign against the tribes; he captured their chieftain and sent him to court.

entries.zh: 偵候者見馬蹤，意寇至，陳家奴遣報元帥，耶律愛奴視之曰：「此野馬也！」
entries.en: Scouts spotted horse tracks and thought the enemy had arrived. Chenjianu reported to the commander, but Yelu Ainu inspected the tracks and said, "These are wild horses!"
entries.literal: Scouts saw horse tracks and thought the enemy had arrived; Chenjianu sent word to the commander. Yelu Ainu looked and said: "These are wild horses!"

entries.zh: 將出獵，賊至，愛奴戰歿。
entries.en: He was about to go out hunting when the raiders struck; Ainu fell in battle.
entries.literal: He was about to go out hunting when the bandits arrived; Ainu died in battle.

entries.zh: 有司詰按，陳家奴不伏，詔釋之。
entries.en: The authorities investigated and pressed charges, but Chenjianu would not confess. An edict ordered his release.
entries.literal: The authorities investigated and pressed charges; Chenjianu would not confess, and an edict released him.

entries.zh: 由是感激，每事竭力。
entries.en: Deeply moved by this, he thereafter exerted himself to the utmost in every task.
entries.literal: From this he was deeply moved and in every matter exerted himself to the utmost.

entries.zh: 後諸部復來侵，陳家奴率兵三往，皆克，邊境遂寧。
entries.en: When the tribes invaded again, Chenjianu led three campaigns against them, winning each time, and the frontier was restored to peace.
entries.literal: Later the tribes again came to invade; Chenjianu led troops on three expeditions, all victorious, and the borderlands were thereafter tranquil.

entries.zh: 以老告歸，不從。
entries.en: He asked to retire on grounds of age, but the request was denied.
entries.literal: He pleaded to retire on grounds of age, but this was not granted.

entries.zh: 道宗崩，為山陵使，致仕。
entries.en: When Emperor Daozong died, he served as commissioner for the imperial mausoleum and then retired from office.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong died, he served as commissioner for the imperial mausoleum, then retired from office.

entries.zh: 年八十卒。
entries.en: He died at the age of eighty.
entries.literal: He died at age eighty.

entries.zh: 蕭素颯，字特免，五院部人。
entries.en: Xiao Susa, whose style name was Temian, was a man of the Five Courts Division.
entries.literal: Xiao Susa, style name Temian, was a man of the Five Courts Division.

entries.zh: 重熙間始仕，累遷北院承旨，彰湣宮使。
entries.en: He entered service during the Chongxi reign and rose through successive promotions to Imperial Secretariat Attendant of the Northern Court and Commissioner of the Zhangmin Palace.
entries.literal: He began office during Chongxi, was repeatedly promoted to Imperial Secretariat Attendant of the Northern Court and Commissioner of the Zhangmin Palace.

entries.zh: 清寧初，歷左皮室詳穩、右夷離畢。
entries.en: Early in the Qingning reign, he served as Xiangwen of the Left Pishi and Right Yilibi.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, he served as Xiangwen of the Left Pishi and Right Yilibi.

entries.zh: 咸雍五年，剖阿裏部叛，素颯討降之，率其酋長來朝。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Xianyong, the Po'ali Division rebelled. Susa campaigned against them, accepted their surrender, and led their chieftains to court.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xianyong, the Po'ali Division rebelled; Susa campaigned, accepted their surrender, and led their chieftains to court.

entries.zh: 帝嘉其功，徙北院林牙，改南院副部署，卒。
entries.en: The emperor commended his achievement, transferred him to Northern Chancellor Linya, then reassigned him as Vice Deployment Commissioner of the Southern Court, after which he died.
entries.literal: The emperor commended his merit, transferred him to Northern Chancellor Linya, changed him to Vice Deployment Commissioner of the Southern Court, and he died.

entries.zh: 子謀魯斡，字回璉，初補夷離畢郎君，遷文班太保。
entries.en: His son Moluwo, whose style name was Huilian, was first appointed Langjun of the Yilibi, then promoted to Grand Protector of the Civil Roster.
entries.literal: His son Moluwo, style name Huilian, was first appointed Langjun of the Yilibi, then transferred to Grand Protector of the Civil Roster.

entries.zh: 大康中，改南京統軍使，為右夷離畢。
entries.en: During the Dakang reign, he was made Army Commander of the Southern Capital and appointed Right Yilibi.
entries.literal: During Dakang, he was changed to Army Commander of the Southern Capital and made Right Yilibi.

entries.zh: 與樞密使耶律阿思論事不合，見忌，出為馬群太保。
entries.en: He clashed with Commissioner of Military Affairs Yelu Asi over policy and, being resented by him, was sent out as Grand Protector of the Horse Herds.
entries.literal: He disagreed with the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yelu Asi in discussion of affairs, was viewed with jealousy, and was sent out as Grand Protector of the Horse Herds.

entries.zh: 北部來侵，謀魯斡破之，以功遷同知烏古敵烈統軍，仍許便宜行事。
entries.en: When the northern tribes invaded, Moluwo defeated them. For this achievement he was made Vice Commander of the Wugu-Dilie Army with authority to act at his own discretion.
entries.literal: When the northern tribes invaded, Moluwo defeated them; for his merit he was transferred to Vice Commander of the Wugu-Dilie Army and was still permitted to act at his own discretion.

entries.zh: 後以讒毀，降領西北路戍軍，復為馬群太保，卒。
entries.en: Later, slandered by his enemies, he was demoted to command the garrison army of the Northwest Circuit, then reappointed Grand Protector of the Horse Herds, and died in office.
entries.literal: Later, because of slander, he was demoted to command the garrison army of the Northwest Circuit, again made Grand Protector of the Horse Herds, and died.

entries.zh: 耶律弘古耶律馬六蕭滴冽耶律適祿耶律陳家奴耶律特麼耶律仙童蕭素颯耶律大悲奴
entries.en: Yelu Honggu, Yelu Maliu, Xiao Dilie, Yelu Shilu, Yelu Chenjianu, Yelu Teme, Yelu Xiantong, Xiao Susa, and Yelu Dabeinu
entries.literal: Yelu Honggu, Yelu Maliu, Xiao Dilie, Yelu Shilu, Yelu Chenjianu, Yelu Teme, Yelu Xiantong, Xiao Susa, Yelu Dabeinu

entries.zh: 姚景行，始名景禧。
entries.en: Yao Jingxing — his original name was Jingxi.
entries.literal: Yao Jingxing — his original name was Jingxi.

entries.zh: 祖漢英，本周將，應歷初來聘，用敵國禮，帝怒，留之，隸漢人宮分。
entries.en: His grandfather Hanying had been a general of the Later Zhou. Early in the Yingli reign he came on embassy and used the rites due an equal state. The emperor was angry, detained him, and assigned him to a Han palace household.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hanying had been a general of the Later Zhou; early in Yingli he came on embassy and used the rites due an equal state; the emperor was angry, detained him, and assigned him to a Han palace household.

entries.zh: 及景行既貴，始出籍，貫興中縣。
entries.en: When Jingxing had risen high, he was first removed from the household register and his domicile was entered as Xingzhong County.
entries.literal: When Jingxing had risen high, he was first removed from the register and his domicile was entered as Xingzhong County.

entries.zh: 景行博學。
entries.en: Jingxing was broadly learned.
entries.literal: Jingxing was broadly learned.

entries.zh: 重熙五年，擢進士乙科，為將作監，改燕趙國王教授。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Chongxi reign he was selected in the second rank of the jinshi examination, became Director of Palace Construction, and was transferred to Instructor to the Prince of Yan and Zhao.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Chongxi he was selected in the second rank of the jinshi examination, became Director of Palace Construction, and was transferred to Instructor to the Prince of Yan and Zhao.

entries.zh: 不數年，至翰林學士，樞密副使，參知政事。
entries.en: Within a few years he reached Hanlin Academician, Deputy Commissioner of the Secretariat, and Participant in Government.
entries.literal: Within a few years he reached Hanlin Academician, Deputy Commissioner of the Secretariat, and Participant in Government.

entries.zh: 性敦厚廉直，人望歸之。
entries.en: By nature he was sincere, generous, and upright, and public esteem turned to him.
entries.literal: By nature he was sincere, generous, and upright, and public esteem turned to him.

entries.zh: 道宗即位，多被顧問，為北府宰相。
entries.en: When Emperor Daozong ascended the throne, he was often consulted and became Chancellor of the Northern Office.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong ascended the throne, he was often consulted and became Chancellor of the Northern Office.

entries.zh: 九年秋，告歸，道聞重元亂，收集行旅，得三百餘騎勤王。
entries.en: In the autumn of the ninth year he requested leave to return home. On the road he heard of Chongyuan's rebellion, gathered his traveling companions, and mustered more than three hundred horsemen to aid the throne.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year he requested leave to return home; on the road he heard of Chongyuan's rebellion, gathered his traveling companions, and obtained more than three hundred horsemen to aid the throne.

entries.zh: 比至，賊已平。
entries.en: By the time he arrived, the rebels had already been pacified.
entries.literal: By the time he arrived, the rebels had already been pacified.

entries.zh: 帝嘉其忠，賜以逆人財產。
entries.en: The emperor praised his loyalty and granted him the property of the rebels.
entries.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty and granted him the property of the rebels.

entries.zh: 咸雍元年，出為武定軍節度使。
entries.en: In the first year of the Xianyong reign he was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianyong he was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.

entries.zh: 明年，驛召拜南院樞密使。
entries.en: The next year he was summoned by relay post and appointed Commissioner of the Southern Court Secretariat.
entries.literal: The next year he was summoned by relay post and appointed Commissioner of the Southern Court Secretariat.

entries.zh: 上從容問治道，引入內殿，出御書及太子書示之，賜什器車仗。
entries.en: The emperor at leisure asked him about the way of governance, brought him into the inner hall, produced imperial writings and the crown prince's writings to show him, and granted household goods, carriages, and equipment.
entries.literal: The emperor at leisure asked him about the way of governance, brought him into the inner hall, produced imperial writings and the crown prince's writings to show him, and granted household goods, carriages, and equipment.

entries.zh: 帝有意伐宋，召景行問曰：「宋人好生邊事，如何？」
entries.en: The emperor intended to attack Song and summoned Jingxing to ask, "The Song are fond of provoking border affairs — what do you advise?"
entries.literal: The emperor intended to attack Song and summoned Jingxing to ask, "The Song are fond of provoking border affairs — what of it?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「自聖宗皇帝以威德懷遠，宋修職貢，迨今幾六十年。
entries.en: He replied, "Since Emperor Shengzong won the distant by majesty and virtue, Song has maintained tribute duties. Down to today that has been nearly sixty years.
entries.literal: He replied, "Since Emperor Shengzong won the distant by majesty and virtue, Song has maintained tribute duties — down to today it is nearly sixty years.

entries.zh: 若以細故用兵，恐違先帝成約。」
entries.en: If we use arms over a trifling matter, I fear we will violate the late emperor's settled agreement."
entries.literal: If we use arms over a trifling matter, I fear we will violate the late emperor's settled agreement."

entries.zh: 上然其言而止。
entries.en: The emperor approved his words and abandoned the plan.
entries.literal: The emperor approved his words and desisted.

entries.zh: 耶律良，字習撚，小字蘇，著帳郎君之後。
entries.en: Yelu Liang, whose style name was Sinian and whose childhood name was Su, was a descendant of the Registered-Tent Attendant Gentleman line.
entries.literal: Yelu Liang, style name Sinian, childhood name Su, was a descendant of the Registered-Tent Attendant Gentleman line.

entries.zh: 生於乾州，讀書醫巫閭山。
entries.en: Born in Qianzhou, he studied on Mount Yiwulü.
entries.literal: Born in Qianzhou, he studied on Mount Yiwulü.

entries.zh: 學既博，將入南山肄業，友人止之曰：「爾無仆禦，驅馳千里，縱聞見過人，年亦垂暮。
entries.en: When his learning was already broad, he was about to enter the southern mountains to continue his studies. A friend stopped him, saying, "You have no servant or carriage. To travel a thousand li — even if your learning surpasses others, your years are already near their end.
entries.literal: When his learning was already broad, he was about to enter the southern mountains to pursue his studies; a friend stopped him, saying, "You have no servant or carriage; to gallop a thousand li — even if your knowledge surpasses others, your years are already near their end.

entries.zh: 今若即仕，已有餘地。」
entries.en: If you take office now, you already have ample scope for achievement."
entries.literal: If you take office now, you already have room enough."

entries.zh: 良曰：「窮通命也，非爾所知。」
entries.en: Liang said, "Failure and success are a matter of fate — not something you can know."
entries.literal: Liang said, "Failure and success are a matter of fate — not something you can know."

entries.zh: 不聽，留數年而歸。
entries.en: He would not listen, remained several years, and then returned.
entries.literal: He would not listen, remained several years, and returned.

entries.zh: 重熙中，補寢殿小底，尋為燕趙國王近侍。
entries.en: During the Chongxi reign he was appointed junior attendant of the sleeping hall and soon became a close attendant of the Prince of Yan and Zhao.
entries.literal: During Chongxi he was appointed junior attendant of the sleeping hall and soon became a close attendant of the Prince of Yan and Zhao.

entries.zh: 以家貧，詔乘廄馬。
entries.en: Because his family was poor, an edict allowed him to ride horses from the imperial stables.
entries.literal: Because his family was poor, an edict allowed him to ride stable horses.

entries.zh: 遷修起居註。
entries.en: He was transferred to compiler of the Veritable Records.
entries.literal: He was transferred to compiler of the Veritable Records.

entries.zh: 會獵秋山，良進《秋遊賦》，上嘉之。
entries.en: When the emperor was hunting at Autumn Mountain, Liang presented his 《Rhapsody on an Autumn Outing》, and the emperor praised it.
entries.literal: When the emperor was hunting at Autumn Mountain, Liang presented the 《Rhapsody on an Autumn Outing》, and the emperor praised it.

entries.zh: 清寧中，上幸鴨子河，作《捕魚賦》。
entries.en: During the Qingning reign, when the emperor visited Duck River, Liang composed his 《Rhapsody on Fishing》.
entries.literal: During Qingning, when the emperor visited Duck River, Liang composed the 《Rhapsody on Fishing》.

entries.zh: 由是寵遇稍隆，遷知制誥，兼知部署司事。
entries.en: From this his favor grew, and he was transferred to Drafting Edicts with concurrent charge of the Deployment Office.
entries.literal: From this his favor rose somewhat; he was transferred to Drafting Edicts and concurrently administered the Deployment Office.

entries.zh: 奏請編御製詩文，目曰《清寧集》；
entries.en: He memorialized requesting that the emperor's poems and prose be compiled under the title 《Qingning Collection》;
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting compilation of the emperor's poems and prose, to be titled the 《Qingning Collection》;

entries.zh: 上命良詩為《慶會集》，親制其序。
entries.en: the emperor ordered that Liang's poems form the 《Celebratory Assembly Collection》 and personally composed its preface.
entries.literal: the emperor ordered Liang's poems to form the 《Celebratory Assembly Collection》 and personally composed its preface.

entries.zh: 頃之，為敦睦宮使，兼權知皇太后宮諸局事。
entries.en: Before long he became Commissioner of the Dunmu Palace and concurrently held acting charge of the various bureaus of the Empress Dowager's palace.
entries.literal: Before long he became Commissioner of the Dunmu Palace and concurrently held acting charge of the various bureaus of the Empress Dowager's palace.

entries.zh: 良聞重元與子涅魯古謀亂，以帝篤於親愛，不敢遽奏，密言於皇太后。
entries.en: Liang heard that Chongyuan and his son Nielugu were plotting rebellion. Because the emperor was deeply devoted to his kin, he did not dare report it at once and spoke secretly to the Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Liang heard that Chongyuan and his son Nielugu were plotting rebellion; because the emperor was deeply devoted to his kin, he did not dare report it at once and spoke secretly to the Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 太皇托疾，召帝白其事。
entries.en: The Grand Empress Dowager feigned illness and summoned the emperor to tell him of the plot.
entries.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager feigned illness and summoned the emperor to inform him of the matter.

entries.zh: 帝謂良曰：「汝欲間我骨肉耶？」
entries.en: The emperor said to Liang, "Do you wish to set my own flesh and blood against one another?"
entries.literal: The emperor said to Liang, "Do you wish to set my flesh and blood against one another?"

entries.zh: 良奏曰：「臣若妄言，甘伏斧锧。
entries.en: Liang replied, "If your servant speaks falsely, I willingly submit to the axe.
entries.literal: Liang memorialized, "If your servant speaks falsely, I willingly submit to the axe.

entries.zh: 陛下不早備，恐墮賊計。
entries.en: If Your Majesty does not prepare early, I fear you will fall into the rebels' trap.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not prepare early, I fear you will fall into the rebels' plot.

entries.zh: 如召涅魯古不來，可卜其事。」
entries.en: If Nielugu is summoned and does not come, that will prove the matter."
entries.literal: If Nielugu is summoned and does not come, the matter can be tested."

entries.zh: 帝從其言。
entries.en: The emperor followed his advice.
entries.literal: The emperor followed his advice.

entries.zh: 使者及門，涅魯古意欲害之，羈於帳下。
entries.en: When the envoy reached the gate, Nielugu intended to kill him and detained him in the tent.
entries.literal: When the envoy reached the gate, Nielugu intended to kill him and detained him under the tent.

entries.zh: 使者以佩刀斷帟而出，馳至行宮，以狀聞。
entries.en: The envoy cut through the tent hangings with his belt knife, fled out, galloped to the traveling palace, and reported what had happened.
entries.literal: The envoy cut through the tent hangings with his belt knife and fled out, galloped to the traveling palace, and reported the situation.

entries.zh: 帝始信。
entries.en: Only then did the emperor believe.
entries.literal: Only then did the emperor believe.

entries.zh: 亂平，以功遷漢人行宮都部署。
entries.en: When the rebellion was pacified, he was transferred for his merit to Garrison Commander of the Han Traveling Palace.
entries.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, for his merit he was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Han Traveling Palace.

entries.zh: 咸雍初，同知南院樞密使事，為惕隱，出知中京留守事。
entries.en: Early in the Xianyong reign he became co-administrator of the Southern Court Secretariat, served as Tiyin, and was sent out to administer the Central Capital garrison command.
entries.literal: Early in Xianyong he became co-administrator of the Southern Court Secretariat, served as Tiyin, and was sent out to administer the Central Capital garrison command.

entries.zh: 未幾卒，帝嗟悼，遣重臣賻祭，給葬具，追封遼西郡王，謚曰忠成。
entries.en: Before long he died. The emperor sighed in grief, sent high ministers with funeral gifts and libations, provided burial goods, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Liaoxi with the posthumous title Zhongcheng.
entries.literal: Before long he died; the emperor sighed in grief, sent high ministers with funeral gifts and libations, provided burial goods, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Liaoxi with posthumous title Zhongcheng.

entries.zh: 九年七月，上獵太子山，耶律良奏重元謀逆，帝召仁先語之。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the ninth year, while the emperor was hunting at Mount Taizi, Yelu Liang reported that Chongyuan was plotting rebellion. The emperor summoned Renxian and told him of it.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year, when the emperor was hunting at Mount Taizi, Yelu Liang reported that Chongyuan was plotting rebellion; the emperor summoned Renxian and told him.

entries.zh: 仁先曰：「此曹凶狠，臣固疑之久矣。」
entries.en: Renxian said, "That crew is fierce and cruel. Your servant has suspected them for a long time."
entries.literal: Renxian said, "This crew is fierce and cruel; your servant has long suspected them."

entries.zh: 帝趣仁先捕之。
entries.en: The emperor urged Renxian to arrest them at once.
entries.literal: The emperor urged Renxian to seize them.

entries.zh: 仁先出，且曰：「陛下宜謹為之備！」
entries.en: Renxian went out, adding as he left, "Your Majesty must take careful precautions!"
entries.literal: Renxian went out, saying as he did so, "Your Majesty should take careful precautions!"

entries.zh: 未及介馬，重元犯帷宮。
entries.en: Before he could even mount his horse, Chongyuan struck at the curtained imperial encampment.
entries.literal: Before he could mount, Chongyuan attacked the curtained palace.

entries.zh: 帝欲幸北、南院，仁先曰：「陛下若舍扈從而行，賊必躡其後；
entries.en: The emperor wished to go to the Northern and Southern courts. Renxian said, "If Your Majesty leaves your escort and goes alone, the rebels will surely follow close behind;
entries.literal: The emperor wished to go to the Northern and Southern courts; Renxian said, "If Your Majesty abandons your escort and goes alone, the rebels will surely follow close behind;

entries.zh: 且南、北大王心未可知。」
entries.en: moreover, the loyalty of the Great Kings of the Northern and Southern courts cannot yet be known."
entries.literal: moreover, the hearts of the Great Kings of the Northern and Southern courts cannot yet be known."

entries.zh: 仁先子撻不也曰：「聖意豈可違乎？」
entries.en: Renxian's son Tabuye said, "How can the sacred will be disobeyed?"
entries.literal: Renxian's son Tabuye said, "How can the sacred will be disobeyed?"

entries.zh: 仁先怒，擊其首。
entries.en: Renxian flew into a rage and struck him on the head.
entries.literal: Renxian grew angry and struck him on the head.

entries.zh: 帝悟，悉委仁先以討賊事。
entries.en: The emperor understood and entrusted the entire campaign against the rebels to Renxian.
entries.literal: The emperor understood and entrusted the entire suppression of the rebels to Renxian.

entries.zh: 乃環車為營，拆行馬，作兵仗，率官屬近侍三十餘騎陣柢枑外。
entries.en: He then ringed the carts into a camp, dismantled the cheval-de-frise to make weapons, and led more than thirty mounted officials and close attendants to form a battle line outside the barrier posts.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ringed the carts into a camp, dismantled the cheval-de-frise, fashioned weapons, and led more than thirty mounted officials and close attendants to form a battle line outside the barrier posts.

entries.zh: 及交戰，賊眾多降。
entries.en: Once battle was joined, many of the rebels surrendered.
entries.literal: When battle was joined, many of the rebels surrendered.

entries.zh: 涅魯古中矢墮馬，擒之，重元被傷而退。
entries.en: Nielugu was struck by an arrow, fell from his horse, and was captured. Chongyuan was wounded and withdrew.
entries.literal: Nielugu was struck by an arrow, fell from his horse, and was captured; Chongyuan was wounded and withdrew.

entries.zh: 仁先以五院部蕭塔剌所居最近，亟召之，分遣人集諸軍。
entries.en: Because Xiao Tala of the Five Courts Division lived nearest, Renxian urgently summoned him and dispatched men in every direction to gather the armies.
entries.literal: Renxian, because Xiao Tala of the Five Courts Division lived nearest, urgently summoned him and sent men in different directions to gather the armies.

entries.zh: 黎明，重元率奚人二千犯行宮，蕭塔剌兵適至。
entries.en: At dawn Chongyuan led two thousand Xi men in an assault on the traveling palace, and Xiao Tala's troops arrived just in time.
entries.literal: At dawn Chongyuan led two thousand Xi men in an attack on the traveling palace, and Xiao Tala's troops arrived just in time.

entries.zh: 仁先料賊勢不能久，俟其氣沮攻之。
entries.en: Renxian judged that the rebel force could not endure long and waited until their spirit flagged before attacking.
entries.literal: Renxian judged that the rebel force could not hold long and waited until their spirit flagged before attacking.

entries.zh: 乃背營而陣，乘便奮擊，賊眾奔潰，追殺二十餘里，重元與數騎遁去。
entries.en: He then drew up his line with the camp at his back, struck hard when the moment favored him, and the rebels broke and fled. The pursuit continued for more than twenty li, and Chongyuan escaped with only a few horsemen.
entries.literal: Thereupon he drew up his line with the camp at his back, struck hard at an opportune moment, the rebels broke and fled, and they were pursued and slain for more than twenty li; Chongyuan escaped with a few horsemen.

entries.zh: 帝執仁先手曰：「平亂皆卿之功也。」
entries.en: The emperor took Renxian by the hand and said, "The pacification of this rebellion is entirely your achievement."
entries.literal: The emperor took Renxian's hand and said, "The pacification of the rebellion is entirely your achievement."

entries.zh: 加尚父，進封宋王，為北院樞密使，親制文以褒之，詔畫《灤河戰圖》以旌其功。
entries.en: He was given the exalted title Imperial Father, advanced to Prince of Song, and made Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat. The emperor personally composed a text in his praise and ordered that the 《Battle Picture of the Luan River》 be painted to honor his merit.
entries.literal: He was given the exalted title Imperial Father, advanced to Prince of Song, made Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat, personally composed a text to praise him, and ordered that the 《Battle Picture of the Luan River》 be painted to honor his merit.

entries.zh: 耶律阿思，字撒班。
entries.en: Yelu Asi, whose style name was Saban.
entries.literal: Yelu Asi, style name Saban.

entries.zh: 清寧初，補祗候郎君。
entries.en: Early in the Qingning reign he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.
entries.literal: Early in Qingning he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 以善射，掌獵事，進渤海近侍詳穩。
entries.en: Because he was skilled at archery he managed hunting affairs and was promoted to xiangwen of the Bohai Close Attendants.
entries.literal: Because he was skilled at archery he managed hunting affairs and was promoted to Xiangwen of the Bohai Close Attendants.

entries.zh: 重元之亂，與護衛蘇射殺涅魯古，賜號靖亂功臣，徙契丹行宮都部署。
entries.en: During Chongyuan's rebellion he and the guard Su shot and killed Nielugu, was granted the title Meritorious in Quelling Disorder, and was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Khitan Traveling Palace.
entries.literal: In Chongyuan's rebellion he together with the guard Su shot and killed Nielugu, was granted the title Meritorious in Quelling Disorder, and was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Khitan Traveling Palace.

entries.zh: 大安初，為北院大王，封漆水郡王。
entries.en: Early in the Da'an reign he became Great King of the Northern Court and was enfeoffed as Prince of Qishui.
entries.literal: Early in Da'an he became Great King of the Northern Court and was enfeoffed as Prince of Qishui.

entries.zh: 壽隆元年，為北院樞密使，監修國史。
entries.en: In the first year of the Shoulong reign he became Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat and supervised compilation of the national history.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shoulong he became Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat and supervised compilation of the national history.

entries.zh: 道宗崩，受顧命，加於越。
entries.en: When Emperor Daozong died he received the dying edict and was given the title yuyue.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong died he received the final imperial command and was given the title yuyue.

entries.zh: 錄乙辛黨人，罪重者當籍其家，阿思受賂，多所寬貰。
entries.en: When Yixin's partisans were registered, those whose crimes were grave should have had their households confiscated, but Asi took bribes and pardoned many.
entries.literal: When Yixin's partisans were registered, those whose crimes were grave should have had their households confiscated, but Asi took bribes and pardoned many.

entries.zh: 蕭合魯嘗言當修邊備，阿思力沮其事，或譏其以金賣國。
entries.en: Xiao Helu once argued that frontier defenses should be strengthened, but Asi strenuously blocked the proposal, and some mocked him for selling the state for gold.
entries.literal: Xiao Helu once said that frontier defenses should be strengthened, but Asi strenuously blocked the proposal, and some mocked him for selling the state for gold.

entries.zh: 後以風疾失音，致仕，加尚父，封趙王。
entries.en: Later he lost his voice to wind disorder, retired from office, was given the exalted title Imperial Father, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: Later, because of wind disorder he lost his voice, retired from office, was given the exalted title Imperial Father, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 薨，年八十，追封齊國王。
entries.en: He died at the age of eighty and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: He died, aged eighty, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 咸雍元年，加於越，改封遼王，與耶律乙辛共知北院樞密事。
entries.en: In the first year of the Xianyong reign he was given the title yuyue, reassigned as Prince of Liao, and jointly administered Northern Court Secretariat affairs with Yelu Yixin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianyong he was given the title yuyue, reassigned as Prince of Liao, and jointly administered Northern Court Secretariat affairs with Yelu Yixin.

entries.zh: 乙辛恃寵不法，仁先抑之，由是見忌，出為南京留守，改王晉。
entries.en: Yixin relied on imperial favor and acted lawlessly. Renxian restrained him, and on that account was resented, sent out as Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital, and reassigned as Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: Yixin relied on favor and acted lawlessly; Renxian restrained him and on that account was resented, sent out as Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital, and reassigned as Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 恤孤惸，禁奸慝，宋聞風震服。
entries.en: He cared for orphans and the destitute, forbade wickedness and evil, and when Song heard of his conduct they were awed into submission.
entries.literal: He cared for orphans and the solitary, forbade wickedness and evil, and when Song heard of it they were awed into submission.

entries.zh: 議者以為自於越休哥之後，惟仁先一人而已。
entries.en: Commentators held that since Yelu Xiuge as yuyue, Renxian alone had been such a man.
entries.literal: Commentators held that since yuyue Xiuge, Renxian alone had been such a man.

entries.zh: 阻卜塔裏幹叛命，仁先為西北路招討使，賜鷹紐印及劍。
entries.en: When the Zubu chieftain Taligan rebelled, Renxian was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit and granted an eagle-button seal and a sword.
entries.literal: When the Zubu chieftain Taligan rebelled, Renxian was made Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit and granted an eagle-button seal and a sword.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「卿去朝廷遠，每俟奏行，恐失機會，可便宜從事。」
entries.en: The emperor instructed him, saying, "You are far from court. If you wait for memorials and orders on every matter, you may miss your chance. You may act at discretion."
entries.literal: The emperor instructed him, saying, "You are far from court; if you wait for memorials and orders on every matter, you may miss opportunities. You may act at discretion."

entries.zh: 仁先嚴斥候，扼敵沖，懷柔服從，庶事整飭。
entries.en: Renxian strictly posted scouts, blocked the enemy's thrusts, treated those who submitted with kindness, and put all affairs in good order.
entries.literal: Renxian strictly posted scouts, blocked the enemy's thrusts, treated the compliant with kindness, and put all affairs in good order.

entries.zh: 塔裏幹復來寇，仁先逆擊，追殺八十餘里。
entries.en: Taligan came raiding again. Renxian met him in counterattack and pursued the enemy for more than eighty li.
entries.literal: Taligan came raiding again; Renxian met him in counterattack and pursued, killing for more than eighty li.

entries.zh: 大軍繼至，又敗之。
entries.en: When the main army arrived, it again defeated them.
entries.literal: When the main army arrived it again defeated them.

entries.zh: 別部把裏斯、禿沒等來救，見其屢挫，不敢戰而降。
entries.en: Subordinate divisions under Balisi, Tumo, and others came to the rescue, but seeing repeated defeats they did not dare fight and surrendered.
entries.literal: Subordinate divisions Balisi, Tumo, and others came to the rescue; seeing repeated defeats, they did not dare fight and surrendered.

entries.zh: 北邊遂安。
entries.en: The northern frontier was thus pacified.
entries.literal: The northern frontier was thus pacified.

entries.zh: 八年卒，年六十，遺命家人薄葬。
entries.en: In the eighth year he died at the age of sixty and left instructions that his family bury him simply.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged sixty, and left instructions that his family bury him simply.

entries.zh: 弟義先、信先，俱有傳。
entries.en: His younger brothers Yixian and Xinxian both have separate biographies.
entries.literal: His younger brothers Yixian and Xinxian both have separate biographies.

entries.zh: 子撻不也。
entries.en: His son was Tabuye.
entries.literal: His son was Tabuye.

entries.zh: 蕭韓家奴，字括寧，奚長渤魯恩之後。
entries.en: Xiao Hanjianu, whose style name was Kuoning, was a descendant of the Xi chieftain Boluen.
entries.literal: Xiao Hanjianu, style name Kuoning, was a descendant of the Xi chieftain Boluen.

entries.zh: 性孝友。
entries.en: By nature he was filial and devoted to his brothers.
entries.literal: By nature he was filial and brotherly.

entries.zh: 太平中，補祗候郎君，累遷敦睦宮使。
entries.en: During the Taiping reign he was appointed Attendant Gentleman and rose through successive appointments to Commissioner of the Dunmu Palace.
entries.literal: During Taiping he was appointed Attendant Gentleman and rose through successive posts to Commissioner of the Dunmu Palace.

entries.zh: 伐夏，為左翼都監，遷北面林牙。
entries.en: On the campaign against Xia he served as Left Wing Commander-in-Chief and was transferred to Northern Chancellor Linya.
entries.literal: On the campaign against Xia he served as Left Wing Commander-in-Chief and was transferred to Northern Chancellor Linya.

entries.zh: 俄為南院副部署，賜玉帶，改奚六部大王，治有聲。
entries.en: Soon he became Deputy Garrison Commander of the Southern Court, was granted a jade belt, was transferred to Great King of the Six Xi Tribes, and his governance won renown.
entries.literal: Soon he became Deputy Garrison Commander of the Southern Court, was granted a jade belt, was transferred to Great King of the Six Xi Tribes, and his governance won renown.

entries.zh: 清寧初，封韓國公，歷南京統軍使、北院宣徽使，封蘭陵郡王。
entries.en: Early in the Qingning reign he was enfeoffed as Duke of Han, served as Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital armies and as Commissioner of the Northern Court Imperial Household, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling.
entries.literal: Early in Qingning he was enfeoffed as Duke of Han, served as Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital armies, and as Commissioner of the Northern Court Imperial Household, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling.

entries.zh: 九年，上獵太子山，聞重元亂，馳詣行在。
entries.en: In the ninth year, when the emperor was hunting at Mount Taizi and heard of Chongyuan's rebellion, he galloped to the traveling palace.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, when the emperor was hunting at Mount Taizi and heard of Chongyuan's rebellion, he galloped to the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 帝倉卒欲避於北、南大王院，與耶律仁先執轡固諫，乃止。
entries.en: The emperor, taken by surprise, wished to flee to the courts of the Northern and Southern Great Kings. Together with Yelu Renxian, Hanjianu seized the reins and remonstrated firmly, and the emperor abandoned the plan.
entries.literal: The emperor in haste wished to flee to the courts of the Northern and Southern Great Kings; together with Yelu Renxian he seized the reins and firmly remonstrated, and the emperor stopped.

entries.zh: 明旦，重元復誘奚獵夫來。
entries.en: At dawn the next day, Chongyuan again induced Xi hunters to come against the court.
entries.literal: At dawn the next day, Chongyuan again induced Xi hunters to come.

entries.zh: 韓家奴獨出諭之曰：「汝曹去順效逆，徒取族滅。
entries.en: Hanjianu went out alone and addressed them, saying, "You abandon loyalty and follow rebellion — you will only bring extermination upon your clans.
entries.literal: Hanjianu went out alone and instructed them, saying, "You abandon obedience and follow rebellion — you will only bring extermination upon your clans.

entries.zh: 何若悔過，轉禍為福！」
entries.en: Why not repent and turn disaster into blessing!"
entries.literal: Why not repent and turn misfortune into blessing!"

entries.zh: 獵夫投仗首服。
entries.en: The hunters cast down their weapons and submitted with bowed heads.
entries.literal: The hunters cast down their weapons and submitted with bowed heads.

entries.zh: 以功遷殿前都點檢，封荊王，賜資忠保義奉國竭貞平亂功臣。
entries.en: For his merit he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front, enfeoffed as Prince of Jing, and granted the title Meritorious in Loyalty, Righteousness, Service to the State, Utter Devotion, and Pacification of Disorder.
entries.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front, enfeoffed as Prince of Jing, and granted the title Meritorious in Loyalty, Righteousness, Service to the State, Utter Devotion, and Pacification of Disorder.

entries.zh: 咸雍二年，遷西南面招討使。
entries.en: In the second year of the Xianyong reign he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianyong he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.

entries.zh: 大康初，徙王吳，賜白海東青鶻。
entries.en: Early in the Dakang reign he was reassigned as Prince of Wu and granted a white sea gyrfalcon.
entries.literal: Early in Dakang he was reassigned as Prince of Wu and granted a white sea gyrfalcon.

entries.zh: 皇太子為乙辛誣構，幽於上京。
entries.en: The crown prince was framed by Yelu Yixin and imprisoned at the Supreme Capital.
entries.literal: The crown prince was framed by Yixin and imprisoned at the Supreme Capital.

entries.zh: 韓家奴上書力言其冤，不報。
entries.en: Hanjianu memorialized forcefully declaring the prince's innocence, but received no response.
entries.literal: Hanjianu memorialized forcefully declaring his innocence, but received no response.

entries.zh: 四年，復為西南面招討使。
entries.en: In the fourth year he again became Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he again became Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.

entries.zh: 例削一字王爵，改王蘭陵，薨。
entries.en: By regulation his single-character princely title was reduced. He was reassigned as Prince of Lanling and died.
entries.literal: By regulation his single-character princely title was reduced; he was reassigned as Prince of Lanling and died.

entries.zh: 子楊九，終右祗候郎君班詳穩，贈同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: His son Yangjiu ended his career as Xiangwen of the Right Attendant Gentlemen Class and was posthumously made Co-Director of the Secretariat Chancellery.
entries.literal: His son Yangjiu ended as Xiangwen of the Right Attendant Gentlemen Class and was posthumously made Co-Director of the Secretariat Chancellery.

entries.zh: 蕭德，字特末隱，楮特部人。
entries.en: Xiao De, whose style name was Temoyin, was a man of the Chute Tribe.
entries.literal: Xiao De, style name Temoyin, was a man of the Chute Tribe.

entries.zh: 性和易，篤學好禮法。
entries.en: He was easygoing by nature, devoted to learning, and fond of ritual and law.
entries.literal: His nature was easygoing; he was devoted to learning and loved ritual and law.

entries.zh: 太平中，領牌印、直宿，累遷北院樞密副使，敷奏詳明，多稱上旨。
entries.en: During the Taiping reign he was put in charge of seals and tally and night watch, rose through successive appointments to Deputy Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat, and in memorials was detailed and clear, often winning approval of the sovereign's intent.
entries.literal: During Taiping he was put in charge of seals and tally and night watch, rose through successive posts to Deputy Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat, and in memorials was detailed and clear, often winning approval of the sovereign's intent.

entries.zh: 詔與林牙耶律庶成修《律令》，改契丹行宮都部署，賜宮戶十有五。
entries.en: An edict ordered him and Linya Yelu Shucheng to compile the Statutes and Ordinances. He was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Khitan Traveling Palace and granted fifteen palace households.
entries.literal: An edict ordered him together with Linya Yelu Shucheng to compile the Statutes and Ordinances; he was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Khitan Traveling Palace and granted fifteen palace households.

entries.zh: 清寧元年，遷同知北院樞密使，封魯國公。
entries.en: In the first year of the Qingning reign he was transferred to co-administrator of the Northern Court Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingning he was transferred to co-administrator of the Northern Court Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

entries.zh: 上以德為先朝眷遇，拜南府宰相。
entries.en: Because the emperor regarded De as one favored by the previous reign, he was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office.
entries.literal: Because the emperor regarded De as one favored by the previous reign, he was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office.

entries.zh: 五年，轉南京統軍使。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital armies.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital armies.

entries.zh: 九年，復為南府宰相。
entries.en: In the ninth year he again became Chancellor of the Southern Office.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he again became Chancellor of the Southern Office.

entries.zh: 重元之亂，推鋒力戰，斬涅魯古首以獻，論功封漢王。
entries.en: During Chongyuan's rebellion he led the van and fought hard, beheaded Nielugu and presented the head, and for his merit was enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
entries.literal: In Chongyuan's rebellion he led the van and fought hard, beheaded Nielugu and presented the head, and for his merit was enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

entries.zh: 咸雍初，以告老歸，優詔不許。
entries.en: Early in the Xianyong reign, on grounds of age he requested retirement and return home, but a gracious edict did not permit it.
entries.literal: Early in Xianyong, on grounds of age he requested retirement and return home, but a gracious edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 久之，加尚父，致仕。
entries.en: After some time he was given the exalted title Imperial Father and retired from office.
entries.literal: After some time he was given the exalted title Imperial Father and retired from office.

entries.zh: 卒，年七十二。
entries.en: He died at the age of seventy-two.
entries.literal: He died, aged seventy-two.

entries.zh: 蕭惟信，字耶寧，楮特部人。
entries.en: Xiao Weixin, whose style name was Yening, was a man of the Chute Tribe.
entries.literal: Xiao Weixin, style name Yening, was a man of the Chute Tribe.

entries.zh: 五世祖霞賴，南府宰相。
entries.en: His fifth-generation ancestor Xialai served as Chancellor of the Southern Office.
entries.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Xialai was Chancellor of the Southern Office.

entries.zh: 曾祖烏古，中書令。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Wugu served as Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Wugu was Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 祖阿古只，知平州。
entries.en: His grandfather Aguzhi served as Administrator of Pingzhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Aguzhi was Administrator of Pingzhou.

entries.zh: 父高八，多智數，博覽古今。
entries.en: His father Gaoba was greatly resourceful and widely read in affairs ancient and modern.
entries.literal: His father Gaoba was greatly resourceful and widely read in affairs ancient and modern.

entries.zh: 開泰初，為北院承旨，稍遷右夷離畢，以幹敏稱，拜南府宰相。
entries.en: Early in the Kaitai reign he served as Northern Court Secretariat Drafter, was gradually transferred to Right Yilibi, was known for capability and keenness, and was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office.
entries.literal: Early in Kaitai he was Northern Court Secretariat Drafter, was gradually transferred to Right Yilibi, was known for capability and keenness, and was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office.

entries.zh: 累遷倒塌嶺節度使，知興中府，復為右夷離畢。
entries.en: He rose through successive appointments to Military Commissioner of Daodaling, Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture, and again Right Yilibi.
entries.literal: He rose through successive posts to Military Commissioner of Daodaling, Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture, and again Right Yilibi.

entries.zh: 陵青誘眾作亂，事覺，高八按之，止誅首惡，餘並釋之。
entries.en: Lingqing incited the masses to rebellion. When the matter came to light, Gaoba investigated it, executed only the chief culprits, and released the rest.
entries.literal: Lingqing incited the masses to rebellion; when the matter came to light, Gaoba investigated it, executed only the chief culprits, and released the rest.

entries.zh: 歸奏，稱旨。
entries.en: On his return he reported, and the emperor was pleased.
entries.literal: On returning he reported, and the emperor was pleased.

entries.zh: 惟信資沈毅，篤誌於學，能辨論。
entries.en: Weixin was by nature steady and resolute, devoted in his pursuit of learning, and skilled in debate.
entries.literal: Weixin was by nature steady and resolute, devoted in his pursuit of learning, and able in debate.

entries.zh: 重熙初始仕，累遷左右丞。
entries.en: He first entered office at the beginning of the Chongxi reign and rose through successive appointments to Left and Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: He first entered office at the beginning of Chongxi and rose through successive posts to Left and Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 十五年，徙燕趙國王傅，帝諭之曰：「燕趙左右多面諛，不聞忠言，浸以成性。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was transferred as Tutor to the Prince of Yan and Zhao. The emperor instructed him, saying, "Those about the prince are mostly flatterers to his face. They do not hear loyal words, and this has gradually become their nature.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred as Tutor to the Prince of Yan and Zhao; the emperor instructed him, saying, "Those about Yan and Zhao are mostly flatterers to the face; they do not hear loyal words, and this has gradually become their nature.

entries.zh: 汝當以道規誨，使知君父之義。
entries.en: You should instruct him in the Way and make him understand the obligations owed to ruler and father.
entries.literal: You should instruct him in the Way and make him understand the obligations toward ruler and father.

entries.zh: 有不可處王邸者，以名聞。」
entries.en: If anyone is unfit to remain in the prince's residence, report his name."
entries.literal: If any cannot remain in the prince's residence, report their names."

entries.zh: 惟信輔導以禮。
entries.en: Weixin guided and instructed him according to ritual propriety.
entries.literal: Weixin guided and instructed him according to ritual.

entries.zh: 十七年，遷北院樞密副使，坐事免官。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat but was dismissed from office for an offense.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat but was dismissed from office for an offense.

entries.zh: 尋復職，兼北面林牙。
entries.en: Before long he was restored to office and concurrently served as Northern Chancellor Linya.
entries.literal: Before long he was restored to office and concurrently served as Northern Chancellor Linya.

entries.zh: 清寧九年，重元作亂，犯灤河行宮，惟信從耶律仁先破之，賜竭忠定亂功臣。
entries.en: In the ninth year of the Qingning reign, when Chongyuan rebelled and attacked the traveling palace on the Luan River, Weixin followed Yelu Renxian in defeating him and was granted the title Meritorious in Utter Loyalty and Pacification of Disorder.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Qingning, when Chongyuan rebelled and attacked the traveling palace on the Luan River, Weixin followed Yelu Renxian in defeating him and was granted the title Meritorious in Utter Loyalty and Pacification of Disorder.

entries.zh: 歷南京留守、左右夷離畢，復為北院樞密副使。
entries.en: He served as Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital, as Left and Right Yilibi, and again as Deputy Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat.
entries.literal: He served as Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital, Left and Right Yilibi, and again as Deputy Commissioner of the Northern Court Secretariat.

entries.zh: 大康中，以老乞骸骨，不聽。
entries.en: During the Dakang reign, on grounds of age he requested retirement, but was not permitted.
entries.literal: During Dakang, on grounds of age he requested retirement, but was not permitted.

entries.zh: 樞密使耶律乙辛譖廢太子，中外知其冤，無敢言者，惟信數廷爭，不得復。
entries.en: The Secretariat Commissioner Yelu Yixin slandered and deposed the crown prince. Within and without the court all knew the prince's innocence, yet none dared speak. Weixin repeatedly argued in court but could not secure his restoration.
entries.literal: The Secretariat Commissioner Yelu Yixin slandered and deposed the crown prince; within and without the court all knew his innocence, yet none dared speak; Weixin repeatedly argued in court but could not secure restoration.

entries.zh: 告老，加守司徒，卒。
entries.en: He announced his retirement, was given the honorific Defender Grandee, and died.
entries.literal: He announced his retirement, was given the honorific Defender Grandee, and died.

entries.zh: 耶律敵烈，字撒懶，采訪使吼五世孫。
entries.en: Yelu Dilie, whose style name was Salan, was a fifth-generation descendant of the Investigation Commissioner Hou.
entries.literal: Yelu Dilie, style name Salan, was a fifth-generation descendant of the Investigation Commissioner Hou.

entries.zh: 寬厚好學，工文詞。
entries.en: He was generous and magnanimous, fond of learning, and skilled in literary composition.
entries.literal: He was generous and magnanimous, fond of learning, and skilled in literary composition.

entries.zh: 重熙末，補牌印郎君，兼知起居註。
entries.en: Late in the Chongxi reign he was appointed Seal-and-Tally Attendant Gentleman and concurrently served as compiler of the Veritable Records.
entries.literal: Late in Chongxi he was appointed Seal-and-Tally Attendant Gentleman and concurrently served as compiler of the Veritable Records.

entries.zh: 清寧元年，稍遷同知永州事，禁盜有功，改北面林牙承旨。
entries.en: In the first year of the Qingning reign he was gradually transferred to co-administrator of Yongzhou affairs. For suppressing banditry he earned merit and was made Northern Chancellor Linya Drafter.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingning he was gradually transferred to co-administrator of Yongzhou affairs; for suppressing banditry he had merit and was made Northern Chancellor Linya Drafter.

entries.zh: 九年，重元作亂，敵烈赴援，力戰平之，遙授臨海軍節度使。
entries.en: In the ninth year, when Chongyuan rebelled, Dilie rushed to aid, fought hard to pacify the rebellion, and was appointed in absentia Military Commissioner of the Linhai Army.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, when Chongyuan rebelled, Dilie rushed to aid, fought hard to pacify the rebellion, and was appointed in absentia Military Commissioner of the Linhai Army.

entries.zh: 十年，徙武安州觀察使。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was transferred to Observation Commissioner of Wu'an Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Observation Commissioner of Wu'an Prefecture.

entries.zh: 咸雍五年，累遷長寧宮使。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Xianyong reign he rose through successive appointments to Commissioner of the Changning Palace.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xianyong he rose through successive posts to Commissioner of the Changning Palace.

entries.zh: 撿括戶部司乾州錢帛逋負，立出納經畫法，公私便之。
entries.en: He audited arrears in money and silk owed to the Households Bureau at Qianzhou, established methods for receipts and disbursements, and both public and private affairs were made convenient.
entries.literal: He audited arrears in money and silk owed to the Households Bureau at Qianzhou, established methods for receipts and disbursements, and both public and private affairs were made convenient.

entries.zh: 大康四年，為南院大王。
entries.en: In the fourth year of the Dakang reign he became Great King of the Southern Court.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Dakang he became Great King of the Southern Court.

entries.zh: 秩滿，部民請留，同知南京留守事。
entries.en: When his term ended, the people of his division asked that he remain, and he became co-administrator of the Southern Capital garrison command.
entries.literal: When his term ended, the people of his division asked that he remain, and he became co-administrator of the Southern Capital garrison command.

entries.zh: 有疾，上命乘傳赴闕，遣太醫視之。
entries.en: When he fell ill, the emperor ordered him to travel by relay post to court and sent the imperial physician to attend him.
entries.literal: When he fell ill, the emperor ordered him to travel by relay post to court and sent the imperial physician to attend him.

entries.zh: 遷上京留守。
entries.en: He was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Supreme Capital.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Garrison Commander of the Supreme Capital.

entries.zh: 大安中，改塌母城節度使。
entries.en: During the Da'an reign he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Tamu City.
entries.literal: During Da'an he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Tamu City.

entries.zh: 以疾致仕，加兼侍中，賜一品俸。
entries.en: He retired on grounds of illness, was additionally made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was granted first-rank salary.
entries.literal: He retired on grounds of illness, was additionally made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was granted first-rank salary.

entries.zh: 八年卒。
entries.en: He died in the eighth year.
entries.literal: He died in the eighth year.

entries.zh: 致仕，不逾月復舊職。
entries.en: He retired from office, but within a month was restored to his former post.
entries.literal: He retired from office, but within a month was restored to his former post.

entries.zh: 丁家艱，起復，兼中書令。
entries.en: He entered mourning for a parent, was recalled from mourning, and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He entered mourning for a parent, was recalled from mourning, and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 上問古今儒士優劣，占對稱旨，知興中府，改朔方軍節度使。
entries.en: The emperor asked about the relative merits of Confucian scholars ancient and modern. His reply pleased the emperor, and he was made Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture, then transferred to Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Army.
entries.literal: The emperor asked about the relative merits of Confucian scholars ancient and modern; his extempore reply pleased the emperor, and he was made Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture, then transferred to Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Army.

entries.zh: 大康初，徙鎮遼興。
entries.en: Early in the Dakang reign he was transferred to garrison Liaoxing.
entries.literal: Early in Dakang he was transferred to garrison Liaoxing.

entries.zh: 以上京多滯獄，命為留守，不數月，以獄空聞。
entries.en: Because the Supreme Capital had many cases held in detention, he was appointed Garrison Commander. Within a few months it was reported that the prisons were empty.
entries.literal: Because the Supreme Capital had many cases held in detention, he was appointed Garrison Commander; within a few months it was reported that the prisons were empty.

entries.zh: 累乞致政，不從。
entries.en: He repeatedly requested retirement, but was not permitted.
entries.literal: He repeatedly requested retirement, but was not permitted.

entries.zh: 復請，許之，加守太師。
entries.en: He requested again and was permitted. He was given the honorific Defender Grand Master.
entries.literal: He requested again and was permitted; he was given the honorific Defender Grand Master.

entries.zh: 卒，遣使吊祭，追封柳城郡王，謚文憲。
entries.en: He died. Envoys were sent with condolences and libations. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Liucheng with the posthumous title Wenxian.
entries.literal: He died; envoys were sent with condolences and libations; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Liucheng with posthumous title Wenxian.

entries.zh: 壽隆五年，詔為立祠。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Shoulong reign an edict ordered a shrine erected for him.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Shoulong an edict ordered a shrine erected for him.

entries.zh: 論曰：灤河之變，重元擁兵行幄，微仁先等，道宗其危乎！
entries.en: The commentators say: At the Luan River crisis, Chongyuan held troops against the traveling encampment. But for Renxian and the others, would not Emperor Daozong have been in peril!
entries.literal: The commentators say: At the Luan River crisis, Chongyuan held troops against the traveling encampment — but for Renxian and the others, would not Emperor Daozong have been in peril!

entries.zh: 當其止幸北、南院，召塔剌兵以靖大難，功宜居首。
entries.en: When he halted the imperial progress to the Northern and Southern courts and summoned Tala's troops to settle the great crisis, his merit should rank first.
entries.literal: When he halted the imperial progress to the Northern and Southern courts and summoned Tala's troops to settle the great crisis, his merit should rank first.

entries.zh: 良以反謀白太后，韓家奴以逆順降奚人，德與阿思殺涅魯古，皆有討賊之力焉。
entries.en: Liang reported the plot of rebellion to the Empress Dowager; Hanjianu, by distinguishing loyalty from rebellion, caused the Xi to submit; Xiao De and Yelu Asi killed Nielugu — all contributed force to the suppression of the rebels.
entries.literal: Liang reported the plot of rebellion to the Empress Dowager; Hanjianu by distinguishing loyalty and rebellion caused the Xi to submit; De and Asi killed Nielugu — all had the power to suppress the rebels.

entries.zh: 仁先齊名休哥，勛德兼備，此其一節歟！
entries.en: Renxian ranks with Yelu Xiuge in fame; merit and virtue together complete — is this not one proof of it!
entries.literal: Renxian ranks with Xiuge in fame; merit and virtue together complete — is this not one proof of it!

entries.zh: 耶律仁先
entries.en: Yelu Renxian
entries.literal: Yelu Renxian

entries.zh: 〈（撻不也）〉
entries.en: (Tabuye)
entries.literal: (Tabuye)

entries.zh: 耶律良蕭韓家奴蕭德蕭惟信蕭樂音奴耶律敵烈姚景行耶律阿思
entries.en: Yelu Liang, Xiao Hanjianu, Xiao De, Xiao Weixin, Xiao Leyinnu, Yelu Dilie, Yao Jingxing, and Yelu Asi
entries.literal: Yelu Liang; Xiao Hanjianu; Xiao De; Xiao Weixin; Xiao Leyinnu; Yelu Dilie; Yao Jingxing; Yelu Asi

entries.zh: 耶律斡特剌孩裏竇景庸耶律引吉楊績趙徽王觀耶律喜孫
entries.en: Yelu Wotela, Hai Li, Dou Jingyong, Yelu Yinji, Yang Ji, Zhao Hui, Wang Guan, and Yelu Xisun
entries.literal: Yelu Wotela, Hai Li, Dou Jingyong, Yelu Yinji, Yang Ji, Zhao Hui, Wang Guan, Yelu Xisun

entries.zh: 楊績，良鄉人。
entries.en: Yang Ji was a native of Liangxiang.
entries.literal: Yang Ji was a man of Liangxiang.

entries.zh: 太平十一年進士及第，累遷南院樞密副使。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Taiping he passed the civil examinations and was repeatedly promoted until he became Vice Commissioner of the Southern Administration.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Taiping he passed the civil examinations and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Southern Administration.

entries.zh: 與杜防、韓知白等擅給進士堂帖，降長寧軍節度使，徙知涿州。
entries.en: Together with Du Fang, Han Zhibai, and others he arbitrarily issued jinshi hall credentials; he was demoted to Military Commissioner of Changning Army and transferred to administer Zhuo Prefecture.
entries.literal: Together with Du Fang, Han Zhibai, and others he arbitrarily issued jinshi hall credentials; he was demoted to Military Commissioner of Changning Army and transferred to administer Zhuo Prefecture.

entries.zh: 清寧初，拜參知政事，兼同知樞密院事，為南府宰相。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qingning he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor, concurrently Vice Director of the Military Affairs Commission, and Chancellor of the Southern Administration.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor, concurrently Vice Director of the Military Affairs Commission, and served as Chancellor of the Southern Administration.

entries.zh: 九年，聞重元亂，與姚景行勤王，上嘉之。
entries.en: In the ninth year, on hearing of Chongyuan's rebellion, he marched with Yao Jingxing to aid the throne, and the emperor commended him.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, hearing of Chongyuan's rebellion, he marched with Yao Jingxing to aid the throne, and the emperor commended him.

entries.zh: 十年，知興中府。
entries.en: In the tenth year he administered Xingzhong Prefecture.
