entries.literal: In the tenth year he administered Xingzhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 咸雍初，入知樞密院事。
entries.en: At the beginning of Xianyong he entered court to administer the Military Affairs Commission.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xianyong he entered to administer the Military Affairs Commission.

entries.zh: 二年，乞致仕，不許，拜南院樞密使。
entries.en: In the second year he asked to retire, but permission was refused, and he was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Administration.
entries.literal: In the second year he requested retirement but was not permitted and was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Administration.

entries.zh: 帝以績舊臣，特詔燕見，論古今治亂，人臣邪正。
entries.en: Because Ji was an old minister, the emperor specially summoned him to a private audience to discuss the order and disorder of ancient and modern times and the wickedness and rectitude of ministers.
entries.literal: Because Ji was an old minister, the emperor specially summoned him to a private audience to discuss the order and disorder of ancient and modern times and the wickedness and rectitude of ministers.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「方今群臣忠直，耶律玦、劉伸而已；
entries.en: The emperor said, "Among the ministers today who are loyal and upright, only Yelu Jue and Liu Shen remain;
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Among the ministers today who are loyal and upright, only Yelu Jue and Liu Shen remain;

entries.zh: 然伸不及玦之剛介。」
entries.en: yet Shen does not match Jue in firm integrity."
entries.literal: yet Shen does not match Jue in firm integrity."

entries.zh: 績拜賀曰：「何代無賢，世亂則獨善其身，主聖則兼濟天下。
entries.en: Ji bowed in congratulation and said, "What age has lacked worthy men? When the age is chaotic one keeps oneself whole; when the ruler is sage one benefits all under Heaven.
entries.literal: Ji bowed in congratulation and said: "What age has lacked worthy men? When the age is chaotic one keeps oneself whole; when the ruler is sage one benefits all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 陛下銖分邪正，升黜分明，天下幸甚。」
entries.en: Your Majesty minutely distinguishes the wicked and the upright and promotes and demotes with clarity—great fortune for the realm."
entries.literal: Your Majesty minutely distinguishes the wicked and the upright and promotes and demotes with clarity—great fortune for the realm."

entries.zh: 累表告歸，不許，封趙王。
entries.en: He repeatedly memorialized asking to return home, but permission was refused, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: He repeatedly memorialized asking to return home but was not permitted and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 大康中，以例改王遼西。
entries.en: During the Dakang era, by precedent his title was changed to Prince of Liaoxi.
entries.literal: During Dakang, by precedent his princedom was changed to Liaoxi.

entries.zh: 致仕，加守太保，薨。
entries.en: He retired from office, was promoted to Defender Grand Guardian, and died.
entries.literal: He retired, was promoted to Defender Grand Guardian, and died.

entries.zh: 子貴忠，知興中府。
entries.en: His son Guizhong administered Xingzhong Prefecture.
entries.literal: His son Guizhong administered Xingzhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 論曰：孩裏、引吉之為臣也，當乙辛擅權、蕭革貪黷之日，雖與同官，而能以正自處，不少阿唯，其過人遠矣。
entries.en: The commentary says: As ministers, Hai Li and Yinji lived in the days when Yixin monopolized power and Xiao Ge was greedy and corrupt; though they served alongside such men, they were able to maintain themselves by rectitude and would not fawn or agree—how far they surpassed others.
entries.literal: The commentary says: As ministers, Hai Li and Yinji lived in the days when Yixin monopolized power and Xiao Ge was greedy and corrupt; though they held office with such men, they were able to maintain themselves by rectitude and did not fawn or agree—how far they surpassed others.

entries.zh: 傳曰：「歲寒知松柏之後雕。」
entries.en: The Classic says, "Only when the year turns cold do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither."
entries.literal: The Classic says: "Only when the year turns cold do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither."

entries.zh: 二子有焉。
entries.en: These two men had it.
entries.literal: These two men had it.

entries.zh: 若斡特剌之戰功，竇景庸之讞獄，楊績之忠告，亦賢矣夫。
entries.en: As for Wotela's military achievements, Dou Jingyong's adjudication of cases, and Yang Ji's loyal counsel—they too were worthy men indeed.
entries.literal: As for Wotela's military achievements, Dou Jingyong's adjudication of cases, and Yang Ji's loyal counsel—they too were worthy men.

entries.zh: 孩裏，字胡輦，回鶻人。
entries.en: Hai Li, whose style name was Hunian, was a Uyghur.
entries.literal: Hai Li, style name Hunian, was a Uyghur.

entries.zh: 其先在太祖時來貢，願留，因任用之。
entries.en: His ancestors had come to offer tribute in the time of Taizu, asked to remain, and were therefore given office.
entries.literal: His forebears had come to offer tribute in the time of Taizu, wished to remain, and were therefore employed in office.

entries.zh: 孩裏重熙間歷近侍長。
entries.en: During the Chongxi era Hai Li successively served as chief palace attendant.
entries.literal: In the Chongxi era Hai Li successively served as chief palace attendant.

entries.zh: 清寧九年，討重元之亂有功，加金吾衛上將軍，賜平亂功臣。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Qingning he had merit in suppressing the rebellion of Chongyuan and was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard and granted the merit title Pacifier of Disorder.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Qingning he had merit in suppressing the rebellion of Chongyuan and was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard, granted the merit title "Pacifier of Disorder."

entries.zh: 累遷殿前都點檢，以宿衛嚴肅稱。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted until he became Commander of the Palace Front and was known for the strictness with which he maintained palace guard duty.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Commander of the Palace Front and was known for the strictness of his palace guard service.

entries.zh: 大康初，加守太子太保。
entries.en: At the beginning of Dakang he was promoted to Defender Heir Apparent Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dakang he was promoted to Defender Heir Apparent Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 二年，加同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In the second year he was promoted to Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Chancellery.

entries.zh: 三年，改同知南院宣徽使事。
entries.en: In the third year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Southern Administration Commissioner of the Imperial Household.
entries.literal: In the third year he was changed to Vice Director of the Southern Administration Commissioner of the Imperial Household.

entries.zh: 會耶律乙辛出守中京，孩裏入賀；
entries.en: When Yelu Yixin went out to guard the Central Capital, Hai Li entered court to offer congratulations;
entries.literal: When Yelu Yixin went out to guard the Central Capital, Hai Li entered court to offer congratulations;

entries.zh: 及議復召，陳其不可。
entries.en: when the court deliberated recalling him, Hai Li argued that this should not be done.
entries.literal: when deliberation turned to recalling him again, Hai Li stated that this should not be done.

entries.zh: 後乙辛再入樞府，出孩裏為廣利軍節度使。
entries.en: Later, when Yixin again entered the Military Affairs Commission, he had Hai Li sent out as Military Commissioner of Guangli Army.
entries.literal: Later, when Yixin again entered the Military Affairs Commission, he had Hai Li sent out as Military Commissioner of Guangli Army.

entries.zh: 及皇太子被誣，孩裏當連坐，有詔勿問。
entries.en: When the crown prince was falsely accused, Hai Li would have been implicated by association, but an edict ordered that he not be prosecuted.
entries.literal: When the crown prince was falsely accused, Hai Li would have been implicated by association, but an edict ordered that he not be prosecuted.

entries.zh: 大安初，歷品達魯虢部節度使。
entries.en: At the beginning of Da'an he successively served as Military Commissioner of the Pindaluoguo Division.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he successively served as Military Commissioner of the Pindaluoguo Division.

entries.zh: 壽隆五年，有疾，自言吾數已盡，卻醫藥，卒，年七十七。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Shoulong he fell ill, declaring that his allotted span was exhausted; he refused medicine and died at seventy-seven.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Shoulong he fell ill, saying himself that his allotted span was exhausted; he refused medicine and died, aged seventy-seven.

entries.zh: 孩裏素信浮圖。
entries.en: Hai Li had long been a believer in Buddhism.
entries.literal: Hai Li had long believed in Buddhism.

entries.zh: 清寧初，從上獵，墮馬，憒而復蘇。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qingning, while accompanying the emperor on a hunt, he fell from his horse, lost consciousness, and then revived.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, while accompanying the emperor on a hunt, he fell from his horse, lost consciousness, and then revived.

entries.zh: 言始見二人引至一城，宮室宏敞，有衣絳袍人坐殿上，左右列侍，導孩裏升階。
entries.en: He said that at first two men led him to a city of vast palaces and halls, where a man in a crimson robe sat upon the dais with attendants ranked to left and right, and they guided Hai Li up the steps.
entries.literal: He said that at first he saw two men lead him to a city whose palaces and halls were vast and grand; a man in a crimson robe sat upon the dais, attendants stood in rows to left and right, and they guided Hai Li up the steps.

entries.zh: 持牘者示之曰：「本取大腹骨欲，誤執汝。」
entries.en: The man holding the document showed it to him and said, "We originally meant to take Dafugu, but mistakenly seized you."
entries.literal: The man holding the document showed it to him and said: "We originally meant to take Dafugu, but mistakenly seized you."

entries.zh: 牘上書「官至使相，壽七十七」。
entries.en: On the document was written, "Office reaches commissioner and chancellor; lifespan seventy-seven."
entries.literal: On the document was written: "Office reaches commissioner and chancellor; lifespan seventy-seven."

entries.zh: 須臾還，擠之大壑而寤。
entries.en: After a moment he was sent back, thrust into a great ravine, and awoke.
entries.literal: After a moment he returned, was pushed into a great ravine, and awoke.

entries.zh: 道宗聞之，命書其事。
entries.en: Emperor Daozong heard of it and ordered the affair recorded in writing.
entries.literal: Emperor Daozong heard of it and ordered the affair written down.

entries.zh: 後皆驗。
entries.en: Later events all proved it true.
entries.literal: Later events all verified it.

entries.zh: 耶律斡特剌，字乙辛隱，許國王寅底石六世孫。
entries.en: Yelu Wotela, whose style name was Yixin Yin, was a sixth-generation descendant of Prince Xu of State, Yindi.
entries.literal: Yelu Wotela, style name Yixin Yin, was a sixth-generation descendant of Prince Xu of State, Yindi.

entries.zh: 少不喜官祿，年四十一，始補本班郎君。
entries.en: As a young man he cared little for office and emolument; only at forty-one did he first receive appointment as an attendant of the standard corps.
entries.literal: In youth he cared little for official salary and rank; not until age forty-one did he first receive appointment as an attendant of the standard corps.

entries.zh: 時樞密使耶律乙辛擅權，讒害忠良，斡特剌恐禍及，深自抑畏。
entries.en: At the time Yelu Yixin, Commissioner of Military Affairs, held power arbitrarily and slandered loyal ministers; fearing that disaster might reach him, Wotela kept himself deeply subdued and cautious.
entries.literal: At the time the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yelu Yixin monopolized power and slandered the loyal and worthy; Wotela feared calamity would reach him and deeply restrained and humbled himself.

entries.zh: 大康中，為宿直官，歷左、右護衛太保。
entries.en: During the Dakang era he served on night duty at court and successively held the posts of Left and Right Guard Commissioner.
entries.literal: In the Dakang era he served as a night-duty officer and successively held the posts of Left and Right Guard Commissioners.

entries.zh: 大安元年，升燕王傅，徙左夷離畢。
entries.en: In the first year of Da'an he was promoted to Tutor to the Prince of Yan and transferred to the post of Left Tribal Affairs Commissioner.
entries.literal: In the first year of Da'an he was promoted to Tutor to the Prince of Yan and transferred to Left Tribal Affairs Commissioner.

entries.zh: 四年，改北院樞密副使。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Northern Administration.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Vice Commissioner of the Northern Administration of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 帝賜詩褒之，遷知北院樞密使事，賜翼聖佐義功臣。
entries.en: The emperor composed a poem in his praise, promoted him to Acting Commissioner of the Northern Administration, and granted him the merit title Worthy Assistant in Supporting the Sage.
entries.literal: The emperor bestowed a poem in praise of him, promoted him to Acting Commissioner of the Northern Administration, and granted him the merit title "Worthy Assistant in Supporting the Sage."

entries.zh: 北阻卜酋長磨古斯叛，斡特剌率兵進討。
entries.en: When Mogusi, chief of the northern Zubu, rebelled, Wotela led troops to suppress him.
entries.literal: The chief of the northern Zubu, Mogusi, rebelled, and Wotela led troops forward to suppress him.

entries.zh: 會天大雪，敗磨古斯四別部，斬首千餘級，拜西北路招討使，封漆水郡王，加賜宣力守正功臣。
entries.en: Heavy snow fell at the time; he defeated four of Mogusi's sub-divisions, took more than a thousand heads, was appointed Commissioner for Pacification of the Northwest Route, enfeoffed as Prince of Qishui Commandery, and further granted the merit title Upholding Integrity with Dedicated Strength.
entries.literal: It happened that heaven sent heavy snow; he defeated four sub-divisions of Mogusi's forces, beheaded more than a thousand, was appointed Commissioner for Pacification of the Northwest Route, enfeoffed as Prince of Qishui Commandery, and further granted the merit title "Upholding Integrity with Dedicated Strength."

entries.zh: 尋拜南府宰相。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Chancellor of the Southern Administration.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Administration.

entries.zh: 復討閘古胡裏扒部，破之，召為契丹行宮都部署。
entries.en: He again campaigned against the Zanguhuliba tribe, defeated them, and was summoned to serve as Chief Deployer of the Khitan Imperial Camp.
entries.literal: He again attacked the Zanguhuliba tribe, defeated them, and was summoned to serve as Chief Deployer of the Khitan Imperial Camp.

entries.zh: 先是，北、南府有訟，各州府得就按之；
entries.en: Previously, when the Northern and Southern Administrations had lawsuits, each prefecture and district could go on site to investigate them;
entries.literal: Previously, when the Northern and Southern Administrations had lawsuits, each prefecture and district could go and investigate them on the spot;

entries.zh: 比歲，非奉樞密檄，不得鞫問，以故訟者稽留。
entries.en: in recent years, however, unless one held an order from the Military Affairs Commission, one could not conduct interrogations, and for this reason litigants were long detained.
entries.literal: in recent years, unless carrying an order from the Military Affairs Commission, one could not conduct interrogations, and for this reason litigants were detained.

entries.zh: 斡特剌奏請如舊，從之。
entries.en: Wotela memorialized asking that the former practice be restored, and the court agreed.
entries.literal: Wotela memorialized requesting that the old practice be restored, and the request was approved.

entries.zh: 壽隆五年，復為西北路招討使，討耶睹刮部，俘斬甚眾，獲馬、駝、牛、羊各數萬。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Shoulong he again served as Commissioner for Pacification of the Northwest Route and campaigned against the Yedugua tribe, capturing and beheading a great many and taking tens of thousands each of horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Shoulong he again served as Commissioner for Pacification of the Northwest Route, campaigning against the Yedugua tribe; he captured and beheaded a great many, and obtained tens of thousands each of horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

entries.zh: 明年，擒磨古斯，加守太保，賜奉國匡化功臣。
entries.en: The following year he captured Mogusi, was promoted to Defender Grand Guardian, and was granted the merit title Supporting the State and Rectifying Transformation.
entries.literal: The next year he captured Mogusi, was promoted to Defender Grand Guardian, and was granted the merit title "Supporting the State and Rectifying Transformation."

entries.zh: 乾統初，乞致仕，不許，止罷招討。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qiantong he asked to retire, but permission was refused; he was only removed from the pacification command.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qiantong he requested retirement, but was not permitted; he was only removed from the pacification command.

entries.zh: 復兼南院樞密使，封混同郡王。
entries.en: He again served concurrently as Commissioner of the Southern Administration and was enfeoffed as Prince of Huntong Commandery.
entries.literal: He again concurrently held the post of Commissioner of the Southern Administration and was enfeoffed as Prince of Huntong Commandery.

entries.zh: 遷北院樞密使，加守太師，賜推誠贊治功臣。
entries.en: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Northern Administration, promoted to Defender Grand Preceptor, and granted the merit title Sincere in Counsel and Praiseworthy in Governance.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Northern Administration, promoted to Defender Grand Preceptor, and granted the merit title "Sincere in Counsel and Praiseworthy in Governance."

entries.zh: 致仕，薨，謚曰敬肅。
entries.en: He retired from office, died, and was posthumously titled Jingsu.
entries.literal: He retired, died, and was posthumously titled Jingsu.

entries.zh: 耶律引吉，字阿括，品部人。
entries.en: Yelu Yinji, whose style name was Akuo, was a man of the Pin tribe.
entries.literal: Yelu Yinji, style name Akuo, was a man of the Pin tribe.

entries.zh: 父雙古，鎮西邊二十餘年，治尚嚴肅，不殖貨利，時多稱之。
entries.en: His father Shuanggu guarded the western frontier for more than twenty years; his governance was strict, he did not pursue profit, and at the time many praised him.
entries.literal: His father Shuanggu guarded the western frontier for more than twenty years; his governance valued strictness, he did not pursue profit, and at the time many praised him.

entries.zh: 引吉寅畏好義。
entries.en: Yinji was cautious and respectful and loved righteousness.
entries.literal: Yinji was cautious and respectful and loved righteousness.

entries.zh: 以蔭補官，累遷東京副留守、北樞密院侍御。
entries.en: Through hereditary privilege he entered office and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and Palace Attendant of the Northern Military Affairs Commission.
entries.literal: Through hereditary privilege he entered office and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and Palace Attendant of the Northern Military Affairs Commission.

entries.zh: 時蕭革、蕭圖古辭等以佞見任，鬻爵納賄，引吉以直道處其間，無所阿唯。
entries.en: At the time Xiao Ge, Xiao Tuguci, and others were employed for their flattery, selling offices and accepting bribes; Yinji stood among them on the straight path and would not fawn or agree to anything.
entries.literal: At the time Xiao Ge, Xiao Tuguci, and others were employed for their flattery, selling offices and accepting bribes; Yinji stood among them by the straight path and did not fawn or agree to anything.

entries.zh: 改客省使。
entries.en: He was transferred to the post of Reception Commissioner.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Reception Commissioner.

entries.zh: 時朝廷遣使括三京隱戶不得，以引吉代之，得數千餘戶。
entries.en: At the time the court had sent envoys to register hidden households in the Three Capitals without success; Yinji replaced them and obtained more than several thousand households.
entries.literal: At the time the court had sent envoys to register hidden households in the Three Capitals without success; Yinji replaced them and obtained more than several thousand households.

entries.zh: 時昭懷太子知北南院事，選引吉為輔導。
entries.en: At the time Crown Prince Zhaohuai oversaw the affairs of the Northern and Southern Administrations and selected Yinji as his instructor.
entries.literal: At the time Crown Prince Zhaohuai oversaw the affairs of the Northern and Southern Administrations and selected Yinji as his instructor.

entries.zh: 樞密使乙辛將傾太子，惡引吉在側，奏出之，為群牧林牙。
entries.en: Commissioner of Military Affairs Yixin was about to bring down the crown prince and hated having Yinji at his side; he memorialized to have him sent out and appointed him Commissioner of Herds.
entries.literal: The Commissioner of Military Affairs Yixin was about to bring down the crown prince and hated Yinji at his side; he memorialized to have him sent out and appointed him Commissioner of Herds.

entries.zh: 大康元年，乙辛請賜牧地，引吉奏曰：「今牧地褊狹，畜不蕃息，豈可分賜臣下。」
entries.en: In the first year of Dakang, Yixin requested that pasture lands be granted; Yinji memorialized, saying, "At present the pasture lands are narrow and cramped and livestock do not multiply—how can they be divided and granted to subordinates?"
entries.literal: In the first year of Dakang, Yixin requested that pasture lands be granted; Yinji memorialized, saying: "At present the pasture lands are narrow and cramped and livestock do not multiply—how can they be divided and granted to subordinates?"

entries.zh: 帝乃止。
entries.en: The emperor thereupon stopped the matter.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped the matter.

entries.zh: 乙辛由是益嫉之，除懷德軍節度使，徙漠北猾水馬群太保，卒。
entries.en: Yixin therefore hated him all the more, appointed him Military Commissioner of Huaide Army, transferred him to Grand Guardian of the Huashui Horse Herds in the far north, and he died.
entries.literal: Yixin therefore hated him all the more, appointed him Military Commissioner of Huaide Army, transferred him to Grand Guardian of the Huashui Horse Herds in the far north, and he died.

entries.zh: 趙徽，南京人。
entries.en: Zhao Hui was a native of the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: Zhao Hui was a man of the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 重熙五年，擢甲科，累遷大理正。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Chongxi he passed the examinations in the top grade and was repeatedly promoted until he became Chief of the Court of Justice.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Chongxi he passed the examinations in the top grade and was repeatedly promoted to Chief of the Court of Justice.

entries.zh: 清寧二年，銅州人妄毀三教，徽按鞫之，以狀聞，稱旨。
entries.en: In the second year of Qingning a man of Tong Prefecture wantonly slandered the Three Teachings; Hui investigated and interrogated the case, reported it in a memorial, and pleased the emperor.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qingning a man of Tong Prefecture wantonly slandered the Three Teachings; Hui investigated and interrogated the case, reported it in a memorial, and pleased the emperor's intent.

entries.zh: 歷煩劇，有能名。
entries.en: He passed through arduous and demanding posts and earned a reputation for ability.
entries.literal: He passed through arduous and demanding posts and had a reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 累遷翰林學士承旨。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 咸雍初，為度支使。
entries.en: At the beginning of Xianyong he served as Commissioner of Revenue.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xianyong he served as Commissioner of Revenue.

entries.zh: 三年，拜參知政事。
entries.en: In the third year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: In the third year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 出為武定軍節度使，及代，軍民請留。
entries.en: He went out as Military Commissioner of Wuding Army, and when his term ended the soldiers and people asked that he be retained.
entries.literal: He went out as Military Commissioner of Wuding Army, and when his term ended the soldiers and people asked that he be retained.

entries.zh: 後同知樞密院事，兼南府宰相、門下侍郎、平章事。
entries.en: Later he served as Vice Director of the Military Affairs Commission, concurrently Chancellor of the Southern Administration, Vice Minister of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: Later he served as Vice Director of the Military Affairs Commission, concurrently Chancellor of the Southern Administration, Vice Minister of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 致仕，卒。
entries.en: He retired from office and died.
entries.literal: He retired and died.

entries.zh: 追贈中書令，謚文憲。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted the title of Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous title Wenxian.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title of Director of the Department of State Affairs and posthumously titled Wenxian.

entries.zh: 耶律喜孫，字盈隱，永興宮分人。
entries.en: Yelu Xisun, whose style name was Yinyin, was a man of the Yongxing Palace Division.
entries.literal: Yelu Xisun, style name Yinyin, was a man of the Yongxing Palace Division.

entries.zh: 興宗在青宮，嘗居左右輔導。
entries.en: When Xingzong was heir apparent in the Eastern Palace, Xisun had once served at his side as instructor.
entries.literal: When Xingzong was in the Eastern Palace, Xisun had once served at his side as instructor.

entries.zh: 聖宗大漸，喜孫與馮家奴告仁德皇后同宰相蕭浞卜等謀逆事。
entries.en: When Emperor Shengzong was critically ill, Xisun together with Feng Jianu reported that Empress Rende, Chancellor Xiao Pobu, and others were plotting treason.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shengzong was critically ill, Xisun together with Feng Jianu reported that Empress Rende and the chancellor Xiao Pobu and others were plotting treason.

entries.zh: 及欽哀為皇太后稱制，喜孫尤見寵任。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Qin'ai assumed regency, Xisun was especially favored and trusted.
entries.literal: When Empress Dowager Qin'ai assumed regency, Xisun was especially favored and trusted.

entries.zh: 重熙中，其子涅哥為近侍，坐事伏誅。
entries.en: During the Chongxi era his son Niege served as a palace attendant and was executed for an offense.
entries.literal: In the Chongxi era his son Niege served as a palace attendant and was executed for an offense.

entries.zh: 帝以喜孫有翼戴功，且悼其子罪死，欲世其官，喜孫無所出之部，因見馬印文有品部號，使隸其部，拜南府宰相。
entries.en: Because Xisun had merit in supporting the emperor's accession and the emperor also grieved that his son had died for a crime, he wished to make his office hereditary; as Xisun had no division of origin, the emperor saw on a horse-brand the mark of the Pin tribe, had him attached to that tribe, and appointed him Chancellor of the Southern Administration.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Xisun had merit in supporting his accession and also grieved that his son had died for a crime, wished to make his office hereditary; as Xisun had no division of origin, seeing on a horse-brand the mark of the Pin tribe, he had him attached to that tribe and appointed him Chancellor of the Southern Administration.

entries.zh: 尋出為東北路詳穩，卒。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was sent out as Detailed Inspector of the Northeast Route and died.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was sent out as Detailed Inspector of the Northeast Route and died.

entries.zh: 道宗嘗謂大臣曰：「今之忠直，耶律玦、劉伸而已！」
entries.en: Daozong once told his ministers: "Today only Yelu Jue and Liu Shen are truly loyal and upright!"
entries.literal: Daozong once told his great ministers, "Among those loyal and upright today, only Yelu Jue and Liu Shen!"

entries.zh: 宰相楊績賀其得人。
entries.en: Chancellor Yang Ji praised him for recognizing worthy men.
entries.literal: Chancellor Yang Ji congratulated him on getting the right men.

entries.zh: 拜參知政事。
entries.en: Shen was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs.
entries.literal: He was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs.

entries.zh: 上諭之曰：「卿勿憚宰相。」
entries.en: The emperor told him: "Do not hold back for fear of the chancellor."
entries.literal: The emperor instructed him, saying, "You, sir, need not fear the chancellor."

entries.zh: 時北院樞密使乙辛勢焰方熾，伸奏曰：「臣於乙辛尚不畏，何宰相之畏！」
entries.en: Yixin, Northern Privy Commissioner, was at the height of his power; Shen replied: "If I do not fear Yixin, why should I fear the chancellor?"
entries.literal: At that time Northern Chancellery Privy Commissioner Yixin's power and flame were just blazing; Shen memorialized, saying, "Your subject does not even fear Yixin—why fear the chancellor!"

entries.zh: 乙辛銜之，相與排詆，出為保靜軍節度使。
entries.en: Yixin took offense; he and his allies smeared Shen and had him sent out as military commissioner of Baojing Army.
entries.literal: Yixin harbored resentment; together they slandered and drove him out as military commissioner of Baojing Army.

entries.zh: 上終欲大用，加守太子太保，遷上京留守。
entries.en: The emperor still meant to use him at the highest level: Shen was given the honorary title Guardian Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and made regent of the Upper Capital.
entries.literal: The emperor in the end wished to employ him greatly; he was given the added title Guardian Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to regent of the Upper Capital.

entries.zh: 乙辛以事徙鎮雄武，復以崇義軍節度使致仕。
entries.en: Yixin was transferred to Xiongwu on account of his offenses; Liu Shen retired once more, retaining the honorary rank of military commissioner of Chongyi Army.
entries.literal: Yixin, because of a matter, was transferred to command Xiongwu; Shen again retired with the rank of military commissioner of Chongyi Army.

entries.zh: 適燕、薊民饑，伸與致政趙徽、韓造日濟以糜粥，所活不勝算。
entries.en: Just then famine struck Yan and Ji; Shen, together with the retired officials Zhao Hui and Han Zao, distributed porridge daily and saved countless lives.
entries.literal: When Yan and Ji peoples suffered famine, Shen together with retired Zhao Hui and Han Zao daily supplied porridge; those saved cannot be counted.

entries.zh: 大安二年卒，上震悼，賻贈加等。
entries.en: In Da'an 2 he died; the emperor was deeply grieved and granted enhanced funeral gifts and posthumous honors.
entries.literal: In the second year of Da'an he died; the emperor was shaken and grieved, and funeral gifts and posthumous rewards were increased by degrees.

entries.zh: 論曰：兀納當道宗昏惑之會，擁佑皇孫，使乙辛奸計不獲復逞，而遼祚以續，比之屋質立穆宗，非溢美也。
entries.en: The historians comment: At a moment when Daozong had lost his judgment, Wuna protected the imperial grandson and blocked Yixin's treachery from running its course, thereby preserving the Liao succession. To compare him with Yelu Wuzhi's elevation of Muzong is no flattery.
entries.literal: Comment: Wuna, at the time when Daozong was confused and deluded, supported and protected the imperial grandson, causing Yixin's treacherous scheme not to obtain display again, and the Liao line thereby continued—compared to Wuzhi establishing Muzong, this is no excess of praise.

entries.zh: 儼以俊才蒞政，所至有能譽，纂述遼史，具一代治亂，亦云勤矣，但其固寵，不能以禮正家，惜哉。
entries.en: Yan governed with outstanding talent and won a reputation for competence wherever he served; his compilation of the History of Liao, recording an entire age of order and disorder, shows real diligence as well—yet he secured imperial favor through his wife's conduct in the inner palace rather than by keeping his household in ritual order. A pity.
entries.literal: Yan, with outstanding talent administering government, wherever he arrived had reputation for ability; compiling and describing the History of Liao, fully treating one generation's order and chaos, may also be called diligent—but his securing favor, unable to correct the household by ritual, alas.

entries.zh: 劉伸三為大理，民無冤抑，一登戶部，上下兼裕，至與耶律玦並稱忠直，不亦宜乎！
entries.en: Liu Shen thrice held the Court of Justice and left the people free of wrongful oppression; once at the head of the Households Bureau he filled both imperial and local coffers; that he should stand with Yelu Jue among the loyal and upright—is that not exactly as it should be?
entries.literal: Liu Shen thrice served at the Court of Justice, the people without wronged oppression; one ascent to the Households Bureau, upper and lower both ample; reaching being named together with Yelu Jue as loyal and upright—is it not fitting!

entries.zh: 蕭兀納，一名撻不也，字特免，六院部人。
entries.en: Xiao Wuna, also known as Tabuye, courtesy name Te Mian, was from the Six Yuan Division.
entries.literal: Xiao Wuna, also named Tabuye, style Te Mian, a man of the Six Yuan Division.

entries.zh: 其先嘗為西南面拽剌。
entries.en: An ancestor of his had once held the post of zhuala on the Southwestern Route.
entries.literal: His forebear had once served as zhuala of the Southwestern Route.

entries.zh: 兀納魁偉簡重，善騎射。
entries.en: Wuna was tall and imposing, plainspoken and dignified, and excelled at mounted archery.
entries.literal: Wuna was tall and imposing, plain and grave, skilled at mounted archery.

entries.zh: 清寧初，兄圖獨以事入見，帝問族人可用者，圖獨以兀納對，補祗候郎君。
entries.en: Early in Qingning, his elder brother Tuduo came to court on business; when the emperor asked which relatives might serve, Tuduo named Wuna, and Wuna was appointed an attendant gentleman.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, his elder brother Tuduo entered audience on business; the emperor asked which clansmen were usable, Tuduo answered with Wuna, and he was appointed attendant gentleman.

entries.zh: 遷近侍敞史，護衛太保。
entries.en: He rose to inner attendant recorder and then Guardian Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be inner attendant recorder, then Guardian Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 大康初，為北院宣徽使。
entries.en: At the start of Dakang he was made Northern Court Commissioner of the Imperial Household.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, he became Northern Court Commissioner of the Imperial Household.

entries.zh: 時乙辛巳害太子，因言宋魏國王和魯斡之子淳可為儲嗣。
entries.en: Yixin had already destroyed the crown prince and now argued that Chun, son of Heluwo, Prince of Wei of Song, ought to be named heir.
entries.literal: At that time Yixin had already harmed the crown prince, and therefore proposed that Chun, son of Song Prince of Wei Heluwo, could serve as heir designate.

entries.zh: 群臣莫敢言，唯兀納及夷離畢蕭陶隗諫曰：「舍嫡不立，是以國與人也。」
entries.en: No one else among the ministers dared object; only Wuna and Yilibi Xiao Taowei spoke up: "To pass over the legitimate heir is to hand the realm to outsiders."
entries.literal: None of the officials dared speak; only Wuna and Yilibi Xiao Taowei remonstrated, saying, "To set aside the legitimate heir and not establish him is to give the state to others."

entries.zh: 帝猶豫不決。
entries.en: The emperor wavered, unable to decide.
entries.literal: The emperor hesitated and could not decide.

entries.zh: 五年，帝出獵，乙辛請留皇孫，帝欲從之。
entries.en: In the fifth year the emperor went hunting; Yixin asked to keep the imperial grandson at court, and the emperor was inclined to consent.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, the emperor went out hunting; Yixin asked that the imperial grandson be left behind, and the emperor wished to agree.

entries.zh: 兀納奏曰：「竊聞車駕出遊，將留皇孫，茍保護非人，恐有他變。
entries.en: Wuna memorialized: "I understand Your Majesty is about to leave on tour while keeping the imperial grandson behind; if unsuitable men are charged with his protection, I fear disaster.
entries.literal: Wuna memorialized, saying, "I have heard privately that as the imperial carriage goes out on tour, the imperial grandson is to be left behind; if protection should fall to the wrong men, I fear there may be some other turn of events.

entries.zh: 果留，臣請侍左右。」
entries.en: If he stays behind, I beg leave to attend him in person."
entries.literal: If he is indeed left behind, your subject requests to wait at his side."

entries.zh: 帝乃悟，命皇孫從行。
entries.en: The emperor took his meaning and ordered the grandson to come along.
entries.literal: The emperor then understood and ordered the imperial grandson to accompany the journey.

entries.zh: 由此始疑乙辛。
entries.en: From that point the emperor began to doubt Yixin.
entries.literal: From this he first grew suspicious of Yixin.

entries.zh: 頃之，同知南院樞密使事，出乙辛、淳等。
entries.en: Soon afterward, serving as vice administrator of the Southern Chancellery Privy Council, he drove Yixin, Chun, and their faction from court.
entries.literal: Before long, as vice administrator of the Southern Chancellery Privy Council, he banished Yixin, Chun, and the rest.

entries.zh: 帝嘉其忠，封蘭陵郡王，人謂近於古社稷臣。
entries.en: The emperor praised his loyalty and enfeoffed him as Prince of Lanling; contemporaries said he resembled the loyal ministers of old who saved dynasties.
entries.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty, enfeoffed him Prince of Lanling Commandery, and people said he approached the ancient type of minister of state and altars.

entries.zh: 授殿前都點檢。
entries.en: He was appointed Chief Inspector of the Palace Guards.
entries.literal: He was appointed Chief Inspector of the Palace Guards.

entries.zh: 上謂王師儒、耶律固等曰：「兀納忠純，雖狄仁傑輔唐，屋質立穆宗，無以過也。
entries.en: The emperor told Wang Shiru, Yelu Gu, and others: "Wuna's loyalty is unstained. Not even Di Renjie's service to Tang, or Yelu Wuzhi's elevation of Muzong, exceeds what he has done.
entries.literal: The emperor said to Wang Shiru, Yelu Gu, and the others, "Wuna is loyal and pure; even Di Renjie assisting Tang, or Wuzhi establishing Muzong—none surpass him.

entries.zh: 卿等宜達燕王知之。」
entries.en: Tell the Prince of Yan, so that he knows how highly I esteem this."
entries.literal: You gentlemen should convey this to the Prince of Yan so that he knows."

entries.zh: 自是令兀納輔導燕王，益見優寵。
entries.en: From then on Wuna was assigned to guide the Prince of Yan and received even greater favor.
entries.literal: From then on Wuna was ordered to guide and instruct the Prince of Yan, and he received still greater favor.

entries.zh: 大安初，詔尚越國公主，兀納固辭。
entries.en: Early in Da'an he was commanded to marry the Princess of Yue, but Wuna steadfastly refused.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Da'an, an edict ordered him to marry the Princess of Yue, and Wuna firmly declined.

entries.zh: 改南院樞密使，奏請掾史宜以歲月行敘，從之。
entries.en: He was made Southern Chancellery Privy Commissioner and proposed that staff clerks be promoted according to seniority; the court agreed.
entries.literal: He was changed to Southern Chancellery Privy Commissioner; he memorialized that clerks should advance by length of service, and the request was granted.

entries.zh: 壽隆元年，拜北府宰相。
entries.en: In Shoulong 1 he was appointed chancellor of the Northern Court.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shoulong, he was appointed chancellor of the Northern Court.

entries.zh: 蕭兀納耶律儼劉伸耶律胡呂
entries.en: Xiao Wuna, Yelu Yan, Liu Shen, and Yelu Hulu
entries.literal: Xiao Wuna, Yelu Yan, Liu Shen, Yelu Hulu

entries.zh: 耶律胡呂，字蘇撒，弘義宮分人。
entries.en: Yelu Hulu, courtesy name Susa, was from the Hongyi Palace Division.
entries.literal: Yelu Hulu, style Susa, a man of the Hongyi Palace Division.

entries.zh: 其先欲穩，佐太祖有功，為叠烈部夷離堇。
entries.en: His ancestor Yiwen had aided Taizu with distinction and served as yilijin of the Dielie Division.
entries.literal: His forebear Yiwen assisted Taizu with merit and was yilijin of the Dielie Division.

entries.zh: 父楊五，左監門衛大將軍。
entries.en: His father Yang Wu was a general of the Left Gate Guards.
entries.literal: His father Yang Wu, General of the Left Gate Guards.

entries.zh: 胡呂性謙謹，於人無適莫。
entries.en: Hulu was modest and careful by nature and showed no partiality toward anyone.
entries.literal: Hulu by nature was modest and careful; toward people he had no favoring or shunning.

entries.zh: 重熙末，補寢殿小底。
entries.en: Late in Chongxi he was appointed a sleeping-hall attendant.
entries.literal: At the end of Chongxi he was appointed sleeping-hall attendant.

entries.zh: 以善職，屢更華要，遷千牛衛大將軍。
entries.en: For distinguished service he rose through one prestigious post after another and was promoted to general of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
entries.literal: For excellence in office he repeatedly changed to splendid and important posts, and was promoted to General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

entries.zh: 大安中，北阻卜酋磨魯斯叛，為招討都監，與耶律那也率精騎二千討平之，以功為漢人行宮副部署，兼知太和宮事。
entries.en: During Da'an the Northern Zhubu chieftain Molusi rebelled; Hulu served as supervising commissioner of the pacification campaign and, with Yelu Naye, led two thousand picked horsemen to crush the revolt; for this he was made vice deployment commissioner of the Han mobile palace and concurrently administrator of Taihe Palace.
entries.literal: In Da'an, the Northern Zhubu chieftain Molusi rebelled; he served as overall pacification supervising commissioner, together with Yelu Naye led two thousand picked horsemen to suppress and pacify them, and for merit became vice deployment commissioner of the Han Mobile Court, concurrently administering Taihe Palace affairs.

entries.zh: 致仕，加同中書門下平章事，卒。
entries.en: He retired with the added title of Co-Seal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and later died.
entries.literal: He retired, was given the added title Co-Seal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and died.

entries.zh: 蕭巖壽，乙室部人。
entries.en: Xiao Yanshou came from the Yishi tribe.
entries.literal: Xiao Yanshou was a man of the Yishi tribe.

entries.zh: 性剛直尚氣，仕重熙末。
entries.en: Upright and spirited by nature, he began his career late in the Chongxi reign.
entries.literal: By nature upright and proud of spirit; he entered office at the end of the Chongxi era.

entries.zh: 道宗即位，皇太后屢稱其賢，由是進用。
entries.en: After Emperor Daozong acceded, the Empress Dowager repeatedly praised his merit, and he was promoted on that account.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong took the throne, the Empress Dowager repeatedly praised his worth; thereby he was advanced and employed.

entries.zh: 上出獵較，巖壽典其事，未嘗高下於心，帝益重之。
entries.en: Whenever the emperor went out hunting for sport, Yanshou managed the arrangements without favoritism, which deepened the emperor's regard for him.
entries.literal: When the emperor went out to hunt and compete, Yanshou directed the affair, never playing favorites in his heart; the emperor valued him all the more.

entries.zh: 歷文班太保、同知樞密院事。
entries.en: He rose through the posts of Grand Guardian of the Literary Office and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: He successively served as Grand Guardian of the Literary Office and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 咸雍四年，從耶律仁先伐阻卜，破之，有詔留屯，亡歸者眾，由是鐫兩官。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Xianyong he joined Yelu Renxian's campaign against the Zubu; after their defeat he was ordered to hold the frontier, but so many men deserted that he was demoted two ranks.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xianyong, he followed Yelu Renxian in attacking the Zubu and defeated them; there was an edict to remain and garrison; those who fled back were many; on this account two ranks were cut from him.

entries.zh: 十年，討敵烈部有功，為其部節度使。
entries.en: In the tenth year he campaigned successfully against the Dilie tribe and was appointed its military commissioner.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, he attacked the Dilie tribe with merit and became military commissioner of that tribe.

entries.zh: 大康元年，同知南院宣徽使事，遷北面林牙。
entries.en: In the first year of Dakang he became vice director of the Southern Directorate for Palace Provisions and was transferred to Northern Imperial Scribe.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dakang, he served as vice director of the Southern Chancellery Directorate for Palace Provisions and was transferred to Northern Imperial Scribe.

entries.zh: 密奏乙辛以皇太子知國政，心不自安，與張孝傑數相過從，恐有陰謀，動搖太子。
entries.en: In a secret memorial he warned that Yelu Yixin, uneasy now that the crown prince governed state affairs, was meeting Zhang Xiaojie repeatedly and might be plotting against the heir.
entries.literal: In a secret memorial he reported that because the Crown Prince administered state affairs, Yixin was ill at ease, met often with Zhang Xiaojie, and he feared there was a covert plot to shake the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 上悟，出乙辛為中京留守。
entries.en: The emperor took the point and posted Yixin as regent (liushou) of Zhongjing.
entries.literal: The emperor understood, and sent Yixin out as military commissioner at Zhongjing.

entries.zh: 會乙辛生日，上遣近臣耶律白斯本賜物為壽，乙辛因私屬白上：「臣見奸人在朝，陛下孤危。
entries.en: On Yixin's birthday the emperor sent the courtier Yelu Baisiben with gifts; Yixin asked him privately to tell the throne, "I see villains at court and Your Majesty isolated in danger.
entries.literal: It happened to be Yixin's birthday; the emperor sent the close minister Yelu Aisiben to present gifts in congratulation. Yixin privately entrusted him to tell the emperor: "Your servant sees wicked men in court; Your Majesty stands alone in peril.

entries.zh: 身雖在外，竊用寒心。」
entries.en: Though I am away from court, I cannot stop worrying for your safety."
entries.literal: Though my person is outside, within I feel cold at heart."

entries.zh: 白斯本還，以聞。
entries.en: When Baisiben returned he reported this to the emperor.
entries.literal: Aisiben returned and reported it.

entries.zh: 上遣人賜乙辛車，諭曰：「無慮弗用，行將召矣。」
entries.en: The emperor sent Yixin a carriage with the message, "Have no fear—I shall summon you back soon."
entries.literal: The emperor sent someone to bestow a carriage on Yixin, instructing him: "Do not worry and do not decline; soon you will be recalled."

entries.zh: 由是反疑巖壽，出為順義軍節度使。
entries.en: From this the emperor instead grew suspicious of Yanshou and appointed him military commissioner of the Shunyi Army.
entries.literal: Thereby he came instead to suspect Yanshou and sent him out as military commissioner of the Shunyi Army.

entries.zh: 乙辛復入為樞密使，流巖壽於烏隗路，終身拘作。
entries.en: Yixin was brought back as Bureau Commissioner; Yanshou was banished to Wulilu for lifelong corvée labor.
entries.literal: Yixin returned and became bureau commissioner; Yanshou was exiled to Wulilu and put to lifelong compulsory labor.

entries.zh: 巖壽雖竄逐，恒以社稷為憂，時人為之語曰：「以狼牧羊，何能久長！」
entries.en: Even in exile he never ceased to anguish over the realm, and people said, "A wolf herding sheep cannot last long!"
entries.literal: Though Yanshou was driven off, he constantly grieved for the altars of state. People of the time made a saying of it: "Using a wolf to herd sheep—how can it last long!"

entries.zh: 三年，乙辛誣巖壽與謀廢立事，執還殺之，年四十九。
entries.en: In the third year Yixin accused him of plotting to depose the emperor and enthrone another; he was seized, brought back, and executed at forty-nine.
entries.literal: In the third year, Yixin framed Yanshou for plotting deposition and enthronement; he was seized, brought back, and killed—aged forty-nine.

entries.zh: 論曰：《易》言「履霜，堅冰至」，謹始也。
entries.en: Commentary: The Book of Changes says, "When frost is underfoot, solid ice is not far behind"—a warning to be careful at the outset.
entries.literal: The commentary says: The Book of Changes says, "Treading on frost, solid ice arrives"—this is caution at the beginning.

entries.zh: 使道宗能從巖壽、撒剌之諫，後何得而誣，太子何得而廢哉？
entries.en: Had Emperor Daozong heeded Yanshou and Sala, how could those frame-ups have followed, or the crown prince been deposed?
entries.literal: If Emperor Daozong could have followed the remonstrances of Yanshou and Sala, how could there later have been framing accusations, how could the Crown Prince have been deposed?

entries.zh: 速撒、撻不也以忠言見殺，國欲無亂，得乎？
entries.en: Susa and Tabuye were slain for honest counsel—could the realm hope to escape turmoil after that?
entries.literal: Susa and Tabuye were killed for loyal words—could the state wish to be without disorder and achieve it?

entries.zh: 石柳之書，亦幸出於乙辛既敗之後，獲行其說。
entries.en: Shiliu's memorial, fortunately submitted only after Yixin's fall, at least found partial fulfillment.
entries.literal: Shiliu's memorial also fortunately appeared after Yixin had already been defeated, and thus his argument could be carried out.

entries.zh: 有國家者，可不知人哉！
entries.en: Can any ruler afford not to know his men!
entries.literal: One who possesses a state—how can he not know men!

entries.zh: 臣前為奸臣所陷，斥竄邊郡。
entries.en: Your servant was once framed by wicked ministers and banished to a frontier commandery.
entries.literal: Your servant was formerly framed by wicked ministers and driven off to a frontier commandery.

entries.zh: 幸蒙召用，不敢隱默。
entries.en: Having been fortunate enough to be recalled to service, I dare not hold my tongue.
entries.literal: Fortunately I have been favored with recall and employment; I dare not conceal and remain silent.

entries.zh: 恩賞明則賢者勸，刑罰當則奸人消。
entries.en: When rewards are clear the worthy are encouraged; when punishments are just the wicked vanish.
entries.literal: When favors and rewards are clear, the worthy are encouraged; when punishments are fitting, wicked men disappear.

entries.zh: 二者既舉，天下不勞而治。
entries.en: When both are in place, the realm is governed without strain.
entries.literal: Once these two are carried out, all under Heaven is governed without labor.

entries.zh: 臣見耶律乙辛身出寒微，位居樞要，竊權肆惡，不勝名狀。
entries.en: I have seen Yelu Yixin rise from humble origins to a pivotal post, usurp power, and commit outrages beyond naming.
entries.literal: Your servant has seen Yelu Yixin, though born of humble origins, occupy a pivotal post, usurp power and unleash wickedness beyond what can be named.

entries.zh: 蔽先帝之明，誣陷順聖，構害忠讜，敗國罔上，自古所無。
entries.en: He blinded the late emperor, falsely condemned Emperor Shunsheng, destroyed loyal remonstrators, and ruined the state while deceiving his sovereign—crimes without precedent.
entries.literal: He obscured the late emperor's judgment, falsely condemned Emperor Shunsheng, plotted against loyal remonstrators, ruined the state, and deceived his sovereign—crimes without precedent.

entries.zh: 賴廟社之休，陛下獲纂成業，積年之冤，一旦洗雪。
entries.en: By the grace of the ancestral temples Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne, and wrongs that festered for years may at last be redressed.
entries.literal: Relying on the blessing of the ancestral temples and altars, Your Majesty has succeeded to the completed enterprise; wrongs accumulated over years were in one day washed clean.

entries.zh: 正陛下英斷，克成孝道之秋。
entries.en: This is precisely the moment for Your Majesty's decisive rule to fulfill filial duty.
entries.literal: It is just when Your Majesty's keen decisiveness can fully accomplish the season of filial piety.

entries.zh: 如蕭得裏特實乙辛之黨，耶律合魯亦不為早辨，賴陛下之明，遂正其事。
entries.en: Xiao Delite was truly of Yixin's party, and Yelu Helu failed to expose this in time; only Your Majesty's discernment set the matter right.
entries.literal: For example, Xiao Delite was in truth of Yixin's faction, and Yelu Helu also did not distinguish the matter early; relying on Your Majesty's clarity, the affair was then set right.

entries.zh: 臣見陛下多疑，故有司顧望，不切推問。
entries.en: I fear Your Majesty's excessive caution leaves officials hesitant and unwilling to pursue the case vigorously.
entries.literal: Your servant sees that Your Majesty is overly doubtful; therefore the responsible offices look about and hesitate, and do not press the inquiry keenly.

entries.zh: 乙辛在先帝朝，權寵無比。
entries.en: Under the late emperor Yixin's power and favor were unrivaled.
entries.literal: Yixin in the Former Emperor's court had power and favor without parallel.

entries.zh: 先帝若以順考為實，則乙辛為功臣，陛下豈得立耶？
entries.en: If the late emperor had believed the accusations against your late father, Yixin would count as a meritorious minister—how then could Your Majesty have ascended the throne?
entries.literal: If the late emperor had believed the accusations against your late father to be true, then Yixin would have been a meritorious minister—how could Your Majesty have been established?

entries.zh: 先帝黜逐嬖後，詔陛下在左右，是亦悔前非也。
entries.en: The late emperor dismissed his favorite consort and kept Your Majesty at his side—itself a sign he regretted his earlier error.
entries.literal: The Former Emperor drove off the favorite consort and ordered Your Majesty to remain at his side—this too was repentance for former error.

entries.zh: 陛下詎可忘父讎不報，寬逆黨不誅？
entries.en: How can Your Majesty leave your father's wrongs unavenged and spare the traitorous faction unpunished?
entries.literal: How can Your Majesty forget your father's enmity unavenged and pardon the rebellious faction unpunished?

entries.zh: 今靈骨未獲，而求之不切。
entries.en: Her remains have yet to be recovered, yet the search is pursued without urgency.
entries.literal: Now her sacred bones have not been recovered, yet the search for them is not keen.

entries.zh: 《傳》曰，聖人之德，無加於孝。
entries.en: The Zhuan says that among a sage's virtues none surpasses filial piety.
entries.literal: The Zhuan says: among the sage's virtues, none surpasses filial piety.

entries.zh: 昔唐德宗因亂失母，思慕悲傷，孝道益著。
entries.en: Tang Dezong once lost his mother in the turmoil of rebellion; his longing and grief made his filial devotion all the more renowned.
entries.literal: Formerly Tang Dezong, through disorder, lost his mother; in longing and grief his filial piety became all the more manifest.

entries.zh: 周公誅飛廉、惡來，天下大悅。
entries.en: When the Duke of Zhou executed Feilian and Elai, the realm rejoiced.
entries.literal: The Duke of Zhou executed Feilian and Elai, and all under Heaven were greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 今逆黨未除，大冤不報，上無以慰順考之靈，下無以釋天下之憤。
entries.en: The traitorous faction still stands unpunished and the great wrong unavenged; your late father's spirit finds no comfort, and the people's outrage finds no release.
entries.literal: Now the rebellious faction has not been removed and the great wrong has not been avenged; above, there is no means to console the spirit of your late father, and below, no means to release the anger of all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 怨氣上結，水旱為沴。
entries.en: Resentment gathers toward heaven, and flood and drought follow as portents.
entries.literal: Resentment's qi rises and knots; flood and drought become calamities.

entries.zh: 臣願陛下下明詔，求順考之瘞所，盡收逆黨以正邦憲，快四方忠義之心，昭國家賞罰之用，然後致治之道可得而舉矣。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to issue a clear edict, find your late father's burial place, apprehend the entire traitorous faction to uphold the law, satisfy loyal subjects everywhere, and make the state's rewards and punishments plain—only then can good governance truly be pursued.
entries.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to issue a clear edict, seek the burial place of your late father, fully apprehend the rebellious faction to rectify the laws of the state, satisfy the hearts of the loyal and righteous in the four quarters, and make manifest the state's use of rewards and punishments—then the way of bringing order may be taken up and carried out.

entries.zh: 謹別錄順聖升遐及乙辛等事，昧死以聞。
entries.en: I respectfully attach a separate record of Emperor Shunsheng's death and Yixin's crimes, and risk my life to lay this before Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Respectfully I separately record the death of Emperor Shunsheng and matters concerning Yixin and the others, risking death to report.

entries.zh: 耶律石柳，字酬宛，六院部人。
entries.en: Yelu Shiliu, whose style was Chouwan, came from the Six Chancelleries tribe.
entries.literal: Yelu Shiliu, styled Chouwan, was a man of the Six Chancelleries tribe.

entries.zh: 祖獨攧，南院大王。
entries.en: His grandfather Duzhan had been Great King of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: His grandfather Duzhan was Great King of the Southern Chancellery.

entries.zh: 父安十，統軍副使。
entries.en: His father Anshi had served as deputy army commissioner.
entries.literal: His father Anshi was deputy commissioner of the army command.

entries.zh: 石柳性剛直，有經世誌。
entries.en: Shiliu was upright and unyielding, with a statesman's ambition.
entries.literal: Shiliu was by nature upright and unyielding, with the will to order the age.

entries.zh: 始為牌印郎君。
entries.en: He began his career as Seal and Patent Gentleman.
entries.literal: He first served as Seal and Patent Gentleman.

entries.zh: 大康初，為夷離畢郎君。
entries.en: Early in Dakang he was made Yilibi Gentleman.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, he became Yilibi Gentleman.

entries.zh: 時樞密使耶律乙辛誣殺皇后，謀廢太子，斥忠賢，進奸黨，石柳惡其所為，乙辛覺之。
entries.en: Bureau Commissioner Yelu Yixin had framed the empress for execution, plotted to depose the crown prince, banished the loyal, and advanced his faction; Shiliu loathed these acts, and Yixin took notice.
entries.literal: At that time Bureau Commissioner Yelu Yixin had framed and killed the empress, plotted to depose the Crown Prince, driven out the loyal and worthy, and advanced wicked factions; Shiliu detested his conduct, and Yixin became aware of it.

entries.zh: 太子既廢，以石柳附太子，流鎮州。
entries.en: After the crown prince was deposed, Shiliu was judged a partisan of the heir and banished to Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: Once the Crown Prince was deposed, Shiliu was deemed attached to the Crown Prince and exiled to Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 天祚即位，召為御史中丞。
entries.en: When Emperor Tianzuo acceded he was recalled as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: When Tianzuo took the throne, he was summoned as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 時方治乙辛黨，有司不以為意。
entries.en: The court was supposed to be prosecuting Yixin's faction, yet the responsible offices treated the matter lightly.
entries.literal: At that time they were just then prosecuting Yixin's faction, but the responsible offices paid it no heed.

entries.zh: 石柳上書曰：
entries.en: Shiliu submitted a memorial that read:
entries.literal: Shiliu submitted a memorial, saying:

entries.zh: 耶律撒剌，字堇隱，南院大王磨魯古之孫。
entries.en: Yelu Sala, whose style was Jinyin, was a grandson of the Southern Chancellery King Molugu.
entries.literal: Yelu Sala, styled Jinyin, was grandson of Molugu, the Southern Chancellery King.

entries.zh: 性忠直沈厚。
entries.en: He was loyal, upright, and grave in character.
entries.literal: By nature loyal, upright, deep, and substantial.

entries.zh: 清寧初，累遷西南面招討使，以治稱。
entries.en: Early in Qingning he rose through posts to Southwest Pacification Commissioner and won renown for his administration.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning he was repeatedly promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest and was famed for his governance.

entries.zh: 咸雍九年，改北院大王。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Xianyong he was made Great King of the Northern Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Xianyong, he was transferred to Great King of the Northern Chancellery.

entries.zh: 未幾，為契丹行宮都部署。
entries.en: Soon after he became chief deployment officer of the Khitan itinerant palace.
entries.literal: Before long, he became chief deployment officer of the Khitan itinerant palace.

entries.zh: 大康二年，耶律乙辛為中京留守，詔百官廷議，欲復召之，群臣無敢正言。
entries.en: In the second year of Dakang, with Yelu Yixin as regent of Zhongjing, the court deliberated recalling him—yet none of the ministers dared speak plainly.
entries.literal: In the second year of Dakang, Yelu Yixin was military commissioner at Zhongjing; an edict called the hundred officials to court deliberation, wishing to recall him again; none of the ministers dared speak frankly.

entries.zh: 撒剌獨奏曰：「蕭巖壽言乙辛有罪，不可為樞臣，故陛下出之；
entries.en: Sala alone memorialized, "Xiao Yanshou showed Yixin guilty of crimes unfit for a bureau chief, and Your Majesty sent him away;
entries.literal: Sala alone submitted: "Xiao Yanshou said Yixin had guilt and could not serve as bureau minister, so Your Majesty sent him out;

entries.zh: 今復召，恐天下生疑。」
entries.en: To summon him back now will only breed suspicion throughout the realm."
entries.literal: if he is now recalled, I fear the empire will grow doubtful."

entries.zh: 進諫者三，不納，左右為之震悚。
entries.en: He pressed his advice three times without success; those around the throne trembled at his boldness.
entries.literal: He advanced remonstrance three times; it was not accepted; those left and right were shaken in awe for him.

entries.zh: 乙辛復為樞密使，見撒剌，讓曰：「與君無憾，何獨異議？」
entries.en: When Yixin returned as commissioner he confronted Sala: "I bear you no personal grudge—why stand alone in opposition?"
entries.literal: Yixin again became bureau commissioner; seeing Sala, he reproached him: "Between us there is no resentment—why oppose alone?"

entries.zh: 撒剌曰：「此社稷計，何憾之有！」
entries.en: Sala replied, "This concerns the fate of the state, not private resentment!"
entries.literal: Sala said: "This is a plan for the altars of state—what resentment is there!"

entries.zh: 乙辛誣撒剌與速撒同謀廢立，詔按無跡，出為始平軍節度使。
entries.en: Yixin accused Sala and Susa of plotting deposition; though the inquiry found nothing, Sala was posted as military commissioner of Shiping.
entries.literal: Yixin framed Sala and Susa as jointly plotting deposition and enthronement; an edict investigated and found no trace; he was sent out as military commissioner of the Shiping Army.

entries.zh: 及蕭訛都斡誣首，竟遣使殺之。
entries.en: When Xiao Eduogan corroborated the frame-up, an envoy was finally sent to execute him.
entries.literal: When Xiao Eduogan made the false accuser's confession, in the end an envoy was sent to kill him.

entries.zh: 乾統間，追封漆水郡王，繪像宜福殿，仍追贈三子官爵。
entries.en: Under Qiantong he was posthumously made Prince of Qishui, his portrait placed in Yifu Hall, and his three sons granted posthumous ranks.
entries.literal: During Qiantong, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qishui and his portrait painted in Yifu Hall; his three sons' offices and titles were also posthumously granted.

entries.zh: 蕭巖壽耶律撒剌蕭速撒耶律撻不也蕭撻不也蕭忽古耶律石柳
entries.en: Xiao Yanshou, Yelu Sala, Xiao Susa, Yelu Tabuye, Xiao Tabuye, Xiao Hugu, and Yelu Shiliu
entries.literal: Xiao Yanshou, Yelu Sala, Xiao Susa, Yelu Tabuye, Xiao Tabuye, Xiao Hugu, Yelu Shiliu

entries.zh: 耶律章奴，字特末衍，季父房之後。
entries.en: Yelü Zhangnu, whose courtesy name was Temoyan, came from the Younger Father branch of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Yelü Zhangnu, courtesy name Temoyan, was a descendant of the Younger Father branch.

entries.zh: 父查剌，養高不仕。
entries.en: His father Zhala lived in cultivated seclusion and never took office.
entries.literal: His father Zhala lived in lofty retirement and did not take office.

entries.zh: 章奴明敏善談論。
entries.en: Zhangnu was quick-witted and an able debater.
entries.literal: Zhangnu was bright and quick and skilled in discourse.

entries.zh: 大安中，補牌印郎君。
entries.en: During the Da'an reign he entered service as a seal-and-signet langjun.
entries.literal: In the Da'an era he was appointed a seal-and-signet langjun.

entries.zh: 乾統元年，累遷右中丞，兼領牌印宿直事。
entries.en: In the first year of Qiantong he rose in due course to right vice censor-in-chief and was also put in charge of palace seal-and-signet night duty.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qiantong he was promoted in succession to right vice censor-in-chief and concurrently directed palace seal-and-signet night duty.

entries.zh: 六年，以直宿不謹，降知內客省事。
entries.en: In the sixth year, for negligence on night duty, he was demoted to director of the Inner Guests Office.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, for laxity on night duty, he was demoted to director of the Inner Guests Office.

entries.zh: 天慶四年，授東北路統軍副使。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Tianqing he was made deputy commander of the Northeast Route army.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqing he was appointed deputy commander of the Northeast Route army.

entries.zh: 五年，改同知咸州路兵馬事。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was reassigned as associate commissioner of military affairs on the Xianzhou Route.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to associate commissioner of military affairs on the Xianzhou Route.

entries.zh: 及天祚親征女直，蕭胡篤為先鋒都統，章奴為都監。
entries.en: When Tianzuo led a personal campaign against the Jurchen, Xiao Hudu was made vanguard supreme commander and Zhangnu army inspector.
entries.literal: When Tianzuo personally campaigned against the Jurchen, Xiao Hudu served as vanguard supreme commander and Zhangnu as army inspector.

entries.zh: 大軍渡鴨子河，章奴與魏國王淳妻兄蕭敵裏及其甥蕭延留等謀立淳，誘將卒三百餘人亡歸。
entries.en: As the main army crossed the Yazi River, Zhangnu joined with Xiao Dili, elder brother of Prince of Wei Chun's wife, and his nephew Xiao Yanliu and others in a plot to enthrone Chun, persuading more than three hundred officers and men to desert and march home.
entries.literal: When the great army crossed the Yazi River, Zhangnu, with the elder brother of Prince of Wei Kingdom Chun's wife Xiao Dili and his nephew Xiao Yanliu and others, plotted to set up Chun and induced more than three hundred officers and soldiers to desert and return.

entries.zh: 既而天祚為女直所敗，章奴乃遣敵裏、延留以廢立事馳報淳。
entries.en: When Tianzuo was soon after defeated by the Jurchen, Zhangnu dispatched Dili and Yanliu to carry word of the planned deposition and enthronement to Chun.
entries.literal: Soon afterward Tianzuo was defeated by the Jurchen; Zhangnu then sent Dili and Yanliu to report the deposition-and-enthronement affair in haste to Chun.

entries.zh: 淳猶豫未決。
entries.en: Chun hesitated and could not bring himself to decide.
entries.literal: Chun hesitated and could not decide.

entries.zh: 會行宮使者乙信持天祚御劄至，備言章奴叛命，淳對使者號哭，即斬敵裏、延留首以獻天祚。
entries.en: Just then the mobile-palace envoy Yixin arrived with an imperial rescript from Tianzuo detailing Zhangnu's treason; Chun wept before the envoy and immediately beheaded Dili and Yanliu, sending their heads to Tianzuo.
entries.literal: It happened that the mobile-palace envoy Yixin arrived bearing Tianzuo's imperial rescript, setting forth Zhangnu's rebellious orders in full; Chun wept before the envoy and at once beheaded Dili and Yanliu and presented their heads to Tianzuo.

entries.zh: 章奴見淳不從，誘草寇數百攻掠上京，取府庫財物。
entries.en: When Chun refused to join him, Zhangnu rallied several hundred marauders to raid the Upper Capital and seize the treasury stores.
entries.literal: Seeing that Chun would not follow him, Zhangnu induced several hundred bandits to attack and plunder the Upper Capital and seize the wealth of the treasury.

entries.zh: 至祖州，率僚屬告太祖廟云：「我大遼基業，由太祖百戰而成。
entries.en: At Zu Prefecture he led his officers before the temple of Taizu and declared, "The foundation of our Great Liao was won through the hundred battles of Taizu.
entries.literal: Reaching Zu Prefecture, he led his subordinate officials to announce at the temple of Taizu, saying, "The foundation of our Great Liao was achieved through the hundred battles of Taizu.

entries.zh: 今天下土崩，竊見興宗皇帝孫魏國王淳道德隆厚，能理世安民，臣等欲立以主社稷。
entries.en: Now the realm is crumbling; we have seen that Emperor Xingzong's grandson, Prince of Wei Chun, is a man of deep virtue who can govern the age and bring peace to the people, and we wish to set him up to rule the state.
entries.literal: Today the realm is collapsing; we have observed that Xingzong Emperor's grandson, Prince of Wei Kingdom Chun, is of lofty virtue and thick moral weight and can govern the age and settle the people—we your servants wish to set him up to preside over the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 會淳適好草甸，大事未遂。
entries.en: But Chun happened to be away on the grasslands at sport, and the great design came to nothing.
entries.literal: It happened that Chun was just then enjoying the grassland marshalling grounds, and the great affair was not accomplished.

entries.zh: 邇來天祚惟耽樂是從，不恤萬機。
entries.en: Of late Tianzuo has given himself only to pleasure and neglected the affairs of government.
entries.literal: Of late Tianzuo has followed only indulgence in pleasure and does not attend to the myriad affairs of state.

entries.zh: 強敵肆侮，師徒敗績。
entries.en: A powerful foe presses the borders, and our armies suffer defeat after defeat.
entries.literal: A powerful enemy rampages in insult, and the army meets defeat.

entries.zh: 加以盜賊蜂起，邦國危於累卵。
entries.en: Bandits rise everywhere, and the state stands in peril as fragile as a tower of eggs.
entries.literal: Added to this, bandits swarm forth like bees, and the state is in danger like a pile of eggs.

entries.zh: 臣等忝預族屬，世蒙恩渥，上欲安九廟之靈，下欲救萬民之命，乃有此舉。
entries.en: We, though unworthy members of the imperial clan, have received grace through generations; above we seek to secure the spirits of the ancestral temples, below we seek to save the lives of the people—this is why we have taken this step.
entries.literal: We your servants are unworthy to share in the imperial clan yet have received favor through the generations; above we wish to settle the spirits of the nine temples, below we wish to save the lives of the myriad people—therefore we have undertaken this act.

entries.zh: 實出至誠，冀累聖垂佑。」
entries.en: Our purpose is wholly sincere, and we pray that the successive sage emperors will grant their blessing."
entries.literal: It truly springs from utmost sincerity, and we hope the successive sages will extend their protection."

entries.zh: 西至慶州，復祀諸廟，仍述所以舉兵之意，移檄州縣、諸陵官僚，士卒稍稍屬心。
entries.en: He marched west to Qing Prefecture, sacrificed again at the various temples, reiterated his reasons for taking up arms, and sent proclamations to the prefectures, counties, and tomb officials; soldiers gradually rallied to his cause.
entries.literal: Going west to Qing Prefecture, he again sacrificed at the various temples, still setting forth the reasons for raising troops, and issued proclamations to the prefectures and counties and the officials of the imperial tombs; soldiers gradually gave him their hearts.

entries.zh: 時饒州渤海及侯概等相繼來應，眾至數萬，趨廣平澱。
entries.en: The Bohai of Rao Prefecture, Hou Kai, and others then came over one after another; his force swelled to tens of thousands and marched toward Guangping Marsh.
entries.literal: At that time the Bohai of Rao Prefecture and Hou Kai and others came to join him in succession; the host reached tens of thousands and pressed toward Guangping Marsh.

entries.zh: 其黨耶律女古等暴橫不法，劫掠婦女財畜。
entries.en: His followers, including Yelü Nügu, grew violent and lawless, seizing women, livestock, and goods.
entries.literal: Among his faction Yelü Nügu and others were violent, lawless, and overbearing, plundering women and livestock and goods.

entries.zh: 章奴度不能制，內懷悔恨；
entries.en: Zhangnu saw he could not control them and was filled with remorse;
entries.literal: Zhangnu judged that he could not control them and inwardly harbored regret;

entries.zh: 又攻上京不克，北走降虜。
entries.en: he then failed to take the Upper Capital and fled north to surrender to the enemy.
entries.literal: again he attacked the Upper Capital without success and fled north to surrender to the enemy.

entries.zh: 順國女直阿鶻產率兵追敗之，殺其將耶律彌裏直，擒貴族二百餘人，其妻子配役繡院，或散諸近侍為婢；
entries.en: The Shunguo Jurchen Ahechan pursued him, routed his force, killed his general Yelü Milizhi, and captured more than two hundred nobles; their wives and children were sent to labor in the embroidery bureau or distributed among the palace attendants as servants;
entries.literal: The Shunguo Jurchen Ahechan led troops in pursuit, defeated him, killed his general Yelü Milizhi, and captured more than two hundred nobles; their wives and children were assigned to labor in the embroidery bureau or dispersed among the close attendants as maids;

entries.zh: 余得脫者皆遁去。
entries.en: those who escaped fled in all directions.
entries.literal: those among the remainder who escaped all fled away.

entries.zh: 章奴詐為使者，欲奔女直，為邏者所獲，縛送行在，伏誅。
entries.en: Zhangnu disguised himself as an envoy and tried to flee to the Jurchen, but patrols seized him, bound him, and sent him to the mobile court, where he was put to death.
entries.literal: Zhangnu pretended to be an envoy and wished to flee to the Jurchen; he was seized by patrols, bound, and sent to the mobile court, where he was executed.

entries.zh: 耶律術者，字能典，於越蒲古只之後，魁偉雄辨。
entries.en: Yelü Paizhe, whose courtesy name was Nengdian, was descended from Yuyue Puguzhi; he was imposing in stature and forceful in debate.
entries.literal: Yelü Paizhe, courtesy name Nengdian, was a descendant of Yuyue Puguzhi, imposing in stature and bold in debate.

entries.zh: 乾統初，補祗候郎君。
entries.en: Early in the Qiantong reign he entered service as an attendant langjun.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qiantong he was appointed an attendant langjun.

entries.zh: 六年，因柴冊，加觀察使。
entries.en: In the sixth year, for his service at the firewood-register ceremony, he was promoted to investigation commissioner.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, on account of the firewood-register ceremony, he was advanced to investigation commissioner.

entries.zh: 天慶五年，受詔監都統耶律斡裏朵戰。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Tianqing he was ordered to oversee the campaign of supreme commander Yelü Woliduo.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqing he received an edict to oversee the campaigning of supreme commander Yelü Woliduo.

entries.zh: 及敗，左遷銀州刺史，徙咸州糺將。
entries.en: After the defeat he was demoted to prefect of Yin and reassigned as jiujiang commissioner at Xian Prefecture.
entries.literal: When defeat came, he was demoted to prefect of Yin Prefecture and transferred to jiujiang commissioner at Xian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 嘗與耶律章奴謀立魏國王淳。
entries.en: He had once joined Yelü Zhangnu in a plot to enthrone Prince of Wei Chun.
entries.literal: He had once joined Yelü Zhangnu in plotting to set up Prince of Wei Kingdom Chun.

entries.zh: 及聞章奴自鴨子河亡去，即引麾下數人往會之。
entries.en: When he learned that Zhangnu had deserted from the Yazi River, he immediately took a few of his men and went to join him.
entries.literal: When he heard that Zhangnu had fled away from the Yazi River, he at once led several men under his command to join him.

entries.zh: 道為遊兵所執，送行在所。
entries.en: On the way he was seized by roving troops and brought to the mobile court.
entries.literal: On the road he was seized by roving troops and sent to the mobile court.

entries.zh: 上問曰：「予何負卿而反？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "What wrong have I done you that you would rebel?"
entries.literal: The emperor asked, "What have I done against you that you rebel?"

entries.zh: 術者對曰：「臣誠無憾。
entries.en: Paizhe answered, "Your servant bears no personal grievance.
entries.literal: Paizhe replied, "Your servant truly has no resentment.

entries.zh: 但以天下大亂，已非遼有，小人滿朝，賢臣竄斥，誠不忍見天皇帝艱難之業一旦土崩。
entries.en: But the realm is in chaos and Liao no longer holds it; petty men fill the court while worthy ministers are driven into exile. I could not bear to watch the Heaven Emperor's hard-won enterprise collapse in a single day.
entries.literal: But the realm is in great disorder and is no longer possessed by Liao; petty men fill the court and worthy ministers are driven off in exile—I truly cannot bear to see the hard-won enterprise of the Heaven Emperor suddenly crumble to earth.

entries.zh: 臣所以痛入骨髓而有此舉，非為身計。」
entries.en: My grief went to the bone, and that is why I acted—not for my own gain."
entries.literal: Your servant's pain entered the marrow of the bones and produced this act—not for his own advantage."

entries.zh: 後數日，復問，術者厲聲數上過惡，陳社稷危亡之本，遂殺之。
entries.en: Several days later the emperor questioned him again; Paizhe raised his voice, listed the emperor's faults one by one, laid bare the roots of the state's ruin, and was then executed.
entries.literal: Several days later he was questioned again; Paizhe in a harsh voice recounted the emperor's faults, set forth the root of the altars' peril and ruin, and was then put to death.

entries.zh: 耶律棠古蕭得裏底蕭酬斡耶律章奴耶律術者
entries.en: Yelü Tanggu, Xiao Delidi, Xiao Chouwo, Yelü Zhangnu, and Yelü Paizhe
entries.literal: Yelü Tanggu, Xiao Delidi, Xiao Chouwo, Yelü Zhangnu, Yelü Paizhe

entries.zh: 耶律阿息保，字特裏典，五院部人。
entries.en: Yelu Axibao, whose courtesy name was Telidian, came from the Five-Yuan tribe.
entries.literal: Yelu Axibao, courtesy name Telidian, was a man of the Five-Yuan tribe.

entries.zh: 祖胡劣，太祖時徙居西北部，世為招討司吏。
entries.en: His grandfather Hulu, in the reign of Taizu, resettled in the northwest, and for generations the family served as clerks in the pacification commission.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hulu, in Taizu's time, moved to the northwest and for generations served as clerks in the pacification commission.

entries.zh: 阿息保慷慨有大志，年十六，以才幹補內史。
entries.en: Axibao was openhanded and ambitious; at sixteen he was appointed Inner Scribe on the strength of his abilities.
entries.literal: Axibao was magnanimous and ambitious; at sixteen he entered service as Inner Scribe on account of his talent.

entries.zh: 天慶初，轉樞密院侍御。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianqing era he was transferred to palace attendant in the Privy Council.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianqing he was transferred to Privy Council palace attendant.

entries.zh: 金人起兵，城境上，遣阿息保問之，金人曰：「若歸阿疏，敢不聽命。」
entries.en: When the Jin took up arms and fortified the frontier, Axibao was dispatched to inquire; the Jin replied, "If you hand back Ashu, we would not dare refuse your command."
entries.literal: When the Jin rose in arms and built fortifications on the border, Axibao was sent to inquire; the Jin said, "If [you] return Ashu, we dare not disobey orders."

entries.zh: 阿息保具以聞。
entries.en: Axibao reported the full exchange to the throne.
entries.literal: Axibao reported all of it in full.

entries.zh: 金兵陷寧江州，邊兵屢敗，遣阿息保與耶律章奴等賫書而東，冀以脅降。
entries.en: After the Jin captured Ningjiang and the border armies suffered defeat after defeat, Axibao was sent east with Yelu Zhangnu and others bearing letters, hoping to intimidate the enemy into submission.
entries.literal: When Jin troops took Ningjiang and frontier forces were repeatedly defeated, Axibao was sent with Yelu Zhangnu and others bearing documents eastward, hoping to coerce submission.

entries.zh: 阿息保曰：「臣前使，依詔開諭，略無所屈。
entries.en: Axibao said, "On my last embassy I delivered the imperial message as instructed and would not yield an inch.
entries.literal: Axibao said, "On my previous mission I expounded the edict and was in no way bent.

entries.zh: 將還，謂臣曰：『若所請不遂，無相見。』
entries.en: As I was leaving they told me, 'If our demands are not met, we shall not meet again.'
entries.literal: When I was about to return they told me, 'If our request is not granted, we shall not meet again.'

entries.zh: 今臣請獨往。」
entries.en: I beg now to go alone."
entries.literal: Now I beg to go alone."

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: The court would not hear of it.
entries.literal: [His request] was not granted.

entries.zh: 將行，別蕭得裏底曰：「不肖適異國，必無生還，願公善輔國家。」
entries.en: Before he set out he bade farewell to Xiao Delidi, saying, "Your unworthy servant is bound for a foreign land and will surely not return alive; may you govern the realm well in my stead."
entries.literal: Before departing he took leave of Xiao Delidi, saying, "Your unworthy servant goes to a foreign land and will certainly not return alive; may you well assist the state."

entries.zh: 既至，阿息保見執。
entries.en: On arrival he was taken prisoner.
entries.literal: When he arrived, Axibao was seized.

entries.zh: 久乃遁歸。
entries.en: Only after a long captivity did he escape and make his way home.
entries.literal: After a long time he escaped and returned.

entries.zh: 蕭胡篤，字合術隱。
entries.en: Xiao Hudu, whose courtesy name was Heshu'yin.
entries.literal: Xiao Hudu, courtesy name Heshu'yin.

entries.zh: 其先撒葛只，太祖時願隸宮分，遂為太和宮分人。
entries.en: His forebear Sagezhi, in the reign of Taizu, asked to be enrolled in palace household service and thus became a man of the Taihe palace household.
entries.literal: His forebear Sagezhi, in Taizu's time, wished to be enrolled in palace household service and thus became a man of the Taihe palace household.

entries.zh: 曾祖敵魯，明醫。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Dilu was a renowned physician.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Dilu was a renowned physician.

entries.zh: 人有疾，觀其形色即知病所在。
entries.en: When a patient fell ill, he could tell at a glance from complexion and bearing where the affliction lay.
entries.literal: When someone fell ill, by observing complexion and form he knew at once where the disease lay.

entries.zh: 統和中，宰相韓德讓貴寵，敵魯希旨，言德讓宜賜國姓，籍橫帳，由是世預太醫選。
entries.en: During the Tonghe era, Chancellor Han Derang enjoyed the highest favor; Dilu read the imperial mood and argued that Derang should be granted the imperial surname and enrolled in the horizontal registers, whereupon the family for generations entered the imperial physician rolls.
entries.literal: In Tonghe, Chancellor Han Derang enjoyed lofty favor; Dilu followed the imperial intent, saying Derang should be granted the imperial surname and enrolled in the horizontal registers, whereupon [the family] for generations entered imperial physician selection.

entries.zh: 子孫因之入官者眾。
