entries.en: Many of his descendants entered office by this connection.
entries.literal: Many descendants entered office through this connection.

entries.zh: 蕭陶蘇斡耶律阿息保蕭乙薛蕭胡篤
entries.en: Xiao Taosuwo, Yelu Axibao, Xiao Yixue, and Xiao Hudu
entries.literal: Xiao Taosuwo, Yelu Axibao, Xiao Yixue, Xiao Hudu

entries.zh: 遼起松漠，太祖以兵經略方內，禮文之事固所未遑。
entries.en: The Liao state rose from the Songmo region. Emperor Taizu conquered the empire by force of arms, and court ritual and letters were naturally left for later.
entries.literal: Liao arose in Songmo; the Taizu Emperor used arms to bring the realm under control, and ritual and literary matters were certainly not yet attended to.

entries.zh: 及太宗入汴，取晉圖書、禮器而北，然後制度漸以修舉。
entries.en: After Emperor Taizong entered Bianjing and carried the Jin libraries and ritual vessels north, institutions were gradually restored.
entries.literal: When the Taizong Emperor entered Bian, he took the Jin dynasty's books and ritual vessels northward; only then were institutions gradually put in order.

entries.zh: 至景、聖間，則科目聿興，士有由下僚擢升侍從，骎驍崇儒之美。
entries.en: Under Emperors Jingzong and Shengzong the civil-service examinations revived, and men rose from low office into the imperial entourage—a swift flowering of Confucian cultivation at court.
entries.literal: By the reigns of Jingzong and Shengzong, examination subjects flourished anew; scholars were raised from junior posts to attendants-in-waiting, and the beauty of honoring Confucian learning advanced swiftly.

entries.zh: 但其風氣剛勁，三面鄰敵，歲時以蒐浯為務，而典章文物，視古猶闕。
entries.en: Yet the realm's spirit remained martial and hard-edged. Enemies pressed on three fronts, and the seasons were given over to hunts and maneuvers; canonical law and cultural patrimony still lagged far behind the ancient model.
entries.literal: Yet its customs were stern and forceful; on three sides it bordered enemies, and year by year hunting and military drill were the chief tasks, while canonical statutes and cultural relics still fell short of antiquity.

entries.zh: 然二百年之業，非數君子為之綜理，則後世惡所考述哉？
entries.en: Still, two centuries of statecraft would have left later ages nothing to study had not a handful of scholars gathered and ordered the record.
entries.literal: Yet for a two-hundred-year enterprise, had not several gentlemen synthesized and ordered it, where would later ages find material for inquiry and narration?

entries.zh: 作《文學傳》。
entries.en: Hence this "Biographies of Literature."
entries.literal: Therefore the "Biographies of Literature" was composed.

entries.zh: 方今最重之役，無過西戍。
entries.en: Today no corvée weighs more heavily than service on the western frontier.
entries.literal: Among present duties, none is heavier than garrison service in the west.

entries.zh: 如無西戍，雖遇凶年，困弊不至於此。
entries.en: Without the western garrisons, even in famine years distress would not run so deep.
entries.literal: Without western garrison duty, even in bad years distress would not reach this degree.

entries.zh: 若能徙西戍稍近，則往來不勞，民無深患。
entries.en: If the western garrisons were shifted somewhat nearer, travel would be less punishing and the people's affliction would ease.
entries.literal: If western garrisons could be moved somewhat nearer, travel back and forth would not be so burdensome and the people would not suffer so deeply.

entries.zh: 議者謂徙之非便：一則損威名，二則召侵侮，三則棄耕牧之地。
entries.en: Critics say relocation would be unwise: it would diminish prestige, invite attack, and abandon cultivated and pastured lands.
entries.literal: Those who debate say relocation would be inexpedient: first, it would diminish prestige; second, it would invite aggression; third, it would abandon lands for farming and herding.

entries.zh: 臣謂不然。
entries.en: Your servant disagrees.
entries.literal: Your servant says this is not so.

entries.zh: 阻卜諸部，自來有之。
entries.en: The Zubu tribes have always been there.
entries.literal: The various Zubu tribes have existed from of old.

entries.zh: 曩時北至臚朐河，南至邊境，人多散居，無所統壹，惟往來抄掠。
entries.en: In earlier times they ranged north to the Luchu River and south to the frontier. Their people lived scattered, without unified rule, and raided one another in turn.
entries.literal: Formerly they ranged north to the Luchu River and south to the borderlands; people lived scattered without unified control and only raided back and forth.

entries.zh: 及太祖西征，至於流沙，阻卜望風悉降，西域諸國皆願入貢。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu marched west as far as the shifting sands, the Zubu submitted at the first rumor of his approach, and the states of the Western Regions all offered tribute.
entries.literal: When the Taizu Emperor campaigned west as far as the shifting sands, the Zubu submitted at the first wind, and the states of the Western Regions all wished to offer tribute.

entries.zh: 因遷種落，內置三部，以益吾國，不營城邑，不置戍兵，阻卜累世不敢為寇。
entries.en: Tribes were resettled inward, three divisions were established within our borders to strengthen the state, and no walled towns or garrison troops were needed. For generations the Zubu did not dare raid.
entries.literal: Tribes were then moved inward and three divisions were established within to strengthen our state; no walled towns were built and no garrison troops posted, and for generations the Zubu did not dare raid.

entries.zh: 統和間，王太妃出師西域，拓土既遠，降附亦眾。
entries.en: During the Tonghe era Queen Dowager Wang campaigned in the Western Regions, extending territory far abroad and winning many submissions.
entries.literal: During Tonghe, the Queen Dowager Wang led troops into the Western Regions; territory was extended far, and submissions were many.

entries.zh: 自後一部或叛，鄰部討之，使同力相制，正得馭遠人之道。
entries.en: Afterward, when one division rebelled, neighboring divisions were sent to punish it, letting them restrain one another by force—the proper way to govern distant peoples.
entries.literal: Thereafter, when one division rebelled, neighboring divisions were sent to punish it, making them restrain one another by shared force—the very way to govern distant peoples.

entries.zh: 及城可敦，開境數千里，西北之民，徭役日增，生業日殫。
entries.en: Once Kedun was fortified and the frontier stretched for thousands of li, northwestern subjects faced rising corvée and shrinking livelihoods day by day.
entries.literal: When Kedun city was built and the border opened for thousands of li, the people of the northwest saw corvée increase daily and livelihoods daily exhausted.

entries.zh: 警急既不能救，叛服亦復不恒。
entries.en: Emergencies could not be met in time, and loyalty and rebellion alike grew unstable.
entries.literal: When emergencies arose they could not be relieved; submission and rebellion were no longer constant.

entries.zh: 空有廣地之名，而無得地之實。
entries.en: The realm held only the name of vast territory, not the reality of controlling it.
entries.literal: There was only the name of broad lands, without the reality of holding them.

entries.zh: 若貪土不已，漸至虛耗，其患有不勝言者。
entries.en: If the appetite for land never ends, the state will be drained little by little, and the harm is beyond telling.
entries.literal: If greed for land continues without end, gradual exhaustion will follow, and the harm is beyond words.

entries.zh: 況邊情不可深信，亦不可頓絕。
entries.en: Frontier loyalties cannot be trusted completely, yet they cannot be cut off all at once.
entries.literal: Moreover, frontier sentiment cannot be deeply trusted, yet it cannot be abruptly severed either.

entries.zh: 得不為益，舍不為損。
entries.en: What is kept may not be gain; what is given up may not be loss.
entries.literal: What is gained may not be benefit; what is abandoned may not be loss.

entries.zh: 國家大敵，惟在南方。
entries.en: The state's gravest foe lies in the south alone.
entries.literal: The state's great enemy lies only in the south.

entries.zh: 今雖連和，難保他日。
entries.en: We are at peace now, but tomorrow cannot be guaranteed.
entries.literal: Though we are allied now, it is hard to guarantee tomorrow.

entries.zh: 若南方有變，屯戍遼邈，卒難赴援。
entries.en: If the south erupts in crisis, distant garrisons cannot send relief in time.
entries.literal: If trouble arises in the south, garrisons are remote and distant, and relief troops can hardly arrive in time.

entries.zh: 我進則敵退，我還則敵來，不可不慮也。
entries.en: When we advance, the enemy retreats; when we withdraw, the enemy returns. This cannot be ignored.
entries.literal: When we advance the enemy retreats; when we withdraw the enemy comes—this cannot go unconsidered.

entries.zh: 方今太平已久，正可恩結諸部，釋罪而歸地，內徙戍兵以增堡障，外明約束以正疆界。
entries.en: Peace has lasted long. Now is the time to win the tribes by grace, pardon offenses and return land, shift garrison troops inward to strengthen defenses, and set clear treaties to fix the borders.
entries.literal: Now that peace has lasted long, it is right to bind the tribes with grace, pardon offenses and return land, move garrison troops inward to strengthen fortifications, and outwardly clarify treaties to fix the borders.

entries.zh: 每部各置酋長，歲修職貢。
entries.en: Each division should have its own chief, with annual tribute.
entries.literal: Each division should have its own chief installed, with annual tribute duties observed.

entries.zh: 叛則討之，服則撫之。
entries.en: Punish rebellion; comfort submission.
entries.literal: If they rebel, punish them; if they submit, comfort them.

entries.zh: 諸部既安，必不生釁。
entries.en: Once the tribes are settled, they will not stir trouble.
entries.literal: Once the tribes are settled, they will surely not create trouble.

entries.zh: 如是，則臣雖不能保其久而無變，知其必不深入侵掠也。
entries.en: Your servant cannot promise they will never change in the long run, but they will not launch deep raids.
entries.literal: Thus, though your servant cannot guarantee that they will never change in the long run, I know they will certainly not launch deep invasions and raids.

entries.zh: 或云棄地則損威，殊不知殫費竭財，以貪無用之地，使彼小部抗衡大國，萬一有敗，損威豈淺？
entries.en: Some say abandoning land damages prestige. They do not see that draining the treasury to seize useless ground and letting small tribes defy a great power—should defeat come once, would the loss of prestige be slight?
entries.literal: Some say abandoning land damages prestige, not knowing that exhausting wealth and draining treasuries to covet useless territory, letting small tribes contend with a great state—if defeat should come, would the loss of prestige be slight?

entries.zh: 或又云，沃壤不可遽棄。
entries.en: Others say fertile soil cannot be abandoned in haste.
entries.literal: Others again say fertile soil cannot be hastily abandoned.

entries.zh: 臣以為土雖沃，民不能久居，一旦敵來，則不免內徙，豈可指為吾土而惜之？
entries.en: Your servant holds that however fertile the soil, people cannot live there long. When enemies come, inhabitants must move inward. How can such land be called ours and cherished?
entries.literal: Your servant holds that though the soil is fertile, the people cannot dwell there long; once enemies come, they must move inward—how can it be called our land and cherished?

entries.zh: 十三年春，上疏曰：「臣聞先世遙輦可汗窪之後，國祚中絕。
entries.en: In the spring of the thirteenth year of Chongxi, he submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that after Khagan Kua of the Yaolian in former ages, the imperial succession was cut off.
entries.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year, he submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that after Khagan Kua of the Yaolian in former ages, the imperial succession was cut off.

entries.zh: 自夷離堇雅裏立阻午，大位始定。
entries.en: From the time the yilijin Yali established Zuwu as khan, the great position was first settled.
entries.literal: From the time the yilijin Yali established Zuwu, the great position was first settled.

entries.zh: 然上世俗樸，未有尊稱。
entries.en: Yet the customs of earlier generations were plain, and no honorific titles were used.
entries.literal: Yet the customs of the upper generations were plain, and no honorific titles existed.

entries.zh: 臣以為三皇禮文未備，正與遙輦氏同。
entries.en: Your servant holds that the ritual texts of the Three Sovereigns were not yet complete—precisely as with the Yaolian clan.
entries.literal: Your servant holds that the ritual texts of the Three Sovereigns were not yet complete—precisely the same as with the Yaolian clan.

entries.zh: 後世之君以禮樂治天下，而崇本追遠之義興焉。
entries.en: Later rulers governed the realm with ritual and music, and the principle of honoring one's roots and remembering the distant arose.
entries.literal: Later rulers governed the realm with ritual and music, and the principle of honoring the root and remembering the distant arose.

entries.zh: 近者唐高祖創立先廟，尊四世為帝。
entries.en: Recently Tang Gaozu established the ancestral temple and honored four generations as emperors.
entries.literal: Recently Tang Gaozu established the ancestral temple and honored four generations as emperors.

entries.zh: 昔我太祖代遙輦即位，乃制文字，修禮法，建天皇帝名號，制宮室以示威服，興利除害，混一海內。
entries.en: Formerly our Taizu Emperor succeeded the Yaolian and took the throne; he devised script, restored ritual law, established the title of Heavenly Emperor, built palaces to display authority and win submission, advanced benefit and removed harm, and unified the realm.
entries.literal: Formerly our Taizu Emperor succeeded the Yaolian and took the throne; he then devised script, restored ritual law, established the title of Heavenly Emperor, built palaces to display authority and submission, advanced benefit and removed harm, and unified the realm within the seas.

entries.zh: 厥後累聖相承，自夷離堇湖烈以下，大號未加，天皇帝之考夷離堇的魯猶以名呼。
entries.en: Thereafter successive sage emperors succeeded one another, yet from the yilijin Hulie downward no grand title was conferred, and the Heavenly Emperor's father, the yilijin Dilu, was still addressed by personal name.
entries.literal: Thereafter successive sage emperors succeeded one another, yet from the yilijin Hulie downward no grand title was conferred, and the Heavenly Emperor's father, the yilijin Dilu, was still addressed by personal name.

entries.zh: 臣以為宜依唐典，追崇四祖為皇帝，則陛下弘業有光，墜典復舉矣。」
entries.en: Your servant holds that it is fitting to follow the Tang precedent and posthumously honor the four ancestors as emperors; then Your Majesty's great enterprise would gain luster and fallen rites would be restored."
entries.literal: Your servant holds that it is fitting to follow the Tang precedent and posthumously honor the four ancestors as emperors; then Your Majesty's great enterprise would gain luster and fallen rites would be restored."

entries.zh: 疏奏，帝納之，始行追冊玄、德二祖之禮。
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor accepted it and first carried out the rites of posthumously enshrining the Xuan and De ancestors.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor accepted it and first carried out the rites of posthumously enshrining the Xuan and De ancestors.

entries.zh: 蕭韓家奴，字休堅，涅剌部人，中書令安摶之孫。
entries.en: Xiao Hanjianu, styled Xiujian, came from the Niela tribe and was a grandson of Chief Councillor An Tuo.
entries.literal: Xiao Hanjianu, style name Xiujian, was a man of the Niela tribe, grandson of Chief Councillor An Tuo.

entries.zh: 少好學，弱冠入南山讀書，博覽經史，通遼、漢文字。
entries.en: He loved learning from boyhood. At twenty he went into the Southern Mountains to read, mastered the classics and histories, and was fluent in both Khitan and Chinese writing.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning; at twenty he entered the Southern Mountains to study, broadly reading the classics and histories and mastering both Khitan and Chinese script.

entries.zh: 統和十四年始仕。
entries.en: He first took office in the fourteenth year of the Tonghe era.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tonghe he first entered office.

entries.zh: 家有一牛，不任驅策，其奴得善價鬻之。
entries.en: The family owned an ox that could not be driven. A servant found a good buyer and sold it.
entries.literal: His household had an ox that could not be driven; a servant obtained a good price and sold it.

entries.zh: 韓家奴曰：「利己誤人，非吾所欲。」
entries.en: Hanjianu said, "Profiting myself while wronging someone else is not what I want."
entries.literal: Hanjianu said, "To profit oneself and harm another is not what I desire."

entries.zh: 乃歸直取牛。
entries.en: He returned the money and reclaimed the ox.
entries.literal: He then returned the payment and took back the ox.

entries.zh: 二十八年，為右通進，典南京栗園。
entries.en: In year twenty-eight of Tonghe he was made Right Vice Commissioner for Forwarding Memorials and put in charge of the Southern Capital's chestnut orchards.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he became Right Vice Commissioner for Forwarding Memorials and supervised the chestnut orchards of the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 重熙初，同知三司使事。
entries.en: Early in the Chongxi era he became Associate Commissioner of the Three Departments.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi he served as Associate Commissioner of the Three Departments.

entries.zh: 四年，遷天成軍節度使，徙彰湣宮使。
entries.en: In year four of Chongxi he was promoted to Military Commissioner of Tiancheng Army, then transferred to Commissioner of Zhangmin Palace.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Tiancheng Army, then moved to Commissioner of Zhangmin Palace.

entries.zh: 帝與語，才之，命為詩友。
entries.en: The emperor spoke with him, recognized his talent, and named him a poetry companion.
entries.literal: The emperor conversed with him, recognized his talent, and appointed him a poetry companion.

entries.zh: 嘗從容問曰：「卿居外有異聞乎？」
entries.en: On one relaxed occasion the emperor asked, "In your posts away from court, have you heard anything noteworthy?"
entries.literal: Once, in an easy mood, he asked, "In your service outside the capital, have you heard anything unusual?"

entries.zh: 韓家奴對曰：「臣惟知炒栗：小者熟，則大者必生；
entries.en: Hanjianu answered, "Your servant knows only how to roast chestnuts: if the small ones are done, the large ones must still be raw;
entries.literal: Hanjianu replied, "Your servant knows only roasting chestnuts: when the small ones are done, the large ones must still be raw;

entries.zh: 大者熟，則小者必焦。
entries.en: if the large ones are done, the small ones will be burnt.
entries.literal: when the large ones are done, the small ones must be scorched.

entries.zh: 使大小均熟，始為盡美。
entries.en: Only when large and small are roasted alike is the result truly perfect.
entries.literal: Only when large and small are equally done is the perfection complete.

entries.zh: 不知其他。」
entries.en: I know nothing beyond that."
entries.literal: I know nothing else."

entries.zh: 蓋嘗掌栗園，故托栗以諷諫。
entries.en: He had once managed the chestnut orchards, and so he used chestnuts as a veiled remonstrance.
entries.literal: For he had once managed the chestnut orchards and therefore used chestnuts as a vehicle for indirect remonstrance.

entries.zh: 帝大笑。
entries.en: The emperor laughed aloud.
entries.literal: The emperor laughed heartily.

entries.zh: 詔作《四時逸樂賦》，帝稱善。
entries.en: The emperor ordered him to write the "Rhapsody on Leisure through the Four Seasons" and praised the result.
entries.literal: He was ordered to compose the "Rhapsody on Leisure and Pleasure through the Four Seasons," and the emperor praised it.

entries.zh: 李澣，初仕晉為中書舍人。
entries.en: Li Han first served the Later Jin as Secretariat Drafter.
entries.literal: Li Han first served the Jin as Secretariat Drafter.

entries.zh: 晉亡歸遼，當太宗崩、世宗立，恟渙不定，澣與高勛等十餘人羈留南京。
entries.en: When the Jin fell he entered Liao service. As Emperor Taizong died and Emperor Shizong was enthroned, the realm was unsettled, and Han with Gao Xun and more than ten others were detained at the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: When Jin fell he returned to Liao; as the Taizong Emperor died and the Shizong Emperor was enthroned, turmoil was unsettled, and Han together with Gao Xun and more than ten others were detained at the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 久之，從歸上京，授翰林學士。
entries.en: After a long while he followed the court back to the Supreme Capital and was made Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: After a long while he followed the court back to the Supreme Capital and was appointed Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 穆宗即位，累遷工部侍郎。
entries.en: When Muzong took the throne, he rose step by step to Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When Muzong took the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 時澣兄濤在汴為翰林學士，密遣人召澣。
entries.en: At that time Han's elder brother Tao was Hanlin Academician at Bianjing and secretly sent someone to summon him.
entries.literal: At that time Han's elder brother Tao was Hanlin Academician at Bian and secretly sent someone to summon Han.

entries.zh: 澣得書，托求醫南京，易服夜出，欲遁歸汴。
entries.en: Han received the letter, pleaded illness to seek treatment at the Southern Capital, changed clothes, slipped out at night, and tried to flee back to Bianjing.
entries.literal: Han received the letter, pleaded illness to seek medical treatment at the Southern Capital, changed clothes and went out at night, intending to flee back to Bian.

entries.zh: 至涿，為僥巡者所得，送之南京，下吏。
entries.en: At Zhuo he was seized by patrol scouts, sent to the Southern Capital, and handed over to the magistrates.
entries.literal: When he reached Zhuo he was seized by patrol scouts, sent to the Southern Capital, and handed over to the magistrates.

entries.zh: 澣伺獄吏熟寢，以衣帶自經；
entries.en: Han waited until the jailers were fast asleep, then hanged himself with his belt;
entries.literal: Han waited until the prison officers were fast asleep, then hanged himself with his belt;

entries.zh: 不死，防之愈嚴。
entries.en: he did not die, and his guard was tightened further.
entries.literal: he did not die, and his guard was made stricter still.

entries.zh: 械赴上京，自投潢河中流，為鐵索牽掣，又不死。
entries.en: In fetters he was sent to the Supreme Capital. He threw himself into midstream of the Huang River, was pulled back on iron chains, and still did not die.
entries.literal: Fettered, he was sent to the Supreme Capital; he threw himself into midstream of the Huang River and was pulled back by iron chains, yet again did not die.

entries.zh: 及抵上京，帝欲殺之。
entries.en: When he reached the Supreme Capital the emperor wished to kill him.
entries.literal: When he reached the Supreme Capital the emperor wished to execute him.

entries.zh: 時高勛已為樞密使，救止之。
entries.en: By then Gao Xun was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and stopped the execution.
entries.literal: At that time Gao Xun was already Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and rescued him, stopping the execution.

entries.zh: 屢言於上曰：「澣本非負恩，以母年八十，急於省覲致罪。
entries.en: He told the throne repeatedly, "Han did not betray your favor. His mother is eighty, and in his urgency to visit her he committed this offense.
entries.literal: He repeatedly told the throne, "Han did not originally betray favor; his mother is eighty years old, and in his urgency to visit her he incurred guilt.

entries.zh: 且澣富於文學，方今少有倫比，若留掌詞命，可以增光國體。」
entries.en: Moreover Han is rich in literary learning and has few equals today. If he is kept to manage edicts and commands, he can add luster to the state."
entries.literal: Moreover Han is rich in literary learning; today few can be compared with him. If he is kept to manage edicts and commands, he can add luster to the state's dignity."

entries.zh: 帝怒稍解，仍令禁錮於奉國寺，凡六年，艱苦萬狀。
entries.en: The emperor's anger eased somewhat, but Han was still confined at Fengguo Temple for six years in every kind of hardship.
entries.literal: The emperor's anger eased somewhat, yet he still ordered Han confined at Fengguo Temple for six years in every kind of hardship.

entries.zh: 會上欲建《太宗功德碑》，高勛奏曰：「非李澣無可秉筆者。」
entries.en: When the emperor wished to erect the Stele of Emperor Taizong's Merits and Virtues, Gao Xun memorialized, "Apart from Li Han there is no one fit to wield the brush."
entries.literal: When the emperor wished to erect the Stele of Taizong's Merits and Virtues, Gao Xun memorialized, "Apart from Li Han there is no one fit to wield the brush."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The edict approved it.
entries.literal: An edict approved this.

entries.zh: 文成以進，上悅，釋囚。
entries.en: When the text was completed and presented, the emperor was pleased and released him.
entries.literal: When the text was completed and presented, the emperor was pleased and released the prisoner.

entries.zh: 尋加禮部尚書，宣政殿學士，卒。
entries.en: Soon he was made Minister of Rites and Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall, then died.
entries.literal: Soon he was further made Minister of Rites and Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall, then died.

entries.zh: 文學上 ○蕭韓家奴李澣
entries.en: Literature 1 ○ Xiao Hanjianu · Li Han
entries.literal: Literature, Part One ○ Xiao Hanjianu, Li Han

entries.zh: 王鼎，字虛中，涿州人。
entries.en: Wang Ding, whose courtesy name was Xuzhong, came from Zhuozhou.
entries.literal: Wang Ding, style name Xuzhong, was a man of Zhuozhou.

entries.zh: 幼好學，居太寧山數年，博通經史。
entries.en: As a boy he loved study; he lived on Mount Taining for years until he had mastered the classics and histories.
entries.literal: From youth he loved learning; he dwelt on Mount Taining for several years and attained thorough mastery of the classics and histories.

entries.zh: 時馬唐俊有文名燕、薊間，適上巳，與同志祓禊水濱，酌酒賦詩。
entries.en: At the time Ma Tangjun enjoyed a literary reputation in the Yan and Ji region. It chanced to be the Shangsi Festival, and he went with friends to perform the spring purification by the water, drinking wine and composing verse.
entries.literal: At that time Ma Tangjun had a literary reputation between Yan and Ji; it happened to be the Shangsi Festival, and with like-minded friends he performed the spring purification rite by the waterside, pouring wine and composing poetry.

entries.zh: 鼎偶造席，唐俊見鼎樸野，置下坐。
entries.en: Ding happened upon the gathering. Tangjun took him for a rustic and gave him the lowest seat.
entries.literal: Ding happened by the gathering; Tangjun saw that Ding was plain and rustic and seated him in the lowest place.

entries.zh: 欲以詩困之，先出所作索賦，鼎援筆立成。
entries.en: Intending to trap him with verse, Tangjun first produced his own poem and demanded a reply; Ding took up the brush and finished one on the spot.
entries.literal: Wishing to embarrass him with poetry, he first presented his own composition and demanded a matching piece; Ding took up the brush and completed it at once.

entries.zh: 唐俊驚其敏妙，因與定交。
entries.en: Tangjun was astonished by his quick wit and thereupon became his sworn friend.
entries.literal: Tangjun marveled at his quick brilliance and therefore formed a sworn friendship with him.

entries.zh: 清寧五年，擢進士第。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Qingning reign he passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Qingning he was selected in the jinshi examinations.

entries.zh: 調易州觀察判官，改淶水縣令，累遷翰林學士。
entries.en: He was posted as judicial aide on the Yizhou Observation Commission, then made magistrate of Laishui County, and rose in time to Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: He was assigned as judicial aide to the Yizhou Observation Commission, then transferred to magistrate of Laishui County, and was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 當代典章多出其手。
entries.en: Most of the age's ritual codes and statutes came from his pen.
entries.literal: Most of the ritual regulations of the age issued from his hand.

entries.zh: 上書言治道十事，帝以鼎達政體，事多咨訪。
entries.en: He memorialized the throne on ten points of governance. The emperor judged Ding thoroughly versed in statecraft and often sought his counsel.
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters of governance; the emperor considered Ding well versed in statecraft and frequently consulted him on affairs.

entries.zh: 鼎正直不阿，人有過，必面詆之。
entries.en: Ding was upright and unyielding: whenever anyone erred, he would rebuke him to his face.
entries.literal: Ding was upright and would not flatter; when someone had a fault he would invariably denounce it to his face.

entries.zh: 壽隆初，升觀書殿學士。
entries.en: At the opening of the Shoulong era he was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Viewing Books.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shoulong he was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Viewing Books.

entries.zh: 一日宴主第，醉與客忤，怨上不知己，坐是下吏。
entries.en: One day at a feast in the princess's residence he grew drunk and quarreled with a guest, complaining that the emperor did not know his worth; for this he was handed over to the magistrates.
entries.literal: One day at a feast in the princess's residence he became drunk and clashed with a guest; he resented that the emperor did not recognize his worth, and for this was sent down to the officials for punishment.

entries.zh: 狀聞，上大怒，杖黥奪官，流鎮州。
entries.en: When the report reached the throne the emperor flew into a rage: Ding was beaten, tattooed, stripped of office, and exiled to Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: When the report reached the throne, the emperor was greatly angered; he was beaten, tattooed, and stripped of office, and exiled to Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 居數歲，有赦，鼎獨不免。
entries.en: After several years an amnesty was proclaimed, but Ding alone was not pardoned.
entries.literal: After several years there was an amnesty, but Ding alone was not included.

entries.zh: 會守臣召鼎為賀表，因以詩貽使者，有「誰知天雨露，獨不到孤寒」之句。
entries.en: It happened that the local commander summoned Ding to draft a congratulatory memorial, and he sent a poem to the envoy with the line, "Who knew heaven's rain and dew would pass the lonely and cold by alone?"
entries.literal: It happened that the defending official summoned Ding to compose a congratulatory memorial; he therefore sent a poem to the envoy, containing the lines, "Who would have known heaven's rain and dew would alone not reach the solitary and cold?"

entries.zh: 上聞而憐之，即召還，復其職。
entries.en: The emperor heard of it, took pity on him, and at once recalled him and restored his office.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of it he took pity on him and immediately recalled him, restoring him to his post.

entries.zh: 乾統六年卒。
entries.en: He died in the sixth year of the Qiantong reign.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Qiantong he died.

entries.zh: 劉輝，好學善屬文，疏簡有遠略。
entries.en: Liu Hui loved learning and was skilled at literary composition; plain in manner, he possessed far-reaching vision.
entries.literal: Liu Hui loved learning and was skilled at composition, plain and sparing in manner, with far-reaching vision.

entries.zh: 大康五年，第進士。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Dakang reign he passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dakang he placed in the jinshi examinations.

entries.zh: 大安末，為太子洗馬，上書言：「西邊諸番為患，士卒遠戍，中國之民疲於飛挽，非長久之策。
entries.en: At the end of the Da'an era he served as Mentor of the Crown Prince and memorialized the throne: "The western tribes are a constant trouble; troops are garrisoned far away while the people of the Central Plains wear themselves out hauling supplies—this is no lasting policy.
entries.literal: At the end of Da'an he served as Mentor of the Crown Prince and submitted a memorial saying: "The various tribes of the western frontier are a source of trouble; soldiers are garrisoned far away and the people of the Central Plains wear themselves out hauling supplies—this is no long-term policy.

entries.zh: 為今之務，莫若城於鹽濼，實以漢戶，使耕田聚糧，以為西北之費。」
entries.en: The urgent task today is to build fortified towns at the salt marshes, settle them with Han households, and have them farm and store grain to supply the northwest."
entries.literal: The urgent task of the day is none better than fortifying cities at the salt marshes, filling them with Han households so that they farm fields and store grain as expenses for the northwest."

entries.zh: 言雖不行，識者韙之。
entries.en: Though his proposal was not adopted, men of insight approved it.
entries.literal: Though his words were not adopted, those with insight approved them.

entries.zh: 壽隆二年，復上書曰：「宋歐陽修編《五代史》，附我朝於四夷，妄加貶訾。
entries.en: In the second year of Shoulong he again memorialized the throne: "The Song scholar Ouyang Xiu compiled the History of the Five Dynasties and placed our dynasty among the four barbarians, recklessly denigrating us.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shoulong he again submitted a memorial saying: "The Song man Ouyang Xiu compiled the History of the Five Dynasties and placed our dynasty among the four barbarians, adding reckless denigration.

entries.zh: 且宋人賴我朝寬大，許通和好，得盡兄弟之禮。
entries.en: Moreover the Song rely on our court's magnanimity, permitted friendship and peace, and enjoy the full observance of brotherly rites.
entries.literal: Moreover the Song people rely on the magnanimity of our court, permitted to maintain friendship and accord, and attain the full observance of brotherly rites.

entries.zh: 今反令臣下妄意作史，恬不經意。
entries.en: Now they let their subjects presumptuously write history, calm and heedless of offense.
entries.literal: Now they have turned instead to letting their subjects presumptuously compose histories, calm and heedless.

entries.zh: 臣請以趙氏初起事跡，詳附國史。」
entries.en: Your servant requests that the Zhao clan's founding deeds be set forth in detail and appended to our national history."
entries.literal: Your servant requests that the Zhao clan's deeds at the founding be set forth in detail and appended to the national history."

entries.zh: 上嘉其言，遷禮部郎中。
entries.en: The emperor commended his words and promoted him to Master of Rites in the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: The emperor commended his words and transferred him to Master of Rites.

entries.zh: 詔以賢良對策，輝言多中時病。
entries.en: The emperor ordered a policy examination for men of talent; Hui's answers largely struck the maladies of the age.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered a policy essay by men of talent; Hui's words largely hit the maladies of the age.

entries.zh: 擢史館修撰，卒。
entries.en: He was promoted to Compiler in the Historiography Institute and died.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Compiler in the Historiography Institute and died.

entries.zh: 耶律孟簡，字復易，於越屋質之五世孫。
entries.en: Yelü Mengjian, courtesy name Fuyi, was the fifth-generation descendant of the Yuyue Wuzhi.
entries.literal: Yelü Mengjian, style name Fuyi, was the fifth-generation descendant of Yuyue Wuzhi.

entries.zh: 父劉家奴，官至節度使。
entries.en: His father Liu Jianu rose to the rank of military commissioner.
entries.literal: His father Liu Jianu rose to the post of military commissioner.

entries.zh: 孟簡性穎悟。
entries.en: Mengjian was quick and perceptive by nature.
entries.literal: Mengjian was by nature quick and perceptive.

entries.zh: 六歲，父晨出獵，俾賦《曉天星月詩》，孟簡應聲而成，父大奇之。
entries.en: At six, when his father went hunting at dawn and asked him to compose a poem on "Stars and Moon at Daybreak," Mengjian answered as soon as the words were spoken, and his father was astonished.
entries.literal: At six years old, when his father went out hunting at dawn and had him compose a poem on "Stars and Moon at Daybreak," Mengjian responded as soon as the words were spoken; his father was greatly astonished.

entries.zh: 既長，善屬文。
entries.en: When he grew up he became skilled at literary composition.
entries.literal: When grown he was skilled in literary composition.

entries.zh: 大康初，樞密使耶律乙辛以奸險竊柄，出為中京留守，孟簡與耶律庶箴表賀。
entries.en: At the beginning of Dakang, Privy Councillor Yelü Yixin seized power through treachery and was sent out as Commissioner of the Central Capital; Mengjian and Yelü Shuzhen submitted a congratulatory memorial.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, the Privy Councillor Yelü Yixin by treacherous craft usurped power and was sent out as Commissioner of the Central Capital; Mengjian together with Yelü Shuzhen submitted a congratulatory memorial.

entries.zh: 未幾，乙辛復舊職，銜之，謫巡磁窯關。
entries.en: Before long Yixin returned to his former post and bore a grudge; Mengjian was demoted to patrol the Ciyao Pass.
entries.literal: Before long Yixin resumed his former post and bore a grudge; Mengjian was demoted to patrol duty at the Ciyao Pass.

entries.zh: 時雖以讒見逐，不形辭色。
entries.en: Though driven out through slander, he showed no change in speech or countenance.
entries.literal: Though at the time he was driven out through slander, he showed no change in speech or countenance.

entries.zh: 遇林泉勝地，終日忘歸。
entries.en: When he came upon fine scenery of forest and spring he would linger all day and forget to return.
entries.literal: When he came upon fine scenery of forest and spring he would forget to return all day.

entries.zh: 明年，流保州。
entries.en: The following year he was exiled to Baozhou.
entries.literal: The next year he was exiled to Baozhou.

entries.zh: 及聞皇太子被害，不勝哀痛，以詩傷之，作《放懷詩》二十首。
entries.en: When he heard that the crown prince had been murdered he was overcome with grief; he mourned him in verse and composed twenty poems entitled Poems of Letting Go the Heart.
entries.literal: When he heard that the crown prince had been murdered he could not overcome his grief; he mourned him in verse and composed twenty poems entitled "Poems of Letting Go the Heart."

entries.zh: 自序云：「禽獸有哀樂之聲，螻蟻有動靜之形。
entries.en: In his preface he wrote: "Beasts and birds have sounds of sorrow and joy; ants and insects have forms of movement and stillness.
entries.literal: In his preface he wrote: "Beasts and birds have sounds of sorrow and joy; ants and insects have forms of movement and stillness.

entries.zh: 在物猶然，況於人乎？
entries.en: If it is so even among things, how much more among human beings?
entries.literal: If it is so even among things, how much more among men?

entries.zh: 然賢達哀樂，不在窮通禍福之間。
entries.en: Yet for the worthy and penetrating, sorrow and joy do not depend on poverty or success, fortune or disaster.
entries.literal: Yet for the worthy and penetrating, sorrow and joy lie not between poverty and success, fortune and disaster.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：『樂天知命，故不憂。』
entries.en: The Classic of Changes says: 'Content with heaven and knowing fate, and therefore without worry.'
entries.literal: The Classic of Changes says: 'Content with heaven and knowing fate, therefore without worry.'

entries.zh: 是以顏淵簞瓢自得，此知命而樂者也。
entries.en: Thus Yan Yuan with his bamboo basket was self-sufficient—this is knowing fate and finding joy in it.
entries.literal: Thus Yan Yuan with his bamboo basket was self-sufficient—this is knowing fate and being joyful.

entries.zh: 予雖流放，以道自安，又何疑耶？」
entries.en: Though I am in exile, I rest secure through the Way—what doubt remains?"
entries.literal: Though I am in exile, I rest secure through the Way—what doubt remains?"

entries.zh: 大康中，始得歸鄉里。
entries.en: During the Dakang era he was at last able to return home.
entries.literal: In the Dakang era he was at last able to return to his native place.

entries.zh: 詣闕上表曰：「本朝之興，幾二百年，宜有國史以垂後世。」
entries.en: He went to court and submitted a memorial: "Since our dynasty rose, nearly two hundred years have passed; there ought to be a national history to hand down to posterity."
entries.literal: He went to court and submitted a memorial saying: "Since our dynasty rose, it has been nearly two hundred years; there ought to be a national history to hand down to posterity."

entries.zh: 乃編耶律曷魯、屋質、休哥三人行事以進。
entries.en: Thereupon he compiled the career records of Yelü Helu, Wuzhi, and Xiuge and presented them to the throne.
entries.literal: Thereupon he compiled the career records of Yelü Helu, Wuzhi, and Xiuge and presented them.

entries.zh: 上命置局編修。
entries.en: The emperor ordered that a bureau be established for compilation.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered that a bureau be established for compilation.

entries.zh: 孟簡謂余官曰：「史筆天下之大信，一言當否，百世從之。
entries.en: Mengjian told the other officials: "The historiographer's brush is the great trust of the realm; whether a single word is right or wrong, a hundred generations will follow it.
entries.literal: Mengjian told the other officials: "The historiographer's brush is the great trust of the realm; whether a single word is right or wrong, a hundred generations will follow it.

entries.zh: 茍無明識，好惡徇情，則禍不測。
entries.en: Without clear judgment, if likes and dislikes follow private feeling, disaster is unforeseeable.
entries.literal: If there is no clear judgment and likes and dislikes follow private feeling, then disaster is unforeseeable.

entries.zh: 故左氏、司馬遷、班固、范曄俱罹殃禍，可不慎歟！」
entries.en: Therefore Zuo Qiuming, Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and Fan Ye all suffered calamity—is caution not required!"
entries.literal: Therefore Zuo Qiuming, Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and Fan Ye all suffered calamity—is caution not required!"

entries.zh: 乾統中，遷六院部太保。
entries.en: During the Qiantong era he was transferred to Grand Protector of the Six Tribes Commission.
entries.literal: In the Qiantong era he was transferred to Grand Protector of the Six Tribes Commission.

entries.zh: 處事不拘文法，時多笑其迂。
entries.en: In handling affairs he did not stick to written regulations; at the time many laughed at him as pedantic.
entries.literal: In handling affairs he did not stick to written regulations; at the time many laughed at him as pedantic.

entries.zh: 孟簡聞之曰：「上古之時，無簿書法令而天下治。
entries.en: When Mengjian heard this he said: "In high antiquity there were no ledgers and laws, yet the realm was governed.
entries.literal: When Mengjian heard this he said: "In high antiquity there were no ledgers and laws yet the realm was governed.

entries.zh: 蓋簿書法令適足以滋奸幸，非聖人致治之本。」
entries.en: Ledgers and laws are just enough to breed crafty favor—they are not the foundation by which sages bring order."
entries.literal: Ledgers and laws are just enough to breed crafty favor; they are not the foundation by which sages bring order."

entries.zh: 改高州觀察使，修學校，招生徒。
entries.en: He was made Commissioner of Gaozhou for Observation, built schools, and enrolled students.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of Gaozhou for Observation, built schools, and enrolled students.

entries.zh: 遷昭德軍節度使。
entries.en: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhaode Army.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhaode Army.

entries.zh: 以中京饑，詔與學士劉嗣昌減價糶粟。
entries.en: When the Central Capital suffered famine, the emperor ordered him and Academician Liu Sichang to sell grain at reduced prices.
entries.literal: Because the Central Capital suffered famine, the emperor ordered that he together with Academician Liu Sichang sell grain at reduced price.

entries.zh: 事未畢，卒。
entries.en: Before the task was finished he died.
entries.literal: Before the task was finished he died.

entries.zh: 耶律谷欲，字休堅，六院部人。
entries.en: Yelü Guyu, courtesy name Xiujian, was a man of the Six Tribes Commission.
entries.literal: Yelü Guyu, style name Xiujian, was a man of the Six Tribes Commission.

entries.zh: 父阿古只，官至節度使。
entries.en: His father Aguozhi rose to the rank of military commissioner.
entries.literal: His father Aguozhi rose to the post of military commissioner.

entries.zh: 谷欲沖淡有禮法，工文章。
entries.en: Guyu was mild and unassuming, observant of ritual propriety, and accomplished at literary composition.
entries.literal: Guyu was mild and detached, observant of ritual propriety, and accomplished in literary composition.

entries.zh: 統和中，為本部太保。
entries.en: During the Tonghe era he served as Grand Protector of his native commission.
entries.literal: In the Tonghe era he served as Grand Protector of his native commission.

entries.zh: 開泰中，稍遷塌母城節度使。
entries.en: During the Kaitai era he was gradually promoted to Military Commissioner of Tamucheng.
entries.literal: In the Kaitai era he was gradually transferred to Military Commissioner of Tamucheng.

entries.zh: 鞫霸州疑獄，稱旨，授啟聖軍節度使。
entries.en: He investigated doubtful cases in Bazhou; his work pleased the emperor, and he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qisheng Army.
entries.literal: He investigated doubtful cases in Bazhou; his work pleased the emperor, and he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qisheng Army.

entries.zh: 太平中，復為本部太保。
entries.en: During the Taiping era he again served as Grand Protector of his native commission.
entries.literal: In the Taiping era he again served as Grand Protector of his native commission.

entries.zh: 謝病歸，俄擢南院大王。
entries.en: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home; shortly afterward he was promoted to King of the Southern Commission.
entries.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home; shortly afterward he was promoted to King of the Southern Commission.

entries.zh: 嘆風俗日頽，請老，不許。
entries.en: He lamented that customs were daily in decline and asked to retire, but the request was denied.
entries.literal: He lamented that customs daily declined and requested retirement, but permission was not granted.

entries.zh: 興宗命為詩友，數問治要，多所匡建。
entries.en: Emperor Xingzong made him a poetry companion and often asked him about essentials of governance; he offered much corrective counsel.
entries.literal: Emperor Xingzong appointed him a poetry companion and frequently asked him about essentials of governance; he offered much corrective counsel.

entries.zh: 奉詔與林牙耶律庶成、蕭韓家奴編遼國上世事跡及諸帝《實錄》，未成而卒，年九十。
entries.en: By imperial order he joined Linya Yelü Shucheng and Xiao Hanjianu in compiling the deeds of earlier Liao affairs and the Veritable Records of the various emperors; he died before the work was finished, at the age of ninety.
entries.literal: By imperial order he together with Linya Yelü Shucheng and Xiao Hanjianu compiled the deeds of earlier Liao affairs and the Veritable Records of the various emperors; before completion he died, aged ninety.

entries.zh: 文學下 ○王鼎耶律昭劉輝耶律孟簡耶律谷欲
entries.en: Literature (Part 2) — Wang Ding, Yelü Zhao, Liu Hui, Yelü Mengjian, and Yelü Guyu
entries.literal: Literature (Part 2) ○ Wang Ding, Yelü Zhao, Liu Hui, Yelü Mengjian, Yelü Guyu

entries.zh: 漢以璽書賜二千石，唐疏刺史、縣令於屏，以示獎率，故二史有《循吏》、《良吏》之傳。
entries.en: Under the Han, imperial edicts sealed with the dynastic seal were conferred on the two-thousand-dan officials; under the Tang, the names of prefects and county magistrates were inscribed on screens as models of reward and emulation—hence both histories include biographies of Diligent Officials and Good Officials.
entries.literal: The Han used imperial-sealed documents to bestow on the two-thousand-dan officials; the Tang inscribed prefects and county magistrates on screens to display encouragement and standards—hence the two histories have biographies of "Diligent Officials" and "Good Officials."

entries.zh: 遼自太祖創業，太宗撫有燕、薊，任賢使能之道，亦略備矣。
entries.en: From the time Emperor Taizu founded the Liao state and Emperor Taizong brought Yan and Ji under rule, the practice of appointing worthies and putting talent to use was largely in place as well.
entries.literal: From the Liao, since Emperor Taizu founded the enterprise and Emperor Taizong pacified and held Yan and Ji, the way of appointing worthies and employing the able was also largely complete.

entries.zh: 然惟朝廷參置國官，吏州縣者多遵唐制。
entries.en: Yet only at court were national offices established in concert; administration of prefectures and counties largely followed Tang practice.
entries.literal: Yet only at court were national offices jointly established; those who administered prefectures and counties mostly followed Tang institutions.

entries.zh: 歷世既久，選舉益嚴。
entries.en: As generations passed, recruitment and selection grew ever stricter.
entries.literal: As generations passed, selection and appointment grew stricter.

entries.zh: 時又分遣重臣巡行境內，察賢否而進退之。
entries.en: The court also sent senior ministers on circuit through the realm to inspect officials and advance or remove them according to merit.
entries.literal: At the time they also dispatched senior ministers in separate missions to tour within the borders, examining worthiness and unworthiness to promote or dismiss.

entries.zh: 是以治民、理財、決獄、弭盜，各有其人。
entries.en: Thus for governing the people, managing revenue, adjudicating cases, and suppressing banditry, there were men fit for each task.
entries.literal: Therefore in governing the people, managing finances, deciding cases, and quelling banditry, each had its man.

entries.zh: 考其德政，雖未足以與諸循、良之列，抑亦可謂能吏矣。
entries.en: Judged by their conduct in office, they may not fully measure up to the ranks of diligent and good officials, yet they may still be called capable administrators.
entries.literal: Examining their virtuous administration, although not sufficient to rank with the various diligent and good officials, they may still be called capable officials.

entries.zh: 作《能吏傳》。
entries.en: Hence this "Biographies of Capable Officials."
entries.literal: This composes the "Biographies of Capable Officials."

entries.zh: 大公鼎，渤海人，先世籍遼陽率賓縣。
entries.en: Da Gongding was a Bohai native whose family had long been registered in Shuai-bin County in Liaoyang.
entries.literal: Da Gongding was a man of Bohai; his forebears were registered in Shuai-bin County, Liaoyang.

entries.zh: 統和間，徙遼東豪右以實中京，因家於大定。
entries.en: During the Tonghe reign, powerful families of eastern Liao were relocated to populate the Central Capital, and his household thereafter made its home in Dading.
entries.literal: During the Tonghe era, powerful families of eastern Liao were moved to populate the Central Capital, and his family therefore settled in Dading.

entries.zh: 曾祖忠，禮賓使。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Zhong served as Director of Ceremonial Reception.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Zhong was Director of Ceremonial Reception.

entries.zh: 父信，興中主簿。
entries.en: His father Xin was Registrar of Xingzhong.
entries.literal: His father Xin was Registrar of Xingzhong.

entries.zh: 公鼎幼莊願，長而好學。
entries.en: Gongding was grave and dutiful as a boy and devoted himself to study as he grew.
entries.literal: Gongding in youth was solemn and earnest; grown, he loved learning.

entries.zh: 咸雍十年，登進士第，調沈州觀察判官。
entries.en: In the tenth year of the Xianyong era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed acting investigating commissioner of Shenzhou.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Xianyong he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Acting Investigating Commissioner of Shenzhou.

entries.zh: 時遼東雨水傷稼，北樞密院大發瀕河丁壯以完堤防。
entries.en: At that time heavy rains in eastern Liao had damaged the harvest, and the Northern Privy Council conscripted large numbers of men along the riverbanks to repair the dikes.
entries.literal: At the time rains in eastern Liao damaged the crops; the Northern Privy Council greatly mobilized able-bodied men along the river to complete the dikes.

entries.zh: 有司承令峻急，公鼎獨曰：「邊障甫寧，大興役事，非利國便農之道。」
entries.en: The responsible offices enforced the order with harsh urgency, but Gongding alone said, "The frontier has only just settled down. To launch major corvée projects now is not the way to serve the state or ease the burden on farmers."
entries.literal: The offices, carrying out orders harshly and urgently, Gongding alone said: "The frontier has only just been pacified; to launch great labor projects is not the way to benefit the state and ease farming."

entries.zh: 乃疏奏其事。
entries.en: He thereupon submitted a memorial on the matter.
entries.literal: He then memorialized the matter in a memorial.

entries.zh: 朝廷從之，罷役，水亦不為災。
entries.en: The court approved his request, halted the corvée, and the floods never became a catastrophe.
entries.literal: The court assented, halted the labor, and the waters likewise did not become a disaster.

entries.zh: 瀕河千里，人莫不悅。
entries.en: For a thousand li along the river, the people were universally grateful.
entries.literal: Along the river for a thousand li, none among the people failed to rejoice.

entries.zh: 改良鄉令，省徭役，務農桑，建孔子廟學，部民服化。
entries.en: As magistrate of Liang Township he streamlined local administration, reduced corvée, promoted farming and sericulture, and founded a Confucian temple and school; the people of his district were thoroughly won over.
entries.literal: He was reassigned as magistrate of Liangxiang, reduced corvée and labor service, devoted effort to farming and sericulture, built a Confucian temple and school, and the people of his district submitted to transformation.

entries.zh: 累遷興國軍節度副使。
entries.en: He was promoted in due course to vice military commissioner of Xingguo Army.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Xingguo Army.

entries.zh: 時有隸鷹坊者，以羅畢為名，擾害田里。
entries.en: At the time men attached to the imperial Falcon Office, operating under the name of "netting and closing" (for hawking), preyed on the countryside and harassed the farming districts.
entries.literal: At the time there were men attached to the Falcon Office who, under the name of "netting and closing," harassed and harmed the fields and hamlets.

entries.zh: 歲久，民不堪。
entries.en: Year after year the people could endure it no longer.
entries.literal: Year after year, the people could not bear it.

entries.zh: 公鼎言於上，即命禁戢。
entries.en: Gongding reported the abuse to the throne, and an immediate order was issued to suppress it.
entries.literal: Gongding spoke to the throne, and an order was immediately issued to forbid and restrain them.

entries.zh: 會公鼎造朝，大臣諭上嘉納之意，公鼎曰：「一郡獲安，誠為大幸；
entries.en: When Gongding came to court, a senior minister conveyed the emperor's praise and approval. Gongding said, "That one commandery has found peace is indeed a great blessing;
entries.literal: When Gongding came to court, a senior minister conveyed the emperor's intent to commend and accept his service; Gongding said: "That one commandery has found peace is truly a great fortune;

entries.zh: 他郡如此者眾，願均其賜於天下。」
entries.en: yet many other commanderies suffer the same abuse. I beg that this benefit be extended equally throughout the realm."
entries.literal: many other commanderies suffer likewise—I wish to extend this grace equally to all under Heaven."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court granted his request.
entries.literal: The court assented.

entries.zh: 徙長春州錢帛都提點。
entries.en: He was transferred to serve as chief intendant of cash and silks at Changchunzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Chief Intendant of Cash and Silks at Changchunzhou.

entries.zh: 車駕如春水，貴主例為假貸，公鼎曰：「豈可輟官用，徇人情？」
entries.en: When the imperial carriage went to the spring hunt, noble ladies routinely sought loans from the treasury. Gongding said, "How can official funds be suspended to indulge private favor?"
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage went to the spring hunt, noble ladies customarily sought loans; Gongding said: "How can one halt official funds to indulge personal favor?"

entries.zh: 拒之。
entries.en: He refused them.
entries.literal: He refused them.

entries.zh: 頗聞怨詈語，曰：「此吾職，不敢廢也。」
entries.en: He heard much bitter complaint, but said, "This is my duty, and I dare not neglect it."
entries.literal: He heard much resentful cursing and said: "This is my duty—I dare not neglect it."

entries.zh: 俄拜大理卿，多所平反。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed director of the Court of Review and reversed many wrongful convictions.
entries.literal: Shortly he was appointed Director of the Court of Review and reversed many wrongful convictions.

entries.zh: 天祚即位，歷長寧軍節度使、南京副留守，改東京戶部使。
entries.en: When Emperor Tianzuo acceded, he served successively as military commissioner of Changning Army and vice guardian of the Southern Capital, then was appointed commissioner of the Eastern Capital Revenue Bureau.
entries.literal: When Emperor Tianzuo took the throne, he served successively as Military Commissioner of Changning Army and Vice Guardian of the Southern Capital, then was changed to Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Revenue Bureau.

entries.zh: 時盜殺留守蕭保先，始利其財，因而倡亂。
entries.en: At that time bandits murdered the guardian Xiao Baoxian, at first for his wealth and thereby inciting wider disorder.
entries.literal: At the time bandits killed the Guardian Xiao Baoxian, at first coveting his wealth and thereby inciting disorder.

entries.zh: 民亦互生猜忌，家自為鬥。
entries.en: The populace grew mutually suspicious, and households took up arms against one another.
entries.literal: The people also mutually bred suspicion, and households fought among themselves.

entries.zh: 公鼎單騎行郡，陳以禍福，眾皆投兵而拜曰：「是不欺我，敢弗聽命。」
entries.en: Gongding rode alone through the commandery, explaining the consequences of obedience and rebellion. The people cast down their weapons and bowed, saying, "This man does not deceive us—we dare not disobey his command."
entries.literal: Gongding rode alone through the commandery, setting forth fortune and misfortune; the multitude all cast down weapons and bowed, saying: "This man does not deceive us—we dare not disobey his command."

entries.zh: 安輯如故。
entries.en: Tranquility was restored as before.
entries.literal: Tranquility and order were restored as before.

entries.zh: 拜中京留守，賜貞亮功臣，乘傳赴官。
entries.en: He was appointed guardian of the Central Capital, granted the title Meritorious Minister of Upright Integrity, and traveled to his post by imperial relay.
entries.literal: He was appointed Guardian of the Central Capital, granted the title Meritorious Minister of Upright Integrity, and went to his post by relay.

entries.zh: 時盜賊充斥，有遇公鼎於路者，即叩馬乞自新。
entries.en: Bandits and robbers filled the land. Those who met Gongding on the road would halt his horse and beg to reform.
entries.literal: At the time bandits and robbers filled the land; those who met Gongding on the road would immediately knock on his horse and beg to reform.

entries.zh: 公鼎給以符約，俾還業，聞者接踵而至。
entries.en: Gongding issued them written pledges of amnesty and sent them back to their trades; word spread and others came in steady succession.
entries.literal: Gongding gave them tally-pledges and enabled them to return to their occupations; those who heard came one after another.

entries.zh: 不旬日，境內清肅。
entries.en: Within ten days the entire jurisdiction was pacified.
entries.literal: Within less than ten days, the territory within the borders was clear and orderly.

entries.zh: 天祚聞之，加賜保節功臣。
entries.en: When Tianzuo heard of this, he additionally granted him the title Meritorious Minister Who Guards Integrity.
entries.literal: Tianzuo heard of it and additionally granted him the title Meritorious Minister Who Guards Integrity.

entries.zh: 時人心反側，公鼎慮生變，請布恩惠以安之，為之肆赦。
entries.en: Popular sentiment was still unsettled. Fearing further unrest, Gongding petitioned for a display of imperial grace to reassure the people, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: At the time hearts were unsettled; Gongding feared trouble would arise, requested that favor be spread to settle them, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 公鼎累表乞歸，不許。
entries.en: Gongding repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, but permission was denied.
entries.literal: Gongding repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; it was not granted.

entries.zh: 會奴賊張撒八率無賴嘯聚，公鼎欲擊而勢有不能。
entries.en: When the slave-rebel Zhang Sabba rallied desperadoes in open revolt, Gongding wished to attack but found his forces inadequate.
entries.literal: When the slave-bandit Zhang Sabba led ruffians in clamorous assembly, Gongding wished to strike but found his strength insufficient.

entries.zh: 嘆曰：「吾欲謝事久矣，為世故所牽，不幸至此，豈命也夫！」
entries.en: He sighed and said, "I have long wished to leave office, yet worldly affairs kept me bound. To come to this unhappy pass—can it be fate?"
entries.literal: He sighed and said: "I have long wished to withdraw from office, yet was dragged along by worldly affairs; unhappily it has come to this—is it fate!"

entries.zh: 因憂憤成疾。
entries.en: He fell ill from worry and indignation.
entries.literal: He thereby fell ill from worry and indignation.

entries.zh: 保大元年卒，年七十九。
entries.en: He died in the first year of the Baoda era, at the age of seventy-nine.
entries.literal: In the first year of Baoda he died, aged seventy-nine.

entries.zh: 能吏 ○大公鼎蕭文馬人望耶律鐸魯斡楊遵勖王棠
entries.en: Capable Officials — Da Gongding, Xiao Wen, Ma Renwang, Yelü Duoluwo, Yang Zunxu, and Wang Tang
entries.literal: Capable Officials ○ Da Gongding, Xiao Wen, Ma Renwang, Yelü Duoluwo, Yang Zunxu, Wang Tang

entries.zh: ○邢簡妻陳氏耶律氏常哥耶律奴妻蕭氏耶律朮者妻蕭氏耶律中妻蕭氏
entries.en: ○ Lady Chen, wife of Xing Jian; the Yelü clanswoman Changge; Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Nu; Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Shuzhe; Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Zhong
entries.literal: ○ The wife of Xing Jian, Lady Chen; the Yelü clanswoman Changge; the wife of Yelü Nu, Lady Xiao; the wife of Yelü Shuzhe, Lady Xiao; the wife of Yelü Zhong, Lady Xiao

entries.zh: 邢簡妻陳氏，營州人。
entries.en: Lady Chen, wife of Xing Jian, came from Yingzhou.
entries.literal: The wife of Xing Jian, Lady Chen, was a native of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 父陘，五代時累官司徒。
entries.en: Her father Chen Xing rose repeatedly to the post of Minister over the Masses (situ) under the Five Dynasties.
entries.literal: Her father Chen Xing repeatedly held the office of situ (Minister over the Masses) during the Five Dynasties period.

entries.zh: 陳氏甫笄，涉通經義，凡覽詩賦，輒能誦，尤好吟詠，時以女秀才名之。
entries.en: As soon as Lady Chen came of age, she had mastered the classics; whatever poetry or fu she read, she could recite from memory; she loved composing verse above all, and people called her the "female scholar."
entries.literal: When Lady Chen had just reached the age of pinning up her hair, she had thoroughly grasped the meaning of the classics; whenever she looked upon poetry and fu, she could at once recite them; she especially loved composing verse, and at the time she was styled the "female xiucai."

entries.zh: 年二十，歸於簡。
entries.en: At twenty she married Xing Jian.
entries.literal: At the age of twenty she was married to Jian.

entries.zh: 孝舅姑，閨門和睦，親黨推重。
entries.en: She was devoted to her parents-in-law, kept the household harmonious, and won the respect of kin and neighbors.
entries.literal: She was filial toward her parents-in-law; the inner quarters were harmonious; relatives and associates held her in esteem.

entries.zh: 有六子，陳氏親教以經。
entries.en: She bore six sons and taught them the classics herself.
entries.literal: She had six sons; Lady Chen personally instructed them in the classics.

entries.zh: 後二子抱樸、抱質皆以賢，位宰相。
entries.en: Two of her sons, Baopu and Baozhi, later proved themselves worthy men and rose to the chancellorship.
entries.literal: Later two of her sons, Baopu and Baozhi, both proved worthy and reached the rank of chief minister.

entries.zh: 統和十二年卒。
entries.en: She died in the twelfth year of Tonghe (994).
entries.literal: She died in the twelfth year of the Tonghe reign period.

entries.zh: 睿智皇后聞之，嗟悼，贈魯國夫人，刻石以表其行。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Ruizhi heard of her death, she sighed in grief, granted her the title Lady of Lu, and had a stone inscription carved to commemorate her conduct.
entries.literal: When the Empress Dowager Ruizhi heard of it, she sighed and mourned, bestowed upon her the title Lady of Lu, and had stone carved to commemorate her conduct.

entries.zh: 及遷祔，遣使以祭。
entries.en: When her remains were moved to joint burial with her husband, the court sent an envoy to perform the rites.
entries.literal: When her remains were moved to joint entombment, the court sent an envoy to offer sacrifice.

entries.zh: 論者謂貞靜柔順，婦道母儀始終無慊雲。
entries.en: Commentators said she was chaste, quiet, gentle, and compliant—a model of wifehood and motherhood from first to last, without a single lapse.
entries.literal: Commentators said she was chaste, quiet, gentle, and compliant—wifehood and motherhood in model form, from beginning to end without fault.

entries.zh: 耶律中妻蕭氏，小字挼蘭，韓國王惠之四世孫。
entries.en: Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Zhong, known by the childhood name Ruolan, was a fourth-generation descendant of King Hui of Han.
entries.literal: The wife of Yelü Zhong, Lady Xiao, childhood name Ruolan, fourth-generation descendant of King Hui of Han.

entries.zh: 聰慧謹願。
entries.en: Intelligent, clever, careful, and dutiful.
entries.literal: Intelligent, clever, careful and obedient.

entries.zh: 年二十歸於中，事夫敬順，親戚咸譽其德。
entries.en: At twenty she married Zhong; she served her husband with respect and compliance, and kinfolk all praised her virtue.
entries.literal: At twenty she married Zhong; in serving her husband she was respectful and compliant; kinfolk all praised her virtue.

entries.zh: 中嘗謂曰：「汝可粗知書，以前貞淑為鑒。」
entries.en: Zhong once told her, "You should gain some rough knowledge of books, and take the chaste and worthy women of old as your mirror."
entries.literal: Zhong once said to her, "You should have some rough knowledge of books; take former women of chaste integrity as your mirror."

entries.zh: 遂發心誦習，多涉古今。
entries.en: Thereupon she devoted herself to study and recitation, and ranged widely through ancient and modern writings.
entries.literal: Thereupon she set her mind to recite and study, and ranged widely through ancient and modern works.

entries.zh: 天慶中，為賊所執，潛置刃於履，誓曰：「人欲汙我者，即死之。」
entries.en: During Tianqing she was seized by bandits; she secretly hid a blade in her shoe and swore, "Whoever would defile me shall die by it at once."
entries.literal: In the Tianqing period she was seized by bandits; she secretly placed a blade in her shoe and swore, "Whoever wishes to defile me shall die by this at once."

entries.zh: 至夜，賊遁而免。
entries.en: By night the bandits fled, and she escaped.
entries.literal: By night the bandits fled and she escaped.

entries.zh: 久之，帝召中為五院都監，中謂妻曰：「吾本無宦情，今不能免。
entries.en: After a long interval the emperor summoned Zhong to be Chief Superintendent of the Five Tribes; Zhong said to his wife, "I never wished for office, yet now I cannot escape it.
entries.literal: After a long time the emperor summoned Zhong to be Chief Superintendent of the Five Tribes; Zhong said to his wife, "I originally had no wish for office, yet now cannot escape it.

entries.zh: 我當以死報國，汝能從我乎？」
entries.en: I shall repay the state with my life—will you follow me?"
entries.literal: I shall repay the state with my death—can you follow me?"

entries.zh: 挼蘭對曰：「謹奉教。」
entries.en: Ruolan answered, "I respectfully accept your instruction."
entries.literal: Ruolan replied, "I respectfully accept your instruction."

entries.zh: 及金兵徇地嶺西，盡徙其民，中守節死。
entries.en: When Jin troops overran the territory west of the mountains and relocated all the people, Zhong held to his integrity and died.
entries.literal: When Jin troops overran the land west of the mountains, they moved all the people; Zhong guarded his integrity and died.

entries.zh: 挼蘭悲戚不形於外，人怪之。
entries.en: Ruolan showed no outward sign of grief, and people found it strange.
entries.literal: Ruolan's grief and sorrow did not show outwardly; people found it strange.

entries.zh: 俄躍馬突出，至中死所自殺。
entries.en: Suddenly she spurred her horse and dashed out, rode to where Zhong had died, and killed herself.
entries.literal: Suddenly she spurred her horse and burst forth, reaching the place where Zhong had died, and killed herself.

entries.zh: 耶律氏，太師適魯之妹，小字常哥。
entries.en: A woman of the Yelü clan, sister of Grand Preceptor Shilu, was known by the childhood name Changge.
entries.literal: A woman of the Yelü clan, younger sister of Grand Preceptor Shilu, childhood name Changge.

entries.zh: 幼爽秀，有成人風。
entries.en: As a child she was bright and graceful, with the poise of a grown woman.
entries.literal: In youth she was clever and elegant, with the bearing of an adult.

entries.zh: 及長，操行修潔，自誓不嫁。
entries.en: When she came of age, her conduct was refined and pure, and she vowed never to marry.
entries.literal: When she had grown, her conduct was cultivated and pure; she vowed never to marry.

entries.zh: 能詩文，不茍作。
entries.en: She could write poetry and prose, but would not compose lightly or without purpose.
entries.literal: She could compose poetry and prose and would not write carelessly.

entries.zh: 讀《通曆》，見前人得失，歷能品藻。
entries.en: Reading the Comprehensive Chronicles, she could appraise and classify the successes and failures of past rulers whenever she encountered them.
entries.literal: Reading the Comprehensive Chronicles, whenever she saw the gains and losses of men of old, she could always appraise and classify them.

entries.zh: 咸雍間，作文以述時政。
entries.en: During the Xianyong reign she wrote an essay setting forth her views on current affairs.
entries.literal: During the Xianyong era she wrote an essay to set forth current government.

entries.zh: 其略曰：「君以民為體，民以君為心。
entries.en: Its gist ran: "The ruler takes the people as his body; the people take the ruler as their heart.
entries.literal: Its gist said: "The ruler takes the people as his body; the people take the ruler as their heart.

entries.zh: 人主當任忠賢，人臣當去比周，則政化平，陰陽順。
entries.en: The sovereign should employ the loyal and worthy; ministers should cast off cliques and factions—then government will be even and yin and yang will be in harmony.
entries.literal: The sovereign ought to employ the loyal and worthy; ministers ought to remove factional cliques—then government will be made level and yin and yang will be in harmony.

entries.zh: 欲懷遠則崇恩尚德，欲強國則輕徭薄賦。
entries.en: To win over distant peoples, honor benevolence and virtue; to strengthen the state, lighten corvée labor and reduce taxes.
entries.literal: If one wishes to cherish those afar, then esteem benevolence and honor virtue; if one wishes to strengthen the state, then lighten corvée labor and reduce taxes.

entries.zh: 四端五典為治教之本，六府三事實生民之命。
entries.en: The Four Beginnings and Five Canons are the foundation of rule and instruction; the Six Storehouses and Three Affairs are the lifeblood of the people.
entries.literal: The Four Beginnings and Five Canons are the root of governance and instruction; the Six Storehouses and Three Affairs are the fate of the living people.

entries.zh: 淫侈可以為戒，勤儉可以為師。
entries.en: Let extravagance be your warning and thrift your teacher.
entries.literal: Extravagance may serve as a warning; thrift may serve as a teacher.

entries.zh: 錯枉則人不敢詐，顯忠則人不敢欺。
entries.en: Set crooked things straight and none will dare to cheat; make loyalty plain and none will dare to deceive.
entries.literal: Rectifying the crooked, then people will not dare to cheat; displaying loyalty, then people will not dare to deceive.

entries.zh: 勿泥空門，崇飾土木；
entries.en: Do not cling to the empty gates of Buddhism, lavishing adornment on earth and timber;
entries.literal: Do not cling to the empty gates, adorning and decking out earth and timber;

entries.zh: 勿事邊鄙，妄費金帛。
entries.en: do not treat the borderlands lightly, squandering gold and silk in vain.
entries.literal: Do not treat the border regions lightly, recklessly wasting gold and silk.

entries.zh: 滿當思溢，安必慮危。
entries.en: When the cup is full, think of spillage; when you are secure, reckon with danger.
entries.literal: When full, think of overflowing; when secure, consider danger.

entries.zh: 刑罰當罪，則民勸善。
entries.en: When punishments fit the crime, the people are moved toward goodness.
entries.literal: When punishments match crimes, then the people will be encouraged to do good.

entries.zh: 不寶遠物，則賢者至。
entries.en: If you do not treasure exotic goods from afar, the worthy will come to you.
entries.literal: If one does not treasure distant goods, then the worthy will come.

entries.zh: 建萬世磐石之業，制諸部強橫之心。
entries.en: Build an enterprise firm as bedrock for ten thousand generations, and curb the overbearing hearts of the tribes.
entries.literal: Establish the enterprise of the eternal bedrock cliff, restrain the hearts of the various tribes that are overbearing.

entries.zh: 欲率下則先正身，欲治遠則始朝廷。」
entries.en: To lead those below, first set your own person right; to govern what is distant, begin at court."
entries.literal: If one wishes to lead those below, one must first rectify oneself; if one wishes to govern what is far, one must begin at court."

entries.zh: 上稱善。
entries.en: The emperor praised her essay as excellent.
entries.literal: The sovereign praised it as good.

entries.zh: 時樞密使耶律乙辛愛其才，屢求詩，常哥遺以回文。
entries.en: At the time Commissioner of Military Affairs Yelü Yixin admired her talent and repeatedly asked her for poems; Changge sent him a palindrome verse in reply.
entries.literal: At the time the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yelü Yixin admired her talent and repeatedly asked for poems; Changge sent him a palindrome verse.

entries.zh: 乙辛知其諷己，銜之。
entries.en: Yixin knew she was satirizing him and harbored a grudge.
entries.literal: Yixin knew that it satirized him and bore resentment.

entries.zh: 大康三年，皇太子坐事，乙辛誣以罪，按無跡，獲免。
entries.en: In the third year of Dakang (1077), when the heir apparent was implicated in a case, Yixin falsely charged him with a crime; the investigation found no evidence, and the prince was spared.
entries.literal: In the third year of Dakang, when the heir apparent was implicated in an affair, Yixin falsely charged him with a crime; though investigated with no trace found, he escaped punishment.

entries.zh: 會兄適魯謫鎮州，常哥與俱，常布衣疏食。
entries.en: When her elder brother Shilu was banished to Zhen Prefecture, Changge went with him and lived always in plain clothes on simple fare.
entries.literal: When her elder brother Shilu was demoted to Zhen Prefecture, Changge went with him, always wearing plain clothes and eating simple food.

entries.zh: 人問曰：「何自苦如此？」
entries.en: Someone asked her, "Why do you torment yourself like this?"
entries.literal: Someone asked, "Why torment yourself in this way?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「皇儲無罪遭廢，我輩豈可美食安寢。」
entries.en: She answered, "The heir apparent was innocent yet deposed—how can people like us eat fine food and sleep in peace?"
entries.literal: She replied: "The heir apparent was innocent yet deposed—how can we of his party eat fine food and sleep in peace?"

entries.zh: 及太子被害，不勝哀痛。
entries.en: When the heir apparent was killed, her grief was beyond bearing.
entries.literal: When the heir apparent was killed, she was overcome with unbearable grief.

entries.zh: 年七十，卒於家。
entries.en: At seventy she died at home.
entries.literal: At the age of seventy she died at home.

entries.zh: 耶律奴妻蕭氏，小字意辛，國舅駙馬都尉陶蘇斡之女。
entries.en: Lady Xiao, wife of Yelü Nu, known by the childhood name Yixin, was the daughter of the State Uncle and Commandant-escort (imperial son-in-law) Taosuwo.
entries.literal: The wife of Yelü Nu, Lady Xiao, childhood name Yixin, daughter of the State Uncle and Commandant-escort Taosuwo.

entries.zh: 母胡獨公主。
entries.en: Her mother was Princess Hudu.
entries.literal: Her mother was Princess Hudu.

entries.zh: 意幸美姿容，年二十始適奴。
entries.en: Yixin was graced with fine features; at twenty she was first married to Nu.
entries.literal: Yixin possessed a fine countenance; at twenty she was first married to Nu.

entries.zh: 事親睦族，以孝謹聞。
entries.en: She treated her kin with care and kept the clan harmonious, and was known for filial devotion.
entries.literal: She served kin with harmony toward the clan and was known for filial reverence.

entries.zh: 嘗與娣姒會，爭言厭魅以取夫寵，意辛曰：「厭魅不若禮法。」
entries.en: Once, at a gathering of sisters-in-law, they argued over whether witchcraft was the better way to win a husband's favor; Yixin said, "Witchcraft is not as good as ritual propriety."
entries.literal: Once at a gathering of sisters-in-law they disputed whether witchcraft was better to win a husband's favor; Yixin said, "Witchcraft is not as good as ritual and law."

entries.zh: 眾問其故，意辛曰：「修己以潔，奉長以敬，事夫以柔，撫下以寬，毋使君子見其輕易，此之為禮法，自然取重於夫。
entries.en: When they asked why, Yixin said, "Cultivate yourself in purity, serve your elders with respect, attend your husband with gentleness, and treat those below with generosity; do not let any worthy man see you behave lightly. That is ritual propriety, and by it you will naturally win your husband's regard.
entries.literal: The assembly asked the reason; Yixin said, "Cultivate oneself to purity, serve elders with respect, attend the husband with gentleness, nurture those below with generosity—do not let gentlemen see one's lightness; this is ritual and law, and naturally one will be honored by the husband.

entries.zh: 以厭魅獲寵，獨不愧於心乎！」
entries.en: To win favor through witchcraft—would you not be ashamed before your own heart!"
entries.literal: To gain favor through witchcraft—would one not alone be ashamed before one's heart!"

entries.zh: 聞者大慚。
entries.en: Those who heard were deeply ashamed.
entries.literal: Those who heard were greatly ashamed.

entries.zh: 初，奴與樞密使乙辛有隙。
entries.en: Earlier, Nu and Commissioner of Military Affairs Yixin had been at odds.
entries.literal: At first Nu and the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yixin had a rift.

entries.zh: 及皇太子廢，被誣奪爵，沒入興聖宮，流烏古部。
entries.en: When the heir apparent was deposed, Nu was falsely accused, stripped of his rank, confined in the Xingsheng Palace, and exiled to the Wugu tribe.
entries.literal: When the heir apparent was deposed, he was falsely accused, his nobility stripped, and he was confiscated into the Xingsheng Palace and exiled to the Wugu tribe.

entries.zh: 上以意辛公主之女，欲使絕婚。
entries.en: Because Yixin was a princess's daughter, the emperor wished to dissolve the marriage.
entries.literal: Because the emperor considered Yixin a daughter of the princess, he wished to make her end the marriage.

entries.zh: 意辛辭曰：「陛下以妾葭莩之親，使免流竄，實天地之恩。
entries.en: Yixin declined, saying, "Your Majesty, because I am kin by marriage, has spared me banishment—that is grace vast as Heaven and Earth.
entries.literal: Yixin declined, saying, "Your Majesty, owing to my humble kinship by marriage, has spared me exile—that is truly the grace of Heaven and Earth.

entries.zh: 然夫歸之義，生死以之。
entries.en: Yet the righteousness of a wife who follows her husband is to live and die with him.
entries.literal: Yet the righteousness of a wife following her husband is to live or die with him.

entries.zh: 妾自笄年從奴，一旦臨難，頓爾乖離，背綱常之道，於禽獸何異？
entries.en: From the day I pinned up my hair I have followed Nu; now, at the first stroke of hardship, to be torn from him at once and turn my back on the constant way—how would that differ from the beasts?
entries.literal: From the year I pinned up my hair I followed Nu; suddenly meeting hardship and at once being torn apart—to turn my back on the constant way of the norms would make me no different from beasts!

entries.zh: 幸陛下哀憐，與奴俱行，妾即死無恨！」
entries.en: If Your Majesty will pity me and let me go with Nu, I shall die without regret!"
entries.literal: May Your Majesty pity me and let me go with Nu together—then even if I die I shall have no regret!"

entries.zh: 帝感其言，從之。
entries.en: The emperor, moved by her words, granted her request.
entries.literal: The emperor, moved by her words, assented.

entries.zh: 意辛久在貶所，親執役事，雖勞無難色。
entries.en: Yixin long remained in exile, personally performing menial labor; though the work was hard, her face showed no distress.
entries.literal: Yixin long remained at the place of banishment, personally performing menial tasks; though toilsome, her face showed no difficulty.

entries.zh: 事夫禮敬，有加於舊。
entries.en: In serving her husband with ritual respect, she was even more devoted than before.
entries.literal: In serving her husband with ritual respect, she was even more so than before.

entries.zh: 壽隆中，上書乞子孫為著帳郎君。
entries.en: During Shoulong she submitted a memorial asking that her sons and grandsons be enrolled as registered gentlemen of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: During Shoulong, she submitted a memorial asking that her sons and grandsons be made zhuanglang gentlemen.

entries.zh: 帝嘉其節，召舉家還。
entries.en: The emperor praised her integrity and summoned her entire household home.
entries.literal: The emperor praised her integrity and summoned her whole family to return.

entries.zh: 子國隱，乾統間始仕。
entries.en: Her son Guoyin first entered office during Qiantong.
entries.literal: Her son Guoyin began to hold office in the Qiantong period.

entries.zh: 保大中，意辛在臨潢，謂諸子曰：「吾度盧彥倫必叛，汝輩速避，我當死之。」
entries.en: During Baoda, while Yixin was at Linhuang, she told her sons, "I am sure Lu Yanlun will rebel—you must flee at once; I shall die for it."
entries.literal: In Baoda, Yixin was at Linhuang and told her sons, "I judge that Lu Yanlun will certainly rebel—you all flee quickly; I shall die for this."

entries.zh: 賊至，遇害。
entries.en: When the rebels came, she was killed.
entries.literal: When the bandits arrived, she met with disaster and was killed.

entries.zh: 直魯古，吐谷渾人。
entries.en: Zhilugu was a native of Tuyuhun.
entries.literal: Zhilugu was a man of Tuyuhun.

entries.zh: 初，太祖破吐谷渾，一騎士棄橐反射，不中而去。
