entries.en: Early on, when Taizu routed the Tuyuhun, one rider cast down a bag and shot back at it; his arrow missed, and he rode away.
entries.literal: At the beginning, when Taizu defeated Tuyuhun, one rider abandoned a bag and shot back at it; he missed and departed.

entries.zh: 及追兵開橐視之，中得一嬰兒，即直魯古也。
entries.en: When the pursuers opened the bag and looked inside, they found an infant — Zhilugu himself.
entries.literal: When the pursuing troops opened the bag and looked, they obtained an infant within — this was Zhilugu.

entries.zh: 因所俘者問其故，乃知射橐者嬰之父也。
entries.en: They questioned the captives about what had happened and learned that the man who shot the bag was the child's father.
entries.literal: Through those who had been captured they asked the reason, and thus knew that the one who shot the bag was the infant's father.

entries.zh: 世善醫，雖馬上視疾，亦知標本。
entries.en: His family had long practiced medicine; even when treating the sick from horseback, he could distinguish root cause from symptom.
entries.literal: For generations they excelled at medicine; even when examining illness on horseback, he knew root and branch.

entries.zh: 意不欲子為人所得，欲殺之耳。
entries.en: He had not wanted his son to fall into enemy hands and had meant only to kill the child.
entries.literal: His intention was that he did not wish his son to be taken by others — he had meant to kill him, that was all.

entries.zh: 由是進於太祖，淳欽皇后收養之。
entries.en: He was then brought before Taizu, and Empress Chunqin took him in and raised him.
entries.literal: Because of this he was presented to Taizu, and Empress Chunqin adopted and raised him.

entries.zh: 長亦能醫，專事針灸。
entries.en: As an adult he too practiced medicine, devoting himself to acupuncture and moxibustion.
entries.literal: When he grew up he too could practice medicine, specializing in acupuncture and moxibustion.

entries.zh: 太宗時，以太醫給侍。
entries.en: Under Taizong he served as an imperial physician in attendance.
entries.literal: In Taizong's time he served as imperial physician in attendance.

entries.zh: 嘗撰《脈訣》、《針灸書》，行於世。
entries.en: He once wrote Pulse Diagnosis and A Book on Acupuncture and Moxibustion, both of which circulated widely.
entries.literal: He once compiled Pulse Diagnosis and A Book on Acupuncture and Moxibustion, which circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 年九十卒。
entries.en: He died at the age of ninety.
entries.literal: He died at the age of ninety.

entries.zh: 王白，冀州人，明天文，善卜筮，晉司天少監，太宗入汴得之。
entries.en: Wang Bai was a native of Jizhou who understood astronomy and excelled at divination; he had served as Jin's Associate Director of the Bureau of Astronomy, and Taizong acquired him when he entered Bian.
entries.literal: Wang Bai was a man of Jizhou. He understood astronomy and excelled at divination and milfoil; he had been Jin's Associate Director of the Bureau of Astronomy, and Taizong obtained him when he entered Bian.

entries.zh: 應歷十九年，王子只沒以事下獄，其母求卜，白曰：「此人當王，未能殺也，毋過憂。」
entries.en: In the nineteenth year of Yingli, Prince Zhizhimei was imprisoned on a charge; his mother sought divination, and Bai said, "This man is destined to be king — he cannot yet be killed. Do not worry excessively."
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yingli, Prince Zhizhimei was imprisoned on a charge; his mother sought divination, and Bai said, "This man is destined to be king — he cannot yet be killed. Do not worry excessively."

entries.zh: 景宗即位，釋其罪，封寧王，竟如其言。
entries.en: When Jingzong ascended the throne, he released Zhizhimei and enfeoffed him as Prince of Ning — exactly as Bai had predicted.
entries.literal: When Jingzong ascended the throne, he released him from his crime and enfeoffed him as Prince of Ning — exactly as Bai had said.

entries.zh: 凡決禍福多此類。
entries.en: His readings of fortune and misfortune were mostly of this kind.
entries.literal: In deciding fortune and misfortune, his judgments were mostly of this kind.

entries.zh: 保寧中，歷彰武、興國二軍節度使。
entries.en: During the Baoning era he served in succession as military commissioner of the Zhangwu and Xingguo armies.
entries.literal: During Baoning he served in succession as military commissioner of the Zhangwu and Xingguo armies.

entries.zh: 撰《百中歌》行於世。
entries.en: He wrote the "Song of a Hundred Hits," which circulated widely.
entries.literal: He compiled the "Song of a Hundred Hits," which circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 方技 ○直魯古王白魏璘耶律敵魯耶律乙不哥
entries.en: Arts and Techniques ○ Zhilugu, Wang Bai, Wei Lin, Yelü Diru, and Yelü Yibuge
entries.literal: Arts and Techniques ○ Zhilugu, Wang Bai, Wei Lin, Yelü Diru, Yelü Yibuge

entries.zh: 羅衣輕，不知其鄉里。
entries.en: Luo Yiqing's place of origin is not recorded.
entries.literal: Luo Yiqing—his native place is unknown.

entries.zh: 滑稽通變，一時諧謔，多所規諷。
entries.en: Quick-witted and adaptable, he was the leading comic at court and often couched admonition in playful speech.
entries.literal: Witty and resourceful, for a time the foremost in jest and banter, he offered much indirect remonstrance.

entries.zh: 興宗敗於李元昊也，單騎突出，幾不得脫。
entries.en: After Emperor Xingzong's defeat at the hands of Li Yuanhao of Western Xia, he fled the field alone and nearly failed to get away.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xingzong was defeated by Li Yuanhao, he broke through alone on horseback and barely escaped.

entries.zh: 先是，元昊獲遼人，輒劓其鼻，有奔北者惟恐追及。
entries.en: Before this, Yuanhao had captured Liao soldiers and routinely mutilated their noses, so men fleeing homeward lived in terror of being overtaken.
entries.literal: Earlier, whenever Yuanhao captured men of Liao, he would slice off their noses; those who fled north feared only that pursuers would catch them.

entries.zh: 故羅衣輕止之曰：「且觀鼻在否？」
entries.en: Luo Yiqing therefore halted him and quipped, "Let us first check whether your nose is still in place."
entries.literal: Therefore Luo Yiqing stopped him and said: "First let us see whether your nose is still there."

entries.zh: 上怒，以毳索系帳後，將殺之。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage, bound him with a fur cord behind the tent, and prepared to put him to death.
entries.literal: The emperor was enraged, tied him with a fur rope behind the tent, and was about to execute him.

entries.zh: 太子笑曰：「打諢底不是黃幡綽！」
entries.en: The crown prince laughed and said, "The fellow cracking jokes is no Huang Fanchuo!"
entries.literal: The crown prince laughed and said: "The one doing the comic patter is no Huang Fanchuo!"

entries.zh: 羅衣輕應聲曰：「行兵底亦不是唐太宗！」
entries.en: Luo Yiqing shot back at once, "And the one commanding the army is no Emperor Taizong of Tang either!"
entries.literal: Luo Yiqing answered on the spot: "The one leading troops in the field is no Emperor Taizong of Tang either!"

entries.zh: 上聞而釋之。
entries.en: Hearing this, the emperor set him free.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard this, he released him.

entries.zh: 上嘗與太弟重元狎昵，宴酣，許以千秋萬歲後傳位。
entries.en: The emperor had grown overly familiar with his younger brother Chongyuan; deep in wine at a banquet, he promised to abdicate in his favor in the distant future.
entries.literal: The emperor had once been on intimate terms with his younger brother Chongyuan; when the feast grew merry, he promised to pass the throne to him after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years.

entries.zh: 重元喜甚，驕縱不法。
entries.en: Chongyuan was elated and became arrogant and unrestrained.
entries.literal: Chongyuan was overjoyed and grew arrogant and lawless.

entries.zh: 又因雙陸，賭以居民城邑。
entries.en: They also played backgammon, wagering whole towns and their populations.
entries.literal: They also wagered at backgammon, staking towns and their inhabitants.

entries.zh: 帝屢不競，前後已償數城。
entries.en: The emperor lost again and again and had already forfeited several cities.
entries.literal: The emperor repeatedly lost and had already paid over several cities.

entries.zh: 重元既恃梁孝王之寵，又多鄭叔段之過，朝臣無敢言者，道路以目。
entries.en: Chongyuan enjoyed favor comparable to Prince Xiao of Liang under Emperor Wen of Han and repeated the overreaching of Duke Zhuang's brother Shuduan; no minister dared remonstrate, and travelers only dared signal their alarm with their eyes.
entries.literal: Chongyuan both relied on favor like Prince Xiao of Liang and committed faults like Duke Zhuang's younger brother Shuduan; court officials dared not speak, and people on the road exchanged glances in fear.

entries.zh: 一日復博，羅衣輕指其局曰：「雙陸休癡，和你都輸去也！」
entries.en: One day they were at the board again; Luo Yiqing pointed at the game and said, "Enough of this backgammon folly—you are going to lose everything to him!"
entries.literal: One day they were gambling again; Luo Yiqing pointed at the board and said: "Stop being mad about backgammon—you will lose everything to him!"

entries.zh: 帝始悟，不復戲。
entries.en: The emperor finally took the point and gave up the game.
entries.literal: The emperor then understood and no longer played.

entries.zh: 清寧間，以疾卒。
entries.en: He died of illness during the Qingning period.
entries.literal: During the Qingning era he died of illness.

entries.zh: ◎宦官 ○王繼恩趙安仁
entries.en: ◎ Eunuch Officials ○ Wang Jien and Zhao Anren
entries.literal: ◎ Eunuch Officials ○ Wang Jien and Zhao Anren

entries.zh: 趙安仁，字小喜，深州樂壽人，自幼被俘。
entries.en: Zhao Anren, whose style was Xiaoxi, came from Leshou in Shenzhou and had been taken captive as a boy.
entries.literal: Zhao Anren, style name Xiaoxi, a native of Leshou in Shenzhou, was captured while still a child.

entries.zh: 統和中，為黃門令、秦晉國王府祗候。
entries.en: During the Tonghe reign he served as Yellow Gate Commandant and attendant at the mansion of the Prince of Qin and Jin.
entries.literal: During the Tonghe era he served as Yellow Gate Commandant and attendant at the mansion of the Prince of Qin and Jin.

entries.zh: 王薨，授內侍省押班、禦院通進。
entries.en: After the prince's death he was appointed chief steward of the Inner Attendant Service and courier of the Imperial Park.
entries.literal: When the prince died, he was appointed chief of the Inner Attendant Service and Imperial Park courier.

entries.zh: 開泰八年，與李勝哥謀奔南土，為遊兵所擒。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Kaitai he plotted with Li Shengge to escape south and was caught by patrol troops.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Kaitai, he plotted with Li Shengge to flee to the southern lands and was seized by roving troops.

entries.zh: 初，仁德皇后與欽哀有隙，欽哀密令安仁伺皇后動靜，無不知者。
entries.en: Earlier Empress Rende and Empress Dowager Qin'ai were estranged; Qin'ai secretly set Anren to spy on the empress's every move, and nothing escaped him.
entries.literal: Earlier, Empress Rende and Qin'ai were at odds; Qin'ai secretly ordered Anren to watch the empress's movements—nothing escaped his knowledge.

entries.zh: 仁德皇后威權既重，安仁懼禍，復謀亡歸。
entries.en: When Empress Rende's power grew formidable, Anren feared for his life and again plotted to escape south.
entries.literal: Once Empress Rende's authority had grown heavy, Anren feared disaster and again plotted to flee home.

entries.zh: 仁德欲誅之，欽哀以言營救。
entries.en: Rende sought to have him executed, but Qin'ai interceded for him.
entries.literal: Rende wished to execute him; Qin'ai pleaded on his behalf.

entries.zh: 聖宗曰：「小喜言父母兄弟俱在南朝，每一念，神魂隕越。
entries.en: Emperor Shengzong said, "Xiaoxi reports that his parents and brothers all remain in the Song realm; the mere thought of them overwhelms his spirit.
entries.literal: Emperor Shengzong said: "Xiaoxi says that his parents and brothers are all in the Southern Court; at every thought his spirit and soul are overwhelmed.

entries.zh: 今為思親，冒死而亡，亦孝子用心，實可憐憫。」
entries.en: Now, moved by love for his family, he risked death to flee. That is the heart of a filial son and truly calls for compassion."
entries.literal: Now, longing for kin, he risked death to flee—this too is a filial son's heart and truly deserves pity."

entries.zh: 赦之。
entries.en: He was pardoned.
entries.literal: He was pardoned.

entries.zh: 重熙初，欽哀攝政，欲廢帝，立少子重元。
entries.en: Early in the Chongxi era Empress Dowager Qin'ai served as regent, sought to depose the emperor, and planned to enthrone her younger son Chongyuan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi, Qin'ai acted as regent, wished to depose the emperor, and install her younger son Chongyuan.

entries.zh: 帝與安仁謀，遷太后慶州守陵，授安仁左承宣、監門衛大將軍，充契丹漢人渤海內侍都知，兼都提點。
entries.en: The emperor conspired with Anren, sent the empress dowager to Qingzhou to tend the imperial tombs, and appointed Anren Left Commissioner of Announcement and Grand General of the Gate Guards, making him superintendent of Khitan, Han, and Bohai inner attendants and chief intendant as well.
entries.literal: The emperor plotted with Anren, moved the empress dowager to Qingzhou to guard the tombs, and appointed Anren Left Commissioner of Announcement, Grand General of the Gate Guards, and superintendent of Khitan, Han, and Bohai inner attendants, also chief intendant.

entries.zh: 會上思太后，親馭奉迎，太后責曰：「汝負萬死，我嘗營救。
entries.en: When the emperor missed his mother and went in person to escort her back, the empress dowager reproached him: "You deserved death a thousand times over, yet I once saved your life.
entries.literal: When the emperor came to miss the empress dowager and personally drove out to welcome her back, the empress dowager rebuked him: "You deserve ten thousand deaths; I once pleaded for your life.

entries.zh: 不望汝報，何為離間我母子耶！」
entries.en: I asked for no reward—why have you driven us mother and son apart!"
entries.literal: I did not expect repayment from you—why have you driven a wedge between mother and son!"

entries.zh: 安仁無答。
entries.en: Anren had nothing to say.
entries.literal: Anren had no reply.

entries.zh: 後不知所終。
entries.en: What became of him afterward is not recorded.
entries.literal: Later his end is unknown.

entries.zh: 論曰：名器所以礪天下，非賢而有功則不可授，況宦者乎！
entries.en: Commentary: Honorary titles and insignia exist to sharpen the realm's virtue; they must not be granted without merit and worthiness—and least of all to eunuchs.
entries.literal: Commentary says: Titles and regalia are what hone the realm; if one is not worthy and has no merit, they must not be granted—how much more so for eunuchs!

entries.zh: 繼恩為內謁者，安仁為黃門令，似矣，何至溺於私愛，而授以觀察使、大將軍耶？
entries.en: Jien as Inner Attendant and Anren as Yellow Gate Commandant would have been fitting enough—how could private affection run so deep that they were made military commissioners and grand generals?
entries.literal: Jien as Inner Attendant and Anren as Yellow Gate Commandant would seem fitting enough—how could favoritism go so far as to grant them military commissioner and grand general?

entries.zh: 《易》曰：「負且乘，致寇至。」
entries.en: The Book of Changes says, "He carries a burden yet rides in a carriage—bandits will come upon him."
entries.literal: The Book of Changes says: "He bears a burden yet rides in a carriage—robbers will come."

entries.zh: 此安仁所以不克有終，繼恩幸而免歟？
entries.en: Is this not why Anren failed to end well, while Jien was fortunate enough to escape a similar fate?
entries.literal: This is why Anren could not see his course through to the end, while Jien was fortunate to escape—is it not?

entries.zh: 《周禮》，寺人掌中門之禁。
entries.en: The Rites of Zhou assign palace stewards to guard the inner gates.
entries.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, palace stewards guard the inner gates.

entries.zh: 至巷伯詩列於《雅》，勃貂功著於晉，雖忠於所事，而非其職矣。
entries.en: Later the "Palace Steward" ode entered the Greater Odes, and Bo Diao won fame in Jin—loyal to their masters, perhaps, but already acting outside their proper charge.
entries.literal: By the time the Palace Steward ode was placed among the Greater Odes, and Bo Diao's achievements were celebrated in Jin, though loyal to those they served, this was no longer their proper office.

entries.zh: 漢、唐中世，竊權蠹政，有不忍言者，是皆寵遇之過。
entries.en: In the middle Han and Tang periods eunuchs seized power and poisoned government, producing scandals too grim to relate in full—all the result of excessive favor.
entries.literal: In the middle periods of Han and Tang, they usurped power and ruined government—there are things one cannot bear to recount—all excesses of favor.

entries.zh: 遼宦者二人，其賢不肖皆可為後世鑒，故傳焉。
entries.en: Liao produced two eunuchs whose conduct, good and bad, can instruct posterity; that is why they are recorded here.
entries.literal: Two Liao eunuchs—the worthy and the unworthy alike may serve as mirrors for later ages; therefore they are given biographies.

entries.zh: 王繼恩，棣州人。
entries.en: Wang Jien came from Dizhou.
entries.literal: Wang Jien was a native of Dizhou.

entries.zh: 睿智皇后南征，繼恩被俘。
entries.en: When Empress Ruizhi marched south, Jien was taken prisoner.
entries.literal: When Empress Ruizhi campaigned south, Jien was captured.

entries.zh: 初，皇后以公私所獲十歲已下兒容貌可觀者近百人，載赴涼陘，並使閹為豎，繼恩在焉。
entries.en: Earlier the empress had gathered nearly a hundred children under ten, handsome boys taken in raids and by other means, sent them to Liangjin, and had them all castrated as palace attendants; Jien was one of them.
entries.literal: At first the empress took nearly a hundred children under ten years of age, of pleasing appearance, gained through public and private means, conveyed them to Liangjin, and had them all castrated to serve as attendants; Jien was among them.

entries.zh: 聰慧，通書及遼語。
entries.en: Clever and quick to learn, he mastered written Chinese and the Khitan language.
entries.literal: Intelligent and clever, he mastered books and the Khitan language.

entries.zh: 擢內謁者、內侍左廂押班。
entries.en: He rose to Inner Attendant and chief steward of the left wing of the inner palace.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Inner Attendant and chief of the left wing of the Inner Service.

entries.zh: 聖宗親政，累遷尚衣庫使、左承宣、監門衛大將軍、靈州觀察使、內庫都提點。
entries.en: After Emperor Shengzong assumed personal rule, Jien was promoted in succession to Director of the Imperial Wardrobe, Left Commissioner of Announcement, Grand General of the Gate Guards, Military Commissioner of Lingzhou, and Chief Intendant of the Inner Treasury.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shengzong took personal rule, he was repeatedly promoted—to Director of the Imperial Wardrobe, Left Commissioner of Announcement, Grand General of the Gate Guards, Military Commissioner of Lingzhou, and Chief Intendant of the Inner Treasury.

entries.zh: 繼恩好清談，不喜權利，每得賜賚，市書至萬卷，載以自隨，誦讀不倦。
entries.en: Jien loved scholarly talk and cared nothing for power or gain; whenever he received rewards he bought books by the thousands, carried them wherever he went, and read without cease.
entries.literal: Jien loved pure conversation and disliked power and profit; whenever he received gifts, he would buy books by the ten thousand scrolls, carry them with him, and read without tiring.

entries.zh: 每宋使來聘，繼恩多充宣賜使。
entries.en: Whenever Song envoys arrived on diplomatic missions, Jien was often appointed to distribute imperial gifts.
entries.literal: Whenever Song envoys came on embassy, Jien often served as commissioner of gifts and grants.

entries.zh: 後不知所終。
entries.en: What became of him afterward is not recorded.
entries.literal: Later his end is unknown.

entries.zh: 伶官 ○羅衣輕
entries.en: Music Officials ○ Luo Yiqing
entries.literal: Music Officials ○ Luo Yiqing

entries.zh: 及長，美風儀，外和內狡。
entries.en: When he grew up he had a fine bearing—outwardly mild, inwardly crafty.
entries.literal: When he reached maturity he had fine bearing; outwardly mild, inwardly crafty.

entries.zh: 重熙中，為文班吏，掌太保印，陪從入宮。
entries.en: During the Chongxi era he served as a clerical officer of the Civil Registry, kept the grand preceptor's seal, and accompanied the court into the palace.
entries.literal: During Chongxi he served as a clerical officer of the Civil Registry, kept the grand preceptor's seal, and accompanied the court into the palace.

entries.zh: 皇后見乙辛詳雅如素宦，令補筆硯吏；
entries.en: The empress saw Yixin refined and elegant like a seasoned courtier and ordered him made a brush-and-ink clerk;
entries.literal: The empress saw Yixin refined and elegant like a long-serving official and ordered him made a brush-and-ink clerk;

entries.zh: 帝亦愛之，累遷護衛太保。
entries.en: The emperor also favored him, and he was repeatedly promoted to Guards Commissioner.
entries.literal: The emperor also favored him, and he was repeatedly promoted to Guards Commissioner.

entries.zh: 道宗即位，以乙辛先朝任使，賜漢人戶四十，同知點檢司事，常召決疑議，升北院同知，歷樞密副使。
entries.en: When Emperor Daozong succeeded, Yixin—already a trusted servant of the previous reign—was granted forty Han households, made Associate Commissioner of the Palace Inspection Office, and often summoned to settle doubtful matters. He rose to associate administrator of the Northern Commission and served as associate commissioner of the Commissioner's Office.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong succeeded, because Yixin had served in the previous reign, he was granted forty Han households, made Associate Commissioner of the Palace Inspection Office, was often summoned to resolve doubtful matters, was raised to associate administrator of the Northern Commission, and served as associate commissioner of the Commissioner's Office.

entries.zh: 清寧五年，為南院樞密使，改知北院，封趙王。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Qingning he became commissioner of the Southern Commissioner's Office, was transferred to administer the Northern Commission, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Qingning he became commissioner of the Southern Commissioner's Office, was transferred to administer the Northern Commission, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 九年，耶律仁先為南院樞密使，時駙馬都尉蕭胡睹與重元黨，惡仁先在朝，奏曰：「仁先可任西北路招討使。」
entries.en: In the ninth year Yelü Renxian was commissioner of the Southern Commissioner's Office. Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Xiao Huzhu, allied with Chongyuan's faction, hated Renxian's presence at court and memorialized, "Renxian may be appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit."
entries.literal: In the ninth year Yelü Renxian was commissioner of the Southern Commissioner's Office. At that time Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Xiao Huzhu was allied with Chongyuan's faction, hated Renxian's presence at court, and memorialized, saying, "Renxian may be appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit."

entries.zh: 帝將從之。
entries.en: The emperor was inclined to agree.
entries.literal: The emperor was about to agree.

entries.zh: 乙辛奏曰：「臣新參國政，未知治體。
entries.en: Yixin memorialized, "Your servant has newly entered state affairs and does not yet know the principles of governance.
entries.literal: Yixin memorialized, saying, "Your servant has newly entered state affairs and does not yet know the principles of governance.

entries.zh: 仁先乃先帝舊臣，不可遽離朝廷。」
entries.en: Renxian is an old minister of the late emperor and must not be abruptly removed from court."
entries.literal: Renxian is an old minister of the late emperor and must not be abruptly removed from court."

entries.zh: 帝然之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The emperor agreed.

entries.zh: 重元亂平，拜北院樞密使，進王魏，賜匡時翊聖竭忠平亂功臣。
entries.en: After Chongyuan's rebellion was put down, he was appointed commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office, advanced to Prince of Wei, and granted the title of merit for aiding the sage, exhausting loyalty, and pacifying rebellion in a time of crisis.
entries.literal: When Chongyuan's rebellion was pacified, he was appointed commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office, advanced to Prince of Wei, and granted the title of merit for aiding the sage, exhausting loyalty, and pacifying rebellion in a time of crisis.

entries.zh: 咸雍五年，加守太師。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Xianyong he was given the added rank of Defender Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xianyong he was given the added rank of Defender Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 詔四方有軍旅，許以便宜從事，勢震中外，門下饋賂不絕。
entries.en: An edict allowed him, wherever military affairs arose in the four quarters, to act at discretion. His power shook court and countryside alike, and gifts at his gate never ceased.
entries.literal: An edict allowed him, wherever there were military affairs in the four quarters, to act at discretion; his power shook court and countryside alike, and gifts at his gate never ceased.

entries.zh: 凡阿順者蒙薦擢，忠直者被斥竄。
entries.en: All who flattered him won promotion; the loyal and upright were driven out.
entries.literal: All who flattered him won promotion; the loyal and upright were driven out.

entries.zh: 五年正月，上將出獵，乙辛奏留皇孫，上欲從之。
entries.en: In the first month of the fifth year, as the emperor prepared to go hunting, Yixin asked that the imperial grandson be left behind, and the emperor was inclined to agree.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, when the emperor was about to go hunting, Yixin memorialized to keep the imperial grandson behind; the emperor wished to agree.

entries.zh: 同知點檢蕭兀納諫曰：「陛下若從乙辛留皇孫，皇孫尚幼，左右無人，願留臣保護，以防不測。」
entries.en: Associate Commissioner of the Palace Inspection Office Xiao Wuna remonstrated: "If Your Majesty leaves the grandson behind as Yixin wishes, he is still a child with no one trustworthy at his side. Allow me to stay and guard him against mishap."
entries.literal: Associate Commissioner of the Palace Inspection Office Xiao Wuna remonstrated, saying, "If Your Majesty follows Yixin in keeping the imperial grandson, the grandson is still young and will have no one at his side; I beg to remain to protect him, to guard against the unforeseen."

entries.zh: 遂與皇孫俱行。
entries.en: The emperor took the grandson with him on the hunt.
entries.literal: He then went together with the imperial grandson.

entries.zh: 由是上始疑乙辛，頗知其奸。
entries.en: From this the emperor first began to suspect Yixin and to see something of his treachery.
entries.literal: From this the emperor first grew suspicious of Yixin and came to know his treachery fairly well.

entries.zh: 會北幸，將次黑山之平澱，上適見扈從官屬多隨乙辛後，惡之，出乙辛知南院大王事。
entries.en: On a tour of the north, as the court was about to encamp at the Pingdian ford on Black Mountain, the emperor noticed how many attendants trailed behind Yixin and took offense; Yixin was transferred to the post of Grand Prince of the Southern Commission.
entries.literal: When the emperor was on a northern tour and was about to halt at the Pingdian of Black Mountain, he happened to see that many of the attendant officials followed behind Yixin; he disliked this and sent Yixin out to serve as Grand Prince of the Southern Commission.

entries.zh: 及例削一字王爵，改王混同，意稍自安。
entries.en: When, by the usual rule, one character was stripped from his princely title and he was redesignated Prince of Huntong, he felt somewhat reassured.
entries.literal: When by precedent one character was cut from his princely title and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huntong, his mind grew somewhat at ease.

entries.zh: 及赴闕入謝，帝即日遣還，改知興中府事。
entries.en: When he came to court to offer thanks, the emperor sent him back the same day and reassigned him as Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture.
entries.literal: When he came to the capital to enter thanks, the emperor that same day sent him back and changed his appointment to Administrator of the Xingzhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 七年冬，坐以禁物鬻入外國，下有司議，法當死。
entries.en: In the winter of the seventh year he was convicted of selling contraband abroad; the case was referred to the judicial offices, and the statute called for death.
entries.literal: In the winter of the seventh year he was charged with selling forbidden goods into foreign states; the matter was referred to the relevant offices for deliberation, and by law he should die.

entries.zh: 乙辛黨耶律燕哥獨奏當入八議，得減死論，擊以鐵骨朵，幽於來州。
entries.en: Yixin's ally Yelü Yangge alone argued that the Eight Deliberations should apply; the sentence was reduced from death, Yixin was beaten with the iron mace, and imprisoned at Laizhou.
entries.literal: Yixin's partisan Yelü Yangge alone memorialized that he should enter the Eight Deliberations, and a reduced sentence from death was obtained; he was struck with the iron mace and confined at Laizhou.

entries.zh: 後謀奔宋及私藏兵甲事覺，縊殺之。
entries.en: Later, when his plot to flee to Song and his secret store of arms were discovered, he was strangled.
entries.literal: Later his plot to flee to Song and his private hoard of weapons and armor came to light, and he was strangled to death.

entries.zh: 乾統二年，發冢，戮其屍。
entries.en: In the second year of Qiantong his tomb was opened and his corpse was publicly shamed.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qiantong his tomb was opened and his corpse was disgraced.

entries.zh: 耶律燕哥，字善寧，季父房之後。
entries.en: Yelü Yangge, whose courtesy name was Shaning, was descended from the Lesser Father House.
entries.literal: Yelü Yangge, courtesy name Shaning, was a descendant of the Lesser Father House.

entries.zh: 四世祖鐸穩，太祖異母弟。
entries.en: His fourth-generation ancestor Duowen was a younger half-brother of Emperor Taizu.
entries.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Duowen was the Taizu Emperor's younger half-brother.

entries.zh: 父曰豁裏斯，官至太師。
entries.en: His father Huolisi rose to the rank of Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: His father, named Huolisi, reached the office of Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 燕哥狡佞而敏。
entries.en: Yangge was cunning, fawning, and quick-witted.
entries.literal: Yangge was crafty, fawning, and quick.

entries.zh: 清寧間，為左護衛太保。
entries.en: During the Qingning era he served as Left Guards Commissioner.
entries.literal: During Qingning he served as Left Guards Commissioner.

entries.zh: 大康初，轉北面林牙。
entries.en: At the start of the Dakang era he was made Northern Palace Secretary.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dakang he was transferred to Northern Palace Secretary.

entries.zh: 初，耶律乙辛自中京留守復為樞密使，以燕哥為耳目，凡聞見必以告。
entries.en: When Yelü Yixin returned from the Central Capital to the Commissioner's Office, he used Yangge as his eyes and ears, reporting everything he heard or saw.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Yelü Yixin returned from Military Governor of the Central Capital to Commissioner of the Commissioner's Office, he used Yangge as eyes and ears; whatever he heard or saw he always reported.

entries.zh: 乙辛愛而薦之，帝亦以為賢，拜左夷離畢。
entries.en: Yixin favored and recommended him; the emperor too judged him worthy and appointed him Left Yilibi.
entries.literal: Yixin favored him and recommended him; the emperor also considered him worthy and appointed him Left Yilibi.

entries.zh: 及皇太子被誣，帝遣燕哥往訊之，太子謂燕哥曰：「帝惟我一子，今為儲嗣，復何求，敢為此事！
entries.en: When the crown prince was framed, the emperor sent Yangge to question him. The prince said, "The emperor has only one son, and I am his heir—what could I possibly gain by such a plot!
entries.literal: When the crown prince was falsely accused, the emperor sent Yangge to interrogate him; the prince said to Yangge, "The emperor has only me as a son; I am now heir apparent—what more could I seek that I would dare do such a thing!

entries.zh: 公與我為昆弟行，當念無辜，達意於帝。」
entries.en: We stand as brothers in rank—think of my innocence and plead my case to the emperor."
entries.literal: You and I are as brothers in rank; you ought to think of my innocence and convey my meaning to the emperor."

entries.zh: 禱之甚懇。
entries.en: He begged him with desperate earnestness.
entries.literal: He prayed to him most earnestly.

entries.zh: 蕭十三聞之，謂燕哥曰：「宜以太子言易為伏狀。」
entries.en: When Xiao Shisan heard of this he told Yangge, "Twist the prince's words into a confession."
entries.literal: Xiao Shisan heard of it and said to Yangge, "You ought to turn the crown prince's words into a confession with ease."

entries.zh: 燕哥頷之，盡如所教以奏。
entries.en: Yangge agreed and reported to the throne exactly as he had been taught.
entries.literal: Yangge nodded assent and memorialized exactly as instructed.

entries.zh: 及太子被逐，乙辛殺害忠良，多燕哥之謀，為契丹行宮都部署。
entries.en: After the crown prince was banished, Yixin's slaughter of loyal officials owed much to Yangge's counsel; Yangge was made Overall Deployer of the Khitan Traveling Palace.
entries.literal: When the crown prince was driven out, Yixin killed and harmed the loyal and good—much of it was Yangge's plotting—and he became Overall Deployer of the Khitan Traveling Palace.

entries.zh: 五年夏，拜南府宰相，遷惕隱。
entries.en: In the summer of the fifth year he was made Chancellor of the Southern Commission and then promoted to Tiyin.
entries.literal: In the summer of the fifth year he was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Commission and transferred to Tiyin.

entries.zh: 大安三年，為西京留守，致仕。
entries.en: In the third year of Da'an he became Military Governor of the Western Capital, then retired from office.
entries.literal: In the third year of Da'an he served as Military Governor of the Western Capital and then retired.

entries.zh: 壽隆初，以疾卒。
entries.en: Early in the Shoulong era he died of illness.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shoulong he died of illness.

entries.zh: 大康元年，皇太子始預朝政，法度修明。
entries.en: In the first year of the Dakang era, the crown prince began to take part in government, and regulations were enforced with new rigor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dakang, the crown prince first took part in court government, and laws and standards were put in good order.

entries.zh: 乙辛不得逞，謀以事誣皇后。
entries.en: Unable to have his way, Yixin plotted to frame the empress on a false charge.
entries.literal: Yixin could not have his way and plotted to frame the empress on a charge.

entries.zh: 后既死，乙辛不自安，又欲害太子。
entries.en: Once the empress was dead, Yixin grew uneasy and turned his mind again to destroying the crown prince.
entries.literal: After the empress died, Yixin was ill at ease and again wished to harm the crown prince.

entries.zh: 乘間入奏曰：「帝與后如天地並位，中宮豈可曠？」
entries.en: Seizing a moment to address the throne, he said, "Emperor and empress stand together like Heaven and earth—how can the inner palace be left vacant?"
entries.literal: Seizing an opportunity he entered and memorialized, saying, "Emperor and empress stand like Heaven and earth side by side—how can the inner palace stand empty?"

entries.zh: 盛稱其黨駙馬都尉蕭霞抹之妹美而賢。
entries.en: He then spoke at length of the beauty and virtue of the sister of his ally, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Xiao Xiamo.
entries.literal: He lavishly praised the sister of his partisan, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Xiao Xiamo, as beautiful and worthy.

entries.zh: 上信之，納於宮，尋冊為皇后。
entries.en: The emperor believed him, brought the woman into the palace, and soon installed her as empress.
entries.literal: The emperor believed him, took her into the palace, and soon enfeoffed her as empress.

entries.zh: 時護衛蕭忽古知乙辛奸狀，伏橋下，欲殺之。
entries.en: The guardsman Xiao Hugu, who knew Yixin's treachery, lay in ambush beneath a bridge intending to kill him.
entries.literal: At that time the guardsman Xiao Hugu knew Yixin's treacherous conduct, lay in wait under a bridge, and wished to kill him.

entries.zh: 俄暴雨壞橋，謀不遂。
entries.en: A sudden downpour wrecked the bridge, and the plot came to nothing.
entries.literal: Soon a violent rainstorm destroyed the bridge, and the plot did not succeed.

entries.zh: 林牙蕭巖壽密奏曰：「乙辛自皇太子預政，內懷疑懼，又與宰相張孝傑相附會。
entries.en: Palace Secretary Xiao Yanshou submitted a secret memorial: "Ever since the crown prince entered government, Yixin has been inwardly fearful, and he has been in league with Chief Minister Zhang Xiaojie.
entries.literal: Palace Secretary Xiao Yanshou secretly memorialized, saying, "Since the crown prince began to share in government, Yixin has harbored suspicion and fear within, and moreover he has joined forces with the chief minister Zhang Xiaojie.

entries.zh: 恐有異圖，不可使居要地。」
entries.en: I fear he harbors ulterior designs; he must not be left in a position of power."
entries.literal: I fear he has ulterior designs and he must not be allowed to hold a crucial post."

entries.zh: 出為中京留守。
entries.en: Yixin was transferred out to serve as Military Governor of the Central Capital.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Military Governor of the Central Capital.

entries.zh: 乙辛泣謂人曰：「乙辛無過，因讒見出。」
entries.en: Yixin wept and told others, "I have done nothing wrong; it is slander that has driven me out."
entries.literal: Yixin wept and said to others, "Yixin has no fault; it is because of slander that I have been sent out."

entries.zh: 其黨蕭霞抹輩以其言聞於上。
entries.en: His partisans, including Xiao Xiamo, repeated these words to the emperor.
entries.literal: His partisans Xiao Xiamo and the like reported his words to the emperor.

entries.zh: 上悔之。
entries.en: The emperor came to regret the decision.
entries.literal: The emperor regretted it.

entries.zh: 無何，出蕭巖壽為順義軍節度使，詔近臣議召乙辛事。
entries.en: Before long Xiao Yanshou was posted away as Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army, and the emperor ordered his close advisers to deliberate on recalling Yixin.
entries.literal: Before long, Xiao Yanshou was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army, and an edict ordered close ministers to discuss recalling Yixin.

entries.zh: 北面官屬無敢言者，耶律撒剌曰：「初以蕭巖壽奏出乙辛，若所言不當，宜坐以罪，若當，則不可復召。」
entries.en: None of the Northern Court officials dared speak up until Yelü Sala said, "Yixin was removed on Xiao Yanshou's memorial. If that memorial was wrong, Yanshou should be punished; if it was right, Yixin must not be brought back."
entries.literal: Among the Northern Court officials none dared speak; Yelü Sala said, "At first Yixin was sent out on Xiao Yanshou's memorial—if what he said was improper, he should be punished for a crime; if it was proper, then Yixin must not be recalled."

entries.zh: 累諫不從。
entries.en: He remonstrated again and again, but the emperor would not listen.
entries.literal: He remonstrated repeatedly but was not heeded.

entries.zh: 乃復召為北院樞密使。
entries.en: Yixin was nevertheless recalled and reappointed Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office.
entries.literal: Yixin was then recalled and made Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office.

entries.zh: 張孝傑，建州永霸縣人。
entries.en: Zhang Xiaojie was a native of Yongba County in Jianzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Xiaojie was a native of Yongba County in Jianzhou.

entries.zh: 家貧，好學。
entries.en: His family was poor, but he loved learning.
entries.literal: His family was poor, but he loved learning.

entries.zh: 重熙二十四年，擢進士第一。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year of Chongxi he placed first in the jinshi examinations.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Chongxi he was promoted first in the jinshi examinations.

entries.zh: 清寧間，累遷樞密直學士。
entries.en: During the Qingning era he was repeatedly promoted to Direct Academician of the Commissioner's Office.
entries.literal: During Qingning he was repeatedly promoted to Direct Academician of the Commissioner's Office.

entries.zh: 咸雍初，坐誤奏事，出為惠州刺史。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Xianyong era, for a mistaken memorial he was sent out as Prefect of Huizhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xianyong, for a mistaken memorial he was sent out as Prefect of Huizhou.

entries.zh: 俄召復舊職，兼知戶部司事。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled to his former post and concurrently directed Revenue Bureau affairs.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled to his former post and concurrently directed Revenue Bureau affairs.

entries.zh: 三年，參知政事，同知樞密院事，加工部侍郎。
entries.en: In the third year he became associate participant in governance, associate administrator of the Commissioner's Office, and supplemental Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the third year he became associate participant in governance, associate administrator of the Commissioner's Office, and supplemental Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 八年，封陳國公。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.

entries.zh: 上以孝傑勤幹，數問以事，為北府宰相。
entries.en: Because the emperor found Xiaojie diligent and capable and often consulted him on affairs, he became chancellor of the Northern Commission.
entries.literal: Because the emperor found Xiaojie diligent and capable and often consulted him on affairs, he became chancellor of the Northern Commission.

entries.zh: 漢人貴幸無比。
entries.en: No Han subject had ever enjoyed such favor.
entries.literal: No Han subject had ever enjoyed such favor.

entries.zh: 大康元年，賜國姓。
entries.en: In the first year of the Dakang era he was granted the imperial clan surname.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dakang he was granted the imperial clan surname.

entries.zh: 明年秋獵，帝一日射鹿三十，燕從官。
entries.en: The next year during the autumn hunt the emperor shot thirty deer in a single day and feasted his attendants.
entries.literal: The next year during the autumn hunt the emperor shot thirty deer in a single day and feasted his attendants.

entries.zh: 酒酣，命賦《雲上於天詩》，詔孝傑坐禦榻旁。
entries.en: When the wine was deep he ordered a composition of the "Clouds Rising to Heaven" poem and had Xiaojie seated beside the imperial couch.
entries.literal: When the wine was deep he ordered a composition of the "Clouds Rising to Heaven" poem and had Xiaojie seated beside the imperial couch.

entries.zh: 上誦《黍離》詩：「知我者謂我心憂，不知我者謂我何求。」
entries.en: The emperor recited the Shu Li poem: "Those who know me say my heart is troubled; those who do not know me ask what I seek."
entries.literal: The emperor recited the Shu Li poem: "Those who know me say my heart is troubled; those who do not know me ask what I seek."

entries.zh: 孝傑奏曰：「今天下太平，陛下何憂？
entries.en: Xiaojie memorialized, "All under Heaven is at peace today—what does Your Majesty have to worry about?
entries.literal: Xiaojie memorialized, saying, "All under Heaven is at peace today—what does Your Majesty have to worry about?

entries.zh: 富有四海，陛下何求？」
entries.en: You possess the four seas—what does Your Majesty still seek?"
entries.literal: You possess the four seas—what does Your Majesty still seek?"

entries.zh: 帝大悅。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 三年，群臣侍燕，上曰：「先帝用仁先、化葛，以賢智也。
entries.en: In the third year, as the hundred officials attended a banquet, the emperor said, "The late emperor employed Renxian and Huage for their wisdom and talent.
entries.literal: In the third year, as the hundred officials attended a banquet, the emperor said, "The late emperor employed Renxian and Huage for their wisdom and talent.

entries.zh: 朕有孝傑、乙辛，不在仁先、化葛下，誠為得人。」
entries.en: I have Xiaojie and Yixin, who are no inferior to Renxian and Huage—truly I have found capable men."
entries.literal: I have Xiaojie and Yixin, who are no inferior to Renxian and Huage—truly I have found capable men."

entries.zh: 歡飲至夜，乃罷。
entries.en: They drank in joy until night before dispersing.
entries.literal: They drank in joy until night before dispersing.

entries.zh: 時皇太子以母後之故，憂見顏色。
entries.en: The crown prince, grieving his mother's death, wore sorrow plain on his face.
entries.literal: At that time the crown prince, on account of his mother's death, showed grief in his countenance.

entries.zh: 乙辛黨欣躍相慶，讒謗沸騰，忠良之士，斥逐殆盡。
entries.en: Yixin's faction rejoiced openly while slander swirled through the court and loyal officials were driven out almost to a man.
entries.literal: Yixin's faction leaped for joy and congratulated one another; slander boiled over, and loyal and good men were driven out almost to the last man.

entries.zh: 乙辛因蕭十三之言，夜召蕭得裏特謀構太子，令護衛太保耶律查剌誣告耶律撒剌等同謀立皇太子。
entries.en: Acting on Xiao Shisan's counsel, Yixin summoned Xiao Delite by night to plot against the crown prince and had Guards Commissioner Yelü Chala accuse Yelü Sala and others of conspiring to put the prince on the throne.
entries.literal: On Xiao Shisan's words, Yixin by night summoned Xiao Delite to plot framing the crown prince, and ordered Guards Commissioner Yelü Chala to lodge a false accusation that Yelü Sala and others had conspired to install the crown prince.

entries.zh: 詔按無跡而罷。
entries.en: An investigation ordered by edict found no evidence, and the case was dropped.
entries.literal: An edict ordered investigation; no trace was found and the matter was dropped.

entries.zh: 又令牌印郎君蕭訛都斡詣上誣首：「耶律查剌前告耶律撒剌等事皆實，臣亦與其謀。
entries.en: He then had Seal-and-Token Gentleman Xiao Eduo appear before the throne with a fabricated confession: "Yelü Chala's earlier charge against Yelü Sala and the others was true, and I was party to the plot as well.
entries.literal: He again ordered Seal-and-Token Gentleman Xiao Eduo to go before the emperor with a false confession: "Yelü Chala's earlier accusation against Yelü Sala and the rest was all true, and I too took part in the plot.

entries.zh: 本欲殺乙辛等而立太子。
entries.en: Our plan was to kill Yixin and his faction and set up the crown prince.
entries.literal: We originally intended to kill Yixin and the rest and establish the crown prince.

entries.zh: 臣等若不言，恐事白連坐。」
entries.en: If we kept silent, we feared we would be punished together once the plot was exposed."
entries.literal: If we ministers did not speak, I feared that when the affair came to light we would be implicated together."

entries.zh: 詔使鞫劾，乙辛迫令具伏。
entries.en: The emperor ordered an inquiry, and Yixin tortured the accused until they confessed.
entries.literal: An edict ordered interrogation; Yixin forced them to confess in full.

entries.zh: 上怒，命誅撒剌及速撒等。
entries.en: Enraged, the emperor ordered Sala, Susa, and the others put to death.
entries.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered the execution of Sala, Susa, and the rest.

entries.zh: 乙辛恐帝疑，引數人庭詰，各令荷重校，繩系其頸，不能出氣，人人不堪其酷，惟求速死。
entries.en: Fearing the emperor's doubts, Yixin had several men questioned in the courtyard, loaded with heavy cangues and ropes drawn tight about their necks until they could scarcely breathe; broken by the torment, each man begged only for a swift death.
entries.literal: Yixin feared the emperor's doubts; he brought several men into the courtyard for questioning, had each bear heavy cangues, and bound ropes about their necks so they could not breathe; every man could not endure the cruelty and only begged to die quickly.

entries.zh: 反奏曰：「別無異辭。」
entries.en: He then reported back, "They have nothing further to say."
entries.literal: He instead memorialized, saying, "There is no other testimony."

entries.zh: 時方暑，屍不得瘞，以至地臭。
entries.en: It was high summer, and the bodies could not be buried in time; the stench filled the ground.
entries.literal: It was then midsummer; the corpses could not be buried, until the ground reeked.

entries.zh: 乃囚皇太子於上京，監衛者皆其黨。
entries.en: The crown prince was imprisoned at the Supreme Capital under guards who were all Yixin's men.
entries.literal: The crown prince was then imprisoned at the Supreme Capital; all the supervising guards were his partisans.

entries.zh: 尋遣蕭達魯古、撒把害太子。
entries.en: Soon afterward Xiao Dalugu and Saba were dispatched to murder the crown prince.
entries.literal: Soon Xiao Dalugu and Saba were sent to harm the crown prince.

entries.zh: 乙辛黨大喜，聚飲數日。
entries.en: Yixin's faction celebrated with feasting that lasted for days.
entries.literal: Yixin's faction was greatly pleased and gathered to drink for several days.

entries.zh: 上京留守蕭撻得以卒聞。
entries.en: Xiao Tade, Military Governor of the Supreme Capital, was able to report the prince's death in detail.
entries.literal: The Military Governor of the Supreme Capital, Xiao Tade, was able to report the death in full.

entries.zh: 上哀悼，欲召其妻，乙辛陰遣人殺之，以滅其口。
entries.en: The emperor mourned and wished to summon the prince's wife, but Yixin secretly had her killed to silence anyone who might speak.
entries.literal: The emperor mourned and wished to summon the prince's wife; Yixin secretly sent men to kill her, to silence witnesses.

entries.zh: 是年夏，乙辛譖皇太子，孝傑同力相濟。
entries.en: That summer, when Yixin slandered the crown prince, Xiaojie worked hand in hand with him.
entries.literal: That summer Yixin slandered the crown prince, and Xiaojie lent his strength in mutual support.

entries.zh: 及乙辛受詔按皇太子黨人，誣害忠良，孝傑之謀居多。
entries.en: When Yixin was ordered to investigate the crown prince's supposed faction and framed loyal men, most of the plotting came from Xiaojie.
entries.literal: When Yixin received the edict to investigate the crown prince's partisans and falsely harmed the loyal and good, Xiaojie's schemes made up the greater part.

entries.zh: 乙辛薦孝傑忠於社稷，帝謂孝傑可比狄仁傑，賜名仁傑，乃許放海東青鶻。
entries.en: Yixin praised Xiaojie as loyal to the realm; the emperor compared him to Di Renjie, granted him the name Renjie, and allowed the eastern-sea green falcon to be sent forth.
entries.literal: Yixin recommended Xiaojie as loyal to the altars of state; the emperor said Xiaojie could be compared to Di Renjie, bestowed the name Renjie, and then permitted the release of the eastern-sea green falcon.

entries.zh: 六年，既出乙辛，上亦悟孝傑奸佞，尋出為武定軍節度使。
entries.en: In the sixth year, once Yixin had been removed, the emperor also saw through Xiaojie's treachery and soon posted him away as Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, after Yixin had been sent out, the emperor also perceived Xiaojie's treachery and flattery, and soon sent him out as Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.

entries.zh: 坐私販廣濟湖鹽及擅改詔旨，削爵，貶安肅州，數年乃歸。
entries.en: Convicted of smuggling salt from Guangji Lake and altering an imperial edict on his own authority, he was stripped of rank, banished to Ansu Prefecture, and allowed to return only years later.
entries.literal: He was charged with privately trafficking salt from Guangji Lake and altering an edict on his own authority; his noble rank was stripped, he was demoted to Ansu Prefecture, and only after several years did he return.

entries.zh: 大安中，死於鄉。
entries.en: He died at home during the Da'an era.
entries.literal: In the Da'an era he died in his native place.

entries.zh: 乾統初，剖棺戮屍，以族產分賜臣下。
entries.en: Early in Qiantong his coffin was opened and his corpse shamed, and his family's property was divided among officials as gifts.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qiantong his coffin was opened and his corpse disgraced, and his clan property was divided and bestowed on subordinates.

entries.zh: 蕭十三，蔑古乃部人。
entries.en: Xiao Shisan came from the Miegunai Division.
entries.literal: Xiao Shisan was a man of the Miegunai Division.

entries.zh: 父鐸魯斡，歷官節度使。
entries.en: His father Duolugun had served as Military Commissioner.
entries.literal: His father Duolugun had served in office as Military Commissioner.

entries.zh: 十三辨黠，善揣摩人意。
entries.en: Shisan was clever and shrewd, adept at reading what others wished to hear.
entries.literal: Shisan was discerning and sharp, skilled at reading people's intentions.

entries.zh: 清寧間，以年勞遷護衛太保。
entries.en: During Qingning he was promoted to Guards Commissioner on the strength of long service.
entries.literal: During Qingning, on account of years of service he was transferred to Guards Commissioner.

entries.zh: 大康初，耶律乙辛復入樞府，益橫恣。
entries.en: At the start of Dakang, Yelü Yixin returned to the Commissioner's Office and grew more domineering than ever.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, Yelü Yixin again entered the Commissioner's Office and grew still more overbearing and unrestrained.

entries.zh: 時十三出入乙辛家，以朝臣不附者輒使出之，十三由宿衛遷殿前副點檢。
entries.en: Shisan was constantly at Yixin's house; any courtier who would not join their faction was promptly posted away, and Shisan rose from palace guard to Associate Commissioner of the Palace Front Office.
entries.literal: At that time Shisan went in and out of Yixin's house; whenever court ministers did not attach themselves to him he would have them sent out, and Shisan rose from palace guard duty to Associate Commissioner of the Palace Front Office.

entries.zh: 三年夏，護衛蕭忽古等謀殺乙辛，事覺下獄。
entries.en: In the summer of the third year the guardsman Xiao Hugu and others plotted to assassinate Yixin; when the plot was discovered they were thrown into prison.
entries.literal: In the summer of the third year the guardsmen Xiao Hugu and others plotted to kill Yixin; the affair came to light and they were imprisoned.

entries.zh: 十三謂乙辛曰：「今太子猶在，臣民屬心。
entries.en: Shisan told Yixin, "The crown prince is still alive, and officials and commoners alike look to him.
entries.literal: Shisan said to Yixin, "The crown prince still lives, and officials and people look to him in their hearts.

entries.zh: 大王素無根柢之助，復有誣皇后之怨。
entries.en: Your Highness has never had a firm base of support, and you still bear the grudge of having framed the empress.
entries.literal: Your Highness from of old has had no deep-rooted support, and moreover bears the resentment of having framed the empress.

entries.zh: 若太子立，王置身何地？
entries.en: If the crown prince succeeds to the throne, where will that leave Your Highness?
entries.literal: If the crown prince is established, where will Your Highness place himself?

entries.zh: 宜熟計之。」
entries.en: You must think this through carefully."
entries.literal: You ought to think it through carefully."

entries.zh: 乙辛曰：「吾憂此久矣！」
entries.en: Yixin replied, "I have worried about that for a long time!"
entries.literal: Yixin said, "I have worried about this for a long time!"

entries.zh: 是夜，召蕭得裏特謀所以構太子事。
entries.en: That very night he summoned Xiao Delite to plot how to frame the crown prince.
entries.literal: That night he summoned Xiao Delite to plot how to frame the crown prince.

entries.zh: 十三計既行，尋遷殿前都點檢，兼同知樞密院事。
entries.en: Once Shisan's scheme succeeded, he was soon promoted to Commissioner of the Palace Front Office and made Associate Administrator of the Commissioner's Office as well.
entries.literal: Once Shisan's plan had been carried out, he was soon transferred to Commissioner of the Palace Front Office and concurrently Associate Administrator of the Commissioner's Office.

entries.zh: 復令蕭訛都斡等誣首耶律查剌前告耶律撒剌等事皆實，詔究其事。
entries.en: He again had Xiao Eduo and others confess falsely that Yelü Chala's earlier charge against Yelü Sala and his associates had been true, and the emperor ordered a full inquiry.
entries.literal: He again had Xiao Eduo and the rest lodge a false confession that Yelü Chala's earlier accusation against Yelü Sala and the rest was all true, and an edict ordered investigation of the affair.

entries.zh: 太子不服，別遣夷離畢耶律燕哥問太子，太子具陳所以見誣之狀。
entries.en: The crown prince protested his innocence, so Yilibi Yelü Yangge was sent to question him; the prince laid out in detail how he had been framed.
entries.literal: The crown prince would not submit; separately Yilibi Yelü Yangge was sent to question the crown prince, and the prince set forth in full the circumstances of how he had been falsely accused.

entries.zh: 十三聞之，謂燕哥曰：「如此奏，則大事去矣，當易其辭為伏款。」
entries.en: When Shisan heard of this he told Yangge, "Report it that way and the whole scheme collapses—you must turn his words into a confession."
entries.literal: Shisan heard of it and said to Yangge, "If you memorialize in this way, the great affair will be lost; you ought to change his words into a confession of guilt."

entries.zh: 燕哥入，如十三言奏之。
entries.en: Yangge went in and reported exactly as Shisan had instructed.
entries.literal: Yangge entered and memorialized as Shisan had said.

entries.zh: 上大怒，廢太子。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage and deposed the crown prince.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and deposed the crown prince.

entries.zh: 太子將出，曰：「我何罪至是！」
entries.en: As the crown prince was led away he cried, "What crime have I committed to deserve this!"
entries.literal: As the crown prince was about to go out, he said, "What crime have I committed to come to this!"

entries.zh: 十三叱令登車，遣衛卒闔車門。
entries.en: Shisan shouted at him to get into the carriage and had guardsmen slam the door shut.
entries.literal: Shisan shouted at him to mount the carriage and sent guardsmen to shut the carriage door.

entries.zh: 是年，遷北院樞密副使，復陳陰害太子計，乙辛從之。
entries.en: That year he was made Associate Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office; he again proposed a secret plot against the crown prince, and Yixin agreed.
entries.literal: That year he was transferred to Associate Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office; he again set forth a secret plan to harm the crown prince, and Yixin followed it.

entries.zh: 及乙辛出知南院大王事，亦出十三為保州統軍使，卒。
entries.en: When Yixin was transferred to Grand Prince of the Southern Commission, Shisan was posted away as Military Commander of Baozhou, where he died.
entries.literal: When Yixin was sent out to serve as Grand Prince of the Southern Commission, Shisan was also sent out as Military Commander of Baozhou and died there.

entries.zh: 乾統間，剖棺戮屍。
entries.en: During the Qiantong era his coffin was opened and his corpse was publicly shamed.
entries.literal: During Qiantong his coffin was opened and his corpse was disgraced.

entries.zh: 二子：的裏得、念經，皆伏誅。
entries.en: His two sons, Dilede and Nianjing, were both executed.
entries.literal: His two sons, Dilede and Nianjing, both submitted to execution.

entries.zh: 奸臣上 ○耶律乙辛張孝傑耶律燕哥蕭十三
entries.en: Treacherous Ministers, Part 1 ○ Yelü Yixin, Zhang Xiaojie, Yelü Yangge, and Xiao Shisan
entries.literal: Treacherous Ministers 1 ○ Yelü Yixin, Zhang Xiaojie, Yelü Yangge, Xiao Shisan

entries.zh: 論曰：舜流共工，孔子誅少正卯，治奸之法嚴矣。
entries.en: The commentary says: Shun exiled Gong Gong, and Confucius executed Shaozheng Mao—the standards for dealing with traitors were severe indeed.
entries.literal: Commentary says: Shun exiled Gong Gong, Confucius executed Shaozheng Mao—the law for governing traitors was stern indeed.

entries.zh: 後世不是之察，反以為忠而信任之，不至於流毒宗社而未已。
entries.en: Later ages lacked such discernment and instead took traitors for loyal men and trusted them, not stopping until their poison had spread through the altars of state.
entries.literal: Later ages lacked such discernment and instead took them for loyal men and trusted them, not stopping until poison spread through altars and state.

entries.zh: 道宗之於乙辛是也。
entries.en: Emperor Daozong's treatment of Yixin was exactly such a case.
entries.literal: Emperor Daozong's treatment of Yixin was exactly this.

entries.zh: 當其留仁先，討重元，若真為國計者；
entries.en: When he kept Yelü Renxian at court and campaigned against Chongyuan, it looked as though he truly had the state's interests at heart;
entries.literal: When he kept Renxian and campaigned against Chongyuan, it seemed as if he truly acted for the state;

entries.zh: 不知包藏禍心，待時而發耳。
entries.en: who could have known that he was hiding a treacherous heart and biding his time to strike.
entries.literal: not knowing he harbored a treacherous heart and waited for the moment to strike.

entries.zh: 一旦專權，又得孝傑、燕哥、十三為之腹心，故肆惡而無忌憚。
entries.en: Once he held power alone and had Zhang Xiaojie, Yelü Yange, and Xiao Shisan as his inner circle, he therefore committed evil without restraint or fear.
entries.literal: Once he monopolized power and gained Xiaojie, Yange, and Shisan as his inner core, he therefore unleashed evil without restraint.

entries.zh: 始誣皇后，又殺太子及其妃，其禍之酷，良可悲哉。
entries.en: First he slandered the empress, then killed the crown prince and his consort—the cruelty of the harm he wrought is truly lamentable.
entries.literal: First he slandered the empress, then killed the crown prince and his consort—the cruelty of the disaster is truly lamentable.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 君子所親，莫皇后、太子若也。
entries.en: Among those whom a gentleman holds dear, none compare with the empress and the crown prince.
entries.literal: Among those a gentleman cherishes, none are like the empress and crown prince.

entries.zh: 奸臣殺之而不知，群臣言之而不悟。
entries.en: Treacherous ministers killed them, yet he did not know; the assembled ministers spoke out, yet he did not understand.
entries.literal: Treacherous ministers killed them yet he did not know; the assembled ministers spoke yet he did not awaken.

entries.zh: 一時忠讜，廢戮幾盡。
entries.en: For a time the loyal and outspoken were nearly all destroyed or put to death.
entries.literal: For a time the loyal and outspoken were nearly all destroyed and executed.

entries.zh: 雖黑山親見官屬之盛，僅削一字王號，至私藏甲兵然後誅之。
entries.en: Even when at Black Mountain the emperor personally saw the grandeur of Yixin's retinue, only one character was struck from his princely title; not until he was found secretly hoarding armor and weapons was he put to death.
entries.literal: Even when at Black Mountain he personally witnessed the splendor of his staff, only a single character was cut from his princely title; not until he secretly hoarded armor and weapons was he executed.

entries.zh: 籲！
entries.en: Ah!
entries.literal: Ah!

entries.zh: 乙辛之罪，固非一死可謝天下，抑亦道宗不明無斷有以養成之也。
entries.en: Yixin's crimes truly could not be answered by death alone; yet it was also Daozong's dimness and want of resolution that had nurtured them.
entries.literal: Yixin's crimes truly could not be expiated by death alone; yet also Daozong's dimness and lack of resolution nurtured them.

entries.zh: 如蕭餘里也輩，忘君黨惡，以饕富貴，雖幸而死諸牖下，其得免於遺臭之辱哉！
entries.en: Men such as Xiao Yulili forgot their sovereign and sided with evil to gorge themselves on wealth and rank; though fortunate enough to die in their own homes, how could they escape the shame of a name that stinks forever!
entries.literal: Men like Xiao Yulili forgot their lord and sided with evil to gorge on wealth and rank; though fortunate to die in their own houses, how could they escape the shame of a stinking legacy!

entries.zh: 蕭餘里也，字訛都碗，國舅阿剌次子。
entries.en: Xiao Yulili, whose style name was Eduowan, was the second son of State Uncle Ala.
entries.literal: Xiao Yulili, style name Eduowan, was the second son of State Uncle Ala.

entries.zh: 便佞滑稽，善女工。
entries.en: He was obsequious and facetious, and excelled at needlework and other domestic crafts.
entries.literal: Fawning and buffoonish, skilled in women's crafts.

entries.zh: 重熙間，以外戚進。
entries.en: During the Chongxi era he rose through his ties as an imperial in-law.
entries.literal: During Chongxi, he advanced through maternal kinship.

entries.zh: 清寧初，補祗候郎君，尚鄭國公主，拜駙馬都尉，累遷南面林牙。
entries.en: At the start of Qingning he entered service as an attendant langjun, married the Princess of Zheng State, was made Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and was promoted step by step to Southern Court linya.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, he was appointed attendant langjun, married the Princess of Zheng State, invested as Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and rose through posts to Southern Court linya.

entries.zh: 以父阿剌為蕭革所譖，出餘里也為奉先軍節度使。
entries.en: When his father Ala was slandered by Xiao Ge, Yulili was posted out as military commissioner of the Fengxian Army.
entries.literal: Because his father Ala was slandered by Xiao Ge, Yulili was sent out as military commissioner of Fengxian Army.

entries.zh: 十年冬，召為北面林牙。
entries.en: In the winter of the tenth year he was recalled to serve as Northern Court linya.
entries.literal: In the tenth winter, he was summoned as Northern Court linya.

entries.zh: 咸雍中，會有告餘里也與族人術哲謀害耶律乙辛，按無狀，出為寧遠軍節度使。
entries.en: During Xianyong someone reported that Yulili and his kinsman Shuzhe had plotted to kill Yelü Yixin; the inquiry found nothing, and he was sent out as military commissioner of the Ningyuan Army.
entries.literal: During Xianyong, there was a report that Yulili and his clansman Shuzhe plotted to kill Yelü Yixin; investigation found no substance, and he was sent out as military commissioner of Ningyuan Army.

entries.zh: 自後餘里也揣乙辛意，傾心事之，薦為國舅詳穩。
entries.en: After that Yulili read Yixin's wishes and threw himself into serving him, and was recommended for the post of State Uncle xiangwen.
entries.literal: Thereafter Yulili gauged Yixin's intentions and devoted himself wholeheartedly; he was recommended as State Uncle xiangwen.

entries.zh: 大康初，封遼西郡王。
entries.en: At the start of Dakang he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liaoxi Commandery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liaoxi Commandery.

entries.zh: 時乙辛擅恣，凡不附己者出之，乃引餘里也為北府宰相，兼知契丹行宮都部署事。
entries.en: Yixin was then ruling arbitrarily: anyone who would not side with him was posted away. He brought Yulili in as Chancellor of the Northern Prefecture and concurrently put him in charge of Khitan mobile-palace deployments.
entries.literal: At the time Yixin acted with unchecked power; whoever did not attach to him was sent away. He then brought in Yulili as Chancellor of the Northern Prefecture and concurrently administrator of Khitan mobile-palace deployments.

entries.zh: 及乙辛謀構皇太子，餘里也多助成之，遂知北院樞密事，賜推誠協贊功臣。
entries.en: When Yixin schemed against the crown prince, Yulili did much to make it succeed; he was then put in charge of Northern Court privy affairs and granted the title Meritorious Subject of Sincere Support.
entries.literal: When Yixin plotted against the crown prince, Yulili greatly helped bring it about; he then administered Northern Court privy affairs and was granted the title Meritorious Subject of Sincere Support.

entries.zh: 以女侄妻乙辛子綏也，恃勢橫肆，至有無君之語，朝野側目。
entries.en: He gave his niece in marriage to Yixin's son Suiye, and, trusting in his power, behaved with brazen arrogance, even uttering words that showed no regard for the sovereign; the court and the realm looked on in dismay.
entries.literal: He married his niece to Yixin's son Suiye, relied on his power and acted with reckless arrogance, even speaking words that denied the sovereign; court and countryside watched askance.

entries.zh: 帝出乙辛知南院大王事，坐與乙辛黨，以天平軍節度使歸第。
entries.en: When the emperor sent Yixin out to administer Southern Court great king affairs, Yulili, as a member of Yixin's faction, was made military commissioner of the Tianping Army and sent home.
entries.literal: The emperor sent Yixin out to administer Southern Court great king affairs; because Yulili was of Yixin's faction, he was made military commissioner of Tianping Army and sent home.

entries.zh: 尋拜西北路招討使。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Northwest Circuit pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Northwest Circuit pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 以母憂去官，卒。
entries.en: He resigned on mourning for his mother and died.
entries.literal: He left office on account of his mother's mourning and died.

entries.zh: 蕭訛都斡，國舅少父房之後。
entries.en: Xiao Eduwo was descended from the State Uncle Shaofu branch.
entries.literal: Xiao Eduwo was a descendant of the State Uncle Shaofu branch.

entries.zh: 咸雍中，補牌印郎君。
entries.en: During Xianyong he was appointed seal-and-tally langjun.
entries.literal: During Xianyong he was appointed seal-and-tally langjun.

entries.zh: 大康三年，樞密使乙辛陰懷逆謀，乃令護衛太保耶律查剌誣告耶律撒剌等廢立事。
entries.en: In the third year of Dakang, Privy Commissioner Yixin secretly harbored treasonous intent and had Defender of the Guard grand guardian Yelü Zhala falsely accuse Yelü Sala and others of plotting to depose the emperor and install another.
entries.literal: In the third year of Dakang, Privy Commissioner Yixin secretly harbored treasonous designs and had Defender of the Guard grand guardian Yelü Zhala falsely accuse Yelü Sala and others of plotting deposition and installation.

entries.zh: 詔按無狀，皆補外。
entries.en: An edict ordered an inquiry; when nothing was found, all were posted to offices outside the capital.
entries.literal: An edict ordered investigation; finding no substance, all were assigned to outer posts.

entries.zh: 頃之，訛都斡希乙辛意，欲實其事，與耶律塔不也等入闕誣首：「耶律撒剌等謀害乙辛，欲立皇太子事，臣亦預謀。
entries.en: Before long Eduwo divined Yixin's intent and, wanting to make the accusation stick, entered the palace with Yelü Tabuye and others to make a false confession: "Yelü Sala and the others plotted to kill Yixin and put the crown prince on the throne; I too was in on the plot.
entries.literal: Before long Eduwo guessed Yixin's wish and, wishing to make the charge real, entered the palace with Yelü Tabuye and others to confess falsely: "Yelü Sala and others plotted to kill Yixin and install the crown prince; I too took part in the plot.

entries.zh: 今不自言，恐事泄連坐。」
entries.en: If I do not speak up now, I fear that when the matter comes out I will be punished along with the rest."
entries.literal: If I do not speak now, I fear that when the affair leaks out I will be implicated."

entries.zh: 帝果怒，徙皇太子於上京。
entries.en: The emperor was indeed enraged and transferred the crown prince to the Upper Capital.
entries.literal: The emperor was indeed enraged and moved the crown prince to the Upper Capital.

entries.zh: 訛都斡尚皇女趙國公主，為駙馬都尉。
entries.en: Eduwo married the imperial daughter, Princess of Zhao State, and was made Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant.
entries.literal: Eduwo married the imperial daughter Princess of Zhao State and served as Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant.

entries.zh: 後與乙辛議不合，銜之，復以車服僭擬人主，被誅。
entries.en: Later he disagreed with Yixin and nursed a grievance; he was again executed for carriages and regalia that imitated the sovereign's.
entries.literal: Later he fell out with Yixin over policy and bore a grudge; again, for carriages and regalia that usurped the sovereign's, he was executed.

entries.zh: 訛都斡臨刑，語人曰：「前告耶律撒刺事，皆乙辛教我。
entries.en: As Eduwo faced execution he told those present: "The earlier charge against Yelü Sala—Yixin taught me every word of it.
entries.literal: At execution Eduwo told others: "The earlier accusation against Yelü Sala—Yixin taught me all of it.

entries.zh: 恐事彰，殺我以滅口耳！」
entries.en: He is afraid the truth will come out, so he kills me to seal my lips!"
entries.literal: Fearing the affair would be exposed, he kills me to silence me!"

entries.zh: 耶律塔不也，仲父房之後。
entries.en: Yelü Tabuye was descended from the Zhongfu branch.
entries.literal: Yelü Tabuye was a descendant of the Zhongfu branch.

entries.zh: 以善擊鞠幸於上，凡馳騁，鞠不離杖。
entries.en: Because he excelled at cuju he won the emperor's favor; whenever he rode at full speed, the ball never left his stick.
entries.literal: Because he excelled at cuju he won the sovereign's favor; whenever he galloped, the ball never left his mallet.

entries.zh: 咸雍初，補祗候郎君。
entries.en: At the start of Xianyong he was appointed attendant langjun.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xianyong he was appointed attendant langjun.

entries.zh: 與耶律乙辛善，故內外畏之。
entries.en: He was on good terms with Yelü Yixin, and for that reason everyone at court feared him.
entries.literal: Friendly with Yelü Yixin, so inside and outside the court feared him.

entries.zh: 及太子被譖，按無跡，塔不也附乙辛，欲實其誣，與訛都斡等密奏：「太子謀亂事本實，臣不首，恐事覺連坐。」
entries.en: When the crown prince was slandered and the inquiry found nothing, Tabuye sided with Yixin to make the charge stick; with Eduwo and others he secretly memorialized: "The crown prince's plot of rebellion was real; if I do not come forward first, I fear that when it is discovered I will be punished with the rest."
entries.literal: When the crown prince was slandered and investigation found no trace, Tabuye attached himself to Yixin to make the slander real; with Eduwo and others he secretly memorialized: "The crown prince's plot of rebellion was real; if I do not confess first, I fear discovery will implicate me."

entries.zh: 帝信之，廢太子。
entries.en: The emperor believed them and deposed the crown prince.
entries.literal: The emperor believed it and deposed the crown prince.

entries.zh: 改延慶宮副使。
entries.en: He was reassigned as deputy commissioner of Yanqing Palace.
entries.literal: He was changed to deputy commissioner of Yanqing Palace.

entries.zh: 壽隆元年，為行宮都部署。
entries.en: In the first year of Shoulong he became mobile-palace chief deployer.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shoulong, he was made mobile-palace chief deployer.

entries.zh: 天祚嗣位，以塔不也黨乙辛，出為特免部節度使。
entries.en: When Tianzu succeeded to the throne, Tabuye, as a partisan of Yixin, was posted out as military commissioner of the Tejian tribe.
entries.literal: When Tianzu succeeded, because Tabuye was of Yixin's faction, he was sent out as Tejian tribe military commissioner.

entries.zh: 及樞密使耶律阿思大索乙辛舊黨，塔不也以賂獲免。
entries.en: When Privy Commissioner Yelü Asi launched a sweeping purge of Yixin's old faction, Tabuye bought his way free.
entries.literal: When Privy Commissioner Yelü Asi broadly hunted old Yixin partisans, Tabuye escaped through bribery.

entries.zh: 徙敵烈部節度使，復為敦睦宮使。
entries.en: He was transferred to military commissioner of the Dilie tribe, then restored as commissioner of Dunmu Palace.
entries.literal: He was transferred as Dilie tribe military commissioner, then restored as Dunmu Palace commissioner.

entries.zh: 天慶元年，出為西北路招討使。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianqing he was posted out as Northwest Circuit pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianqing, he was sent out as Northwest Circuit pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 以疾卒。
entries.en: He died of illness.
entries.literal: He died of illness.

entries.zh: 蕭圖古辭，字何寧，楮特部人。
entries.en: Xiao Tuguci, whose style name was Hening, was a man of the Zhute tribe.
entries.literal: Xiao Tuguci, style name Hening, was of the Zhute tribe.

entries.zh: 仕重熙中，以能稱，累遷左中丞。
entries.en: He served during Chongxi, won renown for his ability, and was promoted step by step to Left Vice Censor.
entries.literal: He served in Chongxi, was famed for ability, and rose through posts to Left Vice Censor.

entries.zh: 清寧初，歷北面林牙，改北院樞密副使。
entries.en: At the start of Qingning he served as Northern Court linya, then became associate Northern Court privy commissioner.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, he served as Northern Court linya, then changed to associate Northern Court privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 辨敏，善伺顏色，應對合上意。
entries.en: He was quick and perceptive, skilled at reading the emperor's mood, and his replies always suited the sovereign's wishes.
entries.literal: Sharp-witted, skilled at reading expressions; his replies matched the sovereign's mind.

entries.zh: 皇太后嘗曰：「有大事，非耶律化哥、蕭圖古辭不能決。」
entries.en: The empress dowager once said, "For any great matter, nothing can be decided without Yelü Huage and Xiao Tuguci."
entries.literal: The empress dowager once said: "For great affairs, nothing can be settled without Yelü Huage and Xiao Tuguci."

entries.zh: 眷遇日隆。
entries.en: His favor grew greater day by day.
entries.literal: His favor day by day grew.

entries.zh: 知北院樞密使事。
entries.en: He was put in charge of Northern Court privy commissioner affairs.
entries.literal: He administered Northern Court privy commissioner affairs.

entries.zh: 六年，出知黃龍府。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was sent out to administer Huanglong Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he was sent out to administer Huanglong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 八年，拜南府宰相。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was made Chancellor of the Southern Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, he was invested as Chancellor of the Southern Prefecture.

entries.zh: 頃之，為北院樞密使，詔許便宜從事。
entries.en: Before long he became Northern Court privy commissioner, and an edict allowed him to act at his own discretion.
entries.literal: Before long he was made Northern Court privy commissioner; an edict permitted discretionary action.

entries.zh: 為人奸佞有餘，好聚斂，專愎，變更法度。
entries.en: In character he was surpassingly treacherous and fawning, greedy for gain, wilfully obstinate, and given to changing laws and institutions.
entries.literal: As a man he was abundantly treacherous and fawning, fond of extortion, wilfully obstinate, and altered laws and institutions.

entries.zh: 為樞密數月，所薦引多為重元黨與，由是免為庶人。
entries.en: After only a few months as privy commissioner, most of those he recommended proved to be partisans of Chongyuan; for this he was stripped of rank and made a commoner.
entries.literal: As privy commissioner for several months, most he recommended were Chongyuan's partisans; thereby he was demoted to commoner.

entries.zh: 後沒入興聖宮，卒。
entries.en: Later his property was confiscated to Xingsheng Palace, and he died.
entries.literal: Later he was confiscated to Xingsheng Palace; he died.

entries.zh: 蕭餘里也耶律合魯蕭得裏特蕭訛都斡蕭達魯古耶律塔不也蕭圖古辭
entries.en: Xiao Yulili, Yelü Helu, Xiao Delite, Xiao Eduwo, Xiao Dalugu, Yelü Tabuye, and Xiao Tuguci
entries.literal: Xiao Yulili, Yelü Helu, Xiao Delite, Xiao Eduwo, Xiao Dalugu, Yelü Tabuye, Xiao Tuguci

entries.zh: 轄底，字涅烈袞，肅祖孫夷離堇怗剌之子。
entries.en: Xiadǐ, whose style name was Nieliegun, was the son of the ürün chijin Dila, who was a grandson of Suzu.
entries.literal: Xiadǐ, courtesy name Nieliegun, was the son of the ürün chijin Dila, descendant of Emperor Suzu of the Yaonian clan.

entries.zh: 幼黠而辯，時險佞者多附之。
entries.en: As a youth he was sharp-witted and quick of tongue, and many crafty sycophants of the day rallied to him.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever and eloquent, and at the time many treacherous flatterers attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 遙輦痕德堇可汗時，異母兄罨古只為叠剌部夷離堇。
entries.en: During the reign of Khan Hendejin of the Yaolian line, his elder half-brother Angu'zhi served as ürün chijin of the Diela tribe.
entries.literal: In the time of Khan Hendejin of the Yaolian, his elder half-brother Angu'zhi was ürün chijin of the Yaonian tribe.

entries.zh: 故事，為夷離堇者，得行再生禮。
entries.en: By established custom, whoever assumed the office of ürün chijin was entitled to perform the rebirth ceremony.
entries.literal: By precedent, one who became ürün chijin was permitted to perform the ritual of rebirth.

entries.zh: 罨古只方就帳易服，轄底遂取紅袍、貂蟬冠，乘白馬而出。
entries.en: While Angu'zhi was still in his tent changing clothes, Xiadǐ seized a red robe and a sable cicada cap, mounted a white horse, and rode forth.
entries.literal: Angu'zhi had just entered the tent to change his garments when Xiadǐ took a red robe and sable cicada cap, mounted a white horse, and rode out.

entries.zh: 乃令黨人大呼曰：「夷離堇出矣！」
entries.en: He ordered his partisans to cry out: "The ürün chijin has emerged!"
entries.literal: He then had his faction shout aloud: "The ürün chijin has come forth!"

entries.zh: 眾皆羅拜，因行柴冊禮，自立為夷離堇。
entries.en: The crowd prostrated themselves in ranks; he then performed the chice ritual of investiture and declared himself ürün chijin.
entries.literal: All bowed down in ranks, whereupon he performed the chice ritual and installed himself as ürün chijin.

entries.zh: 與於越耶律釋魯同知國政。
entries.en: He shared governance of the realm with Yelü Shilu, who held the honorary title of yuyue.
entries.literal: Together with the yuyue Yelü Shilu he jointly administered state affairs.

entries.zh: 及釋魯遇害，轄底懼人圖己，挈其二子叠裏特、朔刮奔渤海，偽為失明。
entries.en: After Shilu was killed, Xiadǐ feared others would plot against him; he fled to Bohai with his sons Dialite and Shuogua and pretended to be blind.
entries.literal: When Shilu met with violence, Xiadǐ feared that others would plot against him; he took his two sons Dialite and Shuogua and fled to Bohai, feigning blindness.

entries.zh: 後因球馬之會，與二子奪良馬奔歸國。
entries.en: Later, at a ball-game meeting, he and his two sons seized fine horses and raced back to the Khitan realm.
entries.literal: Later, at a ball-and-horse gathering, he and his two sons seized fine horses and galloped back to the state.

entries.zh: 益為奸惡，常以巧辭獲免。
entries.en: He grew still more wicked, yet time and again talked his way out of punishment with clever speeches.
entries.literal: He grew ever more treacherous and wicked, yet often escaped punishment through clever words.

entries.zh: 太祖將即位，讓轄底，轄底曰：「皇帝聖人，由天所命，臣豈敢當！」
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu was about to ascend the throne, he offered the realm to Xiadǐ; Xiadǐ replied, "The Son of Heaven is a sage ordained by Heaven—how could a subject such as I dare accept it!"
entries.literal: When the Taizu Emperor was about to take the throne, he offered it to Xiadǐ; Xiadǐ said: "The emperor is a sage appointed by Heaven—how dare your subject presume to accept!"

entries.zh: 太祖命為於越。
entries.en: The emperor then appointed him yuyue.
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor appointed him yuyue.

entries.zh: 及自將伐西南諸部，轄底誘剌葛等亂，不從者殺之。
entries.en: When the emperor led troops in person against the southwestern tribes, Xiadǐ incited Cige and others to revolt and killed those who refused to join.
entries.literal: When he personally led a campaign against the tribes of the southwest, Xiadǐ incited Cige and others to rebel; those who would not follow he killed.

entries.zh: 車駕還至赤水城，轄底懼，與剌葛俱北走，至榆河，為追兵所獲。
entries.en: When the imperial procession returned to Chishui City, Xiadǐ took fright and fled north with Cige; at the Yu River they were overtaken and captured.
