entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Chishui City, Xiadǐ grew afraid; he fled north together with Cige, reached the Yu River, and was captured by pursuing troops.

entries.zh: 太祖問曰：「朕初即位，嘗以國讓，叔父辭之；
entries.en: Emperor Taizu asked, "When I first took the throne I offered you the realm, and you, Uncle, declined it;
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor asked: "When I first took the throne I once offered you the realm, and Uncle declined it;

entries.zh: 今反欲立吾弟，何也？」
entries.en: why do you now seek to set up my younger brother instead?"
entries.literal: why now do you wish instead to set up my younger brother?"

entries.zh: 轄底對曰：「始臣不知天子之貴，及陛下即位，衛從甚嚴，與凡庶不同，臣嘗奏事心動，始有窺覦之意。
entries.en: Xiadǐ answered, "At first I did not grasp how exalted the Son of Heaven was. After Your Majesty took the throne, your escort was so strict and so unlike that of common men that when I once presented a memorial my heart stirred, and only then did I begin to covet the throne.
entries.literal: Xiadǐ replied: "At first your subject did not know the exalted status of the Son of Heaven; after Your Majesty took the throne, your guards and attendants were exceedingly strict and unlike those of ordinary folk. When I once presented a memorial my heart was stirred, and only then did I begin to harbor designs of usurpation.

entries.zh: 度陛下英武，必不可取；
entries.en: I judged that Your Majesty was heroic and martial and could never be overthrown;
entries.literal: I judged Your Majesty to be heroic and martial and surely impossible to seize;

entries.zh: 諸弟懦弱，得則易圖也。
entries.en: your younger brothers were weak—once one of them held power, he would be easy to overthrow.
entries.literal: your younger brothers were weak and timid—if one obtained the throne, he would be easy to plot against.

entries.zh: 事若成，豈容諸弟乎！」
entries.en: Had the plot succeeded, would I have spared your brothers!"
entries.literal: If the affair succeeded, how could I have tolerated those younger brothers!"

entries.zh: 太祖謂諸弟曰：「汝輩乃從斯人之言耶！」
entries.en: The emperor said to his brothers, "You actually listened to this man!"
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor said to his younger brothers: "You actually followed this man's words!"

entries.zh: 叠剌曰：「謀大事者，須用如此人；
entries.en: Diela replied, "Great undertakings require men like him;
entries.literal: Diela said: "One who plots a great undertaking must employ men such as this;

entries.zh: 事成亦必去之。」
entries.en: once the deed is done, he must certainly be removed."
entries.literal: when the affair succeeds, he must surely be removed."

entries.zh: 轄底不復對。
entries.en: Xiadǐ said nothing more.
entries.literal: Xiadǐ made no further reply.

entries.zh: 囚數月，縊殺之。
entries.en: After months in confinement he was strangled.
entries.literal: After several months in prison he was strangled to death.

entries.zh: 將刑，太祖謂曰：「叔父罪當死，朕不敢赦。
entries.en: Before the execution, Emperor Taizu said, "Uncle, your crime deserves death, and I dare not pardon you.
entries.literal: When he was about to be executed, the Taizu Emperor said to him: "Uncle's crime merits death, and I dare not pardon it.

entries.zh: 事有便國者，宜悉言之。」
entries.en: If anything would serve the realm, speak of it fully."
entries.literal: If there is anything that would benefit the state, you should speak of it fully."

entries.zh: 轄底曰：「叠剌部人眾勢強，故多為亂，宜分為二，以弱其勢。」
entries.en: Xiadǐ said, "The Diela tribe is large and strong, which is why it so often rebels; divide it in two to weaken its power."
entries.literal: Xiadǐ said: "The Yaonian tribe is numerous and powerful, and for this reason it often breeds rebellion; it should be divided in two to weaken its strength."

entries.zh: 子叠裏特。
entries.en: His son was Dialite.
entries.literal: His son Dialite.

entries.zh: 叠裏特，字海鄰。
entries.en: Dialite, whose style name was Hailin.
entries.literal: Dialite, courtesy name Hailin.

entries.zh: 有膂力，善馳射，馬躓不仆。
entries.en: He was powerfully built and skilled at mounted archery; even when his horse stumbled he would not be thrown.
entries.literal: He possessed great physical strength, excelled at mounted archery, and when his horse stumbled would not fall.

entries.zh: 尤神於醫，視人疾，若隔紗睹物，莫不悉見。
entries.en: He was uncannily gifted in medicine; when he examined an illness it was as though he saw through a veil—nothing was hidden from him.
entries.literal: He was especially miraculous in medicine; when he examined a person's illness it was as if he viewed objects through gauze—nothing escaped his sight.

entries.zh: 太祖在潛，已加眷遇，及即位，拜叠剌部夷離堇。
entries.en: Even before Taizu took the throne he had favored Dialite; once enthroned, he appointed him ürün chijin of the Yaonian tribe.
entries.literal: While the Taizu Emperor was still in the background, he had already shown him special favor; upon taking the throne he appointed him ürün chijin of the Yaonian tribe.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗思鹿醢解酲，以山林所有，問能取者。
entries.en: Taizu once craved pickled deer to clear his head after drinking; as it could be found in the hills, he asked who could fetch it.
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor once longed for pickled deer to sober his wine; since it was to be found in the mountains and forests, he asked who could obtain it.

entries.zh: 叠裏特曰：「臣能得之。」
entries.en: Dialite said, "I can get it."
entries.literal: Dialite said: "Your subject can obtain it."

entries.zh: 乘內廄馬逐鹿，射其一。
entries.en: He mounted a horse from the imperial stables, chased deer, and brought one down with a shot.
entries.literal: He mounted an imperial stable horse to pursue deer and shot one.

entries.zh: 欲復射，馬跌而斃。
entries.en: As he prepared a second shot, the horse stumbled and fell dead.
entries.literal: As he was about to shoot again, the horse stumbled and died.

entries.zh: 叠裏特躍而前，弓猶不弛，復獲其一。
entries.en: Dialite sprang forward without slackening his bow and took another deer.
entries.literal: Dialite leaped forward, his bow still unslackened, and took another.

entries.zh: 帝歡甚曰：「吾弟萬人敵！」
entries.en: The emperor was delighted and exclaimed, "My brother is a match for ten thousand men!"
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "My brother is a match for ten thousand men!"

entries.zh: 會帝患心痛，召叠裏特視之。
entries.en: When the emperor suffered heart pain, he summoned Dialite to examine him.
entries.literal: It happened that the emperor suffered heart pain and summoned Dialite to examine him.

entries.zh: 叠裏特曰：「膏肓有瘀血如彈丸，然藥不能及，必針而後愈。」
entries.en: Dialite said, "There is congealed blood the size of a pellet in the deepest recesses of the chest; medicine cannot reach it—only acupuncture will cure you."
entries.literal: Dialite said: "In the region of the vitals there is congealed blood like a pellet, yet medicine cannot reach it; only needling will bring recovery."

entries.zh: 帝從之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The emperor followed his advice.

entries.zh: 嘔出瘀血，痛止。
entries.en: He vomited the clotted blood and the pain stopped.
entries.literal: He vomited forth the congealed blood and the pain ceased.

entries.zh: 帝以其親，每加賜賚；
entries.en: Because he was kin, the emperor showered him with gifts;
entries.literal: Because he was a kinsman, the emperor repeatedly bestowed gifts upon him;

entries.zh: 然知其為人，未嘗任以職。
entries.en: yet knowing his character, he never gave him real responsibility.
entries.literal: yet knowing his character, he never entrusted him with office.

entries.zh: 後從剌葛亂，與其父轄底俱縊殺之。
entries.en: Later he joined Cige's rebellion and was strangled along with his father Xiadǐ.
entries.literal: Later he followed Cige in rebellion and was strangled to death together with his father Xiadǐ.

entries.zh: 察割，字歐辛，明王安端之子。
entries.en: Chaguo, whose style name was Ouxin, was the son of Prince Ming'an Anduan.
entries.literal: Chaguo, courtesy name Ouxin, was the son of Prince Ming'an Anduan.

entries.zh: 善騎射。
entries.en: He was skilled at mounted archery.
entries.literal: He excelled at mounted archery.

entries.zh: 貌恭而心狡，人以為懦。
entries.en: His manner was respectful but his heart was cunning, and people mistook him for a coward.
entries.literal: In appearance he was deferential but in heart crafty; people took him for timid.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「此凶頑，非懦也。」
entries.en: Taizu said, "He is vicious and stubborn—not timid at all."
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor said: "This man is fierce and obstinate—not timid."

entries.zh: 其父安端嘗使奏事，太祖謂近侍曰：「此子目若風駝，面有反相。
entries.en: Once when his father sent him to report at court, Taizu told his attendants, "This man's eyes are like a camel's in a gale, and his face bears the look of a rebel.
entries.literal: His father Anduan once sent him to present a memorial; the Taizu Emperor said to his close attendants: "This man's eyes are like those of a camel in the wind, and his face bears the marks of a rebel.

entries.zh: 朕若獨居，無令入門。」
entries.en: If I am alone, do not let him through the door."
entries.literal: If I am alone, do not let him enter the gate."

entries.zh: 世宗即位於鎮陽，安端聞之，欲持兩端。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang, Anduan heard the news and tried to hedge between the rivals.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang, Anduan heard of it and wished to keep to both sides.

entries.zh: 察割曰：「太弟忌刻，若果立，豈容我輩！
entries.en: Chaguo said, "The Imperial Younger Brother is jealous and cruel; if he really becomes emperor, he will never spare us!
entries.literal: Chaguo said: "The Imperial Younger Brother is jealous and harsh; if he truly takes the throne, how could he tolerate us!

entries.zh: 永康王寬厚，且與劉哥相善，宜往與計。」
entries.en: Prince Yongkang is generous and friendly with Liu Ge—we should go consult with them."
entries.literal: Prince Yongkang is generous and moreover on good terms with Liu Ge; we should go and consult with him."

entries.zh: 安端即與劉哥謀歸世宗。
entries.en: Anduan then joined Liu Ge in plotting to submit to Shizong.
entries.literal: Anduan thereupon plotted with Liu Ge to submit to Emperor Shizong.

entries.zh: 及和議成，以功封泰寧王。
entries.en: When peace was concluded, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taining for his service.
entries.literal: When the peace agreement was concluded, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taining for his merit.

entries.zh: 涅魯古，小字耶魯綰。
entries.en: Nielugu, whose childhood name was Yeluwan.
entries.literal: Nielugu, pet name Yeluwan.

entries.zh: 性陰狠。
entries.en: He was secretive and ruthless by nature.
entries.literal: By nature he was secretive and cruel.

entries.zh: 興宗一見，謂曰：「此子目有反相。」
entries.en: At first sight Emperor Xingzong said, "This boy's eyes bear the look of a rebel."
entries.literal: At one sight Emperor Xingzong said: "This child's eyes bear the marks of rebellion."

entries.zh: 重熙十一年，封安定郡王。
entries.en: In Chongxi 11 he was made Prince of Anding.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongxi he was enfeoffed as Prince of Anding commandery.

entries.zh: 十七年，進王楚，為惕隱。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Prince of Chu and appointed tiyin.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to Prince of Chu and made tiyin.

entries.zh: 清寧三年，出為武定軍節度使。
entries.en: In Qingning 3 he was posted as Military Commissioner of Wuding.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qingning he was sent out as Military Commissioner of Wuding.

entries.zh: 七年，知南院樞密使事，說其父重元詐病，俟車駕臨問，因行弒逆。
entries.en: In the seventh year he took charge of Southern Commission affairs and urged his father Chongyuan to feign illness so that when the emperor came to inquire in person, they could strike.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he became Director of Southern Commission affairs; he urged his father Chongyuan to feign illness and wait for the imperial visit to inquire, then assassinate him.

entries.zh: 九年秋獵，帝用耶律良之計，遣人急召涅魯古。
entries.en: During the autumn hunt of the ninth year, the emperor adopted Yelü Liang's counsel and urgently summoned Nielugu.
entries.literal: In the ninth year during the autumn hunt, the emperor followed Yelü Liang's plan and urgently summoned Nielugu.

entries.zh: 涅魯古以事泄，遽擁兵犯行宮。
entries.en: When Nielugu learned the plot was exposed, he hastily raised troops and assaulted the traveling palace.
entries.literal: Nielugu, learning the affair was exposed, hastily gathered troops and attacked the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 南院樞密使許王仁先等率宿衛士討之。
entries.en: Southern Commissioner Prince Xu Renxian and others led the palace guards against him.
entries.literal: The Southern Commission Director Prince Xu Renxian and others led the palace guards to attack him.

entries.zh: 涅魯古躍馬突出，為近侍詳穩渤海阿廝、護衛蘇射殺之。
entries.en: Nielugu spurred his horse and broke out of the line, but was shot down by the close attendant commander Bohai Asi and the guard Su.
entries.literal: Nielugu leaped his horse and rushed out; he was shot and killed by the close attendant commander Bohai Asi and guard Su.

entries.zh: 滑哥，字斯懶，隋國王釋魯之子。
entries.en: Huage, whose style name was Silan, was the son of Shilu, King of Sui.
entries.literal: Huage, courtesy name Silan, was the son of Shilu, King of Sui.

entries.zh: 性陰險。
entries.en: He was secretive and treacherous by nature.
entries.literal: By nature he was secretive and treacherous.

entries.zh: 初蒸其父妾，懼事彰，與克蕭臺哂等共害其父，歸咎臺哂，滑哥獲免。
entries.en: He first violated his father's concubine; fearing exposure, he murdered his father with Ke Xiao Taishan and others, blamed Taishan, and Huage went unpunished.
entries.literal: At first he violated his father's concubine; fearing the affair would be exposed, together with Ke Xiao Taishan and others he jointly murdered his father, shifted the blame onto Taishan, and Huage escaped punishment.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，務廣恩施，雖知滑哥凶逆，姑示含忍，授以惕隱。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, he sought to extend favor broadly; though he knew Huage was vicious and rebellious, he temporarily showed forbearance and appointed him tiyin.
entries.literal: When the Taizu Emperor took the throne, he sought to extend grace widely; though he knew Huage was vicious and rebellious, for the moment he showed forbearance and appointed him tiyin.

entries.zh: 六年，滑哥預諸弟之亂。
entries.en: In the sixth year Huage joined in his younger brothers' revolt.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, Huage took part in his younger brothers' rebellion.

entries.zh: 事平，群臣議其罪，皆謂滑哥不可釋，於是與其子痕只俱淩遲而死，敕軍士恣取其產。
entries.en: After order was restored, the ministers debated his crime; all agreed Huage could not be spared; he and his son Henji were then executed by dismemberment, and soldiers were permitted to seize his goods at will.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, the assembled ministers deliberated on his crime; all said Huage must not be released; thereupon he and his son Henji were both executed by dismemberment, and an edict allowed soldiers to help themselves to his property freely.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「滑哥不畏上天，反君弒父，其惡不可言。
entries.en: The emperor said, "Huage fears neither Heaven nor his obligations; he rebelled against his lord and murdered his father—his wickedness is beyond words.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Huage does not fear Heaven above; he turned against his lord and murdered his father—his wickedness is beyond words.

entries.zh: 諸弟作亂，皆此人教之也。」
entries.en: My younger brothers' rebellion was all instigated by this man."
entries.literal: The rebellion of my younger brothers was all taught by this man."

entries.zh: 天祿五年七月，帝幸太液谷，留飲三日，察割謀亂不果。
entries.en: In the seventh month of Tianlu 5, the emperor visited Taiye Valley and lingered there drinking for three days; Chaguo plotted a revolt but failed.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Tianlu, the emperor visited Taiye Valley and remained drinking for three days; Chaguo plotted rebellion but it did not succeed.

entries.zh: 帝伐周，至詳古山，太后與帝祭文獻皇帝於行宮，群臣皆醉。
entries.en: On campaign against Zhou, the court reached Xianggu Mountain; the empress dowager and emperor offered sacrifice to Emperor Wenxian at the traveling palace, and the whole court was drunk.
entries.literal: The emperor campaigned against Zhou, reached Xianggu Mountain, and the empress dowager and emperor sacrificed to Emperor Wenxian at the traveling palace; the assembled ministers were all drunk.

entries.zh: 察割歸見壽安王，邀與語，王弗從。
entries.en: Chaguo went to Prince Shou'an and asked to speak with him; the prince refused.
entries.literal: Chaguo returned and went to see Prince Shou'an, inviting him to speak; the prince would not comply.

entries.zh: 察割以謀告耶律盆都，盆都從之。
entries.en: Chaguo revealed the plot to Yelü Pendu, who joined him.
entries.literal: Chaguo disclosed the plot to Yelü Pendu, and Pendu followed him.

entries.zh: 是夕，同率兵入弒太后及帝，因僭位號。
entries.en: That night they led their troops in and murdered the empress dowager and the emperor, then seized the imperial title.
entries.literal: That evening they together led troops in, murdered the empress dowager and the emperor, and thereupon usurped the imperial title.

entries.zh: 百官不從者，執其家屬。
entries.en: Officials who refused to follow had their families seized as hostages.
entries.literal: For officials who would not follow, they seized their families.

entries.zh: 至夜，閱內府物，見碼瑙碗，曰：「此希世寶，今為我有！」
entries.en: That night he inspected the inner treasury, found an agate bowl, and exclaimed, "A treasure of the age—and now it is mine!"
entries.literal: At night he examined the objects of the inner treasury, saw an agate bowl, and said: "This is a treasure rare in the world—now it is mine!"

entries.zh: 詫於其妻。
entries.en: He showed it proudly to his wife.
entries.literal: He showed it to his wife in wonder.

entries.zh: 妻曰：「壽安王、屋質在，吾屬無噍類，此物何益！」
entries.en: His wife said, "Prince Shou'an and Wuzhi are still alive—we shall not leave a soul alive; what good is this bowl!"
entries.literal: His wife said: "Prince Shou'an and Wuzhi are still alive—our kind will not leave a mouthful; what good is this object!"

entries.zh: 察割曰：「壽安年幼，屋質不過引數奴，詰旦來朝，固不足憂。」
entries.en: Chaguo said, "Shou'an is young, and Wuzhi commands only a handful of slaves—they will come to court at dawn; there is nothing to fear."
entries.literal: Chaguo said: "Prince Shou'an is young, and Wuzhi is no more than a man leading a few slaves; at dawn they will come to court—surely there is nothing to worry about."

entries.zh: 其黨矧斯報壽安、屋質以兵圍於外，察割尋遣人弒皇后於柩前，倉惶出陣。
entries.en: His follower Shengsi reported that Shou'an and Wuzhi had surrounded them outside with troops; Chaguo then sent men to murder the empress before the coffin and hurried out to give battle in confusion.
entries.literal: His partisan Shengsi reported to Prince Shou'an and Wuzhi that troops had surrounded them outside; Chaguo soon sent men to murder the empress before the coffin, then rushed out in disarray to take the field.

entries.zh: 壽安遣人諭曰：「汝等既行弒逆，復將若何？」
entries.en: Prince Shou'an sent a messenger to declare, "You have already murdered your sovereign—what do you plan to do next?"
entries.literal: Prince Shou'an sent someone to declare: "You have already committed regicide—what more do you intend?"

entries.zh: 有夷離堇劃者委兵歸壽安王，餘眾望之，徐徐而往。
entries.en: An ürün chijin named Hua laid down his arms and went over to Prince Shou'an; the rest of the troops watched him and drifted over one by one.
entries.literal: An ürün chijin named Hua cast down his weapons and submitted to Prince Shou'an; the rest of the troops watched him and followed slowly.

entries.zh: 察割知其不濟，乃系群官家屬，執弓矢脅曰：「無過殺此曹爾！」
entries.en: Seeing that he could not prevail, Chaguo bound the officials' families, took up bow and arrow, and threatened, "I need only kill this crowd!"
entries.literal: Chaguo knew he would not succeed; he bound the families of the assembled officials, seized bow and arrow, and threatened: "Nothing more than killing this lot!"

entries.zh: 叱令速出。
entries.en: He shouted for them to come out at once.
entries.literal: He shouted, ordering them to hurry out.

entries.zh: 時林牙耶律敵獵亦在系中，進曰：「不有所廢，壽安王何以興？
entries.en: Among those bound was the linya Yelü Dilie, who came forward and said, "Unless someone is removed, how can Prince Shou'an ascend the throne?
entries.literal: At the time the linya Yelü Dilie was also among those bound; he stepped forward and said: "Unless something is abolished, how can Prince Shou'an rise?

entries.zh: 籍此為辭，猶可以免。」
entries.en: Use that as your plea and you may yet save yourselves."
entries.literal: Using this as your plea, you may still escape punishment."

entries.zh: 察割曰：「誠如公言，誰當使者？」
entries.en: Chaguo said, "If you are right, who shall go as envoy?"
entries.literal: Chaguo said: "If what you say is true, who shall be the envoy?"

entries.zh: 敵獵請與罨撒葛同往說之，察割從其計。
entries.en: Dilie offered to go with Yansage to negotiate; Chaguo agreed.
entries.literal: Dilie asked to go with Yansage to persuade them; Chaguo followed his plan.

entries.zh: 壽安王復令敵獵誘察割，臠殺之。
entries.en: Prince Shou'an then had Dilie lure Chaguo out and had him hacked to pieces.
entries.literal: Prince Shou'an then had Dilie lure Chaguo out and dismembered him.

entries.zh: 諸子皆伏誅。
entries.en: His sons were all put to death.
entries.literal: His sons were all executed.

entries.zh: 重元，小字孛吉只，聖宗次子。
entries.en: Chongyuan, whose childhood name was Beijizhi, was the second son of Emperor Shengzong.
entries.literal: Chongyuan, pet name Beijizhi, was the second son of Emperor Shengzong.

entries.zh: 材勇絕人，眉目秀朗，寡言笑，人望而畏。
entries.en: His talent and bravery were unmatched; his face was handsome and clear; he spoke and laughed little, and men feared him at first sight.
entries.literal: His talent and courage surpassed others; his features were handsome and bright; he spoke little and laughed rarely; people feared him at a glance.

entries.zh: 太平三年，封秦國王。
entries.en: In Taiping 3 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taiping he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

entries.zh: 聖宗崩，欽哀皇后稱制，密謀立重元。
entries.en: After Shengzong's death, Empress Dowager Qin'ai ruled as regent and secretly plotted to set Chongyuan on the throne.
entries.literal: When Shengzong died, Empress Dowager Qin'ai assumed regency and secretly plotted to establish Chongyuan.

entries.zh: 重元以所謀白於上，上益重之，封為皇太弟。
entries.en: Chongyuan reported the plot to the emperor, who valued him all the more and enfeoffed him as Imperial Younger Brother.
entries.literal: Chongyuan disclosed the plot to the throne; the emperor esteemed him all the more and enfeoffed him as Imperial Younger Brother.

entries.zh: 歷北院樞密使、南京留守、知元帥府事。
entries.en: He served in turn as Commissioner of the Northern Commission, Prefect of Nanjing, and Director of the Marshal's Bureau.
entries.literal: He successively held the posts of Commissioner of the Northern Commission, Prefect of Nanjing, and Director of the Marshal's Bureau.

entries.zh: 重元處戎職，未嘗離輦下。
entries.en: Though Chongyuan held a military post, he never strayed far from the imperial carriage.
entries.literal: Chongyuan held military office but never left the vicinity of the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 先是契丹人犯法，例須漢人禁勘，受枉者多。
entries.en: Previously, when Khitan broke the law they were tried by Han officials, and many were wronged.
entries.literal: Previously, when Khitan violated the law they had to be tried by Han officials, and many suffered injustice.

entries.zh: 重元奏請五京各置契丹警巡使，詔從之，賜以金券誓書。
entries.en: Chongyuan memorialized that each of the Five Capitals should have Khitan patrol commissioners; the court approved, and he was granted a golden pledge certificate.
entries.literal: Chongyuan memorialized requesting that each of the Five Capitals establish Khitan patrol commissioners; the edict approved it, and he was granted a golden certificate of pledge.

entries.zh: 道宗即位，冊為皇太叔，免拜不名，為天下兵馬大元帥，復賜金券、四頂帽、二色袍，尊寵所未有。
entries.en: When Daozong ascended the throne, Chongyuan was made Imperial Younger Uncle, exempted from bowing and from having his name spoken aloud, appointed Grand Marshal of all armies under Heaven, and again given golden certificates, a four-peaked cap, and a two-colored robe—honors never granted before.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong took the throne, he was installed as Imperial Younger Uncle, exempted from bowing and from having his name spoken, made Grand Marshal of all armies and horses under Heaven, and again granted golden certificates, a four-peaked cap, and a two-colored robe—honors without precedent.

entries.zh: 清寧九年，車駕獵灤水，以其子涅魯古素謀，與同黨陳國王陳六、知北院樞密事蕭胡睹等凡四百餘人，誘脅弩手軍陣於帷宮外。
entries.en: In Qingning 9, while the emperor hunted on the Luan River, Chongyuan—acting on the long-laid plot of his son Nielugu—joined Prince of Chen Chen Liu, Northern Commissioner Xiao Hudu, and more than four hundred others to coerce the crossbow troops into forming battle lines outside the curtain palace.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Qingning, when the imperial carriage hunted on the Luan River, relying on the longstanding plot of his son Nielugu together with the co-conspirator Prince of Chen Chen Liu, Commissioner of the Northern Commission Xiao Hudu, and more than four hundred others, they coerced the crossbow corps to form ranks outside the curtain palace.

entries.zh: 將戰，其黨多悔過效順，各自奔潰。
entries.en: Just before battle, many of his followers repented and went over to the emperor, scattering in flight.
entries.literal: As battle was about to begin, many of his partisans repented and submitted, each fleeing in rout.

entries.zh: 重元既知失計，北走大漠，嘆曰：「涅魯古使我至此！」
entries.en: Realizing his plan had failed, Chongyuan fled north into the desert and cried, "Nielugu has brought me to this pass!"
entries.literal: Chongyuan, knowing his plan had failed, fled north into the great desert and sighed: "Nielugu brought me to this!"

entries.zh: 遂自殺。
entries.en: Thereupon he took his own life.
entries.literal: Thereupon he killed himself.

entries.zh: 逆臣上
entries.en: Rebellious Officials, Part One
entries.literal: Rebellious Ministers, Upper Part

entries.zh: 蕭翰，一名敵烈，字寒真，宰相敵魯之子。
entries.en: Xiao Han, also called Dilie, whose style was Hanzhen, was the son of Chancellor Dilu.
entries.literal: Xiao Han, also named Dilie, style Hanzhen, was the son of Chancellor Dilu.

entries.zh: 天贊初，唐兵圍鎮州，節度使張文禮遣使告急。
entries.en: Early in the Tianzan era, Tang forces besieged Zhen Prefecture, and the military commissioner Zhang Wenli sent envoys begging for relief.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianzan, Tang troops besieged Zhen Prefecture, and Military Commissioner Zhang Wenli sent envoys in urgent appeal.

entries.zh: 翰受詔與康末怛往救，克之，殺其將李嗣昭，拔石城。
entries.en: Han received orders and marched to the rescue with Kang Moda; they took the city, killed the Tang general Li Sizhao, and seized Shicheng.
entries.literal: Han received the edict and went to the rescue with Kang Moda, took the city, killed its general Li Sizhao, and captured Shicheng.

entries.zh: 會同初，領漢軍侍衛。
entries.en: At the start of the Huitong era, he commanded the Han-army guard corps.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, he led the Han-army guard.

entries.zh: 八年，伐晉，敗晉將杜重威，追至望都。
entries.en: In the eighth year he campaigned against Jin, routed the Jin general Du Chongwei, and pursued him as far as Wangdu.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, campaigning against Jin, he defeated the Jin general Du Chongwei and pursued him to Wangdu.

entries.zh: 翰奏曰：「可令軍下馬而射。」
entries.en: Han submitted a memorial: "Have the army dismount and shoot."
entries.literal: Han memorialized, saying, "The army may be ordered to dismount and shoot."

entries.zh: 帝從其言，軍士步進。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his advice, and the troops advanced on foot.
entries.literal: The Emperor followed his words, and the soldiers advanced on foot.

entries.zh: 敵人持短兵猝至，我軍失利。
entries.en: The enemy closed in at once with side arms, and our forces were beaten.
entries.literal: The enemy, bearing short weapons, came suddenly, and our army was defeated.

entries.zh: 帝悔之曰：「此吾用言之過至此！」
entries.en: The emperor repented and said, "This is what comes of heeding that counsel!"
entries.literal: The Emperor regretted it and said, "This is where taking my words has led!"

entries.zh: 及從駕入汴，為宣武軍節度使。
entries.en: When the court entered Bian, he was made military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.
entries.literal: When he followed the imperial procession into Bian, he became Military Commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

entries.zh: 會帝崩欒城，世宗即位。
entries.en: When the emperor died at Luancheng, Shizong succeeded him.
entries.literal: When the Emperor died at Luancheng, Shizong took the throne.

entries.zh: 翰聞之，委事於李從敏，徑趨行在。
entries.en: On hearing the news, Han left his duties to Li Congmin and hurried straight to the imperial camp.
entries.literal: On hearing this, Han entrusted affairs to Li Congmin and went straight to the imperial camp.

entries.zh: 是年秋，世宗與皇太后相拒於潢河橫渡，和議未定。
entries.en: That autumn Shizong and the empress dowager faced each other at Huanghe Hengdu, and no settlement had yet been reached.
entries.literal: That autumn, Shizong and the Empress Dowager confronted each other at Huanghe Hengdu, and peace terms were not settled.

entries.zh: 太后問翰曰：「汝何怨而叛？」
entries.en: The empress dowager asked Han, "What grievance drove you to rebel?"
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager asked Han, "What grievance made you rebel?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣母無罪，太后殺之，以此不能無憾。」
entries.en: He answered, "My mother was innocent, yet Your Majesty put her to death—for that I cannot be without bitterness."
entries.literal: He replied, "My mother was guiltless, yet Your Majesty killed her; for this I cannot be without resentment."

entries.zh: 初耶律屋質以附太后被囚，翰聞而快之，即囚所謂曰：「汝嘗言我輩不及，今在狴犴，何也？」
entries.en: Earlier Yelü Wuzhi had been imprisoned for siding with the empress dowager; when Han heard of it he was delighted, and at the prison he said, "You once claimed we were beneath you—now you sit in a cage; what of that?"
entries.literal: Earlier Yelü Wuzhi had been imprisoned for siding with the Empress Dowager; Han heard of it and rejoiced, and at the prison said to him, "You once said we were not your equal—now you are in the cage; what of it?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「第願公不至如此！」
entries.en: Wuzhi answered, "I only hope you never come to this pass!"
entries.literal: He replied, "I only wish you would not come to this!"

entries.zh: 翰默然。
entries.en: Han said nothing.
entries.literal: Han was silent.

entries.zh: 天祿二年，尚帝妹阿不裏。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianlu he married the emperor's younger sister Abuli.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianlu, he married the Emperor's younger sister Abuli.

entries.zh: 後與天德謀反，下獄。
entries.en: Later he conspired to rebel with Tiande and was thrown into prison.
entries.literal: Later he plotted rebellion with Tiande and was cast into prison.

entries.zh: 復結惕隱劉哥及其弟盆都亂，耶律石剌告屋質，屋持遽入奏之，翰等不伏。
entries.en: He again joined with Tiyin Liuge and Liuge's younger brother Pendu in a plot; Yelü Shila reported it to Wuzhi, who rushed in to inform the throne, but Han and his fellows would not confess.
entries.literal: He again joined Tiyin Liuge and his younger brother Pendu in disorder; Yelü Shila informed Wuzhi, and Wuzhi at once entered and reported it; Han and the others would not confess.

entries.zh: 帝不欲發其事，屋質固諍以為不可，乃詔屋質鞫按。
entries.en: The emperor did not wish to bring the matter to light, but Wuzhi argued strenuously that this could not stand, and the emperor ordered Wuzhi to investigate and try the case.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not wish to expose the affair; Wuzhi remonstrated firmly that it could not be allowed, and an edict ordered Wuzhi to investigate and try the case.

entries.zh: 翰伏辜，帝竟釋之。
entries.en: Han confessed, yet the emperor ultimately set him free.
entries.literal: Han confessed his guilt, yet the Emperor in the end released him.

entries.zh: 復與公主以書結明王安端反，屋質得其書以奏，翰伏誅。
entries.en: He again conspired with the princess by letter to join Prince Ming'an Anduan in rebellion; Wuzhi obtained the letter and presented it to the throne, and Han was put to death after confessing.
entries.literal: He again, with the princess by letter, joined Prince Ming'an Anduan in rebellion; Wuzhi obtained the letter and memorialized with it, and Han was executed on confession.

entries.zh: 劉哥，字明隱，太祖弟寅底石之子。
entries.en: Liuge, whose style was Mingyin, was a son of Taizu's younger brother Yindishi.
entries.literal: Liuge, style Mingyin, was the son of Taizu's younger brother Yindishi.

entries.zh: 幼驕狠，好陵侮人，長益凶狡。
entries.en: As a boy he was arrogant and brutal and loved to bully others; as a man he grew only more savage and cunning.
entries.literal: As a child he was arrogant and fierce, fond of bullying others; grown, he became all the more vicious and cunning.

entries.zh: 太宗惡之，使守邊僥，累遷西南邊大詳穩。
entries.en: Taizong disliked him and posted him to guard the Jiao frontier; he rose through repeated promotions to Grand Xiangwen of the southwestern border.
entries.literal: Taizong disliked him and sent him to guard the frontier of Jiao, and he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Xiangwen of the southwestern border.

entries.zh: 會同十年，叔父安端從帝伐晉，以病先歸，與劉哥鄰居。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Huitong his uncle Anduan accompanied the emperor against Jin but came home early with illness and became Liuge's neighbor.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Huitong, his uncle Anduan followed the Emperor in the campaign against Jin, returned early on account of illness, and lived as Liuge's neighbor.

entries.zh: 世宗立於軍中，安端議所往，劉哥首建附世宗之策，以本部兵助之。
entries.en: When Shizong was proclaimed in the army, Anduan debated which side to take; Liuge was first to urge siding with Shizong and supported him with his tribal troops.
entries.literal: When Shizong was established in the army, Anduan debated where to go; Liuge was the first to propose attaching to Shizong and aided him with his own tribal forces.

entries.zh: 時太后命皇太弟李胡率兵而南，劉哥、安端遇於泰德泉。
entries.en: The empress dowager had ordered the imperial younger brother Li Hu to march south with an army; Liuge and Anduan met him at Taide Spring.
entries.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager ordered the Imperial Younger Brother Li Hu to lead troops south; Liuge and Anduan met him at Taide Spring.

entries.zh: 既接戰，安端墜馬。
entries.en: When battle was joined, Anduan was thrown from his horse.
entries.literal: Once battle was joined, Anduan fell from his horse.

entries.zh: 王子天德馳至，欲以槍刺之。
entries.en: Prince Tiande galloped up and tried to run him through with a spear.
entries.literal: Prince Tiande galloped up and wished to stab him with a spear.

entries.zh: 劉哥以身衛安端，射天德，貫甲不及膚。
entries.en: Liuge shielded Anduan with his own body, shot at Tiande, and the arrow pierced his armor without touching his skin.
entries.literal: Liuge shielded Anduan with his body, shot Tiande, and the arrow pierced his armor without reaching the flesh.

entries.zh: 安端得馬復戰，太弟兵敗。
entries.en: Anduan remounted and fought on, and the younger brother's army was routed.
entries.literal: Anduan regained a horse and fought again; the Younger Brother's army was defeated.

entries.zh: 劉哥與安端朝於行在。
entries.en: Liuge and Anduan presented themselves at the imperial camp.
entries.literal: Liuge and Anduan attended court at the imperial camp.

entries.zh: 及和議成，太后問劉哥曰：「汝何怨而叛？」
entries.en: After peace was made, the empress dowager asked Liuge, "What grievance made you rebel?"
entries.literal: When peace was concluded, the Empress Dowager asked Liuge, "What grievance made you rebel?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣父無罪，太后殺之，以此怨耳。」
entries.en: He answered, "My father was innocent, yet Your Majesty killed him—that is my grievance."
entries.literal: He replied, "My father was guiltless, yet Your Majesty killed him; for this there is resentment."

entries.zh: 事平，以功為惕隱。
entries.en: When the affair was settled, he was made tiyin for his service.
entries.literal: When affairs were settled, for his merit he was made Tiyin.

entries.zh: 天祿中，與其弟盆都、王子天德、侍衛蕭翰謀反，耶律石剌發其事，劉哥以飾辭免。
entries.en: During the Tianlu era he plotted rebellion with his younger brother Pendu, Prince Tiande, and the guard Xiao Han; Yelü Shila exposed the plot, but Liuge talked his way free.
entries.literal: During Tianlu, with his younger brother Pendu, Prince Tiande, and Guard Xiao Han he plotted rebellion; Yelü Shila exposed the affair, and Liuge escaped by polished excuses.

entries.zh: 後請帝博，欲因進酒弒逆，帝覺之，不果，被囚。
entries.en: Later he invited the emperor to gamble, planning to murder him when he served wine; the emperor sensed it, the plot failed, and Liuge was imprisoned.
entries.literal: Later he asked the Emperor to gamble, intending to assassinate him when presenting wine; the Emperor perceived it, it did not succeed, and he was imprisoned.

entries.zh: 一日，召劉哥，鎖項以博。
entries.en: One day the emperor summoned Liuge and gambled with him while a collar was locked about his neck.
entries.literal: One day the Emperor summoned Liuge and, with his neck locked, gambled with him.

entries.zh: 帝問：「汝實反耶？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "Did you really rebel?"
entries.literal: The Emperor asked, "Did you truly rebel?"

entries.zh: 劉哥誓曰：「臣若有反心，必生千頂疽死！」
entries.en: Liuge swore, "If I harbor rebellion in my heart, may I die of the thousand-headed carbuncle!"
entries.literal: Liuge swore, "If your servant harbors a rebellious heart, may he die of a thousand-headed carbuncle!"

entries.zh: 遂貰之。
entries.en: The emperor then pardoned him.
entries.literal: He was then pardoned.

entries.zh: 耶律屋質固諍，以為罪在不赦。
entries.en: Yelü Wuzhi argued strenuously that the offense was beyond pardon.
entries.literal: Yelü Wuzhi remonstrated firmly, holding that the crime was unpardonable.

entries.zh: 上命屋質按之，具服。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Wuzhi to investigate, and Liuge confessed everything.
entries.literal: The sovereign ordered Wuzhi to investigate; Liuge fully confessed.

entries.zh: 詔免死，流烏古部，果以千頂疽死。
entries.en: An edict spared his life and banished him to the Wugu tribe, where he did in fact die of the thousand-headed carbuncle.
entries.literal: An edict spared his life and exiled him to the Wugu tribe; he indeed died of the thousand-headed carbuncle.

entries.zh: 弟盆都。
entries.en: His younger brother Pendu.
entries.literal: His younger brother Pendu.

entries.zh: 牒蠟，字述蘭，六院夷離堇蒲古只之後。
entries.en: Diepa, whose style was Shulan, was a descendant of Puguzhi, yilieqin of the Six Courts.
entries.literal: Diepa, style Shulan, was a descendant of Puguzhi, yilieqin of the Six Courts.

entries.zh: 天顯中，為中臺省右相。
entries.en: During the Tianxian era he was right chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: During Tianxian he served as right chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 會同元年，與趙思溫持節冊晉帝。
entries.en: In the first year of Huitong he joined Zhao Siwen in bearing credentials to invest the Jin emperor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Huitong he went with Zhao Siwen bearing credentials to invest the Jin emperor.

entries.zh: 及我師伐晉，至滹沱河，降晉將杜重威，牒蠟功居多。
entries.en: When the Liao army marched against Jin and reached the Hutuo River, the Jin general Du Chongwei surrendered, and Diepa's contribution was the greatest.
entries.literal: When our army campaigned against Jin and reached the Hutuo River, the Jin general Du Chongwei surrendered; Diepa's merit was greatest.

entries.zh: 大同元年，平相州之叛，斬首數萬級。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he put down the rebellion at Xiang Prefecture and took tens of thousands of heads.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong he quelled the rebellion at Xiang Prefecture and beheaded tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，遣使馳報，仍命牒蠟執偏將術者以來。
entries.en: When Shizong succeeded, he sent envoys at once with the news and also ordered Diepa to seize the deputy general Shuzhe and bring him in.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he sent envoys in haste with the news and also ordered Diepa to seize the deputy general Shuzhe and bring him.

entries.zh: 其使誤入術者營，術者得詔，反誘牒蠟，執送太后。
entries.en: The envoy mistakenly entered Shuzhe's camp; Shuzhe got the edict and instead lured Diepa in, seized him, and sent him to the empress dowager.
entries.literal: The envoy mistakenly entered Shuzhe's camp; Shuzhe received the edict and instead lured Diepa, seized him, and sent him to the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 牒蠟亡歸世宗。
entries.en: Diepa escaped and rejoined Shizong.
entries.literal: Diepa fled and returned to Shizong.

entries.zh: 和約既成，封燕王，為南京留守。
entries.en: Once peace was made he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan and appointed regent of the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: After peace was concluded he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan and made regent of the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 天祿五年，察割弒逆，牒蠟方醉，其妻扶入察割之幕，因從之。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Tianlu, when Chagai murdered the emperor, Diepa was drunk; his wife helped him into Chagai's tent, and he went along.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianlu, when Chagai committed regicide, Diepa was drunk; his wife helped him into Chagai's tent, and he followed along.

entries.zh: 明旦，壽安王討亂，凡脅從者皆棄兵降；
entries.en: At dawn Prince Shou'an put down the rebellion; all who had been coerced laid down their arms and surrendered;
entries.literal: At dawn Prince Shou'an suppressed the disorder; all who had been coerced cast down their weapons and surrendered;

entries.zh: 牒蠟不降，陵遲而死。
entries.en: Diepa refused to surrender and was executed by dismemberment.
entries.literal: Diepa would not surrender and was executed by dismemberment.

entries.zh: 妻子皆誅。
entries.en: His wife and children were all executed.
entries.literal: His wife and children were all put to death.

entries.zh: 朗，字歐新，季父房罨古只之孫。
entries.en: Lang, whose style was Ouxin, was a grandson of Yanguzhi of the younger father's house.
entries.literal: Lang, style Ouxin, was a grandson of Yanguzhi of the younger father's house.

entries.zh: 性輕佻，多力，人呼為「虎斯」。
entries.en: He was frivolous by nature and immensely strong; people called him "Husi."
entries.literal: By nature he was frivolous and possessed great strength; people called him "Husi."

entries.zh: 天顯間以材勇進，每戰輒克，由是得名。
entries.en: During the Tianxian era he rose through talent and valor; he won every battle he fought and thereby made his name.
entries.literal: During Tianxian he advanced through talent and courage; in every battle he prevailed, and thereby gained renown.

entries.zh: 會同九年，太宗入汴，命知澶淵，控扼河渡。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Huitong, when Taizong entered Bian, Lang was ordered to oversee Chanyuan and hold the river crossing.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Huitong, when Taizong entered Bian, he was ordered to oversee Chanyuan and control the river crossing.

entries.zh: 天祿元年，燕、趙已南皆應劉知遠，朗與汴守蕭翰棄城歸闕。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianlu, Yan, Zhao, and all lands to the south rallied to Liu Zhiyuan; Lang and Bian's defender Xiao Han abandoned the city and returned to court.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianlu, Yan, Zhao, and all to the south answered Liu Zhiyuan; Lang and Bian's defender Xiao Han abandoned the city and returned to court.

entries.zh: 先是，朗祖罨古只為其弟轄底詐取夷離堇，自是族中無任六院職事者；
entries.en: Earlier Lang's grandfather Yanguzhi had had the yilieqin title fraudulently taken by his younger brother Xiadi; from then on no one in the clan held office in the Six Courts;
entries.literal: Earlier Lang's grandfather Yanguzhi had had the yilieqin title seized from him by fraud through his younger brother Xiadi; from then on no one in the clan held office in the Six Courts;

entries.zh: 世宗不悉其事，以朗為六院大王。
entries.en: Shizong did not know the full story and appointed Lang great king of the Six Courts.
entries.literal: Shizong did not know the full story and made Lang great king of the Six Courts.

entries.zh: 及察割作亂，遣人報朗曰：「事成矣！」
entries.en: When Chagai rebelled, he sent word to Lang: "It is done!"
entries.literal: When Chagai rebelled, he sent someone to inform Lang, saying, "The affair has succeeded!"

entries.zh: 朗遣詳穩蕭胡裏以所部軍往，命曰：「當持兩端，助其勝者。」
entries.en: Lang sent the xiangwen Xiao Huli with his tribal troops and ordered, "Keep to both sides and help whichever side wins."
entries.literal: Lang sent the xiangwen Xiao Huli with his tribal forces and ordered, "Hold to both sides and aid whichever wins."

entries.zh: 穆宗即位，伏誅，籍其家屬。
entries.en: When Muzong succeeded, Lang was put to death and his household was confiscated.
entries.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Lang was executed on confession and his household was confiscated.

entries.zh: 海思，字鐸袞，隋國王釋魯之庶子。
entries.en: Haishi, whose style was Duogun, was a secondary son of Shilu, King of Sui.
entries.literal: Haishi, style Duogun, was the secondary son of King of Sui Shilu.

entries.zh: 機警口辯。
entries.en: He was quick-witted and a gifted debater.
entries.literal: He was quick-witted and eloquent in debate.

entries.zh: 會同五年，詔求直言。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Huitong the court issued an edict calling for blunt counsel.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Huitong an edict sought blunt counsel.

entries.zh: 時海思年十八，衣羊裘，乘牛詣闕。
entries.en: Haishi was then eighteen; clad in a sheepskin coat, he rode an ox to the palace.
entries.literal: At that time Haishi was eighteen, wore a sheepskin coat, and came to the palace riding an ox.

entries.zh: 有司問曰：「汝何故來？」
entries.en: The officials asked, "Why have you come?"
entries.literal: The officials asked, "For what reason have you come?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「應詔言事。
entries.en: He answered, "To respond to the edict and speak my mind.
entries.literal: He replied, "In response to the edict to speak on affairs.

entries.zh: 茍不以貧稚見遺，亦可備直言之選。」
entries.en: If you do not dismiss me for being poor and young, I may yet qualify among those chosen to speak plainly."
entries.literal: If I am not rejected for poverty and youth, I may also be fit for the selection of blunt speech."

entries.zh: 有司以聞。
entries.en: The officials reported this to the throne.
entries.literal: The officials reported it.

entries.zh: 會帝將出獵，使謂曰：「俟吾還則見之。」
entries.en: The emperor was about to go hunting and sent word: "Wait until I return, and then you shall be received."
entries.literal: As the Emperor was about to go hunting, he sent word saying, "Wait until I return, then you shall be received."

entries.zh: 海思曰：「臣以陛下急於求賢，是以來耳；
entries.en: Haishi said, "I came because Your Majesty is eager to find worthy men;
entries.literal: Haishi said, "Your servant came because Your Majesty is eager to seek the worthy;

entries.zh: 今反緩於獵，請從此歸。」
entries.en: yet now you put the hunt first. I shall take my leave."
entries.literal: now you are instead slow for the hunt—your servant asks to return from here."

entries.zh: 帝聞，即召見賜坐，問以治道。
entries.en: When the emperor heard this, he summoned Haishi at once, gave him a seat, and questioned him on the art of government.
entries.literal: On hearing this, the Emperor at once summoned him, granted him a seat, and questioned him on the way of governance.

entries.zh: 命明王安端與耶律頗德試之，數日，安端等奏曰：「海思之材，臣等所不及。」
entries.en: He ordered Prince Ming'an Anduan and Yelü Pode to test him; after several days they reported, "Haishi's ability is beyond what we can match."
entries.literal: He ordered Prince Ming'an Anduan and Yelü Pode to test him; after several days Anduan and the others memorialized, "Haishi's talent is what your servants cannot match."

entries.zh: 帝召海思問曰：「與汝言者何如人也？」
entries.en: The emperor summoned Haishi and asked, "What sort of men were those who tested you?"
entries.literal: The Emperor summoned Haishi and asked, "What sort of men were those who spoke with you?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「安端言無收檢，若空車走峻阪；
entries.en: He answered, "Anduan's speech has no restraint—it is like driving an empty cart down a steep slope;
entries.literal: He replied, "Anduan's speech has no restraint, like an empty cart running a steep slope;

entries.zh: 頗德如著靴行曠野射鴇。」
entries.en: Pode is like wearing boots to stalk bustards across open country."
entries.literal: Pode is like wearing boots to walk the open wilds and shoot bustards."

entries.zh: 帝大笑。
entries.en: The emperor laughed aloud.
entries.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly.

entries.zh: 擢宣徽使，屢任以事。
entries.en: He was promoted to commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and repeatedly entrusted with important duties.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and repeatedly entrusted with affairs.

entries.zh: 帝知其貧，以金器賜之，海思即散於親友。
entries.en: Knowing he was poor, the emperor gave him gold vessels, which Haishi immediately distributed among his kin and friends.
entries.literal: The Emperor knew he was poor and bestowed gold vessels on him; Haishi at once distributed them among kin and friends.

entries.zh: 後從帝伐晉有功。
entries.en: Later he followed the emperor against Jin and distinguished himself.
entries.literal: Later he followed the Emperor in the campaign against Jin and had merit.

entries.zh: 世宗即位於軍中，皇太后以兵逆於潢河橫渡。
entries.en: When Shizong was proclaimed in the army, the empress dowager marched against him with troops at Huanghe Hengdu.
entries.literal: Shizong was established in the army; the Empress Dowager opposed him with troops at Huanghe Hengdu.

entries.zh: 太后遣耶律屋質責世宗自立。
entries.en: The empress dowager sent Yelü Wuzhi to rebuke Shizong for proclaiming himself emperor.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager sent Yelü Wuzhi to reproach Shizong for establishing himself on his own.

entries.zh: 屋質至帝前，諭旨不屈；
entries.en: Wuzhi came before Shizong and delivered the empress dowager's message without yielding;
entries.literal: Wuzhi came before the Emperor and conveyed the decree without yielding;

entries.zh: 世宗遣海思對，亦不遜，且命之曰：「汝見屋質勿懼！」
entries.en: Shizong sent Haishi to answer, and he too was unyielding; Shizong even told him, "When you see Wuzhi, have no fear!"
entries.literal: Shizong sent Haishi to reply, and he too was not deferential, and moreover ordered him, saying, "When you see Wuzhi, do not fear!"

entries.zh: 海思見太后還，不稱旨。
entries.en: Haishi met the empress dowager and returned, having failed to satisfy the emperor.
entries.literal: Haishi saw the Empress Dowager and returned, not to the Emperor's satisfaction.

entries.zh: 既和，領太后諸局事。
entries.en: After peace was made, he oversaw the empress dowager's various bureaus.
entries.literal: After peace, he oversaw the Empress Dowager's various bureaus.

entries.zh: 穆宗即位，與冀王敵烈謀反，死獄中。
entries.en: When Muzong succeeded, he plotted rebellion with Prince Ji Dilie and died in prison.
entries.literal: When Muzong took the throne, he plotted rebellion with Prince Ji Dilie and died in prison.

entries.zh: 敵獵，字烏輦，六院夷離堇術不魯之子。
entries.en: Dilie, whose style was Wulian, was the son of Shubulu, yilieqin of the Six Courts.
entries.literal: Dilie, style Wulian, was the son of Shubulu, yilieqin of the Six Courts.

entries.zh: 少多詐。
entries.en: From youth he was highly deceitful.
entries.literal: From youth he was greatly deceitful.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，為群牧都林牙。
entries.en: When Shizong succeeded, he was appointed linya of the Directorate of Herds.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was made linya of the Directorate of Herds.

entries.zh: 察割謀亂，官僚多被囚系。
entries.en: When Chagai plotted rebellion, many officials were thrown into prison.
entries.literal: When Chagai plotted rebellion, many officials were imprisoned.

entries.zh: 及壽安王與耶律屋質率兵來討，諸黨以次引去。
entries.en: When Prince Shou'an and Yelü Wuzhi marched against them with troops, the rebel factions withdrew one by one.
entries.literal: When Prince Shou'an and Yelü Wuzhi led troops to suppress them, the factions withdrew one after another.

entries.zh: 察割度事不成，即詣囚所，持弓矢脅曰：「悉殺此曹！」
entries.en: Seeing that he could not prevail, Chagai went to the prison, took up bow and arrow, and threatened, "Kill them all!"
entries.literal: Chagai judged that the affair would not succeed; he went at once to the prison, took up bow and arrow, and threatened, "Kill this whole lot!"

entries.zh: 敵獵進曰：「殺何益於事？
entries.en: Dilie came forward and said, "What good would killing do?
entries.literal: Dilie stepped forward and said, "What good would killing do?

entries.zh: 竊料屋質將立壽安王，故為此舉，且壽安未必知。
entries.en: I suspect Wuzhi means to set up Prince Shou'an—that is why he has done this, and Shou'an may not even know.
entries.literal: I privately judge that Wuzhi intends to set up Prince Shou'an; that is why he has done this, and Shou'an may not even know.

entries.zh: 若遣人藉此為辭，庶可免。」
entries.en: Send someone with that as your plea and you may yet save yourselves."
entries.literal: If you send someone using this as a plea, you may yet escape."

entries.zh: 察割曰：「如公言。
entries.en: Chagai said, "You are right.
entries.literal: Chagai said, "As you say.

entries.zh: 誰可使者？」
entries.en: Who shall go?"
entries.literal: Who can be sent?"

entries.zh: 敵獵曰：「大王若不疑，敵獵請與罨撒葛同往說之。」
entries.en: Dilie said, "If you do not doubt me, I ask to go with Yansage to negotiate with them."
entries.literal: Dilie said, "If Your Highness does not doubt me, Dilie asks to go with Yansage to persuade them."

entries.zh: 察割遣之。
entries.en: Chagai sent them off.
entries.literal: Chagai sent them.

entries.zh: 壽安王用敵獵計，誘殺察割，凡被脅之人無一被害者，皆敵獵之力。
entries.en: Prince Shou'an used Dilie's stratagem to lure Chagai out and kill him; not one of those who had been coerced was harmed, and that was entirely Dilie's doing.
entries.literal: Prince Shou'an used Dilie's plan to lure and kill Chagai; of all who had been coerced, not one was harmed—it was all Dilie's doing.

entries.zh: 亂既平，帝嘉賞，然未顯用。
entries.en: After the rebellion was put down, the emperor praised and rewarded him but did not give him prominent office.
entries.literal: After the disorder was settled, the emperor praised and rewarded him, yet did not give him prominent employment.

entries.zh: 敵獵失望，居常怏怏，結群不逞，陰懷不軌。
entries.en: Disappointed, Dilie lived in constant resentment, joined malcontents, and secretly plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: Dilie was disappointed; he lived in constant resentment, joined a band of unruly men, and secretly harbored disloyal designs.

entries.zh: 應歷三年，與其黨謀立婁國，事覺，陵遲死。
entries.en: In the third year of Yingli he conspired with his followers to set up Louguo; when the plot was discovered, he was executed by dismemberment.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yingli he plotted with his faction to set up Louguo; when the affair was exposed, he died by dismemberment.

entries.zh: 蕭翰耶律牒蠟耶律朗耶律劉哥
entries.en: Xiao Han, Yelü Diepa, Yelü Lang, and Yelü Liuge
entries.literal: Xiao Han, Yelü Diepa, Yelü Lang, Yelü Liuge

entries.en: Pendu)〉
entries.literal: (Pendu)〉 (alternate name, closing parenthesis)〉

entries.zh: 耶律海思耶律敵獵蕭革
entries.en: Yelü Haishi, Yelü Dilie, and Xiao Ge
entries.literal: Yelü Haishi, Yelü Dilie, Xiao Ge

entries.zh: 蕭胡睹，字乙辛。
entries.en: Xiao Hudu, whose courtesy name was Yixin.
entries.literal: Xiao Hudu, courtesy name Yixin.

entries.zh: 口吃，視斜，發卷，伯父孝穆見之曰：「是兒狀貌，族中未嘗有。」
entries.en: He stuttered, his eyes looked askew, and his hair curled; when his uncle Xiao Xiaomu saw him he said, "This boy's looks are unlike anything our clan has ever produced."
entries.literal: He stuttered, his gaze was skewed, and his hair curled; when his uncle Xiao Xiaomu saw him he said, "This boy's appearance is unlike anything our clan has ever had."

entries.zh: 及壯，魁梧桀傲，好揚人惡。
entries.en: When he grew up he was tall and imposing, fierce and overbearing, and loved to broadcast other people's faults.
entries.literal: When he reached maturity he was tall and imposing, fierce and arrogant, and fond of broadcasting others' faults.

entries.zh: 重熙中，為祗候郎君。
entries.en: During the Chongxi era he served as an attendant gentleman.
entries.literal: During the Chongxi era he served as an attendant gentleman.

entries.zh: 俄遷興聖宮使，尚秦國長公主，授駙馬都尉。
entries.en: Before long he was promoted to commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace, married the eldest princess of Qin, and was appointed imperial son-in-law commandant.
entries.literal: Before long he was promoted to commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace, married the eldest princess of Qin, and was appointed imperial son-in-law commandant.

entries.zh: 以不諧離婚，復尚齊國公主，為北面林牙。
entries.en: Because the marriage had grown discordant he divorced her, then married the princess of Qi and was made a Northern Court linya.
entries.literal: Because the marriage was discordant he divorced, then married the princess of Qi and was made a Northern Court linya.

entries.zh: 清寧中，歷北、南院樞密副使，代族兄術哲為西北路招討使。
entries.en: During Qingning he served in turn as associate privy commissioner of the Northern and Southern Courts, then replaced his clansman Shuzhe as Northwestern Route pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: During Qingning he successively held the posts of associate privy commissioner of the Northern and Southern Courts, and replaced his clansman Shuzhe as Northwestern Route pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 時蕭革與蕭阿剌俱為樞密使，不協，革以術哲為阿剌所愛，嫉之。
entries.en: At that time Xiao Ge and Xiao Ala were both privy commissioners and did not get along; Ge envied Shuzhe because Ala favored him.
entries.literal: At that time Xiao Ge and Xiao Ala were both privy commissioners and were at odds; Ge envied Shuzhe because Ala favored him.

entries.zh: 朮哲受代赴闕，先嘗借官粟，留直而去。
entries.en: Shuzhe was relieved of his post and went to court; he had earlier borrowed official grain and departed while still owing his commission stipend.
entries.literal: Shuzhe was relieved and went to court; he had earlier borrowed official grain and left still owing his commission stipend.

entries.zh: 胡睹希革意，發其事，術哲因得罪。
entries.en: Hudu, hoping to please Ge, exposed the affair, and Shuzhe was punished as a result.
entries.literal: Hudu, hoping to please Ge, exposed the matter, and Shuzhe was punished accordingly.

entries.zh: 胡睹又欲要權，歲時獻遺珍玩、畜產於革，二人相愛過於兄弟。
entries.en: Hudu also sought to win power; year after year he sent Ge rare curios and livestock, and the two grew as close as brothers.
entries.literal: Hudu also sought to seize power; each year he presented Ge with rare objects and livestock, and the two became closer than brothers.

entries.zh: 胡睹族弟敵烈為北克，薦國舅詳穩蕭胡篤於胡睹，胡睹見其辨給壯勇，傾心交結。
entries.en: Hudu's clansman Dilie served as a Northern ke; he recommended the imperial uncle's detail-stable Xiao Huduo to Hudu, and when Hudu saw how eloquent and bold he was he gave himself wholeheartedly to the friendship.
entries.literal: Hudu's clansman Dilie served as a Northern ke; he recommended the imperial uncle's detail-stable Xiao Huduo to Hudu, and when Hudu saw his eloquence and martial courage he devoted himself to befriending him.

entries.zh: 每遇休沐，言論終日，人皆怪之。
entries.en: Whenever they had a day off they talked from morning to night, and everyone thought it odd.
entries.literal: Whenever they had a rest day they talked all day long, and everyone found it strange.

entries.zh: 會胡睹同知北院樞密事，奏胡篤及敵烈可用，帝以敵烈為旗鼓拽剌詳穩，胡篤為宿直官。
entries.en: When Hudu became associate administrator of Northern Court privy affairs, he memorialized that Huduo and Dilie were fit for service; the emperor appointed Dilie drum-and-banner zhala detail-stable and Huduo a night-duty officer.
entries.literal: When Hudu became associate administrator of Northern Court privy affairs, he memorialized that Huduo and Dilie were fit for service; the emperor appointed Dilie drum-and-banner zhala detail-stable and Huduo night-duty officer.

entries.zh: 及革構陷其兄阿剌，胡篤陰為之助，時人醜之。
entries.en: When Ge framed his elder brother Ala, Huduo secretly helped him, and people of the time despised him for it.
entries.literal: When Ge framed his elder brother Ala, Huduo secretly aided him, and people of the time despised him for it.

entries.zh: 撒剌竹，孟父房滌冽之孫。
entries.en: Salazhu was a grandson of the Greater Father house Di Lie.
entries.literal: Salazhu was a grandson of the Greater Father house Di Lie.

entries.zh: 性凶暴。
entries.en: His nature was fierce and brutal.
entries.literal: His nature was fierce and brutal.

entries.zh: 清寧中，累遷宣徽使，改殿前都點檢，首與重元謀亂。
entries.en: During Qingning he was repeatedly promoted to palace commissioner and then made front-hall chief inspector; he was the first to plot rebellion with Chongyuan.
entries.literal: During Qingning he was repeatedly promoted to palace commissioner and then changed to front-hall chief inspector; he was first to plot rebellion with Chongyuan.

entries.zh: 會帝獵灤河，重元恐事泄，與扈從軍倉卒而戰。
entries.en: When the emperor hunted on the Luan River, Chongyuan feared the plot would leak out and fought hastily with the escort troops.
entries.literal: When the emperor hunted on the Luan River, Chongyuan feared the affair would leak and fought hastily with the escort troops.

entries.zh: 其子涅魯古既死，同黨潰散。
entries.en: After his son Nielugu died, the conspirators collapsed and scattered.
entries.literal: After his son Nielugu had died, the conspirators collapsed and scattered.

entries.zh: 撒剌竹適在畋所，聞亂，劫獵夫以援。
entries.en: Salazhu happened to be at the hunting grounds; hearing of the disturbance, he seized huntsmen to come to their aid.
entries.literal: Salazhu happened to be at the hunting grounds; hearing of the disturbance, he seized huntsmen to reinforce them.

entries.zh: 既至，知涅魯古已死，大悔恨之，謂曰：「我輩惟有死戰，胡為若兒戲，自取殞滅？
entries.en: When he arrived and learned Nielugu was already dead, he was filled with bitter regret and said, "Our side has only to fight to the death—why treat this like child's play and bring ruin on ourselves?
entries.literal: When he arrived and learned Nielugu was already dead, he greatly regretted it and said, "Our side has only to fight to the death—why act like child's play and bring ruin on ourselves?

entries.zh: 今行宮無備，乘夜劫之，大事可濟。
entries.en: The mobile palace is now unguarded; raid it by night and the great affair may yet succeed.
entries.literal: The mobile palace is now unguarded; raid it by night and the great affair may succeed.

entries.zh: 若俟明旦，彼將有備，安知我眾不攜貳？
entries.en: If we wait until dawn they will be prepared—who knows whether our men will not turn disloyal?
entries.literal: If we wait until dawn they will be prepared—who knows whether our host will not turn disloyal?

entries.zh: 一失機會，悔將無及。」
entries.en: Once the opportunity is lost, regret will come too late."
entries.literal: Once the opportunity is lost, regret will come too late."

entries.zh: 重元、蕭胡睹等曰：「今夕但可四面圍之，勿令外軍得入，彼何能備！」
entries.en: Chongyuan, Xiao Hudu, and the others said, "Tonight we need only surround them on all four sides and not let outside troops enter—how can they be prepared!"
entries.literal: Chongyuan, Xiao Hudu, and others said, "Tonight we need only surround them on all four sides and not let outside troops enter—how can they be prepared!"

entries.zh: 不從。
entries.en: They would not listen to him.
entries.literal: He was not obeyed.

entries.zh: 遲明，投仗而走，撒剌竹戰死。
entries.en: Near dawn they cast aside their weapons and fled; Salazhu died in battle.
entries.literal: Near dawn they cast aside their weapons and fled; Salazhu died in battle.

entries.zh: 蕭叠裏得，字胡睹堇，國舅少父房之後。
entries.en: Xiao Dielide, whose courtesy name was Hudu Jin, was a descendant of the imperial uncle's Lesser Father house.
entries.literal: Xiao Dielide, courtesy name Hudu Jin, was a descendant of the imperial uncle's Lesser Father house.

entries.zh: 父雙古，尚鈿匿公主，仕至國舅詳穩。
entries.en: His father Shuanggu married Princess Dianni and rose to the post of imperial uncle's detail-stable.
entries.literal: His father Shuanggu married Princess Dianni and rose to imperial uncle's detail-stable.

entries.zh: 叠裏得幼警敏不羈，好射獵。
entries.en: Dielide was sharp-witted and unruly as a boy and loved hunting.
entries.literal: Dielide in youth was sharp-witted and unrestrained, and loved hunting.

entries.zh: 太平中，以外戚補祗候郎君，歷延昌宮使、殿前副點檢。
entries.en: During Taiping, as a maternal kinsman he was appointed attendant gentleman and served as Yanchang Palace commissioner and deputy front-hall inspector.
entries.literal: During Taiping, as a maternal relative he was appointed attendant gentleman, and served as Yanchang Palace commissioner and deputy front-hall inspector.

entries.zh: 重熙十三年伐夏，叠裏得將偏師首入敵境，多所俘掠，遷都點檢，改烏古敵烈部都詳穩。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Chongxi, during the campaign against Xia, Dielide led a detached force that was first to enter enemy territory and took many captives and much booty; he was promoted to metropolitan inspector and reassigned as overall detail-stable of the Wugu and Dilie tribes.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chongxi during the campaign against Xia, Dielide led a detached force that first entered enemy territory and took many captives and booty; he was promoted to metropolitan inspector and reassigned as overall detail-stable of the Wugu and Dilie tribes.

entries.zh: 十八年，再舉西伐，叠裏得奏：「軍馬器械之事，務在選將，夏人豈為難制，但嚴設斥堠，不用掩襲計，何慮不勝？」
entries.en: In the eighteenth year another western campaign was launched; Dielide memorialized, "Matters of horses, arms, and equipment depend on choosing the right generals. Are the Xia people truly so hard to control? Only set scouts strictly and do not rely on surprise raids—why should we fear we cannot win?"
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year a western campaign was launched again; Dielide memorialized, "Matters of army mounts and weapons depend on choosing generals; are the Xia people so hard to control? Only set scouts strictly and do not use surprise-raid tactics—why worry about not winning?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「卿其速行，無後軍期。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Set out at once; do not fall behind the army's schedule."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "You should set out at once; do not miss the army's schedule."

entries.zh: 既而叠裏得失利還，復為都點檢。
entries.en: Before long Dielide returned after a setback and was again made metropolitan inspector.
entries.literal: Before long Dielide returned after a setback and was again made metropolitan inspector.

entries.zh: 十九年，夏人來侵金肅軍，上遣叠裏得率輕兵督戰，至河南三角川，斬候者八人，擒觀察使，以功命知漢人行宮都部署事，出為西南面招討使。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year the Xia invaded Jinsu Army; the emperor sent Dielide with light troops to oversee the fighting. At Sanjiaochuan south of the river he beheaded eight scouts and captured a surveillance commissioner; for this merit he was appointed to administer the Han mobile palace deployment and sent out as Southwestern Route pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year the Xia invaded Jinsu Army; the emperor sent Dielide with light troops to oversee the fighting; reaching Sanjiaochuan south of the river, he beheaded eight scouts, captured a surveillance commissioner, and for his merit was appointed to administer the Han mobile palace deployment and sent out as Southwestern Route pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 族弟黃八家奴告其主私議宮掖事，叠裏得寢之。
entries.en: A clansman's slave named Huangba reported that his master had privately discussed inner-palace affairs; Dielide suppressed the report.
entries.literal: A clansman's slave Huangba reported that his master had privately discussed palace inner matters; Dielide suppressed it.

entries.zh: 事覺，決大杖，削爵為民。
entries.en: When the affair came to light he was sentenced to heavy cudgeling and stripped of his noble rank to commoner status.
entries.literal: When the affair came to light he was sentenced to heavy cudgeling and stripped of rank to commoner status.

entries.zh: 清寧中，上以所坐事非叠裏得所犯，起為南京統軍使。
entries.en: During Qingning the emperor held that the offense for which he had been punished was not one Dielide had committed, and restored him as Nanjing supreme commander.
entries.literal: During Qingning the emperor held that the offense for which he had been punished was not what Dielide had done, and restored him as Nanjing supreme commander.

entries.zh: 至是，從重元子涅魯古等亂，敗走被擒，伏誅。
entries.en: At this juncture he joined Nielugu and the others in Chongyuan's rebellion, was defeated and fled, was captured, and was executed.
entries.literal: At this juncture he joined Nielugu and others in Chongyuan's rebellion, was defeated and fled, was captured, and was executed.

entries.zh: 耶律乙辛知北院樞密事，胡睹位在乙辛下，意怏怏不平。
entries.en: Yelü Yixin administered Northern Court privy affairs; Hudu stood below Yixin in rank and was resentful and ill at ease.
entries.literal: Yelü Yixin administered Northern Court privy affairs; Hudu ranked below Yixin and was discontent and resentful.

entries.zh: 初，胡睹嘗與重元子涅魯古謀逆，欲其速發。
entries.en: Earlier Hudu had plotted rebellion with Chongyuan's son Nielugu and wanted him to move quickly.
entries.literal: Earlier Hudu had once plotted rebellion with Chongyuan's son Nielugu and wished him to act quickly.

entries.zh: 會車駕獵太子山，遂與涅魯古脅弩手軍犯行宮。
entries.en: When the emperor hunted at Mount Taizi, he joined Nielugu in coercing the crossbow troops to attack the mobile palace.
entries.literal: When the emperor hunted at Mount Taizi, he joined Nielugu in coercing the crossbow troops to attack the mobile palace.

entries.zh: 既戰，涅魯古中流矢而斃，眾皆逃散。
entries.en: Once battle was joined Nielugu was struck by an arrow and died; the whole force fled and scattered.
entries.literal: Once battle was joined Nielugu was struck by an arrow and died; the host all fled and scattered.

entries.zh: 時同黨耶律撒剌竹適在圍場，聞亂，率獵夫來援。
entries.en: At that time their fellow conspirator Yelü Salazhu happened to be at the hunting grounds; hearing of the disturbance, he led huntsmen to reinforce them.
entries.literal: At that time their fellow conspirator Yelü Salazhu happened to be at the hunt grounds; hearing of the disturbance, he led huntsmen to reinforce them.

entries.zh: 其黨謂胡睹等曰：「我軍甚眾，乘其無備，中夜決戰，事冀有成；
entries.en: His confederates said to Hudu and the others, "Our force is very large; if we strike while they are unprepared and fight a decisive battle at midnight, the affair may yet succeed;
entries.literal: His confederates said to Hudu and the others, "Our force is very large; if we strike while they are unprepared and fight a decisive battle at midnight, the affair may yet succeed;

entries.zh: 若至明日，其誰從我？」
entries.en: but if we wait until tomorrow, who will still follow us?"
entries.literal: if we wait until tomorrow, who will follow us?"

entries.zh: 胡睹曰：「倉卒中黑白不辨，若內外軍相應，則吾事去矣。
entries.en: Hudu said, "In the heat of the moment friend and foe cannot be told apart; if the inner and outer armies coordinate, our cause is lost.
entries.literal: Hudu said, "In the chaos of the moment friend and foe cannot be distinguished; if the inner and outer armies coordinate, our cause is lost.

entries.zh: 黎明而發，何遲之有！」
entries.en: To set out at dawn—what delay is there!"
entries.literal: To set out at dawn—what delay is there!"

entries.zh: 重元聽胡睹之計，令四面巡警待旦。
entries.en: Chongyuan followed Hudu's plan and ordered patrols on all four sides to wait until dawn.
entries.literal: Chongyuan followed Hudu's plan and ordered patrols on all sides to wait until dawn.

entries.zh: 是夜，同黨立重元僭位號，胡睹自為樞密使。
entries.en: That night the conspirators set Chongyuan up with a usurped title, and Hudu made himself privy commissioner.
entries.literal: That night the conspirators set up Chongyuan with a usurped title; Hudu made himself privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 明日戰敗，胡睹被創，單騎遁走，至十七濼，投水死。
entries.en: The next day they were defeated; Hudu was wounded, fled alone on horseback to the Seventeen Marshes, and drowned himself.
entries.literal: The next day they were defeated in battle; Hudu was wounded, fled alone on horseback, reached the Seventeen Marshes, and drowned himself.

entries.zh: 五子，同日誅之。
entries.en: His five sons were executed on the same day.
entries.literal: His five sons were executed on the same day.

entries.zh: 奚回離保，一名翰，字挼懶，奚王忒鄰之後。
entries.en: Xi Huilibao, also named Han, whose courtesy name was Rou Lan, was a descendant of the Xi king Te Lin.
entries.literal: Xi Huilibao, also named Han, courtesy name Rou Lan, was a descendant of the Xi king Te Lin.

entries.zh: 善騎射，趫捷而勇，與其兄鱉裏剌齊名。
entries.en: Skilled at mounted archery, swift and brave, he was as renowned as his elder brother Bie Lila.
entries.literal: Skilled at mounted archery, swift and brave, he was as renowned as his elder brother Bie Lila.

entries.zh: 大安中，車駕幸中京，補護衛，稍遷鐵鷂軍詳穩。
entries.en: During Da'an, when the emperor visited Zhongjing, he was appointed to the guard and was gradually promoted to Iron Hawk Army detail-stable.
entries.literal: During Da'an when the emperor visited Zhongjing he was appointed to the guard, and was gradually promoted to Iron Hawk Army detail-stable.

entries.zh: 天慶間，徙北女直詳穩，兼知咸州路兵馬事，改東京統軍。
entries.en: During Tianqing he was transferred to Northern Jurchen detail-stable, concurrently administered Xianzhou Route military affairs, and was made Eastern Capital supreme commander.
entries.literal: During Tianqing he was transferred to Northern Jurchen detail-stable, concurrently knew Xianzhou Route military affairs, and was changed to Eastern Capital supreme commander.

entries.zh: 既而諸蕃入寇，番破之，遷奚六部大王，兼總知東路兵馬事。
entries.en: Before long, when various frontier peoples invaded, he repeatedly defeated them, was promoted to great king of the Six Xi Tribes, and concurrently oversaw Eastern Route military affairs.
entries.literal: Before long when various frontier peoples invaded he repeatedly defeated them, was promoted to great king of the Six Xi Tribes, and concurrently oversaw Eastern Route military affairs.

entries.zh: 保大二年，金兵至，天祚播遷，回離保率吏民立秦晉國王淳為帝。
entries.en: In the second year of Baoda the Jin troops arrived; Tianzuo was driven into flight; Huilibao led officials and commoners to install the Prince of Qin and Jin, Chun, as emperor.
entries.literal: In the second year of Baoda Jin troops arrived; Tianzuo was driven into flight; Huilibao led officials and commoners to install Prince of Qin and Jin Chun as emperor.

entries.zh: 淳偽署回離保知北院樞密事，兼諸軍都統，屢敗宋兵。
entries.en: Chun falsely appointed Huilibao to administer Northern Court privy affairs and serve concurrently as overall commander of all armies, and he repeatedly defeated Song troops.
entries.literal: Chun falsely appointed Huilibao to know Northern Court privy affairs and concurrently overall commander of all armies, and he repeatedly defeated Song troops.

entries.zh: 淳死，其妻普賢女攝事。
entries.en: When Chun died his wife, Lady Puxian, assumed control of affairs.
entries.literal: When Chun died his wife, the Lady Puxian, assumed affairs.

entries.zh: 是年，金兵由居庸關入，回離保知北院，即箭笴山自立，號奚國皇帝，改元天復，設奚、漢、渤海三樞密院，改東、西節度使為二王，分司建官。
entries.en: That year Jin troops entered through Juyong Pass; Huilibao, who still held Northern Court affairs, at once declared himself independent on Arrow Bamboo Mountain, styled himself emperor of the Xi state, changed the era name to Tianfu, established three privy councils for Xi, Han, and Bohai, changed the eastern and western military commissioners into two kings, and divided offices to establish a government.
entries.literal: That year Jin troops entered through Juyong Pass; Huilibao, who still held Northern Court affairs, at once declared himself independent on Arrow Bamboo Mountain, styled himself emperor of the Xi state, changed the era name to Tianfu, established three privy councils for Xi, Han, and Bohai, changed the eastern and western military commissioners to two kings, and divided offices to establish officials.

entries.zh: 時奚人巴輒、韓家奴等引兵擊附近契丹部落，劫掠人畜，群情大駭。
entries.en: At that time the Xi men Baze and Han Jianu and others led troops against nearby Khitan tribes, plundering people and livestock, and popular feeling was greatly alarmed.
entries.literal: At that time the Xi men Baze and Han Jianu and others led troops to attack nearby Khitan tribes, plundering people and livestock; popular feeling was greatly alarmed.

entries.zh: 會回離保為郭藥師所敗，一軍離心，其黨耶律阿古哲與其甥乙室八斤等殺之，偽立凡八月。
entries.en: When Huilibao was defeated by Guo Yaoshi the whole army lost heart; his faction Yelü Aguzhe and his nephew Yishi Bajin and others killed him; his false reign had lasted only eight months in all.
entries.literal: When Huilibao was defeated by Guo Yaoshi the whole army lost heart; his faction Yelü Aguzhe and his nephew Yishi Bajin and others killed him; his false reign lasted only eight months in all.

entries.zh: 古叠，本宮分人，不知姓氏。
entries.en: Gudie was originally from the founding-khan household division; his surname is unknown.
entries.literal: Gudie was originally from the founding-khan household division; his surname is unknown.

entries.zh: 好戲狎，不喜繩檢。
entries.en: He loved playful familiarity and did not care for restraint.
entries.literal: He loved playful familiarity and did not like restraint.

entries.zh: 膂力過人，善擊鞠。
entries.en: His strength surpassed other men's, and he excelled at cuju.
entries.literal: His physical strength surpassed others', and he excelled at cuju.

entries.zh: 重熙初，為護衛，歷宿直官。
entries.en: Early in Chongxi he served as a guardsman and passed through night-duty officer posts.
entries.literal: Early in Chongxi he served as a guardsman and passed through night-duty officer posts.

entries.zh: 十三年，西征，以古叠為先鋒。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of the western expedition Gudie was made vanguard.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of the western expedition, Gudie was made vanguard.

entries.zh: 夏人伏兵掩之，古叠力戰，麾下士多歿，乃單騎突出。
entries.en: Xia troops lay in ambush and struck him; Gudie fought fiercely, many of the men under his command were killed, and he broke out alone on horseback.
entries.literal: Xia troops ambushed him with concealed forces; Gudie fought fiercely, many of his soldiers under him perished, and he broke out alone on horseback.

entries.zh: 遇夏王李元昊來圍，勢甚急。
entries.en: He encountered the Xia ruler Li Yuanhao coming to surround him; the situation grew extremely desperate.
entries.literal: He encountered the Xia ruler Li Yuanhao coming to surround him; the situation was extremely pressing.

entries.zh: 古叠馳射，應弦輒仆，躍馬直擊中堅，夏兵不能當，晡乃還營。
entries.en: Gudie galloped and shot; wherever his arrow struck a man fell; he spurred his horse straight at the enemy center; the Xia troops could not withstand him, and at dusk he returned to camp.
entries.literal: Gudie galloped and shot; wherever his arrow struck men fell; he spurred his horse straight at the enemy center; the Xia troops could not withstand him, and at dusk he returned to camp.

entries.zh: 改興聖宮太保。
entries.en: He was reassigned as grand guardian of the Xingsheng Palace.
entries.literal: He was reassigned as Xingsheng Palace grand guardian.

entries.zh: 清寧九年，從重元、涅魯古亂，與扈從兵戰，敗而遁，追擒之，陵遲而死。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Qingning he joined Chongyuan and Nielugu's rebellion, fought the emperor's escort troops, was defeated and fled, was pursued and captured, and died by dismemberment.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Qingning he joined Chongyuan and Nielugu's rebellion, fought the emperor's escort troops, was defeated and fled, was pursued and captured, and died by dismemberment.

entries.zh: 逆臣下 ○蕭胡睹蕭叠裏得古叠耶律撒剌竹奚回離保蕭特烈
entries.en: Rebellious Officials 3: Xiao Hudu, Xiao Dielide, Gudie, Yelü Salazhu, Xi Huilibao, and Xiao Telie
entries.literal: Rebellious Officials 3: Xiao Hudu, Xiao Dielide, Gudie, Yelü Salazhu, Xi Huilibao, Xiao Telie

entries.zh: 遼之初興，與奚、室韋密邇，土俗言語大概近俚。
entries.en: When the Liao state first emerged, it lay close to the Xi and Shiwei peoples, and its local customs and language were largely rustic and colloquial.
entries.literal: When Liao first arose, it was close to the Xi and Shiwei; local custom and speech were generally near to the vulgar.

entries.zh: 至太祖、太宗，奄有朔方，其治雖三用漢法，而先世奇首、遙輦之制尚多存者。
entries.en: By the reigns of Emperor Taizu and Emperor Taizong, the Liao had seized the northern frontier. Although their administration repeatedly adopted Chinese law, many institutions of the earlier Qishou and Yaolian eras still survived.
entries.literal: By the Taizu and Taizong Emperors, they covered the northern regions; though their governance thrice employed Han law, many institutions of earlier generations — the Qishou and Yaolian systems — still remained.

entries.zh: 子孫相繼，亦遵守而不易。
entries.en: Their descendants preserved these customs in succession, altering nothing.
entries.literal: Successive descendants also preserved them without change.

entries.zh: 故史之所載，官制、宮衛、部族、地理，率以國語為之稱號。
entries.en: Accordingly, the offices, palace guards, tribal divisions, and place names recorded in the history are for the most part designated in the Khitan state language.
entries.literal: Therefore what the history records — official institutions, palace guards, tribal divisions, and geography — generally uses the state language for its designations.

entries.zh: 不有注釋以辨之，則世何從而知，後何從而考哉。
