entries.en: Without explanatory glosses to clarify them, how could the present age understand them, or later generations verify them?
entries.literal: Without annotations to distinguish them, how would the age know, and how would posterity investigate?

entries.zh: 今即本史三互研究，撰次遼國語解以附其後，庶幾讀者無齟齬之患云。
entries.en: We have therefore cross-referenced the three sections of this history and compiled an Explanation of the Liao State Language to append here, so that readers need not stumble over unfamiliar terms.
entries.literal: Now, taking this history's three sections for mutual study, we compile and arrange an Explanation of the Liao State Language to append after it, so that readers may be free from the trouble of discord.

entries.zh: 太祖紀
entries.en: Annals of Emperor Taizu
entries.literal: Annals of Taizu

entries.zh: 耶律氏、蕭氏 本紀首書太祖姓耶律氏，繼書皇后蕭氏，則有國之初，已分二姓矣。
entries.en: Yelü and Xiao: the annals open by giving Taizu's surname as Yelü and the empress's as Xiao — showing that two clans were distinguished from the very founding of the state.
entries.literal: Yelü Clan, Xiao Clan — the basic annals first record Taizu surnamed Yelü, then record the empress surnamed Xiao; thus from the founding of the state, two surnames were already divided.

entries.zh: 有謂始興之地曰世裏，譯者以世裏為耶律，故國族皆以耶律為姓。
entries.en: One account holds that the land where the dynasty arose was called Shili; translators rendered this as Yelü, and the imperial clan accordingly adopted Yelü as its surname.
entries.literal: Some say the place of initial rise was called Shili; translators took Shili as Yelü, so the state clan all took Yelü as surname.

entries.zh: 有謂述律皇后兄子名蕭翰者，為宣武軍節度使，其妹複為皇后，故後族皆以蕭為姓。
entries.en: Another account says that Xiao Han, nephew of Empress Shulü and Military Commissioner of the Xuanwu Army, had a sister who also became empress; the consort clan therefore took the surname Xiao.
entries.literal: Some say Empress Shulü's elder brother's son, named Xiao Han, was Military Commissioner of Xuanwu Army; his younger sister again became empress, so the consort clan all took Xiao as surname.

entries.zh: 其說與紀不合，故陳大任不取。
entries.en: These explanations conflict with the annals, and Chen Daren rejected them.
entries.literal: These explanations do not accord with the annals, so Chen Daren did not accept them.

entries.zh: 又有言以漢字書者曰耶律、蕭，以契丹字書者曰移剌、石抹，則亦無可考矣。
entries.en: Some also say that in Chinese characters the names appear as Yelü and Xiao, while in Khitan script they appear as Yila and Shimo — but this too cannot be substantiated.
entries.literal: There is also a saying that written in Han characters they are Yelü and Xiao, written in Khitan script they are Yila and Shimo — but this too cannot be verified.

entries.zh: 大迭烈府 即迭剌部之府也。
entries.en: Great Dielie Prefecture: the administrative seat of the Diela tribe.
entries.literal: Great Dielie Prefecture — that is, the prefecture of the Diela tribe.

entries.zh: 初，阻午可汗與其弟撒裏本領之，及太祖以部夷離 即位，因強大難制，析為二院。
entries.en: Originally Khan Zuwu and his brother Saben jointly governed it. When Taizu acceded as tribal yilij, the tribe had grown so powerful that it was split into two courts.
entries.literal: At first, Khan Zuwu and his younger brother Saben jointly led it; when Taizu acceded as tribal yilij, because it was strong and hard to control, it was divided into two courts.

entries.zh: 烈、剌音相近。
entries.en: The characters lie and la are phonetically similar.
entries.literal: Lie and la sound close to each other.

entries.zh: 龍眉宮 太祖取天梯、蒙國、別魯三山之勢於葦澱，射金齪箭以識之，名龍眉宮。
entries.en: Dragon Eyebrow Palace: Taizu selected a site at a reed marsh where three mountains — Tianti, Mengguo, and Bielu — converged, marked it by shooting a golden cuo arrow, and named it Dragon Eyebrow Palace.
entries.literal: Dragon Eyebrow Palace — Taizu took the terrain formed by the three mountains Tianti, Mengguo, and Bielu at the reed marsh, shot a golden cuo arrow to mark it, and named it Dragon Eyebrow Palace.

entries.zh: 神冊三年，築都城於其地，臨潢府是也。
entries.en: In the third year of the Sence era, a capital was built there — present-day Linhuang Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the third year of Sence, a capital city was built on that site — this is Linhuang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 齪，測角切，箭名。
entries.en: Cuo, pronounced with the ce initial and jiao final: the name of an arrow type.
entries.literal: Cuo — ce angle cut; the name of an arrow.

entries.zh: 烏魯古、阿里只 太祖及述律后受諲譔降時所乘二馬名也，因賜諲譔夫婦以為名。
entries.en: Ulugu and Alizhi: names of two horses ridden by Taizu and Empress Shulü when accepting Yinzhuan's surrender; they were bestowed on Yinzhuan and his wife.
entries.literal: Ulugu and Alizhi — the names of two horses ridden when Taizu and Empress Shulü received Yinzhuan's surrender; they were bestowed on Yinzhuan and his wife as names.

entries.zh: 萬役陷河冶 地名。
entries.en: Wanyi Xianhe Ye: a place name.
entries.literal: Wanyi Xianhe Ye — a place name.

entries.zh: 本漢土垠縣，有銀礦。
entries.en: Originally the Han county of Tuyin, which contained silver mines.
entries.literal: Originally Han Tuyin County; it had silver mines.

entries.zh: 太祖募民立寨以專采煉，故名陷河冶。
entries.en: Taizu recruited settlers to establish a mining colony there, hence the name Sunken River Smeltery.
entries.literal: Taizu recruited people to establish a stockade for exclusive mining and smelting, hence the name Xianhe Ye.

entries.zh: 屬珊 應天皇後從太祖征討，所俘人戶有技藝者置之帳下，<一一>名屬珊，蓋比珊瑚之寶。
entries.en: Shushan: Empress Yingtian followed Taizu on campaign; skilled captives were placed in her tent,<Note 11> named Shushan — like the treasure of coral.
entries.literal: Shushan — Empress Yingtian followed Taizu on campaign; captives with skills were placed under her tent,<One One> named Shushan — likened to the treasure of coral.

entries.zh: 橫帳 德祖族屬號三父房，稱橫帳，宗室之尤貴者。
entries.en: Hengzhang: Dezu's clansmen formed the Three Father Houses, called Hengzhang — the most exalted branch of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: Hengzhang — Dezu's clansmen were called the Three Father Houses, termed Hengzhang — the most noble of the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 景宗、聖宗紀
entries.en: Annals of Emperors Jingzong and Shengzong
entries.literal: Annals of Jingzong and Shengzong

entries.zh: 龍錫金佩 太祖從兄鐸骨札以本帳下蛇鳴，命知蛇語者神速姑解之，知蛇謂穴傍樹中有金，往取之，果得金，以為帶，名「龍錫金」。
entries.en: Dragon-Given Gold Belt: Taizu's cousin Duoguzha heard a snake cry under his tent and summoned Shensu Gu, who understood snake speech; the snake said gold lay in a tree by its burrow; they retrieved it and fashioned a belt called "Dragon-Given Gold."
entries.literal: Dragon-Given Gold Belt — Taizu's cousin Duoguzha heard a snake cry under his tent and summoned Shensu Gu, who understood snake speech; the snake said gold lay in a tree by its burrow; they retrieved it and fashioned a belt called "Dragon-Given Gold."

entries.zh: 史自遷、固，以迄晉、唐，其為書雄深浩博，讀者未能盡曉。
entries.en: From Sima Qian and Ban Gu through the Jin and Tang dynasties, the histories they wrote are vast and profound — so much so that readers cannot fully grasp them on their own.
entries.literal: Histories from Sima Qian and Ban Gu down through the Jin and Tang — their books are grand, deep, vast, and abstruse; readers cannot fully comprehend them.

entries.zh: 於是裴 、顏師古、李賢、何超、董沖諸儒，訓詁音釋，然後制度、名物、方言、奇字，可以一覽而周知。
entries.en: Scholars such as Pei Yin, Yan Shigu, Li Xian, He Chao, and Dong Chong then supplied phonetic and exegetical notes, making it possible to survey institutions, material objects, regional speech, and obscure characters in a single reading and understand them completely.
entries.literal: Thereupon Pei Yin, Yan Shigu, Li Xian, He Chao, Dong Chong, and other scholars provided exegetical and phonetic glosses, so that institutions, objects, dialect terms, and unusual characters could be surveyed at a glance and fully understood.

entries.zh: 其有助於後學多矣。
entries.en: They have been of immense benefit to later generations of scholars.
entries.literal: Their help to later students is great indeed.

entries.zh: 天祚自絕，大石茍延。
entries.en: Emperor Tianzuo brought ruin upon himself, while Yelü Dashi barely managed to prolong the line.
entries.literal: Emperor Tianzuo cut himself off; Yelü Dashi barely prolonged survival.

entries.zh: 國既丘墟，史亦蕪茀。
entries.en: The state lay in ruins, and its history too was overgrown and neglected.
entries.literal: The state already a ruinous mound, the history too was overgrown and neglected.

entries.zh: 耶律儼語多避忌，陳大任辭乏精詳。
entries.en: Yelü Yan's account was full of evasions and taboo; Chen Daren's text lacked precision and detail.
entries.literal: Yelü Yan's language was full of tabooed avoidance; Chen Daren's text lacked refinement and detail.

entries.zh: 《五代史》系之終篇，宋舊史埒諸載記。
entries.en: The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 relegated it to a closing appendix; the old Song histories treated it as a mere chronicle.
entries.literal: The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 attached it at the final chapter; the old Song histories ranked it among the annalistic records.

entries.zh: 予奪各徇其主，傳聞況失其真。
entries.en: Praise and blame each served its own master, and hearsay all the more distorted the truth.
entries.literal: Praise and blame each followed its own lord; hearsay moreover lost the truth.

entries.zh: 我世祖皇帝一視同仁，深加湣惻。
entries.en: Our Emperor Shizu treated all peoples alike with compassion and was deeply moved to pity.
entries.literal: Our Shizu Emperor treated all with equal benevolence and deeply added pity and compassion.

entries.zh: 嘗敕詞臣，撰次三史，首及於遼。
entries.en: He once ordered the court scholars to compile the three histories, giving first place to the Liao.
entries.literal: He once commanded literary officials to compile the three histories, beginning with Liao.

entries.zh: 六十餘年，歲月因循，造物有待。
entries.en: For more than sixty years the work dragged on, as though Heaven itself still waited for the right moment.
entries.literal: For more than sixty years the months and years dragged on; the Creator had yet to be awaited.

entries.zh: 臣脫脫誠惶誠恐頓首：欽惟皇帝陛下，如堯稽古，而簡寬容眾；
entries.en: Your subject Toqto'a, in deepest reverence and fear, bows his head and reports: I respectfully observe that Your Majesty, like Yao in studying antiquity, is concise in manner yet magnanimous toward all;
entries.literal: Your subject Toqto'a, in sincere trepidation and fear, bows his head: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty, like Yao in examining antiquity, is concise yet broad in tolerating the multitude;

entries.zh: 若舜好問，而浚哲冠倫。
entries.en: like Shun in his love of inquiry, yet profound in wisdom and unmatched among men.
entries.literal: like Shun in loving inquiry, yet profound in wisdom and foremost among men.

entries.zh: 講經兼誦乎祖謨，訪治旁求乎往牒。
entries.en: You lecture on the classics while reciting the plans of the ancients, and in seeking good government you consult widely the records of the past.
entries.literal: In lecturing on the classics you also recite the ancestral plans; in seeking good government you broadly search former documents.

entries.zh: 茲修史事，斷自宸衷。
entries.en: Now the work of compiling history proceeds from Your Majesty's own resolve.
entries.literal: Now the task of revising history is decided from Your Majesty's own heart.

entries.zh: 睿旨下而征聘行，朝士賀而遺逸起。
entries.en: Once Your sagely decree was issued, recruitment began; court officials rejoiced and hidden scholars came forward.
entries.literal: When the sagely decree descended, recruitment went forth; court officials rejoiced and recluses arose.

entries.zh: 於是命臣脫脫以中書右丞相領都總裁，中書平章政事臣鐵睦爾達世、中書右丞今平章政事臣賀惟一、御史中丞今翰林學士承旨臣張起巖，翰林學士臣歐陽玄、侍御史今集賢侍講學士兼國子祭酒臣呂思誠、翰林侍講學士臣揭傒斯奉命為總裁官。
entries.en: Thereupon Your Majesty appointed your subject Toqto'a, Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, as overall chief compiler, and ordered the Secretariat Councilor Tiemuer Dashi, Right Vice Chancellor and now Councilor He Wei, Censor-in-Chief and now Hanlin Expositor-in-Chief Zhang Qiyan, Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xuan, Attending Censor and now Academician Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Concurrent Director of the Imperial Academy Lü Sicheng, and Hanlin Lecturer Jie Xisi to serve as chief compilers.
entries.literal: Thereupon Your Majesty appointed your subject Toqto'a, as Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, to head the overall chief compilation; the Secretariat Councilor Tiemuer Dashi, the Right Vice Chancellor and now Councilor He Wei, the Censor-in-Chief and now Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief Zhang Qiyan, the Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xuan, the Attending Censor and now Academician Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Concurrent Director of the Imperial Academy Lü Sicheng, and the Hanlin Lecturer Jie Xisi were all ordered to serve as chief compilers.

entries.zh: 中書遴選儒臣宗文太監今兵部尚書臣廉惠山海牙、翰林直學士臣王沂、秘書著作佐郎臣徐昺、國史院編修官臣陳繹曾分撰《遼史》。
entries.en: The Secretariat selected the scholar-officials Zongwen Supervisor and now Minister of War Lian Hui Shanhaiya, Hanlin Academician Expositor Wang Yi, Secretariat Assistant Compiler Xu Bing, and National History Office Compiler Chen Yiceng to draft the 《History of Liao》 in sections.
entries.literal: The Secretariat selected the Confucian officials Zongwen Supervisor and now Minister of War Lian Hui Shanhaiya, Hanlin Academician Expositor Wang Yi, Secretariat Assistant Compiler Xu Bing, and National History Office Compiler Chen Yiceng to draft the 《History of Liao》 in separate parts.

entries.zh: 起至正三年四月，迄四年三月。
entries.en: Work began in the fourth month of the third year of Zhizheng and was completed in the third month of the fourth year.
entries.literal: Beginning in the fourth month of the third year of Zhizheng, ending in the third month of the fourth year.

entries.zh: 發故府之櫝藏，集遐方之匭獻，搜羅剔抉，刪潤研劘。
entries.en: We opened the archives of former offices, gathered memorials submitted from distant regions, searched and sifted the sources, and edited, polished, and refined the text.
entries.literal: We opened the casket stores of former offices, gathered memorial submissions from distant regions, searched and collected, sifted and selected, deleted, polished, refined, and carved.

entries.zh: 紀誌表傳，備成一代之書；
entries.en: The annals, treatises, tables, and biographies are now complete as a history of a full dynasty;
entries.literal: Basic annals, treatises, tables, and biographies were fully completed as a book of one dynasty;

entries.zh: 臧否是非，不迷千載之實。
entries.en: praise and blame, right and wrong, do not obscure the truth of a thousand years.
entries.literal: approval and disapproval, right and wrong, do not obscure the reality of a thousand years.

entries.zh: 臣脫脫叨承隆寄，幸睹成功。
entries.en: Your subject Toqto'a has been honored with this weighty commission and is fortunate to see the work completed.
entries.literal: Your subject Toqto'a presumptuously received this weighty commission and was fortunate to witness its completion.

entries.zh: 載宣日月之光華，願效涓埃之補報。
entries.en: May it reflect the splendor of sun and moon; I wish only to repay Your grace with the smallest service.
entries.literal: May it bear forth the splendor of sun and moon; I wish to render a mote's worth of repayment in supplement.

entries.zh: 我朝之論議歸正，氣之直則辭之昌；
entries.en: Our dynasty's judgments are upright; where the moral tone is straight, the writing flourishes;
entries.literal: Our dynasty's discussions return to the upright; where the spirit is straight, the language flourishes;

entries.zh: 遼國之君臣有知，善者喜而惡者懼。
entries.en: and the rulers and ministers of Liao who understand will rejoice at what is good and fear what is evil.
entries.literal: the rulers and ministers of the Liao state who have understanding—the good will rejoice and the wicked will fear.

entries.zh: 所撰本紀三十卷、志三十二卷、表八卷、列傳四十六卷，各著論贊，具存體裁，隨表以聞。
entries.en: The work comprises thirty juan of annals, thirty-two juan of treatises, eight juan of tables, and forty-six juan of biographies, each with its discussion and appraisal, fully preserving proper historiographical form, and is herewith submitted with this memorial.
entries.literal: What was compiled: thirty juan of basic annals, thirty-two juan of treatises, eight juan of tables, and forty-six juan of biographies, each with appended discussions and encomia, fully preserving the literary form, are submitted together with this memorial.

entries.zh: 上塵天覽，下情無任慚懼戰汗屏營之至。
entries.en: Though unworthy to meet Your exalted gaze, I submit it with deepest shame, fear, and trembling reverence.
entries.literal: It ascends to defile the Heavenly View; below, my feelings cannot bear the utmost of shame, fear, trembling sweat, and guarded trepidation.

entries.zh: 臣脫脫誠惶誠懼頓首頓首謹言。
entries.en: Your subject Toqto'a, in deepest reverence and fear, bows his head repeatedly and respectfully submits this report.
entries.literal: Your subject Toqto'a, in sincere trepidation and fear, bows his head, bows his head, and respectfully states.

entries.zh: 進遼史表
entries.en: Memorial Table on the Presentation of the History of Liao
entries.literal: Memorial Table Presenting the History of Liao

entries.zh: 二十年春二月，元福建行省參政袁天祿以福寧降。
entries.en: In the second month of spring in the twentieth year Yuan Tianlu, associate administrator of the Fujian Branch Secretariat, surrendered Funing.
entries.literal: In the second month of spring in the twentieth year Yuan Fujian Branch Secretariat Associate Administrator Yuan Tianlu submitted Funing.

entries.zh: 三月戊子，征劉基、宋濂、章溢、葉琛至。
entries.en: On wuzi day in the third month he summoned Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen to court.
entries.literal: On the day wuzi of the third month he summoned Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen to come.

entries.zh: 夏五月，徐達、常遇春敗陳友諒於池州。
entries.en: In the fifth month of summer Xu Da and Chang Yuchun defeated Chen Youliang at Chizhou.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of summer Xu Da and Chang Yuchun defeated Chen Youliang at Chizhou.

entries.zh: 閏月丙辰，友諒陷太平，守將朱文遜，院判花雲、王鼎，知府許瑗死之。
entries.en: On bingchen day in the intercalary month Youliang seized Taiping; the defender Zhu Wensun, Vice Commissioners Hua Yun and Wang Ding, and Prefect Xu Yuan were killed.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, day bingchen, Youliang took Taiping; the defending general Zhu Wensun, administrative vice commissioner Hua Yun and Wang Ding, and prefect Xu Yuan died for it.

entries.zh: 未幾，友諒弒其主徐壽輝，自稱皇帝，國號漢，盡有江西、湖廣地，約士誠合攻應天，應天大震。
entries.en: Soon after, Youliang murdered his master Xu Shouhui, declared himself emperor of Han, held all Jiangxi and Huguang, and joined Zhang Shicheng in a planned assault on Yingtian—the capital was thrown into alarm.
entries.literal: Before long Youliang murdered his lord Xu Shouhui, styled himself emperor, state title Han, fully held Jiangxi and Huguang lands, and agreed with Shicheng to jointly attack Yingtian—Yingtian was greatly shaken.

entries.zh: 諸將議先復太平以牽之，太祖曰：「不可。
entries.en: His commanders urged recapturing Taiping first to pin Youliang down; Taizu said, "No.
entries.literal: The generals discussed first recovering Taiping to pin him; Taizu said: "Cannot.

entries.zh: 彼居上游，舟師十倍於我，猝難復也。」
entries.en: He holds the upper river; his fleet outnumbers ours ten to one—we cannot retake Taiping in a rush."
entries.literal: He occupies the upper reaches; his naval forces are ten times ours—suddenly hard to recover."

entries.zh: 或請自將迎擊，太祖曰：「不可。
entries.en: Some urged him to lead the army out to meet them; Taizu said, "No.
entries.literal: Some asked him to lead in person to meet the attack; Taizu said: "Cannot.

entries.zh: 彼以偏師綴我，而全軍趨金陵，順流半日可達，吾步騎急難引還，百里趨戰，兵法所忌，非策也。」
entries.en: He would tie us down with a diversion while his main fleet raced for Jinling—half a day's sail downstream. Our foot and horse could not turn back in time; to fight a hundred li from home is what doctrine forbids."
entries.literal: He would use a detached force to detain us while his full army rushed Jinling—downstream half a day could reach; our infantry and cavalry urgently hard to pull back—a hundred li to rush to battle is what military law forbids; not a strategy."

entries.zh: 乃馳諭胡大海搗信州牽其後，而令康茂才以書紿友諒，令速來。
entries.en: He galloped orders to Hu Dahai to raid Xinzhou and threaten Youliang's rear, and had Kang Maocai lure him east with a forged letter.
entries.literal: He then galloped orders to Hu Dahai to strike Xinzhou in the rear to pull him, and ordered Kang Maocai with a letter to deceive Youliang and make him come quickly.

entries.zh: 友諒果引兵東。
entries.en: Youliang took the bait and marched east.
entries.literal: Youliang indeed led troops east.

entries.zh: 於是常遇春伏石灰山，徐達陣南門外，楊璟屯大勝港，張德勝等以舟師出龍江關，太祖親督軍盧龍山。
entries.en: Chang Yuchun hid at Lime Mountain, Xu Da formed line at the south gate, Yang Jing held Dasheng Harbor, Zhang Desheng and others took the fleet out through Longjiang Pass, and Taizu commanded in person from Lulong Mountain.
entries.literal: Thereupon Chang Yuchun lay in ambush at Lime Mountain, Xu Da formed battle at the south gate, Yang Jing encamped at Dasheng Harbor, Zhang Desheng and others with naval forces issued from Longjiang Pass, and Taizu personally supervised the army at Lulong Mountain.

entries.zh: 乙丑，友諒至龍灣，眾欲戰，太祖曰：「天且雨，趣食，乘雨擊之。」
entries.en: On yichou day Youliang reached Longwan; his men wanted to fight at once; Taizu said, "Rain is coming—eat first, then strike in the storm."
entries.literal: On the day yichou Youliang reached Longwan; the crowd wished to fight; Taizu said: "Heaven will soon rain—hurry and eat, strike them in the rain."

entries.zh: 須臾，果大雨，士卒競奮，雨止合戰，水陸夾擊，大破之，友諒乘別舸走。
entries.en: Rain burst upon them; the troops fought all the harder; when it cleared they closed on land and water together, shattered the Han fleet, and Youliang fled in a small boat.
entries.literal: In a moment rain indeed fell heavily; soldiers competed in vigor; when rain stopped they joined battle; land and water attacked from both sides and greatly defeated them; Youliang rode another boat and fled.

entries.zh: 遂復太平，下安慶，而大海亦克信州。
entries.en: He recovered Taiping, took Anqing, and Hu Dahai seized Xinzhou as well.
entries.literal: He then recovered Taiping, took Anqing, and Dahai also took Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 初，太祖令茂才紿友諒，李善長以為疑。
entries.en: Earlier Taizu had ordered Maocai's ruse; Li Shanchang had doubted it.
entries.literal: Earlier Taizu had ordered Maocai to deceive Youliang; Li Shanchang thought it doubtful.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「二寇合，吾首尾受敵，惟速其來而先破之，則士誠膽落矣。」
entries.en: Taizu said, "With both enemies allied we would be caught between them—only by drawing Youliang in and breaking him first will Shicheng lose heart."
entries.literal: Taizu said: "The two bandits united—we receive the enemy front and rear; only by hastening his coming and first breaking him will Shicheng's courage fall."

entries.zh: 已而士誠兵竟不出。
entries.en: In the end Zhang Shicheng's troops never marched.
entries.literal: Before long Shicheng's troops indeed did not come out.

entries.zh: 丁卯，置儒學提舉司，以宋濂為提舉，遣子標受經學。
entries.en: On dingmao day he established the Confucian Learning Promotion Office under Song Lian and set his son Biao to the classics.
entries.literal: On the day dingmao he established the Confucian Learning Promotion Office, with Song Lian as promoter, and sent his son Biao to receive classical learning.

entries.zh: 六月，耿再成敗石抹宜孫於慶元，宜孫戰死，遣使祭之。
entries.en: In the sixth month Geng Zaocheng defeated Shimo Yisun at Qingyuan; Yisun fell in battle and Taizu sent envoys to sacrifice to him.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Geng Zaocheng defeated Shimo Yisun at Qingyuan; Yisun died in battle; he sent envoys to offer sacrifice.

entries.zh: 秋九月，徐壽輝舊將歐普祥以袁州降。
entries.en: In the ninth month of autumn Ou Pu Xiang, a former officer of Xu Shouhui, surrendered Yuanzhou.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Xu Shouhui's old general Ou Pu Xiang submitted Yuanzhou.

entries.zh: 冬十二月，復遣夏煜以書諭國珍。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of winter he again sent Xia Yu with a letter summoning Guozhen.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of winter he again sent Xia Yu with a letter to instruct Guozhen.

entries.zh: 冬十月甲辰，遣起居注吳琳、魏觀以幣求遺賢於四方。
entries.en: On jiachen day in the tenth month of winter he sent imperial diarists Wu Lin and Wei Guan with gifts to seek worthy men in every quarter.
entries.literal: On day jiachen in the tenth month of winter he sent imperial diarists Wu Lin and Wei Guan with gifts to seek worthy men throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 丙午，令百官禮儀尚左。
entries.en: On bingwu day he ordered that official ceremony honor the left.
entries.literal: On day bingwu he ordered that ceremonial precedence in the bureaucracy honor the left.

entries.zh: 改李善長左相國，徐達右相國。
entries.en: Li Shanchang was made left chief councillor and Xu Da right chief councillor.
entries.literal: Li Shanchang was made left chief councillor, Xu Da right chief councillor.

entries.zh: 辛亥，祀元臣余闕於安慶，李黼於江州。
entries.en: On xinhai day he offered sacrifice to the Yuan loyalists Yu Que at Anqing and Li Fu at Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: On day xinhai he sacrificed to the Yuan loyalists Yu Que at Anqing and Li Fu at Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 壬子，置御史臺。
entries.en: On renzi day the Censorate was established.
entries.literal: On day renzi the Censorate was established.

entries.zh: 癸丑，湯和為征南將軍，吳禎副之，討國珍。
entries.en: On guichou day Tang He was made grand general for the southern expedition and Wu Zhen his deputy, to campaign against Guozhen.
entries.literal: On day guichou Tang He was made grand general for the southern expedition and Wu Zhen his deputy, to attack Guozhen.

entries.zh: 甲寅，定律令。
entries.en: On jiayin day laws and ordinances were promulgated.
entries.literal: On day jiayin laws and ordinances were promulgated.

entries.zh: 戊午，正郊社、太廟雅樂。
entries.en: On wuwu day the ceremonial music of the suburban altars and Imperial Temple was set right.
entries.literal: On day wuwu the ritual music of the suburban altars and Imperial Temple was corrected.

entries.zh: 本紀第一 太祖一
entries.en: Annals 1: Taizu, Part One
entries.literal: Annals 1, Taizu 1

entries.zh: 冬十月，燕兵自劉家口間道襲陷大寧，守將硃鑒死之。
entries.en: In the tenth month Yan's men slipped through Liujiakou by a hidden track, stormed Daning, and killed its defender Zhu Jian.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Yan's troops by a hidden route through Liujiakou suddenly attacked and took Daning; defending commander Zhu Jian died in the affair.

entries.zh: 總兵官劉真、都督陳亨援大寧，亨叛降燕。
entries.en: Commander Liu Zhen and Regional Commander Chen Heng marched to relieve Daning; Heng turned traitor and joined Yan.
entries.literal: Regional commander Liu Zhen and Commander Chen Heng went to relieve Daning; Heng rebelled and surrendered to Yan.

entries.zh: 燕以寧王權及朵顏三衛卒歸北平。
entries.en: Prince Yan brought Prince Ning Zhu Quan and the Uriankhai auxiliaries back to Beiping.
entries.literal: Yan, with Prince of Ning Zhu Quan and the troops of the three Uriankhai divisions, returned to Beiping.

entries.zh: 辛亥，李景隆重圍北平，燕兵還救。
entries.en: On xinhai Li Jinglong pressed Beiping hard; Yan's army wheeled home to its relief.
entries.literal: On the xinhai day, Li Jinglong heavily besieged Beiping; Yan's troops returned to the rescue.

entries.zh: 十一月辛未，李景隆及燕兵戰於鄭村壩，敗績，奔德州，諸軍盡潰。
entries.en: On xinwei of the eleventh month Li Jinglong met Yan at Zheng Village Dam, was shattered, fled to Dezhou, and the host dissolved.
entries.literal: On the xinwei day of the eleventh month, Li Jinglong fought Yan's troops at Zheng Village Dam, suffered defeat, fled to Dezhou, and the armies were wholly routed.

entries.zh: 燕王棣再上書於朝。
entries.en: Prince Yan Zhu Di again memorialized the throne.
entries.literal: Prince of Yan Zhu Di again submitted a memorial to the court.

entries.zh: 帝為罷齊泰、黃子澄官，仍留京師。
entries.en: Jianwen dismissed Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng from office yet kept them in the capital.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon dismissed Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng from office but kept them at the capital.

entries.zh: 或云帝由地道出亡。
entries.en: Others held that he had slipped away through a hidden passage.
entries.literal: Some say the emperor escaped through a secret tunnel.

entries.zh: 正統五年。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Zhengtong reign.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of the Zhengtong reign.

entries.zh: 有僧自雲南至廣西，詭稱建文皇帝。
entries.en: A monk came up from Yunnan into Guangxi and pretended to be the Jianwen emperor.
entries.literal: A monk from Yunnan arrived in Guangxi, falsely claiming to be the Jianwen emperor.

entries.zh: 恩恩知府岑瑛聞於朝。
entries.en: Cen Ying, prefect of En'en, reported the matter to the throne.
entries.literal: Cen Ying, prefect of En'en, reported it to the court.

entries.zh: 按問，乃鈞州人楊行祥，年已九十余，下獄，閱四月死。
entries.en: Under interrogation he proved to be Yang Xingxiang of Junzhou, already past ninety; he was thrown into prison and died four months later.
entries.literal: On investigation, he was Yang Xingxiang of Junzhou, already more than ninety years old; he was imprisoned and died four months later.

entries.zh: 同謀僧十二人，皆戍遼東。
entries.en: Twelve monks who had aided the plot were all exiled to Liaodong.
entries.literal: Twelve monks who had conspired with him were all banished to Liaodong.

entries.zh: 自後滇、黔、巴、蜀間，相傳有帝為僧時往來跡。
entries.en: After that, across Yunnan, Guizhou, Ba, and Shu, people kept saying they could trace the emperor's wanderings from the years he had lived as a monk.
entries.literal: Afterward, throughout Yunnan, Guizhou, Ba, and Shu, tradition held that traces remained of the emperor's comings and goings when he had been a monk.

entries.zh: 正德、萬曆、崇禎間，諸臣請續封帝後，及加廟諡，皆下部議，不果行。
entries.en: Under the Zhengde, Wanli, and Chongzhen emperors, ministers repeatedly asked that the Jianwen line be enfeoffed again and that temple rites and a posthumous title be granted; each proposal went to the ministries and died there.
entries.literal: During the Zhengde, Wanli, and Chongzhen reigns, various ministers requested renewed enfeoffment for the emperor's heirs and the addition of temple honors and posthumous titles; each time the matter was referred to the ministries for discussion and was not carried out.

entries.zh: 大清乾隆元年，詔廷臣集議，追諡曰恭閔惠皇帝。
entries.en: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, the Qing court ordered its ministers to convene and bestowed the posthumous title Emperor Gongmin Hui.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Qianlong reign of the Great Qing, an edict ordered the court ministers to assemble in deliberation and conferred the posthumous title Emperor Gongmin Hui.

entries.zh: 贊曰：惠帝天資仁厚。
entries.en: The eulogy says: Emperor Hui was naturally humane and generous.
entries.literal: The eulogy says: The Kind Emperor was naturally humane and generous.

entries.zh: 踐阼之初，親賢好學，召用方孝孺等。
entries.en: At the start of his reign he honored worthy men and loved learning, calling up Fang Xiaoru and others.
entries.literal: At the beginning of his reign he honored the worthy and loved learning, summoning and employing Fang Xiaoru and others.

entries.zh: 典章制度，銳意復古。
entries.en: In statutes and institutions he was intent on restoring antiquity.
entries.literal: In statutes and institutions he was keen to restore antiquity.

entries.zh: 嘗因病晏朝，尹昌隆進諫，即深自引咎，宣其疏於中外。
entries.en: Once, when illness made him late for court, Yin Changlong remonstrated; he at once took the blame upon himself and published the memorial throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Once, because of illness he held court late; Yin Changlong remonstrated, and he immediately took deep blame upon himself and published the memorial within and without the court.

entries.zh: 又除軍衞單丁，減蘇、松重賦，皆惠民之大者。
entries.en: He also released sole surviving sons in guard and battalion service and cut the crushing levies of Suzhou and Songjiang—measures that greatly benefited the people.
entries.literal: He also abolished sole-son service in guard and battalion households and reduced the heavy levies of Suzhou and Songjiang—all great benefits to the people.

entries.zh: 乃革命而後，紀年復稱洪武，嗣是子孫臣庶以紀載為嫌，草野傳疑，不無訛謬。
entries.en: After the usurpation the reign was again dated to Hongwu; thereafter heirs, officials, and commoners shrank from recording the truth, and popular rumor bred errors.
entries.literal: After the dynastic change, the reign era again was called Hongwu; thereafter descendants, officials, and commoners shrank from recording it, and popular rumor spread, not without error.

entries.zh: 更越聖朝，得經論定，尊名壹惠，君德用彰，懿哉。
entries.en: Under the present sage dynasty, canonical deliberation settled the matter; his honored name was unified as Hui, and his sovereign virtue stands revealed—admirable indeed!
entries.literal: Crossing into the sage dynasty, canonical discussion settled the matter; his honored name was unified as Hui, and his sovereign virtue was thereby displayed—how admirable!

entries.zh: 恭閔惠皇帝諱允炆。
entries.en: Emperor Gongmin Hui bore the tabooed name Yunwen.
entries.literal: Emperor Gongmin the Kind, tabooed name Yunwen.

entries.zh: 太祖孫，懿文太子第二子也。
entries.en: He was Taizu's grandson and the second son of the heir apparent Yiwen.
entries.literal: Grandson of Taizu, second son of heir apparent Yiwen.

entries.zh: 母妃呂氏。
entries.en: His mother was Consort Lü.
entries.literal: His mother was consort Lü.

entries.zh: 帝生潁慧好學，性至孝。
entries.en: From childhood he was keen-witted and devoted to study, and filial piety ran to the marrow of his nature.
entries.literal: From birth he was sharp-witted and fond of learning; his nature was supremely filial.

entries.zh: 年十四，待懿文太子疾，晝夜不暫離。
entries.en: At fourteen, while nursing the heir apparent Yiwen through his illness, he kept his bedside day and night without a single absence.
entries.literal: At age fourteen, when attending to heir apparent Yiwen's illness, day and night he did not leave for a moment.

entries.zh: 更二年，太子薨，居喪毀瘠。
entries.en: Two years later the heir apparent died, and in mourning he wasted nearly to death.
entries.literal: Two years later the heir apparent died; in mourning he wasted away.

entries.zh: 太祖撫之曰：「而誠純孝，顧不念我乎。」
entries.en: Taizu drew him close and said, "Your filial devotion is pure—but have you no room left to think of me?"
entries.literal: Taizu comforted him, saying: "You are truly pure in filial piety—yet do you spare no thought for me?"

entries.zh: 洪武二十五年九月，立為皇太孫。
entries.en: In the ninth month of Hongwu 25, he was installed as heir apparent grandson.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year of Hongwu, he was established as heir apparent grandson.

entries.zh: 二十九年，重定諸王見東宮儀制，朝見後於內殿行家人禮，以諸王皆尊屬也。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year the court revised how princes attended the Eastern Palace: after the formal audience they were to observe family courtesy in the inner hall, for the princes were all the heir's senior kin.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the protocol for princes' audiences with the Eastern Palace was revised: after the court audience they were to perform family rites in the inner hall, because the princes were all senior kin.

entries.zh: 初，太祖命太子省決章奏，太子性仁厚，於刑獄多所減省。
entries.en: Earlier Taizu had set the heir apparent to sift and decide memorials; humane by temperament, the heir often lightened penalties in criminal matters.
entries.literal: Initially Taizu had charged the heir apparent to review and decide on memorials and documents; the heir apparent's nature was humane and generous, and in criminal cases he often reduced sentences.

entries.zh: 至是以命太孫，太孫亦復佐以寬大。
entries.en: The same charge passed to the heir apparent grandson, who again tempered judgment with mercy.
entries.literal: Now the same charge was given to the heir apparent grandson, and the heir apparent grandson again assisted with leniency.

entries.zh: 嘗請於太祖，遍考禮經，參之歷朝刑法，改定洪武《律》畸重者七十三條，天下莫不頌德焉。
entries.en: He once asked Taizu to comb the ritual classics and, against the penal codes of past dynasties, soften seventy-three harsh articles of the Hongwu Code; the empire rang with praise.
entries.literal: He once petitioned Taizu to examine comprehensively the ritual classics and, consulting punishments of successive dynasties, revise seventy-three articles of the Hongwu Code that were excessively severe; throughout the realm none failed to praise his virtue.

entries.zh: 秋七月壬午朔，大祀天地於南郊，奉太祖配。
entries.en: On the renwu new moon in the seventh month he offered the great suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, with Taizu joined in the rite.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, on the renwu new moon, he performed the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb, with Taizu accompanying in the rite.

entries.zh: 詔：「今年以洪武三十五年為紀，明年為永樂元年。
entries.en: An edict declared: "This year shall count as Hongwu 35; next year begins Yongle 1.
entries.literal: Edict: "This year shall be reckoned as the thirty-fifth year of Hongwu; next year shall be the first year of Yongle.

entries.zh: 建文中更改成法，一復舊制。
entries.en: Every Jianwen reform is rolled back to the old order.
entries.literal: Laws and institutions changed during the Jianwen reign are all restored to the former system.

entries.zh: 山東、北平、河南被兵州縣，復徭役三年，未被兵者與鳳陽、淮安、徐、滁、揚三州蠲租一年，餘天下州縣悉蠲今年田租之半。」
entries.en: War-ravaged districts in Shandong, Beiping, and Henan owe no corvée for three years; untouched districts together with Fengyang, Huai'an, and the prefectures of Xu, Chu, and Yang are granted one year's rent remission; everywhere else, half this year's land tax is forgiven."
entries.literal: In Shandong, Beiping, and Henan, districts and counties that suffered warfare are exempted from corvée labor for three years; those untouched by warfare, together with Fengyang, Huai'an, and the three prefectures Xu, Chu, and Yang, have land tax remitted for one year; all other districts and counties throughout the realm have half of this year's land tax remitted."

entries.zh: 癸未，召前北平按察使陳瑛為左副都御史，盡復建文朝廢斥者官。
entries.en: On guiwei he recalled former Beiping surveillance commissioner Chen Ying as left vice censor-in-chief and restored every officeholder cashiered under Jianwen.
entries.literal: On guiwei, he summoned the former Beiping surveillance commissioner Chen Ying to be Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and fully restored the offices of those dismissed in the Jianwen reign.

entries.zh: 甲申，復官制。
entries.en: On jiashen the former official hierarchy was restored.
entries.literal: On jiashen, the official system was restored.

entries.zh: 癸巳，改封吳王允熥廣澤王，衡王允熞懷恩王，徐王允𤐤敷惠王，隨母妃呂氏居懿文太子陵園。
entries.en: On guisi he demoted Prince Wu Zhu Yunhuang to Prince of Guangze, Prince Heng Zhu Yunxiao to Prince of Huai'en, and Prince Xu Zhu Yunxi to Prince of Fuhui, setting them with their mother Consort Lü at Crown Prince Yiwen's mausoleum.
entries.literal: On guisi, he changed the enfeoffment of Prince Wu Zhu Yunhuang to Prince of Guangze, Prince Heng Zhu Yunxiao to Prince of Huai'en, and Prince Xu Zhu Yunxi to Prince of Fuhui, to dwell with their mother, Consort Lü, at Crown Prince Yiwen's mausoleum park.

entries.zh: 癸卯，江陰侯吳高督河南、陝西兵備，撫安軍民。
entries.en: On guimao the Marquis of Jiangyin, Wu Gao, took charge of military readiness in Henan and Shaanxi and steadied troops and civilians.
entries.literal: On guimao, the Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao supervised military readiness in Henan and Shaanxi and pacified soldiers and civilians.

entries.zh: 甲辰，尚書嚴震直、王鈍，府尹薛正言等巡視山西、山東、河南、陝西。
entries.en: On jiachen Ministers Yan Zhenzhi and Wang Dun, metropolitan magistrate Xue Zhengyan, and others toured Shanxi, Shandong, Henan, and Shaanxi.
entries.literal: On jiachen, Ministers Yan Zhenzhi and Wang Dun, prefectural magistrate Xue Zhengyan, and others inspected Shanxi, Shandong, Henan, and Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 八月壬子，侍讀解缙、編修黄淮入直文淵閣。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on renzi, Reader-in-Waiting Xie Jin and Compiler Huang Huai took up duty in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the renzi day, Reader-in-Waiting Xie Jin and Compiler Huang Huai entered attendance at the Wenyuan Pavilion.

entries.zh: 尋命侍讀胡廣，修撰楊榮，編修楊士奇，檢討金幼孜、胡儼同入直，並預機務。
entries.en: Soon he also summoned Hu Guang, Yang Rong, Yang Shiqi, Jin Youzi, and Hu Yan to the same inner service, each to share in the highest counsel.
entries.literal: Soon he ordered Reader-in-Waiting Hu Guang, Compiler Yang Rong, Compiler Yang Shiqi, Reviser Jin Youzi, and Hu Yan likewise to enter attendance, all participating in confidential affairs of state.

entries.zh: 執兵部尚書铁铉至，不屈，殺之。
entries.en: Tie Xuan, minister of war, was brought in chains. He would not bow. He was executed.
entries.literal: Tie Xuan, Minister of War, was brought in under arrest; he would not submit; he was killed.

entries.zh: 左軍都督劉真鎮遼東。
entries.en: Liu Zhen, left commander-in-chief, was posted to guard Liaodong.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen, Left Commander-in-Chief of the Army, was stationed in Liaodong.

entries.zh: 丁巳，分遣御史察天下利弊。
entries.en: On dingsi he sent censors abroad to survey what helped or hurt the realm.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day, censors were dispatched in separate missions to inspect the benefits and harms throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 戊午，都督何福為征虏將軍，鎮宁夏，節制陕西行都司。
entries.en: On wuwu Commander He Fu was named General Who Subdues the Barbarians, garrisoned at Ningxia, and given charge of the Shaanxi regional command.
entries.literal: On the wuwu day, Commander He Fu was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and stationed in Ningxia, with control over the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission.

entries.zh: 都督同知韩观练兵江西，節制广東、福建。
entries.en: Assistant Commander Han Guan drilled troops in Jiangxi and held authority over Guangdong and Fujian.
entries.literal: Assistant Commander Han Guan trained troops in Jiangxi and had control over Guangdong and Fujian.

entries.zh: 甲子，西平侯沐晟鎮云南。
entries.en: On jiazi the Marquis of Xiping, Mu Sheng, took up his post in Yunnan.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, the Marquis of Xiping Mu Sheng was stationed in Yunnan.

entries.zh: 九月甲申，論靖難功，封丘福淇國公，朱能成國公，張武等侯者十三人，徐祥等伯者十一人。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on jiashen, service in the Pacification was rewarded: Qiu Fu became Duke of Qi, Zhu Neng Duke of Cheng; thirteen men including Zhang Wu were made marquises and eleven including Xu Xiang were made earls.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the jiashen day, rewards for pacifying the difficulty were assessed; Qiu Fu was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, Zhu Neng as Duke of Cheng, Zhang Wu and others as marquises—thirteen men—and Xu Xiang and others as earls—eleven men.

entries.zh: 論欸附功，封驸馬都尉王宁為侯，茹瑺、陳瑄及都督同知王佐皆為伯。
entries.en: Those who had come over in time were also honored: the emperor’s son-in-law Wang Ning was made a marquis; Ru Yao, Chen Xuan, and Assistant Commander Wang Zuo were each made an earl.
entries.literal: Rewards for timely submission were assessed; the Emperor’s Son-in-Law Wang Ning was enfeoffed as marquis; Ru Yao, Chen Xuan, and Assistant Commander Wang Zuo were all made earls.

entries.zh: 甲午，定功臣死罪减禄例。
entries.en: On jiawu he fixed the rule that a meritorious minister condemned to death might instead suffer a cut in stipend.
entries.literal: On the jiawu day, the precedent was fixed whereby meritorious officials guilty of capital crimes might have their stipends reduced instead.

entries.zh: 乙未，徙山西民無田者實北平，賜之钞，复五年，韩观為征南將軍，鎮广西。
entries.en: On yiwei landless families from Shanxi were resettled in Beiping, paid in paper notes, and granted five years’ tax relief. Han Guan was named General Who Campaigns South and posted to Guangxi.
entries.literal: On the yiwei day, commoners of Shanxi without land were moved to settle in Beiping; they were given paper money; taxes were remitted for five years; Han Guan was made General Who Campaigns South and stationed in Guangxi.

entries.zh: 成祖啟天弘道高明肇運聖武神功純仁至孝文皇帝諱棣，太祖第四子也。
entries.en: Chengzu, the Emperor Wen, whose posthumous titles ran through Opener of Heaven, Broadener of the Way, Lofty and Bright, Founder of the Fortune, Sacred in Martial Valor and Divine in Achievement, Pure in Benevolence and Supreme in Filial Piety, bore the personal name Di and was the fourth son of the dynastic founder.
entries.literal: Chengzu, Emperor Wen, styled Opener of Heaven, Broadener of the Way, Lofty and Bright, Founder of the Fortune, Sacred in Martial Valor and Divine in Achievement, Pure in Benevolence and Supreme in Filial Piety — taboo name Di — was the fourth son of Taizu.

entries.zh: 母孝慈高皇后。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Ma, posthumously honored as the Xiaoci Gao Empress.
entries.literal: His mother was the Empress Xiaoci Gao.

entries.zh: 洪武三年，封燕王。
entries.en: In Hongwu year 3 he received the title Prince of Yan.
entries.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.

entries.zh: 十三年，之籓北平。
entries.en: In year 13 he took up residence in his apanage at Beiping.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he went to his fief at Beiping.

entries.zh: 王貌奇偉，美髭髯。
entries.en: The Prince was striking in stature, with a fine beard and mustache.
entries.literal: The Prince's appearance was singularly imposing; his beard and mustache were handsome.

entries.zh: 智勇有大略，能推誠任人。
entries.en: He combined wisdom and courage with far-reaching design, and won service by treating men with open sincerity.
entries.literal: Wise and brave, possessed of great strategic vision, he could employ men by extending sincere trust.

entries.zh: 二十三年，同晉王討乃兒不花。
entries.en: In year 23 he joined the Prince of Jin in a campaign against Nir Buqa.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, together with the Prince of Jin he campaigned against Nir Buqa.

entries.zh: 晉王怯不敢進，王倍道趨迤都山，獲其全部而還，太祖大喜。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin hung back in fear, but the Prince of Yan forced the march to Yidu, captured the whole enemy host, and returned in triumph. Taizu was delighted.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin was timid and dared not advance; the Prince doubled his march to Yidu, took the entire enemy force, and returned. Taizu was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 是後屢帥諸將出征，並令王節制沿邊士馬，王威名大振。
entries.en: After that he often led the generals in the field and was given authority over frontier soldiers and horses; his name resounded along the border.
entries.literal: Thereafter he repeatedly led the generals on campaign and was also ordered to command the border troops and horses along the frontier. The Prince's renown greatly increased.

entries.zh: 三十一年閏五月，太祖崩，皇太孫即位，遺詔諸王臨國中，毋得至京師。
entries.en: In intercalary fifth month of year 31 Taizu died and the imperial grandson took the throne. The dying edict kept the princes in their domains and barred them from the capital.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year, intercalary fifth month, Taizu died; the imperial grandson ascended the throne. The testamentary edict ordered the princes to remain governing their domains and not come to the capital.

entries.zh: 王自北平入奔喪，聞詔乃止。
entries.en: The Prince left Beiping to mourn but turned back when he heard the edict.
entries.literal: The Prince set out from Beiping to rush to the funeral but, on hearing the edict, halted.

entries.zh: 時諸王以尊屬擁重兵，多不法。
entries.en: The senior princes, each commanding a great army, had grown lawless.
entries.literal: At the time the princes, as senior kin holding heavy armies, frequently acted unlawfully.

entries.zh: 帝納齊泰、黃子澄謀，欲因事以次削除之。
entries.en: The emperor took Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng's counsel and planned to pick them off one by one when occasion offered.
entries.literal: The emperor adopted the counsel of Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng and wished to use occasion to remove them one by one.

entries.zh: 憚燕王強，未發，乃先廢周王橚，欲以牽引燕。
entries.en: Dreading the Prince of Yan's strength, he held back and first deposed Prince Zhou Zhu Su, hoping to bait the Prince of Yan into the open.
entries.literal: Fearing the Prince of Yan's strength, he did not act at once; he first deposed Prince Zhou Zhu Su, intending to draw out the Prince of Yan.

entries.zh: 於是告訐四起，湘、代、齊、岷皆以罪廢。
entries.en: Accusations then flew from every quarter; the princes of Xiang, Dai, Qi, and Min were all stripped of rank on criminal charges.
entries.literal: Then accusations arose on every side; the princes of Xiang, Dai, Qi, and Min were all deposed on charges of crime.

entries.zh: 王內自危，佯狂稱疾。
entries.en: The Prince felt himself marked and played the madman, pleading sickness.
entries.literal: The Prince inwardly felt endangered and feigned madness, claiming illness.

entries.zh: 泰、子澄密勸帝除王，帝未決。
entries.en: Tai and Zicheng secretly pressed the emperor to destroy the Prince, but he could not bring himself to act.
entries.literal: Tai and Zicheng secretly urged the emperor to eliminate the Prince, but the emperor had not decided.

entries.zh: 建文元年夏六月，燕山百戶倪諒告變，逮官校於諒、周鐸等伏誅。
entries.en: In the sixth month of summer in Jianwen year 1, Ni Liang, a Yan Mountain centurion, denounced a plot; palace aides were seized, and Yu Liang, Zhou Duo, and others were put to death.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the first year of Jianwen, Ni Liang, a centurion of Yan Mountain, reported a plot; official aides were arrested; Yu Liang, Zhou Duo, and others were executed.

entries.zh: 下詔讓王，幷遣中官逮王府僚，王遂稱疾篤。
entries.en: An edict rebuked the Prince and palace eunuchs were sent to seize his household staff; he then claimed to be deathly ill.
entries.literal: An edict reproaching the Prince was issued, and palace eunuchs were also sent to arrest the Prince's staff; the Prince then claimed grave illness.

entries.zh: 都指揮使謝貴、布政使張昺以兵守王宮。
entries.en: Regional Commander Xie Gui and Administration Commissioner Zhang Bing ringed the palace with troops.
entries.literal: Regional Commander Xie Gui and Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Bing held the prince's palace with troops.

entries.zh: 王密與僧道衍謀，令指揮張玉、朱能潛納勇士八百人入府守衞。
entries.en: The Prince plotted in secret with the monk Daoyan and had Zhang Yu and Zhu Neng slip eight hundred picked warriors into the palace to guard it.
entries.literal: The Prince secretly plotted with the monk Daoyan and ordered commanders Zhang Yu and Zhu Neng to smuggle eight hundred stalwart men into the palace to defend it.

entries.zh: 二十二年七月，成祖崩於榆木川。
entries.en: In the seventh month of Yongle 22 Chengzu died at Yumu River.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of year twenty-two Chengzu died at Yumu River.

entries.zh: 八月甲辰，遺詔至，遣皇太孫迎喪開平。
entries.en: In the eighth month on jiachen the death testament reached the capital and the imperial great-grandson was sent to meet the bier at Kaiping.
entries.literal: In the eighth month on jiachen the final edict arrived; the imperial great-grandson was dispatched to receive the coffin at Kaiping.

entries.zh: 丁未，出夏原吉等於獄。
entries.en: On dingwei Xia Yuanji and the others were freed from custody.
entries.literal: On dingwei Xia Yuanji and others were released from prison.

entries.zh: 丁巳，即皇帝位。
entries.en: On dingsi he ascended the throne.
entries.literal: On dingsi he assumed the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 大赦天下，以明年為洪熙元年。
entries.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the coming year was declared the first year of the Hongxi reign.
entries.literal: Great pardon under Heaven; the coming year was made the first year of Hongxi.

entries.zh: 罷西洋寶船、迤西市馬及雲南、交阯採辦。
entries.en: The western treasure voyages, the Yili horse fairs, and the procurement offices in Yunnan and Jiaozhi were abolished.
entries.literal: Western treasure fleets, Yili horse markets, and procurement in Yunnan and Jiaozhi were abolished.

entries.zh: 戊午，復夏原吉、吳中官。
entries.en: On wuwu Xia Yuanji and Wu Zhong were reinstated.
entries.literal: On wuwu Xia Yuanji and Wu Zhong were restored to office.

entries.zh: 己未，武安侯鄭亨鎮大同，保定侯孟瑛鎮交阯，襄城伯李隆鎮山海，武進伯朱榮鎮遼東。
entries.en: On jiwei Wu'an Marquis Zheng Heng took command at Datong, Baoding Marquis Meng Ying at Jiaozhi, Xiangcheng Earl Li Long at Shanhaiguan, and Wujin Baron Zhu Rong in Liaodong.
entries.literal: On jiwei Zheng Heng Marquis of Wu'an garrisoned Datong, Meng Ying Marquis of Baoding Jiaozhi, Li Long Earl of Xiangcheng the Shanhai pass, Zhu Rong Baron of Wujin Liaodong.

entries.zh: 復設三公、三孤官，以公、侯、伯、尚書兼之。
entries.en: The grand titles of the Three Dukes and Three Preceptors were revived, to be filled by nobles and ministers in joint appointment.
entries.literal: The offices of Three Dukes and Three Preceptors were restored, held concurrently by dukes, marquises, earls, and ministers.

entries.zh: 進楊榮太常寺卿，金幼孜戶部侍郎，兼大學士如故，楊士奇為禮部左侍郎兼華蓋殿大學士，黃淮通政使兼武英殿大學士，俱掌內制，楊溥為翰林學士。
entries.en: Yang Rong was made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, Jin Youzi Vice Minister of Revenue, both retaining their grand secretary posts; Yang Shiqi became Left Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of Huagai Hall; Huang Huai Commissioner of the Transmission Office and Grand Secretary of Wuying Hall, all drafting imperial orders; Yang Pu was appointed Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: Yang Rong promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Jin Youzi Vice Minister of Revenue, all Grand Secretaries as before; Yang Shiqi Minister of Rites left and Grand Secretary of Huagai Hall; Huang Huai Commissioner of the Transmission Office and Grand Secretary of Wuying Hall—all handling inner drafts; Yang Pu made Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 辛酉，鎮遠侯顧興祖充總兵官，討廣西叛蠻。
entries.en: On xinyou Zhenyuan Marquis Gu Xingzu was appointed supreme commander to quell rebellious Man in Guangxi.
entries.literal: On xinyou Gu Xingzu Marquis of Zhenyuan was made supreme commander to suppress rebel tribes in Guangxi.

entries.zh: 甲子，汰冗官。
entries.en: On jiazi redundant offices were cut.
entries.literal: On jiazi superfluous officials were culled.

entries.zh: 乙丑，召漢王高煦赴京。
entries.en: On yichou the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, was ordered to come to court.
entries.literal: On yichou the Prince of Han Gao Xu was summoned to the capital.

entries.zh: 戊辰，官吏謫隸軍籍者放還鄉。
entries.en: On wuchen officials who had been demoted to soldier rolls were allowed to return to their villages.
entries.literal: On wuchen officials banished to military registers were sent home.

entries.zh: 己巳，詔文臣年七十致仕。
entries.en: On jisi an edict required civil officials to retire at seventy.
entries.literal: On jisi an edict fixed retirement at seventy for civil officials.

entries.zh: 九月癸酉，交阯都指揮方政與黎利戰於茶籠州，敗績，指揮同知伍雲力戰死。
entries.en: In the ninth month on guiyou Fang Zheng, regional commander in Jiaozhi, met Li Lei at Chalong and was beaten; Assistant Commander Wu Yun died in fierce combat.
entries.literal: In the ninth month on guiyou Fang Zheng regional commander of Jiaozhi fought Li Lei at Chalong Prefecture and was defeated; Assistant Commander Wu Yun died fighting stubbornly.

entries.zh: 丙子，召尚書黃福於交阯。
entries.en: On bingzi Minister Huang Fu was recalled from Annam.
entries.literal: On bingzi Minister Huang Fu was recalled from Jiaozhi.

entries.zh: 庚辰，河溢開封，免稅糧，遣右都御史王彰撫恤之。
entries.en: On gengchen floods from the Yellow River inundated Kaifeng; taxes in grain were waived and Right Censor-in-chief Wang Zhang was dispatched to relieve the district.
entries.literal: On gengchen the Yellow River burst its banks at Kaifeng; grain taxes were remitted and Censor-in-chief Wang Zhang was sent to comfort the people.

entries.zh: 壬午，敕自今官司所用物料於所產地計直市之，科派病民者罪不宥。
entries.en: On renwu an edict required all government supplies to be bought at market rates in the localities where they were produced; officials who still levied burdens on the people would not be spared.
entries.literal: On renwu an edict: from now materials used by government offices shall be purchased at fair value where produced—those who injure the people by corvée levies shall not be pardoned.

entries.zh: 癸未，禮部尚書呂震請除服，不許。
entries.en: On guwei Minister of Rites Lü Zhen asked permission to leave off mourning garb; the request was denied.
entries.literal: On guwei Minister of Rites Lü Zhen petitioned to end mourning dress; not permitted.

entries.zh: 乙酉，增諸王歲祿。
entries.en: On yiyou the yearly allotments of the imperial princes were raised.
entries.literal: On yiyou the annual stipends of princes were increased.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以風憲官備外任，命給事中蕭奇等三十五人為州縣官。
entries.en: On bingxu, to fill outer posts with men of integrity, thirty-five supervising secretaries led by Xiao Qi were made prefectural and county officials.
entries.literal: On bingxu, because surveillance officials were needed in outside posts, thirty-five supervising secretaries including Xiao Qi were appointed district magistrates.

entries.zh: 丁亥，黎利寇清化，指揮同知陳忠戰死。
entries.en: On dinghai Li Lei attacked Thanh Hoa and Assistant Commander Chen Zhong fell fighting.
entries.literal: On dinghai Li Lei raided Thanh Hoa; Assistant Commander Chen Zhong died in battle.

entries.zh: 戊子，始設南京守備，以襄城伯李隆為之。
entries.en: On wuzi the Nanjing defense command was established for the first time under Xiangcheng Earl Li Long.
entries.literal: On wuzi the Nanjing garrison command was first established, with Li Long Earl of Xiangcheng as commander.

entries.zh: 乙未，散畿內民所養官馬於諸衛所。
entries.en: On yiwei government horses kept by civilians in the metropolitan districts were turned over to the guards.
entries.literal: On yiwei commoners' official horses within the capital region were distributed among guard units.

entries.zh: 戊戌，賜吏部尚書蹇義及楊士奇、楊榮、金幼孜銀章各一，曰「繩愆糾繆」，諭以協心贊務，凡有闕失當言者，用印密封以聞。
entries.en: On wuxu Personnel Minister Jian Yi plus Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, and Jin Youzi received silver seals inscribed "Correct errors and amend faults," with orders to work as one and seal confidential memorials whenever they found fault.
entries.literal: On wuxu Minister of Personnel Jian Yi and Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, Jin Youzi were each given a silver seal reading "Correct errors and rectify mistakes," told to assist in concert and to report shortcomings sealed under the seal.

entries.zh: 贊曰：「當靖難師起，仁宗以世子居守，全城濟師。
entries.en: The eulogy says, "When the armies of the pacification rose, Renzong as heir apparent held the city, kept it whole, and fed the host.
entries.literal: The eulogy says: "When the troops of the pacification of troubles rose, Renzong as heir apparent held the city, preserved it whole, and succored the army.

entries.zh: 其後成祖乘輿，歲出北征，東宮監國，朝無廢事。
entries.en: Afterward, when Chengzu took the field and campaigned north year after year, the Eastern Palace governed the realm and the court knew no neglect.
entries.literal: Afterward, when Chengzu took the field and campaigned north year upon year, the Eastern Palace governed the realm and the court knew no neglect.

entries.zh: 然中遘媒孽，瀕於危疑者屢矣，而終以誠敬獲全。
entries.en: Yet he met slanderers again and again and often stood on the brink of ruin—yet in the end sincerity and reverence preserved him.
entries.literal: Yet he met slanderers time and again and often stood on the brink of peril—yet in the end sincerity and reverence preserved him.

entries.zh: 善乎其告人曰「吾知盡子職而已，不知有讒人也」，是可為萬世子臣之法矣。
entries.en: How apt his words to others: 'I know only to fulfill a son's duty; I do not know that there are slanderers'—a model for sons and ministers through ten thousand ages.
entries.literal: How apt his saying to others: 'I know only to fulfill a son's duty; I do not know that there are slanderers'—this may serve as the model for sons and ministers through ten thousand ages.

entries.zh: 在位一載。
entries.en: He reigned one year.
entries.literal: He reigned one year.

entries.zh: 用人行政，善不勝書。
entries.en: In appointing men and ordering the state, his good deeds could not all be recorded.
entries.literal: In appointing men and ordering the state, his good deeds could not all be recorded.

entries.zh: 使天假之年，涵濡休養，德化之盛，豈不與文、景比隆哉。」
entries.en: Had Heaven granted him more years to nurture and restore the people, would not the fullness of his moral sway have rivaled the glory of the Wen and Jing reigns?"
entries.literal: Had Heaven granted him more years to nurture and restore the people, would not the fullness of his moral sway have rivaled the glory of the Wen and Jing reigns?"

entries.zh: 仁宗敬天體道純誠至德弘文欽武章聖達孝昭皇帝，諱高熾，成祖長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Renzong—honored after death as one who revered Heaven, embodied the Way, and united pure sincerity, supreme virtue, literary cultivation, martial achievement, sagely wisdom, and filial devotion—was named Gaochi and was the eldest son of the Chengzu Emperor.
entries.literal: The Renzong Emperor, revering Heaven and embodying the Way, pure and sincere in utmost virtue, cultured in literature and martial in achievement, sagely and filially accomplished, taboo name Gaochi, was Chengzu's eldest son.

entries.zh: 母仁孝文皇后，夢冠冕執圭者上謁。
entries.en: His mother, the Empress of Benevolent Filiality and Culture, dreamed of a figure in court robes and cap bearing a jade tablet who bowed before her.
entries.literal: His mother was the Empress of Benevolent Filiality and Culture; she dreamed of one in cap and regalia holding a jade tablet who came to pay homage.

entries.zh: 寤而生帝。
entries.en: When she awoke she gave birth to the future emperor.
entries.literal: On waking she bore the emperor.

entries.zh: 幼端重沉靜，言動有經。
entries.en: As a boy he was grave and composed, his words and actions always measured.
entries.literal: In youth he was dignified, weighty, and calm; speech and conduct had constant measure.

entries.zh: 稍長習射，發無不中。
entries.en: As he grew he trained in archery and never missed his mark.
entries.literal: When grown a little he practiced archery; every shot struck.

entries.zh: 好學問，從儒臣講論不輟。
entries.en: He delighted in scholarship and debated unceasingly with the scholar-officials.
entries.literal: He loved learning; with Confucian ministers he discussed without ceasing.

entries.zh: 夏四月庚戌，處州賊犯崇安，殺都指揮吳剛。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, on gengxu, Chuzhou bandits attacked Chong'an and killed Regional Commander Wu Gang.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengxu, Chuzhou bandits attacked Chong'an and killed Regional Commander Wu Gang.

entries.zh: 壬戌，湖廣、貴州苗賊大起，命王驥討之。
entries.en: On renxu Miao bandits rose on a great scale in Huguang and Guizhou, and Wang Ji was ordered to attack them.
entries.literal: On the day renxu, Miao bandits rose on a great scale in Huguang and Guizhou; Wang Ji was ordered to attack them.

entries.zh: 乙丑，遣御史十三人同中官督福建、浙江銀課。
entries.en: On yichou thirteen censors were sent with palace eunuchs to supervise the silver-mining levy in Fujian and Zhejiang.
entries.literal: On the day yichou, thirteen censors were dispatched together with palace eunuchs to supervise the silver-mining levy in Fujian and Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 五月丙戌，陳懋擊破沙縣賊。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on bingxu, Chen Mao defeated the bandits of Shaxian.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bingxu, Chen Mao defeated the bandits of Shaxian.

entries.zh: 壬辰，旱，太監金英同法司錄囚。
entries.en: On renchen drought struck; the eunuch Jin Ying joined the judiciary in reviewing prisoners.
entries.literal: On the day renchen, there was drought; the eunuch Jin Ying together with the judiciary reviewed prisoners.

entries.zh: 己亥，侍讀學士張益直文淵閣，預機務。
entries.en: On jihai Zhang Yi, reader-in-waiting, was assigned direct duty at the Wenyuan Pavilion to share in deliberation.
entries.literal: On the day jihai, Reader-in-waiting Zhang Yi was assigned direct duty at the Wenyuan Pavilion to deliberate on state affairs.

entries.zh: 庚子，巡按福建御史汪澄棄市，并殺前巡按御史柴文顯。
entries.en: On gengzi Fujian touring censor Wang Cheng was executed in the market, and the former touring censor Chai Wenxian was killed as well.
entries.literal: On the day gengzi, Fujian touring censor Wang Cheng was executed in the market, and the former touring censor Chai Wenxian was also killed.

entries.zh: 六月庚戌，靖州苗犯辰溪，都指揮高亮戰死。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on gengxu, Jingzhou Miao attacked Chenxi and Regional Commander Gao Liang fell in battle.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the day gengxu, Jingzhou Miao attacked Chenxi; Regional Commander Gao Liang died in battle.

entries.zh: 丙辰，南京謹身諸殿災。
entries.en: On bingchen several halls of the Jinshen complex in Nanjing burned.
entries.literal: On the day bingchen, several halls of the Jinshen complex in Nanjing burned.

entries.zh: 甲子，修省。
entries.en: On jiazi the court undertook self-reform and austerity.
entries.literal: On the day jiazi, the court undertook self-reform and austerity.

entries.zh: 詔河南、山西班軍番休者盡赴大同、宣府．乙丑，西寧侯宋瑛總督大同兵馬。
entries.en: An edict ordered Henan and Shanxi garrison troops on rotational leave to march to Datong and Xuanfu. On yichou Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, took command of military affairs at Datong.
entries.literal: An edict ordered rotational-leave garrison troops of Henan and Shanxi all to proceed to Datong and Xuanfu. On the day yichou, Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, supervised military affairs at Datong.

entries.zh: 己巳，赦天下。
entries.en: On jisi a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: On the day jisi, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 戊寅，平鄉伯陳懷，駙馬都尉井源，都督王貴、吳克勤，太監林壽，分練京軍於大同、宣府，備瓦剌。
entries.en: On wuyin Chen Huai, Earl of Pingxiang, Chief Commandant-escort Jing Yuan, Commissioners Wang Gui and Wu Keqin, and the eunuch Lin Shou were assigned in separate parties to drill capital troops at Datong and Xuanfu against the Oirats.
entries.literal: On the day wuyin, Chen Huai, Earl of Pingxiang, Chief Commandant-escort Jing Yuan, Commissioners Wang Gui and Wu Keqin, and the eunuch Lin Shou were assigned in separate parties to drill capital troops at Datong and Xuanfu in preparation against the Oirats.

entries.zh: 秋七月己丑，瓦剌也先寇大同，參將吳浩戰死，下詔親征。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, on jichou, Esen of the Oirats raided Datong; Vice Commissioner Wu Hao fell in battle, and the throne ordered a personal campaign.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jichou, Esen of the Oirats raided Datong; Vice Commissioner Wu Hao died in battle, and an edict ordered the Emperor's personal campaign.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書王直帥羣臣諫，不聽。
entries.en: Wang Zhi, minister of personnel, led the officials in remonstrance, but the emperor would not listen.
entries.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi led the officials in remonstrance; this was not heeded.

entries.zh: 癸巳，命郕王居守。
entries.en: On guisi the Prince of Cheng was ordered to remain and guard the capital.
entries.literal: On the day guisi, the Prince of Cheng was ordered to remain and guard the capital.

entries.zh: 是日，西寧侯宋瑛、武進伯朱冕與瓦剌戰於陽和，敗沒。
entries.en: That same day Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, and Zhu Mian, Earl of Wujin, fought the Oirats at Yanghe and were wiped out.
entries.literal: That day Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, and Zhu Mian, Earl of Wujin, fought the Oirats at Yanghe and were defeated and lost.

entries.zh: 甲午，發京師。
entries.en: On jiawu the army set out from the capital.
entries.literal: On the day jiawu, the army set out from the capital.

entries.zh: 乙未，次龍虎臺，軍中夜驚。
entries.en: On yiwei the host halted at Longhu Terrace, and the army panicked in the night.
entries.literal: On the day yiwei, it halted at Longhu Terrace; there was a night alarm in the army.

entries.zh: 丁酉，次居庸關。
entries.en: On dingyou the host halted at Juyong Pass.
entries.literal: On the day dingyou, it halted at Juyong Pass.

entries.zh: 辛丑，次宣府。
entries.en: On xinchou the host halted at Xuanfu.
entries.literal: On the day xinchou, it halted at Xuanfu.

entries.zh: 羣臣屢請駐蹕，不許。
entries.en: The officials repeatedly begged him to halt his march, but he would not consent.
entries.literal: The officials repeatedly asked that he halt his progress; this was not permitted.

entries.zh: 丙午，次陽和。
entries.en: On bingwu the host halted at Yanghe.
entries.literal: On the day bingwu, it halted at Yanghe.

entries.zh: 八月戊申，次大同。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on wushen, the Emperor encamped at Datong.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wushen, he halted at Datong.

entries.zh: 鎮守太監郭敬諫，議旋師。
entries.en: Defender-attendant eunuch Guo Jing remonstrated and urged a withdrawal.
entries.literal: Guo Jing, the defender-attendant eunuch, remonstrated and urged withdrawal.

entries.zh: 己酉，廣寧伯劉安為總兵官，鎮大同。
entries.en: On jiyou Liu An, Baron of Guangning, was made overall commander and posted to Datong.
entries.literal: On the day jiyou, Liu An, Baron of Guangning, was made commander-in-chief and stationed at Datong.

entries.zh: 庚戌，師還。
entries.en: On gengxu the army turned back.
entries.literal: On the day gengxu, the army returned.

entries.zh: 丁巳，次宣府。
entries.en: On dingsi he encamped at Xuanfu.
entries.literal: On the day dingsi, he halted at Xuanfu.

entries.zh: 庚申，瓦剌兵大至，恭順侯吳克忠、都督吳克勤戰沒，成國公朱勇、永順伯薛綬救之，至鷂兒嶺遇伏，全軍盡覆。
entries.en: On gengshen Oirat forces came in strength; Wu Kexiong, Marquis of Gongshun, and Regional Commander Wu Keqin fell in battle; Zhu Yong, Duke of Cheng, and Xue Sui, Earl of Yongshun, marched to relieve them but at Ya'er Ridge met an ambush and the entire host was wiped out.
entries.literal: On the day gengshen, Oirat troops arrived in force; Marquis of Gongshun Wu Kexiong and Regional Commander Wu Keqin fell in battle; Duke of Cheng Zhu Yong and Earl of Yongshun Xue Sui went to their rescue—at Ya'er Ridge they met an ambush and the whole army was destroyed.

entries.zh: 辛酉，次土木，被圍。
entries.en: On xinyou he halted at Tumu and was surrounded.
entries.literal: On the day xinyou, he halted at Tumu and was besieged.

entries.zh: 壬戌，師潰，死者數十萬。
entries.en: On renxu the army broke; deaths ran into the hundreds of thousands.
entries.literal: On the day renxu, the army collapsed; several hundred thousand died.

entries.zh: 英國公張輔，泰寧侯陳瀛，駙馬都尉井源，平鄉伯陳懷，襄城伯李珍，遂安伯陳塤，修武伯沈榮，都督梁成、王貴，尚書王佐、鄺埜，學士曹鼐、張益，侍郎丁鉉、王永和、[2]副都御史鄧棨等，皆死，帝北狩。
entries.en: Zhang Fu, Duke of Ying; Chen Ying, Marquis of Taining; Jing Yuan, Commander of Horse; Chen Huai, Baron of Pingxiang; Li Zhen, Baron of Xiangcheng; Chen Kun, Baron of Suian; Shen Rong, Baron of Xiuwu; Regional Commanders Liang Cheng and Wang Gui; Ministers Wang Zuo and Kuang Ye; Academicians Cao Nai and Zhang Yi; Vice Ministers Ding Xuan and Wang Yonghe; and Vice Censor-in-chief Deng Qi, among others—all fell; the Emperor was borne north.
entries.literal: Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, Marquis of Taining Chen Ying, Commander of Horse Jing Yuan, Baron of Pingxiang Chen Huai, Baron of Xiangcheng Li Zhen, Baron of Suian Chen Kun, Baron of Xiuwu Shen Rong, Regional Commanders Liang Cheng and Wang Gui, Ministers Wang Zuo and Kuang Ye, Academicians Cao Nai and Zhang Yi, Vice Ministers Ding Xuan and Wang Yonghe, [2] and Vice Censor-in-chief Deng Qi, among others—all perished; the Emperor went on a northern hunt.

entries.zh: 甲子，京師聞敗，羣臣聚哭於朝，侍講徐珵請南遷，兵部侍郎于謙不可。
entries.en: On jiazi word of defeat reached the capital; the court assembled in tears; Lecturer Xu Cheng urged removal to the south; Vice Minister Yu Qian forbade it.
entries.literal: On the day jiazi, the capital heard of defeat; officials gathered weeping at court; Lecturer Xu Cheng proposed relocating south; Vice Minister of War Yu Qian forbade it.

entries.zh: 乙丑，皇太后命郕王監國。
entries.en: On yichou the Empress Dowager ordered the Prince of Cheng to oversee the realm as regent.
entries.literal: On the day yichou, the Empress Dowager ordered the Prince of Cheng to act as regent.

entries.zh: 戊辰，帝至大同。
entries.en: On wuchen the captive Emperor reached Datong.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen, the Emperor reached Datong.

entries.zh: 己巳，皇太后命立皇子見深為皇太子。
entries.en: On jisi the Empress Dowager had Zhu Jianshen named crown prince.
entries.literal: On the day jisi, the Empress Dowager ordered the prince Jianshen established as Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 辛未，帝至威寧海子。
entries.en: On xinwei he came to Weining Lake.
entries.literal: On the day xinwei, the Emperor reached Weining Lake.

entries.zh: 甲戌，至黑河。
entries.en: On jiaxu he reached the Black River.
entries.literal: On the day jiaxu, he reached the Black River.

entries.zh: 九月癸未，郕王即位，遙尊帝為太上皇帝。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on guimao, the Prince of Cheng took the throne and from afar honored the captive as Retired Emperor.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the day guimao, the Prince of Cheng ascended the throne and honored the Emperor from afar as Retired Emperor.

entries.zh: 英宗法天立道仁明誠敬昭文憲武至德廣孝睿皇帝，諱祁鎮，宣宗長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Yingzong—honored after death as one who patterned himself on Heaven, established the Way, and united benevolence, brilliance, sincerity, reverence, literary glory, martial achievement, supreme virtue, broad filial devotion, and sagely wisdom—was named Zhu Qizhen and was the eldest son of Emperor Xuanzong.
entries.literal: The Yingzong Emperor, patterning Heaven and establishing the Way, benevolent, bright, sincere, reverent, illustrious in culture, manifest in martial virtue, of utmost virtue, broadly filial, and sagely, taboo name Qizhen, was the Xuanzong Emperor's eldest son.

entries.zh: 母貴妃孫氏。
entries.en: His mother was Noble Consort Sun.
entries.literal: His mother was Noble Consort Sun.

entries.zh: 生四月，立為皇太子，遂冊貴妃為皇后。
entries.en: When he was four months old he was named crown prince, and Noble Consort Sun was at once elevated to empress.
entries.literal: At four months he was established Crown Prince; the noble consort was then enfeoffed as Empress.

entries.zh: 贊曰：憲宗早正儲位，中更多故，而踐阼之後，上景帝尊號，卹于謙之冤，抑黎淳而召商輅，恢恢有人君之度矣。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Xianzong had been confirmed as heir early and weathered many trials before he took the throne; once enthroned he honored the Jingtai Emperor with a posthumous title, cleared Yu Qian's wrongful death, suppressed Li Chun and recalled Shang Lu—acts that showed the measure of a true ruler.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Xianzong secured the heirship early and passed through many trials before he took the throne; once enthroned he honored the Jingtai Emperor with a posthumous title, redressed the injustice done to Yu Qian, suppressed Li Chun and recalled Shang Lu—conduct that showed the breadth of a true ruler.

entries.zh: 時際休明，朝多耆彥，帝能篤於任人，謹於天戒，蠲賦省刑，閭里日益充足，仁、宣之治於斯復見。
entries.en: His age was bright and settled, and the court held many seasoned worthies; the Emperor was steadfast in appointing men, heedful of Heaven's warnings, and generous in remitting levies and easing punishments, so that villages grew ever more prosperous and the governance of Renzong and Xuanzong seemed to return.
entries.literal: His age was one of peace and brilliance, and the court held many seasoned worthies; the Emperor was steadfast in appointing men, heedful of Heaven's warnings, remitting levies and easing punishments, so that villages grew ever more prosperous and the governance of Renzong and Xuanzong appeared again.

entries.zh: 顧以任用汪直，西廠橫恣，盜竊威柄，稔惡弄兵。
entries.en: Yet because he employed Wang Zhi, the Western Depot ran rampant, stole imperial authority, and—grown wicked through long license—stirred up war at will.
entries.literal: Yet because he employed Wang Zhi, the Western Depot ran rampant, stole imperial authority, and, grown wicked through long license, toyed with war.

entries.zh: 夫明斷如帝而為所蔽惑，久而後覺，婦寺之禍固可畏哉。
entries.en: That so discerning a ruler could still be misled, and only awaken after long delay, shows how dreadful the harm of palace women and eunuchs can be.
entries.literal: That a ruler so discerning should yet be deluded by such men, and only awaken after long delay, shows how dreadful the harm of women and eunuchs can be.

entries.zh: 成化十二年
entries.en: The twelfth year of the Chenghua reign.
entries.literal: Chenghua year twelve.

entries.zh: 穆宗，契天隆道淵懿寬仁顯文光武純德弘孝莊皇帝，諱載垕，世宗第三子也。
entries.en: Emperor Muzong—honored after death as one who manifested Heaven, upheld the grand Way, and united profound graciousness, broad benevolence, brilliant culture, glorious martial accomplishment, pure virtue, expansive filial piety, and solemnity—was named Zhu Zaihou and was the third son of Emperor Shizong.
entries.literal: Muzong, the Emperor of Manifesting Heaven, Upholding the Grand Way, Profound and Gracious, Broad and Benevolent, Brilliant in Culture, Glorious in Martial Accomplishment, Pure in Virtue, Expansive in Filial Piety and Solemnity, taboo name Zaihou, was Shizong's third son.

entries.zh: 母杜康妃。
entries.en: His mother was Consort Du, of the Kang rank.
entries.literal: His mother was Consort Du of the Kang rank.

entries.zh: 嘉靖十八年二月封裕王，與莊敬太子、景恭王同日受冊。
entries.en: In the second month of Jiajing eighteen he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu, invested on the same day as Crown Prince Zhuangjing and Prince Jing Gong.
entries.literal: In Jiajing year eighteen, second month, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu, receiving investiture on the same day as Crown Prince Zhuangjing and Prince Jing Gong.

entries.zh: 已而莊敬薨，世宗以王長且賢，繼序已定，而中外危疑，屢有言者，乃令景王之國。
entries.en: When Crown Prince Zhuangjing died soon after, Shizong—holding that the Prince of Yu was eldest and worthy and the succession already settled, though court and realm remained uneasy and many spoke out—sent Prince Jing to his fief.
entries.literal: Thereafter Crown Prince Zhuangjing died; Shizong, because the prince was eldest and worthy and the succession was already settled, yet court and realm were uneasy and many spoke out, ordered Prince Jing to depart for his fief.

entries.zh: 四十五年十二月庚子，世宗崩。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of Jiajing forty-five, on gengzi, Shizong died.
entries.literal: Jiajing year forty-five, twelfth month, day gengzi: Shizong died.

entries.zh: 壬子，即皇帝位。
entries.en: On renzi he ascended the imperial throne.
entries.literal: Day renzi: he ascended the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 以明年為隆慶元年，大赦天下。
entries.en: The next year was declared Longqing one, and amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: The next year was declared Longqing year one, and amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 先朝政令不便者，皆以遺詔改之。
entries.en: Measures of the prior reign found inconvenient were all changed by testamentary edict.
entries.literal: Prior administration measures found inconvenient were all changed by testamentary edict.

entries.zh: 召用建言得罪諸臣，死者卹錄。
entries.en: Officials who had been punished for remonstrance were recalled to office, and the dead were granted posthumous honors and rehabilitation.
entries.literal: Officials who had been punished for remonstrance were recalled to office; the dead were granted posthumous honors and rehabilitation.

entries.zh: 方士悉付法司治罪，罷一切齋醮工作及例外採買。
entries.en: Daoist adepts were all handed over to the judicial offices for punishment, and all fasting-sacrifice projects and exceptional purchases were abolished.
entries.literal: Daoist adepts were all handed over to the judicial offices for punishment; all fasting-sacrifice projects and exceptional purchases were abolished.

entries.zh: 免明年天下田賦之半，及嘉靖四十三年以前逋賦。
entries.en: Half of the next year's land tax throughout the realm was remitted, along with arrears dating before Jiajing forty-three.
entries.literal: Half of next year's land tax throughout the realm was remitted, along with arrears before Jiajing forty-three.

entries.zh: 釋戶部主事海瑞於獄。
entries.en: Hai Rui, principal official of the Ministry of Revenue, was released from prison.
entries.literal: Hai Rui, principal official of the Ministry of Revenue, was released from prison.

entries.zh: 是年，土魯番入貢。
entries.en: That year Turfan sent a tribute mission.
entries.literal: That year, Turfan sent tribute.

entries.zh: 二年春正月己卯，給事中石星疏陳六事，杖闕下，斥為民。
entries.en: In spring of Longqing two, on jimao of the first month, Supervising Secretary Shi Xing memorialized on six matters, was beaten at court, and reduced to commoner status.
entries.literal: In year two, spring, first month, day jimao: Supervising Secretary Shi Xing memorialized on six matters, was beaten at court, and reduced to commoner status.

entries.zh: 二月丁酉，寇犯柴溝堡。
entries.en: In the second month, on dingyou, raiders attacked Chaigou Fort.
entries.literal: Second month, day dingyou: raiders violated Chaigou Fort.

entries.zh: 守備韓尚忠戰死。
entries.en: Garrison Commander Han Shangzhong was killed in battle.
entries.literal: Garrison Commander Han Shangzhong died in battle.

entries.zh: 己亥，耕耤田。
entries.en: On jihai the emperor plowed the sacred field.
entries.literal: Day jihai: the emperor plowed the sacred field.

entries.zh: 丁未，如天壽山，謁長陵、永陵。
entries.en: On dingwei he went to Tianshou Mountain and paid homage at Changling and Yongling.
entries.literal: Day dingwei: he went to Tianshou Mountain and paid homage at Changling and Yongling.

entries.zh: 庚戌，還宮，免所過田租有差。
