entries.en: On gengxu he returned to the palace and remitted field rent along the route in varying degrees.
entries.literal: Day gengxu: he returned to the palace and remitted field rent along the route in varying degrees.

entries.zh: 三月辛酉，立皇子翊鈞為皇太子，詔赦天下。
entries.en: In the third month, on xinyou, Prince Zhu Yijun was invested as crown prince and an edict proclaimed amnesty throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Third month, day xinyou: the prince Zhu Yijun was invested as crown prince; an edict proclaimed amnesty throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 乙丑，廣西總兵官俞大猷討廣東賊。
entries.en: On yichou Guangxi Regional Commander Yu Dayou campaigned against the Guangdong bandits.
entries.literal: Day yichou: Guangxi Regional Commander Yu Dayou campaigned against the Guangdong bandits.

entries.zh: 戊辰，賜羅萬化等進士及第、出身有差。
entries.en: On wuchen Luo Wanhua and others received jinshi ranks, palace degrees, and provincial degrees according to merit.
entries.literal: Day wuchen: Luo Wanhua and others were granted jinshi ranks, palace degrees, and provincial degrees according to merit.

entries.zh: 丙子，幸南海子。
entries.en: On bingzi the emperor visited the Southern Park.
entries.literal: Day bingzi: the emperor visited the Southern Park.

entries.zh: 戊寅，京師地震，命百官修省。
entries.en: On wuyin an earthquake shook the capital and officials were ordered to undertake self-examination.
entries.literal: Day wuyin: the capital was shaken by earthquake; officials were ordered to undertake self-examination.

entries.zh: 夏六月庚辰，遣使兩畿錄囚。
entries.en: In the sixth month of summer, on gengchen, envoys were dispatched to the two metropolitan regions to review prisoners.
entries.literal: Summer, sixth month, day gengchen: envoys were dispatched to the two metropolitan regions to review prisoners.

entries.zh: 己丑，廣東賊曾一本寇廣州，殺知縣劉師顏。
entries.en: On jichou the Guangdong bandit Zeng Yiben raided Guangzhou and killed Magistrate Liu Shiyan.
entries.literal: Day jichou: the Guangdong bandit Zeng Yiben raided Guangzhou and killed Magistrate Liu Shiyan.

entries.zh: 秋七月己酉，賊入廉州。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiyou, the bandits entered Lianzhou.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiyou: the bandits entered Lianzhou.

entries.zh: 丙寅，徐階致仕。
entries.en: On bingyin Xu Jie retired from office.
entries.literal: Day bingyin: Xu Jie retired.

entries.zh: 冬十月戊寅，免南畿被災秋糧，振淮、徐飢。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on wuyin, autumn grain tax was forgiven in the disaster-stricken Southern Metropolitan Region and relief was distributed in Huai and Xu for famine.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuyin: autumn grain in disaster-stricken Southern Metropolitan Region was remitted, and relief was distributed in Huai and Xu for famine.

entries.zh: 己亥，廢遼王憲㸅為庶人。
entries.en: On jihai Prince Liao Xianbi was degraded to commoner status.
entries.literal: Day jihai: Prince Liao Xianbi was degraded to commoner status.

entries.zh: 甲辰，免畿內、河南被災秋糧，十一月壬子，宣府總兵官馬芳襲俺答於長水海子，又敗之鞍子山。
entries.en: On jiachen autumn grain tax was forgiven within the metropolitan region and in Henan; in the eleventh month, on renzi, Xuanfu Regional Commander Ma Fang raided Anda at Changshui Lake and again defeated him at Anzi Mountain.
entries.literal: Day jiachen: autumn grain within the metropolitan region and in Henan was remitted; eleventh month, day renzi: Xuanfu Regional Commander Ma Fang raided Anda at Changshui Lake and again defeated him at Anzi Mountain.

entries.zh: 辛酉，免江西被災稅糧，戊辰，祀天於南郊。
entries.en: On xinyou tax grain was forgiven in disaster-stricken Jiangxi; on wuchen the court sacrificed to Heaven at the Southern Suburb.
entries.literal: Day xinyou: tax grain in disaster-stricken Jiangxi was remitted; day wuchen: Heaven was sacrificed to at the Southern Suburb.

entries.zh: 己巳，命廣東、福建督撫將領會剿曾一本。
entries.en: On jisi the governors-general and surveillance commissioners of Guangdong and Fujian and their generals were ordered to combine forces against Zeng Yiben.
entries.literal: Day jisi: the governors-general and surveillance commissioners of Guangdong and Fujian and their generals were ordered to combine forces against Zeng Yiben.

entries.zh: 十二月庚寅，世宗神主祔太廟。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on gengyin, Shizong's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, day gengyin: Shizong's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 丁酉，限勳戚莊田。
entries.en: On dingyou estates held by meritorious kin were limited.
entries.literal: Day dingyou: estates of meritorious kin were limited.

entries.zh: 是年，琉球入貢。
entries.en: That year Ryukyu sent a tribute mission.
entries.literal: That year, Ryukyu entered with tribute.

entries.zh: 隆慶元年春正月丙寅，罷睿宗明堂配享。
entries.en: In spring of Longqing one, on bingyin of the first month, the court abolished Ruizong's paired sacrifice at the Bright Hall.
entries.literal: In Longqing year one, spring, first month, day bingyin: paired sacrifice to Ruizong at the Bright Hall was abolished.

entries.zh: 戊辰，复鄭王厚烷爵。
entries.en: On wuchen Prince Zheng Houwan's title was restored.
entries.literal: Day wuchen: Prince Zheng Houwan's title was restored.

entries.zh: 丁丑，追尊母康妃為孝恪皇太后。
entries.en: On dingchou his mother, Consort Kang, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Xiaoke.
entries.literal: Day dingchou: his mother, Consort Kang, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Xiaoke.

entries.zh: 二月戊子，祭大社大稷。
entries.en: In the second month, on wuzi, the court sacrificed to the Great Earth and Great Grain.
entries.literal: Second month, day wuzi: the Great Earth and Great Grain were sacrificed to.

entries.zh: 乙未，冊妃陳氏為皇后。
entries.en: On yiwei Consort Chen was invested as empress.
entries.literal: Day yiwei: Consort Chen was invested as empress.

entries.zh: 吏部侍郎陳以勤為禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士，禮部侍郎張居正為吏部左侍郎兼東閣大學士，預機務。
entries.en: Chen Yiqin, vice minister of personnel, was made minister of rites and also grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion; Zhang Juzheng, vice minister of rites, was made left vice minister of personnel and also grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion; both entered state deliberations.
entries.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Chen Yiqin was made Minister of Rites and concurrent Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion; Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Juzheng was made Left Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion; both joined deliberation on state affairs.

entries.zh: 三月壬申，葬肅皇帝於永陵。
entries.en: In the third month, on renshen, the late Shizong was buried at Yongling.
entries.literal: Third month, day renshen: the Su Emperor was buried at Yongling.

entries.zh: 乙酉，土蠻犯遼陽，指揮王承德戰歿。
entries.en: On yiyou the Tumeng raided Liaoyang and Commandant Wang Chengde was killed in battle.
entries.literal: Day yiyou: the Tumeng raided Liaoyang; Commandant Wang Chengde died in battle.

entries.zh: 夏四月丙戌朔，享太廟。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the bingxu new moon, the court offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingxu new moon: the Imperial Ancestral Temple was offered sacrifice.

entries.zh: 丙午，禁屬國毋獻珍禽異獸。
entries.en: On bingwu vassal states were forbidden to present rare birds and exotic beasts.
entries.literal: Day bingwu: vassal states were forbidden to present rare birds and exotic beasts.

entries.zh: 丁未，御經筵。
entries.en: On dingwei the emperor attended the Classics Lecture.
entries.literal: Day dingwei: the emperor attended the Classics Lecture.

entries.zh: 五月己未，黃河決口工成。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on jiwei, work on the Yellow River breach was completed.
entries.literal: Fifth month, day jiwei: work on the Yellow River breach was completed.

entries.zh: 辛酉，祀地於北郊。
entries.en: On xinyou the court sacrificed to the earth at the Northern Suburb.
entries.literal: Day xinyou: the earth was sacrificed to at the Northern Suburb.

entries.zh: 丁丑，高拱罷。
entries.en: On dingchou Gao Gong was removed from office.
entries.literal: Day dingchou: Gao Gong was dismissed.

entries.zh: 六月戊戌，以霪雨修省，素服避殿，御皇極門視事。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on wuxu, amid prolonged rain the emperor undertook self-examination, wore plain dress, avoided the main hall, and conducted affairs from the Huangji Gate.
entries.literal: Sixth month, day wuxu: because of prolonged rain the emperor undertook self-examination, wore plain dress, avoided the main hall, and conducted affairs from the Huangji Gate.

entries.zh: 是月，新河復決。
entries.en: That month the new canal breached again.
entries.literal: That month, the new canal breached again.

entries.zh: 秋七月辛巳，招撫山東、河南被災流民，复五年。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, on xinsi, the court pacified and settled displaced persons in disaster-stricken Shandong and Henan and remitted their taxes for five years.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day xinsi: displaced persons in disaster-stricken Shandong and Henan were pacified and settled; taxes were remitted for five years.

entries.zh: 八月癸未朔，釋奠於先師孔子。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on the guiwei new moon, libation was offered to Confucius.
entries.literal: Eighth month, day guiwei new moon: libation was offered to Confucius.

entries.zh: 九月乙卯，俺答寇大同，詔嚴戰守。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on yimao, Anda raided Datong and the court ordered strict defense.
entries.literal: Ninth month, day yimao: Anda raided Datong; an edict ordered strict defense.

entries.zh: 癸亥，俺答陷石州，殺知州王亮採，掠交城、文水。
entries.en: On guihai Anda took Shizhou, killed Prefect Wang Liangcai, and plundered Jiaocheng and Wenshui.
entries.literal: Day guihai: Anda took Shizhou, killing Prefect Wang Liangcai and plundering Jiaocheng and Wenshui.

entries.zh: 壬申，土蠻犯薊鎮，掠昌黎、盧龍，至於灤河。
entries.en: On renshen the Tumeng raided Jizhou Garrison and plundered Changli and Lulong as far as the Luan River.
entries.literal: Day renshen: the Tumeng raided Jizhou Garrison, plundering Changli and Lulong as far as the Luan River.

entries.zh: 詔宣大總督侍郎王之誥還駐懷來，巡撫都御史曹亨駐兵通州。
entries.en: The court ordered Xuan-Da regional commander Wang Zhigao to return and encamp at Huailai, and surveillance commissioner Cao Heng to station troops at Tongzhou.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Xuan-Da Regional Commander Vice Minister Wang Zhigao to return and encamp at Huailai, and Surveillance Commissioner Cao Heng to encamp troops at Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 甲戌，郭朴致仕。
entries.en: On jiaxu Guo Pu retired from office.
entries.literal: Day jiaxu: Guo Pu retired.

entries.zh: 免襄陽、鄖陽被災秋糧。
entries.en: Autumn grain tax was forgiven in disaster-stricken Xiangyang and Yunyang.
entries.literal: Autumn grain in disaster-stricken Xiangyang and Yunyang was remitted.

entries.zh: 乙亥，總兵官李世忠援永平，與敵戰於撫寧，京師戒嚴。
entries.en: On yihai Regional Commander Li Shizhong reinforced Yongping and fought the enemy at Funing, and the capital was placed on alert.
entries.literal: Day yihai: Regional Commander Li Shizhong reinforced Yongping and fought the enemy at Funing; the capital was placed on alert.

entries.zh: 冬十月丙戌，寇退，京師解嚴。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on bingxu, the raiders withdrew and the capital's alert was lifted.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingxu: the raiders withdrew and the capital's alert was lifted.

entries.zh: 甲辰，諭群臣議邊防事宜。
entries.en: On jiachen the emperor instructed the ministers to deliberate on frontier defense.
entries.literal: Day jiachen: the ministers were instructed to deliberate on frontier defense.

entries.zh: 寧夏總兵官雷龍出塞邀擊河套部，敗之。
entries.en: Lei Long, regional commander of Ningxia, went beyond the border to intercept the Ordos tribes and defeated them.
entries.literal: Ningxia Regional Commander Lei Long went beyond the border to intercept the Ordos tribes and defeated them.

entries.zh: 十一月癸亥，祀天於南郊。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on guihai, the court sacrificed to Heaven at the Southern Suburb.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, day guihai: Heaven was sacrificed to at the Southern Suburb.

entries.zh: 是年，廣東賊大起。
entries.en: That year banditry erupted on a large scale in Guangdong.
entries.literal: That year, bandits rose on a large scale in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 琉球入貢。
entries.en: Ryukyu sent a tribute mission.
entries.literal: Ryukyu entered with tribute.

entries.zh: 嘉靖二年四月，始命興獻帝家廟亭祀，樂用八佾。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the second year of Jiajing, orders were first given for pavilion sacrifice at the family temple of the Offering Emperor Xing, with music using eight rows of dancers.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Jiajing, orders were first given for pavilion sacrifice at the family temple of the Offering Emperor Xing, with music using eight rows of dancers.

entries.zh: 初，禮官議廟制未決，監生何淵上書，請立世室於太廟東。
entries.en: At first, while ritual officials had not settled the temple system, the student He Yuan memorialized requesting establishment of an Eternal Chamber east of the Grand Temple.
entries.literal: At first, when ritual officials had not settled the temple system, the student He Yuan memorialized requesting establishment of an Eternal Chamber east of the Grand Temple.

entries.zh: 禮部尚書汪俊等皆謂不可。
entries.en: Minister of Rites Wang Jun and others all said it could not be done.
entries.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Jun and others all said it could not be done.

entries.zh: 帝諭奉先殿側別立一室，以盡孝思。
entries.en: The emperor instructed that a separate chamber be built beside the Hall of Ancestors to fulfill filial devotion.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed that a separate chamber be built beside the Hall of Ancestors to fulfill filial devotion.

entries.zh: 禮官集議言：「奉慈之建，禮臣據姜嫄特廟而言。
entries.en: The ritual officials assembled and deliberated, saying: “The building of the Hall of Maternal Kindness—ritual ministers spoke on the basis of Jiang Yuan’s special temple.
entries.literal: The ritual officials assembled and deliberated, saying: “The building of the Hall of Maternal Kindness—ritual ministers spoke on the basis of Jiang Yuan’s special temple.

entries.zh: 至爲本生父立廟大內，古所未有，惟漢哀爲定陶共王建廟京師，不可爲法。」
entries.en: As for building a temple within the inner palace for one’s birth father, there has never been such a thing in antiquity; only Han Aidi built a temple in the capital for Prince Gong of Dingtao—this cannot serve as a model.”
entries.literal: As for building a temple within the inner palace for one’s birth father, there has never been such a thing in antiquity; only Han Aidi built a temple in the capital for Prince Gong of Dingtao—this cannot serve as a model.”

entries.zh: 詹事石珤等亦言不可。
entries.en: The Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Shi Bao and others also said it could not be done.
entries.literal: The Grand Mentor Shi Bao and others also said it could not be done.

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: He did not listen.
entries.literal: He did not listen.

entries.zh: 葺奉慈殿後爲觀德殿以奉之。
entries.en: The rear of the Hall of Maternal Kindness was repaired as the Hall of Observing Virtue to receive his worship.
entries.literal: The rear of the Hall of Maternal Kindness was repaired as the Hall of Observing Virtue to receive his worship.

entries.zh: 四年四月，淵已授光祿寺署丞，覆上書請立世室，崇祀皇考於太廟，禮部尚書席書等議：「天子七廟，周文、武並有功德，故立文、武世室於三昭穆之上。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Yuan had already been appointed vice director of a bureau of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and again memorialized requesting establishment of an Eternal Chamber and exalted sacrifice to the imperial father in the Grand Temple; Minister of Rites Xi Shu and others deliberated: “The Son of Heaven has seven temples; Zhou Wen and Wu both had merit and virtue, and therefore established the Wen and Wu Eternal Chambers above the three zhao and three mu.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Yuan had already been appointed acting vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and again memorialized requesting establishment of an Eternal Chamber and exalted sacrifice to the imperial father in the Grand Temple; Minister of Rites Xi Shu and others deliberated: “The Son of Heaven has seven temples; Zhou Wen and Wu both had merit and virtue, and therefore established the Wen and Wu Eternal Chambers above the three zhao and three mu.

entries.zh: 獻皇帝追稱帝號，未爲天子。
entries.en: The Offering Emperor was posthumously given an imperial title but was never Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: The Offering Emperor was posthumously given an imperial title but was never Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 淵妄爲諛詞，乞寢其奏。」
entries.en: Yuan presumptuously made flattering words; we beg that his memorial be laid aside.”
entries.literal: Yuan presumptuously made flattering words; we beg that his memorial be laid aside.”

entries.zh: 帝令再議，書等言：「將置主於武宗上。
entries.en: The emperor ordered further deliberation; Shu and others said: “If the tablet is placed above Wuzong.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered further deliberation; Shu and others said: “If the tablet is placed above Wuzong.

entries.zh: 則武宗君也，分不可僭。
entries.en: Then Wuzong was sovereign, and the rank could not be usurped.
entries.literal: then Wuzong was sovereign, and the division cannot be usurped.

entries.zh: 置武宗下，則獻皇叔也，神終未安。」
entries.en: If placed below Wuzong, then the Offering Emperor was his uncle, and the spirit would never be at peace.”
entries.literal: If placed below Wuzong, then the Offering Emperor was his uncle, and the spirit would never be at peace.”

entries.zh: 時廷臣於稱考稱伯，異同相半，至議祔廟，無一人以爲可者。
entries.en: At that time among court ministers on calling him Father or calling him Uncle, opinions were evenly divided; but when it came to enshrinement in the temple, not one person thought it permissible.
entries.literal: At that time among court ministers on calling him Father or calling him Uncle, opinions were half and half; but when it came to enshrinement in the temple, not one person thought it permissible.

entries.zh: 學士張璁、桂萼亦皆以爲不可，書復密疏爭之。
entries.en: Academicians Zhang Cong and Gui E also all thought it could not be done; Shu again sent a secret memorial arguing against it.
entries.literal: Academicians Zhang Cong and Gui E also all thought it could not be done; Shu again sent a secret memorial arguing against it.

entries.zh: 帝不聽，復令會議。
entries.en: The emperor did not listen and again ordered joint deliberation.
entries.literal: The emperor did not listen and again ordered joint deliberation.

entries.zh: 乃準漢宣故事，於皇城內立一禰廟，如文華殿制。
entries.en: They then followed the story of Han Xuan, establishing a temple to the father within the imperial city, on the model of the Wenhua Hall.
entries.literal: They then followed the story of Han Xuan, establishing a temple to the father within the imperial city, on the model of the Wenhua Hall.

entries.zh: 籩豆樂舞，一用天子禮。
entries.en: Sacrificial vessels, music, and dance all used Son of Heaven rites.
entries.literal: Sacrificial vessels, music, and dance all used Son of Heaven rites.

entries.zh: 帝親定其名曰世廟。
entries.en: The emperor personally fixed its name as the Eternal Temple.
entries.literal: The emperor personally fixed its name as the Eternal Temple.

entries.zh: 五年七月，諭工部以觀德殿窄隘，欲別建於奉天殿左。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the fifth year he instructed the Ministry of Works that the Hall of Observing Virtue was cramped and he wished to build separately to the left of the Hall of Supreme Heaven.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year he instructed the Ministry of Works that the Hall of Observing Virtue was cramped and he wished to build separately to the left of the Hall of Supreme Heaven.

entries.zh: 尚書趙璜謂不可，不聽。
entries.en: Minister Zhao Huang said it could not be done; he did not listen.
entries.literal: Minister Zhao Huang said it could not be done; he did not listen.

entries.zh: 乃建於奉先之東，曰崇先殿。
entries.en: It was then built to the east of the Hall of Ancestors and called the Hall of Honoring the Ancestor.
entries.literal: It was then built to the east of the Hall of Ancestors and called the Hall of Honoring the Ancestor.

entries.zh: 十三年，命易承天家廟曰隆慶殿。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year orders were given to change the Chengtian family temple to the Longqing Hall.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year orders were given to change the Chengtian family temple to the Longqing Hall.

entries.zh: 十五年，以避渠道，遷世廟，更號曰獻皇帝廟，遂改舊世廟曰景神殿，寢殿曰永孝殿。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year, to avoid a canal, the Eternal Temple was moved and renamed the Temple of the Offering Emperor; the old Eternal Temple was then changed to the Jingshen Hall, and the sleeping hall to the Yongxiao Hall.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, to avoid a canal, the Eternal Temple was moved and renamed the Temple of the Offering Emperor; the old Eternal Temple was then changed to the Jingshen Hall, and the sleeping hall to the Yongxiao Hall.

entries.zh: 志第二十八 禮六
entries.en: Treatise 28: Rites 6
entries.literal: Treatise 28: Rites 6

entries.zh: 〈（吉禮六）〉
entries.en: (Auspicious Rites 6)
entries.literal: (Auspicious Rites 6)

entries.zh: 洪武元年，中書省臣會官議奏，王者遣將，所以討有罪，除民害也。
entries.en: In the first year of Hongwu, Secretariat officials convened colleagues to deliberate and memorialize: when a sovereign dispatches a general, it is to punish the guilty and remove harm from the people.
entries.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, members of the Secretariat convened officials to deliberate and memorialize: when a king dispatches a general, it is to punish the guilty and remove harm from the people.

entries.zh: 《書》稱大禹徂徵，《詩》美南仲薄伐。
entries.en: The Book of Documents speaks of Yu the Great setting out on campaign; the Book of Odes praises Nan Zhong's expedition.
entries.literal: The Documents speaks of Yu the Great setting out on campaign; the Odes praises Nan Zhong's expedition.

entries.zh: 《史記》引《兵書》曰：「古王者之遣將，跪而推轂。」
entries.en: The Records of the Grand Historian quotes the Art of War: "When ancient kings dispatched generals, they knelt and pushed the chariot wheel forward."
entries.literal: The Records of the Grand Historian quotes the Art of War: "When ancient kings dispatched generals, they knelt and pushed the chariot wheel."

entries.zh: 漢高命韓信爲將，設壇具禮。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu of Han appointed Han Xin as general and established an altar with full ceremony.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han appointed Han Xin as general and established an altar with full ceremony.

entries.zh: 北齊親授斧鉞。
entries.en: Under the Northern Qi, the emperor personally bestowed the battle-axe and ceremonial axe.
entries.literal: The Northern Qi personally bestowed the battle-axe and ceremonial axe.

entries.zh: 唐則告於廟社，又告太公廟。
entries.en: Under the Tang, announcement was made at the temples of the ancestral spirits and of the soil and grain, and also at the Temple of the Grand Duke.
entries.literal: The Tang announced at the temples of the ancestral spirits and the soil and grain, and also at the Temple of the Grand Duke.

entries.zh: 宋則授旌節於朝堂，次告廟社，又禡祭黃帝。
entries.en: Under the Song, banners and credentials were bestowed in the audience hall; next came announcement at the temples of the ancestral spirits and of the soil and grain, and a ma sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor.
entries.literal: The Song bestowed banners and credentials in the audience hall, then announced at the temples of the ancestral spirits and the soil and grain, and also performed the ma sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor.

entries.zh: 今定遣將禮，皇帝武弁服，御奉天殿。
entries.en: The rite for dispatching generals is now fixed as follows: the emperor wears military cap and dress and presides in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
entries.literal: Now the rite for dispatching generals is fixed: the emperor wears military cap and dress and presides in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

entries.zh: 大將軍入就丹墀，四拜，由西陛入殿，再拜跪。
entries.en: The grand general enters and takes position on the red steps, performs four bows, enters the hall by the western steps, and again bows and kneels.
entries.literal: The grand general enters and takes position on the red steps, performs four bows, enters the hall by the western steps, and again bows and kneels.

entries.zh: 承製官宣制，以節鉞授大將軍。
entries.en: The edict-recipient official announces the edict and bestows the credentials and battle-axe upon the grand general.
entries.literal: The edict-recipient official announces the edict and bestows the credentials and battle-axe upon the grand general.

entries.zh: 大將軍受之，以授執事者，俯伏，興，再拜出。
entries.en: The grand general receives them, passes them to the attendants, prostrates himself, rises, bows again, and withdraws.
entries.literal: The grand general receives them, passes them to the attendants, prostrates himself, rises, bows again, and withdraws.

entries.zh: 降陛，復位，四拜。
entries.en: He descends the steps, returns to his position, and performs four bows.
entries.literal: He descends the steps, returns to position, and performs four bows.

entries.zh: 駕還宮，大將軍出。
entries.en: The imperial procession returns to the palace; the grand general departs.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage returns to the palace; the grand general departs.

entries.zh: 至午門外勒所部將士，建旗幟，鳴金鼓，正行列，擎節鉞。
entries.en: Outside the Meridian Gate he musters the officers and soldiers under his command, raises banners and standards, sounds gongs and drums, aligns the ranks, and holds aloft the credentials and battle-axe.
entries.literal: At the Meridian Gate he musters the officers and soldiers under his command, raises banners and standards, sounds gongs and drums, aligns the ranks, and holds aloft the credentials and battle-axe.

entries.zh: 奏樂前導，百官以次送出。
entries.en: Music leads the procession, and officials see him off in order of rank.
entries.literal: Music is played to lead the way, and officials see him off in order.

entries.zh: 造廟宜社之禮，即命大將軍具牲幣，行一獻禮，與遣官祭告廟社儀同。
entries.en: For the rite of visiting the temples of the ancestral spirits and of the soil and grain, the grand general is immediately ordered to prepare sacrificial victims and silks and perform a single offering; the protocol matches that for officials dispatched to announce at those temples.
entries.literal: For the rite of visiting the temples of the ancestral spirits and the soil and grain, the grand general is immediately ordered to prepare sacrificial animals and silks and perform a single offering; the protocol is the same as when officials are dispatched to announce at the temples of the ancestral spirits and the soil and grain.

entries.zh: 其告武成王廟儀，前二日，大將省牲。
entries.en: For the protocol of announcing at the Temple of King Wu Cheng, two days beforehand the grand general inspects the sacrificial victims.
entries.literal: For the protocol of announcing at the Temple of King Wu Cheng, two days beforehand the grand general inspects the sacrificial victims.

entries.zh: 祭日，大將於幕次僉祝版，入就位，再拜。
entries.en: On the day of sacrifice, the grand general at the tent pavilion jointly signs the prayer text, enters and takes position, and performs two bows.
entries.literal: On the day of sacrifice, the grand general at the tent pavilion jointly signs the prayer text, enters and takes position, and performs two bows.

entries.zh: 詣神位前上香、奠帛、再拜。
entries.en: He proceeds before the spirit tablet, offers incense and lays silk, and bows twice.
entries.literal: He proceeds before the spirit tablet, offers incense and lays silk, and bows twice.

entries.zh: 進熟酌獻，讀祝，再拜。
entries.en: He presents the cooked offering and libation, reads the prayer, and bows twice.
entries.literal: He presents the cooked offering and libation, reads the prayer, and bows twice.

entries.zh: 詣位，再拜。
entries.en: He returns to his position and bows twice.
entries.literal: He proceeds to his position and bows twice.

entries.zh: 飲福受胙，復再拜。
entries.en: He drinks the blessing wine and receives the sacrificial meat, then bows twice again.
entries.literal: He drinks the blessing wine and receives the sacrificial meat, then bows twice again.

entries.zh: 徹豆，望燎。
entries.en: The dishes are removed, and they gaze upon the burning of the offerings.
entries.literal: The dishes are removed, and they gaze upon the burning.

entries.zh: 其配位，亦大將行禮。
entries.en: At the associated spirit tablets, the grand general likewise performs the rites.
entries.literal: At the associated spirit tablets, the grand general likewise performs the rites.

entries.zh: 兩廡陪祀，諸將分獻。
entries.en: In the two side halls for collateral sacrifice, the various generals make separate offerings.
entries.literal: In the two side halls for collateral sacrifice, the various generals make separate offerings.

entries.zh: 洪武四年七月，蜀夏明升降表至京師，太祖命中書集議受降禮。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Hongwu, Ming Sheng of Shu-Xia presented a surrender memorial at the capital; the founding emperor ordered the Secretariat to convene deliberation on the rite of receiving surrender.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Hongwu, Ming Sheng of Shu-Xia presented a surrender memorial at the capital; the founding emperor ordered the Secretariat to convene deliberation on the rite of receiving surrender.

entries.zh: 省部請如宋太祖受蜀主孟昶降故事，擬明升朝見日，皇帝御奉天門，升等於午門外跪進待罪表。
entries.en: The ministries requested following the precedent of Song Taizu receiving the surrender of the Shu ruler Meng Chang: on the day of Ming Sheng's audience, the emperor would preside at the Gate of Supreme Harmony, and Ming Sheng would kneel outside the Meridian Gate to present a memorial awaiting judgment.
entries.literal: The ministries requested following the precedent of Song Taizu receiving the surrender of Shu ruler Meng Chang: on the day Ming Sheng was to have audience, the emperor would preside at the Gate of Supreme Harmony, and Ming Sheng would kneel outside the Meridian Gate to present a memorial awaiting judgment.

entries.zh: 侍儀使捧表入，宣表官宣讀訖，承製官出傳制。
entries.en: The ceremonial attendant bore the memorial in; the edict-announcing official finished reading it; the edict-recipient official came forth to transmit the edict.
entries.literal: The ceremonial attendant bore the memorial in; the edict-announcing official finished reading it; the edict-recipient official came forth to transmit the edict.

entries.zh: 升等皆俯伏於地，侍儀舍人掖升起，其屬官皆起，跪聽宣制釋罪。
entries.en: Ming Sheng and his party all prostrated themselves on the ground; ceremonial ushers helped them rise; their subordinate officials all rose and knelt to hear the edict proclaiming absolution.
entries.literal: Ming Sheng and his party all prostrated themselves on the ground; ceremonial ushers helped them rise; their subordinate officials all rose and knelt to hear the edict proclaiming absolution.

entries.zh: 升等五拜，三呼萬歲。
entries.en: Ming Sheng and his party performed five bows and thrice shouted "Long live the emperor!"
entries.literal: Ming Sheng and his party performed five bows and thrice shouted "Long live the emperor!"

entries.zh: 承製官傳制，賜衣服冠帶。
entries.en: The edict-recipient official transmitted the edict bestowing robes, caps, and belts.
entries.literal: The edict-recipient official transmitted the edict bestowing robes, caps, and belts.

entries.zh: 侍儀舍人引升入丹墀中四拜。
entries.en: Ceremonial ushers led Ming Sheng up onto the red steps, where he performed four bows at the center.
entries.literal: Ceremonial ushers led Ming Sheng up onto the red steps, where he performed four bows in the center.

entries.zh: 侍儀使傳旨，升跪聽宣諭，俯伏四拜，三呼萬歲，又四拜出。
entries.en: The ceremonial attendant transmitted the imperial instruction; Ming Sheng knelt to hear the proclamation, prostrated himself and performed four bows, thrice shouted "Long live the emperor!", performed four more bows, and withdrew.
entries.literal: The ceremonial attendant transmitted the imperial instruction; Ming Sheng knelt to hear the proclamation, prostrated himself and performed four bows, thrice shouted "Long live the emperor!", performed four more bows, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 百官行賀禮。
entries.en: The officials performed the congratulatory rite.
entries.literal: The officials performed the congratulatory rite.

entries.zh: 帝以昶專治國政，所爲奢縱，升年幼，事由臣下，免其叩頭伏地上表請罪禮，惟命升及其官屬朝見，百官朝賀。
entries.en: The emperor held that Meng Chang had personally governed state affairs and acted with extravagance and license, while Ming Sheng was young and affairs were decided by his ministers; he exempted them from the rite of knocking the head and prostrating to present a memorial pleading guilt, ordering only that Ming Sheng and his officials attend audience while the officials offered congratulation.
entries.literal: The emperor held that Chang had personally governed state affairs and acted with extravagance and license, while Ming Sheng was young and matters were decided by his ministers; he exempted them from the rite of knocking the head and prostrating on the ground to present a memorial pleading guilt, ordering only that Ming Sheng and his officials attend audience while the officials offered congratulation.

entries.zh: 洪武三年六月，左副將軍李文忠北征大捷，遣官送所俘元孫買的裏八剌及寶冊至京師。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the third year of Hongwu, Left Deputy General Li Wenzhong won a great victory on the northern campaign and dispatched officials to bring to the capital the Yuan imperial grandson Maidibali and the precious registers among the captives.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Hongwu, the Left Deputy General Li Wenzhong won a great victory on the northern campaign and dispatched officials to send to the capital the Yuan imperial grandson Maidibali and the precious registers among the captives.

entries.zh: 百官請行獻俘禮。
entries.en: The officials requested performance of the captive-presentation rite.
entries.literal: The officials requested that the captive-presentation rite be performed.

entries.zh: 帝不許，事詳《本紀》。
entries.en: The emperor did not consent; details are given in the Basic Annals.
entries.literal: The emperor did not consent; details are in the Basic Annals.

entries.zh: 止令服本俗服，朝見畢，賜中國衣冠就謝。
entries.en: He ordered only that they wear their native dress; after audience they were granted Chinese robes, caps, and belts and then gave thanks.
entries.literal: He ordered only that they wear their native dress; after audience they were granted Chinese robes, caps, and belts and then gave thanks.

entries.zh: 復謂省臣曰：「故國之妃朝於君者，元有此禮，不必效之。」
entries.en: He further told the provincial officials: "When a consort of a fallen state has audience with the sovereign, the Yuan had such a rite, but there is no need to imitate it."
entries.literal: He further told the provincial officials: "When a consort of a fallen state has audience with the sovereign, the Yuan had such a rite, but there is no need to imitate it."

entries.zh: 亦令衣本俗服，入見中宮，賜中國服就謝。
entries.en: She too was ordered to wear her native dress, enter to see the empress, and after being granted Chinese dress, give thanks.
entries.literal: She too was ordered to wear her native dress, enter to see the empress, and after being granted Chinese dress, give thanks.

entries.zh: 十一月，大將軍徐達及文忠等師還，車駕出勞於江上。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, Grand General Xu Da, Wenzhong, and the others returned with their armies; the imperial carriage went out to welcome them on the river.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, Grand General Xu Da and Wenzhong and the others returned with their armies; the imperial carriage went out to welcome them on the river.

entries.zh: 明日，達率諸將上《平沙漠表》。
entries.en: The next day, Xu Da led the generals in presenting the Memorial on Pacifying the Desert Sands.
entries.literal: The next day, Xu Da led the generals in presenting the Memorial on Pacifying the Desert Sands.

entries.zh: 帝御奉天殿，皇太子親王侍，百官朝服陪列，達、文忠奉表賀。
entries.en: The emperor presided in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the crown prince and imperial princes attended; officials in court dress stood in attendance as Xu Da and Wenzhong presented the memorial of congratulation.
entries.literal: The emperor presided in the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the crown prince and imperial princes attended; officials in court dress stood in attendance; Xu Da and Wenzhong presented the memorial in congratulation.

entries.zh: 禮成，退自西階。
entries.en: When the rite was complete, they withdrew by the western steps.
entries.literal: When the rite was complete, they withdrew by the western steps.

entries.zh: 皇太子親王入賀。
entries.en: The crown prince and imperial princes entered to offer congratulations.
entries.literal: The crown prince and imperial princes entered to offer congratulations.

entries.zh: 後定，凡大捷，擇日以宣，其日不奏事，百官吉服賀，即日遣官薦告郊廟。
entries.en: It was later fixed that for every great victory a day would be chosen for announcement; on that day no memorials would be heard; officials in festive dress would offer congratulations; and officials would be dispatched the same day to offer thanks at the suburban altars and temples.
entries.literal: It was later fixed that for every great victory a day would be chosen for announcement; on that day no memorials would be heard; officials in festive dress would offer congratulations; and on the same day officials would be dispatched to offer thanks at the suburban altars and temples.

entries.zh: 中捷以下，止宣捷，不祭告慶賀。
entries.en: For moderate victories and below, only the victory was announced, without sacrificial thanksgiving or congratulatory rites.
entries.literal: For moderate victories and below, only the victory was announced, without sacrificial announcement or congratulation.

entries.zh: 洪武元年閏七月，詔定軍禮。
entries.en: In the intercalary seventh month of the first year of Hongwu, an edict established military ceremonial regulations.
entries.literal: In the intercalary seventh month of the first year of Hongwu, an edict fixed military rites.

entries.zh: 中書省臣會儒臣言：古者天子親征，所以順天應人，除殘去暴，以安天下。
entries.en: Members of the Secretariat convened Confucian scholars, who stated that in antiquity the Son of Heaven's personal campaign accorded with Heaven and responded to the people, eliminating the cruel and removing the violent to pacify all under Heaven.
entries.literal: Secretariat members convened Confucian scholars and stated: in antiquity, when the Son of Heaven personally campaigned, it was to accord with Heaven and respond to the people, eliminate the cruel and remove the violent, and thereby pacify all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 自黃帝習用干戈以徵不享，此其始也。
entries.en: From the time of the Yellow Emperor, arms were used to campaign against those who failed to offer tribute—this was where the practice began.
entries.literal: From the Yellow Emperor, arms were accustomed to be used to campaign against those who did not offer tribute—this was its beginning.

entries.zh: 周制，天子親征，則類於上帝，宜於大社，造於祖廟，禡於所徵之地，及祭所過山川。
entries.en: Under Zhou institutions, when the Son of Heaven personally campaigned, he offered categorical sacrifices to the Supreme Lord, presented suitable offerings at the Great Soil Altar, made announcements at the ancestral temple, performed ma sacrifices at the campaign destination, and sacrificed at mountains and rivers along the route.
entries.literal: Under Zhou institutions, when the Son of Heaven personally campaigned, he performed categorical offerings to the Supreme Lord, suitable offerings at the Great Soil Altar, announcements at the ancestral temple, ma sacrifices at the place to be campaigned against, and sacrifices at mountains and rivers passed along the way.

entries.zh: 師還，則奏凱獻俘於廟社。
entries.en: When the army returned, victory was reported and captives presented at the ancestral temple and soil-and-grain altar.
entries.literal: When the army returned, victory was reported and captives presented at the temple and altar.

entries.zh: 後魏有宣露布之制。
entries.en: The Later Wei had a regulation for proclaiming victory bulletins to the realm.
entries.literal: Later Wei had a regulation for proclaiming victory bulletins.

entries.zh: 唐仍舊典，宋亦間行焉。
entries.en: Tang retained the old canon, and Song likewise observed it on occasion.
entries.literal: Tang followed the old canon, and Song also carried it out from time to time.

entries.zh: 於是歷考舊章，定爲親征禮奏之。
entries.en: Thereupon, after examining the old regulations throughout, they codified the rites for the emperor's personal campaign and submitted a memorial.
entries.literal: Thereupon, having examined the old regulations throughout, they fixed them as the rites for personal campaign and memorialized them.

entries.zh: 前期，擇日祭告天地神祠行禡祭禮。
entries.en: In the preparatory period, a date was chosen for sacrificing and announcing to Heaven, Earth, and shrines of the spirits, and the ma-sacrifice rites were performed.
entries.literal: Beforehand, a day was chosen to sacrifice and announce to Heaven, Earth, and spirit shrines, conducting the ma-sacrifice rites.

entries.zh: 凡所過山川嶽鎮海瀽用太牢，其次少牢，又次特牲。
entries.en: For all mountains, rivers, peaks, guardian mountains, and seas along the route, a tai lao offering was used; if lesser, a shao lao; and if still lesser, a single victim.
entries.literal: For all mountains, rivers, peaks, guardian mountains, and seas passed, great offerings were used; next, lesser offerings; and below that, special victims.

entries.zh: 若行速，止用酒脯，祭器籩豆各一。
entries.en: If the march was hurried, only wine and dried meat were offered, with one basket-tray and one stem-cup as sacrificial vessels.
entries.literal: If marching swiftly, only wine and dried meat were used, with one of each sacrificial vessel, bian and dou.

entries.zh: 前期，齋一日。
entries.en: During the preparatory period, all observed a one-day fast.
entries.literal: Beforehand, fast for one day.

entries.zh: 皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，省牲視滌。
entries.en: The emperor wore the tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe, inspected the sacrificial victims, and supervised their cleansing.
entries.literal: The emperor wore the tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe, inspected the victims, and oversaw washing.

entries.zh: 祭之日，服武弁，行一獻禮。
entries.en: On the day of sacrifice, he wore the military cap and performed the single-presentation offering.
entries.literal: On the day of sacrifice, he wore the military cap and performed the one-presentation rite.

entries.zh: 凱旋，告祭宗社，禮與出師同。
entries.en: Upon triumphant return, he announced and sacrificed at the ancestral temple and soil-and-grain altar, with rites identical to those for dispatching an army.
entries.literal: Upon triumphant return, he announced and sacrificed at the ancestral temple and soil altar; the rites were the same as for dispatching an army.

entries.zh: 獻俘廟社，以露布詔天下，然後論功行賞。
entries.en: Captives were presented at the temple and altar, a victory bulletin was proclaimed to all under Heaven, and only then was merit assessed and rewards granted.
entries.literal: Captives were presented at the temple and altar; a victory bulletin was proclaimed to all under Heaven; then merit was assessed and rewards granted.

entries.zh: 永樂、宣德、正統間，率遵用之。
entries.en: From the Yongle through Xuande and Zhengtong reigns, these rites were generally followed.
entries.literal: Between the Yongle, Xuande, and Zhengtong reigns, they were generally followed and employed.

entries.zh: 太祖又以先王射禮久廢，弧矢之事專習於武夫，而文士多未解，乃詔國學及郡縣生員皆令習射，頒儀式於天下。
entries.en: The founding emperor further held that the archery rites of former kings had long been abandoned, bow and arrow skills were practiced only by military men while most literati did not understand them; he therefore ordered students of the National University and prefectural and county schools all to practice archery and promulgated the protocol throughout the realm.
entries.literal: The founding emperor further held that the archery rites of former kings had long been abandoned, bow and arrow skills were practiced only by military men while most literati did not understand them; he therefore ordered students of the National University and prefectural and county schools all to practice archery and promulgated the protocol throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 朔望則於公廨或閒地習之。
entries.en: On the first and fifteenth of each month they practiced at government offices or open ground.
entries.literal: On the first and fifteenth of the month they practiced at government offices or open ground.

entries.zh: 其官府學校射儀，略仿大射之式而殺其禮。
entries.en: The archery protocol for government offices and schools followed the grand archery form in outline but reduced the ceremony.
entries.literal: The archery protocol for government offices and schools followed the grand archery form in outline but reduced the ceremony.

entries.zh: 射位初三十步，自後累加至九十步。
entries.en: The shooting position began at thirty paces and was progressively increased to ninety paces.
entries.literal: The shooting position began at thirty paces and was progressively increased to ninety paces.

entries.zh: 射四矢，以二人爲耦。
entries.en: Four arrows were shot, with two persons forming a pair.
entries.literal: Four arrows were shot, with two persons forming a pair.

entries.zh: 其制洪武三年定。
entries.en: Its regulations were fixed in the third year of Hongwu.
entries.literal: Its regulations were fixed in the third year of Hongwu.

entries.zh: 凡郊廟祭祀，先期行大射禮，工部制射侯等器。
entries.en: For all suburban and temple sacrifices, the grand archery rite was performed in advance; the Ministry of Works made archery targets and other implements.
entries.literal: For all suburban and temple sacrifices, the grand archery rite was performed in advance; the Ministry of Works made archery targets and other implements.

entries.zh: 其射鵠有七。
entries.en: There are seven types of shooting target.
entries.literal: There are seven shooting targets.

entries.zh: 虎鵠五采，天子用之。
entries.en: The five-colored tiger target is used by the Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: The tiger target in five colors is used by the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 熊鵠五采，皇太子用之。
entries.en: The five-colored bear target is used by the crown prince.
entries.literal: The bear target in five colors is used by the crown prince.

entries.zh: 豹鵠五采，親王用之。
entries.en: The five-colored leopard target is used by imperial princes.
entries.literal: The leopard target in five colors is used by imperial princes.

entries.zh: 豹鵠四採，文武一品、二品者用之。
entries.en: The four-colored leopard target is used by civil and military officials of the first and second ranks.
entries.literal: The leopard target in four colors is used by civil and military officials of the first and second ranks.

entries.zh: 糝鵠三採，三品至五品用之。
entries.en: The three-colored grain-paste target is used by officials of the third through fifth ranks.
entries.literal: The grain-paste target in three colors is used by officials of the third through fifth ranks.

entries.zh: 狐鵠二採，六品至九品用之。
entries.en: The two-colored fox target is used by officials of the sixth through ninth ranks.
entries.literal: The fox target in two colors is used by officials of the sixth through ninth ranks.

entries.zh: 布鵠無採，文武官子弟及士民俊秀用之。
entries.en: The plain cloth target is used by sons of civil and military officials and talented commoners.
entries.literal: The cloth target without colors is used by sons of civil and military officials and talented commoners.

entries.zh: 凡射時，置乏於鵠右。
entries.en: Whenever shooting takes place, the screen is placed to the right of the target.
entries.literal: Whenever shooting takes place, the screen is placed to the right of the target.

entries.zh: 乏又名容，見《周禮·大司馬》服不氏，職執旗及待獲者以蔽身。
entries.en: The screen is also called the cover; it appears in the Zhou Rites under the Grand Marshal's Fu Bu Shi, whose duty is to hold the banner and shield the retriever from view.
entries.literal: The screen is also called the cover; it appears in the Zhou Rites, Grand Marshal, Fu Bu Shi, whose duty is to hold the banner and shield the retriever from view.

entries.zh: 設楅及韋，當射時置於前，以齊矢。
entries.en: The arrow-frame and leather mat are set out before shooting to align the arrows.
entries.literal: The arrow-frame and leather mat are set out before shooting to align the arrows.

entries.zh: 設射中五。
entries.en: Five types of hit-markers are set out.
entries.literal: Five types of hit-markers are set out.

entries.zh: 皮樹中，天子大射用之。
entries.en: The leather tree-marker is used in the Son of Heaven's grand archery.
entries.literal: The leather tree-marker is used in the Son of Heaven's grand archery.

entries.zh: 閭中，天子宴射用之。
entries.en: The lane-marker is used in the Son of Heaven's banquet archery.
entries.literal: The lane-marker is used in the Son of Heaven's banquet archery.

entries.zh: 虎中，皇太子親王射用之。
entries.en: The tiger marker is used in archery by the crown prince and imperial princes.
entries.literal: The tiger marker is used in archery by the crown prince and imperial princes.

entries.zh: 兕中，一品至五品文武官用之。
entries.en: The rhinoceros marker is used by civil and military officials of the first through fifth ranks.
entries.literal: The rhinoceros marker is used by civil and military officials of the first through fifth ranks.

entries.zh: 鹿中，六品至九品及文武官子弟士民俊秀通用之。
entries.en: The deer marker is used in common by officials of the sixth through ninth ranks, sons of officials, and talented commoners.
entries.literal: The deer marker is used in common by officials of the sixth through ninth ranks, sons of officials, and talented commoners.

entries.zh: 其職事，設司正官二，掌驗射者品級尊卑人力強弱而定耦，其中否則書於算，兵部官職之。
entries.en: For duties: two rectifying officials verify shooters' rank, seniority, and physical strength to form pairs; hits and misses are recorded on tallies—Ministry of War officials hold this office.
entries.literal: For duties: two rectifying officials are appointed, who verify shooters' rank, seniority, and physical strength to form pairs; hits and misses are recorded on tallies—Ministry of War officials hold this office.

entries.zh: 司射二，掌先以強弓射鵠誘射，以鼓衆氣，武職官充之。
entries.en: Two archery masters first shoot the target with a strong bow to lead the shooting and rouse everyone's spirit—military officials fill this role.
entries.literal: Two archery masters first shoot the target with a strong bow to lead the shooting and rouse everyone's spirit—military officials fill this role.

entries.zh: 司射器官二，掌辨弓力強弱，分爲三等，驗人力強弱以授，工部官職之。
entries.en: Two archery-equipment officials distinguish bow strength, divide bows into three grades, and verify human strength to assign them—Ministry of Works officials hold this office.
entries.literal: Two archery-equipment officials distinguish strong and weak bow strength, divide them into three grades, verify human strength to assign them—Ministry of Works officials hold this office.

entries.zh: 舉爵者，掌以馬湩授中者飲，光祿寺官職之。
entries.en: The cup-raisers give mare's milk to those who hit the mark to drink—Court of Imperial Entertainments officials hold this office.
entries.literal: The cup-raisers give mare's milk to those who hit to drink—Court of Imperial Entertainments officials hold this office.

entries.zh: 請射者，掌定耦射。
entries.en: The shooting-requesters manage forming pairs for shooting.
entries.literal: The shooting-requesters manage forming pairs for shooting.

entries.zh: 射畢，再請某耦射，侍儀司職之。
entries.en: When shooting is finished, they again request such-and-such a pair to shoot—the Ceremonial Attendants Directorate holds this office.
entries.literal: When shooting is finished, they again request such-and-such a pair to shoot—the Ceremonial Attendants Directorate holds this office.

entries.zh: 待獲者、掌矢納於司射器者，以隸僕供其役。
entries.en: Retrievers and those who place arrows in the archery master's vessel are supplied by menial servants.
entries.literal: Retrievers and those who place arrows in the archery master's vessel are supplied by menial servants.

entries.zh: 執旗者六人，掌於容後執五色旗。
entries.en: Six banner-bearers hold the five-colored banners behind the screen.
entries.literal: Six banner-bearers hold the five-colored banners behind the screen.

entries.zh: 如射者中的，舉紅旗應之。
entries.en: If the shooter hits the center, they raise the red banner in response.
entries.literal: If the shooter hits the center, they raise the red banner in response.

entries.zh: 中採，舉採旗應之。
entries.en: If he hits a colored fold, they raise the colored banner in response.
entries.literal: If he hits a colored fold, they raise the colored banner in response.

entries.zh: 偏西，舉白旗。
entries.en: If the shot lands off-center toward the west, they raise the white banner.
entries.literal: If the shot misses toward the west, they raise the white banner.

entries.zh: 偏東，舉青旗。
entries.en: If the shot lands off-center toward the east, they raise the green banner.
entries.literal: If the shot misses toward the east, they raise the green banner.

entries.zh: 過於鵠舉黃旗。
entries.en: If the shot passes beyond the target, they raise the yellow banner.
entries.literal: If the shot passes beyond the target, they raise the yellow banner.

entries.zh: 不及鵠，舉黑旗。
entries.en: If it falls short of the target, they raise the black banner.
entries.literal: If it falls short of the target, they raise the black banner.

entries.zh: 軍士二人掌之。
entries.en: Two soldiers manage this.
entries.literal: Two soldiers manage this.

entries.zh: 引禮二，掌引文武官進退，侍儀司舍人職之。
entries.en: Two ushers lead civil and military officials forward and back—Ceremonial Attendants Directorate clerks hold this office.
entries.literal: Two ushers manage leading civil and military officials forward and back—Ceremonial Attendants Directorate clerks hold this office.

entries.zh: 志第三十三 禮十一
entries.en: Treatise 33: Rites Eleven
entries.literal: Treatises 33: Rites 11

entries.en: (Military Rites)
entries.literal: (Military Rites)

entries.zh: 世宗崩，令旨免命婦哭臨。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong died, a directive exempted ladies of rank from weeping at the lying-in-state.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong passed away, a directive exempted ladies of rank from weeping at the lying-in-state.

entries.zh: 隆慶元年正月，未及二十七日，帝衰服御宣治門，百官素服、腰絰奉慰。
entries.en: In the first month of the first year of Longqing, before the twenty-seven days had passed, the emperor in full mourning conducted affairs at the Gate of Proclaiming Governance while officials in plain dress and waist mourning bands presented comforting condolences.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Longqing, before twenty-seven days had passed, the emperor in full mourning conducted affairs at the Gate of Proclaiming Governance; all officials in plain dress and waist mourning bands presented comforting condolences.

entries.zh: 發引，帝行遣奠禮。
entries.en: When the funeral procession departed, the emperor performed the dispatch offering rite.
entries.literal: When the procession departed, the emperor performed the dispatch offering rite.

entries.zh: 至朝祖，則遣官捧帛行禮。
entries.en: For the ancestral visit, officials were dispatched to bear the silks and perform the rites.
entries.literal: At the ancestral visit, officials were dispatched to bear the silks and perform the rites.

entries.zh: 梓宮至順天府，皇親命婦及三品以上命婦祭，餘如舊制。
entries.en: When the imperial bier reached Shuntian Prefecture, imperial relatives among ladies of rank and ladies of rank of the third grade and above offered sacrifice; everything else followed the old regulations.
entries.literal: When the catalpa coffin reached Shuntian Prefecture, imperial relatives among ladies of rank and ladies of rank of the third grade and above offered sacrifice; the rest followed the old regulations.

entries.zh: 光宗即位，禮部言：「喪服列代皆有制度，而斷自孝宗。
entries.en: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, the Ministry of Rites reported: "Each generation has its own regulations for mourning dress, but the standard was set by Hongzhi.
entries.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, the Ministry of Rites reported: "Mourning dress for each generation all has regulations, but they take Hongzhi as the cutoff.

entries.zh: 蓋孝宗篤於親，喪禮詳且備，故武、世、穆三廟皆宗之。
entries.en: Hongzhi was deeply devoted to his parents, and his mourning rites were detailed and complete; for this reason the reigns of Wuzong, Shizong, and Muzong all took him as their model.
entries.literal: This is because Hongzhi was devoted to his parents, and his mourning rites were detailed and complete; therefore the three temples of Wuzong, Shizong, and Muzong all took him as their model.

entries.zh: 今遵舊制，以衰服御文華門視事，百官素服朝參，候梓宮發引除。」
entries.en: We now follow the old regulations: conduct affairs at the Wenhua Gate in full mourning, with all officials attending court in plain dress, and doff mourning only after the imperial bier procession has departed."
entries.literal: Now we follow the old regulations: in full mourning conduct affairs at the Wenhua Gate, all officials in plain dress attend court, and wait until the catalpa coffin procession departs before doffing mourning."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: This was approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 明自仁宗獻陵以後，規制儉約。
entries.en: From the Hongxi Emperor's Xianling tomb onward, Ming regulations were economical.
entries.literal: From the Ming, after Renzong's Xianling tomb, the regulations were economical.

entries.zh: 世宗葬永陵，其制始侈。
entries.en: When Shizong was buried at Yongling, tomb regulations first became extravagant.
entries.literal: When Shizong was buried at Yongling, its regulations first became extravagant.

entries.zh: 及神宗葬定陵，給事中惠世揚、御史薛貞巡視陵工，費至八百餘萬云。
entries.en: When Shenzong was buried at Dingling, Supervising Secretary Hui Shiyang and Censor Xue Zhen inspected the tomb construction; the cost is said to have exceeded eight million taels.
entries.literal: When Shenzong was buried at Dingling, Supervising Secretary Hui Shiyang and Censor Xue Zhen inspected the tomb works; the expense is said to have reached more than eight million.

entries.zh: 志第三十四 禮十二
entries.en: Treatise 34: Rites, Part Twelve
entries.literal: Treatise 34, Rites 12

entries.zh: 〈（凶禮一）〉
entries.en: (Mourning Rites, Part One)
entries.literal: (Mourning Rites 1)

entries.zh: ◎儀衛 《周官》，王之儀衛分掌於天官、春官、夏官之屬，而蹕事則專屬於秋官。
entries.en: ◎ Ceremonial Guards. Under the Offices of Zhou, the sovereign's ceremonial escort was apportioned among the bureaus of Heaven, Spring, and Summer; clearing the imperial way fell solely to the Autumn Office.
entries.literal: ◎ Ceremonial Guards. In the Offices of Zhou, the king's ceremonial guards and escorts were divided among the subordinate offices of Heaven, Spring, and Summer, while road-clearing duties belonged exclusively to the Autumn Office.

entries.zh: 漢朝會，則衛官陳車騎，張旗幟。
entries.en: At Han court assemblies, guard officers deployed chariots and cavalry and raised banners and standards.
entries.literal: At Han imperial assemblies, guard officers arrayed chariots and horsemen and unfurled banners and standards.

entries.zh: 唐沿隋制，置衛尉卿，掌儀仗帳幕之事。
entries.en: The Tang adopted the Sui arrangement, appointing a Director of the Imperial Guard to manage ceremonial equipment and ceremonial canopies.
entries.literal: The Tang followed the Sui system and established the Director of the Imperial Guard, who oversaw ceremonial regalia and canopy affairs.

entries.zh: 宋衛 尉領左右金吾衛司、左右金吾仗司、六軍儀仗司，主清道、徼巡、排列、奉引儀 仗。
entries.en: In Song times the Imperial Guard Directorate supervised the Left and Right Golden Crow guard offices, their ceremonial branches, and the Six Armies Ceremonial Office, responsible for clearing the way, patrol, marshaling formations, and leading the ceremonial train.
entries.literal: Under the Song, the Imperial Guard Directorate oversaw the Left and Right Golden Crow Guard Offices, the Left and Right Golden Crow Ceremonial Offices, and the Six Armies Ceremonial Office, charged with road clearing, patrol, formation, and presentation of ceremonial regalia.

entries.zh: 元置拱衛司，領控鶴戶以供其事。
entries.en: The Yuan created the Imperial Escort Directorate, drawing on Crane-Control households to perform these services.
entries.literal: The Yuan established the Imperial Escort Directorate, which oversaw Crane-Control households to supply its duties.

entries.zh: 歷代制度雖有沿革異同，總以謹出入之防， 嚴尊卑之分。
entries.en: Institutions varied from dynasty to dynasty, yet all aimed to guard ingress and egress and to enforce the hierarchy of rank.
entries.literal: Although institutions changed through the dynasties, in general they strictly guarded access and strictly distinguished superior from inferior.

entries.zh: 慎重則尊嚴，尊嚴則整肅，是故文謂之儀，武謂之衛。
entries.en: Careful observance yields dignity, and dignity yields discipline; the civil aspect is therefore called ceremony and the martial aspect guard.
entries.literal: When cautious and weighty, there is dignity; when dignified, there is order—hence the civil aspect is called ceremony and the martial aspect is called guard.

entries.zh: 天子出，車 駕次第謂之鹵簿。
entries.en: When the emperor went abroad, the ordered procession of his carriage escort was termed the guard of honor.
entries.literal: When the Son of Heaven went forth, the ordered sequence of his carriage escort was called the guard of honor.

entries.zh: 而唐制四品以上皆給鹵簿，則君臣並得通稱也。
entries.en: Under Tang rules, however, officials of the fourth rank and above also received a guard of honor, so ruler and subject alike could use the term.
entries.literal: Yet under Tang regulations all officials of the fourth rank and above were granted a guard of honor, so the term could be used alike for ruler and subject.

entries.zh: 明初詔禮官， 鹵簿彌文，務從省節，以示尚質去奢之意。
entries.en: Early in the dynasty the emperor instructed the ritual officials to pare back the guard of honor, keeping it spare to signal a preference for plainness over luxury.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Ming an edict ordered the ritual officials that the guard of honor had grown overly elaborate and should be simplified to show esteem for simplicity and rejection of extravagance.

entries.zh: 凡正、至、聖節、朝會，及冊拜、接 見蕃臣，儀鸞司陳設儀仗。
entries.en: On New Year's Day, the winter solstice, imperial birthdays, court assemblies, investiture ceremonies, and audiences with foreign envoys, the Ceremonial Phoenix Office deployed the ceremonial train.
entries.literal: For the first day of the year, the winter solstice, sacred festivals, court assemblies, investiture audiences, and receptions of foreign tributaries, the Ceremonial Phoenix Office set out ceremonial regalia.

entries.zh: 而中宮、東宮、親王皆有儀仗之制。
entries.en: The empress, the heir apparent, and imperial princes each had prescribed ceremonial trains as well.
entries.literal: The empress, the heir apparent, and imperial princes each had their own regulations for ceremonial regalia.

entries.zh: 後或隨時增飾， 要以洪武創制爲準則焉。
entries.en: Later reigns sometimes added embellishments, yet the Hongwu founding code remained the touchstone.
entries.literal: Later additions were made from time to time, but the Hongwu founding regulations remained the standard.

entries.zh: 茲撮《集禮》所載大凡，以備考覈。
entries.en: What follows excerpts the principal entries in the Collected Rites for reference and verification.
entries.literal: Here the main points recorded in the Collected Rites are excerpted for reference and verification.

entries.zh: 其郡王及皇妃、東 宮妃以下儀仗，載在《會典》者，並著於篇云。
entries.en: The ceremonial trains of territorial princes, imperial consorts, and consorts of the heir apparent and below, as recorded in the Statutes, are likewise included here.
entries.literal: The ceremonial regalia of territorial princes, imperial consorts, and consorts of the heir apparent and below, as recorded in the Statutes, are also set down in this chapter.

entries.zh: 洪武元年十月，定元旦朝賀儀：金吾衛於奉天門外分設旗幟。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Hongwu's first year the New Year's congratulatory audience was codified: the Golden Crow Guard posted banners outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Hongwu the New Year's Day congratulatory audience was fixed: the Golden Crow Guard set out banners outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

entries.zh: 宿衛於午門外 分設兵仗。
entries.en: The Palace Guard deployed arms outside the Meridian Gate.
entries.literal: The Palace Guard set out weapons outside the Meridian Gate.

entries.zh: 衛尉寺於奉天殿門及丹陛、丹墀設黃麾仗。
entries.en: The Imperial Guard Office arrayed yellow command regalia at the hall doors, on the red steps, and in the red courtyard.
entries.literal: The Imperial Guard Office set yellow command regalia at the doors of the Hall of Supreme Harmony and on the red steps and courtyard.

entries.zh: 內使監擎執於殿上。
entries.en: Palace attendants bore regalia inside the hall.
entries.literal: The Directorate of Palace Attendants bore items inside the hall.

entries.zh: 凡遇 冬至、聖節、冊拜、親王及蕃使來朝，儀俱同。
entries.en: The winter solstice, imperial birthdays, investitures, visits by imperial princes, and audiences with foreign envoys all followed the same arrangement.
entries.literal: Whenever the winter solstice, sacred festivals, investiture audiences, visits of imperial princes, or audiences with foreign envoys occurred, the ceremonies were the same.

entries.zh: 其宣詔赦、降香，則惟設奉天殿 門及丹陛儀仗、殿上擎執云。
entries.en: For amnesty proclamations and incense offerings, only the hall-door and red-step regalia and items borne within the hall were deployed.
entries.literal: For proclamation of amnesties and descent of incense, only regalia at the hall doors and red steps and items borne inside the hall were set out.

entries.zh: 其陳布次第，午門外，刀、盾、殳、叉各置於東西， 甲士用赤。
entries.en: The disposition ran thus: outside the Meridian Gate, sabers, shields, spears, and forks stood east and west, manned by soldiers in red armor.
entries.literal: The order of arrangement: outside the Meridian Gate, sabers, shields, spears, and forks were placed east and west, with armored soldiers in red.

entries.zh: 奉天門外中道，金吾、宿衛二衛設龍旗十二，分左右，用青甲士十二 人。
entries.en: Along the central avenue outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, the Golden Crow and Palace Guards posted twelve dragon banners, six to a side, borne by twelve soldiers in green armor.
entries.literal: On the central way outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, the Golden Crow and Palace Guards set twelve dragon banners, left and right, with twelve soldiers in green armor.

entries.zh: 北斗旗一、纛一居前，豹尾一居後，俱用黑甲士三人。
entries.en: One Big Dipper banner and one command banner led; one leopard-tail standard followed—three soldiers in black armor for each.
entries.literal: One Big Dipper banner and one great banner went before, one leopard-tail standard behind, each with three soldiers in black armor.

entries.zh: 虎豹各二，馴象六， 分左右。
entries.en: Two tiger and two leopard figures apiece and six trained elephants were posted to left and right.
entries.literal: Two each of tiger and leopard figures, six trained elephants, divided left and right.

entries.zh: 左右布旗六十四：左前第一行，門旗二，每旗用紅甲士五人，內一人執 旗，旗下四人執弓箭。
entries.en: Sixty-four cloth banners to left and right: on the left front, first row, two gate banners, each with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.
entries.literal: Sixty-four cloth banners left and right: on the left front, first row, two gate banners, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.

entries.zh: 第二行，月旗一，用白甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人 執弩；
entries.en: Second row: one moon banner with five soldiers in white armor—one bearing it, four beneath with crossbows.
entries.literal: Second row, one moon banner, with five soldiers in white armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.

entries.zh: 青龍旗一，用青甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。
entries.en: One Azure Dragon banner with five soldiers in green armor—one bearing it, four beneath with crossbows.
entries.literal: One Azure Dragon banner, with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.

entries.zh: 第三行，風、雲、 雷、雨旗各一，每旗用黑甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭；
entries.en: Third row: one wind, cloud, thunder, and rain banner apiece, each with five soldiers in black armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.
entries.literal: Third row, one each of wind, cloud, thunder, and rain banners, each with five soldiers in black armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.

entries.zh: 天馬、白澤、 朱雀旗各一，每旗用紅甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭。
entries.en: One Heavenly Horse, White Marsh, and Vermilion Bird banner apiece, each with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.
entries.literal: One each of Heavenly Horse, White Marsh, and Vermilion Bird banners, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.

entries.zh: 第四行，木、 火、土、金、水五星旗各一，隨其方色，每旗用甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四 人執弩，其甲木青、火紅、土黃、金白、水黑、熊旗、鸞旗各一，每旗用紅甲士 五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。
entries.en: Fourth row: one banner each for Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water, colored to their directions, each with five armored soldiers—one bearing the banner, four beneath with crossbows—armor green for Wood, red for Fire, yellow for Earth, white for Metal, black for Water; plus one bear and one phoenix banner, each with five soldiers in red armor.
entries.literal: Fourth row, one each of Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water Five Stars banners, in their directional colors, each with five armored soldiers, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows—their armor being green for Wood, red for Fire, yellow for Earth, white for Metal, black for Water; one bear banner and one phoenix banner, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.

entries.zh: 第五行角、亢、氐、房、心、尾、箕旗各一， 每旗用青甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭。
entries.en: Fifth row: one banner each for Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket, each with five soldiers in green armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.
entries.literal: Fifth row, one each of Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket banners, each with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.

entries.zh: 第六行鬥、牛、女、虛、危、 室、壁旗各一，每旗用青甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。
entries.en: Sixth row: one banner each for Dipper, Ox, Girl, Void, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall, each with five soldiers in green armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with crossbows.
entries.literal: Sixth row, one each of Dipper, Ox, Girl, Void, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall banners, each with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.

entries.zh: 右前第一行， 門旗二，每旗用紅甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭。
entries.en: On the right front, first row: two gate banners, each with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.
entries.literal: On the right front, first row, two gate banners, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.

entries.zh: 第二行，日旗一， 用紅甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩；
entries.en: Second row: one sun banner with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing it, four beneath with crossbows.
entries.literal: Second row, one sun banner, with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.

entries.zh: 白虎旗一，用白甲士五人，內一人 執旗，旗下四人執弩。
entries.en: One White Tiger banner with five soldiers in white armor—one bearing it, four beneath with crossbows.
entries.literal: One White Tiger banner, with five soldiers in white armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.

entries.zh: 第三行，江、河、淮、濟旗各一，隨其方色，每旗用甲士 五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭，其甲江紅、河白、淮青、濟黑；
entries.en: Third row: one Yangtze, Yellow River, Huai, and Ji banner apiece, each with five armored soldiers—armor red for the Yangtze, white for the Yellow River, green for the Huai, black for the Ji.
entries.literal: Third row, one each of Yangtze, Yellow River, Huai, and Ji banners, in their directional colors, each with five armored soldiers, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows—their armor being red for the Yangtze, white for the Yellow River, green for the Huai, black for the Ji.

entries.zh: 天祿、白 澤、玄武旗各一，每旗用甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭，天祿、白澤 紅甲，玄武黑甲。
entries.en: One Heavenly Blessing, White Marsh, and Dark Warrior banner apiece, each with five armored soldiers—Heavenly Blessing and White Marsh in red armor, Dark Warrior in black.
entries.literal: One each of Heavenly Blessing, White Marsh, and Dark Warrior banners, each with five armored soldiers, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows—Heavenly Blessing and White Marsh in red armor, Dark Warrior in black armor.

entries.zh: 第四行，東、南、中、西、北五嶽旗各一，隨其方色，每旗用 甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩，其甲東嶽青、南嶽紅、中嶽黃、西嶽白、 北嶽黑；
entries.en: Fourth row: one banner each for the eastern, southern, central, western, and northern sacred peaks, each with five armored soldiers—armor green, red, yellow, white, and black respectively.
entries.literal: Fourth row, one each of the eastern, southern, central, western, and northern Five Sacred Peaks banners, in their directional colors, each with five armored soldiers, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows—their armor being green for the eastern peak, red for the southern, yellow for the central, white for the western, black for the northern.

entries.zh: 熊旗、麟旗各一，每旗用紅甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。
entries.en: One bear and one qilin banner, each with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with crossbows.
entries.literal: One bear banner and one qilin banner, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.

entries.zh: 第 五行，奎、婁、胃、昴、畢、觜、參旗各一，每旗用青甲士五人，內一人執旗， 旗下四人執弓箭。
entries.en: Fifth row: one banner each for Striding Legs, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars, each with five soldiers in green armor.
entries.literal: Fifth row, one each of Striding Legs, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars banners, each with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.

entries.zh: 第六行，井、鬼、柳、星、張、翼、軫旗各一，每旗用青甲士 五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。
entries.en: Sixth row: one banner each for Well, Ghost, Willow, Star, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot, each with five soldiers in green armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with crossbows.
entries.literal: Sixth row, one each of Well, Ghost, Willow, Star, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot banners, each with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.

entries.zh: 奉天門外，拱衛司設五輅。
entries.en: Outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony the Imperial Escort Directorate arrayed the five imperial carriages.
entries.literal: Outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, the Imperial Escort Directorate set the five imperial carriages.

entries.zh: 玉輅居中；
entries.en: The jade carriage at center.
entries.literal: The jade carriage in the center.

entries.zh: 左金 輅，次革輅；
entries.en: To its left the gold carriage, then the leather carriage.
entries.literal: To the left the gold carriage, then the leather carriage.

entries.zh: 右象輅，次木輅。
entries.en: To its right the ivory carriage, then the wood carriage.
entries.literal: To the right the ivory carriage, then the wood carriage.

entries.zh: 俱並列。
entries.en: All aligned abreast.
entries.literal: All ranged in parallel.

entries.zh: 典牧所設乘馬於文武樓之南，各三，東 西相向。
entries.en: The Pasturage Office posted riding horses south of the Civil and Military Tower, three on each side, facing one another east and west.
entries.literal: The Pasturage Office set riding horses south of the Civil and Military Tower, three each, facing east and west.

entries.zh: 丹墀左右布黃麾仗凡九十，分左右，各三行。
entries.en: Ninety pieces of yellow command regalia lined the red courtyard to left and right, three rows on each side.
entries.literal: To left and right of the red courtyard were arrayed ninety pieces of yellow command regalia, divided left and right, three rows each.

entries.zh: 左前第一行，十五：黃蓋 一，紅大傘二，華蓋一，曲蓋一，紫方傘一，紅方傘一，雉扇四，朱團扇四。
entries.en: Left front, first row—fifteen items: one yellow canopy, two large red umbrellas, one flowered and one curved canopy, one purple and one red square umbrella, four pheasant-tail fans, and four vermilion round fans.
entries.literal: Left front, first row, fifteen items: one yellow canopy, two large red umbrellas, one flowered canopy, one curved canopy, one purple square umbrella, one red square umbrella, four pheasant-tail fans, four vermilion round fans.

entries.zh: 第 二行，十五：羽葆幢二，豹尾二，龍頭竿二，信幡二，傳教幡二，告止幡二，絳 引幡二，黃麾一。
entries.en: Second row—fifteen: two feathered canopy staffs, two leopard-tail standards, two dragon-head poles, two each of trust, instruction, stop, and crimson guide banners, and one yellow command staff.
entries.literal: Second row, fifteen: two feathered canopy staffs, two leopard-tail standards, two dragon-head poles, two trust banners, two instruction banners, two stop banners, two crimson guide banners, one yellow command staff.

entries.zh: 第三行，十五：戟氅五，戈氅五，儀鍠氅五。
entries.en: Third row—fifteen: five halberd pennants, five dagger-axe pennants, and five ceremonial bell pennants.
entries.literal: Third row, fifteen: five halberd pennants, five dagger-axe pennants, five ceremonial bell pennants.

entries.zh: 右前第一行，十 五：黃蓋一，紅大傘二，華蓋一，曲蓋一，紫方傘一，紅方傘一，雉扇四，朱團 扇四。
entries.en: Right front, first row—fifteen: the same array as on the left.
entries.literal: Right front, first row, fifteen: one yellow canopy, two large red umbrellas, one flowered canopy, one curved canopy, one purple square umbrella, one red square umbrella, four pheasant-tail fans, four vermilion round fans.

entries.zh: 第二行，十五：羽葆幢二，豹尾二，龍頭竿二，信幡二，傳教幡二，告止 幡二，絳引幡二，黃麾一。
entries.en: Second row—fifteen: matching the left side in every item.
entries.literal: Second row, fifteen: two feathered canopy staffs, two leopard-tail standards, two dragon-head poles, two trust banners, two instruction banners, two stop banners, two crimson guide banners, one yellow command staff.

entries.zh: 第三行，十五：戟氅五，戈氅五，儀鍠氅五。
entries.en: Third row—fifteen: five halberd pennants, five dagger-axe pennants, and five ceremonial bell pennants.
entries.literal: Third row, fifteen: five halberd pennants, five dagger-axe pennants, five ceremonial bell pennants.

entries.zh: 皆校尉 擎執。
entries.en: Guard commandants bore them all.
entries.literal: All were borne by guard commandants.

entries.zh: 丹陛左右，拱衛司陳幢節等仗九十，分左右，爲四行。
entries.en: Flanking the red steps, the Imperial Escort Directorate arrayed ninety canopy staffs and allied regalia in four rows to each side.
entries.literal: To left and right of the red steps, the Imperial Escort Directorate displayed ninety canopy staffs and other regalia, divided left and right into four rows.

entries.zh: 左前第一行，響節 十二，金節三，燭籠三。
entries.en: Left front, first row: twelve sounding staffs, three gold staffs, and three candle lanterns.
entries.literal: Left front, first row: twelve sounding staffs, three gold staffs, three candle lanterns.

entries.zh: 第二行，青龍幢一，班劍三，吾杖三，立瓜三，臥瓜三， 儀刀三，鐙杖三，戟三，骨朵三，朱雀幢一。
entries.en: Second row: one Azure Dragon canopy staff, three each of court swords, ceremonial staffs, standing and reclining melons, ceremonial blades, stirrup staffs, halberds, and maces, and one Vermilion Bird canopy staff.
entries.literal: Second row: one Azure Dragon canopy staff, three court swords, three ceremonial staffs, three standing melons, three reclining melons, three ceremonial blades, three stirrup staffs, three halberds, three maces, one Vermilion Bird canopy staff.

entries.zh: 右前第一行，響節十二，金節三， 燭籠三。
entries.en: Right front, first row: twelve sounding staffs, three gold staffs, and three candle lanterns.
entries.literal: Right front, first row: twelve sounding staffs, three gold staffs, three candle lanterns.

entries.zh: 第二行，白虎幢一，班劍三，吾杖三，立瓜三，臥瓜三，儀刀三，鐙杖 三，戟三，骨朵三，玄武幢一。
entries.en: Second row: one White Tiger canopy staff, three each of the same weapons and regalia as on the left, and one Dark Warrior canopy staff.
entries.literal: Second row: one White Tiger canopy staff, three court swords, three ceremonial staffs, three standing melons, three reclining melons, three ceremonial blades, three stirrup staffs, three halberds, three maces, one Dark Warrior canopy staff.

entries.zh: 皆校尉擎執。
entries.en: Guard commandants bore them all.
entries.literal: All were borne by guard commandants.

entries.zh: 奉天殿門左右，拱衛司陳設：左行， 圓蓋一，金腳踏一，金水盆一，團黃扇三，紅扇三；
entries.en: Beside the doors of the Hall of Supreme Harmony the Imperial Escort Directorate posted: on the left, one round canopy, one gold footrest, one gold water basin, three round yellow fans, and three red fans.
entries.literal: To left and right of the doors of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, the Imperial Escort Directorate set out: on the left, one round canopy, one gold footrest, one gold water basin, three round yellow fans, three red fans.
