entries.literal: The robe was yellow, round-collared and narrow-sleeved; front, back, and both shoulders each had one gold coiled dragon woven.

entries.zh: 帶用玉，靴以皮為之。
entries.en: The belt was of jade, and the boots were leather.
entries.literal: The belt used jade; boots were made of leather.

entries.zh: 先是，洪武二十四年，帝微行至神樂觀，見有結網巾者。
entries.en: Earlier, in Hongwu 24 (1391), the emperor went incognito to the Divine Music Observatory and saw a man wearing a net cap.
entries.literal: Earlier, in Hongwu 24, the emperor went incognito to the Divine Music Observatory and saw someone wearing a net cap.

entries.zh: 翼日，命取網巾，頒示十三布政使司，人無貴賤，皆裹網巾，於是天子亦常服網巾。
entries.en: The next day he ordered net caps collected and issued to the thirteen provincial commissions; thereafter men of every rank wore them, and the Son of Heaven adopted the net cap as part of his daily dress as well.
entries.literal: The next day he ordered net caps taken and issued to the thirteen provincial administrative commissions; people without distinction of noble or base all wrapped net caps — thus the Son of Heaven also wore a net cap as daily dress.

entries.zh: 又《會典》載皇太孫冠禮有云：「掌冠跪加網巾」，而皇帝、皇太子冠服，俱闕而不載。
entries.en: The Collected Statutes also record, in the imperial great-grandson's capping rite, that "the cap officer kneels and sets the net cap in place," yet the capping dress of the emperor and crown prince is nowhere recorded.
entries.literal: Also the Collected Statutes record the imperial great-grandson's capping rite as saying, "The cap officer kneels and adds the net cap," yet the crown dress of the emperor and crown prince are both omitted and not recorded.

entries.zh: 嘉靖七年，更定燕弁服。
entries.en: In Jiajing 7 (1528) the casual court cap dress was revised.
entries.literal: In Jiajing 7 the casual court cap dress was revised.

entries.zh: 初，帝以燕居冠服，尚沿習俗，諭張璁考古帝王燕居法服之制。
entries.en: At first, finding that the emperor's dress for private residence still followed ordinary custom, he instructed Zhang Cong to investigate how ancient emperors dressed for ritual occasions at leisure.
entries.literal: Initially, because the emperor's dress for private residence still followed custom, he instructed Zhang Cong to examine the ancient regulations for emperors' ritual dress at leisure.

entries.zh: 璁乃採《禮書》「玄端深衣。」
entries.en: Cong then drew from the Book of Rites the passage, "Dark robe and deep garment."
entries.literal: Cong then adopted from the Book of Rites the passage, "Dark robe and deep garment."

entries.zh: 之文，圖注以進。
entries.en: and submitted it with illustrated commentary.
entries.literal: and submitted an illustrated commentary.

entries.zh: 帝為參定其制，諭璁詳議。
entries.en: The emperor had him work out the regulations and instructed Cong to submit a detailed proposal.
entries.literal: The emperor had him determine the regulations and instructed Cong to deliberate in detail.

entries.zh: 璁言：「古者冕服之外，玄端深衣，其用最廣。
entries.en: Cong said, "In antiquity, apart from the court robes and crown, the dark robe and deep garment were the most widely worn garments.
entries.literal: Cong said: "In antiquity, beyond the court robes and crown, the dark robe and deep garment had the widest use.

entries.zh: 玄端自天子達於士，國家之命服也。
entries.en: The dark robe extended from the Son of Heaven down to the scholar; it was the dress mandated by the state.
entries.literal: The dark robe extended from the Son of Heaven down to the scholar — it was the state's mandated dress.

entries.zh: 深衣自天子達於庶人，聖賢之法服也。
entries.en: The deep garment extended from the Son of Heaven down to the commoner; it was the ritual dress of the sages.
entries.literal: The deep garment extended from the Son of Heaven down to the commoner — it was the sages' ritual dress.

entries.zh: 今以玄端加文飾，不易舊制，深衣易黃色，不離中衣，誠得帝王損益時中之道。」
entries.en: To adorn the dark robe without abandoning the old form, and to make the deep garment yellow while keeping the inner robe unchanged, truly captures the emperor's way of adapting ancient practice to the proper mean."
entries.literal: Now to use the dark robe with added decorative patterns without changing the old regulations, and to change the deep garment to yellow without departing from the inner robe — truly this attains the emperors' way of additions and subtractions at the timely mean."

entries.zh: 帝因諭禮部曰：「古玄端上下通用，今非古人比，雖燕居，宜辨等威。」
entries.en: The emperor therefore instructed the Ministry of Rites, "In antiquity the dark robe was worn alike by high and low, but we are not the ancients; even in private residence, rank and dignity should be preserved."
entries.literal: The emperor therefore instructed the Ministry of Rites: "In antiquity the dark robe was used alike above and below; today we are not comparable to the men of antiquity — even in private residence, ranks and authority should be distinguished."

entries.zh: 因酌古制，更名曰：「燕弁」，寓深宮獨處、以燕安為戒之意。
entries.en: Accordingly, drawing on ancient practice, the dress was renamed the "Casual Court Cap," expressing the idea of dwelling alone within the inner palace and taking repose and restraint as a warning.
entries.literal: Accordingly considering the ancient regulations, the name was revised to: "Casual Court Cap," conveying the meaning of dwelling alone in the inner palace and taking ease and restraint as a warning.

entries.zh: 其制，冠匡如皮弁之制，冒以烏紗，分十有二瓣，各以金線壓之，前飾五采玉雲各一，後列四山，朱條為組纓，雙玉簪。
entries.en: Its regulations were as follows: the cap frame followed the leather cap (ceremonial), covered with black gauze and divided into twelve petals, each traced with gold thread; the front bore one five-colored jade cloud on each side, the rear four mountain ornaments, vermilion cord tassels, and two jade hairpins.
entries.literal: Its regulations: the cap frame followed the leather cap (ceremonial) form, covered with black gauze and divided into twelve petals, each pressed with gold thread; the front bore one five-colored jade cloud each, the rear arrayed four mountains; vermilion cords served as tassels, with double jade hairpins.

entries.zh: 服如古玄端之制，色玄，邊緣以青，兩肩繡日月，前盤圓龍一，後盤方龍二，邊加龍文八十一，領與兩祛共龍文五九。
entries.en: The robe followed the ancient dark robe: dark in color with green edging; the shoulders bore embroidered sun and moon; one coiled round dragon appeared in front and two coiled square dragons behind; the border carried eighty-one dragon motifs, and the collar and both sleeves together fifty-nine.
entries.literal: The dress followed the ancient dark robe: dark in color with green edging; both shoulders embroidered with sun and moon; one coiled round dragon in front and two coiled square dragons behind; the border added eighty-one dragon designs; collar and both sleeves together had fifty-nine dragon designs.

entries.zh: 衽同前後齊，共龍文四九。
entries.en: The lapel was even front and back, with forty-nine dragon motifs in all.
entries.literal: The lapel was level front and back alike, with forty-nine dragon designs in all.

entries.zh: 襯用深衣之制，色黃。
entries.en: The lining followed the deep-garment cut and was yellow.
entries.literal: The lining followed the deep-garment regulations, yellow in color.

entries.zh: 袂圓祛方，下齊負繩及踝十二幅。
entries.en: The sleeves were round and the cuffs square; the lower hem had tie cords and twelve panels reaching the ankle.
entries.literal: Sleeves were round and cuffs square; the lower hem carried cords and twelve panels reaching the ankle.

entries.zh: 素帶，朱裡青表，綠緣邊，腰圍飾以玉龍九。
entries.en: There was a plain belt, vermilion within and green without, with green edging, and the waist was ornamented with nine jade dragons.
entries.literal: Plain belt, vermilion inside and green outside, with green edging; the waist was ornamented with nine jade dragons.

entries.zh: 玄履，朱緣紅纓黃結。
entries.en: Dark shoes had vermilion edging, red tassels, and yellow knots.
entries.literal: Dark shoes, with vermilion edging, red tassels, and yellow knots.

entries.zh: 白襪。
entries.en: White stockings completed the dress.
entries.literal: White stockings.

entries.zh: 皇帝武弁服：明初親徵遣將服之。
entries.en: The emperor's military cap dress was worn in early Ming when the emperor took the field in person or dispatched generals on campaign.
entries.literal: The emperor's military cap dress: in early Ming, when the emperor personally campaigned or dispatched generals, he wore it.

entries.zh: 嘉靖八年諭閣臣張璁云：「《會典》紀親徵、類禡之祭，皆具武弁服。
entries.en: In Jiajing 8 (1529) the emperor instructed Grand Secretary Zhang Cong, "The Collected Statutes record that personal campaigns and pre-battle prayer sacrifices all require the military cap dress.
entries.literal: In Jiajing 8 the emperor instructed Grand Secretary Zhang Cong: "The Collected Statutes record that personal campaigns and pre-battle prayer sacrifices all require the military cap dress.

entries.zh: 不可不備。」
entries.en: It must be fully provided."
entries.literal: It cannot fail to be complete."

entries.zh: 璁對：「《周禮》有韋弁，謂以韎韋為弁，又以為衣裳。
entries.en: Cong replied: "The Rites of Zhou describes the hide cap, by which crimson leather was used for the cap and also for the robe and skirt.
entries.literal: Cong replied: The Rites of Zhou has the hide cap, meaning that crimson leather was used for the cap and also for the robe and skirt.

entries.zh: 國朝視古損益，有皮弁之制。
entries.en: Our dynasty, adapting ancient practice, already had regulations for the leather cap (ceremonial).
entries.literal: Our dynasty, considering antiquity with additions and subtractions, has the leather cap (ceremonial) regulations.

entries.zh: 今武弁當如皮弁，但皮弁以黑紗冒之，武弁當以絳紗冒之。」
entries.en: The military cap should follow the leather cap (ceremonial), except that the leather cap is covered with black gauze while the military cap should be covered with deep-red gauze."
entries.literal: Now the military cap should be like the leather cap, but the leather cap is covered with black gauze, whereas the military cap should be covered with deep-red gauze."

entries.zh: 隨具圖以進。
entries.en: He then submitted an illustrated plan.
entries.literal: He then submitted an illustrated plan.

entries.zh: 帝報曰：「覽圖有韠形，但無系處。
entries.en: The emperor replied, "The plan shows a knee-flap, but no place to fasten it.
entries.literal: The emperor replied: "On viewing the plan there is a knee-flap shape, but no place to attach it.

entries.zh: 冠制古象上尖，今皮弁則圓。
entries.en: In antiquity the cap was made with a pointed top; today's leather cap is round.
entries.literal: The crown regulations of antiquity imaged a pointed top; today's leather cap is round.

entries.zh: 朕惟上銳取其輕利，當如古制。
entries.en: I believe the pointed top was chosen for lightness and sharpness; the cap should follow the ancient form.
entries.literal: I consider that the pointed top takes lightness and sharpness — it should follow the ancient regulations.

entries.zh: 又衣裳韠舄皆赤色，何謂？
entries.en: And why are the robe, skirt, knee-flap, and shoes all red?
entries.literal: Also the robe, skirt, knee-flap, and shoes are all red — what is the meaning of this?

entries.zh: 且佩綬俱無，於祭用之，可乎？」
entries.en: Moreover, there are no pendants or sash at all — is that acceptable for sacrificial use?"
entries.literal: Moreover pendants and sash are entirely absent — for use in sacrifice, is this acceptable?"

entries.zh: 璁對：「自古服冕弁俱用革帶，以前系韍，後系綬。
entries.en: Cong replied, "From antiquity, ceremonial crowns and caps were always worn with a leather belt, the knee cover fastened in front and the sash behind.
entries.literal: Cong replied: "From antiquity, when wearing the ceremonial crown and cap one always used the leather belt, attaching the knee cover in front and the sash behind.

entries.zh: 韋弁之韠，正系於革帶耳。
entries.en: The hide cap's knee-flap was attached directly to the leather belt.
entries.literal: The knee-flap of the hide cap was precisely attached to the leather belt.

entries.zh: 武事尚威烈，故色純用赤。」
entries.en: Military affairs emphasize awe and force, so the dress is entirely red."
entries.literal: Military affairs esteem majesty and fierceness, so the colors purely use red."

entries.zh: 帝復報璁：「冠服、衣裳、韠舄俱如古制，增革帶、佩綬及圭。」
entries.en: The emperor wrote back to Cong, "The cap, robe, skirt, knee-flap, and shoes should all follow the ancient regulations, with a leather belt, pendant sash, and jade tablet added."
entries.literal: The emperor again replied to Cong: "The cap dress, robe, skirt, knee-flap, and shoes should all follow the ancient regulations, with the addition of leather belt, pendant sash, and tablet."

entries.zh: 乃定制，弁上銳，色用赤，上十二縫，中綴五采玉，落落如星狀。
entries.en: The regulations were then fixed: the cap was pointed and red, with twelve seams on the upper part and five-colored jade strung between them, scattered like stars.
entries.literal: Thereupon the regulations were fixed: the cap was pointed on top, red in color, with twelve seams above, five-colored jade strung in the middle, scattered like stars.

entries.zh: 韎衣、韎裳、韎韐，俱赤色。
entries.en: The crimson-leather robe, skirt, and leggings were all red.
entries.literal: Crimson-leather robe, skirt, and leggings were all red.

entries.zh: 佩、綬、革帶，如常制。
entries.en: The pendants, sash, and leather belt followed the usual regulations.
entries.literal: Pendants, sash, and leather belt followed the ordinary regulations.

entries.zh: 佩綬及韎韐，俱上系於革帶。
entries.en: The pendants, sash, and crimson leggings were all fastened to the leather belt above.
entries.literal: Pendants, sash, and crimson leggings were all attached above to the leather belt.

entries.zh: 舄如裳色。
entries.en: The shoes matched the skirt in color.
entries.literal: Shoes matched the skirt's color.

entries.zh: 玉圭視鎮圭差小，剡上方下，有篆文曰：「討罪安民」。
entries.en: The jade tablet was slightly smaller than the quarter-tablet, square at the top and tapered below, and bore seal-script characters reading, "Subdue crime and pacify the people."
entries.literal: The jade tablet was slightly smaller than the quarter-tablet, cut square above and tapered below, with seal script reading: "Subdue crime and pacify the people."

entries.zh: 嘉靖七年，諭禮部：「朕仿古玄端，自為燕弁冠服，更制忠靜冠服，錫於有位，而宗室諸王制猶未備。
entries.en: In Jiajing 7 (1528) he instructed the Ministry of Rites, "Drawing on the ancient dark robe, I have myself devised the Casual Court Cap dress and further devised the Loyal Serenity crown and dress, bestowing them upon officeholders; yet regulations for the imperial clans and princes remain incomplete.
entries.literal: In Jiajing 7, he instructed the Ministry of Rites: "I follow the ancient dark robe, have myself devised the Casual Court Cap dress, and further devised the Loyal Serenity crown and dress, bestowing them upon officeholders, yet regulations for the imperial clans and princes remain incomplete.

entries.zh: 今酌燕弁及忠靜冠之制，復為式具圖，命曰保和冠服。
entries.en: Now, drawing on the regulations for the Casual Court Cap and the Loyal Serenity cap, I have again prepared models with illustrations and named them the Preservation-and-Harmony crown and dress.
entries.literal: Now, drawing on the regulations for the Casual Court Cap and Loyal Serenity cap, I have again prepared models with illustrations, naming them the Preservation-and-Harmony crown and dress.

entries.zh: 自郡王長子以上，其式已明。
entries.en: For eldest sons of commandery princes and above, the forms are already established.
entries.literal: From the eldest sons of commandery princes upward, the forms are already clear.

entries.zh: 鎮國將軍以下至奉國中尉及長史、審理、紀善、教授、伴讀，俱用忠靜冠服，依其品服之。
entries.en: From State-pacifying Generals down to Supporters-of-the-State Second Captains, together with chief secretaries, judicial reviewers, recorders of goodness, instructors, and study companions, all wear the Loyal Serenity crown and dress according to rank.
entries.literal: From State-pacifying Generals downward to Supporters-of-the-State Second Captains, as well as chief secretaries, judicial reviewers, recorders of goodness, instructors, and study companions, all use the Loyal Serenity crown and dress, wearing them according to rank.

entries.zh: 儀賓及餘官不許概服。
entries.en: Protocol sons-in-law and other officials may not wear them without authorization.
entries.literal: Protocol sons-in-law and other officials may not wear them indiscriminately.

entries.zh: 夫忠靜冠服之異式，尊賢之等也。
entries.en: The distinct styles of the Loyal Serenity crown and dress mark the grades by which the worthy are honored.
entries.literal: The distinct styles of the Loyal Serenity crown and dress mark grades for honoring the worthy.

entries.zh: 保和冠服之異式，親親之殺也。
entries.en: The distinct styles of the Preservation-and-Harmony crown and dress mark the degrees by which kinship is differentiated.
entries.literal: The distinct styles of the Preservation-and-Harmony crown and dress mark degrees within kinship.

entries.zh: 等殺既明，庶幾乎禮之所保，保斯和，和斯安，此錫名之義也。
entries.en: Once grades and degrees are clear, ritual may be preserved; preservation yields harmony, and harmony yields tranquility—this is the meaning of the name bestowed.
entries.literal: Once grades and degrees are clear, ritual may be preserved; preservation yields harmony, and harmony yields tranquility—this is the meaning of the bestowed name.

entries.zh: 其以圖說頒示諸王府，如敕遵行。」
entries.en: Issue the illustrated explanation to all princely establishments and have them obey it as by imperial command."
entries.literal: Issue the illustrated explanation to all princely establishments and have them obey as by imperial command."

entries.zh: 保和冠制，以燕弁為準，用九𧚥，去簪與五玉，後山一扇，分畫為四。
entries.en: The Preservation-and-Harmony cap followed the Casual Court Cap, with nine pleats; the hairpins and five jades were removed; the rear mountain was a single panel divided into four sections.
entries.literal: Regulations for the Preservation-and-Harmony cap: following the Casual Court Cap, with nine pleats; hairpins and the five jades removed; the rear mountain a single panel divided into four sections.

entries.zh: 服，青質青緣，前後方龍補，身用素地，邊用云。
entries.en: The robe was green with green edging, square dragon patches front and back, a plain ground on the body, and cloud motifs on the border.
entries.literal: The robe was green with green edging; square dragon patches front and back; the body used a plain ground and the border cloud motifs.

entries.zh: 襯用深衣，玉色。
entries.en: The lining followed the deep-garment cut and was jade in color.
entries.literal: The lining followed the deep-garment cut, jade in color.

entries.zh: 帶青表綠裡綠緣。
entries.en: The belt was green outside and within, with green edging.
entries.literal: The belt was green outside, green inside, with green edging.

entries.zh: 履用皁綠結，白襪。
entries.en: Shoes were black with green knots, and stockings were white.
entries.literal: Shoes were black with green knots; white stockings.

entries.zh: 皇帝冕服 后妃冠服 皇太子親王以下冠服
entries.en: Imperial sacrificial robes and crowns; crowns and dress for empresses and consorts; crowns and dress for the crown prince, princes, and those of lower rank
entries.literal: Emperor's Court Robes and Crown; Empress and Consorts' Crowns and Robes; Crown Prince, Princes, and Those Below — Crowns and Robes

entries.zh: 太祖籍天下戶口，置戶帖、戶籍，具書名、歲、居地。
entries.en: The Hongwu Emperor registered households empire-wide, issuing household slips and registers that recorded each person's name, age, and place of residence.
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor registered the empire's households, establishing household certificates and registers, fully recording name, age, and place of residence.

entries.zh: 籍上戶部，帖給之民。
entries.en: Registers were filed with the Ministry of Revenue, and slips were distributed to each household.
entries.literal: The registers were submitted to the Ministry of Revenue, and certificates were issued to the people.

entries.zh: 有司歲計其登耗以聞。
entries.en: Each year local officials tallied gains and losses in population and reported upward.
entries.literal: Each year local officials calculated increases and decreases and reported them.

entries.zh: 及郊祀，中書省以戶籍陳壇下，薦之天，祭畢而藏之。
entries.en: At suburban sacrifices, the Secretariat placed the household registers before the altar, presented them to Heaven, and after the ceremony put them in storage.
entries.literal: At suburban sacrifices, the Secretariat of State presented the household registers before the altar, offered them to Heaven, and after the rite stored them away.

entries.zh: 洪武十四年詔天下編賦役黃冊，以一百十戶為一里，推丁糧多者十戶為長，餘百戶為十甲，甲凡十人。
entries.en: In Hongwu 14 (1381) an edict ordered compilation of yellow registers for tax and labor service empire-wide: one hundred and ten households formed a li; the ten households with the heaviest adult-male and grain-tax burden became leaders, and the remaining hundred households were divided into ten jia of ten persons each.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu an edict ordered the empire to compile yellow registers for tax and corvée, taking one hundred and ten households as one li; the ten households with the most adult males and grain tax were made leaders, and the remaining hundred households formed ten jia of ten persons each.

entries.zh: 歲役裏長一人，甲首一人，董一里一甲之事。
entries.en: Each year one li chief and one jia head were called up for duty to oversee the affairs of their li and jia.
entries.literal: Each year one li chief and one jia head were levied for service, supervising the affairs of one li and one jia.

entries.zh: 先後以丁糧多寡為序，凡十年一週，曰排年。
entries.en: Duty rotated in order of adult-male and grain-tax burden, completing a full cycle every ten years — the pai-nian rotation.
entries.literal: Order was determined by the amount of adult males and grain tax, with a full cycle every ten years, called the rotation of years.

entries.zh: 在城曰坊，近城曰廂，鄉都曰裏。
entries.en: Urban units were called fang, suburban ones xiang, and rural districts li.
entries.literal: Within cities they were called fang; near cities, xiang; in rural districts, li.

entries.zh: 裏編為冊，冊首總為一圖。
entries.en: Each li was entered in a register, and the head of each register bore a summary chart for the whole district.
entries.literal: Each li was compiled into a register, and the registers for a district were summarized in one chart.

entries.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不任役者，附十甲後為畸零。
entries.en: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who could not perform labor service were listed after the ten jia as marginal (jiling) households.
entries.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless who could not bear corvée were attached after the ten jia as marginal households.

entries.zh: 僧道給度牒，有田者編冊如民科，無田者亦為畸零。
entries.en: Monks and Daoist priests received ordination certificates; those who held land were registered and taxed like commoners, while landless clergy were also counted as marginal households.
entries.literal: Monks and Daoists were issued ordination certificates; those with land were entered in registers like commoners for taxation, those without land were also classed as marginal.

entries.zh: 每十年有司更定其冊，以丁糧增減而升降之。
entries.en: Every ten years local officials revised the registers, adjusting household rank up or down as adult-male and grain-tax obligations rose or fell.
entries.literal: Every ten years local officials revised the registers, promoting or demoting households according to increases or decreases in adult males and grain tax.

entries.zh: 冊凡四：一上戶部，其三則布政司、府、縣各存一焉。
entries.en: Each register existed in four copies: one sent to the Ministry of Revenue, and one each retained by the provincial administration commission, the prefecture, and the county.
entries.literal: There were four copies of each register: one submitted to the Ministry of Revenue, and the other three kept respectively by the provincial administration commission, prefecture, and county.

entries.zh: 上戶部者，冊面黃紙，故謂之黃冊。
entries.en: The copy filed with the Ministry of Revenue used yellow paper for its cover — hence the name yellow register (huangce).
entries.literal: The copy sent to the Ministry of Revenue had yellow paper on its cover, hence it was called the yellow register.

entries.zh: 年終進呈，送後湖東西二庫庋藏之。
entries.en: At year's end they were submitted and deposited in the eastern and western archives at Rear Lake.
entries.literal: At year's end they were presented and sent to the eastern and western storehouses at Rear Lake for storage.

entries.zh: 歲命戶科給事中一人、御史二人、戶部主事四人釐校訛舛。
entries.en: Each year one supervising secretary from the revenue section of the Secretariat, two censors, and four Ministry of Revenue principal secretaries were assigned to audit and correct discrepancies.
entries.literal: Each year one supervising secretary of the revenue section, two censors, and four principal secretaries of the Ministry of Revenue were ordered to check and correct errors.

entries.zh: 其後黃冊只具文，有司徵稅、編徭，則自為一冊，曰白冊云。
entries.en: In time the yellow register became a dead letter; for actual tax collection and corvée assignment local officials kept a separate working register known as the white register (baice).
entries.literal: Later the yellow register became a mere formality; when local officials collected taxes and arranged corvée, they compiled their own register, called the white register.

entries.zh: 《記》曰：「取財於地，而取法於天。
entries.en: The Record states: "Draw wealth from the land, and take Heaven as your model.
entries.literal: The Record says: "Obtain wealth from the earth, and take one's model from Heaven.

entries.zh: 富國之本，在於農桑。」
entries.en: The foundation of a wealthy state lies in farming and silk production."
entries.literal: The foundation of enriching the state lies in agriculture and sericulture."

entries.zh: 明初，沿元之舊，錢法不通而用鈔，又禁民間以銀交易，宜若不便於民。
entries.en: In the early Ming, following Yuan precedent, coin did not circulate and paper money was used instead; private silver transactions were also banned — measures that would seem to burden the populace.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, following Yuan practice, coinage did not circulate and paper notes were used instead; private trade in silver was also forbidden — which would seem inconvenient for the people.

entries.zh: 而洪、永、熙、宣之際，百姓充實，府藏衍溢。
entries.en: Yet under the Hongwu, Yongle, Hongxi, and Xuande emperors, the common people prospered and government storehouses brimmed with surplus.
entries.literal: Yet during the Hongwu, Yongle, Hongxi, and Xuande reigns, the people were well provided for and the treasury overflowed.

entries.zh: 蓋是時，劭農務墾闢，土無萊蕪，人敦本業，又開屯田、中鹽以給邊軍，餫餉不仰藉於縣官，故上下交足，軍民胥裕。
entries.en: In those years the state vigorously promoted farming and opened new land. Fields did not lie fallow, and people kept to agriculture. Military colonies and the salt-exchange system provisioned the frontier armies without drawing transport and supplies from the government, so court and country had enough and soldiers and civilians alike prospered.
entries.literal: For at that time agriculture was vigorously encouraged and wasteland reclaimed; no land lay fallow, and the people devoted themselves to their primary occupations. Military colonies and the salt-exchange system were also established to provision the frontier armies, so transport and supplies did not have to rely on the government. Thus both high and low had enough, and soldiers and civilians alike prospered.

entries.zh: 其後，屯田壞於豪強之兼併，計臣變鹽法。
entries.en: Later, military colonies were destroyed through land grabs by powerful magnates, and planning ministers revised the salt regulations.
entries.literal: Later, military colonies were ruined by powerful families' encroachments, and finance officials altered the salt laws.

entries.zh: 於是邊兵悉仰食太倉，轉輸住往不給。
entries.en: Border soldiers then came to depend entirely on the central granary, and supply convoys often failed to meet demand.
entries.literal: Thereupon border troops all relied on food from the Grand Storehouse, and transport often could not keep up.

entries.zh: 世宗以後，耗財之道廣，府庫匱竭。
entries.en: After the Jiajing reign, avenues of spending multiplied and the public coffers ran dry.
entries.literal: After the Jiajing Emperor, channels of expenditure multiplied and the treasury was exhausted.

entries.zh: 神宗乃加賦重徵，礦稅四出，移正供以實左藏。
entries.en: The Wanli Emperor responded with heavier assessments and surcharges; mining taxes sprang up on all sides, and regular revenue streams were diverted to fill the left-hand vault.
entries.literal: The Shenzong Emperor then added levies and imposed heavy taxes; mining levies were levied everywhere, and regular tribute was diverted to fill the left treasury.

entries.zh: 中涓羣小，橫斂侵漁。
entries.en: Palace eunuchs and their petty hangers-on levied at will and preyed on the people.
entries.literal: Eunuchs and petty minions exacted at will and plundered.

entries.zh: 民多逐末，田卒汙萊。
entries.en: The people turned increasingly to commerce, and farmland in the end lay fallow and overgrown.
entries.literal: Many people pursued secondary trades, and fields in the end became wasteland.

entries.zh: 吏不能拊循，而覆侵刻之。
entries.en: Officials failed to soothe and guide them, and instead added fresh exactions.
entries.literal: Officials could not comfort and guide them, but instead compounded extortion.

entries.zh: 海內困敝，而儲積益以空乏。
entries.en: The realm fell into distress, even as stored grain and coin grew ever emptier.
entries.literal: The empire grew impoverished, while reserves became ever more depleted.

entries.zh: 昧者多言復通鈔法可以富國，不知國初之充裕在勤農桑，而不在行鈔法也。
entries.en: The misguided often argued that reviving paper currency would enrich the state, unaware that early Ming prosperity came from diligent agriculture and silk production, not from banknote policy.
entries.literal: The ignorant often said that restoring paper money could enrich the state, not knowing that early-Ming abundance lay in diligence in farming and sericulture, not in using paper notes.

entries.zh: 夫韁本節用，為理財之要。
entries.en: Strengthening the economic base and practicing frugality are the heart of sound fiscal policy.
entries.literal: Strengthening the fundamental root and economizing expenditure are the essentials of managing finances.

entries.zh: 明一代理財之道，始所以得，終所以失，條其本末，著於篇。
entries.en: The Ming approach to state finance — how it first prospered and at last failed — is traced here from beginning to end in this chapter.
entries.literal: This treatise sets out the Ming dynasty's approach to state finance from beginning to end: why it succeeded at first and why it ultimately failed.

entries.zh: 其移徙者，明初，當徙蘇、鬆、嘉、湖、杭民之無田者四千餘戶，往耕臨濠，給牛、種、車、糧，以資遣之，三年不徵其稅。
entries.en: For state resettlement, early Ming authorities moved more than four thousand landless households from Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Hangzhou to farm at Linhao, supplying oxen, seed, carts, and travel grain, with a three-year tax exemption.
entries.literal: As for state resettlement, in early Ming more than four thousand landless households from Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Hangzhou were moved to farm at Linhao; they were given oxen, seed, carts, and grain for their journey, and were exempt from taxes for three years.

entries.zh: 徐達平沙漠，徙北平山後民三萬五千八百餘戶，散處諸府衛，籍為軍者給衣糧，民給田。
entries.en: After Xu Da pacified the northern steppe, he resettled more than thirty-five thousand eight hundred households from beyond the Yan mountains across Beiping prefectures and guards; military registrants received clothing and rations, civilians received farmland.
entries.literal: When Xu Da pacified the desert, he moved more than thirty-five thousand eight hundred households from north of the Yan mountains to Beiping, dispersing them among various prefectures and guards; those registered as military were given clothing and grain, commoners were given land.

entries.zh: 又以沙漠遺民三萬二千八百餘戶屯田北平，置屯二百五十四，開地千三百四十三頃。
entries.en: He also settled more than thirty-two thousand eight hundred steppe remnant households in Beiping military colonies — two hundred fifty-four colonies opening one thousand three hundred forty-three qing of land.
entries.literal: He also settled more than thirty-two thousand eight hundred desert remnant households in military colonies in Beiping, establishing two hundred fifty-four colonies and opening one thousand three hundred forty-three qing of land.

entries.zh: 復徙江南民十四萬於鳳陽。
entries.en: He further resettled one hundred forty thousand people from the lower Yangtze region at Fengyang.
entries.literal: He further moved one hundred forty thousand Jiangnan people to Fengyang.

entries.zh: 戶部郎中劉九皋言：「古狹鄉之民，聽遷之寬鄉，欲地無遺利，人無失業也。」
entries.en: Liu Jiugao, a director in the Ministry of Revenue, said: "In antiquity people from overcrowded districts were allowed to move to underpopulated ones, so that no land went unused and no one lacked a livelihood."
entries.literal: Liu Jiugao, director in the Ministry of Revenue, said: "In antiquity people from crowded districts were permitted to move to spacious ones, so that no land would lie unused and no person be without occupation."

entries.zh: 太祖採其議，遷山西澤、潞民於河北。
entries.en: The Hongwu Emperor adopted the proposal and resettled people from Shanxi's Ze and Lu prefectures in Hebei.
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor adopted his proposal and moved the people of Ze and Lu to Hebei.

entries.zh: 眾屢徙浙西及山西民於滁、和、北平、山東、河南。
entries.en: He repeatedly resettled people from western Zhejiang and Shanxi to Chu, He, Beiping, Shandong, and Henan.
entries.literal: Repeatedly he moved people from western Zhejiang and Shanxi to Chu, He, Beiping, Shandong, and Henan.

entries.zh: 又徙登、萊、青民於東昌、兗州。
entries.en: He also moved people from Deng, Lai, and Qing prefectures to Dongchang and Yanzhou.
entries.literal: He also moved people from Deng, Lai, and Qing to Dongchang and Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 又徙直隸、浙江民二萬戶於京師，充倉腳夫。
entries.en: He also moved twenty thousand households from Zhili and Zhejiang to the capital as granary porters.
entries.literal: He also moved twenty thousand households from Zhili and Zhejiang to the capital to serve as granary porters.

entries.zh: 太祖時徙民最多，其間有以罪徙者。
entries.en: Resettlement peaked under the Hongwu Emperor; some deportees were criminals exiled as punishment.
entries.literal: Resettlement was greatest under the Taizu Emperor; among those moved, some were banished for crimes.

entries.zh: 建文帝命武康伯徐理往北平度地處之。
entries.en: The Jianwen Emperor sent Marquis of Wukang Xu Li to Beiping to survey land and arrange resettlement.
entries.literal: The Jianwen Emperor ordered Marquis of Wukang Xu Li to go to Beiping to survey land and settle people.

entries.zh: 成祖核太原、平陽、澤、潞、遼、沁、汾丁多田少及無田之家，分其丁口以實北平。
entries.en: The Yongle Emperor audited households in Taiyuan, Pingyang, Ze, Lu, Liao, Qin, and Fen with many adult males but little or no land, and redistributed their members to populate Beiping.
entries.literal: The Chengzu Emperor audited households in Taiyuan, Pingyang, Ze, Lu, Liao, Qin, and Fen with many adult males but little land or no land at all, and distributed their persons to populate Beiping.

entries.zh: 自是以後，移徙者鮮矣。
entries.en: After that, large-scale state resettlement became rare.
entries.literal: After this, state resettlement became rare.

entries.zh: 初，太祖設養濟院收無告者，月給糧。
entries.en: Early on the Hongwu Emperor established relief hospices for those with no one to support them, issuing monthly grain rations.
entries.literal: At first the Taizu Emperor established relief hospices to take in those with no one to care for them, granting grain each month.

entries.zh: 設漏澤園葬貧民。
entries.en: He established public burial grounds (louzeyuan) for the poor.
entries.literal: He established public burial grounds to inter the poor.

entries.zh: 天下府州縣立義塚。
entries.en: Charitable burial grounds were established in prefectures and counties empire-wide.
entries.literal: Charitable burial grounds were established in prefectures, departments, and counties throughout the empire.

entries.zh: 又行養老之政，民年八十以上賜爵。
entries.en: He also enacted policies honoring the elderly, granting noble ranks to commoners aged eighty or above.
entries.literal: He also implemented policies to support the aged, granting noble ranks to commoners eighty years of age or older.

entries.zh: 復下詔優恤遭難兵民。
entries.en: He further issued edicts granting special relief to soldiers and civilians who had suffered wartime hardship.
entries.literal: He further issued edicts granting favorable relief to soldiers and civilians who had suffered hardship.

entries.zh: 然懲元末豪強侮貧弱，立法多右貧抑富。
entries.en: Yet to punish late-Yuan magnates who had bullied the poor, legislation often favored the poor and restrained the wealthy.
entries.literal: Yet to punish the powerful families of late Yuan who had bullied the poor and weak, legislation often favored the poor and restrained the rich.

entries.zh: 嘗命戶部籍浙江等九布政司、應天十八府州富民萬四千三百餘戶，以次召見，徙其家以實京師，謂之富戶。
entries.en: He once ordered the Ministry of Revenue to register more than fourteen thousand three hundred wealthy households from nine provinces including Zhejiang and from eighteen Yingtian prefectures; summoned in turn, their families were moved to the capital — the so-called wealthy households (fuhu).
entries.literal: He once ordered the Ministry of Revenue to register more than fourteen thousand three hundred wealthy households from nine provincial administration commissions including Zhejiang and eighteen prefectures and departments of Yingtian; they were summoned in turn and their families moved to populate the capital — called wealthy households.

entries.zh: 成祖時，復選應天、浙江富民三千戶，充北京宛、大二縣廂長，附籍京師，仍應本籍徭役。
entries.en: Under the Yongle Emperor, three thousand wealthy households from Yingtian and Zhejiang were again selected as ward chiefs for Wan and Da counties in Beijing, registering in the capital while still liable for corvée at home.
entries.literal: Under the Chengzu Emperor, three thousand wealthy households from Yingtian and Zhejiang were again selected to serve as ward chiefs of Wan and Da counties in Beijing, attaching their registers to the capital while still bearing corvée in their home districts.

entries.zh: 供給日久，貧乏逃竄，輒選其本籍殷實戶僉補。
entries.en: Over time many were ruined and fled; wealthy households from their home districts were then conscripted to replace them.
entries.literal: As supplies continued over time, impoverishment and flight occurred, and wealthy households from their home districts were conscripted to fill the vacancies.

entries.zh: 宣德間定制，逃者發邊充軍，官司鄰裏隱匿者俱坐罪。
entries.en: Under Xuande rules, fugitives were banished to frontier military service, and officials or neighbors who concealed them were punished.
entries.literal: In the Xuande reign regulations were fixed: fugitives were sent to the border as soldiers, and officials and neighbors who concealed them were all punished.

entries.zh: 弘治五年始免解在逃富戶，每戶徵銀三兩，與廂民助役。
entries.en: In Hongzhi 5 (1492) the state stopped forcibly returning fugitive wealthy households; each household instead paid three taels of silver to help ward residents meet labor obligations.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi the practice of escorting fugitive wealthy households back began to be waived; each household paid three taels of silver to assist ward residents in corvée.

entries.zh: 嘉靖中減為二兩，以充邊餉。
entries.en: Under the Jiajing Emperor the levy was reduced to two taels, earmarked for frontier supplies.
entries.literal: In the Jiajing reign it was reduced to two taels, applied to border supplies.

entries.zh: 太祖立法之意，本仿漢徙富民實關中之制，其後事久弊生，遂為厲階。
entries.en: The Hongwu Emperor's policy imitated the Han practice of resettling wealthy households to populate Guanzhong; in time abuses accumulated until it became a source of widespread harm.
entries.literal: The Taizu Emperor's intent in legislating was originally to imitate the Han practice of moving wealthy households to populate Guanzhong; later, as time passed abuses arose, and it became a source of harm.

entries.zh: 戶口之數，增減不一，其可考者，洪武二十六年，天下戶一千六十五萬二千八百七十，口六千五十四萬五千八百十二。
entries.en: Population figures fluctuated unevenly; where records survive, in Hongwu 26 (1393) the empire registered 10,652,870 households and 60,545,812 persons.
entries.literal: Household and population figures rose and fell unevenly; where records survive, in the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu the empire had ten million six hundred fifty-two thousand eight hundred seventy households and sixty million five hundred forty-five thousand eight hundred twelve persons.

entries.zh: 弘治四年，戶九百十一萬三千四百四十六，口五千三百二十八萬一千一百五十八。
entries.en: In Hongzhi 4 (1491) there were 9,113,446 households and 53,281,158 persons.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi there were nine million one hundred thirteen thousand four hundred forty-six households and fifty-three million two hundred eighty-one thousand one hundred fifty-eight persons.

entries.zh: 萬曆六年，戶一千六十二萬一千四百三十六，口六千六十九萬二千八百五十六。
entries.en: In Wanli 6 (1578) there were 10,621,436 households and 60,692,856 persons.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli there were ten million six hundred twenty-one thousand four hundred thirty-six households and sixty million six hundred ninety-two thousand eight hundred fifty-six persons.

entries.zh: 太祖當兵燹之後，戶口顧極盛。
entries.en: Remarkably, under the Hongwu Emperor — right after the devastation of war — registered population was at its peak.
entries.literal: Under the Taizu Emperor, coming after the ravages of war, the population was nevertheless extremely large.

entries.zh: 其後承平日久，反不及焉。
entries.en: Later, after long years of peace, the count actually fell short of that peak.
entries.literal: Later, after long years of peace, it fell short of that level instead.

entries.zh: 靖難兵起，淮以北鞠為茂草，其時民數反增於前。
entries.en: When the Jingnan civil war broke out, the land north of the Huai was laid waste, yet registered population actually rose above the previous count.
entries.literal: When the Jingnan campaign erupted, north of the Huai turned to wild grass, yet at that time the population count actually increased over the previous figure.

entries.zh: 後乃遞減，至天順間為最衰。
entries.en: Thereafter it declined steadily, hitting its lowest point under the Tianshun Emperor.
entries.literal: Afterward it declined in succession, reaching its lowest point in the Tianshun reign.

entries.zh: 成、弘繼盛，正德以後又減。
entries.en: The Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns saw recovery, but after the Zhengde Emperor numbers fell again.
entries.literal: The Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns saw renewed prosperity, but after Zhengde it declined again.

entries.zh: 戶口所以減者，周忱謂：「投倚於豪門，或冒匠竄兩京，或冒引賈四方，舉家舟居，莫可蹤跡也。」
entries.en: Zhou Chen explained the decline: "People attached themselves to powerful households, falsely registered as artisans and hid in the two capitals, or falsely registered as merchants and roamed the empire — whole families living on boats, beyond any official trace."
entries.literal: The reason population declined, Zhou Chen said, was: "They threw themselves on powerful families' protection, or falsely registered as artisans and hid in the two capitals, or falsely registered as merchants and traveled the four quarters; whole families lived on boats with no trace to be found."

entries.zh: 而要之，戶口增減，由於政令張弛。
entries.en: In the end, population rises and falls reflected whether government enforcement was strict or lax.
entries.literal: In sum, increases and decreases in population depended on whether government orders were strict or lax.

entries.zh: 故宣宗嘗與羣臣論歷代戶口，以為「其盛也，本於休養生息，其衰也，由土木兵戎」，殆篤論云。
entries.en: The Xuande Emperor once discussed historical population trends with his ministers, holding that "when flourishing, it rested on nourishing life and letting the people rest; when declining, it was due to civil construction and warfare" — a judgment that rings true.
entries.literal: Therefore the Xuande Emperor once discussed with his ministers the household registers of successive dynasties, holding that "when flourishing, it rested on nourishing life and letting the people rest; when declining, it was due to civil construction projects and warfare" — this was indeed a sound judgment.

entries.zh: 又更定屯守之數。
entries.en: Garrison-farm ratios were also revised.
entries.literal: Colony garrison numbers were also re-fixed.

entries.zh: 臨邊險要，守多於屯。
entries.en: At critical border posts, more troops garrisoned than farmed.
entries.literal: Along dangerous border points, garrisoning exceeded colonies.

entries.zh: 地僻處及輸糧艱者，屯多於守，屯兵百名委百戶，三百名委千戶，五百名以上指揮提督之。
entries.en: Remote posts with difficult supply lines assigned more farmers than garrison soldiers, with centurions commanding 100 colonists, chiliarchs 300, and commanders supervising 500 or more.
entries.literal: In remote places and where grain transport was difficult, colonies exceeded garrisoning; one hundred colony soldiers were entrusted to a centurion, three hundred to a chiliarch, five hundred or more to a commander as supervisor.

entries.zh: 屯設紅牌，列則例於上。
entries.en: Each colony posted red placards listing regulations.
entries.literal: Colonies set up red placards, listing regulations and precedents upon them.

entries.zh: 年六十與殘疾及幼者，耕以自食，不限於例。
entries.en: Soldiers over sixty, disabled, or too young farmed for subsistence without quota restrictions.
entries.literal: Those sixty years of age, disabled, and the young — farming to feed themselves — were not limited by regulation.

entries.zh: 屯軍以公事妨農務者，免徵子粒，且禁衛所差撥。
entries.en: Colonists diverted from farming by official duties were exempted from grain levies, and arbitrary guard requisitions were banned.
entries.literal: Colony soldiers whose public duties obstructed farm work were exempt from grain levy, and guard-post requisitioning was forbidden.

entries.zh: 於時，東自遼左，北抵宣、大，西至甘肅，南盡滇、蜀，極於交阯，中原則大河南北，在在興屯矣。
entries.en: Colonies stretched from Liaodong west to Gansu, south through Yunnan and Sichuan to Jiaozhi, and across central China — garrison farming flourished empire-wide.
entries.literal: At this time, east from Liaodong left, north reaching Xuanfu and Datong, west to Gansu, south through Yunnan and Sichuan to the limit of Jiaozhi, in the central plain then north and south of the Great River — everywhere colonies flourished.

entries.zh: 宣宗之世，屢核各屯，以征戍罷耕及官豪勢要佔匿者，減餘糧之半。
entries.en: Xuande repeatedly audited colonies, halving surplus-grain quotas where campaigns interrupted farming or elites had seized land.
entries.literal: In the Xuande reign, colonies were repeatedly audited; those where campaigns halted farming and official, powerful, and influential persons concealed holdings had surplus grain reduced by half.

entries.zh: 迤北來歸就屯之人，給車牛農器。
entries.en: Tribal peoples submitting from the northern frontier received carts, cattle, and tools.
entries.literal: People coming from the far north to submit and join colonies were given carts, oxen, and farm implements.

entries.zh: 分遼東各衛屯軍為三等，丁牛兼者為上，丁牛有一為中，俱無者為下。
entries.en: Liaodong colonies ranked soldiers by resources: top grade had both labor and oxen, middle had one, bottom had neither.
entries.literal: Colony soldiers of various guards in Liaodong were divided into three grades: those with both adult males and oxen were upper; with one of the two, middle; with neither, lower.

entries.zh: 英宗免軍田正糧歸倉，止徵餘糧六石。
entries.en: Yingzong waived principal-grain deposits to colony granaries, taxing only the six-shi surplus quota.
entries.literal: Yingzong remitted principal grain of military fields returning to granaries; only surplus grain of six shi was levied.

entries.zh: 後又免沿邊開田官軍子粒，減各邊屯田子粒有差。
entries.en: Later he exempted frontier reclaimed land from levies and reduced border colony taxes variably.
entries.literal: Later he also remitted grain levy on frontier opened fields for officers and soldiers, reducing colony grain levies on each frontier with differences.

entries.zh: 景帝時，邊方多事，令兵分為兩番，六日操守，六日耕種。
entries.en: During Jingtai's reign frontier turmoil required alternating six-day garrison and six-day farming shifts.
entries.literal: In Jingdi's time the frontier had many affairs; he ordered troops divided into two shifts — six days on guard, six days farming.

entries.zh: 成化初，宣府巡撫葉盛買官牛千八百，並置農具，遣軍屯田，收糧易銀，以補官馬耗損，邊入稱便。
entries.en: In 1465 Xuanfu coordinator Ye Sheng purchased 1,800 oxen and tools for garrison farming, converting grain to silver for cavalry maintenance — a welcomed frontier reform.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, Xuanfu grand coordinator Ye Sheng bought one thousand eight hundred official oxen and also provided farm tools, dispatched troops to colony farm, collected grain exchanged for silver to supplement official horse losses — border people called it convenient.

entries.zh: 明年，清復言：「東南漕舟，水淺弗能進。
entries.en: The next year Liu Qing spoke again: "The grain ships from the southeast cannot advance because the water is too shallow.
entries.literal: Next year, Qing again said: "Southeast grain transport boats, water shallow cannot advance.

entries.zh: 請自滎澤入沁河，浚岡頭百二十里以通衛河。
entries.en: I ask that they enter the Qin from Xingze, dredge one hundred and twenty li at Gangtou to link with the Wei River.
entries.literal: Request from Xingze enter Qin River, dredge Gangtou one hundred twenty li to connect Wei River.

entries.zh: 且張秋之決，由沁合黃，勢遂奔急。
entries.en: Moreover, the breach at Zhangqiu came from the Qin joining the Yellow River, and the current became swift and violent.
entries.literal: Moreover Zhangqiu's breach, because Qin joined Yellow, momentum then rushed urgent.

entries.zh: 若引沁入衛，則張秋無患。」
entries.en: If the Qin were led into the Wei, Zhangqiu would be spared further trouble."
entries.literal: If lead Qin enter Wei, then Zhangqiu no worry."

entries.zh: 行人王晏亦言：「開岡頭置閘，分沁水，使南入黃，北達衛。
entries.en: Courier Wang Yan also said: "Open Gangtou and install locks to divide the Qin so that one branch flows south into the Yellow River and another north to the Wei.
entries.literal: Courier Wang Yan also said: "Open Gangtou place locks, divide Qin water, make south enter Yellow, north reach Wei.

entries.zh: 遇漲則閉閘，漕可永無患。」
entries.en: When the waters rise, close the locks, and the grain transport will never again be in danger."
entries.literal: Encounter flood then close locks, grain transport can forever no worry."

entries.zh: 並下督漕都御史王竑等核實以聞。
entries.en: Both proposals were forwarded to Wang Hong, the supervising censor-in-chief of grain transport, and others for verification and report.
entries.literal: Both sent down to grain transport supervising censor-in-chief Wang Hong and others verify facts to report.

entries.zh: 明年，給事中何升言：「沁河有漏港已成河。
entries.en: The next year, Supervising Secretary He Sheng said: "On the Qin there is a leaking port that has already formed a full channel.
entries.literal: Next year, supervising secretary He Sheng said: "Qin River has leaking harbor already become river.

entries.zh: 臨清屯聚膠淺之舟，宜使從此入黃，度二旬可達淮。」
entries.en: The boats stalled in shallow water at Linqing should be sent through it into the Yellow River; in about twenty days they could reach the Huai."
entries.literal: Linqing gathered stuck shallow boats, should make them from here enter Yellow, estimate twenty days can reach Huai."

entries.zh: 詔竑及都御史徐有貞閱之。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Wang Hong and Censor-in-Chief Xu Youzhen to inspect the site.
entries.literal: Edict Wang Hong and censor-in-chief Xu Youzhen inspect it.

entries.zh: 既而罷引沁河議。
entries.en: Soon afterward the plan to divert the Qin was dropped.
entries.literal: Soon after abandoned draw Qin River proposal.

entries.zh: 初，王晏請漕沁，有司多言弗利。
entries.en: At first, when Wang Yan proposed using the Qin for grain transport, many local officers said it would not pay.
entries.literal: Initially, Wang Yan requested grain transport Qin, responsible officials many spoke not advantageous.

entries.zh: 晏固爭。
entries.en: Wang Yan pressed his case stubbornly.
entries.literal: Yan firmly contended.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書王直請遣官行河，命侍郎趙榮同晏往。
entries.en: Minister Wang Zhi of the Ministry of Personnel asked that officials be sent to survey the river, and Vice Minister Zhao Rong was ordered to go with Wang Yan.
entries.literal: Ministry of Personnel Minister Wang Zhi requested send officials travel river, ordered Vice Minister Zhao Rong together with Yan go.

entries.zh: 榮亦言不利，議乃寢。
entries.en: Zhao Rong also reported that it would not work, and the plan was shelved.
entries.literal: Rong also spoke not advantageous, proposal then shelved.

entries.zh: 天順八年，都察院都事金景輝復請浚陳橋集古河，分引沁水，北通長垣、曹州、鉅野，以達漕河。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Tianshun, Clerk Jin Jinghui of the Censorate again asked to dredge the Jigu River at Chenqiao, divide off part of the Qin, link it north through Changyuan, Caozhou, and Juye to the grain-transport canal.
entries.literal: Tianshun eighth year, Censorate clerk Jin Jinghui again requested dredge Chenqiao Jigu River, divide draw Qin water, north connect Changyuan, Caozhou, Juye, to reach grain transport river.

entries.zh: 詔按實以聞，未能行也。
entries.en: An edict ordered verification and report, but it could not be carried out.
entries.literal: Edict verify facts to report, unable carry out also.

entries.zh: 淮河泇河衛河漳河沁河滹沱河桑乾河膠萊河
entries.en: The Huai River; the Jia River; the Wei River; the Zhang River; the Qin River; the Hutuo River; the Sanggan River; the Jiao-Lai River.
entries.literal: Huai River, Jia River, Wei River, Zhang River, Qin River, Hutuo River, Sanggan River, Jiao-Lai River.

entries.zh: 興宗孝康皇帝標，太祖長子也。
entries.en: Zhu Biao, posthumously honored as Emperor Xingzong Xiaokang, was Hongwu's eldest son.
entries.literal: Emperor Xingzong Xiaokang, Biao, was the eldest son of Taizu.

entries.zh: 母高皇后。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Gao.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Gao.

entries.zh: 元至正十五年生於太平陳迪家。
entries.en: He was born in 1355 at the home of Chen Di in Taiping.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng of Yuan he was born at Chen Di's house in Taiping.

entries.zh: 太祖為吳王，立為王世子，從宋濂受經。
entries.en: When Hongwu was Prince of Wu, Biao was named heir to the principality and studied the classics under Song Lian.
entries.literal: When Taizu became Prince of Wu, [Biao] was installed as heir to the princely domain and studied the classics under Song Lian.

entries.zh: 吳元年，年十三矣，命省臨濠墓，諭曰：「商高宗舊勞于外，周成王早聞《無逸》之訓，皆知小民疾苦，故在位勤儉，為守成令主。
entries.en: In the first year of the Wu regime, when he was thirteen, he was sent to inspect the ancestral tombs at Fengyang. Hongwu instructed him: "The Shang High Ancestor once labored in the provinces; King Cheng of Zhou was taught the 'Against Idleness' early on—both understood the people's hardships, and so ruled diligently and frugally as successful heirs.
entries.literal: In the first year of Wu, when he was thirteen, he was ordered to inspect the tombs at Linhao, and was instructed: "The Shang High Ancestor formerly toiled abroad; King Cheng of Zhou early heard the teachings of 'Against Idleness'—both knew the hardships of the common people, and therefore were diligent and frugal on the throne, becoming excellent rulers who preserved the inheritance.

entries.zh: 兒生長富貴，習于晏安。
entries.en: You have grown up amid wealth and ease.
entries.literal: You have grown up in wealth and honor, accustomed to ease and comfort.

entries.zh: 今出旁近郡縣，遊覽山川，經歷田野，其因道途險易以知鞍馬勤勞，觀閭閻生業以知衣食艱難，察民情好惡以知風俗美惡，即祖宗所居，訪求父老，問吾起兵渡江時事，識之於心，以知吾創業不易。」
entries.en: Now travel through the neighboring prefectures and counties, see the land and its people, and learn from the roads what saddle-work costs, from village life what food and clothing require, and from local sentiment what customs are sound or corrupt. Where our forebears lived, question the elders about my crossing the Yangtze to raise the army, and fix it in your heart that founding this realm was no easy thing."
entries.literal: Now go out to the nearby commanderies and counties, tour mountains and rivers, pass through fields—thereby learn from the difficulty or ease of the roads the labor of saddle and horse, observe the livelihoods in lanes and hamlets to know the hardship of food and clothing, examine the people's likes and dislikes to know the beauty or ugliness of customs; at the places where the ancestors dwelt, seek out the elders, ask about the affairs when I raised troops and crossed the river, keep them in mind, to know that my founding the enterprise was not easy."

entries.zh: 又命中書省擇官輔行。
entries.en: He also ordered the Secretariat to choose officials to accompany him on the tour.
entries.literal: He also ordered the Secretariat to select officials to accompany the journey.

entries.zh: 凡所過郡邑城隍山川之神，皆祭以少牢。
entries.en: Wherever he passed, he offered the lesser tai-lao sacrifice to the local city-god, mountain, and river deities.
entries.literal: At every commandery and county passed through, the spirits of city walls, moats, mountains, and rivers were all sacrificed to with the lesser tai-lao offering.

entries.zh: 過太平訪迪家，賜白金五十兩。
entries.en: At Taiping he visited Chen Di's home and gave him fifty taels of silver.
entries.literal: Passing Taiping he visited Chen Di's house and bestowed fifty taels of white silver.

entries.zh: 至泗、濠告祭諸祖墓。
entries.en: He reached Sizhou and Fengyang and performed sacrifices at the ancestral graves.
entries.literal: Arriving at Si and Hao, he announced sacrifices at the ancestral tombs.

entries.zh: 是冬從太祖觀郊壇，令左右導之農家，遍觀服食器具，又指道旁荊楚曰：「古用此為撲刑，以其能去風，雖傷不殺人。
entries.en: That winter, accompanying Hongwu to the suburban sacrifice, he was led through farmhouses to see how people ate and dressed. Hongwu pointed to brambles beside the road and said: "The ancients used these for the rod because they drive off wind: they hurt but do not kill.
entries.literal: That winter, following Taizu to observe the suburban altar, [Taizu] had attendants guide him to farm households to inspect food, clothing, and utensils in full, and again pointed to brambles by the road, saying: "In antiquity this was used for flogging punishment, because it can dispel wind; though it wounds, it does not kill.

entries.zh: 古人用心仁厚如此，兒念之。」
entries.en: The ancients' hearts were this humane—keep it in mind, my son."
entries.literal: The ancients' intent was so benevolent and generous—remember this, my son."

entries.zh: 洪武元年正月，立為皇太子。
entries.en: In the first month of Hongwu's first year he was made crown prince.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Hongwu, he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 帶刀舍人周宗上書乞教太子。
entries.en: Zhou Zong, a sword-bearing attendant, memorialized asking that the crown prince receive formal instruction.
entries.literal: The sword-bearing attendant Zhou Zong submitted a memorial requesting instruction for the crown prince.

entries.zh: 帝嘉納。
entries.en: Hongwu approved the proposal.
entries.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.

entries.zh: 中書省都督府請仿元制，以太子為中書令。
entries.en: The Secretariat and the regional command asked to appoint the crown prince Secretariat Director, as under the Yuan.
entries.literal: The Secretariat and the Commissioner's Office requested, following the Yuan system, to make the crown prince Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 帝以元制不足法，令詹同考歷代東宮官制，選勳德老成及新進賢者，兼領東宮官。
entries.en: Hongwu rejected the Yuan precedent, had Zhan Tong study Eastern Palace institutions of past dynasties, and appointed both veteran meritorious officials and promising newcomers to dual posts in the heir apparent's establishment.
entries.literal: The emperor held that the Yuan system was not worth taking as model, ordered Zhan Tong to examine the Eastern Palace offices of successive dynasties, and selected men of merit and long experience together with newly advanced worthies to hold Eastern Palace posts concurrently.

entries.zh: 於是左丞相李善長兼太子少師，右丞相徐達兼太子少傅，中書平章錄軍國重事常遇春兼太子少保，右都督馮宗異兼右詹事，中書平章政事胡廷端、廖永忠、李伯升兼同知詹事院事，中書左、右丞趙庸、王溥兼副詹事，中書參政楊憲兼詹事丞，傅瓛兼詹事，同知大都督康茂才、張興祖兼左右率府使，大都督府副使顧時、孫興祖同知左右率府事，僉大都督府事吳楨、耿炳文兼左右率府副使，御史大夫鄧愈、湯和兼諭德，御史中丞劉基、章溢兼贊善大夫，治書侍御史文原吉、范顯祖兼太子賓客。
entries.en: Li Shanchang, left chancellor, became junior tutor; Xu Da, right chancellor, junior mentor; Chang Yuchun, associate director for military affairs, junior guardian; Feng Zongyi, right commissioner, right household master; Hu Tingduan, Liao Yongzhong, and Li Bosheng, associate directors, associate household masters; Zhao Yong and Wang Pu, vice directors, deputy household masters; Yang Xian, participating secretary, household master assistant; Fu Rong, household master; Kang Maocai and Zhang Xingzu, associate capital commissioners, left and right rate-office commandants; Gu Shi and Sun Xingzu, deputy commissioners, associate commandants; Wu Zhen and Geng Bingwen, commissioners, deputy commandants; Deng Yu and Tang He, censors-in-chief, preceptors; Liu Ji and Zhang Yi, vice censors-in-chief, senior companions; Wen Yuanji and Fan Xianzu, investigating secretaries, crown prince's guests.
entries.literal: Thereupon Left Chancellor Li Shanchang concurrently served as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, Right Chancellor Xu Da as Junior Mentor, Secretariat Associate Director recording military and state affairs Chang Yuchun as Junior Guardian, Right Commissioner Feng Zongyi as Right Household Master, Secretariat Associate Directors Hu Tingduan, Liao Yongzhong, and Li Bosheng as Associate Directors of the Household Master's Office, Left and Right Secretariat Vice Directors Zhao Yong and Wang Pu as Deputy Household Masters, Secretariat Participating Secretary Yang Xian as Household Master Assistant, Fu Rong as Household Master, Associate Directors of the Great Capital Commission Kang Maocai and Zhang Xingzu as Left and Right Commandants of the Rate Offices, Deputy Commissioners of the Great Capital Commission Gu Shi and Sun Xingzu as Associate Commandants of the Rate Offices, Secretariat Affairs Commissioners Wu Zhen and Geng Bingwen as Deputy Commandants of the Rate Offices, Censor-in-Chief Deng Yu and Tang He as Preceptors, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Ji and Zhang Yi as Senior Companions in Goodness, and Investigating Secretaries Wen Yuanji and Fan Xianzu as Crown Prince Guests.

entries.zh: 諭之曰：「朕於東宮不別設府僚，而以卿等兼領者，蓋軍旅未息，朕若有事於外，必太子監國。
entries.en: He told them: "I do not set up a separate Eastern Palace staff but make you serve concurrently because war is not over. If I must be away, the crown prince will govern.
entries.literal: He instructed them, saying: "I do not separately establish household staff for the Eastern Palace but have you hold posts concurrently because the army has not yet ceased; if I have business outside, the crown prince must oversee the state.

entries.zh: 若設府僚，卿等在內，事當啟聞，太子或聽斷不明，與卿等意見不合，卿等必謂府僚導之，嫌隙易生。
entries.en: Separate palace staff would mean you inside reporting upward while the heir might decide poorly and clash with you—you would blame his tutors, and mistrust would follow.
entries.literal: If household staff were set up, when you are inside and matters should be reported, the crown prince might judge unclearly and disagree with you; you would surely say the household staff guided him, and suspicion would easily arise.

entries.zh: 又所以特置賓客諭德等官者，欲輔成太子德性，且選名儒為之，職此故也。
entries.en: Guests and preceptors exist to shape the heir's character; famous scholars were chosen for that reason.
entries.literal: Moreover, the reason for specially setting guests, preceptors, and the like is to assist in completing the crown prince's moral character, and to select renowned Confucians for the post—this is the purpose.

entries.zh: 昔周公教成王克詰戎兵，召公教康王張惶六師，此居安慮危，不忘武備。
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou taught King Cheng to master arms; the Duke of Shao taught King Kang to keep the six hosts on alert—security that still remembers war.
entries.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou taught King Cheng to overcome military matters; the Duke of Shao taught King Kang to deploy the six armies in alarm—this is dwelling in peace yet considering danger, not forgetting military preparedness.

entries.zh: 蓋繼世之君，生長富貴，昵於安逸，不諳軍旅，一有緩急，罔知所措。
entries.en: Succession princes raised in luxury, unused to camps, are helpless when crisis strikes.
entries.literal: For heirs who succeed, growing up in wealth and honor, intimate with ease, unversed in military affairs—when urgency comes, they know not what to do.

entries.zh: 二公之言，其並識之。」
entries.en: Keep both dukes' lessons in mind."
entries.literal: The words of the two dukes—both of you should keep them in mind together."

entries.zh: 是年，命選國子生國琦、王璞、張傑等十餘人，侍太子讀書禁中。
entries.en: That year he chose more than ten National University students, including Guo Qi, Wang Pu, and Zhang Jie, to study with the crown prince inside the palace.
entries.literal: That year he ordered more than ten National University students such as Guo Qi, Wang Pu, and Zhang Jie selected to attend the crown prince reading in the palace.

entries.zh: 琦等入對謹身殿，儀狀明秀，應對詳雅。
entries.en: When they were presented in the Hall of Cultivating the Person, they were graceful and answered with polish.
entries.literal: When Qi and the others entered audience at the Hall of Cultivating the Person, their bearing was bright and elegant and their responses detailed and refined.

entries.zh: 帝喜，因謂殿中侍御史郭淵友等曰：「諸生於文藝習矣，然與太子處，當端其心術，不流浮靡，庶儲德亦獲裨助。」
entries.en: Hongwu was pleased and told the attendant Guo Yuanyou and others: "These students know their letters, but with the heir they must steady their minds and avoid vanity, so his stored virtue may truly gain."
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and therefore said to the palace attendant Guo Yuanyou and others: "The students are practiced in literary arts, yet in dealing with the crown prince they should rectify their minds and not drift into frivolity, so that the heir's virtue may also receive assistance."

entries.zh: 因厚賜之。
entries.en: He then gave them rich gifts.
entries.literal: He therefore rewarded them generously.

entries.zh: 未幾，以梁貞、王儀為太子賓客，秦庸、盧德明、張昌為太子諭德。
entries.en: Soon Liang Zhen and Wang Yi became the crown prince's guests, and Qin Yong, Lu Deming, and Zhang Chang his preceptors.
entries.literal: Before long, Liang Zhen and Wang Yi were made crown prince's guests, and Qin Yong, Lu Deming, and Zhang Chang crown prince's preceptors.

entries.zh: 璁、萼等既驟貴，幹進者爭以言禮希上意。
entries.en: Once Zhang Cong and Gui E were suddenly elevated, careerists competed to opine on ritual to please Jiajing.
entries.literal: After Cong, E, and the others had suddenly risen in rank, those who sought advancement vied to speak on ritual to please the emperor's mind.

entries.zh: 百戶隨全、錄事錢子勳言獻皇帝宜遷葬天壽山。
entries.en: Company commander Sui Quan and clerk Qian Zixun said the Xingxian emperor should be moved to Tianshou Mountain.
entries.literal: Company Commander Sui Quan and Clerk Qian Zixun said the Xingxian emperor should be reburied at Tianshou Mountain.

entries.zh: 禮部尚書席書議：「高皇帝不遷祖陵，太宗不遷孝陵，蓋其慎也。
entries.en: Minister of Rites Xi Shu argued: "Taizu did not relocate the ancestral mound, nor Taizong Xiaoling—such was their caution.
entries.literal: Minister of Rites Xi Shu argued: "The High Emperor did not move the ancestral tomb; Taizong did not move the Xiaoling tomb—such is their caution.

entries.zh: 小臣妄議山陵，宜罪。」
entries.en: Petty officials who rashly discuss the imperial tomb should be punished."
entries.literal: Petty officials rashly discuss the imperial tomb—they should be punished."

entries.zh: 工部尚書趙璜亦言不可。
entries.en: Minister of Works Zhao Huang also said it must not be done.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Zhao Huang also said it could not be done.

entries.zh: 乃止。
entries.en: The proposal was dropped.
entries.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.

entries.zh: 尊陵名曰顯陵。
entries.en: The imperial tomb was given the name Xianling.
entries.literal: The honored mausoleum was named Xianling.

entries.zh: 太子為人友愛。
entries.en: The crown prince was by nature loving and fraternal.
entries.literal: The crown prince was by nature loving and fraternal.

entries.zh: 秦、周諸王數有過，輒調護之，得返國。
entries.en: When the princes of Qin, Zhou, and others repeatedly offended, he would intercede for them and secure their return to their fiefs.
entries.literal: When the princes of Qin, Zhou, and others repeatedly offended, he would mediate for them and secure their return to their domains.

entries.zh: 有告晉王異謀者，太子為涕泣請，帝乃感悟。
entries.en: When someone reported treason by the Prince of Jin, the crown prince wept and pleaded for him until Hongwu was moved.
entries.literal: When someone reported that the Prince of Jin harbored treasonous designs, the crown prince wept and pleaded on his behalf, and the emperor was moved to understanding.

entries.zh: 帝初撫兄子文正、姊子李文忠及沐英等為子，高后視如己出。
entries.en: Hongwu had raised his brother's son Wen Zheng, his sister's son Li Wenzhong, and Mu Ying among others as sons; Empress Gao treated them as her own.
entries.literal: The emperor had earlier raised his elder brother's son Wen Zheng, his elder sister's son Li Wenzhong, and Mu Ying and others as sons; Empress Gao treated them as her own.

entries.zh: 帝或以事督過之，太子輒告高后為慰解，其仁慈天性然也。
entries.en: When Hongwu rebuked them, the crown prince would ask Empress Gao to soothe them—such was his benevolent nature.
entries.literal: When the emperor sometimes rebuked them over affairs, the crown prince would tell Empress Gao to comfort and reconcile them—such was his benevolent nature.

entries.zh: 太子元妃常氏，繼妃呂氏。
entries.en: His first consort was Lady Chang; his second was Lady Lü.
entries.literal: The crown prince's first consort was Lady Chang; his second consort was Lady Lü.

entries.zh: 生子五：長雄英，次建文皇帝，次允熥，次允熞，次允熙。
entries.en: He had five sons: Xiongying, then the future Jianwen emperor, then Yun Teng, Yun Jian, and Yun Xi.
entries.literal: He had five sons: the eldest Xiongying, next the Jianwen emperor, then Yun Teng, Yun Jian, and Yun Xi.

entries.zh: 建文元年追尊為孝康皇帝，廟號興宗。
entries.en: In Jianwen 1 he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaokang, with temple name Xingzong.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwen he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiaokang, with temple name Xingzong.

entries.zh: 燕王即帝位，復稱懿文皇太子。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yan took the throne, Biao was again styled Crown Prince Yiwen.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yan took the throne, [Biao] was again styled Crown Prince Yiwen.

entries.zh: 孝康皇后常氏，開平王遇春女。
entries.en: Empress Xiaokang Lady Chang was the daughter of Prince of Kaiping Chang Yuchun.
entries.literal: Empress Xiaokang Lady Chang was the daughter of Prince of Kaiping Chang Yuchun.

entries.zh: 洪武四年四月冊為皇太子妃。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Hongwu 4 she was made crown prince's consort.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Hongwu she was installed as crown prince's consort.

entries.zh: 十一年十一月薨，諡敬懿。
entries.en: She died in the eleventh month of Hongwu 11 and received the posthumous title Jingyi.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year she died; her posthumous title was Jingyi.

entries.zh: 太祖為輟朝三日。
entries.en: Hongwu suspended court for three days.
entries.literal: Taizu suspended court for three days on her account.

entries.zh: 建文元年追尊為孝康皇后。
entries.en: In Jianwen 1 she was posthumously honored as Empress Xiaokang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwen she was posthumously honored as Empress Xiaokang.

entries.zh: 永樂元年復稱敬懿皇太子妃。
entries.en: In Yongle 1 she was again styled Crown Prince's Consort Jingyi.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongle she was again styled Crown Prince's Consort Jingyi.

entries.zh: 皇太后呂氏，壽州人。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Lady Lü came from Shouzhou.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Lady Lü was a native of Shouzhou.

entries.zh: 父本，累官太常卿。
entries.en: Her father Ben rose to Minister of Ceremonial.
entries.literal: Her father Ben rose through offices to Minister of Ceremonial.

entries.zh: 惠帝即位，尊為皇太后。
entries.en: When the Jianwen emperor took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.
entries.literal: When the Huidi emperor took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 燕兵至金川門，迓太后至軍中，述不得已起兵之故。
entries.en: When the Yan army reached Jinchuan Gate, the prince met the empress dowager at the camp and explained why he had been forced to take up arms.
entries.literal: When the Yan army reached Jinchuan Gate, [the prince] met the empress dowager and brought her to the camp, explaining the unavoidable reasons for raising troops.

entries.zh: 太后還，未至，宮中已火。
entries.en: The empress dowager turned back, but before she arrived the palace was already burning.
entries.literal: The empress dowager returned, but before she arrived the palace was already ablaze.

entries.zh: 既而隨其子允熙居懿文陵。
entries.en: She then lived with her son Yun Xi at the Yiwen tomb.
entries.literal: Thereafter she followed her son Yun Xi to dwell at the Yiwen tomb.

entries.zh: 永樂元年復稱皇嫂懿文太子妃。
entries.en: In Yongle 1 she was again styled Imperial Sister-in-Law, Consort of Crown Prince Yiwen.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongle she was again styled Imperial Sister-in-Law, Consort of Crown Prince Yiwen.

entries.zh: 初，太祖冊常妃，繼冊呂妃。
entries.en: At first Hongwu invested Lady Chang as consort, then Lady Lü.
entries.literal: At first Taizu installed Lady Chang as consort, and afterward installed Lady Lü as consort.

entries.zh: 常氏薨，呂氏始獨居東宮。
entries.en: After Lady Chang died, Lady Lü alone occupied the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: When Lady Chang died, Lady Lü alone occupied the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 而其時秦王樉亦納王保保妹為妃，又以鄧愈女為配，皆前代故事所無也。
entries.en: At the same time Prince of Qin Shuang took Wang Baobao's sister as consort and Deng Yu's daughter as a secondary match—precedents unknown in earlier ages.
entries.literal: At the same time Prince of Qin Fang also took the sister of Wang Baobao as consort and matched himself with Deng Yu's daughter—precedents unknown in earlier ages.

entries.zh: 十年，令自今政事並啟太子處分，然後奏聞。
entries.en: In the tenth year he ruled that all routine business must first go to the crown prince for decision, then be reported upward.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he ordered that from then on all government affairs be first reported to the crown prince for disposition, and only afterward submitted [to the throne].

entries.zh: 諭曰：「自古創業之君，曆涉勤勞，達人情，周物理，故處事鹹當。
entries.en: He told him: "Founding emperors know hardship, human nature, and how the world works, and so judge rightly.
entries.literal: He instructed, saying: "From antiquity, founding rulers have passed through toil, understood human feelings, and comprehended the patterns of things, and therefore handled affairs all appropriately.

entries.zh: 守成之君，生長富貴，若非平昔練達，少有不謬者。
entries.en: Heirs raised in comfort, unless trained beforehand, almost always err.
entries.literal: Rulers who preserve the inheritance, growing up in wealth and honor, unless practiced in ordinary times, seldom avoid error.

entries.zh: 故吾特命爾日臨群臣，聽斷諸司啟事，以練習國政。
entries.en: That is why I order you daily to sit with ministers and decide their memorials—to practice government.
entries.literal: Therefore I specially order you daily to face the ministers and hear and decide the reports of the various offices, to practice state affairs.

entries.zh: 惟仁不失於疏暴，惟明不惑於邪佞，惟勤不溺於安逸，惟斷不牽于文法。
entries.en: Be benevolent and you will not slip into cruelty; be clear-sighted and flatterers will not deceive you; be diligent and ease will not drown you; be decisive and the code will not bind you.
entries.literal: Only with benevolence will one not fail through lax violence; only with clarity will one not be deluded by wicked flattery; only with diligence will one not drown in ease; only with decisiveness will one not be dragged by legal formalities.

entries.zh: 凡此皆心為權度。
entries.en: In all of this the heart is the standard.
entries.literal: All these take the mind as the measure.

entries.zh: 吾自有天下以來，未嘗暇逸，于諸事務惟恐毫髮失當，以負上天付託之意。
entries.en: Since taking the realm I have never rested; I fear the smallest misstep and failing Heaven's charge.
entries.literal: Since I possessed the empire I have never had leisure; in every affair I fear the slightest inappropriateness, lest I fail the trust Heaven bestowed.

entries.zh: 戴星而朝，夜分而寢，爾所親見。
entries.en: You have seen me at court before dawn and abed only after midnight.
entries.literal: Attending court by starlight, sleeping after midnight—you have seen this yourself.

entries.zh: 爾能體而行之，天下之福也。」
entries.en: If you can live by this, the realm will be fortunate."
entries.literal: If you can embody and carry this out, it will be the empire's good fortune."

entries.zh: 時令儒臣為太子講《大學衍義》。
entries.en: Confucian officials were then assigned to lecture him on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning.
entries.literal: At the time Confucian officials were ordered to lecture the crown prince on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning.

entries.zh: 二十二年，置詹事院。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year the Household Master's Office was set up.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year the Household Master's Office was established.

entries.zh: 二十四年八月，敕太子巡撫陝西。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year Hongwu ordered the crown prince to inspect Shaanxi.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year an edict ordered the crown prince to tour and pacify Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 先是，帝以應天、開封為南北京，臨濠為中都。
entries.en: Earlier Hongwu had named Nanjing and Kaifeng the southern and northern capitals and Fengyang the central capital.
entries.literal: Earlier, the emperor had taken Yingtian and Kaifeng as the southern and northern capitals and Linhao as the central capital.

entries.zh: 御史鬍子祺上書曰：「天下形勝地可都者四。
entries.en: Censor Hu Ziqi wrote: "Four places in the realm are fit to be capitals.
entries.literal: The censor Hu Ziqi submitted a memorial, saying: "In the empire there are four strategically superior places that may serve as capitals.

entries.zh: 河東地勢高，控制西北，堯嘗都之，然其地苦寒。
entries.en: The Shanxi plateau commands the northwest and Yao once ruled there, but it is bitterly cold.
entries.literal: The land east of the [Yellow] River is high in terrain and controls the northwest; Yao once made it his capital, yet the region is bitterly cold.

entries.zh: 汴梁襟帶河、淮，宋嘗都之，然其地平曠，無險可憑。
entries.en: Bianliang lies between the Yellow and Huai; the Song capitalized there, but the plain offers no natural defense.
entries.literal: Bianliang is girded by the Yellow and Huai rivers; Song once made it capital, yet its land is broad and level, with no terrain to rely on.

entries.zh: 洛陽周公卜之，周、漢遷之，然嵩、邙非有殽函、終南之阻，澗、瀍、伊、洛非有涇、渭、灞、滻之雄。
entries.en: Luoyang was divined by the Duke of Zhou and used by Zhou and Han, yet Mount Song and Mangshan are not Xiao-Han or Zhongnan, nor are the Jian, Chan, Yi, and Luo the Jing, Wei, Ba, and Chan.
entries.literal: Luoyang the Duke of Zhou divined for; Zhou and Han moved there, yet Song and Mang lack the barriers of Xiao-Han and Zhongnan, and the Jian, Chan, Yi, and Luo lack the might of the Jing, Wei, Ba, and Chan.

entries.zh: 夫據百二河山之勝，可以聳諸侯之望，舉天下莫關中若也。」
entries.en: Who holds the hundred-and-two defiles of Guanzhong commands every lord's gaze; nowhere else in the realm compares."
entries.literal: To hold the superiority of the hundred-and-two rivers and mountains can make the feudal lords look up; in all the empire none matches Guanzhong."

entries.zh: 帝稱善。
entries.en: Hongwu commended the memorial.
entries.literal: The emperor praised it.

entries.zh: 至是，諭太子曰：「天下山川惟秦地號為險固，汝往以省觀風俗，慰勞秦父老子弟。」
entries.en: He now told the heir: "Of all landscapes only Qin is called impregnable; go observe its customs and comfort its elders."
entries.literal: At this time he instructed the crown prince, saying: "Among the mountains and rivers of the empire, only Qin territory is called strategically secure; go to observe customs and comfort the elders and people of Qin."

entries.zh: 於是擇文武諸臣扈太子行。
entries.en: Civil and military officials were then chosen to accompany him.
entries.literal: Thereupon civil and military officials were chosen to escort the crown prince on the journey.

entries.zh: 既行，使諭曰：「爾昨渡江，震雷忽起于東南，導爾前行，是威震之兆也。
entries.en: After his departure a message said: "When you crossed the river yesterday, thunder rose in the southeast and led you on—a sign of commanding majesty.
entries.literal: After he had set out, a messenger instructed, saying: "Yesterday when you crossed the river, thunder suddenly rose in the southeast and guided you forward—this is an omen of awe-inspiring might.

entries.zh: 然一旬久陰不雨，佔有陰謀，宜慎舉動，嚴宿衛，施仁布惠，以回天意。」
entries.en: Yet ten days of cloud without rain suggest conspiracy; move carefully, guard the camp strictly, and show mercy and grace to move Heaven."
