entries.en: When Chen arrived and they spoke together, the Founder was delighted and kept him for confidential counsel, growing more trusting of him each day.
entries.literal: When Chen arrived and he conversed with him, he was greatly pleased; thereupon he was kept to take part in secret deliberations, day by day growing trusted.

entries.zh: 太祖為吳王，授供奉司丞，辭。
entries.en: While the Founder was still King of Wu, Chen was offered the post of deputy director of the Service Bureau, but he declined.
entries.literal: When the Founder was King of Wu, he was appointed Attendant of the Service Bureau; he declined.

entries.zh: 即皇帝位，三授翰林學士，皆辭。
entries.en: After he took the throne, Chen was three times offered the rank of Hanlin Academician, and each time he refused.
entries.literal: Upon assuming the imperial throne, three times he was granted Hanlin Academician; each time he declined.

entries.zh: 乃賜肩輿一乘，衛士十人護出入，以示榮寵。
entries.en: Instead the Emperor gave him a sedan chair and ten guards to attend him whenever he went abroad, as a mark of special honor.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was granted one sedan chair and ten guards to escort him in going out and coming in, to show honor and favor.

entries.zh: 洪武三年，奉命至浙江廉察民隱，還賜金帛。
entries.en: In Hongwu year 3 he was sent to Zhejiang to inquire into the people's grievances; when he returned, the court rewarded him with gold and silk.
entries.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, on orders he went to Zhejiang to investigate and examine the people's hidden grievances; on his return he was bestowed gold and silks.

entries.zh: 除中書左丞，又辭。
entries.en: He was appointed left vice president of the Secretariat, but again declined.
entries.literal: He was appointed Left Vice President of the Secretariat; again he declined.

entries.zh: 明年召對華蓋殿，賜坐，命草《平西詔》。
entries.en: The following year he was summoned to audience in Huagai Hall, given a seat, and ordered to draft the Edict on Pacifying the West.
entries.literal: The next year he was summoned for audience in Huagai Hall, granted a seat, and ordered to draft the "Edict on Pacifying the West."

entries.zh: 授禮部侍郎，兼弘文館大學士，復辭。
entries.en: He was made vice minister of rites and concurrent grand academician of the Hongwen Hall, but once more refused.
entries.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall; again he declined.

entries.zh: 西域進良馬，遇引漢故事以諫。
entries.en: When the Western Regions sent fine horses as tribute, Chen cited Han-dynasty precedents in remonstrance.
entries.literal: The Western Regions presented fine horses; Chen cited Han precedents to remonstrate.

entries.zh: 除太常少卿，固辭。
entries.en: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and firmly declined.
entries.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he firmly declined.

entries.zh: 強之，不可。
entries.en: They pressed the appointment on him, but he would not accept.
entries.literal: They pressed him; he would not accept.

entries.zh: 最後除禮部尚書，又固辭。
entries.en: At last he was made minister of rites, and again firmly declined.
entries.literal: Finally he was appointed Minister of Rites; again he firmly declined.

entries.zh: 帝沉吟良久，從之。
entries.en: The Emperor hesitated a long while, then yielded to his wish.
entries.literal: The Emperor pondered for a long while and assented.

entries.zh: 自是不復強以官。
entries.en: After that the court no longer tried to force an office on him.
entries.literal: From then on he was no longer pressed with office.

entries.zh: 帝嘗從容言欲官其子，遇曰：「臣三子皆幼，學未成，請俟異日。」
entries.en: The Emperor once remarked in an easy tone that he wished to appoint Chen's sons. Chen replied, "Your servant's three sons are still young and have not finished their studies; I beg that Your Majesty wait for another day."
entries.literal: The Emperor once spoke at ease, saying he wished to give office to Chen's sons. Chen said: "Your servant's three sons are all young; their studies are not complete—please wait for another day."

entries.zh: 帝亦弗強也。
entries.en: The Emperor did not press the matter either.
entries.literal: The Emperor likewise did not press.

entries.zh: 遇自開基之始，即侍帷幄。
entries.en: From the very founding of the dynasty Chen had served at the imperial side.
entries.literal: From the beginning of the founding of the state, Chen attended at the imperial curtains.

entries.zh: 帝嘗問保國安民至計，遇對：「以不嗜殺人，薄斂，任賢，復先王禮樂為首務。」
entries.en: When the Emperor once asked him for the supreme policy to secure the realm and settle the people, Chen answered, "The foremost tasks are to refrain from bloodshed, keep taxes light, employ the worthy, and restore the ritual and music of the ancient kings."
entries.literal: The Emperor once asked the supreme plan for securing the state and settling the people. Chen answered: "Take as foremost tasks not being fond of killing people, light taxation, employing the worthy, and restoring the ritual and music of former kings."

entries.zh: 廷臣或有過被譴責，遇力為解，多得全釋。
entries.en: When court officials were faulted and punished, Chen often pleaded on their behalf, and many were spared.
entries.literal: When court ministers at times had faults and were reprimanded and punished, Chen strove to intercede for them, and many were fully released.

entries.zh: 其計畫多秘不傳，而寵禮之隆，勛戚大臣無與比者。
entries.en: Most of his counsel was kept secret, yet the honor the court showed him surpassed even that given to meritorious kinsmen and great ministers.
entries.literal: His plans were mostly secret and not transmitted, yet the loftiness of favor and ceremony shown him—no meritorious kinsmen or great ministers could compare.

entries.zh: 數監幸其第，語必稱「先生」，或呼為「君子」。
entries.en: The Emperor repeatedly visited his home in person, always addressing him as "Master" or calling him "the gentleman."
entries.literal: Several times the Emperor in person visited his residence; in speech he invariably called him "Master," or addressed him as "the gentleman."

entries.zh: 命爵輒辭，終成其高。
entries.en: Whenever ennoblement was offered he declined, and in the end his reputation for lofty integrity was complete.
entries.literal: Whenever ennoblement was commanded he declined; in the end his loftiness was fulfilled.

entries.zh: 十七年卒，賜葬鐘山。
entries.en: He died in year 17 of the reign and was granted burial on Bell Mountain.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; burial on Bell Mountain was granted.

entries.zh: 秦從龍，字元之，洛陽人。
entries.en: Qin Conglong, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was a native of Luoyang.
entries.literal: Qin Conglong, style name Yuanzhi, was a man of Luoyang.

entries.zh: 仕元，官江南行台侍御史。
entries.en: Under the Yuan he served as an attending censor on the Jiangnan regional secretariat.
entries.literal: He served the Yuan; his office was Attending Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 兵亂，避居鎮江。
entries.en: During the military turmoil he took refuge in Zhenjiang.
entries.literal: When soldiers rioted, he avoided trouble and dwelt at Zhenjiang.

entries.zh: 徐達之攻鎮江也，太祖謂之曰：「聞有秦元之者，才器老成，汝當詢訪，致吾欲見意。」
entries.en: When Xu Da was attacking Zhenjiang, the Founder told him, "I have heard of a Qin Yuanzhi, a man of seasoned talent—you should seek him out and convey my wish to meet him."
entries.literal: When Xu Da attacked Zhenjiang, the Founder said to him: "I have heard there is one Qin Yuanzhi, whose talent and capacity are seasoned and mature—you should inquire and seek him out, and convey my wish to see him."

entries.zh: 達下鎮江，訪得之。
entries.en: Xu Da took the city, found him, and brought him in.
entries.literal: Xu Da took Zhenjiang, sought him out, and obtained him.

entries.zh: 太祖命從子文正、甥李文忠奉金綺造其廬聘焉。
entries.en: The Founder sent his nephew Wen Zheng and his sister's son Li Wenzhong with gifts of gold and brocade to Qin's home to invite him.
entries.literal: The Founder ordered his nephew Wen Zheng and his sister's son Li Wenzhong to bear gold and brocade and go to his dwelling to engage him.

entries.zh: 從龍與妻陳偕來，太祖自迎之於龍江。
entries.en: Conglong came with his wife Chen, and the Founder went in person to welcome them at Longjiang.
entries.literal: Conglong came together with his wife Chen; the Founder himself went out to welcome them at Longjiang.

entries.zh: 時太祖居富民家，因邀從龍與同處，朝夕訪以時事。
entries.en: At that time the Founder was staying at a wealthy household; he invited Conglong to lodge with him and consulted him morning and evening on affairs of state.
entries.literal: At that time the Founder lodged at a rich man's house; he therefore invited Conglong to dwell together and morning and evening sought his counsel on current affairs.

entries.zh: 已，即元御史台為府，居從龍西華門外，事無大小悉與之謀。
entries.en: Soon afterward, having made the former Yuan censorate his headquarters, he housed Conglong just outside the Xihua Gate and consulted him on every matter, large or small.
entries.literal: Before long, taking the Yuan Censorate as the headquarters, he lodged Conglong outside the Xihua Gate; matters great and small were all deliberated with him.

entries.zh: 嘗以筆書漆簡，問答甚密，左右皆不能知。
entries.en: They sometimes exchanged written questions and answers on lacquered slips so privately that even those close at hand could not tell what was discussed.
entries.literal: At times he wrote with the brush on lacquered slips; question and answer were very close, and those at his side could not know.

entries.zh: 從龍生日，太祖與世子厚有贈遺，或親至其家燕飲。
entries.en: On Conglong's birthday the Founder and the heir apparent sent lavish gifts, and sometimes the Founder came in person to feast at his home.
entries.literal: On Conglong's birthday the Founder and the heir apparent made generous gifts, or the Founder in person came to his house for a banquet.

entries.zh: 至正二十五年冬，從龍子澤死，請告歸。
entries.en: In the winter of Zhizheng year 25, Conglong's son Ze died, and he asked leave to return home.
entries.literal: In the winter of the twenty-fifth year of Zhizheng, Conglong's son Ze died; he requested leave to return home.

entries.zh: 太祖出郊握手送之。
entries.en: The Founder went out beyond the suburbs, took his hand, and saw him off.
entries.literal: The Founder went out beyond the suburbs, clasped his hand, and saw him off.

entries.zh: 尋病卒，年七十，太祖驚悼。
entries.en: Soon afterward he died of illness at the age of seventy, and the Founder was shocked and deeply grieved.
entries.literal: Before long he died of illness, aged seventy; the Founder was startled and grieved.

entries.zh: 時方督軍至鎮江，親臨哭之，厚恤其家，命有司營葬。
entries.en: He was then directing troops toward Zhenjiang, but came in person to mourn him, gave his family generous relief, and ordered the authorities to arrange the funeral.
entries.literal: At that time he was just directing the army to Zhenjiang; he came in person to weep for him, richly comforted his family, and ordered the officials to arrange the burial.

entries.zh: 葉兌，字良仲，寧海人。
entries.en: Ye Dui, courtesy name Liangzhong, was a native of Ninghai.
entries.literal: Ye Dui, style name Liangzhong, was a man of Ninghai.

entries.zh: 以經濟自負，尤精天文、地理、卜筮之書。
entries.en: He prided himself on statecraft and was especially expert in astronomy, geography, and divination.
entries.literal: He prided himself on statecraft and economics, and was especially refined in books on astronomy, geography, and divination.

entries.zh: 元末，知天運有歸，以布衣獻書太祖。
entries.en: Near the end of the Yuan, seeing that the mandate of Heaven was shifting, he submitted a written plan to the Founder as a private citizen.
entries.literal: At the end of the Yuan, knowing that Heaven's mandate had a destination, as a commoner he presented a memorial to the Founder.

entries.zh: 列一綱三目，言天下大計。
entries.en: It laid out one overarching strategy and three subsidiary points on the grand design for the empire.
entries.literal: He set forth one main theme and three sub-points, speaking of the great plan for the realm.

entries.zh: 時太祖已定寧越，規取張士誠、方國珍。
entries.en: At that time the Founder had already secured Ningyue and was planning to seize Zhang Shicheng and Fang Guozhen.
entries.literal: At that time the Founder had already secured Ning and Yue and was planning to take Zhang Shicheng and Fang Guozhen.
